Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
34de16ba31a98b6ca3895143b1aa9ee703bcb69c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines three technology families that have drawn attention from supply chain researchers and practitioners: blockchain, augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR), and edge computing. The argument is not simply that each yields operational benefits, but that their significance lies in addressing complementary problems within a single domain. Blockchain addresses trust and information integrity in multi-party networks; AR/VR addresses human interface challenges in complex environments; edge computing provides distributed computation enabling real-time responsiveness at scale. Drawing on recent work, the chapter traces how these technologies support the industrial metaverse. Sustainability, resilience, human-centred design, and infrastructure scalability are key themes. It also examines challenges—interoperability, governance gaps, cost barriers, and security exposures—and offers a coherent view of their convergence and implications.</jats:p>

title: Industrial Metaverse in Supply Chain Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
09f40adbf7cb76bff382bbf6d92aec1c8a0bac82.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the concept of the industrial metaverse in supply chain management, highlighting its role in enabling AI-driven virtualization, collaborative decision-making, and sustainable transformation. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, digital twins, IoT, and immersive interfaces create integrated, real-time, and interactive supply chain ecosystems. The study emphasizes the shift from reactive to predictive and autonomous supply chains through simulation, optimization, and data-driven intelligence. It further discusses the role of the industrial metaverse in enhancing multi-stakeholder collaboration, operational efficiency, and environmental sustainability through circular economy practices. A comprehensive framework is proposed to integrate technological, organizational, and strategic dimensions. The chapter contributes by offering insights into building resilient, intelligent, and sustainable supply chain systems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Twin Architecture in Supply Chain Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
d99b6055016f0e8c84e8e502fe276ebb105bc5e1.abstract: <jats:p>The major gap that still exists is the operationalization of the application of the concept of digital twist in the supply chain management although more research has been done on the area. This is more so in the emerging countries where its adoption is impeded by infrastructural and fragmented logistic ecosystems and limited capital. This chapter addresses that gap by introducing digital twin architectures within supply chain processes through a structured conceptual framework to support adaptive governance, anticipate risks, and intelligence in decision-making. Three basic mechanisms are discussed in the chapter such as (1) bi-directional data synchronization in real-time among supply chain nodes; (2) predictive simulation modeling of demand volatility and disruption; and (3) cross-tier visibility as an architecture requirement of coordination. These processes rest on a critical review of the literature, industry experience and systems-thinking concepts.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Digital Twins and Blockchain Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
800c4603905b0b481af418f93c27b335627b538c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops an architecture for combining cognitive digital twins with blockchain ecosystems to deliver predictive business intelligence in the industrial metaverse. It argues that digital-twin initiatives create value only when operational telemetry, semantic context, decision models, and human governance are connected through trusted data-sharing and executable coordination mechanisms. Drawing on research in digital twins, industrial metaverse design, blockchain-enabled provenance, smart contracts, human-centric manufacturing, and explainable AI, the chapter proposes a layered reference architecture, performance metrics, implementation logic, and governance controls. It also examines persistent challenges, including semantic fragmentation, model drift, latency, privacy, interoperability, energy cost, and the oracle problem. The chapter concludes with design recommendations and a research agenda for resilient, trustworthy, and economically useful industrial intelligence systems across networked industrial-metaverse platforms and ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Twins and Blockchain-Enabled Trust for Resilient Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
6cae48cda77d8a51b8ca2bc4b94e05b4a9e8c301.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, we explore the process of achieving supply chain resilience in Industrial Metaverse environments by embedding digital twin technology and blockchain-based distributed trust mechanisms. No single technology is sufficient to address the triple crises of disruption, opacity, and accountability in contemporary supply chains. The chapter makes its case through trans-disciplinary scholarship spanning supply chain management, digital transformation, blockchain governance, and Industry 4.0. They introduce a 5-layer conceptual framework to illustrate how these physical operations, data connectivity, simulation, distributed verification, and governance layers are interdependent among each other via the Digital Twin–Blockchain Trust Framework, which allows us to visualize how such Human-centric smart systems can lead towards Visibility, Traceability, and Adaptive Resilience eventually. Investigates sustainability implications, ethical risks, and cyber vulnerabilities, as well as concrete pathways for managerial adoption.</jats:p>

title: A Framework for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Supply-Chain Optimization (HQCSCO)
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
d1b522f79a68031ab548219a1152e6dfcb83f336.abstract: <jats:p>The study presents the earliest effort to conceptualize SCM integration with quantum computing principles, providing dynamic capabilities for SCM. It proposes a unique interdisciplinary framework that demonstrates where hybrid quantum-classical approaches can realise value, and specifies the conditions that organizations must meet to adopt such methods. In this article, a conceptual framework has been proposed for HQCSCO. This framework facilitates key decision-making areas such as inventory optimisation, production scheduling, and logistics routing, where quantum-enhanced algorithms could supplement classical models to enhance performance. At the managerial level, the framework helps manufacturing leaders to determine viability, prioritize high-impact use cases, and develop future-ready digital capabilities that enhance cost efficiency, agility, and resilience. The research provides a conceptually-based baseline of quantum-facile supply chains and offers a research agenda to investigate the strategic, ethical, and operational implications thereof.</jats:p>

title: Immersive Stock Control for Virtual Depots via Process Digital Twins and Topological Data Analysis
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
181d6ce5803b6924cc02dfd46f21bf24456d4579.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents the development of an advanced inventory management model for virtual warehouses. By combining process digital twins with Topological Data Analysis, this model strives to support supervisors in pinpointing bottleneck formations that standard performance indicators are unable to reveal. The methodology describes how IoT-like intralogistics events are interpreted as augmented point clouds. The methodology also describes how persistent homology is computed through Vietoris-Rips and Alpha-complex filtrations, and how topological indicators are transformed into an immersive decision layer through the framework's comprehensive approach to bottleneck and Wasserstein distances. The computational case interprets fragmentation, routing loops, and volumetric cavities as congestion, vulnerability, and latent capacity indicators. The results show how the persistent topology of the model offers a candidate articulate layer for the process digital twins. The model still needs additional empirical calibration, for operational interventions in a physical warehouse.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Smart Ports and Sustainable Maritime Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
fb27937fd6ed5b67a638e8b71b2617dfc041ff66.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming maritime logistics by improving operational efficiency, sustainability, and digital integration. At the same time, the Industrial Metaverse is reshaping supply chain management through real time data, digital twins, and intelligent decision environments. However, the linkage between these developments remains underexplored. This study conducts a bibliometric and thematic review of 208 Scopus indexed journal articles published between 2013 and 2025 using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix. The analysis identifies key trends and four thematic clusters: smart ports, green shipping, digital transformation, and governance. Findings indicate that existing research is technologically advanced but fragmented, with limited focus on system integration, human interaction, and economic feasibility. The study highlights critical gaps and provides insights for advancing next generation, Industrial Metaverse based maritime supply chains.</jats:p>

title: Challenges of Industry 4.0 Adoption in Malaysia's Ship Repair Industry
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
a5c2578bb1ed98f301ea6bb9016c9962fd028ba1.abstract: <jats:p>The adoption of Industrial Revolution 4.0 (IR 4.0) technologies in Malaysia's ship repair industry presents significant opportunities to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and global competitiveness. However, the transition toward digital transformation remains constrained by multiple structural, technological, and organizational challenges. This study aims to identify and analyze the key barriers to IR 4.0 adoption using a mixed-method approach that integrates literature review and empirical data collected from 175 industry experts. The findings reveal five critical challenges, namely technological infrastructure and investment, data management and integration, workforce skills, cybersecurity, and regulatory frameworks. Among these, infrastructure and data-related challenges emerged as the most significant. The findings contribute to both academic literature and industry practice by offering a comprehensive understanding of IR 4.0 adoption in a developing maritime context.</jats:p>

title: Industrial Metaverse and AI-Driven Food Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
47d3e0515c13fda1af2da5950b7c6fa396315d15.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores how agriculture and food logistics are being transformed through artificial intelligence and Industrial Metaverse-enabled supply chain systems in emerging economies. It examines the shift from traditional linear food systems toward immersive, data-driven, and phygital ecosystems integrating digital twins, blockchain, IoT, and AR/VR technologies. Using a qualitative multiple-case study approach, the research analyzes India, China, Brazil, and Russia to understand how policy reforms, technological adoption, and infrastructure development influence food security and resilience. Findings show that AI-enabled forecasting, real-time monitoring, and immersive simulation improve supply chain efficiency, reduce food waste, and enhance sustainability. However, challenges such as infrastructure gaps, digital inequality, and limited workforce readiness persist. The study emphasizes the importance of integrated policy frameworks and education systems to enable next-generation resilient food supply chains.</jats:p>

title: Sustainability and the Circular Economy in Virtualized Settings
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
ebe6f0b34ee1b19fb405906ddf6f10d2270baad4.abstract: <jats:p>Supply chains are under mounting pressure to reconcile operational performance with environmental responsibility — a tension that conventional efficiency tools and isolated green initiatives have not resolved satisfactorily. This chapter examines how the industrial metaverse, as an integrative platform encompassing digital twins, extended reality interfaces, and AI-enabled analytics, can embed circular economy principles within supply chains. Drawing on recent scholarship, it traces alignment between closed-loop material flows and the informational closure enabled by metaverse environments. Attention is given to enabling conditions and persistent barriers — organisational, technological, and regulatory — shaping adoption. The chapter situates these developments within the digital economy, considering how financial digitalization and platform economics affect viability, and offers practical guidance followed by a research agenda.</jats:p>

title: Energy Paradox

5978dd6e52239fe81f0eae8216a3d68a87b18554.abstract: <jats:p>The consequence of Carbon Savings (CS) on green energy cost reduction (GECR) using Biogas Logistics Optimization (BGLO) in Tanzania is analysed in this work. The quantitative research approach was adopted with 280 respondents of biogas and energy sector. The results indicate that, the CS has a significant satisfactory impact on GECR and BGLO. Moreover, the cost reduction effect of BGLO is meaningfully mediated, works across CS and cost efficiency. The findings reveal that benefits of environmental sustainability depend not just on the environmental sustainability, but also on the efficiency of logistic systems. The study combines both the SCMT and EET to enunciate the relationships. The results suggest from a practical point of view that the performance of biogas systems could be further enhanced by improving the efficiency of logistics infrastructure and logistics coordination. The study provides valuable policy guidance and insights for future research.</jats:p>

title: Ethical Governance and Cybersecurity Frameworks for Decentralized Immersive Supply Chains in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
b543d24b4de0e90e3100ab0ae1c6f35a85be60f6.abstract: <jats:p>The Industrial Metaverse is transforming supply chain management by creating persistent, immersive, and decentralized virtual environments where stakeholders collaborate through digital twins, smart contracts, and spatial computing. This shift introduces ethical and cybersecurity challenges threatening trust, transparency, and resilience. This chapter examines governance and security risks in operating supply chains within shared virtual spaces, addressing three pillars: data sovereignty and intellectual property protection, ethical algorithmic design for automated procurement, and privacy-preserving verification including zero-knowledge proofs. The chapter makes three contributions: it applies the “Decentralization Paradox” to supply chain governance, proposes a Hybrid Governance Framework integrating protocol-level, organizational, and regulatory mechanisms, and develops a Risk Severity Index for threat prioritization. These provide a foundational governance architecture for next-generation supply chain operations.</jats:p>

title: Gcn5 and mTORC1 mediated regulation of autophagy controls Drosophila blood cell homeostasis
container-title: eLife
700db83f75519837e25d45ca5d0f3b8c17d2c4a4.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Blood progenitors are regulated by a variety of systemic and nutritional cues from their environment. In the
                    <jats:italic>Drosophila</jats:italic>
                    lymph gland (LG), the Posterior Signaling Center acts as a stem cell niche striking a balance between progenitors and differentiated blood cells. Autophagy is a vital cellular process that maintains homeostasis by removing unnecessary or dysfunctional cell components through autophagic degradation and recycling. Here, using genetic perturbation analysis, we show that autophagy plays a critical role in regulating LG blood cell homeostasis. General control non-derepressible 5 (Gcn5), a histone acetyltransferase, is expressed in the primary LG lobe, and modulation of Gcn5 levels perturbs LG homeostasis. Our results show that hemocyte-specific Gcn5 modulation controls autophagic flux in the hemocytes. Furthermore, we show that modulation of mTORC1 activity can perturb hematopoiesis. Our results indicate that organismal Gcn5 levels respond to dietary shifts and are modulated by mTORC1 signaling. Chemical intervention shows that mTORC1 overrides the effect exerted by Gcn5 in regulating LG hematopoiesis. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that Gcn5 and mTORC1 regulate autophagy to maintain blood cell homeostasis in
                    <jats:italic>Drosophila</jats:italic>
                    .
                  </jats:p>

title: Beyond Belief Updating: A Framework for Self-Belief Formation
3796862ab71587287fb46c3bdf9532408a32202a.abstract: From early childhood, we form self-beliefs about where we belong, what we are good at, or who loves us. Despite extensive psychological research on self-beliefs, the fundamental question of how they initially form has received surprisingly little attention. Existing work on self-belief updating overlooks two critical limitations. First, it treats self-related learning as arising from isolated events, ignoring that self-beliefs typically emerge from sequences of meaningfully connected experiences. Second, because updating paradigms operate in familiar domains, participants already hold precise prior beliefs intertwined with established motives and emotional states making it impossible to study belief formation from a genuinely uninformed starting point. We propose that studying novel experiential domains addresses both problems: individuals enter such domains with neutral, imprecise self-beliefs, enabling formation of “artificial” self-beliefs through repeated feedback in a controlled setting. As a concrete implementation, we introduce the Learning Of Own Performance (LOOP) task, in which participants form beliefs about their abilities in a novel performance domain. Extensions of this approach could illuminate broader aspects of self-belief formation, including personality and identity. This Perspective bridges psychology, computational neuroscience, and sociology around a foundational question: how do we come to think about ourselves the way we do?

title: Decentralized Finance and Digital Assets: A New Perspective on Financial Management and Risk
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
13b14090a5c64d7c3224b43ae85f72408e707dbf.abstract: <jats:p>Financial services are being transformed, how they are designed, accessed, and managed, by the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi) and digital assets. These innovations via blockchain networks, smart contracts, and tokenization offer alternatives to existing models for payments, lending, investment, and asset exchange. But the economic, institutional and operating risks of financial intermediation are not eroded when transactions are automated. In this conceptual study, the impact of DeFi and digital assets on financial management is explored, including capital allocation, treasury operations, risk management, and the governance of digital assets. It assesses what could be gained from this technology, alongside its potential technological vulnerabilities, market instability, regulatory uncertainty and inability to provide meaningful financial inclusion. An analysis approach is built to present a managerial perspective, which considers digital financial arrangements from an economic function, dependency and accountability standpoint. It points out that sustainable adoption requires coordination of technology with financial management, strong rights, organizational efficiency and appropriate governance. DeFi is therefore a reorganization of financial management and not the automatic replacement of existing financial institutions.</jats:p>

title: Blockchain Technology in Management: Opportunities, Risks and Governance Challenges
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
37cc95f3465e4e0fb32f40a5e9c5644d70c42fdc.abstract: <jats:p>The idea of using blockchain seems to be gaining support as a way to facilitate transactions between organizations which don't have a shared database or administration. The importance of its management, however, is subject to debate. This article provides a critical assessment of the opportunities, risks and governance issues of organizations taking up blockchain technology. Research is synthesized into a focused narrative organized by three themes—Organizational Value, Implementation Constraints and Institutional Governance Responsibilities—that are grounded in the foundational research, further developed by management and information-systems scholarship, and then extended by institutional guidance. Several potential benefits are suggested in the literature: record reconciliation, traceability of the supply chain, auditing and rule-based transaction processing. This is only achievable by partner willingness to share, the validity of the source information and the appropriateness of blockchain over traditional databases. Potential gains might be offset by technical risks, privacy issues, organizational challenges, and uncertainties regarding regulations. In arguing this, the article does not suggest that you can forgo identifiable decision responsibilities, human responsibility or good dispute resolution when you decentralize record validation. Strategic fit, network design, accountability, information stewardship and performance review are the elements of an integrated governance framework. The paper provides an action-oriented consideration of blockchain adoption, considering benefits not as inherent properties of blockchain but rather possibilities that are likely to occur when blockchain is adopted.</jats:p>

title: Managing Investment Decisions and Risk in Decentralized Financial Markets: Evidence from Blockchain-Based Platforms
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
5970dbe0d163fa1f2d86a6ee377a5277f5d7e7c5.abstract: <jats:p>Decentralized finance (DeFi) has provided alternative investment, lending, trading, asset management and other methods via blockchain on both public and private platforms. Unlike traditional financial institutions, DeFi protocols rely on smart contracts for transactions, collateral, and financial returns and do not depend on the entire reliance of the centralized intermediaries. The innovations provide access, transparency and operational efficiency but also financial, technological, liquidity, and governance risks to the investor. This study adopts a structured literature review approach of academic studies, institutional reports and documented platforms mechanisms and investigates the investment decision making and risk management in decentralized financial markets. The cases of platform Uniswap, Aave, Compound, and MakerDAO are not meant to represent an empirical sample, but instead serve as examples to illustrate the platforms. Thematic synthesis take account of the concepts of portfolio theory and information asymmetry, highlighting the centrality of factors like expected return, collateral management, security of smart contracts, the reliability of oracles, concentration of governance, and regulatory uncertainty. It concludes that transparency of record and liquidation automation can enhance transaction discipline, but will not be enough to prevent losses in stressed markets all on its own. The study suggests an integrated decision-making approach that incorporates elements of financial, technological due diligence, governance appraisal, Exposure limits and ongoing monitoring. The results offer a basis for future transaction level tests of the effectiveness of risk adjusted investment strategies.</jats:p>

title: A Survey of Learning-based Method Name Prediction
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
48b81eddcf90694d4fefcd0a971c62e474bcae45.abstract: <jats:p>The choice of method names significantly influences code comprehension and maintenance, posing a considerable challenge, especially for novice developers. Automating the prediction of appropriate method names based on the method code body has emerged as a promising approach to address this challenge. In recent years, numerous Machine/Deep Learning (ML/DL)-based Method Name Prediction (MNP) techniques have been proposed. However, a systematic review of these techniques is currently lacking, hindering future researchers from understanding the research status, development trends, challenges, and opportunities in this field. To fill this gap, in this article, we conduct a systematic literature review on learning-based MNP studies. Specifically, we first perform a thorough review of the literature concerning publication venue, publication year, and contribution types. This analysis enables us to discern trends in studies related to MNP. Second, we depict the general workflow of learning-based MNP techniques, which involves three consecutive subprocesses: context extraction, context preprocessing, and context-based prediction. Subsequently, we investigate contemporary techniques/solutions applied in the three subprocesses. Third, we scrutinize the widely used experimental databases, evaluation metrics, and replication packages utilized in MNP studies. Moreover, we summarize existing empirical studies on MNP to facilitate a quick understanding of their focus and findings for subsequent researchers. Finally, based on a systematic review and summary of existing work, we outline several open challenges and opportunities in MNP that remain to be addressed in future work.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The time course of neural activity predictive of self-initiated movement
6bb29c0fa61a9bb6f281a6f43aa6ce014a54e928.abstract: <jats:p>Decades of research have shown that early ramping activity is a very reliable antecedent of self-initiated movement. However, the dominant paradigm has been to only analyze data epochs culminating in movement, which discounts how often slow ramping might occur when no movement follows. To address this, we introduced a matched control condition that did not culminate in movement. We recorded electroencephalography data and compared these two conditions using a variety of powerful machine-learning classifiers. Although early ramping activity was present, it was not useful in predicting movement. Instead, classification accuracy rose abruptly about 100 ms before movement. By contrast, the traditional approach reproduced the spurious impression of early predictability. Our results substantially constrain the interpretation that early EEG antecedents, including the RP, reflect a commitment to act, instead indicating that EEG-detectable evidence consistent with such a commitment emerges closer to movement onset, in line with the timing of conscious intention and the capacity for late movement inhibition. More broadly, our results show that a reliable antecedent is not necessarily a good predictor, underscoring the need for proper control conditions in time series analyses.</jats:p>

title: Feasibility Analysis of Education in Indonesian Provinces: A Machine Learning Clustering Approach for Regional Classification
container-title: Engineering and Technology Journal
1b5bd0dfe6cab0a4e4dc5dc25d573208b2fdac15.abstract: <jats:p>Education system feasibility varies significantly across Indonesian provinces due to geographic, socioeconomic, and infrastructural disparities. This study applies unsupervised machine learning clustering algorithms (K-Means, Hierarchical Clustering, Gaussian Mixture Models, and Self-Organizing Maps) to classify Indonesian provinces into homogeneous groups based on education feasibility indicators. Using 39 provinces and special territories, we evaluated clustering quality through internal validation metrics (Silhouette coefficient and Davies-Bouldin index) and inter-algorithm agreement measures (Adjusted Rand Index and Normalized Mutual Information). Results demonstrate that Hierarchical Clustering achieves the best Davies-Bouldin index (0.782), while K-Means and GMM produce identical partitions (ARI = 1.0, NMI = 1.0). Self-Organizing Maps identified nine distinct regional education feasibility profiles, with provincial distributions revealing significant heterogeneity in education conditions. These findings provide a quantitative framework for targeted policy interventions and resource allocation to improve education feasibility across Indonesia’s diverse regions.</jats:p>

title: Entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills, and self-esteem in students participating in sports programmes in Colombia

<jats:p>This research presents the results of a systematic review that analyses the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills and self-esteem in students enrolled in sports programmes in Colombia, with the aim of identifying the factors that influence their positive attitude towards entrepreneurial capacity. In the literature review, 100 articles and academic research papers were selected between 2019 and 2025, prioritised from 42,958 results from different resources such as reference databases, multidisciplinary databases, academic repositories and academic journals. The databases with the highest number of results were Scopus, Web of Science, Wiley, Springer Nature, Science Direct, Ebsco Host, among others such as (COnnecting REpositories), Taylor & Francis, and Google Scholar. The results showed an interest in academia to research and reflect on the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, emotional skills, and young people. However, in most studies, entrepreneurial culture is associated with variables such as emotional intelligence and social skills in university contexts, leaving the field of the relationship between these variables and the field of sports somewhat lacking in studies. Studies that explore this relationship in depth conclude that athletes develop socio-emotional skills that make them strong candidates for entrepreneurship. However, there are limitations in the implementation of mechanisms that promote an entrepreneurial culture ( ) in university contexts for young people studying sports programmes.

title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
7e6b65fd0eceaed8ad891218da9c81d3f193d863.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)—executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention’s effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Multi-omic integration using interpretable machine learning reveals genetic mechanisms of trait variation and phenotypic plasticity in switchgrass
d5ecaf8e9c0ab25f0f77449121b30e109d87be40.abstract: <jats:p>Uncovering the genetic architecture of quantitative traits is challenging because polygenic control yields small individual gene effects and because gene–gene and genotype-by-environment interactions add further complexity. To understand the genetic basis of polygenic traits and their plasticity across environments, we integrated genome-wide SNPs and RNA-seq transcript data with interpretable statistical and machine learning models in a switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) diversity panel grown at contrasting field sites in Michigan and Texas. Notably, in addition to single environments, our trait prediction models were able to predict phenotypic differences, across environments i.e., plasticity. By interpreting trait prediction models with explainable machine learning methods, we identified genes that are the most predictive of flowering time and annual biomass production across environments, based on their associated gene expression levels and nearby SNPs. This approach recovered canonical flowering regulators and revealed novel, environment-specific candidate flowering genes. Further, transcriptome models consistently recovered more switchgrass genes homologous to experimentally validated genes in Arabidopsis and rice than SNP-based models. Feature interaction scores from the models also allow the identification of trait- and environment-dependent gene–gene interactions, where flowering time showed stronger and more abundant interactions than biomass. While some of the interactions identified are consistent with the link between flowering time and yield, most are novel predictors that need to be further evaluated. These findings provide insight into the genetic basis of trait variation and plasticity across environments and help prioritize candidate genes for functional validation and cultivar improvement.</jats:p>

title: Endoscopic ultrasound-based deep learning for predicting chemotherapy response in unresectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
container-title: World Journal of Gastroenterology
1f6a560325fb967b8d7fb19fd1972b99328cdc40.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal malignancies, and chemotherapy remains the main treatment option for patients with unresectable disease. Reliable prediction of chemotherapy response is therefore critical for individualized treatment planning. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) provides high-resolution, tumor-specific imaging that may be well suited for deep learning-based prediction of chemotherapy response.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To develop and validate an EUS-based deep learning model for predicting first-line chemotherapy response in patients with unresectable PDAC, and to evaluate its prognostic value for overall survival (OS) stratification.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In this retrospective, single-center study, 190 patients with histologically confirmed PDAC diagnosed between February 2016 and March 2025 were included. All patients were deemed ineligible for upfront surgical resection based on formal multidisciplinary team evaluation, including those with locally advanced or metastatic disease and those considered medically or personally unsuitable for surgery. Patients diagnosed in 2023 or earlier were assigned to the training and internal validation cohort (n  = 152) using five-fold cross-validation, whereas patients diagnosed from January 2024 onward at a separate campus of the same institution constituted a temporally independent test cohort with site separation (n  = 38). Tumor regions of interest were manually annotated on pre-treatment EUS images. Four convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures (VGG19, VGG19-BN, ResNet50, and ResNeXt50) were trained to predict progressive disease, as defined by RECIST version 1.1 after first-line chemotherapy. Model performance was evaluated at the patient level using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and accuracy, and model-derived risk stratification was assessed for OS.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In the independent test cohort, ResNeXt50 demonstrated the best discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.848; sensitivity, 65.38%; specificity, 84.19%), followed by ResNet50 (AUC = 0.844), whereas VGG19-BN (AUC = 0.775) and VGG19 (AUC = 0.614) showed lower performance. Model-predicted probabilities enabled effective risk stratification, with high-risk patients exhibiting significantly shorter OS compared with low-risk patients (log-rank P  < 0.01; hazard ratio = 1.77). In contrast, baseline carbohydrate antigen 19-9-based stratification did not significantly discriminate survival, and CNN-based models demonstrated higher discriminatory performance compared with the conventional serum biomarker.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CNN models based on region-of-interest-level EUS imaging can predict chemotherapy response and provide clinically meaningful prognostic stratification in PDAC. Among the evaluated architectures, ResNeXt50 demonstrated the most consistent and robust performance across independent testing and sensitivity analyses. This noninvasive imaging-based approach shows potential for integration into clinical workflows to support personalized treatment planning.</jats:p>

title: Towards Realistic Project-Level Code Generation via Multi-Agent Collaboration and Semantic Architecture Modeling
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
2e98affb75fe6b1c9fa0a80bf39cb6bb48af6b14.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In recent years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in automated code generation. In real-world software engineering, the growing demand for rapid iteration and continuous delivery underscores the importance of project-level code generation, where LLMs are expected to generate complete software projects directly from complex user requirements. This task, however, presents greater challenges due to larger input scales, multi-modal information, and the need for holistic architectural reasoning. Although existing studies have made initial explorations, they still face key limitations, including unrealistic datasets and unreliable evaluation metrics that fail to reflect real-world complexity, the semantic gap between human-written requirements and machine-interpretable structures, and difficulties in managing hierarchical dependencies and maintaining quality throughout the generation process. To address these limitations, we first introduce
                    <jats:sc>CodeProjectEval</jats:sc>
                    , a project-level code generation dataset built from 18 real-world repositories with 12.7 files and 2,388.6 lines of code per task on average, supplemented with documentation and executable test cases for automatic evaluation. We further propose
                    <jats:sc>ProjectGen</jats:sc>
                    , a multi-agent framework that decomposes projects into architecture design, skeleton generation, and code filling stages with iterative refinement and memory-based context management. Within this framework, we introduce the Semantic Software Architecture Tree, a structured and semantically rich representation that effectively bridges user requirements and source code implementation. Experiments show that
                    <jats:sc>ProjectGen</jats:sc>
                    achieves state-of-the-art performance, passing 52/124 test cases on the small-scale project-level code generation dataset DevBench, a 57% improvement over the baseline approaches, and 310 test cases on
                    <jats:sc>CodeProjectEval</jats:sc>
                    , representing an improvement of roughly tenfold compared to the baselines.
                  </jats:p>

title: Wine, Politics, and Markets
a1477911e3f6fe9d8e457d1b117363ace5c1f507.abstract:
<jats:p>Wine has been at the heart of human civilization for thousands of years, and for centuries governments around the world have regulated wine production, consumption, and trade for reasons ranging from consumer protection and quality assurance to tax revenue and the protection of vineyard owners’ rents. The European Union (EU) alone has introduced more than two thousand wine regulations. Some of today’s regulations date back hundreds of years; others are more recent; and there is considerable variation over time.

The rich history of wine regulation offers fascinating insights into the political economy of public policy and the ways in which such policies persist and evolve. This book examines specific historical developments involving wines that are well known today, such as Champagne, Port, Chianti, and Burgundy. Drawing on original historical sources and multilingual archival research, it provides the first comprehensive analysis of global wine regulations from an integrated political, economic, and historical perspective.

It will appeal to a wide range of readers, including academics and students across disciplines, and anyone interested in wine and wine markets around the world.</jats:p>
