title: Critiquing Normative Portrayals of Latinx/o Masculinities in Higher Education
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
4909877aa5e735ae689cbc8e10eb2e0416ee5f13.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter intends to disrupt the dominant and one-dimensional narratives associated with Latinx/o masculinities, positioning Latinx/o men as being synonymous with machismo. Instead, we argue for understanding Latinx/o masculinities as complex and multi-faceted, drawing upon critical frameworks (e.g., jotería studies, Chicana/Latina feminisms) to illustrate how this area of study must be viewed in more fluid ways. The chapter begins with a brief overview of Latinx/o masculinities scholarship, before then turning to a description of these critical frameworks. We conclude with several implications for scholars and practitioners who are hoping to challenge normative portrayals of Latinx/o masculinities in their work.</jats:p>

title: Cultural Resilience: Native American Men and the Reclamation of Masculinity
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
d519bbb9ff989c287ad7e460afbf9bfc58f1f764.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter examines the intersection of settler colonialism, masculinity, and Native American student experiences in higher education through a decolonial and Indigenous-centered lens. Using the Native Resource Center (NRC) at San Diego State University as a case study, the chapter demonstrates how Indigenous critical praxis can be applied to combat cultural erasure, support Native male identity formation, and restore relational understandings of masculinity. Drawing on Tribal Critical Race Theory, storytelling methodology, and deconstructivist perspectives, this work highlights how historical disruption of Indigenous gender roles, such as through the boarding school era, continues to impact Native men in contemporary educational spaces. Through institutional initiatives such as the Elymash Yuuchaap Program, the Native American Men’s Initiatives Advisory Board (NAMIAB), and events like Orange Shirt Day and the Indigenous Peoples Day: Week of Action, the NRC repositions healing, ceremony, and cultural education as essential components of student development. The chapter calls for the reimagining of student affairs practice, the need for Indigenous-specific masculinity studies, and the integration of relational, community-based approaches to support the success and well-being of Native students.</jats:p>

title: Helping Them Win on and off the Field: Navigating Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL), the Transfer Portal, and Academic Challenges for Supporting First-Generation Black Male Revenue Sport Student-Athletes
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
515794d73bc23714ec5c6d917f04b7dcbbd6b719.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The concept of intersectionality has caught the attention of many higher education stakeholders. While the majority of research has focused on how race, ethnicity, class, and gender impact student success, little research has been done specifically on first-generation black male college student athletes. This chapter will provide a thorough review of research and statistics in a scaffolded manner to ultimately build a case to support the crucial need and value when implementing the concept of intersectionality when wanting to support the success of black male student athletes who are first-generation college students navigating name, image, and likeness, transfer portal, and the higher education journey.</jats:p>

title: Men and Masculine Spaces in Men of Color Programs: A Statewide Perspective
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
8d3d613aa7ac7ab0136d9990e86bf3f7e513da5f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this chapter, we explore the experiences of Men of Color (MOC) in higher education. Over the past 15 years, scholarship on MOC has increased and there also has been an explosion in establishing MOC programs across college campuses that focus on improving retention and matriculation of MOC. Additionally, these programs provide MOC space for connection, bonding, sharing, and learning. We use the California State University Young Men of Color Consortium (CSU YMOC; now Young Men of California Consortium), which includes all 23 CSU campuses, as our context to explore men and masculine spaces in two primary ways. First, we explore the utility of masculine space(s) at CSU Dominguez Hills and Cal Poly Pomona through their respective MOC programs. These programs have a physical space on campus as well as programming that includes men’s retreats and annual convening events. Second, we offer an analysis of the YMOC Consortium annual conference, which brings together students, faculty, and practitioners from each campus where they engage in workshops, discussions, and activities by leading experts in the field. The YMOC Consortium helps educators by giving them the tools they need to create safe and supportive spaces for men on college campuses. We explore how the Consortium helps facilitate space for MOC during the convening and ways that practitioners enhance and expand their toolkits for supporting MOC through varied spaces in their work and efforts.</jats:p>

title: Understanding and Supporting Black Male Student Veterans
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
ca837b759348e4b0bbc5e68875e75524bf89da18.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Black male masculinity and identity development are often shaped by two contrasting forces: larger society’s pro-White definition of what it means to be a Black man, and the Black community’s definition of what it means to be a Black man. There is a similar difference between the influences of military and civilian culture, as those who join the armed forces undergo profound changes to their identities due to both physical and mental conditioning specific to military service. After service, there exists yet another change in identity in the transition back to civilian life. If a Black Male veteran decides to attend college, he is further in an overwhelming combination of these factors which are often not understood or recognized. Therefore, it is readily apparent why this group is still so underrepresented in higher education. This chapter will focus on explaining these intersecting factors within Black male veteran college students to educate and assist university stakeholders such as administrators, faculty and student affairs on how to support their existing students, as well as more effectively recruit and retain this important population.</jats:p>

title: Culture Creators: The Impact of Student-Athlete Status on National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division III College Men
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
3ae212c2722b3a3e10f1f0ad7cafc0eb426c35ea.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Patriarchal systems of power, privilege, and oppression are reinforced by college men every day, but there are certain populations of college men who often have a stronger ability to influence change. Student-athlete men at National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division III institutions are often viewed as “culture creators” on their campuses. Moreover, many of these athletic programs reside at smaller institutions, where the impact of toxic masculinity has potential to be more concentrated. Student-athlete men are often seen as representing hegemonic forms of masculinity, thereby having influence in setting norms of what is expected of men on campus. This chapter explores how participating in athletics and becoming a member of an NCAA Division III collegiate athletic team shapes the construction and perception of masculinity within college student-athlete men. Findings from a recent study will discuss how participants learned masculinity, felt added pressures as student-athletes, and viewed being a man in today’s society. Supporting examples and anecdotes will be provided from years of professional experience working alongside college athlete teams. Recommendations from this chapter include interventions to support student-athlete men in creating a healthy construction of their gender identity.</jats:p>

title: The Tea About the Fraternity: A Critical Autoethnographic Exploration of Masculinity at a White Fraternity
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
6eb34ed71ed14b09820164dcb0840441e05dd7c5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this chapter, I use a critical auto-ethnographic approach to examine the construction of masculinity at a historically white fraternity. For 3 years, I lived in a house with 64 privileged, hypermasculine, and oft-thoughtful men as their House Director. There I was: a 28-year-old gay Middle Eastern Muslim living with the type of students who would have scared me as an undergraduate. Although I held a Master’s in student affairs and was on my way to earning a PhD, nothing could have prepared me for the whirlwind of the fraternity house. It is an understatement to say that my view of how to work with students was challenged to its very core. The experience transformed how I think about masculinity in myself and others. I grappled with the tension between upholding hegemonic masculinity and meeting students where they were. I struggled to express my sexuality within that environment and experienced a new coming out. Throughout my experience, I kept a personal journal where I reflected on what I was experiencing and what it meant to me. In this chapter, I peer through the journals to identify critical moments or incidents that shaped my perception of masculinity. Through self-reflexive exploration, I interrogate myself in relation to, and in the context of, the structures, systems, ideologies, assumptions, and norms underlying the white fraternity culture. My goal is to provide educators with a unique lens of what life in the fraternity was like and how we can better educate and support fraternity men.</jats:p>

title: What Does Studying Greatness Teach Us? Higher Education, Great Man Theory, and Asking Critical Questions About What Leadership Looks Like
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
75cdeaf2e200db859dd2a8743aaf5d91080dc081.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter examines leadership theory, specifically the Great Man Theory, and its persistence in the dynamics of higher education, through the lens of critical masculinity research, critical leadership scholarship, and the process of critical question asking. This chapter seeks to illustrate how leadership theory, as positioned within higher education administration, and the ways leadership learning operates within colleges and universities reinforce a masculinity-focused approach to leadership. Pursuing this aim can further illuminate barriers to more liberatory leadership practices. The chapter will pose questions to the reader as a process of examining and interrogating their understanding of leadership and the persistence of the Great Man Theory in their practices. These questions will bring into focus new possibilities for practice, for aligning forms of leadership learning and development with the stated philosophies on leadership in higher education and with more current theories focused on impact, social change, and disrupting entrenched oppressive systems.</jats:p>

title: Navigating Masculinity and Help-Seeking Amid a Shifting Culture: Lived Experiences of College-Aged Men
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
d315b7383b7038e9bf34563e742b0a7307c98997.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Despite numerous studies suggesting that psychological treatments are equally efficacious for men and women, many men continue to exhibit reluctance toward seeking treatment for their psychological concerns. Numerous explanations have been offered in attempts to understand why this phenomenon occurs. Recent findings suggest that some men have difficulties engaging with specific elements of psychological treatment (Johnson et al., 2012), such as opening up and engaging in a trusting and therapeutic relationship with a stranger. Men’s discomfort regarding psychological services manifests in feelings of uncertainty and hesitation toward treatment (Good & Robertson, 2010). This significant gender disparity in mental health services utilization persists despite mental illness severity. There is a plethora of quantitative studies regarding men’s help-seeking behaviors, however, qualitative investigations into this phenomenon remain scarce. Using a qualitative phenomenological case study, Assadi et al. (2021) examined the attitudes, perceptions, and lived experiences of 12 male college students to uncover barriers and facilitators to mental health service utilization. Findings highlighted the role of gender socialization in shaping emotional expression, the stigma associated with vulnerability, and strategies men use—such as avoidance, compartmentalization, and masking—to protect their masculine identity. While the findings highlight the persistence of traditional gender norms, they also reveal a shifting landscape, with younger generations expressing a growing openness toward emotional well-being and mental health support. The study underscores the importance of aligning interventions with male values, reframing help-seeking as an act of strength rather than weakness.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Heroes and Villains: Moving White Men Past Playing Characters in Social Justice Education
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
2c34b20e7c42018624b22a4aa5517c1756a5e491.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The authors use the popular film The Dark Knight (2008) and the character Harvey Dent/Two-Face as a lens for examining attitudes of undergraduate White men. We contend that Harvey Dent/Two Face’s binary mindset of heroes and villains reflects a growing sentiment of undergraduate White men. When undergraduate White men are exposed to stories of Black, Indigenous, and People of Color, they must contend with stories where they are not main characters. These men then place themselves in relationship to those stories in which they situate themselves as simultaneous heroes and villains. We deconstruct the ways that undergraduate White men do this by drawing on different theories of masculinity and concepts surrounding whiteness. We present praxis for educators to challenge undergraduate White men to extend beyond this binary of hero and villain through authentic introspective reflection.</jats:p>

title: Engaging College Men on the Social Justice Continuum: Frameworks, Strategies and Implications for Practice
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
23ce35405a6878c849d8fb8dd96078f773e0770c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter explores strategies and frameworks for engaging college men in social justice education efforts. It emphasizes the importance of grounding those efforts in democratic, participatory processes that affirm human agency and collaborative change. The concept of hegemony is examined to understand the challenges of achieving socially just change, particularly in relation to gender oppression and hegemonic masculinity. The chapter discusses common strategies for engaging college men in social justice education, including academic curriculum, clubs and organizations, dialog programs, living learning communities, men’s retreats, mentoring programs, peer education, and student conduct. It also introduces theoretical frameworks, including Robert Kegan’s learning positions and gender-aware restorative practices, to guide effective educational strategies. The goal is to foster critical awareness, disrupt oppressive patterns, and promote collective liberation through intentional and inclusive educational practices.</jats:p>

title: BRO-CIAL Justice? The Dynamics of Masculinities Work Within Women’s Centers
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
64ce31c77d2a3ffedbd5a6bd509abcbf8e065c5b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This work explores the evolving landscape of masculinities and men’s engagement programming within Women’s Centers. While Women’s Centers throughout history have primarily supported women and feminist activism, in recent years there has been a growing push to expand gender-inclusive programming. This shift is evident in the adoption of titles like “Gender Equity Center” and programs focusing on “healthy” masculinity—particularly as calls for anti-DEI measures permeate American policy. This is also illustrated by the rise in violence prevention grants calling for men’s engagement, many of which provide Women’s Centers with much-needed funding for their work. This call for inclusion prompts the question: how do men and masculinities fit within these institutions purposefully developed to be safe havens from patriarchal power? In this work, we present a systematic review of men and masculinities theory and practice within Women’s and Gender Equity Centers (WGECs) across American college campuses. We begin with a history of men’s involvement in these centers, highlighting evolution alongside societal understandings of gender. Our analyses reveal three key sites where masculinities are explored: (1) promotion of gender-inclusive spaces, (2) conversations of intersectional privilege, and (3) positioning of men in feminist and violence prevention. We then analyze a Women’s Center at an elite midsize research university as a case study to demonstrate the effectiveness of the strategies described. Based on these findings, we conclude with recommendations for other WGECs aiming to optimize the role of masculinities work in their own spaces.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Constraint: Expanding Masculinities Through Vulnerability and Communal Healing
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
b8c9ce07066eb00ea9ab6f48d53e7aa80dd97a60.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter describes the importance of supporting the student success needs of Men of Color through a focus on masculinities. The Black Men Reflection Group is presented as a best practice that centers an exploration of masculine gender identities through dialog and vulnerability. The participants’ narratives are framed through the Loving Systems framework to offer insight into participant experiences. Recommendations for practice are offered for how institutions of higher education can utilize a communal approach centered in care, stability, commitment, and capacity.</jats:p>

title: “A man’s a man”: Examining Toxic Masculinity in Social Discourse
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
21f5485fb6b4fa3c8caf4891e27eac406ff580fc.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Toxic masculinity, once confined to academic discourse, has become a widely recognized term that is frequently invoked in social discourse (media, popular culture, television, movies, and social media). Its prevalence as a plot device or character trait, however, has often led to inaccurate, reductive, and inflammatory representations of men and masculinity. Increasingly, portrayals of toxic masculinity in social discourse risk oversaturating the narrative landscape and reducing complex masculine behaviors to interchangeable tropes. This trend not only diminishes the explanatory power of the term, but potentially promotes the false idea that all masculinity is inherently toxic, which is a perception that has sparked backlash, overdiagnosis, and skepticism. These distortions complicate efforts to utilize toxic masculinity meaningfully in educational and intervention contexts.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Despite these challenges, discussions of toxic masculinity remain critical. Harmful behaviors associated with it are persistent and pervasive, affecting both society at large and the individuals who embody toxic masculinity. The rigid expectations imposed by toxic masculinity contribute to cycles of violence, isolation, feelings of alienation, and mental health struggles among men, underscoring the urgent need for informed, nuanced discourse.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This chapter responds to these challenges by reclaiming and refining the definition of toxic masculinity, and situating it within broader social and institutional contexts. Through critical analysis of contemporary portrayals of toxic masculinity and thoughtful engagement with social discourse, this text offers strategies for educators, practitioners, and community leaders to foster healthier, more authentic masculine identities. Rooted in education, empathy, and genuine inquiry, these approaches advocate for interventions that move beyond stigma and support positive transformation.</jats:p>

title: Methods in QUEERing and TRANSforming Masculinity and Gender
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
36affef1943ccecafc0c7b885ffe1759402dcc7e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Fostering community and obtaining basic needs are integral to student development and progression in higher education. When these basic necessities are paired with initiatives that question the traditional notions around masculinity, there may be increased persistence and belonging for folk with masculine identities. In pursuing these pathways to success, the authors explore methods of QUEERing and TRANSforming masculinities and how inclusive spaces can encourage positive identity development and belonging. Through challenging the socialization, harmful norms, and white supremacy surrounding masculinity, the described methods seek to center decolonial ideologies that humans experience and express gender and sexuality on a spectrum, not a binary. By treating masculinity as a practice versus a static expression, the proposed curriculum and programming are discussed through application to Men of Color programs and initiatives. In addition, the authors will discuss the implications of integrating developmental approaches that engage the intersections of gender, race, and sexual orientation for people seeking to reevaluate their relationships to masculinity.</jats:p>

title: Moonlight: A Loving Theoretical Representation of Leadership for Black Men
container-title: Critical Praxis of College Men and Masculinities
ef12eeb5fbdaf4b9fd44696665f2d8511a2c3137.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter explores the potential for Black men to challenge and reimagine traditional notions of masculinity by embracing a “love ethic” as depicted in the critically acclaimed film Moonlight. Through a critical analysis of the film’s nuanced portrayal of Black male relationships, intimacy, and vulnerability, this study examines how Moonlight offers a compelling framework for Black men to develop new ways of performing masculinity that prioritize emotional connection, empathy, and self-love. Drawing upon theoretical concepts from Black feminist thought, queer theory, and critical race studies, this chapter investigates the ways in which Moonlight’s central characters navigate complex emotional landscapes and forge intimate connections that defy stereotypical representations of Black masculinity. By analyzing the film’s depiction of love as a transformative force, this study argues that embracing a love ethic can empower Black men to challenge internalized homophobia, confront toxic masculinity, and cultivate healthier relationships with themselves and others. Ultimately, this chapter aims to contribute to ongoing scholarly discussions about the intersections of race, gender, sexuality, and media representation. By theorizing the potential for Black men to utilize a love ethic as a tool for personal and social transformation, this study seeks to offer new insights into the complex and multifaceted nature of Black masculinity in the 21st century.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive correlates of diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space index in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: a preliminary study
container-title: Archives of Clinical Neuropsychology
1e1bf996cda945b0527e40176b2aa62fdc1d4c7d.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index is an imaging-derived metric related to perivascular water diffusion and has been reported to correlate with global cognitive performance in dementia. However, its associations with specific cognitive functions in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) remain underexplored. This study aimed to characterize the cognitive correlates of the DTI-ALPS index in individuals with amnestic MCI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this cross-sectional study, 57 participants with amnestic MCI underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging and a neuropsychological assessment battery. Correlations between the DTI-ALPS index and performance across the assessed cognitive measures were examined before and after adjustment for age, sex, education, and Fazekas score.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Prior to adjustment, the DTI-ALPS index showed significant positive correlations with global cognitive measures, episodic memory retrieval, and semantic verbal fluency. After controlling for potential confounders, only the correlations with episodic memory and semantic verbal fluency remained significant.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The DTI-ALPS index remained significantly associated with episodic memory retrieval and semantic verbal fluency in amnestic MCI after adjustment, suggesting a possible link with frontotemporal network-related cognitive functions. Further studies incorporating multimodal imaging and disease-specific biomarkers are warranted to clarify the biological significance of the DTI-ALPS index and its potential clinical relevance in early cognitive impairment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Playology
516b87233a939c6cf8ec30574d0b1518aad42230.abstract:
<jats:p>Playology: A Media-Critical Exploration of Digital Technologies and Identity in the Global Village offers a sharp, timely exploration of how digital technologies and global media reshape the ways we think, communicate, and understand ourselves. As multinational corporations like Google increasingly mediate our access to information, identity, and civic life, this book examines the profound consequences of living in what it calls the “Googleburg Galaxy.”</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Blending cultural critique with accessible theory, the book traces how our practices of reading, writing, and meaning making have been transformed by digital systems that both empower and constrain. It argues that play—reimagined as a form of critical media literacy—is essential for navigating these complexities. Through play, individuals can question dominant narratives, expose hidden power structures, and reclaim agency over their digital lives.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>By unpacking the ideologies embedded in contemporary media and the subtle ways they shape citizenship, knowledge, and authenticity, Playology: A Media-Critical Exploration of Digital Technologies and Identity in the Global Village invites readers to engage more consciously with the technologies that define modern existence. It is a call to resist passive consumption, embrace creative inquiry, and cultivate the critical literacies necessary for a more open, pluralistic, and humane digital future.</jats:p>

title: Between Artifice and Enlightenment: Queer Critique, Insecurity, and the AI Large Language Model
container-title: Insecurity and the Eclipse of Enlightenment
eb93d5dc2a9e17c6e89c89b29ec656faaa8e39e1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Over several decades, machine learning systems—often described with the double metaphor “artificial intelligence”—have become indispensable computational tools in the flow and mediation of economic and social capital. These systems can, on the surface, appear to deepen the dialectic of enlightenment identified by Horkheimer and Adorno by enabling ever greater domination over natural systems and human agency. They therefore generate widespread concern that computational advances endanger the security and autonomy of human subjects, especially in the sphere of production and exchange. Contemporary social theory offers conceptual tools that go beyond received categories of domination and autonomy, however, to provide a reanalysis of machine learning systems and their implication in social dynamics and economic relations. This chapter focuses on the ways large language model (LLM) systems demonstrate complex affinities with theories of mimesis and simulacrum, and therefore how such systems and require a rethinking of performativity and artifice. Recent queer critique—in which reflection on computational systems and simulacra is proliferating—and contemporary social theory, when read together, thus reveal how rhetoric about LLMs demonstrates slippages between agency, performance, reproduction, representation, and meaning that must be unpacked historically and conceptually before metaphors of the “artificial” and “intelligence” can carry analytical weight in addressing today’s socioeconomic relations. Ultimately, this theoretical-conceptual reading highlights the stakes of the problem of truth in systems where artifice manifests both socially and computationally.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive-affective functions, neighborhood opportunity, and social functioning in youth with neurofibromatosis type 1
container-title: Journal of Pediatric Psychology
2cb14b067c0eae9b7de70db16716ce2cc29c074b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study evaluated associations between social functioning and cognitive-affective functions (CAF), including executive function, face processing, and theory of mind, and neighborhood opportunity, in youth with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Youth with NF1 (n = 37), ages 8–14 (M = 11.8 years), with no prior autism diagnosis, completed assessments of CAF and peer relationships. Parents completed questionnaires on executive function skills, social impairments, and peer relationships. The Childhood Opportunity Index national composite score quantified neighborhood opportunity. Correlation and hierarchical linear regression analyses evaluated associations between social functioning, CAF, and neighborhood opportunity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Executive functioning and neighborhood opportunity were significantly associated with parent reports of social impairments and peer relationships. Executive functioning and facial expression recognition were correlated with self-reported peer relationships, but were not significant in regression models. Facial identity recognition was significantly correlated with social impairments and parent-rated peer relationships. Theory of mind was not associated with any outcome.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Findings underscore the interplay between CAF, neighborhood opportunity, and social functioning in children with NF1. Case conceptualizations should integrate social determinants of health with measures of cognition and behavior. Longitudinal research is needed to understand mechanisms driving variability in social outcomes and inform equitable care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Enhancing Virtual Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
29e1f9bbee2e7b9ef6f5798250cde760a1254465.abstract: <jats:p>Applications of artificial intelligence (AI) are shaping new ways of teaching, including the creation of virtual teachers who can automate the teaching process. AI can combine text-to-image, text-to-speech, lip sync and gesture animation for the creation of virtual avatars who can present and teach. However, despite advancements in technology, there are still issues with the realism of avatars and the ability to synchronize all of these processes in real-time. This chapter discusses the main artificial intelligence technologies that have been used to build automated virtual instructors, including advancements, challenges, and applications. In addition, the author discusses the educational value of these technologies and the need for better algorithms and system designs to foster the reliable, safe, and effective use of artificial intelligence in virtual education.</jats:p>

title: Reassessing Faith and Facts in AI-Augmented Modern Higher Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
7acbc3cc08e83ccb86f74983a4af53870891720e.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into modern higher education has produced a dual impact: while AI has opened new opportunities for innovation in teaching, learning, and research, it has also introduced significant challenges for academic practice. This paper explores how AI reshapes epistemic boundaries by challenging traditional notions and examines how confidence in institutional traditions and technological promise intersects with empirical data and algorithmic reasoning, and the ethical implications for transparent decision-making frameworks. By combining theoretical perspectives with practical examples, this paper highlights how AI is redefining epistemological foundations by the need to strengthen the relationship between faith and facts. The paper argues for a human-centred approach that promotes adaptive learning cultures. It concludes by proposing a forward-looking framework to help modern universities remain grounded in an AI-intensive future.</jats:p>

title: Teaching for Truth and Pluralism
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
8b018e18f17505ad800683cc03f7e7e7a81d7f54.abstract: <jats:p>In the past, higher education has been seen as a citadel of truth, critical thinking, and intellectual integrity. Nonetheless, in modern society, the identity of institutions of higher learning and their quest for truth has been questioned by the increase in tension levels. Due to polarization in politics and academic ideology, a market model in higher institutions of learning, and the ever-growing phenomenon of misinformation, it has become increasingly difficult to distinguish truth from opinion and ideology. There is increasing pressure on higher learning institutions to comply with numerous external demands by governments, corporate institutions, social movements, and so forth, which may affect the research and teaching agendas in a higher learning institution. On the other hand, students have to deal with numerous narrative constructs on online platforms, and it is becoming harder to explain the difference between scholarly writing and appealing but unsupported assertions.</jats:p>

title: Preparing Critical and Culturally Sustaining Decision-Makers in Today's Educational Landscape
container-title: Preparing Pre-Service Educators for Diverse Learners and Communities
610cb6c359599f55cfe882c5c6a785dce2376ff7.abstract: <jats:p>Preparing educators to teach in increasingly diverse classrooms while navigating a politically constrained educational landscape requires more knowledge of culturally responsive teaching and culturally sustaining pedagogy. It demands the intentional development of both critical reflection and critical thinking as complementary competencies for ethical and equitable decision-making. This chapter presents a conceptual framework illustrating how two undergraduate courses, EDUC 310: Teaching in a Diverse Society and EDUC 102: Critical Questions in Education cultivate these capacities through distinct yet interconnected pedagogical approaches. Drawing on classroom activities and assignments from both courses, the chapter demonstrates how structured reflection, collaborative inquiry, and evidence-based analysis prepare future educators to make culturally responsive and culturally sustaining decisions while navigating the complexities of today's educational and political contexts.</jats:p>

title: Regulation of the Use of AI in the Health Sector From a Human Rights Perspective
container-title: Innovation, Governance, and Resilience in Global Health Systems
1a2713af22e11b09e9095d4390eda378d5709e78.abstract: <jats:p>The discussion for the use and regulation of Artificial Intelligence in the healthcare sector from a human rights perspective is much needed due to its intrinsic ethical, social, legal and non-jurisdictional implications. The fourth generation human rights core discourse is focused on the technological advancements, its impact on human lives. Though the fourth-generation human rights are not yet enlisted and explicitly codified through domestic or international legislative body, nevertheless; this is one of the socio-legal discourse after invention of AI. The European Commission has criticized AI systems for not adequately addressing patients' rights health-related risks such as discrimination, privacy concerns, and opaque decision-making processes, etc.</jats:p>

5868f68ca821a8a3140ef8efb963d5a2d6a15df1.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents a comparative assessment of valuable agronomic traits in F₄ cotton hybrids studied in a first-year breeding nursery. The growing period, seed cotton weight per boll, plant productivity, fiber length, and fiber yield were evaluated in comparison with the Andijan-36 standard cultivar. The Bukhara-6 × 010888 combination achieved a plant productivity of 81.5 g and a fiber yield of 40.4%. The S-6524 × 011592 combination had the shortest growing period (114 days) and the greatest fiber length (34.5 mm). The Sulton × 011482 combination showed a plant productivity of 80.0 g and a fiber yield of 39.9%. These results identify the above combinations as valuable breeding materials for further evaluation based on a combination of economically important traits.</jats:p>

d55b438ea047efc4c7a110358eb03ad05e23e863.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents data on the impact of herbicide application against weeds simultaneously with sowing and during the 3–4 true leaf stages of cotton on the duration of the plant growing season. As a result of applying herbicides along with sowing and at the 3–4 true leaf stage of the plant, an extension of the cotton growing season by 1–4 days was observed.</jats:p>

5a53e05c64aff82600f4f8558413e6672eedd469.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents data on the yield of cotton varieties from research conducted at the experimental fields of the Syrdarya scientific-experimental station. The study involved the regionalized “Guliston” variety and the promising "S-5727" variety, which were irrigated one to two times. Irrigation was applied at soil moisture levels of 70-70-60% and 75-75-60% relative to field capacity, with plant densities maintained at 100, 150, and 200 thousand plants per hectare. Taking the boll opening rate into account, it was determined that the cotton yield across the experimental variants averaged between 41.1 and 49.1 centners per hectare.</jats:p>

3177fc183de9d9c0e409c1cddc46647aa5b359a0.abstract: <jats:p>The study investigated the phenological development and duration of the growing season of 11 perennial wheat collection samples. The growing season, calculated from emergence to full maturity, ranged from 225 to 232 days. Among the perennial samples, the earliest-maturing WHEAT-AGROPYRON INTERMEDIUM PARTIAL AMPHIPLOID6 had a growing season of 225 days, while the latest-maturing MADSEN//CHINESE SPRING/PI531718 had 232 days. These differences indicate phenological diversity in the development of perennial wheat genotypes.</jats:p>

69d9be549364767eb4cd15be7d3c8e10711b9280.abstract: <jats:p>The paper analyzes grate constructions used in cotton cleaners for removing large impurities. The aim is to systematize the advantages and limitations of stationary round, triangular and trapezoidal grate bars and to analyze the influence of grate design parameters on the cleaning process. The source material reports triangular grate dimensions of 19, 25 and 12 mm, a 1570 mm placement radius relative to the saw drum and a 40 mm spacing as an effective configuration. For the CHX-3 cleaner, trapezoidal grate bars with dimensions of 25, 16, 12 and 10 mm are reported, while a low efficiency is noted for the 12 mm working edge configuration in CHX-ZM. A grate with different grate-bar diameters and solutions aimed at increasing the degrees of freedom of grate bars are also considered. Since the source material does not contain sufficient quantitative results of a new experiment, numerical efficiency values were not fabricated; the analysis is based on the parameters and conclusions available in the source material.</jats:p>

842147f8478a8792c0ff57ceb94f797caa0f8bcd.abstract: <jats:p>The article investigates the effect of different rates of mineral fertilizers and the Moddus retardant on the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat varieties Krasnodarskaya-99 and Chillaki. The results showed that the application of mineral fertilizers in combination with the retardant had a positive effect on leaf area formation and the photosynthetic potential of plants. The highest values of photosynthetic activity were recorded when mineral fertilizers were applied at a rate of N210P105K70 in combination with Moddus at a rate of 0.4 L/ha. Among the studied varieties, Chillaki demonstrated higher leaf area and photosynthetic potential compared with Krasnodarskaya-99. The obtained results indicate that an optimal combination of mineral nutrition and Moddus retardant application can contribute to improving the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat plants.</jats:p>

title: Unsupervised detection of overshooting defects using hybrid generative and boundary classification models
container-title: Journal of Logic and Computation
b19d81e4c7fded96c96974ee9938770ef3f357d8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Quality control in modern manufacturing increasingly relies on unsupervised anomaly detection to identify structural defects when abnormal samples are critically scarce. This study presents an evaluation of hybrid generative architectures designed to detect complex overshooting anomalies in industrial simple sub-assemblies base plates. We analysed eight distinct model combinations by pairing four advanced generative backbones, including a latent space resampling autoencoder and a denoising diffusion model, with two boundary classification strategies: the one class support vector machine and the deep support vector data description. The experimental results demonstrate that the configuration pairing the latent space resampling autoencoder with the one class support vector machine achieves superior detection capabilities, securing the highest mean area under the curve of 0.7870 alongside absolute statistical dominance. However, our findings reveal a critical architectural vulnerability, as pairing heavily regularized generative latent spaces with the rigid hyperspherical boundaries of the deep data description model invariably degrades detection, driving in the most strongly regularized configuration a systematic inversion of the anomaly score rather than a loss of discriminative power. Ultimately, this research establishes that flexible margin optimization is required to preserve anomaly detection accuracy in complex industrial topologies, providing a framework for deploying reliable automated quality assurance systems.</jats:p>

36d6b77407653d455c80e2f500634a6232d7a5a9.abstract: <jats:p>The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning for Adaptive Management of Renewable Hybrid Power Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
8dbc26d9167ed7772f47b06f9aa8d0293cf7c8ac.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the problem of adaptive control for hybrid renewable energy systems combining photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and battery storage under conditions of generation uncertainty and price volatility. A control strategy based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, which does not require an explicit mathematical model and accounts for long-term consequences, including battery degradation. The control task is formalized as a markov decision process with an integral discounted reward combining economic costs, penalties for energy curtailment, and storage aging losses. Computational experiments on real meteorological data demonstrate that the trained regulator reduces operating costs by 12–15% compared to heuristic strategies, increases the share of renewable energy used by 18–22%, and extends estimated battery life by 15–20%. The results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach over classical methods, particularly under high uncertainty. Limitations and prospects for practical implementation are discussed.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Energy Systems

Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
5f910b7c7ff3cc7a08791e8c37c348d51a9d359d.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Assisted Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Microgrids for Sustainable Rural Electrification

96ab7ef154dc58376a40cf75f589dc662f80d0d9.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter reviews conventional optimization methods and AI-assisted approaches for hybrid renewable energy microgrids, highlighting their roles in system planning, sizing, operation, and control. It also explores emerging technologies, including reinforcement learning, explainable AI, digital twins, and edge AI, that are shaping the next generation of intelligent energy systems. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, the chapter presents a case study of a hybrid renewable energy microgrid in Muanda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, featuring solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, and blue-carbon bioenergy resources. The case study shows how optimization techniques can enhance techno-economic and environmental performance and discusses the potential of AI-based forecasting, intelligent battery management, and reinforcement learning to further improve system reliability, renewable energy utilization, and long-term sustainability.</jats:p>

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities

ff36013178296736d6e2747d2c7e1830b32bd841.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Optimization of Solar Thermal Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
0860e093417810bedf80a8a8c80f3dec419bac99.abstract: <jats:p>Solar thermal systems encounter distinct operational challenges, which hinder their applicability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to solve them. The AI is more flexible and adaptable than traditional methods, which cannot deal with unpredictable factors, including changing weather and fluctuating energy demands. In this chapter, we introduced the solar thermal systems, and then the fundamentals of AI techniques used in solar thermal systems were provided. Subsequently, the application of AI in solar thermal systems was discussed. The advantages of the optimization process of the solar thermal systems were identified, supported by case studies from the real world. Then we identified the limitations and constraints that hinder the integration of AI into the solar thermal system. Finally, the economic benefits of using AI for the optimization of solar thermal systems were explained.</jats:p>

81ed3d5ef17a5775f35361935d09bc66b4b5cc4e.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyses the strategic incorporation of artificial intelligence technology into renewable energy systems to enhance energy security, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability. This chapter aims to examine how intelligent energy management systems, machine learning algorithms, smart grids, decentralized microgrids, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks can enhance the performance and resilience of renewable energy systems. This chapter places emphasis on predictive analytics, battery management, solar forecasting, digital twins, and autonomous energy optimization. The chapter examines the economic, environmental, and technological ramifications of intelligent energy systems, emphasizing their capacity to minimize energy losses, improve system reliability, facilitate decentralized electrification, and expedite sustainable energy transitions towards enhanced national energy independence.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning for Solar Thermal Energy Optimization and Smart Control

fb44f8ecb89dccb4a11eab978ce879fb41e44f26.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.</jats:p>

title: Energy Audits in Tanzanian Industrial SMEs for Methods, Barriers, and M&V-Linked Savings Prioritization

b85063b2e64cb2adf03e3a6fd9c4b42f3f347e50.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.</jats:p>

title: Biogas Production Optimisation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
3a1fabea3f97fb97115f71a9b24c656748b30ad4.abstract: <jats:p>Anaerobic co-digestion is an effective approach for biogas production, but optimizing operating parameters remains challenging due to the interaction of multiple variables. This study integrates ultrasonic pretreatment with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to enhance biogas yield from a mixture of dormitory food waste and pet animal dung. Batch digesters were operated at 37 °C, and daily biogas production was monitored. RSM evaluated the combined effects of ultrasonic temperature (25–65 °C), power (500–1,500 W), and treatment time (35–75 min). Biogas yield ranged from 35% to nearly 68%, with optimum conditions of 53.35 °C, 1,490.83 W, and 57.15 min, producing a predicted yield of 66.47%. The quadratic model showed excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9707; F = 110.33), confirming the importance of simultaneous optimization. The integrated ultrasonic–RSM approach provides a reliable and efficient strategy for maximizing biogas production in anaerobic co-digestion systems.</jats:p>

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
638e43b89445c1c4efd078d51246af0e90e11d12.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.</jats:p>

title: Forecasting Electrical Load and Renewable Energy Generation Using Machine Learning Methods
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ea63ae340e55dcd23a21c92099270e55640a1e65.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The purpose is to show why power systems need models handling nonlinear, non-stationary, and heterogeneous data. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
db14ec7802b2943f0f932ee90ef99812da7cac80.abstract: <jats:p>Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.</jats:p>

title: Integrasi AI dalam Kurikulum Akuntansi Pendidikan Pesantren: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis tentang Kesiapan Teknologi, Pemahaman AI, dan Karakteristik Siswa
container-title: Business and Accounting Education Journal
e0f60edd89c8c829c91e27e2720ae59dca61591c.abstract: <jats:p>Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong transformasi pendidikan akuntansi dan menuntut penyesuaian kurikulum agar sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia kerja digital. Namun, adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi masih dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor, khususnya pada konteks pendidikan pesantren yang memiliki karakteristik unik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kesiapan teknologi, pemahaman AI, dan karakteristik siswa terhadap adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi serta mengidentifikasi faktor yang paling dominan. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Data diperoleh dari 38 artikel ilmiah terindeks Scopus yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2015-2026 dan dianalisis menggunakan sintesis tematik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kesiapan teknologi merupakan faktor yang paling dominan dalam mendorong adopsi AI, diikuti oleh pemahaman AI dan karakteristik siswa. Ketiga faktor tersebut saling melengkapi dalam meningkatkan penerimaan dan pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran akuntansi. Temuan ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan model adopsi teknologi pendidikan serta menjadi dasar pengembangan kurikulum akuntansi berbasis AI di lingkungan pesantren.</jats:p>

title: Reduced desaturation-based detection of sleep apnea events in self-identified Black individuals across two cohorts
container-title: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
5d19a5a40652b4bb7e86172e38b930e89eef65f2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Rationale</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Pulse oximetry may overestimate oxygen saturation in individuals with darker skin pigmentation, potentially reducing detection of desaturation during sleep-disordered breathing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To assess racial/ethnic differences in desaturation-based obstructive event detection and cardiovascular risk, and evaluate heart-rate response as an oximetry-independent marker for risk stratification.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We analyzed participants without cardiovascular disease in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis(MESA) and Sleep Heart Health Study(SHHS). We modeled desaturation-based AHI relative to airflow-defined AHI and examined AHI-ΔHR6, defined by respiratory events with a heart-rate increase ≥6 beats/min. Adjusted Cox models evaluated associations with a composite outcome, major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality(MACE/mortality).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Measurements and Main Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Black participants had 21% and 20% lower proportions of airflow-defined events meeting the ≥4% desaturation criterion than White participants in MESA (ratio 0.79[95% CI,0.68–0.93]; p = 0.003) and SHHS (0.80[0.68–0.94]; p = 0.008), respectively. No other racial/ethnic group showed a lower proportion of airflow-defined events meeting desaturation criteria than White participants. AHI-ΔHR6 event detection was similar between Black and White participants in both cohorts. In Whites participants, desaturation-based events were associated with MACE/mortality in MESA but not in SHHS, while desaturation-based AHI measures were not significantly associated with MACE/mortality in Black individuals in either cohort. In contrast, AHI-ΔHR6 was associated with MACE/mortality in MESA (HR 1.33[1.09–1.63];p=0.006) and SHHS (1.26[1.02–1.55]; p = 0.033).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Desaturation-based scoring identified a lower proportion of reduced flow events in Black than White participants, whereas heart-rate-response-based event detection was similar across groups, suggesting oximetry-related under-detection in individuals with darker pigment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

a1fc8d526224f83eedb1e34addc24c0a8e924a52.abstract: <jats:p>The study investigated the inheritance of important morphological traits, including plant height and the number of lateral branches, in simple and backcross F₁ sesame hybrids involving the local varieties “Onimdar”, “Qora Shahzoda”, “Tashkent-122”, and “Sadaf”. The experiments were conducted under field and laboratory conditions. The patterns of trait formation and the degree of heterosis in the hybrids were analyzed. The number of lateral branches ranged from 5.8 to 6.2 per plant in the local varieties, from 5.7 to 8.7 in simple F₁ hybrids, and from 5.6 to 9.2 in backcross hybrids. Positive heterosis for the number of lateral branches was observed in most of the simple hybrids. Positive inheritance of this trait was also recorded in several backcross combinations. Promising hybrid combinations with high values of plant height and the number of lateral branches were identified. The results indicate that the selected hybrid combinations can be used in sesame breeding to develop valuable initial breeding material with high productivity, stability, and adaptability to local environmental conditions.</jats:p>

title: SUG‘ORILADIGAN YERLAR UCHUN ARPA SELEKSIYASIDA OLIB BORILAYOTGAN TADQIQOTLAR
container-title: Agro ilm
11f8545db76c4de11946113dd99d4f0d407be82d.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of research aimed at identifying valuable initial breeding material for barley breeding on irrigated lands. The studies were conducted in 2023–2026 at the experimental field of the “Farboma selekt” scientific seed-growing farm located in Jomboy district of Samarkand region. A total of 200 barley collection accessions obtained from the international centers ICARDA and CIMMYT, as well as the Institute of Plant Science and the Gallaorol Research and Experimental Station of the Research Institute of Grain and Legume Crops, were studied. The accessions were evaluated for productive tillering, number and weight of grains per spike, 1000-grain weight, yield, earliness, and resistance to diseases, winter conditions and lodging. The study identified valuable barley accessions with high productivity and yield potential. In particular, the Mirzacho‘l, K-22845, K-19985, Temur and K-566244 accessions demonstrated high yield performance. The selected accessions are recommended as valuable initial breeding material for developing new high-yielding, early-maturing and environmentally stress-resistant barley varieties for irrigated lands.</jats:p>

082f36c736e87ce9716851e175549fbf531e9f4b.abstract: The article studies the formation of plant density in chickpea varieties under different irrigation methods and irrigation regimes. The study examined the effects of furrow, drip and sprinkler irrigation, as well as irrigation regimes of 65–70–60%, 70–75–65% and 75–80–70% of field capacity. The results showed that plant density of the Zumrad and Malhotra chickpea varieties varied depending on the irrigation method and soil moisture regime. The highest plant density was recorded under drip irrigation with an irrigation regime of 75–80–70% of field capacity in the Malhotra variety, reaching 282.7 plants/m² at the beginning of the growing period and 275.3 plants/m² at the end. The obtained results demonstrate the importance of selecting an appropriate irrigation method and soil moisture regime for chickpea cultivation.

bf58ced470965b72c39377456736f27ab9f989d9.abstract: High-density orchards require low-vigor saplings. c6659807d302d2c849da551868e62cba0e4f44d7.abstract: This study investigates the effects of dual feedback delays on the stability and vibration characteristics of an electromagnetic suspension (EMS) maglev system. title: Advancing ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a question of optimizing quality, ventilation parameters or both?
container-title: Current Opinion in Critical Care
75c03dd01eeb1c5d70c308b194293340def14a98.abstract: Purpose of review Ventilation is provided to most patients during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). International guidelines emphasize the need for effective intra-arrest ventilation while acknowledging uncertainty regarding the optimal ventilation parameters. This review will discuss how new studies challenge prior beliefs on key ventilation parameters, will highlight challenges and potential solutions for high-quality ventilation and will suggest a translational research approach to advance intra-arrest ventilation. Recent findings A recent observational study reported that higher ventilation rates during in-hospital cardiac arrest may be positively associated with return of spontaneous circulation, challenging common beliefs. Additionally, a pivotal observational study on bag-valve-mask ventilation during out-of-hospital cardiac arrest found that ventilation was frequently ineffective and if so, associated with reduced survival and neurological function. Scoping and systematic reviews on intra-arrest ventilation parameters, ventilation feedback devices and mechanical ventilation have uncovered uncertainties regarding fundamental aspects of intra-arrest ventilation. Summary This review contextualizes the scientific debate on how to optimize intra-arrest ventilation by healthcare professionals. It covers emerging evidence on bag-valve-mask ventilation quality along with controversies around the optimal intra-arrest ventilation parameters, ventilation feedback devices and mechanical ventilation during CPR. Finally, implications for clinical practice are provided, and a translational approach is proposed to advance intra-arrest ventilation.

title: Targeting pH during cardiac arrest and in the postresuscitation period
container-title: Current Opinion in Critical Care
78934592254e178af526ff68835189a0dda84444.abstract: Purpose of review Cardiac arrest carries high mortality and morbidity, driven in part by a profound mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis arising from hypoperfusion during cardiopulmonary resuscitation and ischemia-reperfusion injury after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Severe acidosis impairs cardiovascular function, oxygen delivery, CO 2 transport, and cellular metabolism, potentially worsening outcomes. This review examines the physiological rationale and current evidence for pH-targeted therapies in cardiac arrest. Recent findings Sodium bicarbonate remains the most studied buffer, but randomized trials and observational studies have largely failed to demonstrate improved survival or neurological outcomes. Its efficacy depends critically on adequate ventilation to eliminate generated CO 2 , a frequently overlooked variable. Sodium lactate has emerged as a promising alternative, offering buffering capacity alongside utility as an oxidizable energy substrate, with encouraging experimental data, though clinical evidence remains preliminary. Key gaps persist regarding optimal timing, dosing, and the interaction between buffer administration and ventilatory strategy. Summary Despite limited support for routine bicarbonate use, pH-targeted interventions retain strong physiological plausibility, and remains a promising field for future research.

26d0ef343aac362405b48e632216932c207e646b.abstract: Abstract Grounded in dynamic systems theory, which conceptualizes parent–child interactions as evolving systems of reciprocal influence over time, the main objective of this study was to examine which patterns of parent–child scaffolding in a problem-solving situation were associated with children's early cognitive development and to explore whether these patterns were influenced by prior child characteristics. A total of 193 mother–child dyads (109 girls) were observed during a number–image association task at 48 months. Children were predominantly White (95%) and of Canadian or European ethnic background. Three scaffolding phases were examined using the State Space Grid (SSG): modeling (problem-solving strategies are demonstrated by parents), guidance (characterized by shared participation in task execution), and fading (support is gradually withdrawn and greater initiative is shown by children). Only the fading phase was found to be associated with higher complex executive functioning (β = 0.30) and number knowledge (β = 0.42) 1 year later, at 60 months, controlling for prior child cognitive abilities. Furthermore, higher socioeconomic status, receptive vocabulary, and cognitive flexibility at 42 months were positively associated with fading. These findings highlight the importance of interactional processes that promote children's active participation in problem- solving for subsequent cognitive development.

title: Future cognition in autism: Why episodic future thinking deserves a closer look
container-title: Child Development Perspectives
78eef3a0951038fab962c8b484bb2eaebc21510c.abstract: Abstract Autistic individuals face future-oriented challenges, including managing uncertainty, navigating transitions, and coping with routine disruptions. These difficulties point to underlying differences in how future events are mentally constructed, yet the mechanisms supporting such simulation are underexplored. In this article, we argue that episodic future thinking (EFT)—the capacity to project oneself into the future to preexperience events—provides a key mechanism for understanding these challenges and warrants closer investigation. In autism, differences across temporal specificity, content, and self-reference reflect variation in the construction of future events rather than a uniform deficit in EFT. Similar behavioral outcomes between autistic and nonautistic individuals may also mask qualitative differences in future representations. We propose that EFT should not be treated as uniformly impaired or intact. Rather, EFT provides a structured account of future-oriented difficulties and informs the development of interventions that promote autonomy and well-being.

title: From Variable Palm Residues to Certifiable Low-Carbon Concrete: A Critical Review of POFA and Biochar Processing, Microstructure, Durability, and Performance-Based Standardisation
container-title: Journal of Engineering and Applied Sciences Technology
a6bd87493a7ea384d7aa341ef4992a3abfe4e423.abstract: Palm oil fuel ash (POFA) and palm-biomass biochar have attracted interest as lower-carbon concrete constituents, yet material variability continues to impede confident engineering adoption. This critical qualitative literature review shifts attention from cement-replacement feasibility to the causal relationships among residue origin, processing, cement microstructure, exposure-dependent durability and qualification. Evidence from 2020–2025 journal research is interpreted across mineral-ash treatment, biochar pyrolysis, hydration kinetics, strength and deformation, chloride transport, carbonation, reinforcement corrosion and life-cycle performance. POFA primarily offers potentially reactive siliceous and packing functions; biochar introduces distinct porosity, moisture-management and carbon-retention functions. Neither has universally beneficial effects, and results from non-palm biochars should not be interpreted as direct validation of palm-residue formulations. The review proposes five qualification gates spanning source traceability and environmental safety, processing control, role-specific screening, exposure-based concrete verification and independently monitored pilot deployment. It also outlines an Indonesian tropical/coastal validation roadmap and recommends service-life-equivalent carbon assessment. The principal conclusion is that reproducibility, durability and transparent climate accounting—not impressive isolated strength gains—must determine whether variable palm-derived residues can become certifiable engineering constituents.

title: Bridging or Widening the Gap? AI Policies and Social Justice in Education

9e13e6e7f3a42906186f831be85e28f41f88c8fe.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as a means to improve educational quality, efficiency, and equity. However, when introduced into systems already shaped by inequality, AI risks reproducing rather than reducing social injustice. This chapter examines whether AI policies in education bridge or widen existing gaps, drawing on Nancy Fraser's framework of redistribution, recognition, and representation. Through a comparative analysis of supranational frameworks and national strategies in the United States, China, India, and Türkiye, the chapter identifies persistent tensions between innovation-driven agendas and justice-oriented goals. The findings suggest that equity is often framed in technocratic terms, while issues of power, participation, and accountability remain marginal. The chapter concludes by proposing a justice-centered policy evaluation framework that emphasizes democratic governance, cultural responsiveness, and the right to contest or refuse harmful AI systems.
