title: Cognitive Control as Precision Regulation: From Predictive Coding to Adaptive Behaviou
92b9d5d02374db314134c234f67b82d5aa039d9e.abstract: Cognitive control is traditionally conceptualized as a set of top-down mechanisms that selectand regulate stimulus–response mappings to support goal-directed and flexible behaviour.Traditional accounts have provided fundamental insights into the neural architecture ofcognitive control and identified a set of core control processes, including goal maintenance, taskswitching, control allocation, conflict monitoring, and cognitive effort. However, they rarelyaddress how these functions can be integrated within a common computational architecture.Furthermore, most theories tend to assume that the core control functions use specializedmechanisms that are fundamentally distinct from those supporting action–perception loops.Here, we review an alternative perspective grounded in predictive coding and active inference,according to which cognitive control emerges from hierarchical elaborations of the samegenerative inference supporting perception and action. Within predictive coding and activeinference, the brain continuously generates predictions about sensory inputs, actions, andtheir expected consequences, and updates these predictions on the basis of precision-weightedprediction errors. We argue that the same precision-weighting mechanism, when operatingbeyond sensory processing—to optimize the precision of higher-level beliefs and of courses ofaction (policies)—provides the foundations of cognitive control, allowing a cognitive system tobalance the stability of current goals and task representations against the flexibility requiredto respond to unexpected information and environmental changes. From this perspective, thecore control processes emerge as different facets of precision regulation within a hierarchicalgenerative model: the precision of higher-level beliefs supports goal maintenance and taskswitching; policy precision supports control allocation, setting the balance between habitualand goal-directed control and prioritizing the latter when required by task demands; conflictmonitoring provides information about whether the selected policy continues to produceexpected and preferred outcomes; and cognitive effort reflects the cost of increasing precision tochange the resulting control configuration. Finally, we link the precision-based computations toputative neural processes in frontoparietal networks and neuromodulatory processes spanningdopaminergic, noradrenergic, and cholinergic systems, and derive empirical predictions thatcan test the proposed framework.

title: Exploratory Amplicon-Based Metagenomic Profiling and Chemical Fingerprinting of Three Spontaneously Fermented Southern African Traditional Products
container-title: Foods
d97e1c6855e9baa92ccefe59d05424c39c242880.abstract: <jats:p>Traditional fermented foods are integral to African culinary heritage and nutrition, yet their microbial ecology remains underexplored in many regions. This study employed amplicon sequencing (16S rRNA and ITS) and Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy to characterize the microbial communities and biochemical profiles of spontaneously fermented cow’s milk (amasi), sorghum–maize slurry (ting-type gruel), and sour maize gruel (mahewu). Amasi displayed the highest diversity, dominated by Lactococcus and Malassezia restricta. Mahewu was dominated by Clostridium sensu stricto and Malassezia restricta. The ting-variant showed low diversity with Weissella dominance and Symbiotaphrina species. FTIR spectra corroborated these patterns, highlighting lipid/protein bands in amasi and carbohydrate/organic acid signatures in the fermented cereal products. Beta-diversity analyses confirmed strong substrate-driven separation, with limited shared taxa underscoring ecological specialization. These findings reveal how raw material composition and processing shape spontaneous fermentation outcomes, while highlighting potential safety risks from opportunistic taxa and opportunities for probiotic strain isolation from beneficial taxa. Future studies are required to determine the viability and characteristics of the microbial flora in these fermented beverages to determine if their occurrence is significant. The results in this study show that metagenomic and FT-IR spectroscopy can be used to profile traditional fermented products, but this must be coupled with in-depth metabolite analyses using quantitative instruments and machine learning technologies for predictive fingerprinting to determine the identity, safety, and functionality of these culturally significant foods.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Online Review Information Overload on Platform Churn Intention: The Serial Mediating Role of Cognitive Fatigue and Decision Postponement
container-title: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research
bb2f4aa69793427499e50425d4a16f4e10b0bd47.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how online review information overload is associated with platform churn intention through the serial mediating roles of cognitive fatigue and decision postponement. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory and Ego Depletion Theory, the study proposes that excessive volume and complexity of online reviews are associated with cognitive fatigue, which is in turn associated with decision postponement and, ultimately, with review-engaged consumers’ intention to direct future purchases away from the platform. Survey data were collected from 350 consumers of an online cosmetics shopping platform and analyzed using OLS regression and bootstrap-based serial mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 6, 5000 resamples), controlling for user interface complexity. Results show that information overload was positively associated with cognitive fatigue (beta = 0.482, p < 0.001), cognitive fatigue with decision postponement (beta = 0.534, p < 0.001), and decision postponement with platform churn intention (beta = 0.512, p < 0.001). The serial indirect effect of information overload on churn intention through cognitive fatigue and decision postponement was significant (effect = 0.132, 95% CI [0.075, 0.210]), while the direct effect was not significant (beta = 0.031, p = 0.540). Because all constructs were measured concurrently in a single cross-sectional survey, these results indicate that the data are consistent with the proposed sequence rather than that the sequence is causal or temporally ordered. These findings extend information overload research by identifying a serial indirect association between review overload and provider-level exit intention through cognitive fatigue and decision postponement, after accounting for user interface complexity. Implications for review interface design are offered as recommendations that require further validation. These estimates describe review-engaged consumers in a high-density product category and should not be generalized to platform users who do not consult the review corpus before purchase.</jats:p>

title: How Different Types of Artificial Intelligence Training Relate to Innovative Behavior Among Logistics Employees: A Cognitive–Affective Pathway Model
container-title: Systems
3626048d828e706fb3af96725f40054c01f03f1f.abstract: <jats:p>Despite substantial investments in artificial intelligence (AI) training, logistics organizations often struggle to translate these investments into measurable improvements in employee performance. Drawing on the extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Cognitive Load Theory, and Distributed Cognition Theory, this study examines how three AI-TPACK training dimensions—Strategic, Generative, and Optimization AI Training—are associated with employees’ innovative behavior through cognitive (Task–Technology Fit, AI Self-Efficacy) and affective (Perceived Technology Attractiveness, AI Usage Intention) mechanisms. Survey data from 245 logistics practitioners (cross-sectional, single-source) were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis, competing structural models, and bootstrapped indirect effects in a final integrated model. The originally proposed dual-track structure was not supported; the data favored a cross-linked specification in which cognitive beliefs inform attitudes across tracks and attractiveness precedes usage intention. Strategic AI training was associated with innovative behavior indirectly, Generative AI training both directly and indirectly, and Optimization AI training showed no unique association once the other dimensions were controlled. Neither Training Environment Quality nor Supervisor Support Leadership moderated the hypothesized relationships in a robust way, although both showed direct associations with outcomes (Training Environment Quality with Task–Technology Fit, β = 0.288; Supervisor Support with innovative behavior, β = 0.141). These cross-sectional, single-source associations refine the technology acceptance literature for AI training and inform HRD strategies for digital transformation in logistics.</jats:p>

title: On data-driven profile monitoring using memory-type control charts: a sequential change-detection framework for chemical engineering processes
container-title: Chemical Product and Process Modeling
b67def436ecea9d931006a67d674a91b67491468.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Reliable interpretation of sequential measurements requires methods that can distinguish meaningful changes in process relationships from routine variability. This requirement is particularly important for heat exchangers, where progressive fouling may alter the overall heat-transfer coefficient, its response to operating conditions, and the associated measurement variability. This study develops a data-driven profile-monitoring framework based on a double cumulative sum (DCUSUM) procedure for detecting changes in linear process profiles. The proposed DCUSUM
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    chart simultaneously monitors the profile intercept, slope, and error variance, which represent the response level, sensitivity to the explanatory variable, and residual variability, respectively. Coding the explanatory variable enables independent estimation and monitoring of these characteristics using routinely collected measurements without requiring a detailed physical process model. Performance is evaluated through Monte Carlo simulations under zero-state and steady-state conditions using average, dispersion, median, percentile-based run-length measures, and conditional expected delay. The results confirm that the chart maintains the prescribed in-control performance and that its detection delay and run-length variability decrease systematically as individual or joint shifts increase. Comparisons with Shewhart, EWMA, CUSUM, and DEWMA profile charts demonstrate competitive detection across a broad range of changes, with particularly strong steady-state performance. Application to controlled shell-and-tube heat-exchanger measurements illustrate earlier identification of fouling-related profile changes, thereby supporting reliable condition assessment and timely maintenance decisions. An interactive Shiny application supports chart calibration, performance evaluation, and practical implementation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty
container-title: The American Journal of Sports Medicine
5e557d26328b9962e8144326d6e37e7eb870ccdd.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury induces neuroplastic changes within the central nervous system (CNS) that may persist beyond reconstruction and rehabilitation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose/Hypothesis:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The purpose was to compare neurocognitive performance and cortical oscillatory activity between open-skill athletes (eg, soccer, basketball, or handball players) without ACL injury history and athletes with ACL reconstruction (ACLR) during a probabilistic go/no-go task. It was hypothesized that athletes with ACLR would exhibit poorer behavioral performance and less efficient oscillatory dynamics, particularly higher theta and lower suppression of beta and alpha power oscillations after goal stimulus onset.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Study Design:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Controlled laboratory study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR) performed a probabilistic go/no-go task while electroencephalographic recording was performed. Time-frequency analysis targeted midfrontal theta (4-7 Hz), left-lateralized central beta (15-25 Hz), and posterior alpha (8-12 Hz) oscillations during prestimulus and target stimulus windows. Linear mixed-effects models examined group differences in cognitive performance and oscillatory power.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Athletes with ACLR showed slower response times and lower accuracy (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                      = 0.75-1.09). Midfrontal theta power was attenuated for the ACLR group during the prestimulus phase (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                      = 0.60) yet elevated during target phase trials (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                      = 0.48), indicating a shift from proactive to reactive cognitive control in athletes with ACLR. Left-lateralized central beta (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                      = 0.61) and posterior alpha suppression (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                      = 0.55) were reduced, reflecting impaired motor cortical disinhibition and less efficient visual-attentional resource deployment, especially under high uncertainty conditions.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Athletes with ACLR showed persistent alterations in the cortical oscillatory mechanisms associated with conflict monitoring, motor preparation, and attentional allocation under uncertainty. These neurocognitive alterations may compromise adaptive motor responses in sport contexts characterized by high uncertainty and cognitive mental demand, potentially increasing reinjury risk. These findings support the integration of neurocognitive assessment into return-to-sport protocols.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Clinical Relevance:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Alterations in cortical oscillatory dynamics during decision-making under uncertainty may reflect reduced efficiency in cognitive control, motor preparation, and attentional allocation, which are not detected by standard assessments. Exercise professionals should consider integrating these assessments into return-to-sport protocols to address the persistent CNS alterations that may underlie reinjury risk in athletes with ACLR.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Shape Memory PVA-Tannic Acid/CuO Nanocomposites for Microneedle Patches with Antibiofouling and Antioxidant Properties
container-title: ACS Applied Nano Materials
799ab6c1715a328c880176c6765bcdaed33a6f23.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Shape memory materials capable of responding near physiological temperature are highly desirable for minimally invasive biomedical applications. However, achieving simultaneous mechanical robustness and biological functionality remains challenging. In this study, we developed a multifunctional CuO nanomaterial-reinforced poly(vinyl alcohol)-tannic acid (PVA-TA/CuO) nanocomposite as a temperature-responsive shape memory platform. PVA-functionalized CuO nanostructures with an average diameter of 200− 300 nm and lengths ranging from 0.5 to 1 μm were reinforced into a PVA-TA matrix through dynamic hydrogen bonding and Cu2+-polyphenol coordination interactions. The resulting composite exhibited improved structural stability, an enhanced tensile strength of 9.31 MPa, and a superior thermal stability compared with the PVA-TA composite. Notably, PVA-TA/CuO showed a rapid shape recovery at 40 °C, with dynamic mechanical analysis revealing a temperature-dependent relaxation transition at approximately 38 °C, supporting its near-physiological-temperature shape recovery. The PVA-TA/CuO composite also demonstrated significant antioxidant activity, excellent cytocompatibility, and pronounced antibiofouling behavior, achieving up to 83% and 75% biofilm inhibition against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, respectively. Furthermore, PVA-TA/CuO was successfully fabricated into a mechanically robust microneedle patch with sufficient insertion capability. Overall, our results highlight that nanoscale CuO reinforcement is an effective strategy for engineering mechanically robust, temperature-responsive shape memory materials with multifunctional properties for advanced biomedical applications.</jats:p>

Painting to Save One’s Life. Sally Gabori, Memory and Reparation

9b7ccdc58209b4d358a97435705c7d1e4141b817.abstract: <jats:p>La obra de Sally Gabori, singular artista de la comunidad Kaiardilt, en Australia, es un acto de cuidado y reparación frente al borrado colonial. Empieza a pintar con 81 años, y sus lienzos dan cuenta de su lengua, su cultura, su pueblo y el territorio en que vivió su infancia hasta que un desastre natural, en forma de ciclón y maremoto, obliga a su comunidad a trasladarse a otra isla en la que se impone una política de segregación por la que niños y niñas son separados de sus progenitores, de su lengua materna y sus referentes culturales. Convierte así al arte en un espacio de resistencia y de justicia poética; también en un espacio de cuidados y de construcción colectiva, en tanto que muchos de sus lienzos monumentales son realizados con sus hijas y otras mujeres de su pueblo. Pintar con cuidado no es solo una forma de expresión, es una forma creativa de mantener vivo su pueblo, su legado y su cultura, aun cuando su lengua esté a punto de perderse ya para siempre.</jats:p>

title: Next-Day Prediction of 0–20 cm Volumetric Soil Water Content in a Cotton Field Under Mulched Drip Irrigation in Southern Xinjiang, China, Using an ET0-Informed Trend-Constrained Long Short-Term Memory Model

3bf627288752abae42661b325f610fb92e713408.abstract: <jats:p>Surface soil water content is an important indicator for daily irrigation management in cotton fields under mulched drip irrigation in southern Xinjiang, China. This study evaluated a long short-term memory (LSTM) model incorporating reference crop evapotranspiration (ET0) and a trend-consistency (TC) constraint (ET0-TC-LSTM) for next-day prediction of 0–20 cm volumetric soil water content using the preceding 7 d of observations. Four observation periods during 2022–2025 yielded 468 supervised samples, divided chronologically into 169 training, 153 validation, and 146 test samples. ET0 was included as a feature, and a one-sided training penalty restricted predicted increases beyond a tolerance under recent low-water-input and high vapor pressure deficit (VPD) conditions. Persistence, ridge regression, and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network–LSTM (CNN1D-LSTM) model were included as benchmarks. In the original seed-42 experiment, ET0-TC-LSTM achieved a test coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9574 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.0081 cm3 cm−3, a 29.7% RMSE reduction relative to LSTM. Across ten seeds, the mean RMSE reduction was 2.84%; TC-LSTM had the lowest mean RMSE among the four LSTM variants. Persistence was more accurate, with an RMSE of 0.0046 cm3 cm−3. Sensitivity and conditional analyses showed that the effects of process-informed inputs and penalties depended on parameter settings and evaluation conditions. These results identify improvements within the LSTM framework, but do not establish superiority over persistence for this site and forecast horizon.</jats:p>

title: Caffeine Improves the Motor Components of Agility in Amateur Soccer Players: Limits of Perceptual-Cognitive Enhancement
container-title: Sports
1cd7cc8bcb25240bb265081e2970dc50d53e5446.abstract: <jats:p>Caffeine may enhance motor and cognitive performance in soccer players, yet its effects on specific agility components remain unclear. Sixteen male amateur soccer players (23.5 ± 4.0 years) completed a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Participants ingested 300 mg of caffeine (~3.7 mg·kg−1; CAF) or placebo (PLA). Thirty to 45 min after ingestion, they performed a countermovement jump (CMJ), drop jump (DJ), and three Y-shaped agility tests: planned agility, reactive agility to a light stimulus, and reactive agility to a human stimulus. Paired t-tests and Hedges’ g effect sizes (95% CI) were used to compare conditions. Caffeine significantly improved CMJ height (p = 0.02, ES = 0.30), reactive strength index in the DJ (p = 0.02, ES = 0.35), and planned agility time (p = 0.02, ES = 0.62). No significant effects were observed for reactive agility to light (p = 0.32, ES = 0.10) or human stimulus (p = 0.06, ES = 0.35). These findings suggest that a moderate caffeine dose enhances motor components of agility performance but provides limited benefits for reactive agility. Coaches may consider caffeine supplementation for amateur soccer players to support their performance in motor-dominant tasks rather than reactive agility performance.</jats:p>

title: Nutritional Behaviors, Hydration Status, Cognitive Function, and Physical Performance in Young Athletes: An Integrated Cross-Sectional Analysis
container-title: Sports
a75439f6514456dfd2afe3d1066daaafc3283415.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Athletic performance is influenced by interacting nutritional, psychological, physiological, and hydration-related factors, yet their combined relationships remain insufficiently explored. This study investigated associations between dietary behaviors, psychological characteristics, physical and physiological performance, body composition, and hydration status in young athletes. Methods: A cross-sectional study included 156 male athletes aged 17–22 years. Dietary behaviors were assessed using an Arabic-adapted Adult Eating Behaviour Questionnaire, while psychological characteristics were evaluated using the Test of Attentional and Interpersonal Style. Physical performance was assessed using the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1, handgrip strength, and standing broad jump. Body composition was measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis, and hydration status was assessed using urine specific gravity. Pearson correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction were used to examine associations. Results: Fruit and vegetable consumption and healthier fat-related behaviors were positively associated with muscular strength, whereas sugar and salt intake were negatively associated with cardiorespiratory fitness. Nutritional awareness, environmental factors, and emotional eating were not significantly associated with physical fitness measures. Attention characteristics showed predominantly broad external and internal attentional profiles, while hydration status was weakly associated with selected attentional characteristics. Conclusions: Overall, dietary quality was more consistently associated with physical performance than nutritional awareness alone. The findings support an integrated approach to athlete health and performance that considers nutritional, psychological, and hydration-related factors.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Cybersecurity via Bio-Inspired Intelligence: A Starling Flock Optimized Spiking Neural Network for Resilient Mobile Threat Detection
container-title: Acta Technica Jaurinensis
a0dcd798a93c8836c2e79155fde2906176a33b95.abstract: <jats:p>Real-time threat detection is critical for guaranteeing mobility systems in cognitive environments to function with little disruption. Through monitoring user behavior, system logs, and network traffic, such systems depend on sophisticated analytics and machine learning. This paper presents a new Intrusion Detection System (IDS) architecture leveraging a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) as a classifier and the Starling Flock Optimization Algorithm (SFOA) as a feature selector on the NSL-KDD dataset. The main objective is to enhance the accuracy of classification while lowering feature dimensionality and computational cost for effective real-time detection. SFOA, stimulated by starling flock behavior, dynamically chooses best feature subsets with balance between relevance and redundancy. The SNN, in turn, simulates biological neurons and processes these best features by mapping them into temporal spike trains, employing event-driven processing and Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP) for detailed pattern detection. Our developed model shows excellent performance with accuracy of 99.02%, precision of 98.9%, recall of 99.18%, and a 99.04% F1-score, outperforming SVM, Random Forest, CNN, LSTM, and Transformer models. Based on only 18 chosen features, the model has an extremely fast inference time of 2.3 ms, which is perfect for real-time usage. Comparatives also confirm SFOA is superior to PSO, GWO, ACO, and DE in terms of convergence rate and feature compactness. Ablation experiments validate that SFOA, spike encoding, and STDP learning are all essential to the model's performance, making this hybrid architecture a scalable and energy-efficient solution for sophisticated intrusion detection.</jats:p>

title: Reducing Test Response Volume and Test Time in Direct-Access-Based High-Bandwidth Memory Testing
container-title: Electronics
3802027670530b3880987747fe636a9bdc5f6a1b.abstract: <jats:p>In high-bandwidth memory (HBM) testing through the direct access (DA) port, the response-path bandwidth is far lower than the internal data bandwidth. Because most read responses are fault-free, transferring every response incurs substantial transfer overhead and test time. This paper proposes three fault-data transfer methods. Selective staggered read suppresses fault-free response transfers and overlaps faulty-response transfers with the subsequent read latency. Duplicate fault suppression replaces identical fault responses at consecutive addresses with a short duplicate code. Failing-bit indexing transmits only the positions of failing bits. The proposed architecture controls whether, when, and in which format each response is transferred without modifying the DA port interface or the March command and address sequence. Cycle-accurate simulation of an HBM2 test model shows that, across Random, Column-Correlated, and Row-Correlated Fault models with fault rates of 0.01–5%, the proposed method reduces the DA response data by 99.32–99.99% and the total test time by 44.86–45.01% compared with the conventional method. Synthesis shows that the added logic is smaller than that of on-chip fault collection and signature compaction schemes and independent of the memory capacity. The proposed architecture attains nearly the same test time as on-chip fault collection and signature compaction schemes while delivering every faulty response and its failing-bit positions to the tester, so that its diagnostic coverage is not bounded by on-chip storage.</jats:p>

title: Characterizing KV-Cache Performance in Large Language Model Inference: Context Length, Attention Architecture, and GPU Memory Residency
container-title: Journal of Low Power Electronics and Applications
3e5c72d90ae9a9f80b77836eae16ad31ff6de60f.abstract: <jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) commonly employ key–value (KV) caching to avoid recomputing previous attention states during autoregressive inference. However, its measured performance benefit depends on workload characteristics and the memory environment. This study presents a controlled systems characterization across input context length, model-specific grouped-query attention configurations, and GPU-memory residency. Experiments use Qwen2.5-3B and SmolLM3-3B under verified fully resident conditions with fixed 128-token generation, prompt lengths from 128 to 2048 tokens, randomized cache-enabled/cache-disabled execution, GPU telemetry, and repeated paired validation. End-to-end generation speedup increases from 1.34× to 8.31× for Qwen2.5-3B and from 1.28× to 8.62× for SmolLM3-3B. At 2048 prompt tokens, 30 randomized paired trials confirm mean speedups of 8.10× and 8.51×, corresponding to runtime reductions of 87.65% and 88.25%, while physical GPU-memory utilization remains below 61%. SmolLM3-3B requires twice the theoretical KV-cache storage per token, yet both models show comparable context-dependent scaling in the fully resident regime. Because the models differ in characteristics beyond KV-head count, this cross-model comparison is descriptive and does not attribute the observed performance difference causally to GQA configuration. A separate Mistral-7B case study shows that apparent end-to-end speedup changes substantially under memory pressure; the underlying memory-system mechanism is not isolated. These results establish cache-related end-to-end generation speedup as workload- and system-dependent and demonstrate that meaningful benchmarking requires reporting context length, cache configuration, model and cache footprints, physical accelerator-memory residency, runtime, throughput, and relevant GPU-memory conditions during each inference experiment.</jats:p>

title: Ageing, Digital Literacy, and Interaction Modality in Immersive Virtual Reality: Psychomotor Performance, Cognitive Flexibility, and Their Associations with Processing Speed
container-title: Virtual Worlds
b7cf97b7580bb33b2e64c069a2a07d4f445aa6e3.abstract: <jats:p>Extended reality (XR) increasingly supports training and cognitive assessment, yet the age sensitivity of its interaction techniques is unclear. This study examined age, digital literacy, and interaction modality as correlates of psychomotor and cognitive-flexibility performance in immersive virtual reality (VR). Two hundred and two adults (19–90 years) completed a five-mode Fitts’ law task (eye gaze, head gaze, controller ray-casting, virtual finger, and controller direct touch), the Trail Making Test in VR (TMT-VR), and a digital-literacy questionnaire. Age was associated with slower task times across modes, but controller direct touch carried the steepest relative age gradient while remaining among the fastest in absolute terms; technique altered relative age sensitivity without determining absolute efficiency. Higher digital literacy was associated with faster TMT-VR completion but not Fitts’ law task times. In the planned analyses, a Fitts’ law derived speed score predicted TMT-VR performance beyond age and, in a statistical decomposition, partly accounted for its age association, consistent with shared processing-speed variance. A post hoc exploratory full-battery extension confined the Fitts’ law score association with completion-time and error-adjusted-time indices and the digital-literacy association to error-adjusted-time indices, not wrong-target errors, mean selection distance, or relative Part B indices. Age-inclusive XR assessment should standardise interaction modality, evaluate rather than exclude mid-air direct selection, and interpret cognitive scores alongside digital literacy and psychomotor speed.</jats:p>

title: Assessing instrumental activities of daily living in people with mild‐to‐moderate dementia: Objective and subjective assessments and their cognitive correlates
container-title: Journal of Neuropsychology
a6c931483f016315cd7ea48ae46d9a723cfdc357.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Different methods of assessing instrumental activities of daily living (iADL) may show distinct relationships with cognition in dementia. This study investigated whether these relationships differed across objective, self‐rated, and informant‐rated assessments, with analyses of individual cognitive measures treated as exploratory. Thirty‐seven people with mild‐to‐moderate dementia were recruited from National Health Service memory clinics in North Wales. Participants completed the objective Direct Assessment of Functional Status (DAFS), study‐specific self‐rated and informant‐rated questionnaires based on the DAFS, and self‐rated and informant‐rated versions of the Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ). Cognitive assessment included measures of executive function, attention, memory, and global cognition. Univariable and forced‐entry multiple regression analyses were conducted with Holm‐Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Objective iADL performance showed more frequent associations with cognition than questionnaire‐based ratings. DAFS scores were associated with global cognition, immediate and delayed memory, Trail Making Test Part 4, and Design Fluency scores. In contrast, questionnaire measures showed few associations with cognition. FAQ self‐ratings were associated with depressive symptoms, while FAQ informant ratings were associated with carer burden. In the multivariable model, global cognition remained the only significant cognitive predictor after correction. Across 20 comparisons with questionnaire‐based iADL measures, correlations between cognition and the objective DAFS were larger in absolute magnitude, although only four differences remained significant after correction. The findings suggest that objective, self‐rated, and informant‐rated assessments may capture partially distinct aspects of everyday functioning and should not necessarily be considered interchangeable measures. Global cognitive measures may provide useful indicators of functional ability in mild‐to‐moderate dementia.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Clinical Outcomes: A Systematic Review of Gameful Artefacts for Mild Cognitive Impairment Assessment
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
f83019e32e57e56906de80620dffca38b77a1509.abstract: <jats:p>Gameful artefacts are increasingly used to assess Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), offering a potential complement to the limitations of traditional screening tools. However, while current research emphasises functional outcomes, the quality of gameful design and experience often receives comparatively less systematic attention. This systematic review analyses 43 gameful artefacts for MCI assessment, focusing on gameful design and experience. Our analysis yields three main insights: first, a “transparency gap” exists in reporting; studies primarily rely on static textual descriptions and screenshots. Expanding documentation to include videos or playable demonstrations represents a significant opportunity to better capture the gameful experience. Second, we deconstructed gameful artefacts using a formal game design element framework, providing a theoretical foundation and reference point. Third, we identified a “user gap” indicating that older adults are less involved in the early stages of development, and user evaluations tend to focus primarily on functional outcomes, indicating room for broader integration of player experience metrics. We conclude that gameful experience is not merely an additive feature but is essential to gameful artefacts. This paper calls for standardised reporting protocols, greater involvement of older adults during the early stage of design, and an integrated approach to cognitive assessment within gameplay.</jats:p>

title: The Role of Stress and Repeated Gameplay in Players’ Motivation and Engagement in a Cognitive Assessment Game
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
05d7f858c4eb92617152a6474dbaba18aac0b83b.abstract:
<jats:p>Cognitive assessment games show promise for monitoring players’ mental and cognitive health; however, their long-term effectiveness is threatened by diminishing player retention over repeated sessions in real-life settings. To facilitate better long-term deployment of cognitive games, we examined two key potential challenges: pre-game stress, and repeated game play.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>We conducted an experiment with the cognitive assessment game Tunnel Runner, which was played across two sessions. Before the second playing session, 93 participants were randomly assigned to undergo a Virtual Reality experience that involved either a validated stress-induction or a control procedure. Despite the effectiveness of the stress induction, players’ self-reported engagement and motivation in the game tended to show resilience to stress. Nevertheless, most aspects of players’ self-reported experience, including curiosity, enjoyment, and sense of reward, diminished between sessions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Our work provides early evidence that players’ experience in cognitive games is resilient to stress, yet raises concerns regarding its endurance over repeated play. This highlights the need for design solutions that sustain players’ motivation and engagement over time. Based on our findings, we propose game design approaches for creating stress-resilience and for enhancing the enduring appeal of cognitive games used for long-term cognitive assessment.</jats:p>

title: Multi-stage decision-making in ChatGPT adoption
container-title: Journal of International Students
5ed4c76ea3f6227cfb9926671459696e55544344.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to develop and empirically validate a comprehensive multi-stage decision-making (MSDM) model to explain users’ intention to adopt ChatGPT (Generative AI). Based on cognitive appraisal theory, the model conceptualizes three stages of adoption: (Cognitive) primary appraisal, (emotional) secondary appraisal, and Physical outcome, integrating six key antecedents: social influence (SI), hedonic motivation (HM), facilitating conditions (FC), performance expectancy (PE), effort expectancy (EE), and emotion (EMO) on willingness to use or reject. Using data from 372 prospective ChatGPT users, the findings reveal that SI, HM, and FC positively influence PE and EE. In turn, PE and EE shape users’ emotional responses, which ultimately determine their willingness or objection to adopt ChatGPT. The results show that ChatGPT adoption is a dynamic, stage-wise process driven by interconnected cognitive, motivational, and emotional factors. By offering a structured and integrative framework, this study advances understanding of GenAI adoption and offers valuable insights for researchers and practitioners to examine user behavior and design effective AI-enabled tools & services.</jats:p>

title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson’s disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Cognitive training (CogT) is an established non-pharmacological intervention for people with Parkinson’s disease (PD) and mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI). However, overall effects on cognitive outcomes are small to moderate and interindividually highly heterogeneous. Sleep –especially deep sleep–could be an important determinant of CogT responsiveness in PD, and may have beneficial effects on PD pathophysiology. Therefore, the enhancement of deep sleep by phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) could strengthen the effects of CogT on cognitive symptoms and counteract disease progression.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    PD-CogT-Sleep is a monocentric, partly decentralized, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial that combines two remotely delivered non-pharmacological interventions, to assess the additive effect of PTAS on digital CogT responsiveness in people with PD-MCI. The primary outcome is executive functions; Secondary and exploratory outcomes include further cognitive functions, participant-reported outcome measures, blood-based biomarkers, and high-density sleep electroencephalography markers. Outcomes are assessed at baseline, five weeks post-allocation and at 3-month follow-up. We aim to consecutively recruit
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    =50 participants, who will be randomized 1:1 to receive CogT+PTAS or CogT+Sham.
                  </jats:p>

                  <jats:p>The PD-CogT-Sleep study integrates wearable and digital technologies to systematically combine a novel, non-invasive, sleep-enhancing intervention (PTAS) with established CogT to improve cognition and evaluate PTAS’ disease-modifying potential through its effects on blood-based biomarkers in PD-MCI. The expected results will foster our understanding of the interplay of sleep, cognition, and neurodegeneration, and may guide further development of safe, feasible, scalable, patient-centered, technology-based non-pharmacological interventions counteracting cognitive decline in neurodegenerative diseases.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Alzheimer disease (AD) and α-synuclein copathology frequently co-occur in Parkinson disease (PD), but whether their interaction accelerates longitudinal cognitive decline is unknown.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To investigate whether the cross-sectional interaction between AD biomarker burden (CSF pTau181/Aβ42 ratio) and α-synuclein seed amplification assay (SAA) status translates to accelerated cognitive decline, and to estimate sample sizes for future co-pathology studies.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>We studied 246 dementia-free PD participants from the Parkinson Precision Medicine Initiative, including genetically enriched subgroups, across seven cognitive domains over 12.9 years. Longitudinal trajectories were modeled using inverse probability of continuation weighted generalized estimating equations with Firth penalization, confirmed by linear mixed-effects and Bayesian joint models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A cross-sectional AD×SAA visuospatial synergy was replicated (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                      =0.022), but no longitudinal interaction survived false discovery rate correction (all
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">q</jats:italic>

                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>

title: Cognitive reserve depends on cortical neurochemistry to predict memory after partner-inflicted brain injury
e1bf3d332506209d57d0d9dfd9e59c867d0d5131.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:p>
                  Memory problems are commonplace following brain injury (BI). However, it remains unclear why some report memory problems while others do not, especially following repeated neurotrauma. Cognitive reserve has been widely hypothesized to account for this variation, but testing this account has yielded inconsistent results and proven difficult, likely as it requires a sample spanning a wide range of BI burden with concurrent neuroimaging and cognitive measurement. Here, we combined a wide range of cognitive assessments with measures of neuronal health using magnetic resonance spectroscopy across three brain regions in 62 women who had experienced physical intimate partner violence. Partner-inflicted BI counts ranged from 0 to 420, yet we found that the number of BIs alone did not explain the variance in memory outcomes. Among a small subset with high BI exposure (≥10 BIs;
                  <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                  = 11), BI count explained 5% of the variance in delayed recall, the primary memory outcome, whereas cognitive reserve, inferred from a measure of premorbid functioning, explained almost half (unadjusted in-sample associations). In the full cohort, cognitive reserve predicted memory only among the most heavily injured participants. In a separate model, cognitive reserve predicted memory only when creatine-referenced total N-acetylaspartate, a marker of neuronal health, was lower in the posterior cingulate gyrus and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Ultimately, our findings provide behavioral and neurochemical evidence consistent with the cognitive reserve hypothesis and shed new light on why, despite a high burden of neurotrauma, memory may remain resilient.
                </jats:p>

title: Persistence Through Transformation: A Processual Framework for Knowledge Systems Across Cognitive, Cultural, and Religious Domains
1fb9e9ff16c3d10f9b74df14cafd8884c4fd89b5.abstract: How can knowledge systems preserve competence and identity while the organization supporting them changes? This theoretical article develops a processual framework for investigating persistence through selective transformation. It distinguishes a relational field from four interacting processual dimensions: continuity, discontinuity, selective reorganization, and emergence, while treating recursive epistemic niche construction as a longitudinal feedback mechanism rather than a fifth dimension. The framework brings together four requirements for explanation: an antecedent configuration, a specified organizational change, a capacity treated as persisting, and evidence concerning subsequent transmission. This architecture separates continuity of content, function, and identity and links conceptual change within individuals to the reproduction of distributed practices without assuming identical mechanisms across levels. A worked experimental proposal tests whether opportunities for reorganization preserve competence when inherited procedures no longer fit changed task demands. Religion provides a substantive case in which memory, ritual, epistemic authority, and cultural transmission can be investigated together; mythos, theos, and logos are treated as historical-processual heuristics rather than as universal or obligatory stages. Eight conditional propositions connect the framework to cognitive psychology, cultural evolution, and historical psychology. The account distinguishes descriptive persistence from epistemic justification and specifies conditions under which faithful reproduction should outperform transformation. Its explanatory value depends on comparative prediction, intervention, and prospective failure conditions rather than on treating every instance of change as evidence of emergence

title: Walking Through Memory, Myth, and Heritage: A Socio-Cultural Animation Framework via Cultural Walks and Reflective Journals at Quinta das Lágrimas
b38e0e309483fa5d2c86fb3a78418066fe965682.abstract: <jats:p>This theoretical-pedagogical article presents a proposed socio-cultural animation framework exploring the intersection of heritage education, reflective practice, and pedestrian movement. Grounded in critical pedagogy[1][2], experiential learning theory[3], the philosophy of walking[4], and anthropological perspectives on movement and landscape[5][6], this conceptual model engages diverse demographics—ranging from adolescents and youth to adults and seniors (incorporating principles of geragogy, [7])—using Quinta das Lágrimas in Coimbra, Portugal, as a living pedagogical site. By combining physical movement, sensory contemplation, station-based analysis, and personal reflective journals (_cadernos reflexivos_), this framework aims to transform cultural heritage from a static tourist destination into an active catalyst for lifelong learning, critical consciousness, personal memory construction, and 'learning on the move'[8]. While presented as a conceptual proposal, initial qualitative observations from preliminary pilot trials illustrate its potential for intergenerational heritage education.</jats:p>

title: Investigation of Brain Performance in the Schizophrenia Spectrum Using EEG with Mental and Temporal Effort
container-title: Sensors
875b291fa9828966ee875a7e2eb2b772638081fa.abstract: <jats:p>Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorder, widely known as causing behavioral changes, deprives many professionals—who remain capable of working—their jobs. This study aimed to investigate the use of electroencephalography exam (EEG) combined with standardized mental effort sequence as a complementary tool for clinical diagnosis and to monitor the treatment response in individuals with schizophrenia and those who want to return to professional activities. EEG recordings were acquired before (IR_Initial Register) and after (FR_Final Register) the completion of a set of timed mental effort tasks in a group of 25 clinically stable individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia with positive symptoms and an 11-member healthy volunteer control group. Data from both groups were compared using temporal and spectral descriptors, and the results were analyzed statistically. The results revealed that, in the FR phase, the Vtotal parameter for the schizophrenia group was 7.89% lower, and the frequency parameter was 16.35% lower than in the healthy group. Notable differences were observed in the tolerance parameter for the duration of sustained cognitive effort: 57.9% of healthy volunteers sustained 100% of the effort duration, compared with 6.1% of volunteers with schizophrenia.</jats:p>

title: Rivers remember what outlasts them: a phase diagram of mechanical memory
51fe37da0a64e9a8cf0abac28120c54818925a79.abstract: <jats:p>Rivers are pulse-driven machines, yet after a century of dam building we still lack a framework for how long a channel remembers an individual hydrological event. Here we show that river memory has two stages: an event is written into channel form only when it outlasts the reach-scale water residence time, and it is kept only when the sediment regime that follows does not erase it. A global layer of reach-scale timescales for 79,073 reaches maps where short events can register; regime shifts across five dam systems and a climate-stripped double difference over 898 dam sites show regulation shifting rivers along the measured writing axis of this phase space; nine controlled floods on the Colorado River show one-year retention set by post-flood tributary sediment supply (Spearman = 0.90), not by the flood itself; and 31 analysable Yellow River regulation events — from the only programme decoupling water from sediment pulses — all write in full yet split on retention, three-fifths of scour writes reburied within months while starved-year writes persist. Controlled floods and environmental flows should therefore be designed by hydrodynamics-based memory phase, not by water volume alone.</jats:p>

title: Between support and effort: how managerial need support and employee need crafting longitudinally associate with employee basic psychological needs
container-title: Motivation and Emotion
fb3dc7f771f99372652dc0188710100faadf16da.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Basic psychological needs have been demonstrated to be key drivers of employee work functioning. Studies investigating employees’ basic psychological need states in the workplace have focused on either the influence of contextual factors or the influence of employee crafting, yet there has not been any empirical investigation testing both types of factors simultaneously. Thus, the present study has compared the longitudinal associations from managerial need support and employee work-related need crafting to the satisfaction and frustration of employees’ basic psychological needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness. We hypothesized that both managerial need support and employee work-related need crafting would be distinctly associated with improvements in employee need satisfaction and frustration. We tested three longitudinal models (one per need), with a timeframe of three measurements across four months. Longitudinal results showed that only managerial need support had a positive association with autonomy satisfaction and a negative association with autonomy frustration, alongside with only employee competence crafting having a positive association with competence satisfaction, and both managerial need support and employee relatedness crafting having positive associations with relatedness satisfaction and negative associations with relatedness frustration. These findings highlight the distinct relations, and the complementarity, between contextual and individual factors in supporting employee basic psychological needs.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Early Childhood Mathematics Learning with Digital Manipulatives: Advancing Technology-Enhanced Cognitive Justice
container-title: Journal of Teaching and Learning
64643d039a2d9fc6f9733c2837249bdb85c1aa37.abstract: <jats:p>Transforming early childhood mathematics learning through digital manipulatives can advance technology-enhanced cognitive justice by fostering inclusive, engaging, and equitable experiences. Digital tools such as interactive software, apps, online platforms and games support diverse ways of knowing and enhancing mathematical understanding. However, effective integration is hindered by limited digital access, screen-time management, and teacher preparedness. This study explores (a) how early childhood educators integrate digital manipulatives, (b) the challenges they face, and (c) strategies for effective curriculum incorporation to enhance cognitive justice. Grounded in cognitive justice and constructivist learning theories, this study recognizes diverse epistemologies while promoting active, technology-enhanced learning. Using a hermeneutic phenomenological design, the study collected data from 12 educators sampled through homogeneous purposive sampling via semi-structured interviews, document analysis, and non-participant observations. Findings show teachers use digital manipulatives like YouTube videos and smartboards but struggle with lesson planning and implementation. This highlights gaps in curriculum development for integrating innovative approaches in early mathematics education. Addressing these gaps requires structured teacher training, resource accessibility, and curriculum adaptation to fully harness digital resources to promote technology-enhanced cognitive justice.</jats:p>

title: Augmented Reality Learning Integrated with Cognitive Conflict and STEM: Impact on Students’ Scientific Literacy in Newton’s Universal Law of Gravitation
container-title: Journal of Teaching and Learning
6ca5a11b56c7c886c99aa799749ba98d75926f2f.abstract: <jats:p>Integrating technology with innovative learning plays a crucial role in equipping students with scientific literacy. This research investigated the impact of augmented reality (AR) learning integrated with cognitive conflict (CC) and science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) on students’ scientific literacy using Newton’s universal law of gravitation as the learning material. This research involved 33 upper-secondary students divided into two groups using a quasi-experimental method: one group implemented AR, and the other used traditional learning. The research data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon test (W), Mann-Whitney test (U), and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analysis. The results of the W test revealed that both traditional learning and learning via AR have a positive impact on enhancing students’ scientific literacy. However, the U test results indicate that learning via AR was more effective than traditional learning. In addition, the results of the SEM analysis revealed that the enhancement of scientific literacy was influenced by AR technological characteristics, self-efficacy, and intention to use, which directly affected students’ scientific literacy. Therefore, AR learning integrated with CC and STEM has proven effective in enhancing students’ scientific literacy.</jats:p>

title: Alpha-Methylacyl-CoA Racemase (AMACR) Deficiency Presenting with Epilepsy, Cognitive Decline, and Pigmentary Retinopathy
container-title: Ophthalmic Surgery, Lasers and Imaging Retina
437a904c6495779e0eefc0a48f96ae1a1aa40223.abstract: <jats:p>A 66-year-old woman with long-standing epilepsy and progressive cognitive decline presented with bilateral vision loss (best-corrected visual acuity 1.22 logMAR right eye, 1.10 logMAR left eye). Electrodiagnostic testing showed severe rod-cone dysfunction. Fundus autofluorescence revealed bilateral multifocal geographic hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in a wreath-like pericentral distribution. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated bilateral outer retinal atrophy with ellipsoid zone loss and cystoid macular edema in the left eye. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic AMACR variant (c.154T>C; p.Ser52Pro) and a variant of uncertain significance (c.704C>T; p.Ala235Val). Elevated pristanic acid (152.9 μmol/L) confirmed alpha-methylacyl-CoA racemase (AMACR) deficiency, explaining her neurological disease. Macular edema decreased by 50 μm with topical dorzolamide and a phytanic and pristanic acid-restricted diet, and she reported subjective neurological improvement. Retinal imaging may be the first diagnostic clue to this rare but treatable condition. Ophthalmologists should consider AMACR deficiency in unexplained pigmentary retinopathy with neurological disease.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive-niche-based occupational exposure modeling for quantifying generative AI impacts on employment and educational supply
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
942a52d863954e8748cbc7424159a306f3287da2.abstract: <jats:p>This paper proposes a computable occupational cognitive niche model for quantifying the heterogeneous impact of generative artificial intelligence on employment and education supply. Instead of treating Gen-AI as a uniform jobreplacement factor, occupations are represented as five-dimensional cognitive niche vectors constructed from O*NET task data, and Gen-AI substitution is modeled as a time-varying intensity vector over the same task space. Occupational exposure is then calculated by vector overlap, and employment impacts are estimated by combining exposure scores with BLS baseline projections. Results under the 2034 scenario show clear cross-occupational heterogeneity: software developers obtain the highest exposure score of 0.1620 and a projected employment reduction from 1,918,067 to 1,607,340, while electricians show the lowest exposure score of 0.1052 due to their concentration in physical and context-dependent execution tasks. Graphic designers exhibit an intermediate exposure score of 0.1351, reflecting both vulnerability to generative production and persistence of judgment-intensive tasks. The model further updates task weights to capture within-occupation structural reconfiguration and maps occupational demand shifts to IPEDS-based education supply vectors. Quantitative comparison shows that university supply is concentrated in complex problem solving and rule-based execution, while arts and vocational pathways require differentiated adaptation toward judgment, physical execution, and responsibility-intensive competencies. The proposed framework provides a transparent and extensible method for linking Gen-AI exposure assessment, employment projection, and education supply adjustment in a unified computational model.</jats:p>

title: Integrative hdWGCNA and multi-model validation identify BAIAP2 as a shared neuronal hub for cognitive impairment acrossAlzheimer's disease, diabetic encephalopathy and brain aging
dddc859fd2e035da1744fb093200ae833b38858f.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD), diabetic encephalopathy (DE), and brain aging converge on cognitive decline with overlapping synaptic damage, impaired neuronal plasticity, and hippocampal circuit dysfunction. However, whether these pathological states share a unified neuronal transcriptional architecture remains largely unexplored at single-cell resolution. Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets related to AD, DE, and brain aging from the GEO database with high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis, we identified a conserved neuronal module and hub genes shared across the pathological conditions, pinpointing BAIAP2/IRSp53 as the sole shared neuronal core gene. In vivo , mouse models of all three cognitive disorders exhibited significant spatial memory deficits and consistent downregulation of hippocampal BAIAP2 at both the mRNA and protein levels; immunofluorescence further confirmed a widespread reduction of BAIAP2 in the hippocampal CA1, CA3, and dentate gyrus regions. In vitro , amyloid-β, metabolic stress, and senescence-inducing stimuli each recapitulated BAIAP2 suppression in SH-SY5Y neurons. Collectively, we establish BAIAP2 as a critical synaptic scaffolding hub whose disruption represents a unified neuronal substrate linking neurodegeneration, metabolic brain injury, and brain aging. These findings identify BAIAP2 as a potential target for AD-spectrum therapeutic strategies against cognitive decline.

title: Shape-Memory Photonic–Plasmonic Crystals for Programmable Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
container-title: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces
70204e373daebbbc28823b34c2337a3ef014454a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has emerged as a powerful analytical technique for ultrasensitive molecular detection. Integrating photonic architectures with plasmonic nanostructures provides an effective strategy to enhance SERS by exploiting slow-photon effects. However, continuously and reversibly controlling photonic enhancement remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a shape-memory photonic–plasmonic crystal (SMPPC) that enables programmable slow-photon signal enhancement through reversible structural reconstruction. By exploiting its shape-memory properties, the optical response of SMPPC can be reversibly modulated through solution evaporation or mechanical contact. Structural reconstruction dynamically modulates the spectral detuning between the excitation wavelength and the photonic stopband edge, resulting in a nonmonotonic SERS response governed by the interplay between plasmonic hotspot evolution and slow-photon effect. The fully recovered SMPPC substrate delivers an 8.1-fold enhancement in SERS intensity compared with the plasmonic copolymer SERS substrate. As a proof of concept, the SMPPC substrate enables the detection of antibiotics in municipal wastewater effluents at concentrations down to 471 ppt. This work establishes shape-memory-enabled photonic reconfiguration as a strategy for programmable manipulation of SERS, opening new opportunities for adaptive photonic–plasmonic sensing platforms.</jats:p>

title: Early-Stage Co-Creation and Human-Centered Development of Digital Therapeutics for Cognitive Rehabilitation in Early Neurocognitive Disorders: Convergent Mixed Methods Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
53541a4cf645a31d38e8d41cad81f50e31f7c722.abstract: Abstract Background Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represent critical windows for early neurocognitive intervention, although access to timely, personalized rehabilitation remains limited. Digital health technologies offer opportunities to deliver scalable and individualized cognitive care; however, their successful implementation depends on an understanding of users’ needs, expectations, and barriers. Within a human-centered design (HCD) framework, actively involving end users during the earliest stages of development is essential to ensure that digital rehabilitation is acceptable, usable, and responsive to real-world rehabilitation needs. Objective This study explores the experiences, rehabilitation needs, perceptions, and challenges of individuals with SCD and MCI regarding cognitive telerehabilitation. The findings are intended to inform the early-stage co-creation and human-centered development of digital rehabilitation solutions. Methods The study is framed within an HCD perspective to inform the user-centered development of digital rehabilitation solutions. A convergent mixed methods design was adopted to integrate quantitative assessments with qualitative interviews. The semistructured interview explored 4 thematic domains: neurocognitive abilities, network support, user experience and engagement, and digital divide. Twenty-three individuals with SCD or MCI completed the interview together with measures including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Cognitive Failures Questionnaire (CFQ), and an ad hoc Technological Expertise questionnaire. Qualitative interview data were analyzed using directed content analysis based on 4 predefined thematic domains by 2 independent raters, with interrater agreement assessed using Cohen κ. Qualitative and quantitative findings were subsequently integrated through exploratory Mann-Whitney U tests. Results Twenty-three participants (n=16 female participants; mean age 74.3, SD 7.35 y) were included. Participants reported preserved cognitive performance (MoCA: mean 24.9, SD 3.23), low-to-moderate perceived cognitive difficulties (CFQ: mean 22.4, SD 9.48), and moderate technological familiarity. Qualitative findings revealed memory (n=12, 52.2%), attention/executive (n=6, 26.1%), and language (n=4, 17.4%) difficulties during everyday activities, together with widespread use of compensatory strategies. Participants also described emotional vulnerability, social withdrawal, and feelings of misunderstanding, as well as delayed rehabilitation access despite reporting cognitive concerns to health care professionals. Although most participants had limited prior knowledge of telerehabilitation, they expressed a positive attitude toward home-based rehabilitation, valuing its convenience, flexibility, autonomy, and accessibility when appropriate technological and clinical support was available. Concerns mainly related to limited supervision, technical barriers, and digital literacy. Mixed methods integration showed that perceived technology-related barriers were associated with lower technological competence (median 1.88, IQR 1.69‐2.56 vs median 3.06, IQR 2.75‐3.59; P =.002), while no other significant differences emerged. Conclusions These findings highlight that effective digital rehabilitation should be developed through iterative, user-informed HCD processes that simultaneously address cognitive, emotional, social, and technological dimensions of early neurocognitive decline. Integrated findings highlight the importance of addressing individual needs and incorporating users’ perspectives from the earliest design phases to support usable, engaging, and accessible digital rehabilitation solutions.

title: Herramientas de inteligencia artificial en el desarrollo del pensamiento crítico y las habilidades cognitivas de estudiantes de educación general básica
Artificial intelligence tools in the development of critical thinking and cognitive skills of basic general education students
container-title: Journal of Multidisciplinary Novel Journeys & Explorations
83e529a22ec005b89c0a48b1f388f4efbf266b75.abstract: Objetivo: analizar críticamente la literatura sobre inteligencia artificial (IA), pensamiento crítico y habilidades cognitivas en Educación General Básica (EGB) y niveles escolares comparables. Método: se desarrolló una revisión narrativa de carácter documental basada en publicaciones científicas de 2021 a 2026, diferenciando los trabajos centrados en contextos K-12 de los referentes conceptuales y de investigaciones realizadas en otros niveles educativos. La síntesis se organizó en alfabetización en IA, razonamiento y resolución de problemas, pensamiento crítico, aprendizaje personalizado y mediación docente. Resultados: las revisiones sobre educación escolar describen posibilidades didácticas para explorar modelos de IA, resolver problemas y recibir retroalimentación adaptativa; sin embargo, buena parte de la evidencia corresponde a revisiones, propuestas curriculares o estudios de alfabetización tecnológica, y no a mediciones directas del cambio en pensamiento crítico. La comparación de las fuentes también identifica riesgos relacionados con sesgos, dependencia de respuestas automáticas, privacidad y brechas de acceso. Conclusión: la IA constituye un recurso pedagógico potencialmente valioso, pero sus beneficios cognitivos no son automáticos. Se requiere enseñanza explícita de la evaluación de evidencias, acompañamiento docente y estudios escolares con indicadores válidos y seguimiento longitudinal.

title: Navigating Artificial Intelligence Ambivalence in Radiology: A Conceptual Review of Cognitive, Professional, and Ethical Tensions in Hybrid Human–Algorithm Decision-Making
container-title: Indian Journal of Radiology and Imaging
7e10428860ff85c6a14aad57419d53e1ea5d1a57.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded within radiological practice, enhancing diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in workflows. Nonetheless, radiologists' engagement with AI is characterized by persistent cognitive, professional, and ethical tensions, beyond binary framings of trust versus resistance. These tensions can be conceptualized as AI ambivalence—a stable state in which radiologists recognize the clinical utility of AI whilst simultaneously remaining uneasy about its effects on accountability, autonomy, and justice. A narrative, conceptual approach was taken, synthesizing empirical and theoretical literature across radiology, medical AI, human factors, ethics, and health governance. The analysis focuses on radiological practice, including image interpretation, reporting workflows, triage systems, and professional accountability. Rather than evaluating individual AI tools, the review examines how AI reshapes the conditions under which radiologists exercise clinical judgement within hybrid human–algorithm decision-making. AI ambivalence manifests across three interrelated modalities: cognitive (epistemic uncertainty and automation bias), professional (erosion of autonomy and responsibility–authority mismatch), and ethical (tensions between efficiency, opacity, and accountability). These are sustained by four structural asymmetries in hybrid AI workflows: opacity asymmetry, responsibility asymmetry, performance ambiguity, and temporal instability. Downstream consequences include inconsistent engagement with AI outputs, variable clinical reasoning, medicolegal uncertainty, and organizational friction within health care. AI ambivalence in radiology may be argued to represent an enduring, ethically productive feature of hybrid diagnostic practice. Targeted mitigation should aim to dampen ambivalence where it produces clinical or organizational harm, while preserving reflective skepticism to safeguard professional judgement. Understanding AI ambivalence is essential to ensuring that AI adoption in radiology supplements, rather than supplants, human expertise.

title: Inherited maternal memory T cells protect offspring from respiratory viral infection through disease tolerance
a7066f39eb9339d8c659b0c7d6f9ffac3ddf72dc.abstract: Summary Maternal immune transfer is a powerful mechanism for early-life protection from infection, yet the full repertoire of protective factors remains unknown. We discovered that maternal memory T cells are both necessary and sufficient to protect offspring from lethal respiratory infection. This antigen-specific protection operated independently of maternal antibodies and offspring T cell responses and required IL-10 produced by maternal T cells. Transfer of protective maternal T cells reduced offspring inflammatory responses and lung tissue damage without affecting viral burdens, indicating that maternal memory T cells directly suppress pathogenic innate inflammatory responses to preserve offspring health. Critically, maternal vaccination similarly protected offspring in a T cell-dependent manner. These findings reveal maternal antigen-specific T cell transfer as a complementary immunological defense mechanism to protect offspring against pathogens that escape maternal antibodies, with broad implications for maternal vaccination strategies. title: Chronic hypertension disrupts the blood-brain barrier in the ventral hippocampus in females but not males in a rat model of vascular cognitive impairment
62c8a4bf203494784a8e51bccdf1ce1c5f20abc1.abstract: Background: Chronic hypertension is a leading cause of cerebrovascular disease, ischemic stroke, and cognitive impairment. In addition, anxiety and hypertension often co-exist, however, little is known about the relationship between the two. Understanding how chronic hypertension impacts limbic brain regions such as the ventral hippocampus may provide insight into how cerebrovascular contributes to altered emotional behavior. Methods: An open field task was used to quantify locomotion, exploratory behavior, thigmotaxis, rearing and risk assessment behaviors in adult (7-month-old) male and female normotensive Wistar rats and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR; n=8/group). Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was assessed by measuring extravasation of sodium fluorescein, 3 kDa Texas red dextran and 10 kDa cascade blue into the ventral hippocampus. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays were used to measure markers of vascular signaling, inflammation, and central nervous system-specific proteins indicative of neuroaxonal and glial injury in serum from separate groups of male and female SHR (n=6/group). Main effects and interactions between two independent variables (sex and hypertension) were determined using two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey's post-hoc tests. Circulating factors were compared using a Welch's t-test. Relationships between BBB permeability and anxiety-like behavior were determined using Pearson's correlations. Results: Chronic hypertension increased circulating inflammatory factors and BBB permeability in female but not male rats. BBB permeability did not differ by sex in male and female normotensive rats. There was an anxiolytic effect of chronic hypertension on exploratory-related anxiety-like behavior, including less thigmotaxis, lower latency to cross through the center of the arena, and increased unsupported rearing. Risk assessment behavior, quantified as stretch-attend posture, was increased in female SHR. BBB permeability in the ventral hippocampus was correlated with anxiety-like behavior in females, but not in males, suggesting sex-dependent mechanisms of hypertension-induced changes in emotional behavior. Conclusions: These findings implicate a role for chronic hypertension-induced BBB disruption in neuropsychiatric disorders in the female sex and advances our understanding of cerebrovascular vulnerability in deep limbic brain regions.

title: أثر التداخل بين الذاكرة العاملة والانتباه التنفيذي في اكتساب المفاهيم المجردة لدى طلاب المرحلة الثانوية
The Effect of the Interaction between Working Memory and Executive Attention on the Acquisition of Abstract Concepts among Secondary School Students

49b25447bf2bd95d7691b99310b3f9b63c712632.abstract: يتناول هذا البحث أثر التداخل الوظيفي بين الذاكرة العاملة والانتباه التنفيذي في تفسير اكتساب المفاهيم المجردة لدى طلاب المرحلة الثانوية، في إطار منظور معرفي تكاملي ينظر إلى التعلم بوصفه عملية ديناميكية ناتجة عن تفاعل أنظمة معرفية متعددة. وتبرز أهمية الموضوع في كونه يعالج أحد التحديات المركزية في التعلم المجرد، خاصة في المجالات التي تتطلب معالجة رمزية معقدة، مثل الرياضيات والمنطق، حيث لا يكفي تفسير الأداء المعرفي عبر متغيرات منفصلة، بل من خلال مستوى تكاملها الوظيفي. اعتمد البحث المنهج الوصفي التحليلي ذي الطابع الارتباطي التفسيري، باستخدام تحليل الانحدار المتعدد لاختبار العلاقات المباشرة والتفاعلية بين المتغيرات. وقد جُمعت البيانات من عينة من طلاب المرحلة الثانوية باستخدام أدوات مقننة شملت اختبارات الذاكرة العاملة (اللفظية والبصرية)، ومهام الانتباه التنفيذي مثل اختبار ستروب، إضافة إلى اختبار تحصيلي لقياس مستوى اكتساب المفاهيم المجردة، مع ضبط متغيرات مثل العمر والتحصيل الدراسي. أظهرت النتائج وجود علاقة ارتباطية دالة إحصائيًا بين الذاكرة العاملة والانتباه التنفيذي، كما تبين أن كليهما يسهم في التنبؤ بالأداء المعرفي، غير أن التأثير التفاعلي بينهما كان الأكثر قوة في تفسير اكتساب المفاهيم المجردة، مما يشير إلى أن كفاءة التعلم تعتمد على درجة التكامل بين عمليات التخزين والتنظيم المعرفي. كما كشفت النتائج عن دور وسيط للانتباه التنفيذي في تعزيز فاعلية الذاكرة العاملة أثناء معالجة المعلومات المجردة. وتدعم هذه النتائج بناء نموذج تفسيري يوجّه نحو تطوير استراتيجيات تعليمية قائمة على تنمية الوظائف التنفيذية بصورة تكاملية، مع إعادة النظر في تصميم المناهج بما ينسجم مع الطبيعة البنيوية للتعلم المعرفي.
