0f92cf0cef99de5516ba09ee0eb26631118eae26.abstract: قصيدة "نوبات غريبة من العاطفة عرفتها" لويليام وردزورث، وهي قطعة شعرية ملهمة ضمن سلسلة قصائد لوسي، تجذب القارئ مباشرةً إلى صراع نفسي عميق يخوضه راوٍ يتحول حبه الجارف فجأةً إلى شعور غير منطقي بالخوف من الموت. والجدير بالذكر أن لغة القصيدة تُظهر ضمنيًا بنية معرفية متطورة ترسم رحلة عاشق إلى كوخ حبيبته، حيث يُثير جمال المنظر الطبيعي تحت ضوء القمر فجأةً عالمًا قاتمًا من القلق والخوف. ومع ذلك، فإن هذه التجربة الماضية للراوي لا تنبع من أحداث خارجية فحسب، بل من انفصال قوي وعفوي في وعيه. وهذا يُظهر بوضوح تحديًا للتحليل الأدبي يدفع القارئ مباشرةً إلى رسم خريطة للحالة العاطفية والنفسية لمتحدث تنهار حقيقته فجأةً بفعل إدراك داخلي وذاتي غامض. تتناول هذه الورقة البحثية هذا التحدي بتطبيق نظرية عالم النص (المشار إليها فيما يلي بـ TWT)، وهي نموذج معرفي-أسلوبي شامل طوره ويرث (1999) ثم نقحه جافينز (2007أ، 2007ب). توفر TWT إطارًا شاملًا يتجاوز الفهم الموضوعي للنص إلى بناء المعنى النصي نفسه، انطلاقًا من افتراض أن القراء يُنشئون تمثيلات، أو عوالم نصية، أثناء قراءة الخطاب. في حالة قصيدة وردزورث "نوبات غريبة من العاطفة عرفتها"، تُظهر الأدوات التحليلية لنظرية عالم النص ، وتحديدًا التمييز بين عالم النص المألوف، أي الرحلة المادية، والعالم الفرعي المُضمّن، أي تأملات الراوي في مخاوفه، أنها شاملة لتوجيه التشويق في القصيدة.

title: P083 |  EFFECT OF ATOGEPANT ON COGNITIVE FUNCTION FOLLOWING ACUTE TREATMENT OF MIGRAINE ACROSS MULTIPLE ATTACKS: RESULTS FROM THE ECLIPSE TRIAL
container-title: Confinia Cephalalgica
5bcd0ce104e3d077844c6b70ce9c497f718f365b.abstract: Background. Atogepant is approved for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults and has recently demonstrated its efficacy and safety for the acute treatment of migraine. This analysis evaluated the impact of atogepant 60mg administered as needed (PRN) for acute treatment of migraine on cognitive function assessed by the ability to think clearly.Methods. ECLIPSE was a double-blind (DB), placebo-controlled, multiple-attack, crossover trial evaluating atogepant’s efficacy, safety, and tolerability for acute migraine treatment. Adults with 2-8 monthly moderate-to-severe attacks were randomised to receive atogepant for three qualifying attacks and placebo for one attack during the up to 16-week DB period. Cognitive function scale is a single-item, patient-reported questionnaire measuring participants’ difficulty in ability to think clearly, rated from 0 (not difficult at all) to 3 (very difficult). The proportion of participants achieving the ability to think clearly at 2-, 4-, and 8-hours postdose across attacks 1-4 was an additional (exploratory) efficacy endpoint. Data for atogepant and placebo are presented with nominal P-values.Results. Atogepant treatment resulted in a nominally significant higher proportion of participants achieving the ability to think clearly compared with placebo as early as 2-hours postdose in the first treated attack (OR: 1.78); this effect increased over time through 4- and 8-hours postdose (OR: 3.39, 3.73, respectively). A similar reliable response was observed across attacks 2-4 ().Conclusions. A greater proportion of participants treated with atogepant achieved the ability to think clearly compared to placebo as early as 2-hours and up to 8-hours postdose across multiple attacks.Raffaello Masselli, this individual has been added to this publication author by-line, with the permission of the original authors, for the express purpose of conducting the presentation at a local congress or in a local language. He did not contribute to the content of the publication.

title: P085 |  IMPACT OF PROPHYLACTIC TREATMENT ON COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN MIGRAINE: A CLINICAL EVALUATION USING THE I-MIG-SCOG SCALE
container-title: Confinia Cephalalgica
93dbf3edf886fa7ee2d1fd57d5f3e196a96f1cd3.abstract: Background. Migraine is frequently accompanied by cognitive issues that significantly reduce patients' quality of life. In this regard, we aimed to evaluate the subjective cognitive burden related to migraine in a real-world cohort of patients attending a specialized headache center under advanced prophylaxis, and to analyze the correlation between the I-MIG-SCOG scale score and the residual monthly attack frequency.Methods. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted based on data recorded during outpatient follow-up visits in migraine patients undergoing prophylactic treatment with subcutaneous monoclonal antibodies or gepants. All migraine patients who had a fully completed 9-item I-MIG-SCOG scale at their last visit were included. The severity of the subjective cognitive impairment was quantified using the scale's total score (range 0–18) and correlated with the monthly headache frequency recorded at that visit.Results. The preliminary analysis included 62 patients. The data confirmed a clear positive linear correlation between a high residual attack frequency and a more severe cognitive burden. Patients with a higher frequency of attacks per month showed significantly greater cognitive dysfunction on the I-MIG-SCOG scale (characterized by severe concentration deficits, slowed problem-solving, and anomia), with peak scores ranging between 10 and 15 points. Conversely, patients who achieved optimal clinical control thanks to prophylaxis, with minimal residual frequency (0 to 2 attacks/month), recorded minimal or zero I-MIG-SCOG scores, ranging between 0 and 3 points.Conclusions. The preliminary results of this study consolidate the evidence that the transient attentive and executive difficulties associated with migraine are strictly dependent on the clinical control of attack frequency. An effective prophylactic therapy not only reduces physical pain but is also associated with a drastic reduction in subjective cognitive deficit, substantially improving the patient's global functional status.

title: GraphCLaRa uses graph guided document selection for multihop question answering with compressed memory
246009b48fa2177d7c36f244ba31ae610731ec52.abstract: Abstract Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for multi-hop question answering suffers from noisy context and weak retrieval–generation alignment. Apple’s Continuous Latent Reasoning (CLaRa) improves efficiency by compressing retrieved documents into dense latent memory tokens, but this compression obscures the structural relationships between documents required for multi-hop reasoning. We propose GraphCLaRa, a lightweight (∼1.3M-parameter) graph-based reranker for a frozen CLaRa reader. It constructs a query-aware document graph, propagates evidence with a Graph Attention Network (GAT), and selects a compact document subset with an adaptive context-budget head. Across four single- and multihop QA benchmarks, GraphCLaRa improves answer F1 on three of four datasets (up to +6.6) while using fewer documents, and trails by only 1.1 F1 on the retrieval-saturated benchmark. Our analysis shows that graph-guided selection consistently helps when retrieval leaves room for improvement, whereas on saturated retrieval tasks compression can only discard evidence. These results demonstrate that graph-based evidence propagation complements latent-memory compression.

title: Empirical Evaluation of Normalized Temperature-Scaled Cross-Entropy Pre-training in a Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise–Convolutional Neural Network–Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory–Cross-Attention Framework for Unmanned Surface Vehicle Diesel Engine Fault Diagnosis
container-title: Journal of Dynamics, Monitoring and Diagnostics
d7501646cf5922f790fc34627ac25c7363376dec.abstract: Reliable diagnosis of unmanned surface vehicle (USV) diesel-engine faults requires representations that preserve multiscale vibration content and crank-angle-dependent context. Therefore, a CEEMDAN-CNN-BiLSTM-Cross-Attention framework is constructed, and NT-Xent pre-training is evaluated without presuming that it provides a performance benefit. CEEMDAN generates eight multiscale input channels, a CNN encodes local vibration transients, and the BiLSTM represents within-cycle context. The Cross-Attention uses CNN features as queries and BiLSTM features as keys and values. Six health states recorded on a laboratory diesel-engine platform at 1800 r/min and 80% load are used for experiments. The acquisition order defines the training, validation, and test subsets containing 2100, 450, and 450 cycles, respectively. Across five paired seeds, the Cross-Attention model with NT-Xent pre-training achieve 99.16 ± 0.40% accuracy and 99.15 ± 0.40% macro-F1 on clean test data. Five-fold acquisition-ordered block evaluation yield 99.07 ± 0.32% for both accuracy and macro-F1. Matched protocols, paired statistics, nested ablations, reduced-data tests, and additive-noise tests are used to separate overall framework performance from incremental component effects. NT-Xent pre-training increase clean-test accuracy by +0.09 percentage points relative to supervised training alone (95% CI; -0.95 to 1.13; p = 0.825). The Cross-Attention model scores 0.49 percentage points lower than the without-attention model (p = 0.207). Ordinary instance-level NT-Xent also performs worse at training-data fractions of 1%, 5%, and 10%. Accuracy is fell to 17.56 ± 1.14% at 12 dB, which is close to the chance level for six classes. The framework therefore accurately classifies clean test cycles under a fixed-operating condition , but neither the Cross-Attention model nor NT-Xent pre-training produces a reliable incremental benefit. These findings define the validated scope of the framework. Its performance under different operating conditions, across independent sessions and engines, and in real marine environments remains to be tested independently. Conflict of Interest Statement The authors declare no conflicts of interest.

title: <i>Cognitive offloading</i> dalam pembelajaran di era <i>generative AI</i>: Literasi AI untuk mendorong <i>cognitive empowerment</i> mahasiswa
container-title: Prosiding Seminar Nasional Sanata Dharma Berbagi
54bf6910252fcc432825f21bd418c68e3a6055b5.abstract: Kajian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis bagaimana cognitive offloading melalui penggunaan generative AI (GenAI) dapat memengaruhi cognitive empowerment dan mengidentifikasi peran literasi AI dalam proses tersebut. Permasalahan kajian ini berfokus pada bagaimana pengalihan beban kognitif kepada AI memengaruhi kapasitas belajar mahasiswa dan bagaimana kemampuan literasi AI oleh mahasiswa dapat mencegah berkembangnya ketergantungan kognitif. Metode yang digunakan adalah kajian konseptual melalui telaah literatur integratif terhadap literatur mengenai cognitive offloading, literasi AI, GenAI, metakognisi, dan pembelajaran mandiri. Hasil kajian ini menunjukkan bahwa cognitive offloading tidak secara langsung memberikan sifat negatif, namun terdapat konsekuensi dalam ketergantungan pada tingkat kendali dan keterlibatan kognitif mahasiswa. Literasi AI berperan sebagai kompetensi pengarah melalui kemampuan memahami keterbatasan AI, menggunakan AI secara strategis, mengevaluasi keluaran, mengatur tingkat ketergantungan, dan melakukan refleksi terhadap proses belajar. Kajian ini menegaskan bahwa penggunaan GenAI dapat bergeser dari pengurangan beban berpikir menuju penguatan kapasitas belajar apabila mahasiswa tetap mempertahankan cognitive agency dalam proses pembelajaran.

Hinton introduce this festschrift for Phillip Sipiora, fifteen pieces chosen from the first fifteen volumes of The Mailer Review. Drawing on Mnemosyne as mother of the Muses, Toni Morrison’s “The Site of Memory,” and the wall of Uruk in Gilgamesh, they argue that keeping memory alive means method rather than reverence, and that Mailer studies came of age under Sipiora’s stewardship when it turned from monument to method. title: Cognitive Psychiatry and the natural genesis of concepts: Processuality, co-praxis, co-cognition and conceptual accretivity as foundations of a naturalistic epistemogenesis
Psiquiatría Cognitiva y la génesis natural de los conceptos: Procesualidad, co-praxis, co-cognición y acrecentabilidad conceptual como fundamentos de una epistemogénesis naturalista
Psiquiatria Cognitiva e a gênese natural dos conceitos: Processualidade, co-praxia, co-cognição e acrescentabilidade conceitual como fundamentos de uma epistemogênese naturalística
container-title: Research, Society and Development
9355b127efef3b84fcd8c4bf44c057e6521a255e.abstract: Modern epistemology usually examines concepts once they are already constituted, leaving unexplained how they arise and how they change while remaining recognizably the same. Objective: to propose, from Cognitive Psychiatry, a naturalistic epistemogenesis of concepts grounded in processuality. Methodology: a theoretical, hypothesis-generating essay confronting the proposal with antecedents in Hilbert, Frege, Mill, Pap, Lewis, Dewey, Hegel and Wittgenstein and with recent literature on embodied cognition, active inference, the neuroscience of concepts and dimensional psychiatric nosology. Results and Discussion: knowledge begins with the organism's causal, temporal and functional co-participation with the world (co-praxis); concepts are stable coagulations of these processes, later reworked by cognition operating on its own products (co-cognition). Reification is a necessary instrument of thought, threatened by hyper-reification and de-reification. Conceptual accretivity is proposed as a third way between rigid identity and total replacement: a co-praxic core is preserved while new strata, relations and theoretical hooks accrue, in a surpassing that negates and preserves. Redefinitions change descriptions and interpretations, not the events they refer to. The model is applied to schizophrenia as a syndrome, to the distinction between error and lying, to theoretical hooks that define a function before an entity and to a conceptual pathophysiology of rigidity, fragmentation, hyperassociativity, impoverishment and loss of anchorage. Final Considerations: analyticity can be understood processually, as the structuring persistence of apprehended relations in a globally connected world that admits local syntheses, making the natural history of concepts a legitimate domain of Cognitive Psychiatry.

title: Cognitive Psychiatry and the cosmological genesis of knowledge, consciousness and science: From co-praxization to analogization, conceptualization and intersubjective objectivity
Psiquiatría Cognitiva y la génesis cosmológica del conocimiento, la conciencia y la ciencia: De la co-praxización a la analogización, la conceptualización y la objetividad intersubjetiva
Psiquiatria Cognitiva e a gênese cosmológica do conhecimento, da consciência e da ciência: Da co-praxização à analogização, à conceptualização e à objetividade intersubjetiva
container-title: Research, Society and Development
908da6ff2c7be9a5218dae9472a9cc4a7daad4bf.abstract: Traditional epistemology studies knowledge mainly through its formalized results, such as concepts, propositions and criteria of truth, and leaves the natural processes that precede them insufficiently explained. This article aims to propose, from the standpoint of Cognitive Psychiatry, a naturalistic and psychogenetic model of the genesis of knowledge, consciousness and science. It is a theoretical proposition essay supported by a narrative review of literature published between 2021 and 2026. Knowledge originates in the organism's participation in the processualities of the cosmos through co-praxization, co-synchronization and co-causalization. These operations build neurophysiological tracks that allow automatic analogization of processualities before any conscious hypothesis. Reflexive consciousness arises when the individual virtually reconstructs his own experience, and the interlocutor, who does not share that history, forces its objectification. The concept is a provisional coagulation of lived processualities that compacts, hierarchizes and extends causal chains beyond working memory. Scientific hypotheses emerge as virtual bridges built over gaps between discontinuous segments of experience, using previously incorporated analogies, and error results from legitimate but insufficient analogies. Formal science is a specialized development of an originary scientificity already present in communication, prediction and voluntary action. The model reformulates Meno's paradox, reinterprets the Platonic search for essences as an intuition of an initial analyticity, and gives Michel Meyer's problematology a natural genesis. Two tables, two figures, testable predictions and implications for Psychiatry are presented.

title: Correctness Before Reuse: A CPU Contract Pilot for Kernel Optimization Memory
c209045af9207f19101225adc7b6b10639a09bad.abstract: A kernel that returns a plausible value on its first input may fail when runtime values, specialization parameters, layout, or a partial tile changes. We report a completed CPU validation pilot for such reuse boundaries. A frozen registry of eight host implementations is evaluated on 192 cases across addition, masked row softmax, and RMSNorm, producing 1,536 candidate-case checks. The suite contains 128 nonempty cases and 64 empty-shape contract checks. A host reference and a complete dispatch-metadata key pass all cases. Five of six seeded fault controls pass a benign first-input gate, yet every fault control fails at least one stronger check. Shape-only specialization passes 48/192, cached outputs 128/192, dropped tail rows 102/192, input mutation 160/192, a float16 shortcut 133/192, and naive float32 reduction 188/192. A separate 50-digit Decimal implementation verifies all target arrays within the frozen tolerance, replays all candidate checks, and confirms 40 nonempty input/oracle identities. These results establish an auditable validation artifact, not kernel speedup or learned optimization. The memory stores dispatch metadata rather than compiled code. A separate, uncompiled NKI entrypoint documents the next target-device stage. Future work applies the gate to actual Trainium compilation, profiling, generated candidates, and transfer across workload families under bounded credits.

title: Measurement Invariance of the Adult Self-Report Across Sex and Ethnoracial Status in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
container-title: Assessment
8646ef0f5f6efe421d2d2052807303e5b105ddae.abstract: Understanding sex and ethnoracial group differences in psychopathology is critical to identify mental health disparities. However, the validity of these group differences is often uninterrogated. One threat to validity is measurement bias, where specific items may be more likely to be endorsed by a specific group even without differences in underlying psychopathology. We examined measurement bias using invariance testing in the Adult Self-Report (ASR) in adult parents of children in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study ( N = 8,608). The ASR dimensions demonstrated invariance across sex and ethnoracial groupings, except for Antagonism and Social Maladjustment. These results suggest that some dimensions of the ASR are largely invariant across sex and ethnoracial groupings in this sample, and that group differences in measured scores are likely unconfounded by measurement bias. We report sex and ethnoracial group differences in psychopathology dimensions and discuss limitations of parental psychopathology assessment in the ABCD study.

title: It’s not what you do, it’s how they feel: how humble leadership activates employee affective-cognitive units to foster innovation
container-title: Leadership & Organization Development Journal
34f82aacfc3041d54a5120f0d8a64c87725c688d.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine how humble leadership (HL) influences employee innovative behavior (EIB) through pride and relational identification, drawing on the cognitive-affective personality system (CAPS) theory. We explore the moderating role of employees’ attributions of leader humility to performance improvement motives (PIM) and impression management motives (IMM). Design/methodology/approach This study conducted a three-wave time-lagged survey design with two-week intervals, collecting data from 312 employees working in technology enterprises. Findings This research demonstrates that HL fosters EIB through pride and relational identification. The relationship between HL and pride is amplified when employees attribute leader humility to PIM but attenuated when employees attribute it to IMM. Moreover, employees attribute leader humility to IMM impairs the indirect relationship between HL and EIB via pride and relational identification. Originality/value Drawing on CAPS theory, this research introduces an integrated affective-cognitive mechanism to explain how HL fosters EIB. It further identifies employees’ attributions of leader humility as key contingencies. Moreover, the findings reveal an asymmetric attribution pattern, in which negative attributions exert a stronger influence than positive attributions on the effectiveness of HL. These findings contribute to a more nuanced understanding about the effectiveness of HL, highlighting the active role of employees.

title: Cross-National Cognitive Diagnostic Profiles in PISA 2015 Computer-Based Mathematics Assessment: A Joint Analysis of Attribute Mastery and Response Times
e158fea8626cfaf889ddfa34f3e9123fee80effa.abstract: Abstract This study examined cross-national cognitive diagnostic profiles in the PISA 2015 computer-based mathematics assessment by integrating attribute mastery and response-time information. Eleven education systems were purposively selected to reflect variation in geographic regions, educational contexts, and levels of economic development, and all students included in the analysis responded to the same set of nine test items. Specifically, this study compared students’ attribute mastery probabilities across four PISA 2015 mathematics content domains, i.e., Change and Relationships, Space and Shape, Quantity, and Uncertainty and Data, examined knowledge-state distributions and cross-sectional mastery-order patterns, and evaluated response-time-informed item diagnostics, including slipping, guessing, and discrimination parameters. Using a joint cognitive diagnosis and response time modeling framework, we estimate students’ mastery probabilities and knowledge-state distributions, identify cross-sectional mastery-order patterns, and evaluate item-level diagnostic characteristics. The findings indicate relatively high mastery of Change and Relationships in several education systems, substantial cross-national variation in Quantity and Uncertainty and Data, and a common cross-sectional mastery-order pattern in which Change and Relationships tends to appear earlier than Space and Shape, Quantity, and Uncertainty and Data in the distribution of knowledge states. Response-time-informed item diagnostics further reveal differences in slipping, guessing, and discrimination across items and education systems, suggesting that similar response scores may reflect different response processes and item characteristics. These results demonstrate how cognitive diagnosis and response-time modeling can extend the interpretation of PISA mathematics data beyond overall performance comparisons and provide diagnostic information for curriculum refinement, targeted instructional support, and assessment development.

title: The Oral-Brain Axis and Neighborhood Deprivation: An Ecological Data-Warehouse Analysis of Tooth Loss, Cognitive Disability, and Mental Distress in U.S. ZIP Code Areas
3249184f7063834e3139160b6125de053595c6ce.abstract: Abstract Background. Oral microbial dysbiosis and periodontal disease have been linked to systemic inflammation and cognitive decline, an idea often called the oral-brain axis. Oral disease and cognitive impairment both vary with social conditions, but few analytic systems link neighborhood deprivation to oral and cognitive health across the whole country. Methods. We built a staged SQL data warehouse that combines the 2024 Area Deprivation Index (ADI; 242,297 block group records keyed by 12-digit FIPS and GISJOIN) with the CDC PLACES extract (1,171,563 rows). For four indicators (complete tooth loss in adults aged 65 and older, cognitive disability, frequent mental distress, and dental visit in the past year), ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA) prevalence was linked to county-mean ADI. We estimated Spearman correlations, ADI-quintile gradients, and population-weighted regressions with county-clustered standard errors. Microbiome data were not analyzed. Results. In 29,903 ZCTAs with all four indicators, tooth loss correlated strongly with cognitive disability (ρ = 0.83) and mental distress (ρ = 0.72), and inversely with dental visits (ρ = -0.84). From the least to the most deprived ADI quintile, tooth loss rose from 10.5% to 20.2% (ratio 1.93), cognitive disability from 13.7% to 18.2%, and mental distress from 16.0% to 18.7%, while dental visits fell from 64.4% to 50.4%. Tooth loss was associated with cognitive disability (standardized β = 0.94, 95% CI 0.91-0.96); this was unchanged after adjustment for ADI (β = 0.96), and ADI had no independent association (β = -0.04, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.06). Conclusions. Oral disease, cognitive disability and mental distress tend to occur together in U.S. ZIP areas, and all rise steeply with neighborhood deprivation. These ecological, model-based findings fit a pathway from deprivation through oral disease to cognitive and mental health problems, but they cannot establish one. The pipeline is reproducible and could later be linked to individual-level microbiome cohorts.

title: EXPRESS: Effect of Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction in Elderly Patients Undergoing Abdominal Surgery: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
container-title: Journal of Investigative Medicine
bca12fc2693d7a7010accd52da43c3d9d57b0644.abstract: Objective: To systematically evaluate whether perioperative intravenous dexmedetomidine (DEX) reduces postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) in elderly patients undergoing abdominal surgery. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was performed using PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science from database inception to 15 April 2026. Eligible studies included patients aged ≥60 years undergoing abdominal surgery under general anesthesia and compared intraoperative DEX with placebo. The primary outcome was POCD incidence assessed by the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) or Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Secondary outcomes included MMSE scores, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores; interleukin-6 (IL-6) was summarized narratively because only two trials reported it. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 1 tool. Random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals were used irrespective of heterogeneity, and reporting followed the Framework for Approaches and Methods in Evidence Synthesis (FRAMES). Results: Twelve RCTs comprising 14 comparisons and 1,361 patients were included. DEX significantly reduced POCD on postoperative day 1 (risk ratio [RR]=0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.40–0.59; P<0.001; 95% prediction interval [PI]: 0.35–0.67) and day 3 (RR=0.29, 95% CI: 0.21–0.41; P<0.001; 95% PI: 0.18–0.47). MMSE scores were higher in the DEX group on day 1 (mean difference [MD]=2.75, 95% CI: 0.97–4.53; P=0.009) but not day 3 (MD=2.50, 95% CI: −1.74 to 6.75; P=0.16), with substantial heterogeneity (I 2 >98%). TNF-α concentrations were significantly lower with DEX (MD=−38.70 pg/mL, 95% CI: −76.44 to −0.96; P=0.047), but the very wide CI warrants caution. VAS scores were lower on days 1 and 2 but not day 3 (P=0.093). Subgroup analyses by cognitive assessment instrument, DEX loading dose, and surgical approach showed no significant effect modification (all P≥0.41). In the only trial reporting one-week data, MMSE scores remained higher with DEX on day 7 (MD=0.95, 95% CI: 0.31–1.59), whereas no trial reported POCD incidence beyond day 3. Exploratory publication-bias assessments showed no clear evidence of asymmetry. Conclusion: Perioperative intravenous DEX significantly reduces early POCD incidence on postoperative days 1 and 3 and attenuates the early postoperative TNF-α response in elderly patients undergoing abdominal surgery.

title: Understanding health behaviors and resilience during pandemics: a systematic review of ethical, cognitive, and existential dimensions
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
b086e88c52cf0b3b97bfdf5bff078cc5cb116b3e.abstract: Purpose Pandemic events such as HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 destabilize not only public health systems but also the philosophical and ethical frameworks through which individuals interpret illness. Health behavior influenced by contagion challenges definitions of identity, perceptions of truth, moral reasoning, and core bioethical principles, including autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice. This study employs a triadic lens, such as ontology, epistemology, and axiology, to examine how pandemic crises transform embodied experience, cognition, ethical response, and value-laden behavioral choices. From there, the consequences for health behavior are analyzed within both phenomenological and bioethical domains. Methods Using a phenomenological framework, the study draws on interdisciplinary data, including clinical case reports, psychosocial literature, and first-person narratives. Philosophical constructs from Husserl, Merleau-Ponty, and Carel inform the mapping of existential vulnerability, cognitive distortion, and value formation. Bioethical principles from Beauchamp and Childress guide the interpretation of moral tensions arising in pandemic behavior, while public health ethics frameworks (e.g., Kass) contextualize collective obligations. Psychiatric presentations during COVID-19 provide illustrative grounding for abstract principles. Motivations and frameworks for pandemic health behaviors are reported as outcomes. A review of 134 articles helped frame the cognitive and ethical terrain of pandemic prevention and dissemination. Results Pandemics cause overlapping disruptions across ontological, epistemological, axiological, and bioethical levels. Embodied identity becomes fragmented by diagnostic classification, social distancing, and existential uncertainty, raising tensions between autonomy and relationality. Cognitive processing is hindered by emotional stress, misinformation, and isolation, leading to distorted perceptions of truth and reduced rationality, which complicates beneficent and non-maleficent decision-making. Moral behavior reflects value-based tensions—altruism, denial, concealment, stigma—negotiated within shifting contexts of personal risk, communal obligation, and distributive justice. These patterns illustrate how existential dislocation, epistemic fragmentation, and moral ambiguity shape lived experience and ethical behavior during a pandemic. Conclusion Phenomenology offers vital insights into the human impact of pandemics by examining how relational, cognitive, and ethical dimensions shape illness experiences and health behaviors. Integrating bioethical principles clarifies why individuals struggle with autonomy, responsibility, and fairness during crises. To support recovery and coherence, public health governance must move beyond biomedical control toward emotionally attuned, ethically grounded care that emphasizes relational responsibility, moral imagination, and justice-oriented policy.

title: Uneven development of spatial cognitive subskills in primary school children and theoretical implications for differences in play behavior
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
d1f3823d470364a75b67ebe3af25fbb9b315f3d1.abstract: Outdoor play provides an important context for physical activity and social interaction among primary school children. During play, children with different spatial cognitive abilities often exhibit different behavioral patterns. However, existing research has often overlooked the asynchronous development of spatial cognitive subskills. Consequently, adults tend to use age as a uniform criterion for interpreting children’s play behavior, making it difficult to identify the needs of children with different ability profiles and potentially limiting their participation and quality of experience. This study assessed spatial referencing, the representation of three-dimensional spatial relations, and spatial composition in 462 children in Shenyang, China, using the Silver Drawing Test. Analysis of variance and chi-square tests were used to examine age and sex effects. The results revealed divergent age-related patterns across components of spatial referencing, progressive improvement in three-dimensional representation, and relatively stable spatial composition performance. Sex also interacted with task type. These findings suggest that children’s spatial cognition comprises multiple components that develop unevenly, rather than a single uniformly developing construct. The study offers a cognitive account of differences in children’s play behavior and has implications for play-based early education, curricula supporting the transition from preschool to primary school, and the design of play environments.

title: Olea europaea-derived interventions and cognitive outcomes across cognitive aging, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review of controlled clinical studies
container-title: Frontiers in Nutrition
30c2df4b8af8027e229951d69eb820382196fed0.abstract: Background Olive-derived nutritional exposures range from phenolic-rich extra-virgin olive oil (EVOO) to refined oils, olive-leaf preparations, and isolated bioactives, but these matrices are frequently treated as interchangeable despite major compositional and physiological differences. Objective To systematically evaluate controlled human evidence relating oral Olea europaea -derived interventions to cognitive outcomes across cognitive aging, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's disease (AD), while distinguishing direct efficacy trials from broader dietary-pattern interventions and trials in which olive oil served as an active comparator. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through 26 January 2026 and updated through 18 September 2026. Eligible reports contained a controlled human comparison involving an Olea-derived oral exposure or an olive-oil comparator and reported validated cognitive outcomes. Because the included studies represented different causal contrasts, intervention matrices, populations, instruments, and reporting structures, findings were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2 and GRADE, respectively. Results Thirteen reports representing 12 randomized intervention cohorts were included. Three reports directly tested an Olea-derived intervention, three evaluated EVOO within broader Mediterranean-diet interventions, and seven used olive oil primarily as the comparator for another bioactive intervention. Direct trials reported isolated, outcome-specific differences in ADAS-Cog, blood–brain barrier permeability, functional connectivity, and MMSE preservation, but these findings were inconsistent across global cognition, domain-specific measures, functional outcomes, and biological endpoints. Dietary-pattern findings could not isolate EVOO, whereas active-comparator trials estimated the effects of non-olive interventions relative to heterogeneous olive-oil controls. Three reports were judged at high risk of bias and the remaining ten raised some concerns; none was judged at low overall risk. Certainty was low to very low for most direct and dietary-pattern outcomes. Conclusions Olea europaea -derived interventions should not be interpreted as a single therapeutic entity. Controlled evidence is sparse, heterogeneous, and predominantly of low or very low certainty. Selected studies report outcome-specific signals consistent with cognitive preservation or biological target engagement, but these findings do not establish clinical efficacy for the prevention or treatment of cognitive decline, MCI, or AD. Compositionally defined, adequately powered trials with prespecified clinically meaningful cognitive and functional outcomes are required before clinical recommendations can be made.

title: Effects of cognitive behavioral therapy on psychological and physical outcomes in adults with rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
376500f67085567ca4ad286329357449b7895b27.abstract: Background Pain and functional limitations associated with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) can substantially impair patients’ psychological and physical well-being. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) may alleviate psychological and physical symptoms in patients with RA by modifying maladaptive cognitions and behaviors and promoting adaptive coping with the disease. However, the effect of CBT in RA patients has not been systematically established. Methods PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from database inception to July 9, 2026, for relevant studies. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were independently performed by two reviewers. Any discrepancies were resolved through discussion or adjudicated by a third reviewer. Meta-analyses were primarily implemented through random-effects models. Effect estimates were presented as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Twelve RCTs involving 1,538 participants with RA were incorporated. CBT was associated with lower levels of depression (SMD = −0.35, 95% CI: −0.55 to −0.14, low-certainty evidence), anxiety (SMD = −0.20, 95% CI: −0.32 to −0.08, moderate-certainty evidence), and fatigue (SMD = −0.44, 95% CI: −0.66 to −0.22, low-certainty evidence). At the 6-month follow-up, the pooled SMDs were −0.42 (95% CI, −0.63 to −0.20) for depression and −0.22 (95% CI, −0.43 to −0.01) for anxiety, based on six RCTs with available follow-up data. For sleep, the pooled estimate favored CBT, although this finding was based on only two studies and was supported by very-low-certainty evidence. No statistically significant between-group differences were noted for pain, physical function, or quality-of-life (QoL). Substantial heterogeneity was observed for depression and fatigue, and the 95% prediction intervals crossed the line of no effect for both outcomes. Exploratory subgroup analyses by CBT delivery format revealed no significant differences between subgroups. Conclusion The pooled estimates suggested that CBT may be associated with lower levels of fatigue, anxiety, and depression in patients with RA. However, substantial heterogeneity, prediction intervals crossing the line of no effect, and low certainty of evidence limit the reliability of these outcomes. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261470674 , CRD420261470674.

title: Thalamic subregional signatures of cognitive dysfunction in type 2 diabetes mellitus
container-title: Frontiers in Endocrinology
1b6087bdb89a8ad03a020578f87d3d092f64b895.abstract: Introduction/Objective Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with brain structural changes and cognitive decline, yet its impact on thalamic subregions remains unclear. This study aimed to identify volume changes in thalamic subregions in individuals with T2DM and to examine their associations with cognitive and diabetes-related clinical parameters. Methods In this cross-sectional case-control study, the thalamus was segmented into 25 subregions per hemisphere using FreeSurfer, and the volume of each subregion was calculated. Subregional volumes were compared between patients with T2DM and healthy controls (HC) using a generalized linear model (GLM), and partial correlation analysis was used to examine the associations between these volumetric measures and cognitive indicators. Results We identified five subregions of the thalamus that exhibited differences between the normal control and T2DM groups after correction for multiple comparisons. The left mediodorsal medial magnocellular (MDm) subregion showed volumetric reduction in the T2DM group, whereas four subregions, the right and left limitans/suprageniculate (L-Sg) and the right and left lateral pulvinar (PuL), exhibited volumetric enlargement in the T2DM group. Within the T2DM group, left PuL volume was negatively correlated with AVLT immediate recall (r = -0.35, P = 0.022) and right L-Sg volume was positively correlated with the Digit Span Test (DST) forward score (r = 0.31, P = 0.044); neither survived correction for multiple comparisons. Discussion In this cross-sectional, single-centre sample, T2DM was associated with nucleus-specific, bidirectional thalamic volume differences in the absence of a whole-thalamus difference: smaller left MDm and larger bilateral L-Sg and PuL volumes. Because only T1-weighted images were analysed, the biological substrate of the larger volumes cannot be determined here; neuroinflammation, oedema and gliosis are plausible but untested hypotheses. The imaging-cognition associations were modest and did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion Individuals with T2DM showed cross-sectional, region-specific differences in thalamic subnuclear volumes that were not detectable at the level of the whole thalamus. These are observational associations from a modest single-centre sample; their diagnostic, screening or predictive value is not established and requires longitudinal validation with clinically defined cognitive outcomes and independent replication.

title: Extracellular galectin-3 preferentially through CD44 and PD-1 binds activated T cells and marks memory-phenotype T cell subsets
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
74d68083621fa372cf09d8f724b756fe9e036766.abstract: Background Galectin-3 (Gal-3) is a multifunctional β-galactoside-binding lectin implicated in immune regulation, yet its association with T cell phenotypes under physiological and inflammatory conditions remains incompletely defined. Methods We investigated Gal-3 expression and binding on murine and human T cells across developmental stages, tissues, sex, genetic background, circadian time, and inflammatory disease settings. Results In mice, Gal-3-associated CD4 + and CD8 + T cells were dynamically regulated by age, anatomical location, strain, sex, and circadian rhythm. Gal-3 + T cells displayed increased activation markers, enhanced TCR-associated signaling molecules, elevated cytolytic mediators, increased proliferation, and greater apoptosis. Gal-3 + T cells were enriched within central and effector memory compartments and expressed higher levels of co-inhibitory receptors, including PD-1, with ImageStream analysis confirming Gal-3 co-expressed with PD-1. Recombinant Gal-3 preferentially bound activated, but not resting T cells, and associated with CD44 and CD3, suggesting activation-dependent acquisition of extracellular Gal-3. Re-analysis of human thymocyte and Long COVID single-cell RNA-seq datasets further supported an association between LGALS3 expression and activated/exhausted T cell states. Finally, intracellular staining indicated that T cells are unlikely to be a major source of Gal-3. Conclusion Our findings identify Gal-3 as a context-dependent marker and potential regulator of activated, antigen-experienced T cells, which promotes T cell apoptosis.

title: Memory Services for People With Down Syndrome: A Scoping Review Exploring Models of Care and Access
container-title: Journal of Policy and Practice in Intellectual Disabilities
81b3451fd64af86be5a06a2695403a2219239118.abstract: ABSTRACT More than 95% of people with Down syndrome develop Alzheimer's disease (AD), with a median age of diagnosis of approximately 54 years. However, there is a significant gap in guidance regarding the design of effective memory services and tailored diagnostic pathways. This scoping review aimed to identify and describe existing memory service models and dementia diagnostic pathways for adults with Down syndrome. It was conducted according to the Joanna Briggs Institute's updated methodological guidance for scoping reviews. Four databases (Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE + EMBASE Classic, Ovid PsycINFO and EBSCO CINAHL Plus) were searched using three key concepts: Alzheimer's disease, Down syndrome and memory services. All primary study types published between January 2005 and September 2026 were considered for inclusion. Seventeen studies met the inclusion criteria comprising 12 service evaluations, two prospective cohort studies, one observational study, and two qualitative studies. Thirteen studies were conducted in the United Kingdom. Key service components were the use of validated cognitive assessment tools, structured screening pathways, and multidisciplinary team involvement. This scoping review indicates limited literature describing dedicated memory services and dementia diagnostic pathways for people with Down syndrome. Existing services highlight several key features including multidisciplinary team involvement, baseline and prospective cognitive screening, and the longitudinal use of validated screening tools. Further research, including participatory research, is needed to inform the development and implementation of evidence‐based memory service models for this population.

title: Development of Elective Flexibility and Related Cognitive Functions Across Three Cultures
container-title: Developmental Science
913e607c56d2df833d3aee953368cf2bb971d97e.abstract: ABSTRACT Elective flexibility, the ability to switch between working strategies adaptively, is critical for decision‐making in complex environments. Here we experimentally assessed elective flexibility alongside three related cognitive measures short‐term memory, inhibition, and responsive flexibility–in 325 children and adults (ages 4–81‐years) from three cultures. Elective flexibility performance improved with age for Germans and, to some extent, for Congolese BaYaka and Bandongo participants. Under stable conditions, younger German children were more explorative than older children and adolescents. Next, using interviews with 62 adults from these three cultural groups we found evidence that cultural variation in daily exposure to unpredictable variability corresponded with more elective switching whereas exposure to harshness corresponded with less. By combining richly contextualized cross‐cultural and developmental data with multiple cognitive tests and computational models, this research uniquely contributes to our understanding of the development of children's flexible decision‐making skillsets.

title: Early Adversity and Stressor–Cognitive Style Transactions: A 7-Year Longitudinal Study From Adolescence to Young Adulthood
container-title: Clinical Psychological Science
6cbd0ef4c29b87be0c054291158b3fe6a810cdd0.abstract: Cognitive styles are often viewed as stable vulnerabilities, yet it is unclear whether stressors prospectively shape these styles in adolescence. In this study, we examined time-lagged within-person associations between stressors and cognitive styles, reverse effects, and moderation by early adversity. Data came from 470 U.S. adolescents followed annually for 7 years. Multilevel models separated within-person variance from between-person variance and adjusted for prior outcomes. There was little evidence for general socialization or selection effects: Within-person changes in stressors did not predict later cognitive styles, and cognitive styles did not predict later stressors. Early adversity, however, moderated several associations. Adolescents without adversity showed slightly less negative cognitive styles following higher stressors, whereas higher adversity levels were associated with smaller reductions or increases in negative cognitive styles. Effects were most pronounced for childhood adversity and noninterpersonal stressors. Cognitive-style change may emerge selectively among adolescents with early adversity who encounter specific stressors.

title: High-frequency conductivity was negatively associated with myelin water fraction in the brain of cognitive impairments
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
ebae3136b6e886e8ffb3226972ff24219ce8af7f.abstract: Background Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) are associated with cognitive decline and brain changes, including gray and white matter atrophy. High-frequency conductivity (HFC) and myelin water fraction (MWF) serve as potential biomarkers for these neurological changes. Purpose To evaluate the relationship between HFC and myelin-related metrics (MWF and white matter volume (WMV)) in the context of cognitive decline. Materials and methods This cross-sectional prospective study included 170 participants who were differentially diagnosed as 42 cognitively unimpaired (CU) older participants, 84 with amnestic MCI, and 44 with clinically diagnosed probable AD of mild to moderate severity. MRI techniques were used to measure HFC, MWF, and WMV across defined regions of interest that were (1) voxels with a WMV value greater than 1% and an MWF value greater than 1% (whole brain), (2) the hippocampus, (3) the insula, and (4) the thalamus in each participant. Statistical methods included correlations between these indices and clinical measures, multiple regression analyses of HFC with other MRI indices, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results The robust multiple regression analyses showed that HFC was negatively associated with MWF in the whole-brain, hippocampal, and insular ROIs. Associations between HFC and WMV were region-specific, with a negative association in the whole-brain ROI and a positive association in the insula. Probable AD showed higher HFC in the whole-brain, hippocampal, and thalamic ROIs, while group differences in MWF and WMV were region-specific. Conclusion Lower apparent MWF was associated with higher HFC, suggesting a relationship between tissue microstructural alterations and conductivity. Further research is needed to validate these findings in diverse populations.

title: Beyond cognitive slowing: potential evidence for specific lexical-semantic impairment in multiple sclerosis
container-title: Frontiers in Behavioral Neuroscience
475d6f68db58352444f205f8dc957da9aad800a1.abstract: Background Expressive language difficulties are frequently reported by people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), yet they often go undetected during routine neuropsychological assessments. This study examined expressive language performance in MS group as compared to healthy controls (HC), focusing on lexical access and semantic processing, to determine whether these deficits stem from generalized cognitive slowing or reflect an independent lexical-semantic impairment. Methods Performance level and reaction times (RT) were evaluated in both groups across specialized naming and semantic judgment tasks using the Cambridge Language Battery. Robust regression models were conducted to assess the predictive value of information processing speed (IPS), working memory (WM) and verbal fluency. Results Both groups showed high levels of accuracy, but PwMS had significantly longer reaction times across all tasks with large and consistent effect sizes. Robust regression analyses indicated a clear dissociation between the domains. General cognitive factors, particularly baseline IPS, explained a substantial proportion of variance (22% to 51%) in reaction times, largely reducing between-group RT differences after adjustment in all tasks. Accuracy in the Synonym Judgement Task was primarily related to semantic and phonemic fluency and, when their influence statistically accounted for, between-group differences were largely reduced. Conversely, even the best combination of these cognitive predictors explained less than 10% of the variance in accuracy for the naming tasks, where group differences remained largely unchanged. Discussion These findings demonstrate a robust dissociation between accuracy and speed in PwMS. While general cognitive slowing drives delayed responding, it fails to account for reduced accuracy on demanding language tasks, suggesting that subtle lexical-semantic dysfunction represents a partially independent feature of MS rather than a simple consequence of generalized cognitive slowing.

title: Understanding mathematics anxiety and its impact on cognitive effort in second-grade children: a pupillometry investigation
container-title: Frontiers in Education
f0f7047586d3e417d59781490ce030ca0582876e.abstract: Introduction Many individuals struggle with mathematics, and mathematics anxiety (MA) is associated with poor mathematics performance. The reasons for this association are unclear, but one explanation is that MA reduces the working memory capacity available for problem solving. Because changes in pupil diameter index cognitive effort, this study used pupillometry to examine whether MA is related to cognitive effort in second-grade children. Methods Ninety-eight second-grade pupils in Norway solved easy and hard addition problems while their pupil diameter was recorded with an eye tracker. Arithmetic competence, working memory, and general intelligence were measured as control variables, and the data were analysed with linear mixed models. Results Hard problems elicited more cognitive effort than easy problems. MA moderated this effect: children with higher MA showed a smaller increase in cognitive effort with increasing problem difficulty, even after controlling for arithmetic competence, working memory, and general intelligence. When only correctly solved trials were analysed, the interaction was no longer significant, but higher MA was associated with lower overall cognitive effort. Discussion Children with higher MA did not show the heightened effort predicted by working memory interference accounts; the pattern may instead reflect reduced task engagement or avoidance. Because pupil diameter change indexes overall psychophysiological effort, the precise cognitive and affective mechanisms remain unclear.

title: Metabolic Memory in Oral Inflammation
container-title: Journal of Dental Research
1b21aac914ae396e2dff5c4ed757cda3e94f1e15.abstract: The global rise in metabolic diseases has increased the severity and therapeutic complexity of oral inflammatory disorders. Persistent inflammation driven by metabolic memory presents a central pathological mechanism. Even after metabolic parameters are normalized, abnormal gene expression can persist, leading to prolonged disease progression and recurrent episodes. In the oral cavity, metabolic memory is most clearly evident in periodontitis and impaired wound healing, where sustained immune dysregulation and tissue destruction remain after hyperglycemia or hyperlipidemia has been corrected. Epigenetic reprogramming presents a key molecular mechanism of metabolic memory, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and expression of noncoding RNAs. The epigenetic alterations collectively reprogram immune cell function, driving the dysregulation of innate and adaptive immunity while influencing the fate of oral stromal cells and epithelial cells. Prolonged inflammation contributes to an altered host–microbiota interaction, reinforcing disease persistence and treatment resistance. Metabolic disorders induce coordinated epigenetic changes that can be grouped into permissive and repressive events affecting gene transcription. Permissive events include increased histone acetylation, enrichment of activating histone methylation marks (e.g., H3K4me3), and DNA demethylation at inflammatory gene loci. These modifications promote an open chromatin structure to enhance transcription factor access. Repressive events include increased DNA methylation and enrichment of repressive histone methylation marks (e.g., H3K9me3). DNA methylation typically occurs in promoter regions of genes, and repressive histone changes lead to the formation of compact chromatin, both of which reduce transcriptional activity. Noncoding RNAs generally decrease target messenger RNA stability or inhibit translation further, reinforcing a repressive effect. The combined effect of these modifications is a shift in protein expression that reinforces chronic inflammatory signaling in abnormal metabolic conditions. This review comprehensively summarizes the epigenetic mechanisms by which metabolic memory sustains oral inflammation at molecular, cellular, and tissue levels, as well as potential preventive and therapeutic interventions.

title: The impact of instructional presentation modalities on false memory susceptibility among high school learners
container-title: Frontiers in Education
bd56f27bb18526810d16eb7da2618ebb60e8b2d8.abstract: The present investigation examined the impact of instructional presentation modalities (written text, auditory lecture, and multimedia presentation) on false memory susceptibility among high school learners, while exploring the moderating roles of working memory capacity and prior domain knowledge. Employing a 3 × 2 mixed factorial design, the final analytical sample comprised 165 female 11th-grade students randomly allocated across three experimental conditions ( n = 55 per group). The Deese-Roediger-McDermott (DRM) paradigm was adapted to educationally relevant content, and stimulus exposure was rigorously controlled using PsychoPy. Following a computerized distractor task, participants completed a randomized recognition test. Data were analyzed using Signal Detection Theory metrics: sensitivity ( d ʹ) and response criterion ( C ). A one-way ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of modality on sensitivity and criterion. Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons indicated that the auditory lecture condition yielded lower sensitivity and a more liberal response bias compared to both written text and multimedia conditions, which did not significantly differ from each other. Supplementary ANCOVAs indicated that working memory capacity and prior domain knowledge were significant covariates predicting memory discriminability. The sample comprised female 11th-grade students; findings are therefore restricted to this population. The fixed- versus self-paced confound is also acknowledged. The study concludes that the transient nature of spoken information depletes working memory resources, driving reliance on gist-based processing and exacerbating false recognition. Actionable pedagogical recommendations emphasize supplementing verbal discourse with external textual anchors to safeguard knowledge veridicality.

title: Constructing AI safety: a comparative cognitive-discursive analysis of corporate and regulatory discourses
container-title: Frontiers in Communication
cf4f06bf12ca837506c7011048321337a39f13df.abstract: Background The global proliferation of generative artificial intelligence has transformed safety governance into a highly contested sociopolitical battleground, yet existing discourse studies frequently under-theorize the micro-cognitive mechanisms of epistemic reality construction within AI safety standardization. Objective To investigate how corporate and regulatory actors engineer divergent cognitive realities of AI safety through specific micro-grammatical choices. Methods We proposed an integrated Cognitive-Critical Discourse Analysis framework by synthesizing Langacker's cognitive conception of reality with Fairclough's three-dimensional model, and applied it to a comparative corpus of corporate safety frameworks and regulatory policy documents. Results Tech enterprises engineer a reality of techno-pragmatic containment via active voice, high-certainty evidentiality, and immediate projection to naturalize self-regulation. Conversely, regulatory bodies construct a reality of socio-structural vulnerability using distal modals, passive constructions, and deontic mandates to legitimize state-enforced compliance. Conclusions Linguistic normalization is actively deployed to facilitate or contest corporate epistemic hegemony in AI governance. These findings provide empirical references for revising regulatory discourse and enhancing public media literacy against algorithmic exceptionalism.

title: An Italian auditory gender Stroop walking task: feasibility and preliminary cognitive-motor performance profiling in neurological populations
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
ad04765d62a08b5b83c2df9ebfc59475cc9dadfc.abstract: Introduction Stroop-based paradigms are widely used to probe inhibitory control during locomotion, although auditory Stroop walking tasks remain underexplored in neurological populations. This study introduced an Italian auditory adaptation of the Gender Stroop task and provided a preliminary methodological evaluation of its feasibility and of multidimensional gait, accuracy and verbal-timing information obtained during walking. Methods Forty participants were included: 24 individuals with neurological conditions (multiple sclerosis, n = 8; Parkinson’s disease, n = 8; stroke, n = 8) and 16 controls. Spatiotemporal gait parameters were recorded using a wearable inertial sensor, while Stroop accuracy, verbal response timing, feasibility and acceptability were also assessed. Results Hierarchical clustering of 15 standardized gait variables identified a higher-performance profile ( n = 22) and a low-performance profile ( n = 18), mainly characterized by differences in walking velocity, cadence, and gait cycle duration across walking conditions. In the primary age- and sex-adjusted analysis, clinical status was associated with lower-performance profile membership (OR = 11.15, 95% CI: 1.76–70.68, p = 0.008). The association was no longer statistically significant in the age-matched analysis (Fisher’s exact p = 0.106), while agreement with the full-sample profile assignments remained high. Repeated subsampling indicated moderate cluster stability. Condition-related gait effects and cognitive-verbal changes did not show robust clinical-control differences after FDR correction, indicating that the gait profiles primarily reflected general locomotor performance rather than Stroop-specific cognitive-motor interference. The paradigm was well tolerated, with no adverse events. Discussion Overall, the Italian auditory Gender Stroop walking task was feasible and allowed concurrent assessment of gait and cognitive-verbal performance during a structured cognitive-motor task. Larger, age-balanced and independent samples are required to establish the reproducibility of the gait-performance structure and determine the additional contribution of Stroop accuracy and verbal-timing measures beyond general locomotor performance.

title: Octreotide treatment improves multiple domains of cognitive performance in aged beagle dogs
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
d12948a7c47cee6fd284ff008b073c092dbc6bf2.abstract: Aging in dogs is accompanied by progressive cognitive decline and neuropathological changes that parallel key features of human brain aging and dementia, making canines a highly valuable naturally occurring model for studying aging and neurodegenerative disease. Across species, reduced growth hormone/insulin-like growth factor-1 (GH/IGF-1) signaling is associated with extended lifespan and preserved late-life cognition, whereas chronically elevated somatotropic activity is linked to deficits in memory, attention, and executive function. The effects of pharmacologic GH/IGF-1 suppression on cognition in naturally aging animal models remain unclear. We investigated whether attenuation of IGF-1 signaling with the long-acting somatostatin analog octreotide improves cognitive performance in aged dogs. Twenty-eight aged beagle dogs (7–15 years) experienced in neuropsychological testing were enrolled in a randomized, placebo-controlled study. After a 28-day baseline, dogs received either long-acting octreotide (Sandostatin LAR, 10 mg, i.m.) or placebo, followed by a wash-in interval and 28 days of post-treatment testing. A validated cognitive battery assessed executive function and cognitive flexibility (discrimination reversal), selective attention (variable oddity), and visuospatial working memory (variable delayed non-matching to position). Treated dogs demonstrated significantly improved performance relative to placebo across the three behavioral paradigms with the primary effect being reductions in response latency and task engagement. Pharmacologic IGF-1 suppression with octreotide improves cognitive response efficiency and engagement in aged dogs, particularly in executive and attentional domains. These results support a functional role for somatotropic signaling in late-life cognition and highlight the aged canine as a valuable translational model for geroscience-based interventions targeting age-related cognitive decline.

title: Influence of health communication literacy on student e-cigarette use attitudes in higher education
container-title: Global Knowledge, Memory and Communication
a63486527607e7de9a3e85800923cd440128a7f8.abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyse the influence of health communication literacy on e-cigarette use among university students. Design/methodology/approach The quantitative approach was chosen by the researcher as a research method because it helps to understand based on experience to solve problems related to the influence of health communication literacy on e-cigarette use attitudes in higher education. Data processing in this study used a simple linear regression analysis model. Findings The findings of this study indicate that health literacy is a determining factor for success and progress in the field of individual health. This is because students’ understanding of health communication literacy can improve their knowledge. Unfortunately, the barriers to achieving an adequate level of health literacy depend on the selection of information resources used. Research limitations/implications This study has limitations in research methods. Researchers have not been able to conduct in-depth analyses related to the impact felt by e-cigarette smokers. Given the age of college students still experience vulnerability in starting and continuing e-cigarettes. Thus, they need to be instructed and warned. Practical implications This research has implications for the benefits of health communication for students in higher education related to e-cigarettes. Thus, it can be a basis for academics to be able to develop health communication strategies as a preventive measure for the younger generation in minimising the use of e-cigarettes. Originality/value Generally, previous studies discuss the use of e-cigarettes as an alternative to drug therapy but there are minimal studies that discuss the influence of health communication literacy on e-cigarette use. Moreover, health communication is generally associated with patients and diseases.

title: Sex differences in parietal alpha power during sustained attention are related to conflict monitoring performance in mild cognitive impairment
container-title: Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease
95ba4742c291670708304663b0079284c4ac00c0.abstract: Background Sex differences in cognition among individuals with dementias and prodromal stages such as amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) manifest in variations in severity and prevalence, but underlying brain activity patterns remain unclear. This study is a secondary endpoint study of the Cogmax project. Objective We examined sex differences in parietal alpha power during an attention task (Simple Vigilance Task, SVT) and its association with conflict monitoring (Stroop Color-Word Test Part 3, T score) in individuals with aMCI. Methods The SVT served as the EEG recording condition because of its low cognitive demands and visually driven structure, while the Stroop task provided an independent neuropsychological measure of conflict monitoring. Seventy-seven participants (23 females; 54 males) were included. We analyzed average power spectral density (PSD) across occipital and parietal electrodes (O1-Pz-O2-P7-P8) using multitaper Fourier transform. Normalized alpha power was calculated as integrated 7–11 Hz relative to total 0.1–40 Hz PSD. Results All participants showed high accuracy on the SVT, indicating stable attentional engagement. Covariate-adjusted permutation tests, robust to unbalanced sample sizes, showed that females exhibited higher parietal alpha power and higher Stroop Part 3 T-scores than males. However, when Stroop performance was included as a covariate, the sex difference in alpha power became nonsignificant. A positive correlation between Stroop 3 scores and parietal alpha power was observed in females but not in males, suggesting a sex-specific relationship. Conclusions Parietal alpha activity may be associated with conflict monitoring performance in aMCI, particularly among females, providing evidence for sex-related neural differences in aMCI.

title: A generative network model reveals hierarchical structural memory guiding post-mitotic 3D genome inheritance
5490746647f0a618ac3cd8953937e2e8625e6dbf.abstract: Abstract How three-dimensional (3D) genome organization is reestablished after mitosis to preserve gene regulatory programs and cell identity remains unresolved. We asked whether mitotic chromosome architecture contributes to cellular memory by preserving structural information while maintaining the flexibility required for cellular adaptation. Here we introduce HiCONA, a generative Bayesian framework that infers hierarchical genome organization and quantifies the structural contribution of individual interactions through an Entropy Impact Score. HiCONA resolves genome organization across multiple scales, revealing structure-defining interaction patterns underlying chromatin architecture, independently of experimental modality. We identify structurally impactful chromatin interactions retained during mitosis delineating distinct trajectories of post-mitotic genome reassembly. These mitotically preserved interactions are enriched for active, transcriptionally competent regulatory elements, consistent with a cis-encoded architectural memory subsequently remodeled by trans-acting regulators. Together, our findings suggest that molecular information retained on mitotic chromosomes guides structural trajectories, providing an architectural basis for epigenetic memory and post-mitotic genome inheritance.

title: Mimicry and memory: William Wells Brown reads Le Guide de l’Étranger
container-title: French Cultural Studies
2357ea8259a1f91c814227ff8f8c51b98e14a1b3.abstract: This article explores William Wells Brown’s Parisian travelogue to examine how nineteenth-century Black American tourists experienced and interpreted the capital through the mediating form of the popular guidebook form known as le guide de l’étranger . Brown, guide in hand, positions himself within Parisian spaces and embarks on a complex hermeneutics that vacillates between his lived experiences, the guidebook’s representations, and his perspective as a fugitive slave. Reading Brown’s travelogue, Three Years in Europe; or, Places I Have Seen and People I Have Met , alongside popular guides, this study shows how Brown adopts guide-like narrative forms—reproducing facts, dimensions, and itineraries—to claim agency as an interpreter of Paris and to enact a “fugitive tourism” that both mimics and contests imperial narratives. By tracing his encounters with the city’s monuments and his insistence on bodily emplacement within the spaces of memory, the article argues that Brown transforms the media of tourism into an act of witnessing in the service of an abolitionist aesthetics.

title: Testing working memory benefits long-term memory only when paired with re-exposure
8ac05c094e482e7125d00f32e43aa58ca40504b1.abstract: Testing long-term memory (LTM) is well known to enhance subsequent retention beyond mere re-exposure effects. Recent evidence suggests that testing during working memory (WM) also boosts LTM performance. However, it remains unclear whether these WM testing benefits are a consequence of retrieval or reflect increased familiarity due to re-exposure. In this preregistered study, we aimed to distinguish between these two. Participants memorized four images in their corresponding locations for a subsequent WM test. During this test, an image was presented in one of the memory locations, and participants had to determine whether it matched the memory (retrieval and re-exposure) or not (retrieval but no re-exposure). In an additional color-task condition, the image was presented in a red or green frame, but now participants simply determined the frame color (re-exposure only). Finally, in a no-test condition, no test was presented at all (neither retrieval nor re-exposure). Following an interruption, participants then completed a surprise LTM test involving a two-alternative forced-choice test between one old and one new image. LTM accuracy was higher for an item from the match condition than from the color-task condition, indicating a benefit of WM testing beyond re-exposure. Re-exposure alone also enhanced performance compared to no test. However, LTM performance in the non-matching test condition was no better than the no-test condition, suggesting that testing without re-exposure did not enhance LTM. Together, these findings suggest that while re-exposure benefits retention by itself, testing in WM boosts LTM only when paired with re-exposure to the target item.
