title: Controlling AI Self-Evolution: Balancing Usefulness, Safety, And Human Oversight
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
7862a25fd6d8f9eed5d4a3d28f3fbe9665a87458.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly capable of adapting to new information, improving task performance, modifying operational strategies, and assisting in the development of more advanced computational systems. These capabilities provide significant opportunities for innovation, productivity, scientific discovery, and decision support. However, they also raise concerns regarding the extent to which AI systems should be permitted to change their own behaviour, expand their operational capabilities, or influence the processes through which they are evaluated and controlled. Unrestricted or inadequately supervised adaptation may introduce unintended consequences, including specification gaming, reward manipulation, degradation of previously acquired knowledge, unexpected changes in system behaviour, and reduced human control. The present study examines how AI self-evolution can be controlled without unnecessarily restricting its usefulness. The study adopts a qualitative secondary-research methodology based on published scholarly literature, established AI safety research, technical documentation, international governance principles, and regulatory frameworks. Existing approaches are compared across six dimensions: capability development, human oversight, objective alignment, operational restrictions, accountability, and continuous monitoring. The literature indicates that AI safety cannot be achieved through a single technical intervention or a one-time evaluation. Instead, effective governance requires coordinated controls throughout the AI lifecycle, including development, testing, deployment, adaptation, monitoring, and retirement. Human oversight mechanisms, corrigibility, risk-based evaluation, controlled access to tools, documented change management, and independent assessment provide complementary safeguards. Nevertheless, existing approaches present limitations. Excessive restrictions may prevent beneficial adaptation, while superficial human supervision, incomplete documentation, and reliance on benchmark performance may fail to identify emerging risks. The study therefore proposes a conceptual governance approach based on bounded self-evolution, in which routine and reversible improvements may proceed within predefined limits, while significant changes require additional evaluation and explicit authorization. The proposed approach also emphasizes independent monitoring, rollback capabilities, incident reporting, and clear assignment of responsibility. The study concludes that preserving AI usefulness and maintaining human control should be treated as complementary objectives rather than competing priorities. Although the proposed approach synthesizes existing methods rather than experimentally validating a new technical system, it offers a structured basis for future research into responsible AI adaptation, organizational governance, and the long-term management of increasingly autonomous systems.</jats:p>

title: A Study of Prompt Engineering Techniques for Improving Generative AI Performance
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
b2c79a43653c0775ed92d8beb30ade0adbc160eb.abstract: <jats:p>Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has transformed the way users create content, retrieve information, write code and solve problems. The quality of outputs produced by Generative AI systems depends not only on the underlying model but also on the instructions supplied by users. Prompt engineering is the process of designing, structuring and refining inputs to guide an AI model towards relevant, accurate and useful responses. The present study examines the role of prompt engineering techniques in improving the performance of Generative AI systems, with particular attention to Zero-Shot Prompting, One-Shot and Few-Shot Prompting, Role-Based Prompting, Contextual Prompting and Chain-of-Thought Prompting. The study adopts a descriptive research design and is qualitative in nature, relying on secondary data collected from academic research papers, conference proceedings and published surveys. The literature indicates that carefully structured prompts can improve task alignment, response relevance, reasoning performance and output consistency. However, prompt effectiveness varies according to the task, model, context and evaluation method. The study also identifies limitations such as hallucinations, sensitivity to wording, prompt injection risks, bias and the absence of universally effective prompt templates. It concludes that prompt engineering is an important method for obtaining more reliable results from Generative AI, but should be combined with verification, clear evaluation criteria and responsible AI practices.</jats:p>

f8b52f591df875ac1c2019dd4f4b18ce9752e66d.abstract: <jats:p>Purpose This study aimed to examine AI digital competency and the perceived need for AI utilization education among physical therapy students and to analyze the relationship between the two variables. Methods This crosssectional correlational survey was conducted with 232 physical therapy students at S University using an online survey. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analysis. Results The mean score for AI digital competency was 3.48±0.57, with communication and collaboration showing the highest score at 3.84±0.62 and digital content creation showing the lowest score at 3.03±0.71. The mean score for the perceived need for AI utilization education was 3.91±0.71. Conclusion These results suggest the need for systematic educational support to help physical therapy students effectively use AI in majorrelated learning and clinical problemsolving.</jats:p>

title: HYBRID FEDERATED LEARNING ARCHITECTURE FOR PRIVACY-PRESERVING AI IN GREEN HYDROGEN ENERGY SYSTEMS: A REVIEW
container-title: International Journal of African Sustainable Development Research
7658450ec240730ecffa038cc235234571c1d5f6.abstract: <jats:p>The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, and smart grids into green hydrogen energy systems creates opportunities for improved energy forecasting, electrolyzer optimization, predictive maintenance, and operational efficiency. However, the interconnected nature of these infrastructures introduces significant challenges relating to data privacy, cybersecurity, commercial confidentiality, and organizational compliance. This review examines the potential of a hybrid federated learning architecture for privacy-preserving AI in green hydrogen energy systems. Drawing on literature concerning green hydrogen technologies, federated learning, differential privacy, blockchain-enabled security, Privacy Calculus Theory, and the Selective Organizational Information Privacy and Security Violations Model (SOIPSV), the review synthesizes existing approaches and identifies unresolved technical and governance challenges. It conceptualizes a six-layer architecture comprising edge and local processing, privacy calculus, federated learning, secure aggregation, organizational governance, and global intelligence. The proposed architecture integrates privacy-risk and benefit assessment, decentralized model training, cryptographic protection, and policy-oriented accountability to support collaborative intelligence across distributed hydrogen production facilities and smart grid networks. The framework remains conceptual and has not undergone empirical validation, simulation benchmarking, or real-world deployment. Its predictive performance, computational overhead, privacy guarantees, and scalability remain unverified. The review identifies future research priorities, including formal privacy accounting, adversarial testing, standardized benchmarks, governance operationalization, and pilot implementation. This synthesis provides a foundation for developing and evaluating trustworthy, privacy-aware AI architectures for secure and sustainable green hydrogen infrastructure.</jats:p>

title: Nurses’ Attitudes and Experiences With Generative AI in Clinical Practice: Qualitative Systematic Review
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
86fd6e8d39ee5d7b8d9f5992ff17e4580e39e69d.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The rapid advancement of generative AI (GenAI) holds transformative potential for clinical nursing practice, yet its integration also brings significant risks and uncertainties. Despite growing discourse on AI in health care, frontline nurses’ firsthand experiences, perceptions, and practical needs regarding GenAI remain largely under-synthesized in the existing literature.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This systematic review aimed to synthesize qualitative evidence to clarify the core themes related to clinical nurses’ perceptions, experiences, obstacles, and requirements when using GenAI in real-world clinical settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic search was conducted across 10 electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, VIP Information, SinoMed, and Wanfang) for records published between January 2018 and June 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative and mixed methods studies involving registered nurses that explored their perceptions and experiences of GenAI in clinical practice. Two independent reviewers (MMW and CYZ) performed study selection, quality appraisal, and data extraction, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research. Extracted data encompassed study characteristics, participant demographics, and GenAI-related contextual factors. Data synthesis followed Thomas and Harden’s 3-phase thematic synthesis: initial inductive coding generated descriptive themes, which were subsequently integrated with the Technology Acceptance Model for Artificial Intelligence in Nursing (TAM-AIN) framework to develop higher-order analytical themes. Certainty in the evidence was evaluated using the GRADE-CERQual (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation-Confidence in the Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of the 4350 initially identified records, 13 studies from 6 countries (China: n=6; Saudi Arabia: n=3; United States, Singapore, Australia, and South Korea: n=1 each) met the inclusion criteria, encompassing qualitative data from 234 registered nurses. Three main themes emerged: patterns of nurses’ engagement with GenAI (ranging from passive observation to proactive integration), multidimensional perceived threats to adoption (functional, professional, and accountability-related), and the moderating role of organizational readiness, which influenced whether these threats hindered or facilitated GenAI uptake in practice. The GRADE-CERQual assessment showed moderate to high confidence in all findings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Nurses’ engagement with GenAI ranges from passive observation to proactive integration, accompanied by legitimate concerns about functional reliability, professional role displacement, and accountability ambiguity. The moderating role of organizational readiness further highlights that training, tool optimization, and institutional governance remain critical yet often unmet. These findings necessitate coordinated efforts across workforce development, technological design, and regulatory frameworks. Future research should prioritize the development of clinically validated, context-aware GenAI systems that incorporate human-in-the-loop oversight, ensuring that efficiency gains do not compromise the delivery of compassionate, person-centered care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: A dual-domain shapelet-guided conditional generative framework for imbalanced bearing fault diagnosis
container-title: Engineering Research Express
48dd31af472500c232f66eee2c6d19a8f53f14c5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In bearing fault diagnosis, the scarcity of fault samples creates severe class imbalance and makes minority fault distributions difficult to learn reliably. Existing data-level methods mainly rely on interpolation, neighborhood relationships, or distribution modeling strategies to synthesize minority samples, which may fail to preserve complex temporal structures and fault-related local patterns. Although GAN-based methods provide flexible distribution modeling capabilities, their conditioning mechanisms often lack explicit representation of class-discriminative local patterns across temporal and spectral domains. To address these limitations, we propose ShapeGAN, a dual-domain shapelet-guided conditional generative framework for minority fault sample augmentation. Specifically, ShapeGAN first discovers class-specific temporal shapelets from minority and majority samples and derives the spectral representation of each retained segment using the discrete Fourier transform (DFT). A Conditional Mixing Module samples these paired representations, which are integrated by a bidirectional cross-attention generator. Training then proceeds from single-shapelet to multi-shapelet conditioning through the proposed Two-Stage Mixed Training strategy. Experiments on 24 imbalanced bearing fault scenarios show that ShapeGAN achieves the highest average Macro-F1 and G-Mean with the MLP classifier, while its average AUC remains comparable to that of the strongest baseline. With LSTM and ResNet, ShapeGAN achieves the best average performance across all three metrics, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed augmentation method across different downstream classifier architectures.</jats:p>

title: Epistemic Risks and a Framework for Critical Generative AI‐Mediated Reading
container-title: Reading Research Quarterly
2e0c7730eff79c1ef8dddf722e65bcc22ac3b8bf.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to explain, summarize, and generate information, yet these activities are rarely framed as reading practices. This conceptual paper examines GenAI‐mediated reading, in which readers engage with responses generated by large language models (LLM) during inquiry and knowledge construction. GenAI frequently presents fluent and synthesized responses whose evidentiary basis, source relations, assumptions, and limitations may remain opaque. This paper identifies three epistemic risks: (a) fluent language may be misrecognized as truth, (b) algorithmic authority may encourage the outsourcing of epistemic judgment, and (c) responsive generation may weaken readers' critical monitoring through confirmation, sycophancy, or automation bias. To address these risks, the paper brings together critical reading and critical literacy and proposes the Critical Generative AI‐mediated Reading (CritGAIR) framework. The framework includes three recursive dimensions: (a) reading the response, (b) reading the system, and (c) reading the self. These dimensions direct attention to evaluating claims, evidence, and source credibility; interrogating authority, sociotechnical conditions, representations, and power; and reflecting on readers' prompts, trust, and uptake, respectively. Guiding questions and a hypothetical reading example illustrate how scrutiny can be calibrated to task purpose and consequences of error. The paper outlines educational applications and directions for investigating readers' evaluative processes, judgment quality, and the effort required for critical engagement.</jats:p>

title: Effect of Application-Based Learning Using Generative Artificial Intelligence on Information Literacy of First-Year Medical Students in Yunnan Province
container-title: Interdisciplinary Academic and Research Journal
ae5fca122b81c702af4a0f5001bbeece73180306.abstract:
<jats:p>Background and Aims: This experimental research aimed to 1) compare students’ information literacy before and after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence, 2) compare students’ information literacy after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence with the determined criterion set at 70%, and 3) assess students’ satisfaction after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence.
Methodology: The research instruments were lesson plans, students’ information literacy test, and a satisfaction questionnaire. The appropriateness of the lesson plans overall was at a very high level (M=4.62, SD=0.49). The students’ information literacy test had an IOC between 0.67–1.00, item difficulty (p=0.43-0.60), item discrimination (r=0.25-0.50), and KR20 equal to 0.76. The students’ satisfaction questionnaire had an IOC between 0.67 and 1.00 and a reliability index of 0.85. The statistics used to analyze data were mean, standard deviation, t-test for dependent samples, and t-test for one sample.
Results: 1) students’ information literacy after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence was higher than before at statistically significant level of .01 (t29=18.53, p=.000), 2) students’ information literacy was higher than the determined criterion of 70% at a significance level of .01 (t29=6.00, p=.000) and 3) students’ satisfaction after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence overall was at a high level (M=4.14, SD= 0.85).
Conclusion: The knowledge gained from the research is that a six-step learning management system using Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence (ABL-GAI), which represents an innovative instructional framework that systematically integrates human-AI co-creation into information literacy education. The most significant steps for enhancing students’ information literacy are step 4: Practice the skills + GAI, and step 5: Apply & create + GAI. Furthermore, this method has been shown to boost students' interest in learning and enhance their proficiency in core information literacy competencies, including information definition & planning, seeking & access, analysis, synthesis & communication, and reflection & self-evaluation.</jats:p>

<jats:p>
                    Generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly shaped the landscapes of production since the early 2020s. This report reviews the scholarly debate on geographies of production and includes further developments in the spatiality of digitalisation. It draws on literature on firms that develop and offer AI as a product innovation (geographies of production
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">of</jats:italic>
                    AI) and firms that implement and use AI (geographies of production
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">with</jats:italic>

title: Engineering Assurance for AI-Enabled  Self-Healing Infrastructure: From Damage  Signals to Verified Recovery
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
4dbc74cb9b81b397d67f7ff5aa81c3975af00987.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence, embedded sensing, digital twins and responsive materials are increasingly being explored as ways to create infrastructure that can detect and respond to damage. A warning message or a crack that closes doesn’t prove that the structure has regained its required performance. This review looks at self-healing infrastructure from an engineering-assurance perspective: what needs to be measured what can be inferred, which actions are permissible what needs to be fixed and what needs to be tested before a system can be called fixed. Using the review source and its references the paper separates sensing confidence, diagnosis confidence repair feasibility and recovery evidence as separate considerations. It looks at embedded -electromechanical sensors, fiber-optic and piezoelectric sensing, edge analytics, digital-twin state estimation, AI-based prediction and material-level healing methods. A workflow is suggested that connects a detected problem to an action and then to checks done after the repair. The study finds challenges including outside interference sensors changing over time models not working well in different places repairs not reaching far enough actions that can’t be undone and the difference between a material fixing itself and the whole system working again. The paper ends by saying that safe self-healing should be seen as a claim that needs proof, clear rules and accountable human oversight, in charge—not as something automated.</jats:p>

title: Reconceptualizing student teachers’ AI literacy in the Global South: Towards a teacher AI-readiness mapping framework
container-title: Journal of Education and e-Learning Research
21d1b1f99bf1c1cae765740df5e90c7a8560eff5.abstract: <jats:p>The responsible use of AI in the classroom begins with teachers’ knowledge and skills needed to integrate AI into the educational context. This study used a qualitative single-case study design to examine AI literacy and readiness among pre-service teachers in the Global South. Grounded in a conceptual framework combining AI literacy and technology acceptance, the study explores how pre-service teachers perceive, use, evaluate, and envision AI as their professional roles evolve. Data were generated from open-ended questionnaire responses from 197 first-year Bachelor of Education students enrolled at the University of South Africa, an open distance e-learning institution. Through iterative engagement with the data, six interrelated themes emerged: AI knowledge, AI skills, AI ethics, AI confidence, AI critical reflection, and AI pedagogical imagination. The findings indicate that AI readiness extends beyond technical competence or familiarity with tools. It is developmental, uneven, and shaped by contextual conditions such as access, language, and institutional guidance. Based on these insights, a framework is proposed to map teacher AI readiness and identify readiness gaps. The findings emphasise that teacher education programmes should go beyond tool training to include ethical clarity, policy guidance, confidence, critical thinking, pedagogical design, and equitable access.</jats:p>

title: Embodiment in Human and AI-generated Data Propositions
container-title: Written Communication
4e1174912cbf5bdff50378321feb83cd8238a51c.abstract: <jats:p>Many readers struggle to interpret the truth value of claims that utilize numerical data in mathematical expressions. These struggles can arise from a lack of context for the data, which can lead to misinterpretation of meaning or overattribution of truth, neither of which serves readers in understanding data-driven concepts like “food insecurity.” Some readers do not experience concepts like food insecurity directly, and hence, those concepts become real (or not) through the data used to express them. This research shows how writers assert the meaning of data about food insecurity by grounding it in an embodied sense of what that data means. This writerly approach is contrasted with examples of artificial intelligence-generated claims about “food insecurity” that are less commonly grounded in an embodied sense of truth. The findings are used to suggest what human writers uniquely add to data communication: an embodied, experiential sense of what the data mean.</jats:p>

title: Assessment of the Cybersecurity Posture of the Federal Inland Revenue Service Against  AI-Assisted Threats Using NIST, MITRE and ACGF Frameworks
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
2670d61989c4a42830d463078facbd0127404b40.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is changing how attackers target national institutions, yet most cybersecurity assessments still check whether controls exist without asking whether governance can cope with AI-assisted threats. This study assesses the cybersecurity posture of the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) in Nigeria against AI-assisted threats using an integrated model that combines the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the MITRE adversary knowledge base and the AI Cybersecurity Governance Framework (ACGF).</jats:p>

title: Comparing AI-Assisted 2D and 3D Block-Based Games for Computational Thinking Development in Introductory Programming

b1cc15777bc0e27544c33321efb607c0df6df371.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Computational thinking (CT) is a foundational competency in undergraduate education, yet novice programmers frequently encounter high cognitive demands and declining motivation. Although block-based programming and AI-assisted scaffolding can reduce extraneous load by enabling natural-language interaction, it remains unclear whether embedding these capabilities within immersive three-dimensional environments further enhances CT development through reduced extraneous load and enriched spatial context for schema formation. This study employed a randomized between-subjects design to compare an AI-assisted 3D block-based game (CT Logic 3D) with an AI-assisted 2D counterpart (CT Logic 2D) over a four-week intervention involving fifty undergraduate students (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                    = 50, Mage = 23.3, SD = 1.07). Both conditions shared identical AI translation pipelines and instructional sequences, with spatial dimensionality constituting the sole experimental manipulation. Results indicated that participants in the 3D condition achieved significantly greater gains in CT (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                    = 0.54), stronger delayed retention (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                    = 0.74), and higher near-transfer problem-solving performance (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                    = 0.82). Relative to the 2D group, participants in the 3D condition completed tasks 22% faster (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                    = 1.08), reported lower perceived difficulty (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                    = 0.94), and experienced higher levels of flow (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                    = 0.89) and intrinsic motivation (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">d</jats:italic>
                    = 0.86). Engagement increased throughout the intervention, with the largest efficiency gains observed among absolute novices. Moreover, substantial rates of learner-initiated modification of AI-generated solutions (3D: 76%; 2D: 71%) indicated active rather than passive use of AI scaffolding. Interpreted through Cognitive Load Theory, the findings suggest that combining AI scaffolding with immersive spatial representations produces measurable advantages for CT development beyond those achievable through AI scaffolding alone. Theoretical and practical implications for the design of AI-enhanced CT instruction are discussed.

title: FreshnessAI: AI-Based Freshness and Shelf-Life Prediction for Cut Fruits
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
38abc5ed5a962a2b1cf9a9a8432aacc4f62f9b21.abstract: <jats:p>Cut fruits are minimally processed products that deteriorate quickly after cutting, and shops and food businesses usually judge their freshness by eye. Such inspection is subjective and gives no reliable estimate of how long a piece of cut fruit can still be sold or served safely. This paper presents FreshnessAI, a proposed web and mobile system that applies computer vision and deep learning to assess the freshness of cut fruits from images and to provide shelf-life (expiry) guidance. The system is built around a Python Django backend with two clients: a web application for administrators, fruit shops and restaurants, and a Flutter-based Android application for customers. An AI inference engine built with PyTorch and YOLO pre-processes an uploaded image, detects the fruit type and location, assigns a freshness status (fresh or spoiled) with a confidence score, and produces a shelf-life estimate with advice. Results and images are stored in a MySQL database and media storage, and the YOLO model is trained offline through a pipeline of dataset collection, annotation, augmentation, splitting and GPU-based training. We survey twenty research papers, identify the gaps they leave for cut fruits, and present the requirements, architecture and data flow design. Dataset preparation, training and evaluation are planned for the next phase, and no performance figures are claimed in this paper</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Smart Agriculture: An Integrated Machine Learning Framework for Crop Recommendation, Fertilizer Recommendation and Crop Yield Prediction
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
a8a710443466bcd378000c22ef58f61b10677f66.abstract: <jats:p>Agricultural productivity in India is strongly affected by weather variability, soil degradation and the over- or under-use of fertilizers. Farmers still tend to rely on personal experience when choosing a crop, estimating its yield and deciding how much fertilizer to apply. This paper presents an integrated, web-based decision-support system that performs three tasks within a single framework: crop recommendation, fertilizer recommendation and crop yield prediction. The system takes soil nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium), temperature, humidity, soil pH, rainfall, soil moisture, soil type and crop type as inputs. The pipeline consists of data acquisition from public repositories, cleaning and normalisation, correlation-based feature selection, and model training using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Random Forest (RF). Model performance is evaluated with cross-validation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and correlation-based measures. In the reported experiments, the ANN model for yield prediction reached an accuracy of 94.70% and the Random Forest model for fertilizer recommendation reached 93.94%, and the crop recommendation model [insert accuracy] was the best performer for its task. The models are packaged in a Java (JSP/Servlet, Weka, MySQL) web application that lets farmers obtain all three recommendations from one input form..</jats:p>

title: A Comprehensive Review of AI and IoT-Based Water Pipeline Leakage Detection, Prediction and Monitoring Systems
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
e4e3b4bf29440630b7a09ad804c0fc3b67048a22.abstract: <jats:p>Water pipeline leakage is a major challenge in water distribution and supply systems because undetected leaks can result in water loss, infrastructure damage, economic losses, and inefficient water management [5], [13]. Conventional leakage inspection methods often depend on manual inspection, periodic maintenance, or specialized equipment, which may not provide continuous real-time monitoring [5], [13]. Recent developments in the Internet of Things (IoT), sensor technology, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML) have created opportunities for automated and intelligent pipeline monitoring [9], [11]. This review presents a study of recent techniques used for water pipeline leakage detection, localization, prediction, and monitoring. Different sensing approaches, including flow, pressure, acoustic, and vibration measurements, are reviewed along with machine-learning and deep-learning methods [1], [3], [4], [8], [12], [13]. Existing research demonstrates that pressure and flow measurements are widely used for hydraulic anomaly detection, while vibration and acoustic measurements can provide additional information about leakage events [5], [6], [7]. AI models such as Artificial Neural Networks, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, K-Nearest Neighbors, Convolutional Neural Networks, and ensemble techniques have been investigated for leakage classification and localization [1], [3], [4], [8], [12], [13]. IoT-based systems further enable continuous data acquisition, remote monitoring, and real-time alerts [9], [11]. However, challenges remain in obtaining representative real-world datasets, reducing false alarms, handling sensor noise, and deploying models on resource-constrained edge devices [13], [14], [15]. Based on the reviewed literature, a multi-sensor IoT and AI architecture using flow, pressure, and vibration measurements with Raspberry Pi-based processing is proposed as a suitable direction for a low-cost academic prototype [5], [9], [11], [12]..</jats:p>

author.family: C. V. Nalawade, Sakshi Santosh Dhainje

title: AI-Based Clinical Handover Assistant: Enhancing Patient Safety through Intelligent Clinical Communication
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
6319d7843089011a6b57d3361d0a1d3d54a22c13.abstract: <jats:p>Shift-to-shift handover is one of the most error-prone moments in hospital care. In most hospitals it is still performed through verbal briefings, handwritten notes or free-text electronic health record (EHR) entries, which is time-consuming, inconsistent and rarely restricted to the nurse who actually receives the patient. This paper presents the AI-Based Clinical Handover Assistant, a secure hybrid web and mobile system that automates nurse-to-nurse handover documentation, with escalation to a doctor when the receiving nurse cannot manage a case. An outgoing nurse records a voice or text handover addressed to specific incoming nurses; the audio is normalised with FFmpeg, transcribed by a speech-to-text service and summarised by the Gemini API into a structured SBAR/ISBAR report from which medications, vital observations and pending tasks are extracted. Every record is encrypted before storage and can be decrypted only by its addressed recipients; on escalation it is re-encrypted for the chosen doctor. A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chatbot lets authorised users query their own handovers. The system is built with Django, MySQL and Flutter. We present the literature survey, system architecture and data flow design of the proposed system.</jats:p>

title: Transformasi Pendidikan Dasar melalui Pedagogi Seni Terintegrasi AI: Pengaruh terhadap Kreativitas, Literasi Digital, dan Keterlibatan Siswa
container-title: Indonesian Society and Religion Research
98758b91ace706f1b7e9f2a38ecf72853ab2930e.abstract: <jats:p>Latar Belakang: Kecerdasan buatan (AI) semakin cepat memasuki pendidikan dasar, tetapi bukti mengenai integrasinya dalam pedagogi seni serta implikasinya bagi kreativitas, literasi digital, dan keterlibatan siswa masih tersebar. Metode: Artikel ini merupakan kajian literatur naratif terhadap penelitian bereputasi dan dokumen kebijakan terbitan 2022 ke atas dari Scopus, Google Scholar, dan jurnal terakreditasi Sinta, yang dianalisis secara tematik pada empat variabel: pedagogi seni terintegrasi AI, kreativitas, literasi digital, dan keterlibatan siswa. Hasil: Literatur menunjukkan bahwa pedagogi seni terintegrasi AI paling produktif ketika AI berperan sebagai mitra kokreatif di bawah mediasi guru. Peningkatan kreativitas tampak terutama pada tahap ide dan ekspresi, tetapi berisiko menurunkan keberagaman gagasan; literasi digital berkembang melalui penggunaan kritis, perumusan prompt, dan refleksi etis; keterlibatan paling terlihat pada dimensi emosional dan kognitif, namun rentan terhadap ketergantungan. Implikasi: Sekolah dasar perlu mengadopsi AI dalam pembelajaran seni melalui rancangan yang berpusat pada manusia, dimediasi guru, dan berorientasi proses. Pengujian empiris di sekolah dasar Indonesia diperlukan untuk memvalidasi model konseptual yang diusulkan.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of AI-Powered Learning Assistants on Student Motivation and Motor Skill Performance in Physical Education
container-title: Indonesian Journal of Educational Sciences and Research
29794f5fd3f8a06b3664fc4f19e9d48f7e710f39.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined the impact of AI-powered learning assistants on student motivation and motor skill performance in Physical Education (PE). A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design was used with 60 secondary school students, divided into an experimental group (n = 30) and a control group (n = 30). Over eight weeks, the experimental group used an AI-powered learning assistant that provided real-time feedback, personalized practice guidance, and video-based movement analysis, while the control group received conventional instruction. Motivation was measured with the Situational Motivation Scale, and motor skill performance with standardized skill tests. The experimental group improved motivation by 24.6%, compared with 9.8% in the control group, and motor skill performance by 31.2%, compared with 12.5%. Independent-samples t-tests showed significant between-group differences (p < .05) with large effect sizes. Motivation gains were positively correlated with skill improvement (r = .62). These findings suggest that AI-powered learning assistants can enhance student engagement and accelerate motor skill acquisition in PE. Integrating such tools with teacher guidance is recommended.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Interview Simulator: A Web-Based Platform for Personalised Interview Practice with ATS Resume Analysis, Voice and Visual Analysis
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
8188e6c213540402e59285d2619938617c7be39e.abstract: <jats:p>Interviews are the decisive stage of recruitment, yet many students and job seekers lack realistic, personalised practice and rarely know how an Applicant Tracking System (ATS) will judge their resume. This paper presents the design of an AI-Powered Interview Simulator, a web-based platform that brings ATS resume analysis, personalised question generation, Technical, Aptitude and HR rounds, voice-based answering and visual behaviour analysis into one application. The uploaded resume is scored using ATS rules, and the Gemini API generates questions from the candidate’s own skills, projects and experience. Spoken answers are converted to text with Whisper and evaluated by the Gemini API for relevance, correctness and clarity, while MediaPipe extracts visual indicators from webcam frames. A scoring module combines these results into an overall score and structured feedback. A survey of twenty-three studies shows that existing tools address only one part of interview preparation. The paper presents the proposed architecture and data flow diagrams that form the basis for implementation.</jats:p>

title: Finlet AI: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Financial Intelligence Platform Using Model Context Protocol and Deterministic Risk Governance
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
27dad0acee8d55eb44e2d11a6bed4fb2d73d8d08.abstract: <jats:p>Standalone conversational language models struggle to satisfy audit and compliance standards in institutional equity research. When an equity analyst prompts an ungrounded model to evaluate a listed company, three operational defects appear almost immediately: the model quotes outdated share prices from its pre-training cutoff, invents page or footnote numbers when summarizing regulatory filings, and produces inconsistent numerical risk ratings when executed repeatedly on identical inputs. This paper presents Finlet AI, a twelve-layer multi-agent financial intelligence platform that decouples quantitative market arithmetic and primary-source retrieval from neural text synthesis. Once an analytical query is submitted through our asynchronous FastAPI gateway, a stateful LangGraph supervisor triggers concurrent parallel fan-out across three specialized domain workers covering historical price series, live financial news feeds, and statutory annual reports isolated behind standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool interfaces. Technical price action, 20-day volume momentum ratios, and 30-day annualized volatility (σ	) are computed directly from three-month 30d Open-High-Low-Close-Volume (OHLCV) series fetched via Yahoo Finance. Real-time news catalysts are gathered through Google News RSS syndication and sanitized of HTML markup, while balance-sheet debt and liquidity disclosures are extracted page by page from SEC Form 10-K and Indian annual reports indexed locally in ChromaDB using 384-dimensional all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embeddings. Rather than delegating risk scoring to subjective prompt completion, our Risk & Governance module evaluates a bounded mathematical index weighting volatility (45% weight), news sentiment risk (35% weight), and filing flags (20% weight). Live validation on Reliance Industries (RELIANCE.NS) demonstrates real-time tracking at ₹1,184.50 (−2.03%), 23.1% annualized volatility, 1.0x volume momentum, and a deterministic risk score of 0.365 (LOW), while high-risk runs (≥ 0.65) pause at a persistent SQLite Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) checkpoint before compiling the final ReportLab PDF dossier..</jats:p>

title: Evaluating Fine-Grained Authorisation Strategies for Securing AI Agents That Interact With Enterprise Applications
container-title: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
bd7766e2fb76533be0b6e3e5eb177b8553071b21.abstract: <jats:p>Autonomous artificial intelligence agents equipped with large language model cognitive cores are rapidly transitioning from passive advisory interfaces into active operational actors capable of querying enterprise databases, triggering API workflows, and modifying mission-critical enterprise state. However, granting autonomous agents broad or coarse-grained access tokens introduces severe security vulnerabilities, including indirect prompt injection, confused deputy attacks, and uncontrollable privilege escalation across integrated enterprise applications. This study presents a rigorous empirical evaluation of fine-grained authorization strategies specifically architected for autonomous agent workflows. We evaluate four distinct authorization paradigms: static role-based access control, dynamic attribute-based access control, graph-based relationship access control, and a novel cryptographic delegation capability token architecture. Through extensive benchmarking across five distinct enterprise application scenarios comprising more than two million automated agent transactions, we evaluate decision latency, policy evaluation throughput, least-privilege enforcement precision, and resilience against adversarial prompt manipulation. Our findings demonstrate that while traditional attribute-based models suffer significant latency penalties under deep contextual evaluations, scoped delegation tokens combined with cryptographic boundary attestation achieve sub-ten-millisecond decision latencies while maintaining zero unauthorized state modifications across complex transactional workflows.</jats:p>

title: Teachers’ Trust in Artificial Intelligence and AI Dependency in Teaching and Learning Processes: Literacy and Responsible Use Plan
container-title: Advanced International Journal for Research
d4a37265846d2e8f96db9941fb57d4f577edcde7.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to determine the relationship between teachers’ trust in artificial intelligence (AI) and AI dependency in teaching and learning processes in selected public elementary schools in Loon North District, Schools Division of Bohol, during School Year 2026–2027. Specifically, it examines teachers’ levels of trust in AI in terms of perceived reliability and accuracy, usefulness, confidence in AI-generated outputs, transparency, and perceived risks and concerns. It also assesses AI dependency in lesson planning, instructional material development, assessment preparation, instructional decision-making, professional tasks, and the exercise of independent professional judgment. The study will employ a descriptive-correlational research design involving 60 public elementary school teachers from Loon North Central Elementary School, Pondol Elementary School, and Lawis Elementary School, with 20 respondents from each school. Data will be gathered using a structured questionnaire and analyzed through appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical tools. Frequency counts, percentages, and weighted means will be used to describe respondents’ profiles and determine the levels of trust and dependency, while correlation analysis will establish whether significant relationships exist between the variables at the 0.05 level of significance. The findings are expected to provide an understanding of how teachers’ perceptions of AI relate to their reliance on AI-assisted educational tasks. The study will also identify trust dimensions that may be associated with AI dependency and inform the development of an AI Literacy and Responsible Use Plan. The proposed plan will focus on strengthening AI literacy, promoting ethical and appropriate AI integration, protecting data privacy, verifying AI-generated information, preserving teachers’ professional judgment, and establishing sustainable training, implementation, and evaluation mechanisms. Ultimately, the study seeks to support informed, responsible, and balanced AI use in elementary education while recognizing teachers’ central role in instructional planning and decision-making.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enhanced Blockchain Voting Platform with Multi-Factor Biometric Authentication
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
e69fc174d63404bbfd78b20cc9a98d14ebc26f75.abstract: <jats:p>Electronic voting can improve the accessibility and speed of election workflows, but remote voting introduces challenges involving voter impersonation, repeated voting, centralized record manipulation, limited voter-side confirmation, and the protection of sensitive identity data. This paper presents the design of an AI-enhanced blockchain voting platform that combines a Flutter mobile application with a Python backend, phone-number one-time-password (OTP) verification, device-mediated fingerprint authentication, facial verification with liveness checking, smart-contract-based vote validation, and a blockchain-backed audit record. The proposed workflow guides a voter through OTP verification, fingerprint approval, live facial verification, ballot submission, and receipt generation. During the voting session, the camera and recording service are intended to remain active; security, camera, authentication, or network failures terminate the session and return the user to login. The architecture separates the mobile interface, verification services, backend, application database, smart-contract layer, and ledger. We also identify design constraints that are essential for a credible voting system, particularly ballot secrecy, biometric-data minimization, secure off-chain storage, recording consent and retention, and the distinction between tamper-evident records and end-to-end election verifiability. This is a proposed system design; implementation results and performance measurements are not claimed.</jats:p>

title: MediDocker: An AI-Enabled Healthcare Intelligence Ecosystem Integrating Clinical Decision Support, Predictive Analytics, and Emergency Response
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
d04969a768c3b17a9f37083acda948b7e5571bb5.abstract: <jats:p>Patients keep their health information in places that do not talk to each other: handwritten prescriptions, PDF blood reports, appointment cards and paper bills, and in an emergency nobody can quickly see their blood group or allergies. This paper presents MediDocker, a web platform that keeps these records in one secure place and explains them in plain language. A vision-language model (Qwen2.5-VL, run locally) only copies what a prescription says; every medicine is then verified against RxNorm, an Indian brand dictionary and a hand-checked drug table, and its purpose and warnings come from verified sources, never from the model. Blood (CBC) reports are encrypted, read with a PDF text layer or PaddleOCR, checked by seven plausibility rules, and followed across reports with reference change values, a personal set point and Theil–Sen projection. A LightGBM model trained on 14,134 laboratory-confirmed NHANES participants screens for iron deficiency from the CBC alone and answers only when it is confident, otherwise advising a serum ferritin test. On 1,945 unseen participants from 2021 onwards it reached an AUROC of 0.836 (95% CI 0.816–0.857) and 94.2% accuracy on the 10.6% of cases it decides, with sensitivity 99.6% and specificity 99.3% at its two cut-offs. A record-aware assistant detects emergencies with rules before any language model is used, and an Ed25519-signed emergency QR code can be verified offline by anyone, without login</jats:p>

title: Explainable AI-Based Vehicle Damage Assessment and Insurance Decision Support System
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
b5e0b0d1b3fc9d78ea40c944e0b20b300793ce24.abstract: <jats:p>Vehicle insurance claim processing still depends heavily on manual inspection by human surveyors, which is slow, subjective, and difficult to scale. Existing deep learning systems largely stop at detecting or segmenting damage, and offer no repair cost estimation, no explanation of their predictions, and no clear recommendation on the claim itself. This paper proposes an Explainable AI-based Vehicle Damage Assessment and Insurance Decision Support System that connects damage detection and segmentation, damage type classification, repair cost estimation, fraud risk assistance, and a claim recommendation with a confidence score into one pipeline. Explainability is built in through Grad-CAM, which highlights the image regions behind a prediction, and SHAP/LIME, which expose the factors that drive the cost and decision outputs. The system finally generates an explainable report for both customers and insurance staff. The design is based on a survey of recent work on vehicle damage assessment and is planned for implementation using YOLOv11, OpenCV, and the CarDD dataset together with a custom vehicle image dataset.</jats:p>

title: Copyright Enforcement in the Age of Generative AI
container-title: Legal Research & Analysis
dc8c1dc7281c75a3291f47459f9117bd0ebb2e5c.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (AI) raises significant copyright enforcement issues regarding source acquisition, training data retention, optimization, and output. Current study examines IP rights enforcement via mixed doctrinal and descriptive and documentary methodology where opaque technology intersects with undefined legal standards. The research reviews 97 recorded generative AI cases from 2022 to 2026, including 13 judgments or procedural entries and 13 legislative or other government documents. A total of 132 recorded instances were counted, and duplicate and irrelevant entries were excluded. The proceedings register reflects 79 U.S. cases (81.4% of the total), of which 51 were filed in the Southern District of New York (SDNY). Recorded filings increased from two in 2022 to 37 in the incomplete observation period of 2026, while 62 proceedings show an active public-status label. The largest single uncombined enforcement category concerns training-use allegations, with 32 entries. It neither establish the prevalence of infringement nor evaluate the success of related litigation. Doctrinal analysis reveals that certain evidentiary and remedial issues arise from the reproduction right, training exceptions, rights reservations, human authorship, and copyright management information, among others. The cited judicial developments underscore the importance of distinguishing between allegations and holdings, the source of the training material and subsequent training, and interim versus final decisions. The paper presents a framework that integrates identification and traceable acquisition of rights, their disclosure and legal defence, and the proportionality of the relief sought. It supports documented acquisition practices, interoperable rights reservations, practical licensing pathways, and access to courts while maintaining confidentiality. The framework addresses enforcement barriers and structures responses in a controlled manner. Further research is needed to verify dockets and track outcomes to substantiate stronger claims.</jats:p>

title: AI, National Criminal Procedure Code, Criminal Investigation and Adjudication in Nepal
container-title: Legal Research & Analysis
e168e2940aae8555e08c370c03384f54f8f7b132.abstract: <jats:p>The National Criminal Procedure Code, 2017 confers ample powers to the government to use of science and technology in the investigation and adjudication of criminal offences in Nepal. The Code allows for the filing of a First Information Report (FIR) through electronic means, which aims to facilitate greater accessibility and efficacy in the reporting of crimes. Further, the law allows the investigating agencies to use of technology during investigation in many respects. The statement of accused may be recorded through video conferencing in cases where accused or witness cannot be produced due to physical illness, old age, or security concerns. The law mandates for digital archiving of FIRs so registered. Further, the courts may record the statement of witness through video conferencing, and such statements are required to be digitally archived. The exchange of documents through electronic means and the computerized arrangement for listing the matters and giving dates facilitate technology-enabled court proceedings. The digital and automated case management systems operated by Nepal's courts contribute to the modernization and efficiency of judicial processes. Current study explores the legal frameworks relating to the use of technology in criminal investigation and adjudication in Nepal.</jats:p>

title: The Adjudicative Logic and Functional Role of Chinese Courts in AI Governance
container-title: Legal Research & Analysis
1d0f3a22e2cd01fe8a292892a887518385c02b67.abstract: <jats:p>A structural divide exists between the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and the relative stability of law. In the absence of dedicated AI legislation, response of Chinese courts to novel AI-related disputes through adjudication and their role in AI governance has become an important research topic demanding urgent attention in contemporary law. Adopting a comparative law perspective and drawing on a systematic analysis of typical AI-related cases decided by Chinese courts, this article distills three adjudicative logics employed by Chinese courts in handling AI cases. Firstly, “anthropocentrism”, in copyright and personality rights, courts have consistently maintained that AI is a tool and that humans are the sole bearers of legal responsibility.AI can’t be an author or a rights-holder. Secondly, a “two-stage liability assessment” by distinguishing between “technology development and provision” and “specific use,” courts have achieved a dynamic balance between technology neutrality and accountability for unlawful acts. Thirdly, “judicial development of the law” where existing law provides no explicit answer, courts have filled legal gaps and created adjudicative standards through methods such as application by reference, analogy, and using general clauses. Through comparative analysis with U.S. and EU courts, current research reveals the different models of institutional division of responsibilities underlying the three adjudicative logics: judicial restraint in the United States, legislation-led governance in the European Union, and judicial pioneering in China. Accordingly, this study demonstrates four core functions of Chinese courts in AI governance. These include upholding human legal subjecthood to anchor the foundations of the rule of law, employing the two-stage assessment to achieve dynamic equilibrium, engaging in judicial development of the law to supply rules, and imposing strict accountability to control risks. The Chinese courts’ pathway of “judiciary first, legislation to follow” is neither the “passive judicial waiting” of the United States nor the “legislation-led pioneering” of the European Union, but a realist path rooted in China’s rule-of-law practice, offering a Chinese approach that may inform global AI governance.</jats:p>

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting Organizational AI Adoption: Strategic Alignment, Organizational AI Readiness, and Technology-Organization-Environment Factors
container-title: Scientific Societal & Behavioral Research Journal
20d9c36949d4a166ea9f19603a8c92bfb55b2076.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is no longer only a technical issue. For many organizations, deciding whether and how to use AI also depends on strategy, internal resources, employee readiness, governance, and the external business environment. This study develops an explainable machine learning framework to examine these factors using enterprise survey data from 359 private organizations in Slovakia. The analysis brings together measures of organizational AI maturity, business sentiment, and Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) factors. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using an 80/20 stratified train-test split, five-fold cross-validation, three random seeds, and 5,000 bootstrap resamples. SHAP values and permutation importance were used to understand which variables contributed most to the model predictions. Under the primary definition of adoption, 199 organizations were classified as adopters and 160 as non-adopters. Across the three random seeds, mean ROC-AUC values were 0.823 for Logistic Regression, 0.840 for Random Forest, and 0.851 for XGBoost. The corresponding mean PR-AUC values were 0.856, 0.870, and 0.871. In the primary analysis, TOE organization, technology, and environment together represented about 71.97% of the aggregated mean absolute SHAP contribution. Strategic alignment, perceived measurable AI benefits, privacy maturity, organizational resources, and several technological and environmental factors were among the more influential predictors. Additional analyses using a stricter adoption definition, the cleaned dataset, different random seeds, and a reduced predictor set showed broadly similar patterns. Overall, the study illustrates how explainable machine learning can help examine organizational AI adoption while keeping predictive relationships clearly separate from claims about causation.</jats:p>

title: Virtual biotextile generation using generative adversarial networks: a study on bacterial cellulose for sustainable design
container-title: Textile Research Journal
d5e5583ab1c4fe2b047c2743a96a6346aed7a07e.abstract: <jats:p>With increasing attention to sustainable material development, bio-based materials such as bacterial cellulose (BC) have been widely explored in design research. However, their broader application remains constrained by long production cycles and limited controllability. To address these limitations, this study presents an exploratory investigation of AI-based virtual biomaterial generation under limited-data conditions. Specifically, an image dataset was first constructed from self-cultivated BC samples produced under controlled settings. Three generative adversarial network (GAN)-based models were trained and evaluated for virtual material generation. User perception experiments revealed that StyleGAN-generated samples received the highest ratings in naturalness, sense of growth, and credibility, approaching evaluations of physical BC samples. In addition, an image-to-3D proof-of-concept showed that GAN-generated textures could be used as visual inputs for preliminary 3D shape generation, while cross-material experiments demonstrated the potential for simulating novel material combinations. The findings indicate that, despite limited training data, GAN-generated textiles can capture key visual characteristics of BC and facilitate early-stage design exploration. By integrating biological experimentation with computational generation, this work proposes a AI-assisted framework with the potential to reduce physical material consumption and support sustainable design innovation. The study further suggests that generative models can function not only as visualization tools but also as assistive systems for future material design.</jats:p>

title: Digitally Mediated Managerial Control and Psychosocial Risk in Evolving Digital Workplaces: Work-Related Strain, Organizational Resources, and Differences Between AI and Non-AI Workers
container-title: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
a4e88e055f1ba66f91e9d1965f927bbd476f960a.abstract: <jats:p>Digital technologies increasingly mediate managerial practices, but the robustness of associations between digitally mediated managerial control (DMMC), negative digital work consequences (NDWC), organizational resources, and work-related strain remains uncertain. We analyzed 25,462 digital workers across 30 European countries in the EU-OSHA OSH Pulse 2025 survey. Categorical confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation models incorporated survey weights and country clustering; exploratory multigroup comparisons distinguished workers reporting AI-tool use from other digital workers. The structural model allowed an NDWC–organizational resources residual covariance. In the full sample, DMMC was positively associated with NDWC (β = 0.496) and strain (direct β = 0.111); NDWC was positively associated with strain (β = 0.102), whereas organizational resources were inversely associated with strain (β = −0.097). The standardized indirect association was 0.050. Weighted multigroup estimates suggested four path differences; only the DMMC–NDWC and organizational resources–strain differences remained significant without survey weights. However, 95% confidence intervals from a leave-one-country-out jackknife encompassed zero for all four differences. The DMMC–NDWC standardized path decreased from 0.496 to 0.335 in a common method factor sensitivity model. These cross-sectional findings identify potentially important psychosocial correlates of digitally organized work but do not establish causal effects or robust AI-use-group moderation.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI in EFL academic writing: a critical review and implications for higher education in Uzbekistan
Генеративный искусственный интеллект в академическом письме студентов EFL: критический обзор и выводы для высшего образования Узбекистана
EFL talabalarining akademik yozuvida generativ sun’iy intellekt: tanqidiy sharh va O‘zbekiston oliy ta’limi uchun xulosalar
container-title: Partner conferences of the International Scientific Journal Research Focus
0e7cef66fbfcfbbda8145e89f7b5f53b39847485.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to support academic writing in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education. This focused narrative review critically examines selected empirical studies, research syntheses, and institutional guidance published between 2023 and 2026. It distinguishes improvements in AI-assisted texts from evidence of lasting, independent writing competence and considers feedback, critical thinking, learner autonomy, and academic integrity. The discussion incorporates emerging research from Uzbekistan while acknowledging the limited generalizability of individual institutional studies. The synthesis suggests that AI feedback can support revision when students critically evaluate suggestions, verify sources, and retain responsibility for their writing. As a conceptual contribution, the article proposes a five-stage instructional framework comprising independent planning, targeted AI assistance, critical evaluation, student-led revision, and reflection. The framework has not been empirically tested. The article concludes by identifying priorities for responsible classroom implementation and future research in Uzbek higher education.</jats:p>

title: E-Commerce Claim Verification Under Generative AI: Deterrence and Evidence Selection to Minimize Platform Loss
container-title: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research
351f2c1de3853a675128ea1927cfffd79e6f275a.abstract: <jats:p>We study how an e-commerce platform should allocate verification effort and choose between claimant-generated and transaction-linked evidence as manipulation becomes cheaper. In a sequential game for filed disputes, platform loss includes fraud, verification expenditure, wrongful rejection of legitimate claims and the additional burden of transaction-linked checks. Under the benchmark commitment and deterioration path, incumbent verification rises to maintain zero incremental manipulation and then falls as the platform accommodates manipulation; an initial correction-supported plateau can precede this pattern. Switching evidence bases can minimize loss before or after incremental manipulation begins, with the ordering governed by implementation burden, final-error rates and prevention ceilings. The decision rule compares the additional burden with savings in verification expenditure, residual-fraud loss and legitimate-claim error loss. Joint changes and alternative timing can reverse benchmark selection patterns. Synthetic calculations illustrate the boundaries, while monetary examples show how the per-dispute burden depends on allocable cost and case volume.</jats:p>

title: ClaimTrace: Contradiction-Aware Evidence Lineage for Verifiable AI-Assisted Scientific Literature Reviews
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
1c14944a5be3463080b79031fa3cccc2e34b5e2e.abstract: <jats:p>ClaimTrace is a proposed framework for checking the relationship between scientific review assertions and their cited evidence. Its central mechanism is a typed lineage graph that preserves source identity, assertion boundaries, study conditions and numerical bindings rather than returning a single undifferentiated judgment. This paper specifies eight modules, a five-status annotation taxonomy, conservative contradiction rules and an audit record for evidence-grounded revision. A lightweight Python prototype was implemented and executed on twelve publisher-verified research abstracts. Four source documents were assigned to development and eight to evaluation; no source document occurred in both partitions. Seventy source-derived synthetic diagnostic cases were constructed, including forty-seven evaluation cases. The full prototype matched forty-two evaluation specifications, while a lexical retrieval-only heuristic matched nineteen. These counts measure conformance to constructed test expectations, not predictive accuracy against independent scientific annotations. Retrieval returned the generating source among the top three passages for all thirty-one evaluation queries with a known evidence target. The experiment did not execute a standard LLM judge, a learned natural language inference model, semantic retrieval, independent human annotation or authentic cross-study conflict evaluation. Consequently, the central question of whether typed lineage improves verification relative to retrieval plus an LLM judge remains unanswered. The contribution is a reproducible design and an executed, explicitly provisional implementation diagnostic, with the limitations needed for a subsequent controlled scientific evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Spammedin: An AI-Powered Multi-Agent Framework for LinkedIn Scam Profile and Organization Detection
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
8f55794323da70dec5c3e83243662ec2c9072d36.abstract:
<jats:p>Professional-networking sites like LinkedIn have become central to hiring, career development, and business outreach, but their massive user base has also
turned them into a favourite hunting ground for impersonated recruiters, sham companies, and misleading job or internship postings that prey on unsuspecting users. As the platform grows, reviewing every profile or company page by hand becomes impossible, which calls for a verification approach that is both automated and easy to interpret. This work introduces Spammedin, a multi-agent
AI system that estimates the trustworthiness of a given LinkedIn profile or organization by pooling evidence gathered from text, domain records, visual media, and behavioural cues. Four dedicated agents — Profile, Organization, Image, and Behaviour — work in parallel to assess distinct credibility markers such as account age, how complete the profile information is, connection totals,
endorsement trends, how long a domain has been registered, site reputation, image authenticity, and posting habits. Outputs from these agents are merged in a Feature Fusion stage and then evaluated by a Risk Assessment Agent, which produces a risk value ranging from 0 to 100 and tags the submission as Genuine, Suspicious, or Scam. An Explainability Agent applies SHAP and LIME on top of
each verdict to generate a rationale that a human reader can follow. A working prototype was implemented and tested on sample profile and organization data, and the outcomes show that the multi-agent pipeline functions as intended.</jats:p>

title: The Representation of Indonesian Meaning in Generative Artificial Intelligence-Generated Responses: A Semantic Perspective
container-title: Symposium of Literature, Culture, and Communication (SYLECTION) 2022
7aa9dd050ca4d447c3f3200a9ef2120472bba5c3.abstract: <jats:p>The creation and processing of language, has been revolutionized by generative artificial intelligence. Even though generative AI can produce coherent responses, the meaning representations it produces need to be further assessed using Indonesian semantics principles to make sure they are accurate, consistent, and relevant for the context. The purpose of this study is to characterize how meaning is represented in Indonesian language texts produced by generative artificial intelligence and to examine the semantic properties of these texts in terms of lexical meaning, grammatical meaning, contextual meaning, polysemy, ambiguity, and semantic linkages. The study used content analysis as its research method and a qualitative descriptive methodology. Semantic theory-based methods of data reduction, classification, interpretation, and conclusion formulation were used to study the data. The results show that most of the material may be represented coherently and contextually using generative artificial intelligence. Nonetheless, there are still issues with understanding polysemous meanings, particular semantic relationships, and pragmatic and cultural settings. These results imply that generative artificial intelligence has a great deal of promise as a supplementary tool for semantic studies of the Indonesian language, even though linguists and academics still need to critically validate its outputs.</jats:p>

title: Voices of the North: An AI-Assisted Crowdsourcing Framework for Multimodal Documentation of Northern Malay Dialects
container-title: Symposium of Literature, Culture, and Communication (SYLECTION) 2022
cba3e76f9dc5c3cac142f479de946afd35679890.abstract: <jats:p>Northern Malay (Melayu Utara) dialects are an important part of Malaysia’s linguistic and cultural heritage, yet much of their documentation remains scattered, small-scale, and heavily text-based. Such approaches create a particular problem for dialect research because written forms alone cannot adequately capture pronunciation, phonological variation, intonation, and contextual use. The challenge is further complicated by the limited representation of dialectal and under-resourced language varieties in contemporary language technologies. This paper therefore proposes Voices of the North, an AI-assisted crowdsourcing framework for the multimodal documentation of Northern Malay dialects. The framework brings community knowledge, computational support, and linguistic expertise into a single documentation process. Community members contribute dialect words and expressions together with meanings, examples of use, pronunciation recordings, and geographical information. AI supports early-stage processing through speech transcription, similarity and duplicate detection, text normalization, semantic comparison, and preliminary categorization. It does not determine what constitutes valid dialect data; meaning, pronunciation, contextual suitability, regional usage, and cultural accuracy remain subject to expert linguistic validation. The framework is organized around six connected components: community contribution, crowdsourcing and data management, AI-assisted processing, expert linguistic validation, a multimodal dialect repository, and knowledge application. Kedah dialect is proposed as the initial context for prototype development and evaluation. By preserving written form alongside voice, meaning, context, and place, the framework treats a dialect entry as a situated linguistic record rather than an isolated lexical item. The resulting repository is intended to support linguistic research, education, cultural heritage initiatives, geolinguistic visualization, tourism, and future language technologies.</jats:p>
