                  <jats:p>The LTRO study provided a novel approach by using digital visualization dashboards to fully integrate available data, hence a completely new data-driven/data-first workflow attempts to understand remaining field potential, that complements and challenges conventional modelling approaches. Further, it also offered a strong foundation to take the field development from peripheral to full field pattern flood by addressing the location of remaining oil as an input in design and development for CO2-WAG.</jats:p>

title: Field-Validated AI-Enabled Advanced Process Control for Operating Efficiency in Large-Scale Oil and Gas Separation Trains
container-title: ADIPEC
61eea288e04c693c7fb9d6ee187fbcc02bb96c9c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Conventional oil and gas separation facilities operate under highly variable conditions caused by changing well contributions, gas-oil ratio, water cut, production routing, slugging, and strong interactions among separation, desalting, stabilization, and export systems. These conditions have historically limited the application of Advanced Process Control in upstream production facilities, where optimization commonly depends on independent regulatory control loops, conservative operating targets, delayed laboratory measurements, and frequent operator intervention.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents the full-scale deployment and field validation of an AI-enabled Advanced Process Control (Ai-APC) architecture across five conventional oil and gas separation trains and associated facilities within one of the world's largest onshore oil fields. The Gas Oil Separation Plant, designed for 780,000 BOPD and processing commingled production from more than 600 wells, was optimized using next-generation Dynamic Matrix Control (DMC3™), adaptive process models, and real-time soft sensors for Reid Vapor Pressure and salt prediction. The deployment methodology included site assessment, data conditioning, live-plant dynamic testing, model development and validation, Distributed Control System integration, operator training, closed-loop commissioning, and digital performance auditing using real-time KPI dashboards.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Performance was evaluated from 17 February to 30 March 2026 against a validated pre-APC baseline. The Ai-APC application achieved 99.35% availability and improved oil recovery by 0.31 vol%, equivalent to 2,208 BOPD of incremental production. Lean-gas consumption per barrel of oil decreased by 55%, fresh wash-water consumption decreased by 3%, and the frequency and variability of manual operator intervention decreased by 20%. The deployment also reduced CO2 emissions by 11,666 metric tons and delivered approximately USD 43 million/year in annualized realized value.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The results demonstrate that highly variable conventional separation facilities can be transformed from reactive, laboratory-dependent operation into predictive, quality-aware, and continuously optimized assets. The work establishes a transferable AI-enabled brownfield separation optimization framework integrating adaptive multivariable control, real-time quality inferential, operator decision support, and digital performance assurance. This framework provides a scalable foundation for improving operating efficiency and advancing progressively autonomous upstream production operations.</jats:p>

title: A Stochastic Age-Structured SI Epidemics Model with Logarithmic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Process
container-title: East Asian Journal on Applied Mathematics
364c7093641d8804274636c5be16d2eaad6e6f00.abstract: <jats:p>In this paper, a new stochastic age-structured SI epidemic model with a logarithmic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process is proposed. The study mainly focuses on the long-term behavior of solutions for the proposed stochastic system. For this, the existence and (global) asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the deterministic system without an OU process are first discussed. Then the properties of extinction and asymptotic persistence of solutions for the stochastic system are investigated and the corresponding threshold conditions for them are obtained successfully. This research highlights the importance of considering randomness in the transmission of the epidemic, especially with complex disease mechanisms and random environmental factors. The findings here reveal that, interestingly, the reversion speed of the OU process impacts how quickly the system stabilizes, while the magnitude of random disturbances can alter the stability potentially and even cause a resurgence of an infectious disease which is expected to go extinct.</jats:p>

title: Retrieval-Assisted Scalar Grounding for Natural-Language Optimization: A Diagnostic Study
9c30a1ca37c6eab5ce07baf2583f4964e05614c8.abstract: Abstract Retrieval and structural checks can make natural-language optimization outputs appear usable even when numerical grounding—assigning textual quantities to model parameters—is incomplete. We examine this diagnostic gap through three questions: fixed-catalog schema identification, the validity of coverage/type readiness as a numerical check, and the mechanisms underlying grounding outcomes. On 331 queries from NLP4LP, a benchmark for natural-language linear and mixed-integer linear programming, and 335 schema documents, term frequency–inverse document frequency retrieval and a pretrained dense encoder identify the target schema for 301 and 313 queries. Lexical grounding with multiplicative-word extraction passes coverage/type readiness on 265 queries, but only seven meet the complete stored-reference scalar-tolerance criterion: 2.64% of ready outputs. A mutually exclusive residual partition distinguishes retrieval, coverage, type, and numerical failures. Six grounding procedures under fixed retrieval yield between seven and 46 complete successes, with candidates, scoring, abstention, and decoding changing together. A separate 49-query assignment study with fixed candidates and scores improves exact slot counts without increasing the five whole-instance tolerance successes, limiting attribution to search. The methodological contribution is joint reporting of retrieval, readiness, and complete scalar agreement with explicit assistance, denominators, and evidence boundaries. Reference-derived inventories and benchmark exposure restrict the findings to assisted grounding. Supplementary relationship judgments and author contrasts assisted by artificial intelligence illustrate semantic limits without establishing accuracy. A versioned public release supports saved-record reanalysis; missing historical predictions and restricted originals prevent full experimental reproduction.

title: Selective Memory Operations Shape History-Dependent Population Representations and Choice under Sensory Ambiguity: A Hippocampal-Inspired Dynamic Gating Model
7a8ade6954fca802757d41cdfe76139354887816.abstract: Abstract How does past experience continue to shape behavior? The hippocampal–entorhinal system supports memory-guided behavior, yet how selective memory operations shape population activity and history-dependent choice remains unclear. We introduce a hippocampal-inspired dynamic gating model (HDGM) that integrates predictive recurrence, online associative memory, and feedback-dependent regulation to examine how past experience shapes population representations and subsequent choice under sensory ambiguity. HDGM exhibited distinct history-conditioned population states despite identical current sensory input. Selective disruptions of encoding and associative processing altered subsequent population activity and impaired history-dependent choice. Output-gain modulation increased linear decoding accuracy for task-relevant classes, whereas cross-trial gate reassignment reduced delay-state separation with little change in mean choice performance. Across complementary tasks, population organization, linear information accessibility, and behavioral choice showed distinct responses to selective memory operations. Together, these findings provide a computational framework for investigating how selective memory operations shape the expression of past experience and its relationship to subsequent choice.

title: Mapping gender, agency, and objectification in Arabic poetry: an ontology-guided computational study
c5ccb001f3193530b173043e5f93c74f519763a0.abstract: Abstract Gender, agency, and objectification are important dimensions of how participants and relationships are represented in poetry, yet their systematic study in Arabic verse remains difficult because meaning is often conveyed through metaphor, ellipsis, compressed syntax, and context-dependent relations. This study investigates how gendered agency and objectification are represented across a large corpus of Arabic poetry and examines whether computational analysis can capture these literary-semantic relations while preserving textual evidence and interpretive uncertainty. A neuro-symbolic computational framework was developed to represent participants, events, agency, gender representation, and objectification as explicit, evidence-linked semantic relations. Large language model extraction was combined with formal constraint validation and expert adjudication. Evaluated against an expert-annotated sample of 4,500 verses, automated semantic extraction achieved an F1-score of 0.884 on the hold-out test set. Following evaluation and targeted adjudication within the annotated sample, the resulting constraint-guided pipeline was applied across 31,209 single-verse poems spanning twelve historical periods and eight poetic genres. Corpus-level analysis identified distinct distributions in gendered agency: male-coded participants were classified as active in 61.8\% of agency-related instances, compared with 48.2\% for female-coded participants, while the latter showed higher proportions of reactive and passive involvement. Objectification was distributed across multiple forms, with symbolic objectification emerging as the most frequent category (38.4\%), exceeding direct physical objectification (21.6\%). These results make recurrent patterns of gendered literary representation systematically inspectable at corpus scale while retaining links to textual evidence, ambiguity, and provenance. Ultimately, the study demonstrates how evidence-grounded computational methods can support large-scale investigation of literary representation while retaining interpretive boundaries.

title: Localized patterns and their moving dynamics in a diffusive population-toxicant model with negative toxicant-taxis
d96bdc431f150c1f3c53c9ad25ff0b6d503c0172.abstract: Abstract We investigate the existence of aggregation patterns and their moving dynamics in the population-toxicant model proposed in [10], which incorporates the spatial avoidance response of a population to toxicants characterized by a negative (repulsive) toxicant-taxis term. In the limit of large toxicant-taxis sensitivity, we explicitly construct asymptotic equilibrium spike solutions using formal matched asymptotic expansions, and show that boundary spikes are linearly stable at leading order. In contrast, by deriving an explicit asymptotic formula for the translational eigenvalue, we show that interior spike solutions are linearly unstable to translations of the spike profile. We further derive a reduced system of ordinary differential equations describing the fast motion of the spike center and the slow motion of the spike height for both spatially homogeneous and inhomogeneous toxicant inputs. Our results reveal that spikes drift rapidly toward the nearest domain boundary in homogeneous environments, while they converge to a stable local minimum of the background toxicant concentration in strongly inhomogeneous environments. These asymptotic findings offer a new research direction for subsequent rigorous analytical work. 2020 MSC. 92D25, 35K57, 35K55, 35Q92

title: Dual-Counterfactual Evidence Decomposition and Selective Editing for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
2868774a8e7e6dca2da7ba31edd1b5b6c623b9fc.abstract: Abstract Large vision-language models (LVLMs) often generate fluent but visually unsupported content. Existing training-free methods mainly recalibrate output distributions or edit representations without identifying whether the evidence behind the current claim is visual, linguistic, or shared. This limits intervention precision: unsupported language priors may survive, whereas grounded visual information may be weakened. We introduce a dual-counterfactual evidence decomposition and selective editing framework. Paired visual and linguistic counterfactuals act as sample-specific evidence probes, whose hidden-state responses are decomposed into shared, visual-exclusive, and linguistic-exclusive components. A claim-aware gate attenuates unsupported linguistic evidence only for visually verifiable claims, while an evidence-preserving update protects shared and visual-exclusive support. The method is training-free and requires neither parameter updates nor external verification models. Across three LVLM families, it achieves the highest Accuracy and F1 in all nine POPE backbone--split settings. On CHAIR, it obtains the lowest CHAIR_i on all three evaluated backbones, reducing it by 9.1%-14.7% relative to HulluEdit while maintaining comparable BLEU scores. It also achieves the highest aggregate MME-H on all three backbones, the best results on all four HallusionBench metrics, and a score of 29.3 on MM-Vet. At 23.59 tokens per second, the complete pipeline retains 75.5% of greedy-decoding throughput. These results establish evidence attribution before intervention as an effective and practical strategy for faithful LVLM generation.

title: A A Comparative Study of Multimodal Discourse in Micro-Learning Videos via Intersemiotic Complementarity Theory
container-title: English Language Teaching and Linguistics Studies
76a318cbe0fe51eab76a091b29b6d9d03d7fc425.abstract: With the increasing popularity of online educational videos, how to teach and disseminate these videos has become a challenge for many creators. But few of the current studies discussed the intersemiotic complementarity of micro-learning videos and how to promote their effectiveness through this angle. Based on the intersemiotic complementarity theory, this research explores how the collaborative interaction between micro-learning videos’ image and text affects the effectiveness of teaching and dissemination. This study compares and analyzes the image-text relationship of the two videos, Crash Course (CC) and Home Revise (HR) from ideational, interpersonal and compositional intersemiotic complementarity (IC). The study finds that: (1) For ideational IC, both videos use synonymy, collocation and hyponymy, and repetition is often combined with other relationship types to form a composite type. (2) For interpersonal IC, CC uses a lot of demand shots, and the text mood is diverse, so as to build a sense of interaction. (3) For compositional IC, the layout of CC is more flexible. In contrast, the layout of HR is relatively fixed and monotonous. The results of this study show that good ideational IC can reduce the cognitive burden and promote the teaching effectiveness; highly interactive interpersonal IC can improve audience participation; good compositional IC can balance teaching and fun. This study expands the application of intersemiotic complementarity in video analysis, and also provides inspirations for the design and evaluation of micro-learning videos.

title: Adherence to anti-tuberculosis treatments by patients using an instrument based on the health belief model
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Kesehatan Sandi Husada
35ce24a3c4eef8de597af57df8bed9641bc7ad1d.abstract: Introduction: Several studies report a persistently high rate of non-adherent patients globally, with tuberculosis patients failing to comply with prescribed regimens. Adherence rates often decline during advanced treatment phases due to patients feeling cured, treatment fatigue, or obstacles related to access and employment. The aim of the study was to compare TB patient’s adherence to treatment using two instruments: the researchers AMI-TB and the MMAS-8 questionnaire. Research Methodology: This study employed a cross-sectional observational design with descriptive assessments using two adherence-related instruments. No intervention or repeated measurement was performed. The study population consisted of all registered patients diagnosed with tuberculosis undergoing anti-tuberculosis treatment, totaling 489 patients. A total of 148 respondents participated in this study using simple random sampling. Data were collected using the MMAS-8 and AMI-TB questionnaire. Data analysis included univariate and bivariate analyses using an independent t-test with a significance level of p < 0.05. Results: The average treatment status measured using MMAS-8 was 6.48 (standard deviation = 1.48), and using AMI-TB was 59.13 (standard deviation = 4.13). A previously reported p value of 0.005 resulted from a raw-score comparison; this does not constitute a valid test of comparative adherence because the instruments have different score ranges and conceptual targets. Conclusion: The findings describe adherence-related scores obtained using two conceptually different instruments in the participating tuberculosis services. MMAS-8 assesses self-reported medication-taking behavior, whereas AMI-TB addresses selected Health Belief Model perceptions. These results do not demonstrate superior validity, accuracy, or interchangeability of either instrument. Further study-specific reliability, construct validity, criterion validity, and clinical outcome analyses are needed before recommending routine comparative use. Questionnaires based on the health belief model can be used to measure TB patients' adherence to anti-tuberculosis treatment.

title: Quality-adjusted survival and costs of dialysis modalities in Poland: a lifetime model evaluation
container-title: BMC Nephrology
ffe4493a74b7f177f49925216f66b1e30506cedf.abstract: Abstract Background and Hypothesis Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 4.7 million people in Poland, with around 21,000 patients requiring renal replacement therapy. Among these patients, hemodialysis (HD) is the most commonly used treatment modality. Despite clinical guidelines emphasizing the medical and economic advantages of peritoneal dialysis (PD), its use remains limited. We hypothesize that PD is a more cost-effective option than in-center HD for patients initiating dialysis in Poland. This study aims to evaluate and compare the cost-effectiveness of these two dialysis modalities. Methods We conducted a systematic literature review to compare survival and quality-of-life outcomes between peritoneal dialysis and hemodialysis. We performed a cost-utility analysis using a Markov model from the perspective of the Polish National Health Fund. The model included three health states—dialysis, post-transplant, and death—and applied a lifetime horizon. Health outcomes were expressed as quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and cost inputs were derived from national reimbursement data. Results PD yielded 4.98 QALYs, compared with 4.54 QALYs for in-center HD. The total cost of PD was 569,167 PLN/133,294 EUR/153,829 USD, compared with 478,710 PLN/112,110 EUR/129,381 USD for HD. The incremental cost-utility ratio (ICUR) was 208,489 PLN/48,826 EUR/56,348 USD per QALY, falling below the Polish cost-effectiveness threshold. PD was also associated with lower hospitalization rates and reduced costs related to complications and mortality. Deterministic sensitivity analyses further support these findings across multiple scenarios. The probabilistic sensitivity analysis indicated moderate decision uncertainty, with PD being cost-effective in 54.4% of simulations at the applied willingness-to-pay threshold. Conclusion The model results indicate that peritoneal dialysis is likely to be a cost-effective alternative to in-center hemodialysis in Poland. PD was associated with higher costs and greater effectiveness than in-center HD, resulting in an ICUR below the Polish cost-effectiveness threshold in the base-case analysis. While the findings are limited by available evidence, they suggest that peritoneal dialysis may offer clinical benefits for appropriately selected patients. The results support consideration of strategies to improve access to PD and may inform healthcare policy aimed at expanding patient choice and optimizing resource allocation. Policy initiatives focused on reimbursement, education, and informed modality choice may facilitate greater access to PD while maintaining an individualized approach to dialysis modality selection.

title: HelloTalk as a Digital Communication Space for Korean Language Learning among Indonesian Users: A Qualitative Study
container-title: Jurnal Komunikasi dan Bisnis
42ca5a4036d2f6825577df977fab14b21d30729d.abstract: Digital media have become important communication spaces in which people learn foreign languages beyond formal classrooms. However, research on HelloTalk has largely concentrated on English learners and on pedagogical outcomes such as speaking skills and learner autonomy, and limited attention has been given to how Indonesian users experience HelloTalk as a communication space for learning Korean. This study examines how Indonesian users experience HelloTalk as a digital communication space for Korean language learning, using New Media Theory and Computer-Mediated Communication (CMC) as its analytical framework. A qualitative approach with a post-positivist paradigm was applied. Five Indonesian HelloTalk users who actively learn Korean were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation, and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, with source and technique triangulation. The findings show that informants experience HelloTalk as an interconnected, accessible, interactive, and open-ended space that enables them to communicate with native speakers, receive peer correction, share content, and learn flexibly across time and place. Within the CMC dimensions, informants emphasized wide access to information, fast message exchange, varied learning input, and motivation, while the perceived usefulness of the application depended on the intensity and purpose of use. Informants also reported constraints related to VIP features, time differences, and device limitations. The study argues that HelloTalk functions as a participatory digital communication space in which Korean language learning takes place through interpersonal interaction, peer correction, and user-generated content. The study does not measure language proficiency.

title: The impact of sensorimotor and cognitive capacity on the kinematic performance of instrumental activities of daily living across the lifespan
dbe6069fe100492c67c43ff90f2b11ccfce543f9.abstract: Abstract Background With advancing adult age, sensorimotor and cognitive capacity (e.g., muscular strength) are declining and limitations in instrumental activities of daily living (iADL) are frequently reported. The translation of individual capacity to iADL performance represents a significant research object not only to better understand everyday life behavior but also to apply preventive measures in time. Due to the submaximal nature of iADL, we aimed to identify transition points, beyond which associations between capacity and performance appear, i.e., iADL stop to be submaximal. Methods A set of sensorimotor and cognitive capacity tests and kinematic analyses of hand movements in different complex kitchen tasks were conducted in a sample of 95 healthy adults with an age span of 18 to 93a. An iADL score was derived from the kinematics using a principal component analysis. Transition point segmented regression analyses were applied to examine the association of capacity and the iADL score. Results Most tests reacted to ageing and (negative) outlier frequencies in capacity and, to a weaker extent, in kinematics increased with advancing age. Transition points were identified in most tests and confirmed our hypothesis but were generally high. The best iADL performance was observed in persons between 42 and 58a despite decreased capacity. Discussion It appeared that iADL can be limited by impaired capacity, but profit from experience that can compensate capacity losses to a certain degree. The high transition points point towards the need for early interventions long before subtle alterations in iADL performance become subjectively observable.

title: The Application of the Inquiry Learning Model to Enhance Critical Thinking Skills in Science and Social Studies (IPAS) Instruction for Grade III  Students at SD Negeri 3 Kota Mobagu
container-title: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
070178c4c71681ca5f659e42c59b3321cd362642.abstract: This classroom action research aimed to improve students' critical thinking skills through the Inquiry Learning model in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) lessons on heat energy sources in Grade III at SD Negeri 3 Kotamobagu. The study was conducted in two cycles with 29 students, each cycle consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. Data were collected through an essay test based on five of Ennis' critical thinking indicators (Focus, Reason, Inference, Situation, Clarity) and through observation of teacher and student activities. In Cycle I, the mean critical thinking score was 58.10, with classical mastery (minimum category Good, score ≥ 60) of 51.72%; student activity was 66.25% and teacher activity was 71.43%, both in the Good category. After improvements in Cycle II, namely stronger teacher guidance, guiding questions, and greater student involvement in inquiry activities, the mean score rose to 77.76 with classical mastery of 93.10%; student activity increased to 88.75% and teacher activity to 91.96%, both in the Very Good category. Based on the school's learning objective achievement criterion (score ≥ 75), classical mastery rose from 24.14% to 72.41%, which is still below the 75% target. These results indicate an improvement in students' critical thinking after the implementation of the Inquiry Learning model.

title: KEPRAKTISAN MODEL PEMBELAJARAN SOSIAL EMOSIONAL BERBASIS VIDEO YOUTUBE MINIVILA SEBAGAI MEDIA SCAFFOLDING PADA SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR

d27fb1f1b450c21fe825cad9cbf7215fa2c8de4d.abstract: This study aimed to develop and examine the practicality of a social-emotional learning model based on educational videos from the Minivila YouTube channel as a scaffolding medium for early-grade elementary school students. The study employed a research and development approach adapting the ADDIE model, comprising needs analysis, model design, video product development, expert validation, and limited field trials. The participants involved 10 teachers and 100 early-grade elementary school students selected via purposive sampling. Practicality data were gathered through teacher questionnaires, student questionnaires, and classroom observation sheets, which were subsequently analyzed using descriptive quantitative and qualitative methods. The results revealed that the teacher response reached 94.57% (very practical) and the student response reached 88.78% (very practical). These findings imply that video-based scaffolding guided by a host figure provides a structured, communicative, and practical medium for embedding social-emotional learning in lower elementary classrooms.

title: A Bangla-language retrieval-augmented conversational agent for maternal health in a low-resource setting: design and formative evaluation
b7a713fa17d14289e6fb35f7ac651b94d58a8580.abstract: Abstract Maternal health information in Bangladesh is difficult to access for women with limited literacy and no English, and perinatal mental health remains under-supported. We designed and formatively evaluated Baby and Me, a Bangla-language conversational agent that retrieves from a curated, physician-reviewed corpus of 247 maternal health articles, segmented into 2,945 indexed passages, and generates responses grounded in the retrieved material. A survey of 72 pregnant and postpartum women established design requirements; Bangla-only language preference was universal among women with no formal or primary education, and a quarter of households reported annual income below one lakh Bangladeshi taka. Candidate model configurations were screened against physician-authored reference answers before deployment. Twenty-four respondents then rated the deployed system: ease of use was highest (mean 4.79 of 5) and clarity strong (4.54), while trust (4.29), concern alignment (4.04) and empathy (4.00) were lower and more dispersed. Interviews indicated that the interface showed users that retrieval had occurred but not whether guidance came from aclinically reviewed source, suggesting that process transparency and source attribution are not interchangeable. As a formative study with a modest sample, a single site and no controlled comparison, this work establishes feasibility rather than effectiveness.

title: Lenguaje, postautonomía y común en Facsímil de Alejandro Zambra
Language, Post-Autonomy, and the Common in Alejandro Zambra’s Facsímil
container-title: Cuadernos de Literatura
7572029dbe3e57062ffd39e9416aba66c1bdf219.abstract: This article examines Alejandro Zambra’s Facsímil through the lens of literary post-autonomy, within the context of informational capitalism and biopolitics. It argues that the work subverts the format of the Chilean university entrance exam, shifting from exchange value to use value through a situated writing that articulates the common. The study concludes that Facsímil reconfigures literature as a space of resistance and collective production.​

title: PENERAPAN MODEL PROJECT BASED LEARNING (PjBL)  UNTUK MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR IPAS  SISWA KELAS III UPTD SDN 071030 AFIA

823691802aa3e64c0bbfa43ba95bf7589e8c387b.abstract: Learning outcomes are one of the indicators of the success of the learning process. However, the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia are still relatively low, necessitating a learning model that can improve student learning outcomes. This study aims to improve the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia through the implementation of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model. The research design used was Classroom Action Research (CAR), conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of the planning, implementation, observation, and reflection stages. The research subjects were 20 third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia. Data collection techniques included tests, observations, and documentation. The data were analyzed both quantitatively and qualitatively. The results showed that students’ IPAS learning outcomes in the pre-cycle stage were 30%, then increased to 60% in Cycle I, and rose further to 85% in Cycle II. Based on the research results, it can be concluded that the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model is effective in improving the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia.

title: IMPLEMENTASI MODEL PEMBELAJARAN MAKE A MATCH DALAM MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA KELAS II SD
container-title: STRATEGY : Jurnal Inovasi Strategi dan Model Pembelajaran
6aeb47e471531ba166d18dd50975dd8035e9b78b.abstract: Low learning outcomes in Pancasila Education among second-grade students at UPTD SD Negeri 076674 Orahili Tanoseo indicated the need for a more active and engaging learning process. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Make a Match learning model and the improvement of students’ learning outcomes on the topic “I Care for the Environment.” The study employed Classroom Action Research based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. The participants were 14 second-grade students, consisting of 6 boys and 8 girls. Data were collected through observations of teacher and student activities, learning achievement tests, and field notes. The data were analyzed using qualitative and quantitative descriptive techniques. The results showed an increase in teacher activity from 51% in the first meeting of Cycle I to 92% in the second meeting of Cycle II. Student activity increased from 58% to 95% across the same meetings. Learning outcomes also improved: the mean score in Cycle I was 67.7, with 36% mastery or 5 of 14 students, while Cycle II reached a mean score of 81.6, with 85% mastery or 12 students. The classical mastery therefore exceeded the predetermined success indicator of 75%. Thus, the Make a Match learning model can be used as an alternative approach to increase student engagement and learning outcomes in Pancasila Education at the elementary school level.

title: PENERAPAN MODEL KOOPERATIF TIPE NUMBERED HEAD TOGETHER DALAM MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA MURID KELAS IV
container-title: STRATEGY : Jurnal Inovasi Strategi dan Model Pembelajaran
5f7412aa4d63240a1fc943ebe9f91f9e0447ef63.abstract: The learning outcomes of fourth-grade students in Pancasila Education at UPTD SD Negeri 074048 Luaha Bouso were still low because previous learning tended to be teacher-centered, resulting in limited student activity, collaboration, and participation. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Numbered Head Together (NHT) cooperative learning model and to determine the improvement of students' learning outcomes in Pancasila Education after its implementation. The study employed Classroom Action Research using the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of planning, action, observation, and reflection, with two meetings in each cycle. The subjects were 19 fourth-grade students in the 2025/2026 academic year. Data were collected through observations of teacher and student activities, learning outcome tests, documentation, and field notes, and were analyzed descriptively using qualitative and quantitative approaches. The NHT implementation involved heterogeneous group formation, assigning numbers to group members, presenting questions or tasks, group discussion, random number calling, presentation of answers, and reinforcement. The findings showed that teacher activity increased from 58% in Cycle I Meeting I to 90% in Cycle II Meeting II, while student activity increased from 57.69% to 94.23%. Learning outcomes also improved, as indicated by an increase in the mean score from 62.68 in Cycle I to 80.63 in Cycle II and classical mastery from 47.37% to 84.21%. Therefore, the implementation of NHT improved student participation and learning outcomes in Pancasila Education.

title: Assessing acceptability, feasibility, and utilization in a peer-to-peer tele-critical care model: a mixed-methods analysis to inform scalable remote ICU models
container-title: BMC Anesthesiology
9b302b0de8ed7eacba36c43be98e0a8e74ae6bf7.abstract: Abstract Introduction Critical care in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like Pakistan, particularly in remote areas, is constrained by limited infrastructure and expertise. Telemedicine can bridge this gap by connecting frontline ICU physicians with remote critical care experts. While tele-ICU models have been evaluated in high-income settings, limited evidence exists from LMICs. This study evaluated the acceptability, feasibility, and utilization of a peer-to-peer tele-ICU consultation service launched by Aga Khan University in Pakistan. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods study using 145 survey responses and 10 in-depth interviews of physicians who had utilized a national Tele-ICU consultation service. Quantitative data were collected using a structured survey. Qualitative data were obtained through open-ended survey responses and 10 in-depth interviews. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis by two independent reviewers to identify key themes related to service use, quality, and feasibility. Results Of 219 physicians, 145 (66.2%) responded. Consultations primarily occurred via voice (77.2%) and text (43.4%). Respondents reported high satisfaction across clinical (mean 4.50), process (3.82), and technical (4.18) domains. Key benefits included knowledge enhancement, support for complex cases, and ease of access. The Net Promoter Score was 40.7, indicating favorable satisfaction. Thematic analysis confirmed high satisfaction but highlighted utilization barriers, including administrative hurdles and the difficulty of implementing standardized recommendations within local resource constraints. Conclusion The peer-to-peer Tele-ICU model was perceived as highly acceptable and clinically useful by bedside physician physicians. However, infrastructure resource and workflow limitations might affect its implementation. These finding highlight the potential of remote critical care consultation while identifying the barriers that must be addressed to support wider implementation in resource-limited settings. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Reading–Writing Integration Through ChatGPT-Supported Feedback: Growth, Associations, and Mediated Pathways of Student Engagement in Chinese Classrooms
745d8e2e69b90ad0d1a802097a837b9611e814db.abstract: Abstract Although reading–writing integration has been increasingly advocated in Chinese language education, limited empirical evidence explains how reading, writing, and student engagement become integrated, particularly under AI-supported feedback. To address this issue, this study examined whether ChatGPT-supported feedback improved reading outcomes, writing outcomes, and student engagement, while investigating their interrelationships, the mediating role of student engagement, and the corresponding pathways in reading–writing integration. A total of 400 middle school students from eight intact classes in Shenzhen participated, with 200 students receiving ChatGPT-supported feedback and 200 receiving human-generated feedback. Using a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design, data were analyzed within a quantitative longitudinal framework integrating baseline equivalence tests, 2 × 2 mixed-design ANOVAs, factor-level correlation analyses, and multi-group cross-lagged path analysis to examine changes and temporal relationships among reading, student engagement, and writing across two groups (N = 400). Despite comparable pretest scores, findings showed that Group 1 demonstrated significantly greater pretest–posttest gains in reading, student engagement, and writing, with significant Time × Group interactions and large effects. Correlations further indicated stronger posttest associations among engagement, reading, and writing in Group 1, whereas these relationships remained weak in Group 2. Longitudinal analyses revealed stronger T2 within-time direct and mediating pathways in Group 1, alongside several significant cross-lagged effects, but cross-lagged mediating effects were generally nonsignificant in both groups. The findings theoretically highlight student engagement as a potentially time-sensitive mechanism through which AI-supported learning may strengthen the integration of reading and writing. Practically, they suggest the pedagogical value of AI-supported learning environments for fostering engagement and connecting literacy processes, while emphasizing sustained instructional exposure to consolidate these relationships over time.

title: Brain Tissue Proportionality and General Cognitive Ability Across Three Adult Cohorts
a34e4de781115c698ea0e18eaae41c1c80102edd.abstract: Abstract General cognitive ability may relate to the proportional allocation of brain tissue beyond overall tissue volume. We examined five FreeSurfer compartments using compositional data analysis: cortical gray matter, cerebral white matter, subcortical gray matter, total cerebellum, and brainstem. Human Connectome Project Young Adult data (HCP-YA; N = 1,101) provided discovery estimates; the Dallas Lifespan Brain Study (DLBS; N = 418) and Amsterdam Open MRI Collection ID1000 (AOMIC; N = 926) provided independent cohort tests. Four isometric log-ratio coordinates represented composition, with age, sex, and log total analyzed tissue volume included separately. Composition explained additional cognitive variance in DLBS (partial R² = 4.20%, p = .00154) and AOMIC (partial R² = 1.35%, p = .014). The total-cerebellum-to-cerebral-white-matter contrast selected in HCP was positive in both replication cohorts: standardized β = 0.162 (heteroskedasticity-robust 95% confidence interval 0.072–0.252) in DLBS and 0.097 (0.024–0.170) in AOMIC. Participant-pairs bootstrap intervals supported both associations. Replacing total tissue volume with estimated intracranial volume attenuated the AOMIC association, whereas including both preserved it. Relative macroanatomical allocation is associated with broad cognitive ability conditional on analyzed tissue volume, with differing effect magnitudes across cohorts. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causal tissue trade-offs.

title: From AI readiness to regenerative tourism orientation: a tourist-centric model of smart tourism villages
container-title: ABAC Journal
600067ed573dc780c1bd155c47ed81d59d2f7b38.abstract: Purpose This study develops and validates a tourist-centric model of AI-driven smart tourism villages (AI-DSTV), explaining how perceived digital infrastructure and smart governance relate to tourist acceptance and perceived regenerative tourism orientation (PRTO) through rural authenticity, value co-creation, AI trust, and perceived service value. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey involved 686 domestic tourists who had experienced an AI-supported tourism touchpoint in rural tourism settings in Indonesia. The sample was predominantly young and digitally engaged, with 75.1% aged 18–24 and 68.4% students. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings All 12 hypothesized relationships were significant. Rural authenticity strongly enhanced perceived AI service value, while tourist value co-creation strengthened AI trust and ethical acceptance. Digital infrastructure and smart governance also showed significant downstream effects through authenticity–service-value and co-creation–trust pathways. The model explained 56.3% of PRTO variance. IPMA identified AI trust and ethical acceptance as the most important antecedent of PRTO and the lowest-performing construct, indicating a key managerial priority. Practical implications Rural destinations should prioritize transparent, culturally grounded, participatory and locally accountable AI systems. Strengthening ethical trust, co-creation, and culturally appropriate personalization may offer greater managerial leverage than technological sophistication alone. Originality/value The study extends technology-adoption research beyond behavioral acceptance by introducing PRTO as a tourist-level psychological outcome. It conceptualizes AI-DSTV as a socio-technical ecosystem linking destination readiness with authenticity, co-creation, trust and service evaluation while distinguishing regenerative orientation from verified destination regeneration.

title: White coats in the news feed: the effects of content features on physicians' engagement behaviors in online academic medical communities
container-title: Aslib Journal of Information Management
7353f574ac1fb297470e88c542e86cf0e544ddfd.abstract: Purpose Online academic medical communities (OAMCs) have become central channels for physicians to exchange medical knowledge. Yet a substantial share of physician-generated medical content on these platforms fails to elicit meaningful peer engagement, constraining the dissemination of medical knowledge. Given that the intrinsic features of content in OAMCs are likely key drivers of peer engagement, understanding what makes content appealing is essential. However, the relationship remains unclear. This study aims to address this gap by examining how distinct content features influence different forms of peer engagement in OAMCs. Design/methodology/approach Leveraging data from a leading Chinese OAMC, we operationalize six content features (complexity, subjectivity, professionalism, completeness, informativeness, multimodal information presentation) via natural language processing and examine their effects on physicians' collecting and interacting behaviors and the moderating role of disease severity. Findings Peer physicians prioritize information-rich content for collecting, while favoring discussion-oriented content for interacting. Multimodal, comprehensive content is welcomed, whereas overly sophisticated, highly specialized content is less effective. Disease severity moderates these relationships, with physicians exhibiting greater selectivity in collecting but more interactive under high-severity conditions. Originality/value This study is among the first to uncover the impact of content features on physicians' engagement behaviors while considering disease severity as the moderating variable. By incorporating natural language processing techniques, it extends the information adoption model to online physician platforms and offers actionable guidance for optimizing physician online engagement.

title: Bimbingan Kelompok Teknik Sosiodrama untuk Meningkatkan Regulasi Emosi Siswa SMP
container-title: Observasi : Jurnal Publikasi Ilmu Psikologi
42782bb44b85021f9a458bbdc524f4142cbf50a4.abstract: Emotion regulation among junior high school students remains suboptimal, while school guidance and counseling services tend to be informative and curative. This study reviews the literature on early adolescents' emotion regulation and the effectiveness of sociodrama-based group guidance, and formulates directions for research and practice based on the gaps identified. A literature review with a systematic approach following PRISMA 2020 was conducted on national and international articles published from 2015 to 2026, complemented by preliminary data from SMP Negeri 2 Babelan, Bekasi Regency. The review yields three findings. First, emotion regulation problems among Indonesian adolescents are widespread: 34.9% of adolescents aged 10–17 experience mental health problems, and at the target school 56.86% of students reported difficulty controlling emotions and 87.5% of 367 students fell into the moderate and low categories. Second, studies of sociodrama and role-play group guidance consistently report gains in emotion regulation, but rely on small samples (8–16 students) and designs without control groups. Third, four research gaps emerge: empirical, conceptual, contextual, and analytical. The review proposes sociodrama designed on Gross's process model, tested in a peri-urban school, and analyzed by gender and baseline emotion regulation level.

title: Semantic-Enhanced Graph Regularization Hashing for Large-Scale Cross-Modal Retrieval
container-title: Data Science and Engineering
30f44c37efba6ea513b029ac6b88eb861379da13.abstract: Abstract In the area of large-scale data, cross-modal hashing has attracted significant attention for fast similarity search task due to its low storage requirements and fast retrieval speed. Existing supervised cross-modal hashing learning methods have made extensive attempts to fully exploit supervisory information. Different from previous work, we propose a method named S emantic- E nhanced G raph R egularization H ashing ( SEGRH ), which contributes a new and novel exploration to this research domain. Specifically, our method consists of two core components: contrastive cross-modal fusion and robust semantic preservation. We adopt the pre-trained CLIP model as the backbone to extract modality-specific features, which are subsequently fused via a multimodal Transformer. Robust semantic preservation is designed to mine and integrate high-quality semantic information. SEGRH first leverages positive pointwise mutual information to convert label information into semantic association metrics. Second, the graph Laplacian is incorporated to absorb such semantic cues and further constrain the structure of the hash space. Our SEGRH is capable of performing high-quality multimodal learning and possesses strong semantic consistency modeling capabilities, thereby achieving satisfactory generalization performance. Experimental results on three standard datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods.

title: Digital Agency and the Preservation of the Banggai Language Among the Younger Generation in Banggai City
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
82dd679ddd2968dd144017e18e33b75be95f7aca.abstract: Regional languages are essential components of cultural identity, serving not only as means of communication but also as vehicles for transmitting values, knowledge, and local wisdom across generations. Banggai, spoken in Banggai Laut Regency, has shown signs of declining use among younger generations in family and educational settings. Meanwhile, digital technology offers new opportunities for regional language use and dissemination. This study examines the forms, functions, and factors influencing Banggai language maintenance among young people in Banggai City through the perspective of digital agency, which views youth as active and creative users of digital technology. This qualitative case study involved 29 respondents who completed open-ended questionnaires and three informants who participated in in-depth interviews. Participants aged 15–30 years were purposively selected. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, with source and methodological triangulation. The findings show that 19 respondents use Banggai on social media, primarily in informal conversations with fellow speakers. However, none reported producing Banggai-language content or collaborating on content creation, while digital resources, such as dictionaries, were rarely used. Digital spaces help maintain language use and strengthen linguistic identity and pride, although their contribution to broader language use, learning, and intergenerational transmission remains largely potential. Key supporting factors include preservation motivation and family and school support. Major barriers include limited language use in families and communities, the influence of Indonesian and other languages, restricted vocabulary, social stigma, and scarce digital content and learning resources. Limited device and internet access were not reported as barriers. This study refines digital agency by distinguishing language-use agency from content-production and collaborative agency, highlighting the need for youth-driven digital resources supported by families, schools, and local governments.

title: Successful Rezūm water vapor thermal therapy in a patient with extremely large prostate volume: a case report
container-title: African Journal of Urology
80b8da76a7a29fbd45f835cc0f4c57271e2e3309.abstract: Abstract Background Rezūm water vapor therapy is typically recommended for prostates < 80 mL. Case presentation We report the case of a patient with a prostate measuring 297 mL by transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) who achieved catheter independence and marked symptom improvement following Rezūm therapy. Despite the exceptionally large gland size, the procedure was feasible and resulted in improvements in IPSS and Qmax, and a reduction in PSA at one-year follow-up. Conclusions This case suggests that Rezūm may be a feasible minimally invasive option for carefully selected patients with extremely large prostates.

title: Predicting teachers’ intentions to implement bring your own device and take-home student device programs: a cognitive-affective-behavior framework with sem-ann analysis
container-title: BMC Psychology
c08c91f3c76828a754da5e52d4925d2b352b6979.abstract: Abstract Background Limited attention has been given to teachers’ intentions to implement Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) and Take-Home Student Device (THSD) as an integrated digital learning initiative, particularly from a psychological perspective. Accordingly, this study examines K-12 teachers’ behavioral intention to implement BYOD​ and ​THSD​ programs using the Cognitive–Affective–Behavior (CAB) framework. Methods A survey was conducted with 176 K-12 teachers in Taiwan. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN) analysis, and Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). Results Understanding, ability, and self-confidence were positively associated with behavioral intention. Self-confidence mediated the relationships between the two cognitive factors and behavioral intention. In addition, the IPMA results showed that ability had the highest importance value, followed by self-confidence, whereas understanding showed the highest performance but the lowest importance. Conclusions The findings suggest that teachers’ readiness to implement BYOD and THSD depends not only on their understanding of the programs but also on their perceived ability and confidence to manage the demands of implementation. The study extends CAB-based research on educational technology implementation and provides implications for teacher preparation and digital education policy.

title: Development of an Integrated Aided Language Stimulation (ALS) Intervention Model to Improve Expressive Communication in Autistic Children at UPTD Disability Services Sidoarjo
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
b7b0d11d53ab60f86fec6738c0cba48871fcc2a1.abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often experience difficulties in expressive communication, including requesting, responding, expressing needs, initiating interaction, and maintaining communication. This study aimed to develop an Intervention Model Integrated Aided Language Stimulation (ALS) with Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) to support expressive communication among autistic children at UPTD Services Disability Sidoarjo, Indonesia. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the Four-D model comprising Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate stages. The developed model integrated AAC media, ALS language modeling, functional communication activities, communication opportunities, partner responsiveness, reinforcement, generalization, and evaluation. Expert validation involved four validators representing four areas of expertise: subject matter, special education/autism, communication/AAC, and media. The validation percentage was calculated by dividing the obtained score by the maximum possible score and multiplying by 100%, resulting in 90.5% (very valid). Practicality was assessed through responses from teachers, therapists, and/or companions using the same percentage formula, resulting in 90% (very practical), while implementation was assessed through structured observation and reached 91% (very good). A one-group pretest-posttest limited trial involving five autistic children showed an increase in expressive communication scores from 42/100 (mean = 4.2) to 76/100 (mean = 7.6). The mean N-Gain was 0.65, categorized as moderate improvement according to the study criteria. Because the limited trial involved only five children and did not include a control group, the observed improvement should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of intervention effectiveness. Overall, the findings support the model’s feasibility for further investigation with larger samples and more rigorous comparative designs.

title: Postoperative Behavioural, Cognitive, And Psychological Changes Following General Versus Regional Anaesthesia: A Narrative Review
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
d621feb3aec9694aeab17a9eca4e4b5f53f16d83.abstract: Postoperative behavioural, cognitive, and psychological changes represent an important spectrum of recovery-related complications after surgery and anaesthesia. This narrative review examines the available evidence comparing general anaesthesia with regional anaesthesia, with particular attention to postoperative delirium, delayed neurocognitive recovery, postoperative neurocognitive disorder, behavioural changes, and psychological outcomes. The available literature suggests that these outcomes are multifactorial and are influenced by patient vulnerability, surgical stress, inflammation, pain, sleep disturbance, medications, haemodynamic and respiratory changes, and anaesthetic exposure. Comparative evidence has not consistently demonstrated superiority of regional over general anaesthesia for prevention of postoperative delirium or cognitive dysfunction. Regional techniques may reduce exposure to general anaesthetic agents and postoperative opioid requirements in selected settings, but sedation and other perioperative factors can confound comparisons. Preoperative risk assessment, appropriate anaesthetic depth, effective analgesia, physiological optimisation, and multimodal postoperative care remain important components of prevention. Further well-designed studies using standardised definitions, baseline cognitive assessment, validated outcome measures, and adequate follow-up are needed.

title: Bite-block effects on native s/ʃ and English r/l in child speakers of a language with/without this contrast
container-title: Frontiers in Human Neuroscience
d15c4702e6480bd35e07fb78dd49ffa982f77bdc.abstract: Learning to produce non-native speech contrasts requires developing new phonological categories as well as new articulatory-perceptual mappings for these new categories. However, within the same speakers, it remains unclear how these new categories compare to contrasts that are already fully established in the native language. To examine potential differences between native and non-native sounds, we recorded Japanese children’s (8–12 years) productions of a non-native contrast (English /ɹ/−/l/, indexed by F3–F2) and a native contrast (/s/−/ʃ/, indexed by Center of Gravity). Recordings were done both under normal speaking conditions and under articulatory perturbation induced by a temporary bite-block while listening to a model. Children acoustically differentiated both contrasts under normal speaking conditions, but the two contrasts showed different developmental profiles: differentiation of the native contrast did not vary with age, whereas differentiation of the non-native contrast was significant only in older children. As expected, the bite-block manipulation reduced acoustic distinctness for both contrasts; however, susceptibility to this disruption was age-invariant for the native contrast but increased with age for the non-native contrast.

title: Association between serum ferritin levels and mild cognitive impairment risk in middle-aged and older adults: evidence from the health and retirement study
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
a1dd5cd07688a1411d3f46db5c11fee6690ac5d0.abstract: Background Ferritin serves as the main iron-storage form in the human body. Iron ions are critical for numerous brain-related physiological processes. This study aimed to explore the association between serum ferritin levels and the risk of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in middle-aged and older adults. Methods Participants aged 50 years and above with available cognitive function assessments were selected from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) database. Baseline data for this retrospective cohort study were collected in 2016, and MCI occurrence was recorded through 2022. Cognitive function was assessed using tests of episodic memory and executive function. The primary MCI outcome was based on an operational cognitive-score definition rather than a clinical MCI diagnosis: the cognitive function score was at least one standard deviation (SD) below the age-specific normative value. Cox regression models were employed to explore the association between serum ferritin [tertiles: &lt;76 μg/L, 76-151 μg/L (reference group), ≥151 μg/L] and MCI risk, as well as impairments in episodic memory and executive function. Results A total of 6,572 participants were enrolled in the analytical cohort. Of these, 1,435 (21.84%) participants developed MCI, while 5,137 (78.16%) were free of MCI events. Individuals with serum ferritin ≥151 μg/L were related to a higher risk of MCI [HR = 1.15 (95%CI: 1.01–1.31)] compared to those with serum ferritin 76-151 μg/L, but no association was found in those with serum ferritin &lt;76 μg/L [HR = 1.04 (95%CI: 0.91–1.19)]. Serum ferritin levels showed a significant U-shaped non-linear association with MCI risk ( P non-linear = 0.03). Moreover, individuals with serum ferritin ≥151 μg/L were associated with a higher risk of episodic memory impairment [HR = 1.15 (95%CI: 1.01–1.30)] versus those with serum ferritin 76–151 μg/L. No significant associations were found between serum ferritin and executive dysfunction [HR = 0.99 (95%CI: 0.90–1.10)]. Conclusion High serum ferritin levels were associated with an increased risk of MCI among middle-aged and older adults, especially episodic memory impairment.

title: Model Pre-Solution Posing: Meningkatkan Kemampuan Pemecahan Masalah Matematis pada Materi Pecahan Kelas VI Sekolah Dasar
container-title: JUDIKDAS: Jurnal Ilmu Pendidikan Dasar Indonesia
90637510e1c4d10c0d7233e807fe6619c389ce1f.abstract: Kemampuan memecahkan soal cerita pecahan di kelas VI sekolah dasar masih rendah. Pada tes awal, hanya satu dari 24 murid mencapai kriteria ketuntasan minimal (75), padahal murid yang sama mampu mengerjakan hitungan pecahan biasa dengan baik. Penelitian ini bertujuan meningkatkan kemampuan pemecahan masalah materi pecahan melalui model pengajuan soal tipe pre-solution posing, yaitu murid menyusun soal dari situasi yang diberikan guru lalu menyelesaikannya. Penelitian tindakan kelas ini mengikuti model Kemmis dan McTaggart dalam dua siklus, masing-masing dua pertemuan, dengan subjek seluruh murid kelas VI. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes uraian berdasarkan empat tahap Polya, asesmen diagnostik, serta lembar observasi aktivitas murid dan keterlaksanaan pembelajaran, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Nilai rata-rata meningkat dari 31,5 (SD = 17,4) pada tes awal menjadi 80,4 (SD = 16,3) pada siklus pertama dan 88,4 (SD = 17,4) pada siklus kedua. Persentase murid yang tuntas naik dari 4,2% menjadi 66,7% dan 79,2%, sehingga indikator keberhasilan tercapai pada siklus kedua. Gain ternormalisasi terhadap tes awal sebesar 0,83 (kategori tinggi). Dibandingkan tes awal, peningkatan terbesar terjadi pada tahap memeriksa kembali, sedangkan antarsiklus peningkatan terbesar terjadi pada tahap merencanakan penyelesaian. Lima murid masih memerlukan pendampingan khusus. Model ini layak dipertimbangkan guru untuk melatih murid menentukan operasi hitung pada soal cerita, dan perlu diuji lebih lanjut pada kelas pembanding.

title: Lifestyle associations with hypertension and diabetes risk via metabolic function and physical indicators: a cross-sectional serial mediation model among community adults
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
3f41b31659159fb1e18614bd7be034416f070ced.abstract: Objective To examine whether lifestyle is associated with hypertension and diabetes risk via sequential indirect pathways involving metabolic function and physical indicators among community adults. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 6,178 community adults in Nanning, southern China. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to examine the direct and indirect associations among lifestyle, metabolic function, physical indicators, and disease risk. Bias-corrected bootstrap analyses with 5,000 resamples were performed to evaluate indirect associations. Results The model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.917, RMSEA = 0.048); the chi-square/df ratio (5.19) was elevated, as is common in samples of this size. Physical indicators exhibited the strongest direct association with disease risk ( β = 0.763, P &lt; 0.001), while metabolic function was also positively associated with disease risk ( β = 0.048, P = 0.010). Healthy lifestyle was associated with lower disease risk via indirect pathways involving physical indicators alone ( β = −0.360, P = 0.001) and via the sequential indirect pathway involving metabolic function and physical indicators ( β = −0.011, P = 0.021). For unhealthy lifestyle, indirect associations with higher disease risk were observed via metabolic function ( β = 0.003, P = 0.036) and physical indicators ( β = 0.092, P = 0.014), whereas the sequential indirect pathway was not statistically significant ( P = 0.104). Direct associations of lifestyle with disease risk were small in magnitude (| β | ≤ 0.035) and of limited clinical importance; only the direct association of unhealthy lifestyle reached statistical significance ( β = −0.035, P = 0.013). Conclusion In this cross-sectional sample, lifestyle was associated with hypertension and diabetes risk primarily via indirect pathways involving metabolic function and physical indicators. These findings should be interpreted as correlational and cannot establish causality. They highlight the importance of integrated lifestyle management and early metabolic risk assessment for the prevention of hypertension and diabetes in community settings.

title: Development and internal validation of an interpretable machine learning-based risk stratification model for sarcopenic obesity in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
6dc60ab5481f90f36f0a7911b58344657b56f308.abstract: Objective To analyze the factors associated with sarcopenic obesity (SO) in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2DM), and to develop and internally validate an SO risk stratification model based on interpretable machine learning, thereby providing guidance for the clinical screening of high-risk patients and the implementation of personalized risk assessment. Methods A single-center cross-sectional study design was adopted, enrolling 378 patients with T2DM, who were divided into an SO group and a non-SO group based on SO diagnostic results. Demographic characteristics, disease-related data, anthropometric measurements, and laboratory test results were collected. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set ( n = 265) and a validation set ( n = 113) in a 7:3 ratio. Univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with SO, and based on these results, five risk-stratification models were constructed: logistic regression, random forest, SVM, LightGBM, and XGBoost. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), accuracy, sensitivity, recall, precision, F1 score, and Brier score. Model calibration performance and clinical applicability were assessed using calibration curves, calibration slope, calibration intercept, calibration-in-the-large (CITL), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Supplementary internal validation of the LightGBM model was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and interpretability analysis was conducted using the SHAP method. Results In this study, the detection rate of SO in patients with T2DM was 36.2%, age, ADL, waist circumference, HDL, and 25(OH)D were the primary factors influencing SO. The AUC values of the five models on the validation set ranged from 0.806 to 0.821. Among them, LightGBM achieved the numerically highest AUC in this sample, at 0.821 (95% CI: 0.744–0.897), with an AUPRC of 0.712; however, the DeLong test indicated that the differences in AUC among the models were not statistically significant (all P &gt; 0.05). Overall, the models demonstrated good calibration performance and potential clinical net benefit; however, bootstrap internal validation indicated that LightGBM still exhibited a certain degree of optimism bias and under-calibration. SHAP analysis revealed that age, ADL, waist circumference, HDL, and 25(OH)D contributed significantly to model predictions, with age being the most important predictive feature. Conclusion The SO risk stratification models developed using machine learning methods demonstrated good performance and potential clinical utility, with LightGBM achieving the highest numerical performance. SHAP-based interpretability analysis enhanced model transparency and clinical credibility, providing a reference for assisted screening, risk stratification, and individualized assessment of SO in patients with T2DM.

title: Measuring risk preferences in large language models using adaptive binary search
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
c858d4cf3d1582c91bca6e51bed245e78c2a72cc.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support decision-making in high-stakes domains, where a model's risk preference, its tendency to favor lower-risk or higher-risk options under uncertainty, can shape the decisions it supports. Prior studies measuring these preferences in LLMs have produced mixed results. Several used fixed designs, such as choice lists, which locate the point where a preference changes only as finely as their preset values allow. Adaptive procedures, which adjust each query to earlier responses, concentrate measurement near that point and are established for eliciting human risk preferences. We present such a procedure for LLMs: it poses a choice between a lower-risk and a higher-risk option, varies the expected value of the higher-risk option across steps, locates by binary search the model's tipping point, the point at which its outputs shift to favor the higher-risk option, and reports it as an index of risk preference under one probability structure. We applied the procedure to eight LLMs from four providers (OpenAI, San Francisco, CA, USA; Anthropic, San Francisco, CA, USA; Google, Mountain View, CA, USA; xAI, Palo Alto, CA, USA), using emergency and disaster management vignettes, and tested whether presenting each option's expected value explicitly, rather than leaving it to be inferred, changed the measured preference. Median tipping points for six of the eight models fell near the point of equal expected value under both presentations. Claude Sonnet 4.6's tipping point was higher when the expected value was left to be inferred, with a shift whose bootstrap interval excludes 0; Claude Haiku 4.5's was higher as a point estimate, but its shift interval includes 0. In individual queries, deviations from expected-value maximization concentrated in four models: those of the two Anthropic models all toward the lower-risk option and those of the two Google models almost all toward the higher-risk option. Over the range queried in both presentations, presenting the expected value explicitly reduced these deviations in all four models. Because the two presentations convey the same expected values, the reduction indicates that these models did not respond to them as equivalent. The procedure applies to any model accessible via a text interface and is a reusable tool for comparing and screening models for risk-related decision support.

title: Exploring the nexus of climate-socioeconomic drivers of dengue transmission: a covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI mechanistic model
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
7ee953370ccb5f005a77b7829073a0d6c44813ab.abstract: A deterministic covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI model is developed and used to gain insight into the nexus between climate and socioeconomic parameters and the transmission dynamics of dengue. The model developed a framework that incorporates two external influences: climate and socioeconomic factors. The model is rigorously analyzed, with disease-free and endemic equilibria investigated, and is simulated using data relevant to Medellín, Colombia. We then employ machine learning algorithms as an empirical feature-selection step to identify and rank socioeconomic predictors of dengue incidence, revealing that the unemployed population is the dominant socioeconomic driver. This finding motivates the selection of unemployment as the socioeconomic covariate in the mechanistic model. From our numerical simulation, we computed using temperature only and combined [temperature + socioeconomic (unemployment)] parameters to determine how their influences drive the epidemic spread. Our model suggests that socioeconomic influence can act as a driver alongside temperature, increasing the transmission rate and leading to an earlier peak. The framework is appropriate for endemic settings where socioeconomic and climatic factors are the primary drivers of transmission dynamics. The approach demonstrates how empirical machine-learning insights can inform covariate selection in mechanistic epidemiological models, thereby strengthening interpretation of how socioeconomic and climatic conditions interact to shape epidemic potential.

title: Navigating boundary-less work: how family-supportive leadership reshapes the impact of work-family blurring on professional women’s job engagement and taking charge in the digital transformation
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
71f63b0d55cc469e7c3e29593c1806e48b62c98a.abstract: In the context of a digital transformation that is fundamentally refining the nature of work and leadership dynamics, this research examines the mediating role of job engagement and the moderating role of family supportive supervisor behavior in the relationship between work-family role blurring and taking charge. A moderated mediation model is constructed using boundary theory and work-family border theory as foundational frameworks. The data were collected from 275 professional women in China. Moreover, family supportive supervisor behavior which is a key manifestation of supportive leadership in the modern, boundary-less workplace moderates the relationship between work-family role blurring and job engagement. Additionally, moderated mediation results confirm that a higher level of family supportive supervisor behavior increases professional women’s taking charge level through the indirect effect of work-family role blurring via job engagement. The findings highlight that in an era of pervasive digital connectivity, cultivating family supportive supervisor behaviors is a crucial strategy for management to mitigate role blurring and enhance professional women’s proactive workplace behaviors. This study enriches our understanding of the underlying processes of taking charge by developing a more comprehensive model that integrates the challenges of digital-era work design with the resource-providing function of leadership.

title: Multilevel needs and perceived implementation challenges of mHealth for community frailty management: a qualitative study guided by the Fogg Behavior Model
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
1bb8627d4c51dcc514b6d3fc4038460198138666.abstract: Background Frailty is an important public health challenge in ageing populations and increasingly requires community-based approaches to prevention and management. Mobile health (mHealth) technologies may support health education, self-management, monitoring, and continuity of care among older adults with pre-frailty or frailty. However, successful implementation depends not only on technological usability but also on behavioral, interpersonal, and health-system factors. Evidence regarding these factors from the perspectives of both older adults and community healthcare professionals remains limited. Objective This study aimed to explore the needs and perceived implementation challenges associated with mHealth for community frailty management from the perspectives of older adults with pre-frailty or frailty and community healthcare professionals, and to interpret these factors using the Fogg Behavior Model (FBM). Methods An exploratory qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured face-to-face interviews with 15 community-dwelling older adults with pre-frailty or frailty and 10 community HCPs. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive–deductive thematic analysis approach. Results Seven empirically derived subthemes were developed inductively and subsequently organized into three higher-order interpretive domains corresponding to the FBM dimensions of motivation, ability, and prompts. (1) health-oriented motivation was constrained by limited awareness of frailty and insufficient trust in digital health information; (2) individuals and the primary healthcare system jointly constituted multilevel ability barriers; and (3) mHealth engagement was perceived to depend on complementary action cues and social support. Conclusion Participants perceived the implementation of mHealth in community frailty management as being shaped by interacting factors related to motivation, ability, and prompts. To optimize implementation, attention should be paid to age-friendly design, trustworthy digital health information, frailty and digital health competencies among community HCPs, and coordinated support from family members and healthcare professionals.
