title: Quantified standardized individualized small craniotomy vs. conventional large craniotomy for cerebral herniation secondary to acute supratentorial epidural hematoma: a propensity score-matched study for emergency and battlefield trauma care
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
826f0b8221f442b796424e7c5141b1bdad723462.abstract: Background Acute supratentorial epidural hematoma (EDH) with uncal transtentorial herniation is a fatal emergency for civilian and battlefield trauma. Conventional large craniotomy causes excessive surgical damage inconsistent with damage control surgery (DCS). Current minimally invasive EDH approaches lack standardized bone window metrics, rarely enroll patients with definite brain herniation, and lack battlefield-adapted evidence. This 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) study compared perioperative trauma and long-term neurological outcomes between a stratified quantitative small craniotomy and traditional decompressive surgery. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort included patients with isolated acute EDH and preoperative uncal herniation (2012–2018). Confounders such as age, admission GCS, hematoma volume and anisocoria were balanced via PSM. A five-step CT-guided quantified small craniotomy workflow with tiered 4.0–6.0 cm bone windows was applied. Primary outcomes were operative time and intraoperative blood loss; secondary outcomes covered reoperation risk, hematoma clearance, soft tissue complications, wound healing and 6-month GOS. Results Twenty-two matched pairs (44 patients) were analyzed. Small craniotomy was associated with a 31.1% reduction in operative duration and 71.7% reduction in intraoperative blood loss (both p &lt; 0.001). It lowered persistent scalp numbness and accelerated suture removal (both p &lt; 0.05). No reoperations occurred in either group. No statistically significant intergroup differences in residual hematoma, clearance efficiency and 6-month neurological recovery were detected, although the cohort size limits our capacity to exclude small-to-moderate clinically meaningful differences. Subgroup exploratory analyses are reported in Supplementary Table S1 . Conclusion CT-guided quantified individualized small craniotomy represents a DCS-compliant minimally-invasive surgical option for patients with herniated acute EDH in this selected cohort. No statistically significant between-group differences in hematoma evacuation efficacy or 6-month neurological functional recovery were detected, though our analysis is limited by modest sample size and cannot definitively rule-out small-to-moderate clinically meaningful differences between procedures. The procedure was associated with reduced surgical trauma metrics. This standardized rapid decompression protocol possesses hypothetical translational value for civilian emergency treatment and resource-limited casualty-care scenarios.

title: Hybrid recommendation of healthcare interventions for personalised patient engagement: a leakage-free offline evaluation on synthetic electronic health records
d5ac2bdfffb0df9fb01e25eb3e17f09cb11975b3.abstract: Abstract Digital health platforms often deliver the same content to every patient, which limits engagement. Recommender systems could tailor care plans, medications and procedures to the individual, but evaluations in health settings often lack strong baselines, select hyperparameters on test data, or rely on a single random split. We built a catalogue of 300 recommendable interventions from the April 2020 Synthea sample of 1,171 synthetic patients and compared nine recommenders: random and popularity baselines, content-based filtering on clinical reason codes (CBF), CBF with data-derived item profiles (CBF-D), user-based nearest-neighbour collaborative filtering (kNN), the linear autoencoder EASE, and three weighted hybrids. All hyperparameters were tuned on validation data carved from training only. We report patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals, paired tests, random and temporal splits, ten split seeds, cohort sizes from 113 to 1,171 patients, subgroup performance and a cold-start scenario. The CBF + kNN hybrid outperformed both of its components (NDCG@10 0.692 versus 0.643 for kNN and 0.319 for CBF) with a selected content weight of 0.3. However, the tuned EASE baseline scored higher (0.754), and the best model combined CBF-D with EASE (0.787, 95% CI 0.773-0.802). Under the temporal split, every hybrid outperformed every single-signal model, including EASE. A popularity baseline reached a hit ratio of 0.682 while covering only 9.3% of the catalogue. Hybrid recommendation is a sound basis for personalised engagement, but strong baselines and leakage-free tuning are needed to measure its benefit. Validation on real records with engagement outcomes is the next step.

title: Integrative approaches to acupuncture therapies for post-stroke mild cognitive impairment: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
750e5d10b3af3b8758ad1a9d2ad46cd3741ad839.abstract: Background Post-stroke mild cognitive impairment (PSMCI) frequently occurs after stroke and substantially restricts patients’ functional restoration and overall quality of life. Acupuncture has been widely adopted as an adjunctive intervention; however, the relative efficacy and safety profiles among different acupuncture modalities for PSMCI have not been clearly established. Objective To assess the comparative effectiveness and safety of multiple acupuncture therapies for treating PSMCI via network meta-analysis. Methods RCTs on acupuncture for PSMCI published from their inception to October 2025 were retrieved from nine databases and four clinical trial registries. Study quality was assessed via the Cochrane risk of bias tool. Meta-analysis was performed with ReviewManager and Stata software. Results In total, 47 RCTs featuring 3,680 participants and 15 types of acupuncture-related interventions were included. Electroacupuncture combined with Moxibustion showed the highest efficacy in improving both MoCA score [MD = 5.42, 95%CI (2.10, 8.74)] and total effective rate. Electroacupuncture plus HBOT [MD = 8.00, 95%CI (5.19, 10.82)] and manual acupuncture plus rTMS [MD = 3.42, 95%CI (0.87, 5.97)] were most effective in improving MMSE. Manual acupuncture plus donepezil [MD = 8.67, 95%CI (5.47, 11.88)] and Electroacupuncture plus cognitive training [MD = −8.09, 95%CI (−10.56, −5.62)] achieved the greatest improvement in Barthel index. Moreover, the adverse events of these interventions were acceptable. Conclusion This study suggested that acupuncture was effective and safe for PSMCI treatment. However, the poor methodological quality and uneven evidence quality of existing studies warrant further rigorously designed trials to confirm our findings. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ , identifier CRD420251165945.

title: When fairness breaks down at work: a conceptual model of organisational injustice, work values and employee contextual performance
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
753200a8c21b05980d423731cf1f9ffeb81ffb30.abstract: While there is strong evidence that perceived injustice is related to employee work outcomes, less is known about the human value-based processes that underlie this relationship in the workplace. This conceptual paper advances an integrative model that proposes work values as a mediating process between the relationship between perceived organizational injustice and contextual performance. Based on Organizational Justice Theory and Social Exchange Theory, the paper argues that distributive, procedural, and interactional injustice are not just expected to lead to direct counterproductive or adverse work behavior, but may progressively weaken the salience and enactment of work values, particularly work centrality, by reducing employees’ identification with work, perceived reciprocity, and willingness to invest discretionary effort. This disruption makes voluntary, extra-role behavior, proxy in this study as “contextual performance” less effective in promoting social and psychological functioning in organizations. The paper draws on existing literature in the fields of organizational injustice, organizational work values, and contextual performance to contribute four testable propositions for advancing theory in this field through an integrative approach. Methodologically, the paper adopts an integrative conceptual review and theory-building approach to synthesize classic and contemporary literature on justice perceptions, work values, and contextual performance. The proposed model contributes to organizational behavior theory by repositioning work values as an explanatory mechanism in the injustice performance relationship. It also offers a testable framework for future empirical research and practical insight for organizations seeking to preserve positive discretionary behavior through fair, value-sensitive management systems.

title: A metabolic flux efficiency model reveals mitochondrial triage: H2S reallocates carbon skeletons to match cysteine under cyanide stress in rice
container-title: Frontiers in Plant Science
f0b6fe816940943e4f01ef4c57b007b0b38e0229.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) achieves comparable growth recovery to cysteine (Cys) in rice under cyanide (CN - ) stress, despite Cys being the direct substrate for CN - detoxification and driving a substantially higher assimilation rate via β-cyanoalanine synthase (β-CAS). This paradox implies a fundamental trade-off between immediate detoxification and long-term resilience. Here, we profiled tissue-resolved metabolomics of the TCA cycle intermediates oxaloacetate (OAA) and α-ketoglutarate (α-KG), and their cognate aspartate (Asp)- and glutamate (Glu)-family amino acids, the branches most intimately linked to CN - assimilation, together with transcriptional analysis of their biosynthetic genes. We then developed a Metabolic Flux Efficiency ( MFE ) model, a proof-of-concept framework that integrates these data to estimate relative flux efficiency within the TCA–amino acid (AA) cycle. H 2 S is proposed to execute a mitochondrial triage strategy, depleting root nitrogen reserves (Asn and Gln reduced by 92% and 67%) to liberate carbon skeletons, while boosting root α-KG (+93%) to sustain anaplerotic TCA cycle flux. The calibrated MFE model (Asp family: α = 0.39, β = 1.52; Glu family: α = 0.37, β = 1.64) suggests that metabolic conversion dominates over transcription in governing flux under CN - stress, and predicts that H 2 S redirects flow away from primary nitrogen assimilation (Glu→Gln) toward energy-generating cycles (Orn→Cit). This pattern is consistent with recovery being governed not by nitrogen abundance but by dynamic reallocation of carbon skeletons from storage to biosynthetic and anaplerotic routes. By redefining the mitochondrion as a metabolic regulatory hub that prioritizes reconstruction over mere survival, our work provides a quantitative framework for interpreting metabolic trade-offs and a conceptual basis for engineering stress-resilient crops.

title: Pharmacognostic Standardization, Phytochemical Profiling and Molecular Evaluation of Centella asiatica Extract for Neuroprotection Against Experimental Cognitive Dysfunction
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
10ab585cf81f0d44b566a2bb0fddf202cc267b14.abstract: The present study was designed to standardize Centella asiatica extract and evaluate its phytochemical composition and neuroprotective potential against experimental cognitive dysfunction. The plant material was subjected to pharmacognostic evaluation, physicochemical analysis, preliminary phytochemical screening, and chromatographic profiling. An ethanolic extract of C. asiatica was subsequently investigated in a scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction model in rats. Behavioral performance was assessed using the Morris water maze and Y-maze tests, while biochemical and molecular parameters associated with neuroprotection were evaluated. The extract showed characteristic pharmacognostic features, acceptable physicochemical parameters, and the presence of triterpenoids, flavonoids, phenolics, saponins, and other secondary metabolites. Illustrative results showed that treatment with C. asiatica extract improved spatial learning and spontaneous alternation behaviour, reduced brain acetylcholinesterase activity and oxidative stress, and enhanced antioxidant defence. Molecular evaluation indicated improvement in BDNF expression together with attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings suggest that standardized C. asiatica extract may exert neuroprotective effects through complementary cholinergic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic mechanisms.

title: Tonic neuron position and network topology determine synchronization dynamics
container-title: Cognitive Neurodynamics
275a9bafd1316f2357617f177dc915c918586499.abstract: Abstract Understanding how collective neuronal rhythms emerge from the interplay between network structure and single-neuron dynamics remains a fundamental challenge in neurodynamics. In this work, we show that in small heterogeneous networks, the network topology and the position of a single tonic neuron govern synchronization dynamics. We study minimal four-neuron Huber–Braun motifs composed of one tonic neuron and three bursting neurons coupled via electrical synapses. By systematically varying the tonic neuron’s centrality—quantified through degree and a quasi-Laplacian measure—we identify two critical coupling thresholds: the critical coupling for global phase synchronization and the coupling at which the network returns to synchronized periodic bursting. Remarkably, centrality determines the nature of the synchronized attractor: motifs in which the tonic neuron has low centrality synchronize into tonic spiking, whereas highly central tonic neurons drive the network toward synchronized bursting. Moreover, the networks exhibit nontrivial collective behaviors, including large-ISI “stairway-to-heaven” structures, partial firing death characterized by the coexistence of spiking and subthreshold neurons, and remote synchronization in the star configuration with the tonic neuron at the hub. While the present study focuses on the Huber–Braun model in four-neuron motifs, excitability and electrical coupling are features shared by many conductance-based neuronal models. This motivates the hypothesis that analogous structure–dynamics relationships may also arise in other neuronal models and small network motifs, highlighting the potential role of local structural control in shaping collective neural rhythms.

title: Employing the STEM education model in grade 4 science to develop students’ application competency
container-title: International Journal of Applied Research in Social Sciences
f73d6fb5cbbcb9b0f0060adcd2f242bfc03f56b7.abstract: Developing students' competence to apply acquired knowledge and skills in practice is one of the key objectives of the 2018 General Education Curriculum. In primary education, STEM education has been recognized as an instructional approach that integrates science, technology, engineering, and mathematics through practical problem-solving activities. This study presents the design and implementation of STEM lessons for the topic “Matter” in Grade 4 Science with the aim of developing students' competence in applying acquired knowledge and skills. The research employed theoretical analysis, questionnaire survey, pedagogical experiment, and statistical methods. Based on the characteristics of the topic “Matter”, three STEM lessons were designed and implemented following the engineering design process. The analysis of data from a sample of 71 Grade 4 students (including 36 students in the experimental group and 35 in the control group) showed that STEM-based instruction was associated with improvements in students’ ability to connect scientific knowledge with real-world contexts and in their competence in applying acquired knowledge and skills. The findings provide practical references for primary school teachers in organizing STEM education. Keywords: STEM Education, Grade 4 Science, Matter Topic, Competence in Applying Acquired Knowledge and Skills, Stem Lesson.

title: From Diagnosis by Accumulation to Diagnosis by Layers: Cognitive Psychiatry and Iatrogenic Risk in an Adolescent with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Case Report and Narrative Review
container-title: Asian Journal of Research in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
91dfcb6df22caf160a8be90ab100928fe3a693be.abstract: Background: Adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may show overlapping behavioural descriptions arising from neurodevelopmental features, psychiatric syndromes, environmental stressors and medication effects. Objective: To illustrate a layered psychiatric formulation using the clinical course of an adolescent with ASD, self-harm, restrictive eating, atypical experiences and prolonged psychopharmacological exposure. Methods: Clinical material supplied by the treating team was synthesised as a case report, with a complementary structured narrative review of literature on diagnostic overlap, pharmacotherapy, puberty, safety and feeding. The main PubMed/MEDLINE search covered January 2023 to September 2026, with a subsequent targeted update; evidence selection was purposive rather than systematic. Case Presentation: A 16-year-old adolescent experienced school and adaptive difficulties, sensory sensitivities, food restriction with occasional self-induced vomiting, self-injury and suicidal ideation. Clinical records described sequential exposure to several psychotropic agents. A reduction in lithium dose from 450 to 300 mg/day during the September 2026 admission was followed by improvement in reported hygiene, food variety and family interaction, but later by distress and an urge to self-harm. Co-occurring psychotherapy, environmental changes and uncertain clinical measurements prevent causal attribution. Discussion: The proposed eight-layer framework considers constitutional traits, temperament, neurodevelopment and cognition, psychodynamics, relationships and environment, superimposed syndromes, somatic factors and treatment effects. The concept is heuristic, not a validated diagnostic instrument. Feeding symptoms warrant assessment of sensory selectivity, body-image concerns, compensatory behaviours and nutritional consequences. Evidence associating adverse childhood experiences with neuroimaging measures in autistic samples is relevant context but does not substitute for individual assessment. Conclusion: Longitudinal, risk-sensitive formulation may help identify competing explanations and measurable intervention targets. The clinical sequence does not establish that medication, family circumstances or any single intervention caused the observed outcomes.

title: L3DM: An Open-Source Large 3D Multi-Modality Model on MindSpore with Text-Geometry Alignment
container-title: CAAI Artificial Intelligence Research
6ca9d9ad3a28d6b95cc6784772720f58a51aba2f.abstract: Abstract We present an efficient and scalable MindSpore-based framework for three-dimensional (3D) scene understanding, namely Large 3D Multi-Modality Model (L3DM), with a focus on text-geometry alignment through MindSpore-native multimodal feature integration and key–value (KV) cache adaptation. Our work delivers three key contributions to the community. First, we provide a dedicated MindSpore performance optimization for multi-modal feature inputs and KV cache, resolving prior bottlenecks and enabling stable, high-performance operation where it was previously challenging. Second, we explore zero-shot Chain-of-Thought reasoning for 3D multi-view understanding, providing valuable insights into its limitations for complex spatial reasoning tasks. Third and foremost, we offer the first complete, open-source, and scalable 3D foundation model implementation on the MindSpore platform. This contribution fills a critical gap by providing the community with a fully functional training and inference codebase, pre-trained weights, and pipelines for a multimodal 3D large model—resources that were entirely absent before. Overall, the proposed L3DM method establishes a new, stable, and accurate benchmark solution for 3D understanding on MindSpore, with impressive empirical validation on the ScanQA benchmark. Code is available at https://openi.pcl.ac.cn/OpenAIRobotics/L3DM.

title: Prosody In The English Of Igbo First Language Undergraduates At The Noun Awka Study Centre
container-title: African Journal of Kidney Stones
1d01e6d16fa84ae506714731efcf523311085389.abstract: Background: The study finds that the prosody of the Awka group can be best described as a single remapping of English prosody onto Igbo pitch grammar, a remapping that the low classroom contact appears to sharpen, and suggests that the specific points of tranJsfer identified can be used to provide targeted, self-study pronunciation support. Objective: This study examines the prosody (stress, rhythm and intonation) of the English language spoken by undergraduates of the National Open University of Nigeria (NOUN), Study Centre, Awka, Nigeria, a population whose first language is Igbo and whose prosody has received little attention in the literature. In the framework of the Autosegmental-Metrical (AM) model, it examines the question of whether the forward stress, syllable timing and falling tone reported for Igbo English elsewhere are three independent features, or three aspects of the same feature, and whether a decrease in classroom contact accentuates the transfer from the lexical-tonal grammar of Igbo. The results reveal late word stress, fixed word stress, strong syllable timing, and a falling tone for intonation, even on yes/no questions where English would expect a rising tone, and an imported low boundary tone that is repeated across different types of utterances. Methods: One hundred students were recorded on a word list, a passage and free speech using a mixed auditory and acoustic design, and a twenty-speaker sub-sample analysed acoustically in Praat. Results: These results are interpreted as five surface manifestations of a single underlying cause: the level high-tone habit, the phrase-final low tone, the stability and floating of tone, downdrift, and the weak role of stress in Igbo. title: Hybrid CNN–transformer model with gated feature fusion and GAN-based augmentation for MRI image classification
Hybrides CNN-Transformer-Modell mit GFF („gated feature fusion“) und GAN-basierter Augmentierung zur Klassifizierung von MRT-Bildern
container-title: Die Radiologie
34b0fdb6a7efc369f52ef24dce28ab4e17202351.abstract: Abstract Objective Brain tumor classification based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays a critical role in clinical diagnosis, yet it remains challenging due to high intra-class variability, inter-class similarity, and limited annotated data. To address these challenges, this study proposes a gated hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN)–transformer architecture (GHCT-Net) that effectively integrates local and global feature representations for robust brain tumor classification in data-limited medical imaging scenarios. Methods The proposed framework combines a ConvNeXt-based convolutional branch for fine-grained spatial feature extraction with a Swin Transformer branch for modeling long-range contextual dependencies. A gate-based fusion mechanism is introduced to adaptively balance the contribution of each feature stream. Additionally, a conditional deep convolutional generative adversarial network (cDCGAN) is employed to generate class-consistent synthetic MRI samples to mitigate data scarcity. The model was evaluated on a public dataset of 7023 MRI images across four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no tumor) under three training scenarios: original, traditionally augmented, and GAN-augmented datasets. Results The results demonstrate that the GHCT-Net achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art CNN and Transformer architectures, reaching a classification accuracy of 98.39% on the GAN-augmented dataset. Quantitative analysis, along with confusion matrices, t‑distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) visualizations, and gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) interpretability studies, confirms that the model successfully learns discriminative and clinically relevant features. Conclusion Combining a gated hybrid CNN–transformer architecture with GAN-based data augmentation provides a highly effective and robust solution for brain tumor classification, particularly in scenarios constrained by limited medical imaging data.

title: YOLOv8-CNR: a lightweight fire and smoke detection model for forest fire scenarios based on improved YOLOv8
container-title: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
19c4b1fa33027b89e97fdda65528f592ce5e9c9b.abstract: Introduction To address irregular morphology and drastic scale variations of flame and smoke targets in forest fire detection, and the difficulty of lightweight models in balancing accuracy and real-time performance, this paper proposes YOLOv8-CNR based on improved YOLOv8n. Methods The model optimizes backbone, neck, and loss function: C3_ConvNeXtv2 enhances flame texture and smoke edge representation; RepNCSPELAN4 strengthens multi-scale flow and small-target smoke features; SIoU improves localization of irregular targets. Results On M4SFWD with its trajectory-level split, YOLOv8-CNR achieves 79.8% mAP50 and 39.4% mAP50-95 with 2.52 M parameters, improving 7.5 and 2.6 percentage points over tuned YOLOv8n, at 238.1 FPS. This split eliminates near-duplicate frame leakage across subsets. Because the test set consists entirely of six Scene 4 camera runs that are absent from both training and validation, the M4SFWD results are interpreted as controlled comparisons under a scene-held-out setting rather than same-distribution generalization. Cross-dataset transfer is further evaluated through zero-shot transfer: trained only on M4SFWD, the model achieves 78.3 and 82.7% mAP50 on SMOKE_dataset and FLAME_dataset, respectively. Retrained on these datasets, it achieves 90.2 and 90.4% mAP50, demonstrating favorable real-world applicability. Ablation experiments show complementary and partially overlapping effects among the three modules, with the complete model achieving a 2.6 percentage point improvement in mAP50-95 over the baseline. Discussion The proposed model improves overall and smoke-related precision and recall, while flame precision slightly decreases (81.1% vs. 82.4%), flame mAP50-95 increases from 42.0 to 45.2%. This method provides an efficient solution for real-time flame and smoke detection in complex forest scenarios.

title: Language choice in Saudi medical education: stakeholder perspectives on avoiding Arabic as the medium of instruction
container-title: Frontiers in Education
b172b8c140efe1e4fbc1103107e9fdf0a9c55d8f.abstract: Introduction English-medium instruction remains dominant in Saudi medical education despite growing recognition that Arabic, the official language, can support comprehension, participation, and clinical communication. This qualitative study examined why Arabic continues to be avoided as a medium of instruction in Saudi medical schools and what this reveals about language-of-instruction policy in higher education. Methods Drawing on 71 semi-structured interviews with students, educators, administrators, residents, and physicians across three Saudi medical schools, the study employed hybrid inductive–deductive thematic analysis to identify the institutional and pedagogical factors shaping language choice. Results Four interconnected factors emerged: the limited availability of Arabic medical resources, terminological instability, the perceived indispensability of English for access to scientific knowledge and professional mobility, and learners' cognitive adaptation to English-medium instruction (EMI). Three potential pathways for reform were also identified: immediate bilingual support, transitional hybrid instruction, and the longer-term development of Arabic-medium instruction (AMI) supported by translation and terminology-development initiatives. Discussion The findings suggest that the avoidance of AMI is driven primarily by practical constraints, professional demands, and long-term adaptation to EMI, rather than by opposition to Arabic itself.

title: Integrated metabolomics and transcriptomics reveal retinal alterations in a mouse model of chronic restraint stress protocol-induced anxiety-like behavior
container-title: Frontiers in Molecular Neuroscience
9ad6ebd692b103d822f3e483a4efa41996f0c250.abstract: Background Psychological stress is a potential risk factor for glaucoma, but the association and underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether a chronic restraint stress (CRS) protocol, which includes repeated fasting/water deprivation, is associated with glaucoma-like retinal damage in mice and explored the involved pathways. Methods Adult male mice underwent 4 h daily restraint for 10 days. Anxiety-like behaviors were assessed by open field test (OFT) and elevated plus maze (EPM). Intraocular pressure (IOP) was measured at baseline, day 7, and day 14. Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) survival was quantified by RBPMS immunofluorescence. RNA-seq and untargeted metabolomics (UHPLC-MS/MS) were performed on retinas, followed by integrated analysis, qPCR validation, and a targeted query of the GWAS Catalog for glaucoma-associated SNPs. Results CRS mice showed anxiety-like behaviors, progressive IOP elevation, and reduced RGC numbers. Transcriptomics identified 216 candidate genes with nominal differential expression, with altered oxidoreductase activity and iron ion binding. Metabolomics detected 255 differential metabolites, mainly fatty acids, glycerophospholipids, and amino acids, with nominal enrichment of the thermogenesis pathway. qPCR confirmed upregulation of Cyp2f2, Cyp4f15, Fmo2, S100a9, and Aif1. Integrated analysis identified Fmo2 and Serpine1 as candidate genes that may contribute to the link between the CRS protocol and glaucoma pathogenesis; Serpine1 had records of glaucoma-risk SNPs in the GWAS Catalog. Conclusion The CRS protocol is associated with glaucoma-like retinal degeneration, characterized by IOP elevation, RGC loss, and dysregulation of metabolic, oxidative stress, and inflammatory pathways. Fmo2 and Serpine1 are candidate genes that may link the CRS protocol to glaucoma pathogenesis; however, functional validation is required to establish causality.

title: Cardamine flexuosa extract attenuates neutrophilic airway inflammation in a CSE/LPS-induced murine model
container-title: Frontiers in Pharmacology
88f810bd02369c0ff4c753ebdcfd30bb6033a963.abstract: Introduction Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of disease- related mortality worldwide and is characterized by progressive airflow limitation accompanied by persistent neutrophilic airway inflammation. Macrophage activation plays a key role in this process through the production of pro- inflammatory mediators and neutrophil-attracting chemokines. Methods This study investigated the anti-inflammatory effects of Cardamine flexuosa extract (CFE) in macrophage and cigarette smoke extract (CSE)/lipopolysaccharide (LPS)- induced models, with emphasis on macrophage inflammatory responses and neutrophilic airway inflammation. Results In LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages, CFE reduced nitric oxide production by 77.8% and decreased the secretion of TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), accompanied by reduced MAPK phosphorylation. In a murine model induced by intranasal administration of CSE and LPS, oral CFE reduced total inflammatory cell and neutrophil counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) by 53.9% and 82.9%, respectively, at 200 mg/kg compared with the CSE/LPS group. These effects were associated with reduced pulmonary expression of CXCL-1 and MIP-2 and decreased MAPK phosphorylation. Histological analysis demonstrated attenuation of inflammatory cell infiltration and mucus hypersecretion. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that CFE attenuates macrophage inflammatory responses and neutrophilic airway inflammation in the CSE/LPS-induced murine model, accompanied by reduced inflammatory mediator production and MAPK activation.

title: Associations between cognitive reserve, glymphatic function and cognitive function in mild cognitive impairment
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
b07439303012bc223b7ba87f2dabecd86d618b0c.abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between cognitive reserve (CR) and glymphatic function in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and to examine whether the relationship between CR and cognition is mediated by glymphatic function. Methods 113 MCI individuals and 91 healthy controls (HC) were enrolled to assess the glymphatic function by using diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), perivascular space (PVS) ratings, and choroid plexus volume (CPV). Cognitive reserve index questionnaire (CRIq) was employed to evaluate the comprehensive CR of participants in both groups. The glymphatic function was compared between the two groups and Spearman correlation analyses were performed among the CR, glymphatic function and cognition. Mediation analyses were further conducted to explore potential mediating effects. Results The MCI group had significantly lower bilateral ALPS index and mean ALPS index than the HC group, while the bilateral CPV, basal ganglia (BG)-PVS and centrum semiovale (CS)-PVS scores were significantly higher in the MCI group than the HC group. After controlling for age and sex, bilateral and mean ALPS index were positively correlated with MoCA, MMSE, and VFT scores; mean ALPS index and left ALPS index were positively correlated with AVLT-immediately performance. BG-PVS was negatively correlated with MMSE and VFT scores, and right CPV was negatively correlated with VFT scores. Meanwhile, CRIq was positively correlated with bilateral and mean ALPS index, but was negatively correlated with BG-PVS, and mean ALPS partially mediated the association between CRIq and cognition in the MCI group. Conclusion Mild cognitive impairment individuals exhibit reduced glymphatic activity relative to HC. Comprehensive CR is associated with cognitive function in MCI, with the mean ALPS index statistically mediating a portion of the CR–cognition association.

title: Single-cell analysis reveals transcriptomic patterns in active macrophage activation syndrome and therapeutic potential of albumin-fused interleukin-10 in a mouse model
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
b34f0b57b6e5d2f6093466a07fcd13a166e7dbb5.abstract: Introduction Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) are life-threatening hyperinflammatory conditions. We aimed to characterize immune cell transcriptomic patterns in human MAS and investigate the therapeutic potential of albumin-fused IL-10 protein (SA-IL-10) in a MAS mouse model. Methods We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on bone marrow and peripheral blood samples from patients with newly developed MAS caused by diverse etiologies. We generated paired Seq-Well single-cell transcriptomes from bone marrow and blood of patients with active HLH/MAS. In the absence of a contemporaneous control cohort, technology-matched public Seq-Well marrow and same-laboratory control blood were projected onto the frozen patient atlases as lineage context, not as a case–control comparison. We also evaluated the effect of SA-IL-10 in a CpG-DNA–induced mouse model of MAS. Results Human scRNA-seq identified diverse immune cell populations, including dendritic cells, macrophages, and monocyte subsets. Canonical lineages in the public data were transferred to the expected patient states. Monocyte 1 and macrophage populations expressed transcripts encoding IL-10 receptor subunits and associated signaling molecules, although these findings reflect RNA abundance and do not establish functional responsiveness. Donor-level phagocytosis and interferon-γ programs showed no significant differences after multiple-testing correction. In the mouse model, SA-IL-10 treatment significantly improved anemia, leukocytopenia, splenomegaly, and liver dysfunction and was associated with reduced circulating interferon-γ levels and bone marrow macrophage abundance. Conclusion Human scRNA-seq provides transcriptomic patterns in active HLH/MAS. The therapeutic effects observed in the mouse model support further investigation of SA-IL-10 as a potential treatment for MAS.

title: Sensorimotor recovery, neuropathic pain reduction, and neuroplasticity changes following cognitive multisensory rehabilitation or adaptive fitness in adults with spinal cord injury: a feasibility pilot randomized controlled trial
container-title: Frontiers in Pain Research
9fed6f696e20c514887fb0d7b80050475f38e976.abstract: Introduction Spinal cord injury (SCI) often causes partial or complete sensory and motor loss, disrupting the afferent integration needed for accurate mental body representations (MBR, i.e., body awareness and visuospatial body map). MBR deficits compromise sensorimotor recovery and contribute to neuropathic pain in about 69% of adults with SCI. Medications for neuropathic pain are often ineffective and can cause adverse reactions. Our previous pilot clinical trial showed that Cognitive Multisensory Rehabilitation (CMR), a physical therapy that restores MBR, produced significant, lasting reductions in neuropathic pain, improved sensorimotor function, and enhanced brain function. Building on these results, we examined feasibility and whether 8 weeks of CMR or adaptive fitness (1) improves sensorimotor function and reduces pain; (2) increases sensorimotor- and MBR-related brain activity and connectivity in adults with SCI. Methods Sixteen participants (52 ± 8 years old, 13 ± 10 years post-SCI) were randomized to CMR or adaptive fitness (45 min, 3x/week, 8 weeks); one withdrew. Ten participants had neuropathic pain of ≥3/10. Pain and sensorimotor function were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and 3-month follow-up using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS), and Neuromuscular Recovery Scale (NRS). Functional MRI included resting-state and 4 tasks: imagining feeling the left leg, imagining moving the left leg, whole-body movement imagery, and a sensation task (i.e., gently brushing the big toes with a towel). Results Post-CMR ( n = 8), participants showed significant large within-group AIS effect sizes (touch: d = 1.54; pinprick: d = 1.83; lower limb motor function: d = 1.32) and large (core: d = 2.19) to moderate (arm function: d = 0.69; leg function: d = 0.74) NRS effect sizes. Adaptive fitness ( n = 7) showed non-significant small/moderate AIS (touch: d = 0.49; pinprick: d = 0.53; lower limb motor function: d = 0.74) and NRS effects (core: d = 0.73; arm function: d = 0.34; leg function: d = 0.00). Benefits persisted at follow-up. MCID was exceeded for average pain post-CMR and highest pain at 3-month follow-up. Pain virtually did not change after fitness. CMR increased brain connectivity and activation during leg imagery. During whole-body imagery, CMR increased widespread activation; adaptive fitness showed spatially limited increases. Discussion These preliminary results support CMR's potential to improve function and reduce neuropathic pain in adults with SCI, warranting larger confirmatory trials. Clinical Trial Registration : https://clinicaltrial.gov/ , identifier NCT05167032.

title: Expert-referenced evaluation of large language models for primary suspect drug identification in the FAERS database
container-title: Frontiers in Pharmacology
57b9cdb00045853b362366dbfa179afbfc1c4e16.abstract: Background Accurate identification of primary suspect drugs in adverse event reports is a critical component of post-marketing pharmacovigilance and serves as a foundation for downstream signal detection activities. However, causal attribution in spontaneous reporting systems such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) is inherently challenging. Traditional expert-based assessments are resource-intensive and difficult to scale, highlighting the need for complementary, reproducible approaches. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of large language models (LLMs) in identifying primary suspect drugs in adverse event reports against an expert reference standard. Methods Fifty FAERS case reports were randomly selected for evaluation. Three clinical pharmacy experts established the reference standard by adjudicating the primary suspect drug(s) for each case. LLM-based evaluations were conducted using multiple prompting strategies and model configurations. The performance of LLMs, pharmacy student evaluators, and original FAERS primary suspect designations (ROLE_COD) was assessed by calculating hit rates against the expert reference standard. Results The original FAERS designations demonstrated limited accuracy against the expert reference standard, with a hit rate of 0.778. In contrast, LLM-based assessments achieved consistently high hit rates ranging from 0.867 to 0.920 across diverse prompting strategies and model configurations. Student evaluators achieved a comparable hit rate of 0.872; however, LLM-based evaluations exhibited greater internal consistency and markedly shorter response times. Conclusion LLM-based evaluations demonstrated high accuracy against expert assessments and favorable efficiency relative to student evaluators. These findings highlight the potential utility of LLMs as scalable, readily accessible decision-support tools in pharmacovigilance workflows.

title: A claim-specific evidence-boundary model for plant UDP-glycosyltransferases: from substrate candidates to native function
container-title: Frontiers in Plant Science
30fa125e53f0f1df19a71e80fc6ee96039203299.abstract: UDP-glycosyltransferase (UGT) research now generates far more candidate genes and metabolites than can be assigned experimentally. This Hypothesis and Theory article introduces a claim-specific evidence-boundary model developed from potential inferential transitions encountered when interpreting published UGT evidence; no new experimental data are presented. The model separates two entry filters from two complementary but non-interchangeable claim axes. Experimental accessibility determines which UGT–acceptor–donor combinations can be tested, whereas predictive prioritization orders testing and can redirect efforts to obtain compounds or donors. Once a defined combination enters an experiment, enzyme-dependent product detection and structural characterization delimit the chemical claim, while heterologous reconstruction and native perturbation delimit biological claims. We hypothesize that new evidence will preferentially increase confidence in the claim directly addressed by that evidence, whereas cross-axis evidence alone will not resolve an outstanding chemical or biological claim. The model extends identification and reporting guidance to UGT reaction and native-function claims. It predicts uneven confidence gains across the chemical and biological axes and identifies transitions where claims may outpace evidence. The model generates three testable predictions. Aligned evidence should produce larger confidence gains for the corresponding claim than for a non-aligned claim. Claim inflation should be enriched at prediction-to-reaction, feature-to-structure, and non-native-to-native transitions relative to other evaluable inferential transitions. Boundary-specific reporting should improve inter-evaluator agreement and reduce misclassification when factual information is held constant. The framework may support study design, peer review, and reusable UGT records.

title: Persistent neutrophil maturation deficits associate with cognitive impairment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
ac0aa8b9c9650b24069967ccaa55123144767865.abstract: Introduction Post-COVID-19 condition, or post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), is characterized by persistent cognitive impairments and immune dysregulation. While neutrophils are critical in acute COVID-19, whether their long-term functional dysregulation contributes to PASC, remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the links between immune system changes, symptom severity and cognitive impairment in PASC. Methods In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 40 individuals with self-reported issues with COVID-19 recovery (PASC) and 37 fully recovered (REC) volunteers. Participants were post-infection at either TP1 (from 6 up to 18 months post-infection, 7 PASC, 20 REC) or at TP2 (from 19 up to 36 months post-infection, 33 PASC, 17 REC). We evaluated the Newcastle post-COVID-19 Syndrome Follow Up Screening (NC) scores for symptom severity, and neuropsychological tests for memory, attention, and executive function. Peripheral blood was analyzed using multicolor flow cytometry, ELISA, clustering, and multivariate regression. Results PASC participants in both the TP1 cohort and the TP2 cohort, demonstrated increased NC scores and significant changes in neutrophil numbers and subset composition. In the TP1 cohort, the PASC group showed an increased frequency of activated CD16 + CD62L low neutrophils and a reduced frequency of CXCR4 + TREM-1 + CCR2 + polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs). This was accompanied by elevated soluble TNF receptor 1 (sTNFR1) and decreased sTNFR2 and CXCL12. In the TP2 cohort, PMN-MDSC levels were comparable between REC and PASC groups, alongside increased emergency granulopoiesis regulators IL-3 and IL-6. Multivariate regression revealed significant associations between PMN-MDSC signatures, granulopoiesis-related markers, NC scores, and cognitive test scores in either the TP1 or the TP2 cohort. These results represent cross-sectional observations in participants assessed within the respective post-infection intervals, rather than longitudinal evidence of persistence. The results show that dysregulated granulopoiesis and neutrophil maturation are present even at 18 and 36 months in PASC individuals, potentially associating with overall symptom severity and cognitive impairment. Conclusions Despite limitations in cohort size, requiring validation of the associations in larger cohorts, our findings may contribute to the further understanding of PASC and future new transitional perspectives for PASC management.

title: How does family intellectual-cultural orientation correlate with adolescents’ wellbeing literacy? An empirical analysis based on a chain mediation model
container-title: Frontiers in Psychiatry
3f55b176ae58ae4bd9a204671838105abdc5e700.abstract: Introduction Wellbeing literacy(WL), as a promising emerging concept, offers a possible route for addressing global adolescent mental-health problems. Family intellectual-cultural orientation(FICO) shows a significant statistical association with wellbeing literacy, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods This study used convenience sampling to survey 868 adolescents aged 12–18 years and employed a serial mediation model (PROCESS Model 6) to examine the indirect effects of positive psychological capital and personal growth initiative in the association between family intellectual-cultural orientation and well-being literacy. Results Family intellectual-cultural orientation was significantly correlated with well-being literacy (effect = 0.1151, p &lt; 0.001). The total indirect effect was significant (effect = 0.2414, 95% CI [0.1893, 0.2975]), accounting for 67.7% of the total effect. The separate mediating effects of positive psychological capital (effect = 0.1254, 95% CI [0.0839, 0.1718]) and personal growth initiative (effect = 0.0417, 95% CI [0.0183, 0.0710]), as well as their chain mediating effect (effect = 0.0743, 95% CI [0.0463, 0.1063]), were all significant. Discussion These correlational patterns reveal that family intellectual-cultural orientation is statistically linked to adolescents’ wellbeing literacy via the correlational chain of positive psychological capital(PPC) and personal growth initiative(PGI), which aligns with core assumptions of the resource-gain spiral mechanism proposed by conservation of resources theory. The findings provide empirical evidence for family-education interventions and school-based mental-health education.

title: Physiological markers of low-altitude exercise load for predicting acute mountain sickness: development of an interpretable machine learning model and research web calculator
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
ebb10a5d0b2d2954c1d608ffb7d6d6db97a9b27c.abstract: Acute mountain sickness (AMS) poses a significant threat to individuals ascending to high-altitude regions, yet early identification of susceptible populations remains challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model for estimating AMS risk from exercise-induced physiological responses measured at low altitude. A total of 171 healthy participants were included, with 111 participants (51 AMS events) comprising the development cohort and 60 participants (27 AMS events) forming an external validation cohort. Model development was repeated within a nested cross-validation framework, including LASSO feature selection and algorithm selection within the resampling process. The final locked five-feature model included changes in post-exercise pulse oxygen saturation (ΔSpO 2 ) and cardiac output (ΔCO), sex, smoking history, and drinking history, and combined logistic regression, support vector machine, and random forest by equal-weight soft voting. In the development cohort, pooled outer-fold predictions yielded an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI, 0.791–0.929), an AUPRC of 0.842 (95% CI, 0.748–0.932), and a Brier score of 0.148. The calibration intercept was −0.033 (95% CI, −0.504 to 0.527), the calibration slope was 0.931 (95% CI, 0.664–1.351) and the positive net benefit range was 0.078–0.840. In the external validation cohort, the locked model yielded an AUC of 0.834 (95% CI, 0.723–0.929), an AUPRC of 0.867 (95% CI, 0.758–0.946), and a Brier score of 0.152; the calibration intercept was −0.103 (95% CI, −0.834 to 0.531), the calibration slope was 1.013 (95% CI, 0.655–1.666) and a positive net benefit range of 0.200–0.953. Post-hoc SHAP analysis identified ΔSpO 2 and ΔCO as the two most influential predictors. These findings support an association between low-altitude exercise responses and subsequent AMS. However, the prediction model requires further development and validation in substantially larger cohorts before clinical deployment.

title: A working model linking oxidative stress, histone H3K18 lactylation and ALKBH3 in age-related macular degeneration
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
ea55c9c17fd347e097780166c2dd66c0ec0e3527.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss in the elderly and is driven primarily by retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) dysfunction. Although oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction are well-established early events in AMD, how these bioenergetic deficits relate to chronic inflammation and neovascularization in advanced disease remains incompletely understood. This Hypothesis and Theory article focuses on an oxidative stress–lactate–epigenetic axis as a potential link. Oxidative damage can be followed by a Warburg-like glycolytic shift in experimental and some donor RPE systems, with intracellular lactate accumulation. Lactate can be converted to L-lactyl-CoA for histone lactylation; whether histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la) then promotes IL-6 or VEGFA transcription in human macular RPE is not established. Central to the framework is a proposed H3K18la–ALKBH3 feed-forward loop that would couple epitranscriptomic mRNA stabilization with epigenetic amplification. Emerging interventions aimed at this axis are discussed, including the peptide ghrelin. Ghrelin protects RPE in oxidative preclinical models and can activate AMPK in other systems; a sequence from ghrelin to reduced glycolysis, lactate and H3K18la in AMD RPE is a hypothesis, not an experimentally established AMD mechanism. Combinatorial strategies, such as pairing ALKBH3 inhibitors with metabolic modulators, are therefore hypothesis-generating approaches for earlier intervention.

title: Investigating the transition in ice dynamics from a land- to lake-terminating glacier using a simple glacier dynamics model
container-title: The Cryosphere
625bf3cb51d814830d9946a44dbc3a67e027dd28.abstract: Glaciers interact with adjacent proglacial lakes through a range of thermomechanical processes. These interactions occur in addition to climate-driven ablation and are capable of amplifying or modifying climatic effects through various feedback mechanisms. In particular, the connection between lake water-level and the subglacial hydrological system can reduce basal friction, which in turn leads to increased glacier flow and dynamic thinning. This creates a positive feedback loop in which decreased effective pressure, also driven potentially by negative surface mass balance, enhances flow velocity, in line with similar processes observed at marine-terminating glaciers. Our aim in this study is to introduce a simple model that can be used to understand the critical controls on the dynamic behaviour of glaciers as they transition from land- to lake-terminating systems. Here, we investigate the behaviour of Skaftafellsjökull in Iceland, which has undergone such a transition over the past twenty-five years. More specifically, we use the Shallow Shelf Approximation (SSA) in Elmer/Ice to model ice velocities, incorporating a water pressure-dependent friction law to model basal sliding with a simple parameterization of basal water pressure. The model successfully reproduces the observed velocity patterns, capturing the shift from downstream deceleration near the glacier terminus in 2010 to acceleration in 2018, reflecting the growing influence of the proglacial lake. We find a threshold behaviour between basal water pressure and ice velocity, whereby small increases in water pressure beyond a critical value led to strong acceleration, consistent with previous empirical observations. Furthermore, our results imply that surface thinning exerts a stronger control on the near terminus acceleration than the observed terminus retreat. Our results suggest that the modelling framework developed provides a valuable tool for simulating these complex interactions in a computationally efficient manner.

title: Vibration Control in Cable-Stayed Bridge Towers Using an EL-FRF Model for MTLD-Structure Interaction
4badd65c2c4ce03221062db902b36bc4f6990ee3.abstract: Abstract This study proposes a novel analytical framework, termed the Euler-Lagrange Frequency Response Function (EL-FRF), for modeling the dynamic interaction between structures and multi-tuned liquid damper (MTLD) systems. Derived from Euler-Lagrange equations and incorporating nonlinear shallow-wave theory via equivalent tuned mass damper (TMD) analogies, the EL-FRF provides a non-dimensional transfer function to evaluate broadband vibration suppression under wind loads. Key innovations include its multi-degree-of-freedom formulation for MTLD, enabling optimization of parameters such as tank count (N = 5–15), frequency bandwidth (R = 0.2–0.3), and center mass ratio (~ 60%), demonstrating superior robustness over single-tuned liquid dampers (STLD). Validated through parametric simulations showing 20–30% greater amplitude reductions, the EL-FRF is applied to the tower of the Bai Chay cable-stayed bridge in Vietnam, where MTLD outperforms the existing STLD with reduced damper layers and enhanced lateral vibration control. This method advances passive damper design, offering a versatile tool for structural engineers in seismic and wind-prone regions.

title: Visibility-conditioned recombination in legal-language research across four legal contexts
container-title: International Journal of Legal Discourse
06a669e154421cf396f2f55da5ce738c66a83c76.abstract: Abstract Legal-language scholarship spans disciplines, institutions, languages, and bibliographic systems. This article develops an account of its organization across Common law, Civil law, Islamic law, and the Chinese legal context. Searches of Web of Science, Scopus, and CNKI yielded 9,290 publications through July 31, 2026. Legal context was identifiable in 28.4 percent of records and a focal context in 24.4 percent, while themes were more visible than methods. Theme profiles shared a backbone of discourse, translation, and terminology, yet source ecology crossed contextual boundaries: within each usable source stratum, the three interpretable contexts were more similar to one another than each context’s CNKI and non-CNKI profiles. Contextual variation appeared as functional recombination. Common-law records emphasized judicial reasoning; Civil-law records multilingual transfer; Islamic-law records discourse, terminology, and religious legal texts; and Chinese-context records translation, terminology, and drafting. Chinese multi-axis records increased from 6.8 percent in 2000–2009 to 20.2 percent in 2020–2026. Under the stricter context rule, the six initial shifts gave way to a Common-law discourse increase from 13.2 to 26.6 percent. The findings support visibility-conditioned recombination as a model of how institutional functions and evidence infrastructures shape the observable field.

title: The Age-Period-Cohort (APC) model in medical research: an explanatory analysis of concepts, applications, and public health implications
container-title: Advances in Data Analysis and Classification
e2563067929f455455a948b44029a02b02ccec68.abstract: Abstract To provide a practical guide to the Age-Period-Cohort (APC) model’s core concepts, assumptions, and applications in biostatistics, epidemiology, and demography, helping researchers interpret complex temporal dynamics in health outcomes such as cancer incidence, mortality, and infectious disease trends. To address the major challenge of identifiability in APC analysis where age, period, and cohort effects are linearly dependent—advanced statistical approaches are employed. These include constrained generalized linear models (CGLIMs), the Intrinsic Estimator (IE), Hierarchical APC (HAPC) models, and restricted cubic splines within generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs). Each approach allows disentangling of the three effects to reveal underlying drivers of disease patterns. The APC model has proven effective in public health research. It distinguishes age-related risks from period-based shifts (e.g., due to medical advances) and cohort-specific behaviors (e.g., smoking initiation). Applications range from analyzing long-term cancer incidence trends to understanding infectious disease dynamics and evaluating policy impacts such as tobacco control or vaccination campaigns. The APC model supports evidence-based public health strategies by isolating the independent contributions of aging, historical events, and generational changes. Its continued use enables more targeted interventions and robust evaluations of health policies over time.

title: Mode Switching in Two Blue Large-amplitude Pulsators Observed by OGLE, KMTNet, and DREAMS
container-title: The Astrophysical Journal
b67d0469422dbb66fcc676d1faae8a6d42e57d8a.abstract: Abstract Blue large-amplitude pulsators (BLAPs) are rare, hot, short-period pulsating stars whose rapid oscillations provide a unique probe of stellar interiors and atmospheres. In this paper, we study two short-period BLAPs in the Galactic bulge, Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE)-BLAP-142 ( P ≈ 6.6 minutes) and OGLE-BLAP-148 ( P ≈ 7.5 minutes), by combining light curves from the OGLE, KMTNet, and DREAMS surveys, spanning 17 yr with cadences ranging from minutes to hours to days. We perform generalized Lomb–Scargle periodogram analyses of their light curves and identify, for each BLAP, three closely spaced pulsation modes separated by ∼1%. The dominant mode can switch within timescales of order a year, accompanied by a likely blueward color shift (∼0.1–0.2 mag). The yearly period excursions of the resolved mode families imply apparent ∣ P ̇ / P ∣ values of order 10 −6 –10 −4 yr −1 , large enough to mimic or exceed smooth evolutionary period changes. One mode family in OGLE-BLAP-148 shows a coherent decade-long drift at the ∼10 −5 yr −1 level, but its failure to extrapolate to the earliest and latest epochs suggests a transient mode-family drift rather than secular evolution. Such close-spaced multiple pulsations and mode switching may be common among BLAPs with periods shorter than 10 minutes, and their physical origin remains unclear.

title: Efektivitas Penggunaan Model Cooperative Learning Berbantuan Media Konkret Takalintar Terhadap Pemahaman Konsep Perkalian Bersusun
container-title: Master Journal of Future Education
b41b69bc91eb0f3fc0f2d7c75a35b9f1102d5fd0.abstract: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya pemahaman siswa kelas III SDN 101/II Muara Bungo terhadap konsep perkalian bersusun, khususnya pada tahap penyimpanan angka dan penempatan nilai tempat. Kondisi tersebut ditemukan melalui observasi awal yang menunjukkan pembelajaran matematika masih berpusat pada guru dan belum memanfaatkan media konkret secara optimal. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui pengaruh dan efektivitas model Cooperative Learning berbantuan media konkret Takalintar terhadap pemahaman konsep perkalian bersusun siswa kelas III. Metode yang digunakan adalah eksperimen dengan desain nonequivalent control group design. Sampel ditentukan melalui cluster random sampling sehingga diperoleh kelas III.A sebagai kelas eksperimen (33 siswa) dan kelas III.B sebagai kelas kontrol (33 siswa). Data dikumpulkan melalui tes uraian pada tahap pre-test dan post-test, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji Wilcoxon, uji Mann-Whitney, dan uji N-Gain. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata nilai kelas eksperimen meningkat dari 45,88 menjadi 88,70, jauh lebih tinggi dibandingkan kelas kontrol yang meningkat dari 37,39 menjadi 62,33. Uji Wilcoxon dan Mann-Whitney menunjukkan nilai signifikansi di bawah 0,05, sedangkan uji N-Gain kelas eksperimen sebesar 0,70 (kategori sedang, cukup efektif) dan kelas kontrol sebesar 0,37 (tidak efektif). Dapat disimpulkan bahwa model Cooperative Learning berbantuan media konkret Takalintar berpengaruh dan cukup efektif dalam meningkatkan pemahaman konsep perkalian bersusun siswa kelas III.

title: Efektivitas Model Teams Games Tournament Berbantuan Media Papan Pecahan Terhadap Pemahaman Konsep Penjumlahan dan Pengurangan Pecahan Biasa Siswa Sekolah Dasar
container-title: Master Journal of Future Education
4ae679cab3bf9b2018bee76cea2321367f668198.abstract: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya pemahaman konsep penjumlahan dan pengurangan pecahan biasa pada siswa sekolah dasar. Kondisi tersebut menunjukkan perlunya penerapan model pembelajaran yang mampu meningkatkan keterlibatan dan pemahaman siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh dan efektivitas model Teams Games Tournament berbantuan media papan pecahan terhadap pemahaman konsep penjumlahan dan pengurangan pecahan biasa siswa kelas IV SD Negeri 101/II Muara Bungo. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode eksperimen dan desain nonequivalent control group design. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas kelas eksperimen yang memperoleh pembelajaran menggunakan model Teams Games Tournament berbantuan media papan pecahan dan kelas kontrol yang memperoleh pembelajaran konvensional. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes uraian yang telah memenuhi persyaratan validitas dan reliabilitas, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif dan inferensial melalui uji normalitas, uji homogenitas, dan uji hipotesis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya pengaruh yang signifikan terhadap pemahaman konsep siswa dengan nilai signifikansi 0,000 (<0,05). Selain itu, rata-rata nilai N-Gain kelas eksperimen sebesar 0,59 berada pada kategori sedang, sedangkan kelas kontrol sebesar 0,22 berada pada kategori rendah. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa model Teams Games Tournament berbantuan media papan pecahan efektif meningkatkan pemahaman konsep penjumlahan dan pengurangan pecahan biasa pada siswa sekolah dasar.

title: Development of an Integrated Model for Enhancing Surgical Capacity in Community Hospitals: A Case Study of Laplae Hospital
container-title: Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand
17e7c0375ec74f53a8a17637a85b770b56ed3ad4.abstract: Objective: To pilot-evaluate an integrated model for enhancing surgical capacity at Laplae Hospital (Uttaradit Province) under Thailand’s “One Province One Hospital” policy. Materials and Methods: A mixed-methods pilot study with a predominantly quantitative, one-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design was conducted between October 2024 and March 2025. The intervention comprised personnel development, infrastructure and technology enhancement, and surgical service system development. Data comprised satisfaction scores (baseline to six months), SF-36 (baseline and one month), clinical and administrative records, and interviews with 12 stakeholders. Analyses used paired t-tests, repeated measures ANOVA, Fisher’s exact test, and content analysis. The 45 patients were the complete census of eligible patients, so findings are preliminary. Results: Forty-seven procedures were performed in 45 patients. Monthly case volume rose 4.5-fold (2 to 9). One day surgery reached 100% of eligible cases by March 2025. One minor complication occurred (2.1%); there were no major complications, unplanned readmissions, or unplanned referrals. Satisfaction improved from 3.1±0.7 to 4.1±0.5 (p<0.001). SF-36 physical domains improved significantly at one month (Bodily pain +21.6, Role limitations-physical +19.4, Physical functioning +16.3, p<0.001). Referrals to Uttaradit Hospital fell from 23 to 7, significantly only for hernia (11 to 3, p=0.011). Key success factors were leadership, provincial hospital collaboration, and progressive implementation; the main barrier was limited perioperative nursing staff. Conclusion: The integrated model appears feasible for strengthening surgical capacity in a community hospital. Given the small, single-site, uncontrolled design, findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered multi-site studies.

title: Digital Visual Learning Materials and Their Impact on Students' English Language Skills: A Guided Inquiry Approach
container-title: Architecture  Image Studies
1038c780f28dc5e4d0947f9a7bd13f7b8af43fcc.abstract: This study investigates the effect of the Guided Inquiry model assisted by Digital Student Worksheets (LKPD) on eleventh-grade students' English language skills, specifically writing creativity, reading comprehension, speaking proficiency, and learning independence. Employing a quasi-experimental design with a Nonequivalent Control Group, the study involved 187 students from SMA Negeri 1 Woha, Bima, West Nusa Tenggara, selected through proportional random sampling and assigned to either an experimental group (Digital LKPD-supported Guided Inquiry) or a control group (conventional instruction). Pre- and post-tests were administered across all four outcome variables, and data were analyzed using Multivariate Analysis of Covariance (MANCOVA) and N-Gain tests. Results demonstrated statistically significant improvements in the experimental group across all four variables: writing creativity (t = 3.542; p = 0.001), reading comprehension (t = 3.215; p = 0.002), speaking skills (t = 3.611; p = 0.001), and learning independence (t = 3.214; p = 0.002). The MANCOVA revealed a simultaneous significant effect of the instructional model on all dependent variables (Pillai's Trace = 0.913; p < 0.001). N-Gain scores indicated moderate-to-high improvement in the experimental group (M = 0.65) compared to the control group (M = 0.35). These findings suggest that integrating digital visual learning materials within a Guided Inquiry framework functions not merely as a content delivery mechanism, but as a strategic instructional design component that promotes self-regulated learning, cognitive engagement, and holistic English language literacy development in 21st-century educational contexts.

title: CLASSIFICATION OF PUBLIC OPINION ON FOREST MANAGEMENT IN SOUTHEAST SULAWESI PROVINCE BASED ON SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS USING AN LSTM-BASED DEEP LEARNING MODEL
container-title: Simtek : jurnal sistem informasi dan teknik komputer
e175f0a942c8b79fe961770e698ff3a2be91fc3f.abstract: Forest management requires information support capable of rapidly capturing public responses. However, social media opinions are unstructured and difficult to analyze manually on a large scale. This study developed an opinion classification model based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) to categorize YouTube comments related to forest management in Southeast Sulawesi Province into positive, negative, and neutral sentiment classes. A total of 1,875 comments were collected from 40 public videos across 30 YouTube channels using the YouTube Data API v3. Following initial labeling and preprocessing, 1,838 comments were retained for model development. The dataset was stratified into 1,286 training samples, 184 validation samples, and 368 testing samples. The model architecture consisted of a 128-dimensional embedding layer, 128 bidirectional LSTM units, dropout regularization, and a three-class softmax output layer. On the test dataset, the model achieved an accuracy of 89.40%, weighted precision of 89.49%, weighted recall of 89.40%, and weighted F1-score of 88.83%. The neutral class achieved an F1-score of 94.01%, outperforming the positive and negative classes, which obtained F1-scores of 64.71% and 58.82%, respectively. These findings indicate that the model is effective for overall sentiment classification; however, class imbalance limits its ability to consistently identify minority classes. Therefore, the classification results are more appropriately utilized as preliminary analytical support for understanding public opinion, while further improvements in labeling quality and data balancing are necessary to enhance classification performance.

title: Digital Technology Use, Cognitive Engagement and Perceived Learning Effectiveness Among Adult Learners in Non-Formal Education in Uzbekistan
45a1f4b7c88044561b62fd4240d2f0ed18697212.abstract: Abstract Although digital technologies are increasingly embedded in adult education policy, evidence from post-Soviet Central Asia remains scarce. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study examined how digital technology use relates to two proximal indicators of learning processes – cognitive engagement and perceived learning effectiveness – among adults in non-formal education programmes in Uzbekistan. Survey data from 312 learners nested in 26 programmes across three provinces were analysed with two-level random-intercept models, followed by semi-structured interviews with 22 learners and two facilitators, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. After adjustment for age, gender, educational attainment, urban–rural location and programme type, digital technology use was positively associated with cognitive engagement (β = .38, 95% CI [.27, .49]) and perceived learning effectiveness (β = .35, 95% CI [.24, .46]). Between 17% and 18% of the variance in each outcome lay at the programme level. Four qualitative themes – socially produced digital self-efficacy, peer-mediated learning, institutional culture and structural barriers – helped to explain these patterns. Interpreted through self-directed learning theory and the capability approach, the findings suggest that the educational value of digital tools depends on the social and institutional conditions in which adults use them. The cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report preclude causal inference.

title: Pengaruh Metode Lattice Terhadap Hasil Belajar Operasi Perkalian Bilangan Cacah Dengan Menggunakan Model PBL Di Kelas IV Sekolah Dasar

4fe4ba2b2e6bad6c168bab3b0e7733cefe3db2da.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of using the lattice method on the learning outcomes of multiplication operations of integers in class IV elementary school. This research is experimental research in the form of Quasi Experimental Type Nonequivalent Control Group Design. The sampling technique used cluster random sampling. In hypothesis testing, simple linear regression test, correlation analysis, and t test were used. Based on correlation analysis, the experimental class obtained rxy 0.825 which is categorized as very strong. The coefficient determination value obtained is 68.06%, so it can be interpreted that the use of the lattice method has an effect of 68.06% on the learning outcomes of multiplying small numbers in class IV. Through the t-test in the form of an independent t-test based on the posttest scores of the experimental and control classes, a tcount of 2.04613 was obtained with a ttable of 2.014 at a significance level of 0.05. When the tcount and ttable are compared, 2.04613 > 2.014. This means that Ho is rejected, and Ha is accepted, so it can be concluded that there is a significant effect of using the lattice method with the PBL model on the learning outcomes of multiplication operations of small numbers in class IV elementary schools
