The obtained results indicate that an optimal combination of mineral nutrition and Moddus retardant application can contribute to improving the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat plants.</jats:p>

title: Unsupervised detection of overshooting defects using hybrid generative and boundary classification models
container-title: Journal of Logic and Computation
b19d81e4c7fded96c96974ee9938770ef3f357d8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Quality control in modern manufacturing increasingly relies on unsupervised anomaly detection to identify structural defects when abnormal samples are critically scarce. This study presents an evaluation of hybrid generative architectures designed to detect complex overshooting anomalies in industrial simple sub-assemblies base plates. We analysed eight distinct model combinations by pairing four advanced generative backbones, including a latent space resampling autoencoder and a denoising diffusion model, with two boundary classification strategies: the one class support vector machine and the deep support vector data description. The experimental results demonstrate that the configuration pairing the latent space resampling autoencoder with the one class support vector machine achieves superior detection capabilities, securing the highest mean area under the curve of 0.7870 alongside absolute statistical dominance. However, our findings reveal a critical architectural vulnerability, as pairing heavily regularized generative latent spaces with the rigid hyperspherical boundaries of the deep data description model invariably degrades detection, driving in the most strongly regularized configuration a systematic inversion of the anomaly score rather than a loss of discriminative power. Ultimately, this research establishes that flexible margin optimization is required to preserve anomaly detection accuracy in complex industrial topologies, providing a framework for deploying reliable automated quality assurance systems.</jats:p>

36d6b77407653d455c80e2f500634a6232d7a5a9.abstract: <jats:p>The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning for Adaptive Management of Renewable Hybrid Power Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
8dbc26d9167ed7772f47b06f9aa8d0293cf7c8ac.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the problem of adaptive control for hybrid renewable energy systems combining photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and battery storage under conditions of generation uncertainty and price volatility. A control strategy based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, which does not require an explicit mathematical model and accounts for long-term consequences, including battery degradation. The control task is formalized as a markov decision process with an integral discounted reward combining economic costs, penalties for energy curtailment, and storage aging losses. Computational experiments on real meteorological data demonstrate that the trained regulator reduces operating costs by 12–15% compared to heuristic strategies, increases the share of renewable energy used by 18–22%, and extends estimated battery life by 15–20%. The results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach over classical methods, particularly under high uncertainty. Limitations and prospects for practical implementation are discussed.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
5f910b7c7ff3cc7a08791e8c37c348d51a9d359d.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Assisted Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Microgrids for Sustainable Rural Electrification
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
96ab7ef154dc58376a40cf75f589dc662f80d0d9.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter reviews conventional optimization methods and AI-assisted approaches for hybrid renewable energy microgrids, highlighting their roles in system planning, sizing, operation, and control. It also explores emerging technologies, including reinforcement learning, explainable AI, digital twins, and edge AI, that are shaping the next generation of intelligent energy systems. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, the chapter presents a case study of a hybrid renewable energy microgrid in Muanda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, featuring solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, and blue-carbon bioenergy resources. The case study shows how optimization techniques can enhance techno-economic and environmental performance and discusses the potential of AI-based forecasting, intelligent battery management, and reinforcement learning to further improve system reliability, renewable energy utilization, and long-term sustainability.</jats:p>

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ff36013178296736d6e2747d2c7e1830b32bd841.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Optimization of Solar Thermal Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
0860e093417810bedf80a8a8c80f3dec419bac99.abstract: <jats:p>Solar thermal systems encounter distinct operational challenges, which hinder their applicability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to solve them. The AI is more flexible and adaptable than traditional methods, which cannot deal with unpredictable factors, including changing weather and fluctuating energy demands. In this chapter, we introduced the solar thermal systems, and then the fundamentals of AI techniques used in solar thermal systems were provided. Subsequently, the application of AI in solar thermal systems was discussed. The advantages of the optimization process of the solar thermal systems were identified, supported by case studies from the real world. Then we identified the limitations and constraints that hinder the integration of AI into the solar thermal system. Finally, the economic benefits of using AI for the optimization of solar thermal systems were explained.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Solar Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
81ed3d5ef17a5775f35361935d09bc66b4b5cc4e.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyses the strategic incorporation of artificial intelligence technology into renewable energy systems to enhance energy security, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability. This chapter aims to examine how intelligent energy management systems, machine learning algorithms, smart grids, decentralized microgrids, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks can enhance the performance and resilience of renewable energy systems. This chapter places emphasis on predictive analytics, battery management, solar forecasting, digital twins, and autonomous energy optimization. The chapter examines the economic, environmental, and technological ramifications of intelligent energy systems, emphasizing their capacity to minimize energy losses, improve system reliability, facilitate decentralized electrification, and expedite sustainable energy transitions towards enhanced national energy independence.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning for Solar Thermal Energy Optimization and Smart Control
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
fb44f8ecb89dccb4a11eab978ce879fb41e44f26.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.</jats:p>

title: Energy Audits in Tanzanian Industrial SMEs for Methods, Barriers, and M&V-Linked Savings Prioritization
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
b85063b2e64cb2adf03e3a6fd9c4b42f3f347e50.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.</jats:p>

title: Biogas Production Optimisation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
3a1fabea3f97fb97115f71a9b24c656748b30ad4.abstract: <jats:p>Anaerobic co-digestion is an effective approach for biogas production, but optimizing operating parameters remains challenging due to the interaction of multiple variables. This study integrates ultrasonic pretreatment with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to enhance biogas yield from a mixture of dormitory food waste and pet animal dung. Batch digesters were operated at 37 °C, and daily biogas production was monitored. RSM evaluated the combined effects of ultrasonic temperature (25–65 °C), power (500–1,500 W), and treatment time (35–75 min). Biogas yield ranged from 35% to nearly 68%, with optimum conditions of 53.35 °C, 1,490.83 W, and 57.15 min, producing a predicted yield of 66.47%. The quadratic model showed excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9707; F = 110.33), confirming the importance of simultaneous optimization. The integrated ultrasonic–RSM approach provides a reliable and efficient strategy for maximizing biogas production in anaerobic co-digestion systems.</jats:p>

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
638e43b89445c1c4efd078d51246af0e90e11d12.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.</jats:p>

title: Forecasting Electrical Load and Renewable Energy Generation Using Machine Learning Methods
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ea63ae340e55dcd23a21c92099270e55640a1e65.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The purpose is to show why power systems need models handling nonlinear, non-stationary, and heterogeneous data. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
db14ec7802b2943f0f932ee90ef99812da7cac80.abstract: <jats:p>Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.</jats:p>

title: Integrasi AI dalam Kurikulum Akuntansi Pendidikan Pesantren: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis tentang Kesiapan Teknologi, Pemahaman AI, dan Karakteristik Siswa
container-title: Business and Accounting Education Journal
e0f60edd89c8c829c91e27e2720ae59dca61591c.abstract: <jats:p>Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong transformasi pendidikan akuntansi dan menuntut penyesuaian kurikulum agar sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia kerja digital. Namun, adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi masih dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor, khususnya pada konteks pendidikan pesantren yang memiliki karakteristik unik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kesiapan teknologi, pemahaman AI, dan karakteristik siswa terhadap adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi serta mengidentifikasi faktor yang paling dominan. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Data diperoleh dari 38 artikel ilmiah terindeks Scopus yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2015-2026 dan dianalisis menggunakan sintesis tematik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kesiapan teknologi merupakan faktor yang paling dominan dalam mendorong adopsi AI, diikuti oleh pemahaman AI dan karakteristik siswa. Ketiga faktor tersebut saling melengkapi dalam meningkatkan penerimaan dan pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran akuntansi. Temuan ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan model adopsi teknologi pendidikan serta menjadi dasar pengembangan kurikulum akuntansi berbasis AI di lingkungan pesantren.</jats:p>

title: KUNJUTNING ODDIY VA BEKROSS CHATISHTIRISH NATIJASIDA OLINGAN F1  DURAGAYLARIDA O‘SIMLIK BO‘YI VA YON SHOXLARI SONI BELGILARINING IRSIYLANISHI
container-title: Agro ilm
a1fc8d526224f83eedb1e34addc24c0a8e924a52.abstract: <jats:p>The study investigated the inheritance of important morphological traits, including plant height and the number of lateral branches, in simple and backcross F₁ sesame hybrids involving the local varieties “Onimdar”, “Qora Shahzoda”, “Tashkent-122”, and “Sadaf”. The experiments were conducted under field and laboratory conditions. The patterns of trait formation and the degree of heterosis in the hybrids were analyzed. The number of lateral branches ranged from 5.8 to 6.2 per plant in the local varieties, from 5.7 to 8.7 in simple F₁ hybrids, and from 5.6 to 9.2 in backcross hybrids. Positive heterosis for the number of lateral branches was observed in most of the simple hybrids. Positive inheritance of this trait was also recorded in several backcross combinations. Promising hybrid combinations with high values of plant height and the number of lateral branches were identified. The results indicate that the selected hybrid combinations can be used in sesame breeding to develop valuable initial breeding material with high productivity, stability, and adaptability to local environmental conditions.</jats:p>

title: SUG‘ORILADIGAN YERLAR UCHUN ARPA SELEKSIYASIDA OLIB BORILAYOTGAN TADQIQOTLAR
container-title: Agro ilm
11f8545db76c4de11946113dd99d4f0d407be82d.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of research aimed at identifying valuable initial breeding material for barley breeding on irrigated lands. The studies were conducted in 2023–2026 at the experimental field of the “Farboma selekt” scientific seed-growing farm located in Jomboy district of Samarkand region. A total of 200 barley collection accessions obtained from the international centers ICARDA and CIMMYT, as well as the Institute of Plant Science and the Gallaorol Research and Experimental Station of the Research Institute of Grain and Legume Crops, were studied. The accessions were evaluated for productive tillering, number and weight of grains per spike, 1000-grain weight, yield, earliness, and resistance to diseases, winter conditions and lodging. The study identified valuable barley accessions with high productivity and yield potential. In particular, the Mirzacho‘l, K-22845, K-19985, Temur and K-566244 accessions demonstrated high yield performance. The selected accessions are recommended as valuable initial breeding material for developing new high-yielding, early-maturing and environmentally stress-resistant barley varieties for irrigated lands.</jats:p>

1b789f66974ff8f4fd2e295ce7e9d1f77d3f316f.abstract: <jats:p>The article examines the impact of sowing methods, timing, and rates on the yield and grain quality of chickpea varieties in irrigated lands (under the conditions of the Kashkadarya region). The research results demonstrate the extent of this influence on the productivity and grain quality of chickpea varieties in the irrigated soils of the Kashkadarya region.</jats:p>

2ead1d54242c055a6be9b67d6bb932a0a527fc9a.abstract: <jats:p>The article studies the formation of plant density in chickpea varieties under different irrigation methods and irrigation regimes. The study examined the effects of furrow, drip and sprinkler irrigation, as well as irrigation regimes of 65–70–60%, 70–75–65% and 75–80–70% of field capacity. The results showed that plant density of the Zumrad and Malhotra chickpea varieties varied depending on the irrigation method and soil moisture regime. The highest plant density was recorded under drip irrigation with an irrigation regime of 75–80–70% of field capacity in the Malhotra variety, reaching 282.7 plants/m² at the beginning of the growing period and 275.3 plants/m² at the end. The obtained results demonstrate the importance of selecting an appropriate irrigation method and soil moisture regime for chickpea cultivation.</jats:p>

Within these systems—and using resource-saving cultivation technologies—the study evaluates leaf surface area, dry matter accumulation, chlorophyll content, and indicators of the rice crop's biological potential.</jats:p>

d1d6335ad64612a8fb5eeed16444419c039626bd.abstract: <jats:p>High-density orchards require low-vigor saplings. Scientists have recommended several methods for producing such saplings; the most important among these are bud-grafting onto dwarf rootstocks and the use of a dwarfing interstock. In fruit-growing practice, dwarf rootstocks are propagated via layering and softwood cuttings, after which cultivated varieties are grafted onto them using budding or winter bench grafting.</jats:p>

title: O‘ZBEKISTON HUDUDLARI UCHUN TAVSIYA ETILGAN UZUM NAVLARI

439ef8b09f755e85cf526670a17075cd172f33b8.abstract: <jats:p>The article analyzes the selection and recommendation of grape varieties for different regions of Uzbekistan considering local soil and climatic conditions. Economic and biological characteristics of early-ripening, mid-ripening, table and seedless raisin varieties were summarized together with their regional adaptation. Recommendations for the distribution of varieties across southern, central, valley and northern regions were developed. The analysis indicates that selecting grape varieties according to regional soil and climatic conditions is important for improving yield, product quality and production efficiency.</jats:p>

title: O‘ZBEKISTON IQLIM SHAROITIDA O‘RMA TUTZORLARNING MAVSUMIY O‘SISH DINAMIKASI VA REGENERATSIYA XUSUSIYATLARI

ea346533c1c20f87656be5bba609f0064e2f0e05.abstract: <jats:p>This article evaluates the seasonal growth dynamics of low-stem fodder mulberry plantations under the climatic conditions of Uzbekistan in 2025-2026 based on phenological and biometric indicators. The highest morphological and economically valuable traits were recorded during the summer period. The average shoot length was 136 cm in 2025 and 143.0 cm in 2026. Although 33.5% of the shoot length was damaged by frost in the spring of 2026 due to insufficient lignification following late autumn pruning, the plants demonstrated a high regenerative capacity during the summer period. The results indicate the necessity of optimizing pruning times, ensuring regular irrigation, and creating suitable conditions for the complete lignification of shoots before the onset of winter in order to achieve a high mulberry leaf yield.</jats:p>

5463ba229394efece8ff2e67ed36ce2903f11291.abstract: <jats:p>In the studies, healthy mini-tubers of the potato variety Ranome, propagated in vitro, were planted at an early date, and the resulting crop was cultivated as a double-crop system. The application of the Biogrand biopreparation at a rate of 1,000–1,200 mL/ha during the growing season demonstrated the highest efficacy. In the summer double-cropping system, the yield reached 24.8 t/ha, resulting in an additional yield of 5.4 t/ha, or 21.7%, compared with the control.</jats:p>

It is empirically proven that the Crimean variety 'Krupnoplodnaya' provides the maximum yield (12.8 t/ha) and record profitability (235%), while the ultra-early local variety 'Tashkentskaya rannaya', commercialized at an exceptionally high starting price of 2100 sum/kg, generates the absolute maximum net profit, reaching 40,866 thousand sums per hectare. Synthesizing the obtained data, the authors justify the economic feasibility of combining high-yield and early-ripening cultivars when establishing modern intensive orchards, ensuring a continuous financial inflow.</jats:p>

title: Tau hadronic decay channel reconstruction with a Lorentz-covariant graph attention network
container-title: Physica Scripta
48dd6af93c13d027dd2a5b2312100fb17c5e3a52.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The reconstruction of hadronic decay modes of the
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    lepton is a key task in high-energy physics experiments, directly impacting precision measurements and new physics searches. Conventional reconstruction approaches rely on handcrafted features and rule-based algorithms, which face challenges in handling complex decay topologies and detector effects. In this work, we propose LCGA-Net, a physics-informed deep learning framework for
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    decay channel classification and four-momentum reconstruction. The method represents decay products as particle graphs and employs a multi-head attention mechanism to capture inter-particle correlations. To ensure physical consistency, Lorentz-invariant constraints are explicitly incorporated into the model architecture. A dedicated single-
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    dataset is constructed from the simulation data of the Circular Electron Positron Collider, covering six major hadronic decay modes. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89.2% on the validation set, matching or slightly exceeding baseline models. More importantly, full physics constraints substantially improve the physical plausibility of reconstructed four-momenta—particularly the energy–momentum relation—without degrading classification performance. These results demonstrate that integrating physics priors with attention-based deep learning on particle clouds provides an effective approach for
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    decay reconstruction, with potential applications in future high-energy physics analyses.
                  </jats:p>

55816ce3ad05f99e99fd19b0d898a3c5847daddf.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of studying the effects of different irrigation methods and regimes on the growth, development, productivity indicators, and yield of the "Ispanskaya 73" pumpkin variety and the "Ferrari F1" hybrid under the irrigated light-serozem soil conditions of the southern region of the Surkhandarya Province. 68b917fda5a9eff858671cf5df73d0cbcce02b1c.abstract: <jats:p>This article investigates the effectiveness of biological fertilizers and resource-saving agrotechnologies for potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) cultivation under the natural, climatic, and soil conditions of the Republic of Karakalpakstan. Based on field experiments, the effects of biological fertilizers on potato plant growth and development, tuber formation, yield, and product quality were evaluated. The results showed that, compared with the control, the application of biofertilizers increased plant height by 8-12% and the number of stems by 10-15%, while the number of tubers per plant increased from 7-8 to 9-11 tubers. Yield increased from 22-24 t/ha to 27-32 t/ha, corresponding to an approximately 21-36% increase compared with the control. The starch content of the tubers was 1,5-2,5 percentage points higher than in the control. In addition, the application of biological fertilizers enhanced soil biological activity and improved the uptake of nutrients by plants. The findings demonstrate that integrating biological fertilizers with resource-saving agrotechnologies is a promising agroecological approach for improving the efficiency of potato production under the conditions of Karakalpakstan.</jats:p>

title:
Enhancement of switching characteristics in protonic ECRAM through density-controlled ZrO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    electrolyte via low-temperature atomic layer deposition
container-title: Nanotechnology
b2adbf53142d49e54809b8e49f02b2115ce67429.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Proton-based electrochemical random-access memory (H-ECRAM) has attracted attention as a promising emerging memory for neuromorphic computing due to its analog conductance modulation and high energy efficiency. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is attractive due to its excellent conformality and scalability. However, the inherently high density of ALD-grown electrolyte films limits ionic transport, leading to degraded switching performance of H-ECRAM. In this work, we address this issue by engineering the density of ZrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    electrolytes through low-temperature ALD. By reducing the deposition temperature, the film density is effectively decreased and density-controlled ZrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>

ba2f8cb62b86caf4dd1d343ac5b4545c93d29a4a.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents the findings of a multi-year study evaluating the effects of convective drying temperatures and processing durations on the dried product yield of six promising fig cultivars — Uzbekskiy zheltiy, Krym 9, Krym 29, Krym 43, Karshinskiy cherniy, and Dalmatskiy, grown under the subtropical conditions of Surkhandarya region. Uzbekskiy zheltiy (average yield of 42.04%) and Dalmatskiy (39.17%) exhibited notable technological stability and uniform moisture release, whereas Krym 29 and Krym 43 demonstrated rapid desiccation, achieving target moisture levels 10–15 hours earlier than the other cultivars. title: Self-attention-aided multi-layer CNN-LSTM for non-uniform 4-level differential amplitude modulation and detection with atmospheric turbulence for OWANs

fedd060d0254eff3eb9ce0c2cc0964613783fd42.abstract: <jats:p>This paper proposes an environment-aware four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation and detection scheme assisted by self-attentive multi-layer CNN-LSTM (SA-CNN-LSTM) for optical wireless access networks (OWANs) under atmospheric turbulence, to mitigate severe distortions induced by atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Relying on four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation (NUADM-4) and a self-attention-aided detection algorithm at the receiving terminal, the proposed scheme can effectively suppress both multiplicative turbulence fading and additive Gaussian noise simultaneously. Numerical results reveal that the proposed scheme achieves remarkable bit error rate (BER) improvements compared with conventional detection frameworks for NUADM-4, and it substantially outperforms the classical uniform four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) across diverse turbulence strength regimes. Moreover, the tailored architecture integrating self-attention with multi-layer CNN-LSTM maintains high transmission efficiency, reduces the dimension of the fully-connected layer at the receiver to a certain extent, and accelerates the computation speed compared with the CNN-based algorithm. In comparison with conventional detection-aided algorithms such as vanilla CNN, LSTM, and MLP, the presented scheme delivers a universal BER performance gain. Furthermore, the machine-learning-aided design philosophy for different modulation systems offers a practical design paradigm and implementable solution for the engineering deployment of high-speed OWC systems serving OWANs operating in volatile atmospheric turbulence environments.</jats:p>

title: Bridging or Widening the Gap? AI Policies and Social Justice in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
038583ab9446f69693d78ffd45b815c6af816060.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as a means to improve educational quality, efficiency, and equity. However, when introduced into systems already shaped by inequality, AI risks reproducing rather than reducing social injustice. This chapter examines whether AI policies in education bridge or widen existing gaps, drawing on Nancy Fraser's framework of redistribution, recognition, and representation. Through a comparative analysis of supranational frameworks and national strategies in the United States, China, India, and Türkiye, the chapter identifies persistent tensions between innovation-driven agendas and justice-oriented goals. The findings suggest that equity is often framed in technocratic terms, while issues of power, participation, and accountability remain marginal. The chapter concludes by proposing a justice-centered policy evaluation framework that emphasizes democratic governance, cultural responsiveness, and the right to contest or refuse harmful AI systems.</jats:p>

5fb7b6f93a03dabd2aadb285a6f2da9c7a9936b8.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid urbanization and climate imperatives place cities at the center of energy transformation, yet thermal demand roughly half of urban energy end-use remains under addressed by electricity focused renewable strategies. e5acdeb20d729b725992dc8343811299e03d8c4b.abstract: <jats:p>The corn moth overwinters primarily in the soil in the pupal stage. In the spring, as temperatures rise, the adults emerge and lay eggs on newly sown plots. Upon hatching, the larvae penetrate the soil and feed on germinating seeds, root collars, and young stems. As a result, seedling growth ceases or the plants wither. Development takes 20—40 days, depending on climatic conditions. Most species produce 2—4 generations per year. This article examines the development of the corn moth (Anthomyiidae) and the biological efficacy of control measures against it.</jats:p>

title: СИММЕНТАЛ ЗОТЛИ СИГИРЛАРНИНГ ПУШТДОРЛИК ХУСУСИЯТЛАРИ

18cd92c73dac5749719c45c1bd85abd95a604d36.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents information on the characteristics of Simmental cows belonging to different production types. The study found that the age at first calving was 789.5 days for cows of the dairy type and 795.1 days for those of the dairy-beef type; these figures were 11.1 and 5.5 days lower, respectively, than the age at first calving for cows of the beef-dairy type. Additionally, the service period lasted 78.3 days for dairy-type cows and 81.2 days for dairy-beef-type cows—4.2 and 1.3 days shorter, respectively, than the service period for beef-dairy-type cows. Research findings regarding the duration of the service period indicate that the cow itself is a primary factor determining reproductive performance; this highlights the importance of effectively utilizing cows of dairy and dual-purpose (dairy-beef) types for milk production.</jats:p>

Separating current and potential suitability and using GIS zoning makes it possible to select irrigation technologies that better match local conditions.</jats:p>

ba0ed90ab84fabb0583adc409521ff67536ed2c8.abstract: <jats:p>This article highlights the agrochemical properties of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils of Sharaf Rashidovsky district of the Jizzakh Free Economic Zone (JEZ), reserves of humus, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and potassium. There is a high probability of heavy metal pollution in the region near industrial zones, free economic zones, and irrigation networks. Since these soils have a relatively humic layer, as well as a unique water-retaining structure, heavy metals can accumulate in the soil and negatively affect its agrochemical properties. Heavy metals adhere to soil colloids and retain their activity in the soil for a long time. In the soil under study, the lead content of Pb is 40-80 mg/kg (the norm is 32 mg/kg or more), cadmium CD is 0.5 - 2.0 mg/kg (the norm is 0.5 mg/kg or more), zinc Zn is 150-220 mg/kg (the norm is 100 mg/kg or more). This situation indicates an increase in the level of pollution combined with salinization and carbonate content of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils.</jats:p>

title: LEGUME CROP PRODUCTION IN UZBEKISTAN: AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS OF DETERMINANTS

b7f635d6999751960d8ed769b449e51e02d7f0e9.abstract: <jats:p>This paper examines factors affecting legume production in Uzbekistan using cross-sectional data from 1,225 farmers across 12 districts in the UzFarmBarometer 2024 database. A probit model identifies factors associated with the probability of legume adoption. Results show that older farmers are less likely to cultivate legumes, while larger households and more experienced farmers are more likely to adopt them. Earlier-established farms also show lower adoption. Distance to input markets is positively associated with adoption, whereas distance to output markets is negatively associated with it, reflecting differences in input dependence and transaction costs. We suggest that improving rural market infrastructure, extension services, and stable labor arrangements could support legume cultivation.</jats:p>

title: AI adoption in purchasing and supply management: how institutional voids rewire the UTAUT framework

fd976dc156551128de71dc829f70972275c8141d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study investigates how institutional voids and behavioral factors jointly drive artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in purchasing and supply management (PSM) within emerging economies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Survey data from 200 PSM professionals in Morocco were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test an integrated UTAUT–institutional theory framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Performance expectancy (PE) (ß = 0.530) and social influence (ß = 0.453) primarily drive behavioral intention (BI), while coercive pressure is non-significant (ß = 0.050, p = 0.260). Facilitating conditions (FC) (ß = 0.472) and (BI) (ß = 0.497) exert near-equal direct effects on actual use, confirming an “infrastructure imperative”. Post-hoc multi-group analysis reveals that PE dominates predictive AI adoption, whereas effort expectancy dominates Generative AI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Organizations in emerging economies must pair AI software procurement with dedicated infrastructure, data governance and peer-led change management rather than relying on unsupported mandates.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study demonstrates that institutional voids modify the UTAUT nomological network by elevating FC to a primary co-determinant of technology use, proving infrastructure readiness equals user intention in driving adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Future of work in the era of AI: how technology strategy shapes daily job roles
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
aafce7fbea450e0f9f9a750ed043c623a0abe324.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to explore the impact of organizational technology strategies, particularly in the context of artificial intelligence (AI), on employees’ daily job activities. It also looks at the extent of the transformation and the role of leadership, supportive of innovation and cultural change, in reinforcing the transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The researcher adopted a quantitative research design based on the survey data collected from employees in various industries in Pakistan. The researcher used structural equation modeling to analyze the relationships among technology strategies, organizational facilitators and the transformation of job roles.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research shows that organizations that implement AI and automation alongside digitized processes and advanced data analysis capabilities will experience fundamental changes in their employees’ work functions, skills and job duties. The implementation of digital strategies enhances operational efficiency, but their impact extends beyond this benefit, as they completely transform how work is executed. The presence of an innovation-supportive culture together with strong leadership commitment creates an enhanced effect. The combination of encouragement of organizational experimentation and active leadership support for technological change results in more visible and positive changes in job responsibilities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research findings demonstrate that organizations need to combine technology investments with operational changes to achieve successful digital transformation outcomes. Organizations must establish supportive cultures together with proactive leadership to assist employees throughout the process of organizational change. Organizations need to develop their employees’ skills and build adaptable workforces while maintaining open communication to implement meaningful job role changes that last over time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research contributes to the future of work literature by examining how workers change their job functions at the individual-employee level rather than observing outcomes at the organizational level. The research describes how organizations use technology strategies and organizational enablers to create distinct work environments for the AI age by integrating Job Demands–Resources and Socio-Technical Systems perspectives.</jats:p>

title: The copilot paradox: configurational pathways to human-AI symbiosis in knowledge work
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
10429646653846e10fef0781eea8935c49efcda2.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the “Copilot Paradox” in safety-critical operations, offering insights into how the chronic tension between the algorithm’s increased efficiency and operational vulnerability is subdued through socio-cognitive configurations across time. Design/methodology/approach With the use of a two-wave longitudinal fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), the paper explores the changing dynamics of human–artificial intelligence (AI) symbiosis in the oil and gas industry. Findings Analysis of necessity shows that there is no single condition required in all cases. Sufficiency analysis reveals three distinct, equifinal pathways: buffering, synergy and substitution. At early adoption, institutional re-skilling coupled with psychological safety acts as a buffering mechanism against job insecurity induced by AI. As integration progresses, synergy (fuelled by empowering leadership) and substitution (where team resources fill the gaps in leadership) come to dominate. Practical implications Team psychological safety and capability building are structural safeguards for managers in high-reliability sectors, not optional cultural flourishes. These lessons point to pathways for realising AI copilots while preserving human agency and operational resiliency. Originality/value This paper contributes to paradox theory by developing a socio-cognitive infrastructure that highlights its dynamic, temporal configuration and causal asymmetries. Methodologically, it showcases the new promise of longitudinal fsQCA to model dynamics in algorithms’ infusion by capturing their embeddedness through time.

title: From risk management to AI-enabled governance: five intellectual orientations in EPC and infrastructure project risk governance
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
262b73632bb16a2f06249b0dfe727ae37edc8674.abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesise the intellectual development of engineering–procurement–construction and infrastructure project risk governance and examine whether bibliometric evidence supports five overlapping intellectual orientations. Design/methodology/approach The study combined bibliometric analysis with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and a scripted workflow to examine 173 Scopus-indexed publications (1999–2026). The analytical corpus was derived through relevance validation of 678 candidate records, with provenance checked against an 801-row master ledger. Fifteen provisional 2026 records were excluded from temporal comparisons. Findings The analysis identified five orientations: risk analysis and control (53 documents), performance and overrun (80), governance and relational mechanisms (52), digital information integration (7) and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support (18). The share of period publications addressing performance and overrun increased from 34.7 % in 1999–2018 to 59.7 % in 2023–2025, whereas the digital and AI orientations remained comparatively limited. These patterns concern the published literature and do not establish organizational maturity or realised capability. Research limitations/implications Scopus coverage, title/abstract-based relevance validation, citation lag, analytical thresholds and interpretive coding delimit the findings. Project-level research is required to test the proposed relationships. Practical implications The orientations provide structured review prompts for risk processes, outcome linkage, decision rights, information integration and human oversight of predictive systems; they are not intended as a diagnostic maturity instrument. Originality/value The study connects construction risk, megaproject governance and construction AI through an auditable corpus and an evidence-bounded conceptual framework.

title: Digital and AI tools in informal care: understanding caregivers’ experiences in rural Nigeria
container-title: Working with Older People
3d95ea5e81a5dd3ac98c9f9e80e04a8c952edbad.abstract: Purpose Although informal caregiving for older adults is well-researched, a significant gap exists in understanding how informal caregivers navigate their caregiving roles with the help of digital technologies, especially in rural Nigeria, where internet connectivity is poor and access to digital devices is limited. This study aims to explore how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support care for older adults. Design/methodology/approach The study adopted a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected from 10 informal caregivers, using semi-structured interviews. The data were further analysed thematically using NVivo 14. Findings Results identified that caregivers use digital technology for communication and care coordination, learning and self-empowerment, responding to emergency situations, improving efficiency, reducing stress and maintaining contact between older adults and their diaspora family members. The study also found poor access and limited internet infrastructure as barriers to the use of digital technology to improve caregiving. Research limitations/implications Only caregivers in rural areas were interviewed. This excluded the experiences of caregivers in urban areas, who may face urban economic stressors that shape their overall caregiving experience and their use of digital technology for caregiving. Practical implications The findings highlight the potential of digital technology to support informal caregiving in rural Nigeria. Improving access to affordable digital devices, reliable internet connectivity and digital literacy can enhance care coordination, caregiver support, emergency response and communication with older adults and their families. Originality/value This study is important because it provides new insight into how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support older adults despite limited connectivity and access to digital devices. It highlights both the potential of digital tools to strengthen caregiving and the infrastructural barriers that must be addressed.

title: Librarians' perspectives on AI for environmental sustainability in Ghanaian academic libraries
container-title: Library Hi Tech
931d99d9c196e1b88e58ba8390c4eca27c050aac.abstract: Purpose This study examined academic librarians' perspectives on the potential of artificial intelligence to advance environmental sustainability through sustainable library practices and efficient service delivery. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach was adopted, drawing on semi-structured interviews with 21 academic librarians and guided by the Technology Acceptance Model. Thematic analysis was used to identify key patterns and perspectives on AI adoption for environmental sustainability in academic libraries. Findings The study found that academic librarians recognize AI's potential to advance environmental sustainability through intelligent energy management, predictive maintenance, environmental monitoring, and sustainability planning, yet its practical implementation remains limited. Research limitations/implications The qualitative design and small sample limit generalizability; however, the findings provide contextual insights and a basis for broader research across diverse library settings. Practical implications The findings recommend that universities and library management integrate AI into sustainability planning through effective governance, improved digital infrastructure, and continuous AI literacy training, supported by national policies and investment in responsible AI innovation. Social implications The study highlights the value of AI in advancing environmental sustainability in libraries, emphasizing the need for educational initiatives, institutional policies, and responsible technology adoption. Originality/value This study provides timely empirical insight into AI-enabled environmental sustainability in Ghanaian academic libraries, highlighting the critical gap between librarians' awareness and perceived potential of AI and its limited practical implementation.

title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double‐Blind, Placebo‐Controlled Trial
container-title: Journal of the American Heart Association
47d160a0277168adf9351a8df9bee14429b106b7.abstract: Background Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery. Methods In this single‐center, randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound‐guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge. Results A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention‐to‐treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46–2.15], adjusted P =0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross‐clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06–0.80]; adjusted P =0.022), lower postoperative high‐sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: −2562 ng/L [95% CI, −4301 to −45]; P =0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06–0.98]; adjusted P =0.046). Conclusions While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high‐sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury. Registration URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn ; URL Identifier: ChiCTR2300068572.

title: Capabilities shaping institutional adoption: modeling generative AI adoption in higher education
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
08a009fe077bc5af12d714b4d60c2ab8c6973296.abstract: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet its successful institutional adoption extends beyond technological capability to require effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. This study aims to structurally model the CSFs for GenAI adoption in education using an integrated interpretive structural modeling (ISM)–DEMATEL approach. The authors frame GenAI adoption explicitly as a knowledge management problem, analyzing how governance, infrastructure and privacy conditions enable or inhibit institutional capabilities for creating, sharing and governing GenAI-empowered knowledge. Design/methodology/approach The authors identified ten CSFs through a structured literature review and classified them as enablers, capabilities or outcomes across governance, infrastructure, data privacy, analytics, user experience and academic integrity. To analyze the causal and hierarchical relationships among CSFs, an expert validation was conducted through DEMATEL analysis by 20 experts, followed by ISM modeling, which involved 16 experts. Findings DEMATEL identifies technical infrastructure and scalability (CSF-V), data privacy and security (CSF-VII) and integration with LMS/SSO/enterprise systems (CSF-IX) as prominent causal factors. ISM further positions CSF-V at the deepest foundational level, followed by AI governance, policy and ethics (CSF-III), while assessment integrity and academic honesty (CSF-X) occupies the terminal dependent level. The findings identify assessment integrity (CSF-X), prompt literacy (CSF-IV) and user experience (CSF-VI) as dependent factors, confirming that they emerge from structural readiness rather than acting as independent adoption determinants. Research limitations/implications Results are restricted to expert judgment and defined CSFs, which can reduce generalizability across diverse educational settings. Future research must involve larger samples, validate empirically and use longitudinal designs to study changing relations while also testing the knowledge governance mechanisms revealed in this research. Practical implications The model enables phased prioritization of CSFs for optimal implementation of GenAI. Foundational readiness requires infrastructure, system integration and data governance, followed by governance policies and faculty capacity development, before addressing user experience and academic integrity as dependent outcomes. Originality/value The research provides a systems approach to GenAI adoption in education by presenting an integrated ISM–DEMATEL framework based on TOE and DOI, grounded in knowledge governance theory. It aids authors’ understanding of how technological, organizational and knowledge governance dimensions must be sequentially aligned to enable better implementation of GenAI.

title: Facilitating generative mentoring in higher education: a systematic review and measurement framework for mentoring, generativity, and the minority tax
container-title: International Journal of Mentoring and Coaching in Education
1c4576303f7dc7a655cd1b351ac0a3834966b1b5.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to synthesise how faculty mentoring in higher education has been evaluated in relation to mentor generativity and equity-related pressures (including the minority tax) and to propose a minimum measurement framework for valid evaluation. Design/methodology/approach A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020-guided systematic review was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025647836). The review question was developed using a Sample, Phenomenon of Interest, Design, Evaluation, Research-informed approach appropriate to the inclusion of both quantitative and qualitative evidence. Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and EBSCOhost were searched from database inception to June 2025. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data, study quality was appraised using design-appropriate tools, and findings were narratively synthesised. Findings Eight studies met the inclusion criteria (six quantitative, two qualitative), with most of the evidence from the USA. No study directly measured mentor generativity using validated generativity instruments; instead, studies relied on proxy outcomes (e.g. satisfaction, productivity, promotion). This limits conclusions about the construct validity of generativity and may obscure costs when mentoring demands are high and recognition is low, especially for historically marginalised faculty. Research limitations/implications The evidence base was small (eight studies), predominantly U.S.-based, methodologically heterogeneous, and reliant on proxy outcomes rather than validated measures of mentor generativity. These limitations precluded meta-analysis and causal inference. Future research should directly measure generativity alongside mentoring load, institutional recognition, strain, and equity-related indicators across more diverse regions, disciplines, and institutional contexts. Practical implications The framework provides institutions and researchers with a concise set of indicators to evaluate mentoring programmes, inform workload crediting and promotion criteria, and monitor equity in the distribution and recognition of mentoring labour. Originality/value This review reframes the evaluation of faculty mentoring as a construct-measurement problem and proposes a minimum measurement framework that distinguishes direct generativity from commonly used proxy outcomes. By integrating mentoring load, institutional recognition, strain, and equity considerations, the framework also provides a basis for empirically testing the proposed “generativity paradox”, the conditions under which mentoring may be experienced as renewing, burdensome, or both.

title: The relationship between AI awareness and thriving at work: exploring the moderated mediation model
container-title: European Journal of Training and Development
cfd18b7156538271965b458c0a8e74dbffca959e.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the socially embedded model of thriving and the conservation of resources model, this study aims to investigate the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) awareness, seen as a hindrance stressor, and thriving at work. In particular, it explores how AI anxiety mediates this relationship and how self-efficacy moderates the mediating effect. Design/methodology/approach To securitize the study hypotheses, data were obtained from banking employees via an electronic questionnaire, yielding 320 valid responses. The proposed model relationships were assessed through partial least squares structural equation modeling and process analysis. Findings The results uncover that while AI awareness is not significantly linked to vitality, it is negatively correlated with learning. Furthermore, AI anxiety mediates the direct influence that AI awareness has on dimensions of thriving at work. In addition, self-efficacy acts as a buffer, mitigating the adverse indirect influence of AI awareness on thriving at work through AI anxiety. Practical implications This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and digital literacy programs, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change. Originality/value This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and revise their role descriptions, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change.

title: Demystifying generative AI adoption in higher education: an integrated GRAI–AKM framework
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
2d81d35ddbb0a163d25a04512796c4f2fe000a1d.abstract: Purpose Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet successful institutional adoption requires effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. Existing studies have predominantly relied on individual-level technology acceptance models, providing limited insight into organizational and knowledge management capabilities for sustainable implementation. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed using open-ended written responses from 20 academic professionals recruited through Prolific. The qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis, and the resulting themes were mapped onto the proposed graphs with results and actions interconnected (GRAI) and active knowledge models (AKM) framework (GRAI–AKM). Findings Six themes were identified: (1) professional training and AI literacy, (2) ethical governance and academic integrity, (3) structural capital flexibility and knowledge processes, (4) trust, transparency and relational capital, (5) platform maturity and technological infrastructure and (6) human–AI complementarity. Professional training and AI literacy emerged as the most-discussed themes. The findings suggest that Gen AI adoption depends on the interaction of human, structural, technological, and knowledge resources rather than technology acceptance alone. Research limitations/implications Although based on a qualitative sample and self-reported written responses, the study advances knowledge management research by integrating Intellectual Capital (IC) and the Knowledge-Based View (KBV) into a comprehensive framework. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy, ethical governance, organizational learning and human–AI collaboration for sustainable adoption of Gen AI in higher education. Originality/value The study provides qualitative empirical support for the GRAI–AKM framework, offering a multidimensional perspective on knowledge management for sustainable adoption of Gen AI.

title: Organizational AI orientation, AI self-efficacy and value co-creation: a human-AI collaboration perspective in healthcare
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
6445e52cab7175f314892526d760c6e1d1251ed8.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital to healthcare system transformation. Existing research mainly focuses on the macro-level technological empowerment of AI, yet insufficiently explores how healthcare organizations’ strategic commitment to AI translates into better medical service outcomes through individual psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach From the perspective of human-AI collaboration, we utilize survey data collected from medical staff working in Chinese medical institutions to examine the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions linking organizational AI orientation and AI value co-creation outcomes. Findings Drawing on social cognitive theory, the results reveal that healthcare organizations’ AI orientation is positively related to medical staff’s AI value co-creation outcomes, and AI self-efficacy mediates this relationship. Moreover, their creative self-efficacy positively moderates the relationship between AI self-efficacy and AI value co-creation. Originality/value This study clarifies the micro-level transmission paths between organizational AI orientation and medical staff’s value co-creation outcomes. It provides new insights for hospitals to enhance medical service quality and optimize human-AI collaboration during AI-driven healthcare organizational transformation.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation: a cybernetic perspective
container-title: Kybernetes
406b79671b63af881cd115f6a281bbe0560605cc.abstract: Purpose In the AI era, digital transformation has become essential for enterprises to adapt as complex systems to uncertain business environments. In this work, we aim to analyze the evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation (EDT), focusing on its evolution and impact on enterprise performance from a system cybernetics perspective. Design/methodology/approach We employ evolutionary dynamics analysis grounded in game theory to model the EDT process, and perform an econometric and empirical analysis on a sample of Chinese A-share-listed enterprises from 2009 to 2023. The approach encompasses heterogeneity analysis, moderation effect models, such as testing enterprise environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors and market concentration, and threshold effect analyses. Findings The evolutionary dynamics analysis finds that increasing the risk-averse benefits of traditional enterprises and reducing the additional benefit coefficient would hinder EDT. Increasing the investment of technology enterprises in internal resource restructuring accelerates the transformation process. Empirically, AI significantly contributes to EDT. ESG positively moderates the relationship between AI and EDT, while market concentration exerts a negative moderating effect. Furthermore, AI and EDT show an inverted U-shaped trend when R&D intensity exceeds a specific threshold, while a U-shaped trend is observed when enterprise performance exceeds a specific threshold. Originality/value In this work, we uncover the complex, non-linear cybernetic feedback loops, such as U-shaped and inverted U-shaped, and boundary conditions, such as ESG and market concentration for AI-driven EDT, offering systemic strategies for enterprises adapting to the digital ecosystem.

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
9a1bf248111e208571dfad68b70369f36fefa354.abstract: Purpose Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index. Findings An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic constraint on the posterior mass attributable to the critical state (talert = 70.0%), the model outputs Bayesian probabilities alongside LLM-extracted textual evidence, yielding an anticipation interval of 1.33 reporting cycles relative to the documented administrative response. Originality/value The neuro-symbolic framework bridges the gap between deep learning perception and causal inference in construction management. By coupling LLM-driven zero-shot ordinal extraction with DBN causal reasoning, the research establishes an auditable framework for risk documentation. The integrated framework transitions AI from an opaque prediction model into an accountable decision-support tool, providing stakeholders with transparent explainable AI diagnostics and supporting a shift from reactive mitigation to proactive, evidence-based risk prevention.

328c2811455766f15c52fe23724799c45e0d5bbc.abstract: The article investigates the effect of irrigation on the formation and accumulation of nodule bacteria in the root system of the chickpea varieties “Yulduz” and “Milyutin-6” under meadow sierozem soil conditions in the Samarkand region. In the irrigated treatment, three irrigations were applied during the growing season at rates of 700, 1200, and 1200 m³/ha, respectively.
