title: Academic librarians' perceptions of new skills, competencies and professional development needs in the AI age
container-title: Library Hi Tech
3610c8c0f0d1c535e41c0b71849dce304d1c7a28.abstract: Purpose This study examined academic librarians' perceptions of new skills and competencies, use of AI tools and professional development needs. Design/methodology/approach An online survey was distributed via professional networks, and data were collected and analysed from 155 valid respondents across Australia, European countries and the USA. Findings The findings demonstrate that the highly ranked new skills needed by academic librarians included AI tools and output evaluation, application of data governance and management, AI literacy instruction and integration of AI into curricula. The new competencies consisted of ethical implementation and governance, critical analysis and evaluation of AI tools and AI literacy and conceptual understanding of AI. AI tools could be used to improve information service provisions through responsible and ethical information management and discovery. Key training and knowledge areas included critical evaluation of AI-generated content. Hands-on tutorials with case studies and in-person or hybrid workshops were the most suitable training formats. Practical implications The findings are helpful and practical for academic librarians to develop new skills and competencies and support professional development and curriculum renewal. Originality/value The new contribution of this study lies in the identification of important new skills and competencies that academic librarians need to utilise AI tools in a successful way, mitigate associated potential risks and adapt to changing professional roles.

title: Beyond the laggard myth: time-series analysis of AI job market dynamics in construction
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
4e1908c31127b7c180069c373440c5cd8dc5cf0e.abstract: Purpose This study presents one of the first time-series, cross-industry analyses of the artificial intelligence (AI) job market for the construction sector. It benchmarks construction against both digital and traditional industries to interrogate prevailing assumptions of linear diffusion and temporal catch-up in AI workforce adoption. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 51 months of Lightcast job postings (January 2021–March 2025), with construction defined as ANZSIC Division E, the study employs an interpretable analytical toolkit comprising Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess decomposition (period = 12), month-of-year bootstrap tests on detrended series, cross-correlation analysis with bootstrap confidence bands, Newey–West trend estimation on sectoral share ratios and conservative one-step Exponential Smoothing State-Space (ETS) forecasts. All results are re-estimated excluding the partial final month (March 2025) as a sensitivity check. Findings Construction's AI hiring is very sparse, accounting for under 1% of AI postings and is more volatile than hiring in peer sectors, but it grew fastest: annual construction postings rose more than fourfold between 2021 and 2024, against increases of 13% and 9% in the digital and traditional sectors, whose postings peaked in 2022. Construction's share of AI postings relative to both comparators therefore rises (converges) rather than falls. No delayed-follower pattern is detected: no lag at which the comparator sectors lead construction is statistically reliable, and the short-run associations that are detected are weak, near-contemporaneous and sensitive to the sample end. Unlike the comparator sectors, construction shows no statistically significant within-year seasonality and short-horizon ETS forecasts do not improve on a seasonal-naïve benchmark. These findings are robust to the exclusion of the partial final month of data. Construction thus appears as a low-base, fast-growing entrant with its own hiring dynamics, not a “laggard” following digital-sector cycles with a delay. Practical implications The findings suggest that construction firms should prioritise internal capability building and domain-specific AI skills where external hiring is thin, support flexible, year-round upskilling, and design policy and vendor strategies tailored to the sector's operational realities rather than importing digital-sector playbooks. Originality/value This study provides among the first data-driven, time-series evidence that qualifies the dominant “late adopter” narrative in construction. It shows that construction's low level of AI hiring coexists with the fastest growth and a rising share, without a delayed-follower timing pattern, distinguishing a low starting point from a lagging trajectory and offering an empirically grounded alternative to technologically deterministic accounts of cross-industry AI adoption.

title: Combined imaging of myocardial scar and fat using AI-guided dual bright- and black-blood late gadolinium enhancement
container-title: European Heart Journal - Imaging Methods and Practice
ae0982a8e8e213a8cea9fa3564d8cc1d02f304ce.abstract: Abstract Aims Characterization of myocardial scar and fat is clinically important for diagnosis, risk stratification, and procedural planning in cardiomyopathies. While black-blood late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) improves scar conspicuity, fat remains hyperintense and may confound interpretation. We aimed to develop and evaluate SPOT-DIXON, a dual bright- and black-blood LGE sequence with Dixon water-fat separation and artificial intelligence (AI)-guided analysis, enabling simultaneous and co-registered quantification of myocardial scar and intra- and extra-cardiac fat. Methods SPOT-DIXON alternates bright- and black-blood LGE preparations on consecutive heartbeats while acquiring dual-echo data for Dixon water-fat separation. Simulations, phantom experiments, and validations in a prospective cohort of 36 patients referred for cardiac MRI were performed. An AI model automatically segmented the left ventricular (LV) wall on bright-blood water images, with contours propagation to scar and fat images. Results Simulations and phantoms confirmed preserved bright- and black-blood contrast and accurate water-fat separation. In patients, AI-based LV wall segmentation showed excellent agreement with manual delineation (global DICE=84.4 ± 4.0%). SPOT-DIXON yielded higher scar volume, burden, and transmurality measurements than reference sequences, while LV wall volume was similar between sequences. Novel quantitative metrics, including intramyocardial fat burden expressed relative to scar mass, were feasible only with SPOT-DIXON. Acquisition times were comparable across sequences (5min55s ± 2min17 s), while AI-based analysis substantially reduced post-processing time to 2.1 ± 0.7 seconds. Conclusion AI-guided SPOT-DIXON enables simultaneous, co-registered assessment of myocardial scar and fat within a single LGE acquisition. This approach overcomes key limitations of current workflows and introduces novel quantitative markers of fibrofatty remodelling with potential clinical relevance in cardiomyopathies.

title: Water footprint of large AI models: risks to global water security and sustainable optimization strategies
container-title: Water Policy
71384b0b7ce71aeb82049c155da192ce552f67b9.abstract: ABSTRACT Diagram linking AI model training and inference to lifecycle water use, estimated at 4.2–6.6 billion m³ annually by 2027, and showing water reuse, efficient cooling, smarter workloads, and standardized reporting as strategies to protect global water security. The rapid proliferation of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models has introduced a significant yet underexamined environmental challenge: freshwater consumption. This narrative review synthesizes scientific literature, industry sustainability reports, and case studies to quantify the water footprint of AI systems across their full lifecycle, from semiconductor fabrication and data center operations to electricity generation and supply chains. Direct water use occurs primarily through evaporative and liquid cooling in data centers, where a single large facility can consume 11,000–19,000m3/day. Indirect water use is embedded in electricity generation and chip manufacturing, with advanced fabrication plants drawing 10,000–37,000m3/day. Major technology companies, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta, collectively consume billions of cubic meters in 2022–2024, with consumption rising alongside accelerating AI deployment. Critically, over 52% of the world's top 100 data centers are projected to be located in high water stress regions by 2030, where AI infrastructure increasingly competes with agricultural, municipal, and ecological needs. Sustainable alternatives, including immersion cooling, nonpotable water reuse, and AI-driven workload optimization, offer measurable reductions but remain inconsistently adopted. The direct and indirect water footprints of AI models during their entire lifecycle are reviewed. Two of the main direct water usage sources are semiconductor manufacturing and data center cooling. Clip manufacturing and electricity generation significantly increase the indirect water footprint of AI. In areas with scarce freshwater supplies, the growth of AI technology may worsen water stress. Standardized reporting frameworks and lifecycle-based water accounting are urgently needed to safeguard global water security.

title: University students' disciplinary perspectives on generative AI after two years of its widespread use
container-title: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
e5ed294fd6697fa9565e5119f14a79e5ae870103.abstract: Purpose This study explores how university students use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) across various disciplines, including STEM, Business, Education Futures, Clinical & Health Sciences (CHS), Creative and Allied Health & Human Performance (AHHP). It aims to identify discipline-based perspectives, perceived benefits, ethical boundaries and the support needs required for responsible use of GenAI tools. Design/methodology/approach A survey was conducted approximately two years after the widespread use of GenAI, by which time participants were expected to be familiar with its use. Students were categorised based on their discipline, English fluency, mode of learning and level of study. Their responses were analysed to compare usage patterns, satisfaction levels and ethical considerations across disciplines. Findings The results highlight that student perspectives on GenAI tools are discipline-dependent. STEM and Education Futures showed the highest acceptance, while CHS and Business students were more cautious and sceptical about accuracy and ethical issues. Non-native English speakers rated GenAI tools more favourably as aids for writing and comprehension. Novice users expressed enthusiasm, while expert users showed dissatisfaction due to errors and false information. Research limitations/implications The study relied on self-reported perceptions and represents a single institutional context. Broader investigations are recommended, with a particular focus on equity groups such as students with disabilities, low-SES students and remote learners. Practical implications Different approaches were suggested for integrating GenAI into learning. STEM students favoured comparative tasks; CHS recommended support for diagnostic reasoning; Allied Health preferred role-playing simulations; Education Futures highlighted lesson planning; and Business students suggested case-based and productivity uses. Originality/value The study provides cross-disciplinary analyses of GenAI use by students and proposes approaches for ethical and discipline-specific integration into university curricula.

title: Teacher Monitoring Strategies for AI-Aided Student Writing Outputs Toward Policy Guidelines

c2aefe7750439a7c6d21abaa77f9bc7919a3e53b.abstract: This study examined the extent to which senior high school teachers monitor AI-generated written outputs, focusing on the use of AI detectors, manual review, and cross-checking results. The study respondents were teachers from the Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) strand of Philippine Christian University-Dasmariñas. The researchers collected data through a structured questionnaire and analyzed it using descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation. Results showed that teachers used AI detectors and cross-checking to a moderate extent, while they used manual review to a high extent and found it significant. Teachers faced challenges such as limitations in AI detection tools and time constraints in manual evaluation and cross-checking. These findings highlight the importance of a layered monitoring approach, where teacher judgment remains central, and AI tools serve as supplementary aids. The study provides evidence for developing clear guidelines and practices that balance ethical assessment, professional discretion, and responsible integration of AI in student writing evaluation. title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality–Emotional Attachment–Loyalty Pathway in 2025–2026
container-title: Revista Cultura Científica
7447b8bdae9fbb1f476fe7e2a877364778cb869e.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although online-shopping participation should not be interpreted as a direct measure of AI adoption or retailer-specific investment. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). The study considers a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.

title: From Routine Fixed Schedules to Signals: A Condition-Responsive, AI-Augmented Pigging Intelligence Framework for Localised Internal Corrosion Control in Crude Oil and Water Injection Pipelines
container-title: ADIPEC
bb102d5cbb0ad65fc316c638ad53cb6149af8dab.abstract: Abstract Pigging plans in most operating companies globally are scheduled by calendar days. Pipeline segments are pigged every 30, 60 or 90 days based on the historical fixed maintenance schedules set during commissioning, regardless of the real time corrosion dynamics of the pipeline when in service. However, in most crude oil and water injection lines where the corrosion environment shifts with well stream composition, throughput and bacteria activity, the fixed schedule methodology of pigging does not prevent escalation of corrosion events. A five-year trending of several pipeline ILI data shows why 63% of anomalies deeper than 18% wall thickness were found in segments fully compliant with their pigging schedule. A 24-month study across 312 km length of pipelines compared condition-responsive segments against fixed 30-day controls showed that the mean maximum pit depth growth fell by 54.5% with over 80% drop in reactive integrity actions. Furthermore, the chemical inhibitor wetting efficiency increased by 18 points with 22.5% reduction in pigging runs. More so, 78% of the anomaly's clusters were located at the 5 to 7 o'clock orientation and concentrated in pipelines where inhibitor wetting had dropped below 69%. Sulphate Reducing Bacteria (SRB) and Iron Oxidizing Bacteria (IOB) counts proved the strongest leading indicators in the corrosion index, which is what should be expected in MIC-susceptible water injection systems. This paper proposes and validates the Pigging Intelligence Framework (PIF), in which pig runs are triggered by corrosion signals rather than fixed maintenance schedules. The PIF has three layers namely: the Corrosion Signal Index (CSI), supervised machine learning model and a root cause framework. The CSI combines flow velocity, BS&W content, microbiological activity, inhibitor residuals and ILI pit depth progression into a continuously updated risk score for each segment. Furthermore, the supervised machine learning model, trained on five years of pigging records and post-pig debris analytics from the pipelines, identifies the leading indicators of accelerated pitting. A root cause investigation tool anchored in NACE SP0106 ensures every unacceptable corrosion event produces a traceable corrective action, with outputs mapped to SAP PM and the integrity database. The study posits that pigging should be timed, based on the state of the pipeline and integrity condition of the medium rather than pigging as a historical norm. Therefore, it put forwards an A.I augmented framework in which pigging frequency, chemical dosing and inspection strategy recalibrate continuously from model output, closing the loop between detection, diagnosis and action.

title: The Skills Intelligence Engine for an AI-Ready Energy Workforce
container-title: ADIPEC
8f4721afded7a4529d81dc5465a5e908e8a7d7fd.abstract: Abstract As digitalization and AI reshape the energy industry, operators must transform large technical workforces without eroding core domain expertise. The challenge goes beyond training digital specialists; it requires evolving domain professionals into domain-plus-AI, domain-plus-digital, and domain-plus-business practitioners. This paper presents a framework of energy organization's Skills Intelligence Infrastructure, a single engine linking learning activity, curated curricula, skills maps, HR data, and a conversational AI agent (beta) that bridges HR and business to support upskilling, mobility, promotion readiness, and strategic workforce planning. The infrastructure was developed through a four-layer architecture. First, a unified data foundation integrates employee learning activity with HR data, enabling segmentation by role, organization, geography, seniority, and business area. Second, curated curricula and skills maps are designed with business owners to align with enterprise priorities across AI, machine learning, data, operations, sustainability, project management, safety-critical training, sales, and domain competence. These resources support aspirational and promotion-linked roles while clarifying expectations, gaps, and priorities. Third, persona-driven experiences serve employees and managers: employees pursue pathways, identify gaps and future requirements, and build T-shaped capability—deep domain expertise broadened by AI, digital, project, and business skills—while managers monitor development, assess the regional distribution of skills, and identify talent opportunities for mobility, promotion, and hiring. Fourth, a conversational AI agent lets employees ask which skills target roles require and which pathways to prioritize, while managers evaluate talent against skills, learning records, pathway completion, and readiness indicators. Deployed across approximately 8,000 professionals, the platform delivers curated curricula for more than 60 aspirational roles, including 12 promotion-linked roles, and hundreds of pathways across digital, AI, data, project management, safety, sales, and domain expertise. As the enterprise system of record for capability, it provides end-to-end visibility into the AI upskilling funnel: more than 3,000 employees advancing their skills, more than 1,500 certified data science practitioners, and early identification of domain data scientist candidates. It surfaces more than 150 AI-powered innovation projects across the E&P lifecycle and tracks participation in an enterprise's strategic development program. For managers, it reveals skills trends across regions, business lines, and disciplines, exposing hidden capability gaps and talent opportunities. By favoring internal development over hiring, it has reduced recruitment costs for scarce digital talent and improved satisfaction with learning and career development. Unlike commercial talent-marketplace platforms, this skills-based workforce intelligence solution is purpose-built for a large technical energy workforce. It links HR and business through manager-owned skills maps, integrates siloed domain certifications and critical pathways, and operationalizes the domain-to-domain-plus-AI transformation at scale. It supports upskilling, talent conversion, mobility, promotion readiness, compliance tracking, and build-versus-hire decisions. Future enhancements will infer skills from roles, projects, and experience and extend the AI agent into talent management. This provides a foundation on which the energy workforce can build as AI reshapes the industry.

title: From Multi-Agent Models to Enterprise Intelligent Agents: An AI-Powered Knowledge Compilation and Production Optimisation Platform for Oil and Gas Field Development
container-title: ADIPEC
e7d8f78e3172f82ea9630dc2347efccce5549eed.abstract: Abstract Oil and gas field development planning remains a slow, expert-dependent workflow, with multi-year plans scattered across subsidiaries in heterogeneous formats and tacit knowledge locked in individual experts. This paper presents an enterprise scientific research agent that compiles development plans into a unified knowledge base and enables autonomous scheme generation, simulation and continuous optimisation at enterprise scale. The architecture fuses a 240-indicator standardised ontology, multi-modal LLM knowledge compilation, a lifecycle-aware knowledge graph (facts, states, events), a RAG-augmented three-tier memory, long-horizon multi-agent orchestration (Build and Optimize modes with frozen-evidence acceptance), a unified MCP tool bus, and a git-style model relation tree that makes every run traceable and reversible. The platform has compiled 2,924 development plans across 14 subsidiaries of a national oil company. In a black-oil case, the agent autonomously generated water-flooding well-pattern schemes in two hours without human intervention, raising the ten-year recovery factor from 18.9% to 34.6% against a 30% target, while planning-cycle latency was substantially reduced. The results confirm that progressing from multi-agent research models to unified enterprise intelligent agents is a scalable path toward knowledge-driven decision-making in large, multi-asset petroleum portfolios.

title: A deep learning-based method for enhanced prediction of long-term diaphragm wall deflections using multi-source data
container-title: AI in Civil Engineering
04ff52c9850c5be57a455789b03eadf78fd2ea9f.abstract: Abstract Machine learning-based autoregressive models are widely applied to deformation prediction of braced excavations, yet they often suffer from pronounced error accumulation and deteriorated accuracy in long-term forecasting. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multi-source information fusion framework for predicting diaphragm wall deformation that integrates construction information with historical wall-deflection data. By incorporating construction-related dynamic features as auxiliary inputs, the proposed model effectively strengthens long-term dependency learning and reduces the propagation of autoregressive errors. A depth-weighted loss coefficient is further introduced to prioritize accuracy in shallow regions where deformation is most critical, and a 1D U-Net decoder is employed to enhance profile-level reconstruction through multi-scale spatial feature extraction. The framework is validated using two deep excavation projects on Nanjing Metro Line 11. For excavation-induced deformation, the model demonstrates stable and accurate multi-step prediction performance for diaphragm wall deflection, even under long forecasting steps. Comparative analyses further confirm that the proposed fusion architecture provides superior long-term robustness under limited monitoring data. The results highlight the method’s potential as a practical tool for deformation forecasting and construction risk management in foundation pit engineering.

title: AI-Agent-Built Fiber-Sensing Interpretation Platform for Real Well Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
ccebed683e4632e963d6055547994a210645342a.abstract: Abstract Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and distributed temperature sensing (DTS) are fiber-optic technologies that turn an optical fiber into a distributed sensor array. Originally developed in the telecommunications and defense sectors, these methods were adopted by the oil and gas industry. DTS entered thermal-recovery surveillance in the mid-1990s (Brown and Hartog 2002), and DAS followed more widely after the first downhole trials in 2009 (Molenaar et al. 2012). They now expand the observational basis for well logging by providing distributed temperature and acoustic measurements over the instrumented interval at survey-specific spatial and temporal sampling. However, interpretation-tool development has lagged acquisition technology: multiple vendor formats, multiday survey volumes, and job-specific processing still leave much of the acquired data underused relative to acquisition cost. An engineer-directed development approach was evaluated in which a domain engineer used general-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents to construct a DAS/DTS and well-log interpretation software environment. Development was performed against field-surveillance data sets from multiple vendors and job types. As application scope increased, unstructured agent use was replaced by a documentation-driven operating framework comprising architecture rules, task-scoped guidance, decision ownership, plan-before-implementation, and automated numerical and regression checks. The implemented environment provided multiformat data access, stream-from-disk review of multiday surveys, synchronized visualization, deterministic processing, and restorable sessions. A first usable environment was completed within weeks and subsequently used to implement and evaluate two interpretation workflows across multiple surveys. For injection surveillance, channel-coherence processing, masked ridge extraction, and engineering quality control converted recurring low-frequency DAS responses into a common-frame thermal-slug trajectory library. For gas lift surveillance, operating-state DTS traces were combined with a dimensionless dual-band DAS coincidence field and reviewed with completion geometry, surface measurements, and event history. The workflows derive interpretive confidence from recurrence across events and concurrence across measurements, respectively. The results establish the feasibility of locating governed software implementation near domain expertise. Individual engineers and small technical teams can thereby retain tested methods within a shared technical foundation, shortening the cycle from field observation to reproducible operational workflow from many months to a few days.

title: Reinventing the Upstream Control Room: An Agentic AI Approach to Early Deviation Detection and Remediation
container-title: ADIPEC
814f64384a16578a8104462a5d301e3b7903e939.abstract: Abstract The upstream control room is where production, injection, chemical, and emissions performance are monitored against target, and where operational deviations must be detected and resolved before they compound into lost output, avoidable emissions, or safety exposure. In practice, this task is hindered by four recurring gaps observed across production operations: no automated system alerts operators to an emerging shortfall before it has already grown; shortfalls are not always reconciled consistently across the control room, well- performance, and subsurface teams; compensation to recover a shortfall is often arranged ad hoc through informal communication, bypassing structured, formal validation and slowing recovery; and diagnosing the cause of a shortfall still depends on individual operator experience and a manual search through troubleshooting documentation. Left unaddressed, these gaps translate directly into slower recovery, inconsistent decisions across shifts, and lost production, chemical, and energy value. This paper presents the design, implementation, and early learnings of a Next-Generation Central Control Room (NextGen CCR), an artificial-intelligence-native decision-support layer deployed in an offshore upstream pilot to enable early operational-drift detection and structured remediation while preserving human decision authority. The solution combines near-real-time operational data, optimized operating envelopes, planned-activity context, and several thousand pages of procedural knowledge within a layered architecture that integrates deterministic analytics, large language models, and an operational knowledge graph. Deviations are detected against targets and envelopes, contextualized against planned activities and equipment status, and investigated by orchestrated, domain-specific agents that produce ranked, evidence-backed diagnoses and prioritized, standards-compliant recommendations. A scoped conversational assistant offers deeper guidance grounded in operating philosophies and equipment manuals, and human validation is embedded throughout the workflow. Early pilot results show improved end-of-day production prediction and faster, evidence-based investigation of critical alarms, with change management recognized as central to sustained adoption.

title: Edge AI-Enabled Autonomous Well Testing with Hybrid Virtual Flow Metering for Production Surveillance
container-title: ADIPEC
45303c509f31289d89fc7070f5b221238703c72a.abstract: Abstract Production surveillance is fundamental to sustaining reservoir performance, optimizing production, and enabling informed operational decision-making across large upstream assets. Conventional well-testing programs, however, remain highly dependent on manual initiation, operator experience, continuous monitoring, and post-test validation, resulting in inconsistent data quality, low test-success rates, and inefficient use of scarce testing infrastructure such as multiphase flow meters and test separators. This paper presents the development and phased field deployment of an Edge Artificial-Intelligence (AI) enabled Autonomous Well Testing framework integrated with Hybrid Virtual Flow Metering (VFM) for production surveillance in one of the world's largest onshore oil-producing assets. The solution combines machine learning, real-time edge analytics, operational-technology (OT) integration, and automated decision support to improve well-test execution, quality assurance, and production-data reliability while progressively reducing manual intervention. The framework continuously evaluates well readiness, operating stability, and test-quality conditions using both real-time and historical production data. It supports assisted, semi-autonomous, and fully autonomous testing modes, and dynamically determines whether a test should continue, be extended, be shortened, or be aborted. Automated failure diagnostics, keyed to pre-agreed rejection criteria, provide the operator with the probable cause of failure and a recommended corrective action, improving transparency and accelerating decision-making. In parallel, a hybrid virtual flow metering model estimates well production from routinely available surface measurements and is automatically recalibrated whenever a validated physical test becomes available, targeting an accuracy within 5% of the reference multiphase meter. A proof-of-concept was implemented on a representative well-gathering platform and subsequently scaled. Field results demonstrated a 50% reduction in failed well tests, an approximately threefold increase in testing throughput, test-duration reductions to under 24 hours for stable wells, and approximately 200 operational hours saved per month through early termination of non-productive tests. AI prediction accuracy approached 85% against reference measurements, and the hybrid VFM enabled a 10–15% reduction in physical testing frequency while maintaining surveillance coverage. The results demonstrate that autonomous well testing is technically feasible, operationally beneficial, and scalable across large upstream assets. The paper details the architecture, AI methodology, stability-assessment logic, VFM calibration approach, OT-cybersecurity considerations, quantified results, and a roadmap toward closed-loop autonomous field operations.

title: Active Learning-Assisted Human-In-The-Loop Framework for Rapid Borehole Image Annotation: Enabling AI-Powered Geological Interpretation at Scale
container-title: ADIPEC
a2d9600cc9e2691000ceac0374ce127fe222b9f4.abstract: Abstract Borehole image interpretation is a cornerstone of subsurface characterization in the oil and gas industry, providing high-resolution, azimuthally oriented data for in-situ stress estimation, wellbore stability assessment, and reservoir quality evaluation. Despite its geological significance, this process remains largely manual: expert geologists must individually review and annotate high-resolution image logs that can span thousands of feet per well, investing hundreds of hours per project before any automated prediction is available. This paper presents an integrated Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) active learning framework designed to overcome this annotation bottleneck. The system supports detection of geological features, particularly formation dips, from acoustic and resistivity image logs. It operates through three concurrent modules: (1) an interactive annotation interface overlaying model predictions on borehole images for expert review and correction; (2) an asynchronous background training engine leveraging the DINOv3 visual foundation model for deep feature extraction and continuous refinement of a lightweight convolutional segmentation head; and (3) an active learning selection module employing entropy-based uncertainty sampling that identifies and prioritizes the most informative depth intervals. Experimental results show that uncertainty sampling provides a measurable early-round advantage. Between 20 and 160 annotated images in the reference-well experiment, uncertainty sampling increases mean IoU by 1.74% and mean Dice/F1 by 1.44% relative to sequential depth-order selection. It also reaches a predefined early-convergence criterion of a mean angular error below 10° for two consecutive rounds, with a decrease in the confirming round, using 50 annotated images compared with 60 for sequential selection (16.7% fewer annotations). Validation across four wells, including the reference well, shows that uncertainty sampling reduces the annotation volume required to reach 95% of final IoU by 24.3% on average, with well-specific reductions ranging from 0% to 62.5%. In the architecture comparison, DINOv3 Projected Layers 3&6 outperforms DINOv3 Full Features across all three metrics, achieving 4.84° ± 0.25° angular error, 0.4409 ± 0.0071 IoU, and 0.6084 ± 0.0075 Dice/F1 with approximately 48,000 trainable parameters.

title: Closing the Verification Gap: AI-Assisted Assessment of F&G Barrier Effectiveness in Ageing LNG Facilities
container-title: ADIPEC
2f880d460c9e6f6c6435a2593da327a7b2f160d5.abstract: Abstract Fire and gas (F&G) detection systems are credited as an independent protection layer in the safety cases of liquefied natural gas (LNG) and gas-processing facilities, yet the evidence supporting that credit is, in most operating plants, a coverage assessment performed once at design time and never re-verified. UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) release data for offshore installations (2001–2008) show that fixed gas detection failed to detect 36% of major and 69% of significant hydrocarbon releases (McGillivray and Hare 2008); ISA-TR84.00.07 cites an effective detection rate of about 60% from the same data. This paper names that discrepancy the verification gap: the difference between the coverage a facility holds on paper and what its layout delivers under real, time-varying conditions. The paper presents full physics sweep mapping — an AI-assisted methodology that quantifies this gap using documents the facility already possesses. Deterministic document extraction converts safety registers and C&E matrices into a structured facility model; spatial reconstruction places units, graded areas, and detectors where documents carry no coordinates; a physics pipeline sweeps gas-dispersion scenarios across the site wind rose, surrogate-accelerated with every output reproducible by the underlying solver. Coverage is scored per scenario against ISA-TR84.00.07-aligned voting criteria, and the result is expressed as a graded barrier register — credited, at risk, or lost — in which each verdict traces to its documentary and physical evidence. The methodology is demonstrated on an anonymised Middle East gas-processing facility with more than twenty years in service. From two source documents, the pipeline extracted 15 detectors, 28 release scenarios, and 13 equipment items, reconstructed the facility model, and resolved dispersion behaviour across eight wind directions in seconds on a single CPU. Against a hypothetical wind-blind posture crediting all five documented safety-instrumented scenarios — the implicit position of a facility with no current study — the wind-resolved assessment sustained credit for one in five, found three of eight wind directions effectively blind, and separated risk-weighted (~88%) from geographic (~60%) coverage. The methodology additionally yields per-barrier minimum detectable leak size, a probability-of-detection field, per-scenario time-to-detect, a sensor-count marginal-value curve (plateau at 29 of 30 modelled heads), and inverse-mode source localisation. The paper argues that barrier verification should be a recurring property of an operating facility rather than a frozen design artefact — the acute case being congested, long-lived LNG liquefaction trains — and quantifies, for one real facility, how far the paper position and the physics position can diverge.

title: AI-Assisted Automated Compositional PVT Modeling: Model Construction, EOS Tuning, and Validation Using Laboratory and Field Data
container-title: ADIPEC
5113a9d39da266ddb16242f58784dad92ac0f754.abstract: Abstract Accurate PVT models are essential for predicting the phase behavior of reservoir fluids in digital twins, reservoir simulation models, and integrated asset models. Conventional tuning is usually based on manual adjustment or mathematical regression of equation-of-state (EOS) parameters against laboratory experiments performed near reservoir temperature. Although manual adjustment can reproduce experimental curves with high accuracy, the resulting model may still show significant deviations under actual field operating conditions or for other tests from the same formation. Mathematical regression can also provide acceptable numerical accuracy, but it often produces physically inconsistent trends in PVT-model parameters with molecular weight. This study presents an automatic tuning algorithm for gas-condensate PVT models that combines a step-by-step tuning approach with optimization objective functions and uses both laboratory measurements and field data. Field low-temperature separation data are included because they represent operating conditions that differ substantially from standard PVT experiments and therefore provide an important test of model reliability. The workflow also incorporates AI-assisted data preparation, using large language models to extract and structure component compositions, PVT experiments, and separation data from laboratory reports. The extraction workflow was validated on 6 laboratory reports. The average field-level extraction accuracy was 90 %, while the time required for preparing one PVT dataset was reduced from approximately 5-8 hours of manual entry to 10 minutes of engineering review and correction. The AI layer therefore reduces routine data-entry effort while retaining engineering control before EOS initialization and tuning. The algorithm is based on a staged constrained optimization approach combining physically guided parameter tuning, best-state selection with guard constraints, and local numerical refinement. It tunes the main thermodynamic parameters controlling phase behavior, including the critical properties of heavy fractions, binary interaction coefficients (BICs), acentric factors, and shift parameters. The procedure aims to reproduce laboratory PVT data and field predictions of separator-fluid density and condensate-gas factor under production conditions. The approach can be applied to individual reservoir-fluid systems or to several systems simultaneously. Global tuning produces a consistent set of model parameters and prevents improvement for one fluid composition from causing unacceptable errors for others. The model was tested using fluid data from a Russian gas-condensate field and demonstrated good agreement with laboratory and field measurements. The practical relevance of the study lies in automated PVT-model tuning for real gas-condensate reservoir fluids and in extending model validation beyond laboratory experiments. In this study, the algorithm was tested using six fluid compositions from different Russian fields. The tuned models can be used for separator calculations, production forecasting, field-development studies, monitoring, and integration into digital field-management and production-simulation systems.

title: Optimizing Reservoir Monitoring Plans with AI and Material Balance in Middle East Carbonate Reservoirs
container-title: ADIPEC
8f9f7dc4b7a495a507729dc1619e80f6a0a4f5ae.abstract: Abstract An integrated artificial-intelligence (AI) and material-balance (MB) workflow is extended from a reservoir-pressure-prediction algorithm into a closed-loop reservoir-monitoring decision system and validated through operational deployment in Middle East carbonate reservoirs. Building on the hybrid AI + MB pressure-prediction workflow of SPE-221813, this study adds three elements that convert prediction into decision: (i) reliability-validated uncertainty quantification producing calibrated P10/P50/P90 pressure maps; (ii) a formal, confidence-weighted value-of-information (VOI) survey-prioritization algorithm with budget-constrained selection; and (iii) the first field-deployed, operationally adopted Reservoir Monitoring Plan (RMP) optimization, with cross-reservoir validation across contrasting drive mechanisms. The workflow couples XGBoost/Random-Forest regression to a material balance with a Fetkovich aquifer, restricting ML to physically anchored residual learning. On Reservoir A, a mature waterflooded carbonate (21 wells), the model predicts reservoir pressure with a held-out test-fold RMSE of ≈50 psi (13 test events; 95% CI ≈36–81 psi) against measured surveys, with P10–P90 bands calibrated to an observed 80% coverage on 100 forecast–realization pairs (95% CI ≈71–87%). Applied to the 2026 planning cycle, the AI + MB RMP reduced planned pressure surveys by 15% versus the engineer-driven baseline while preserving ≈88% of aggregated VOI, and was adopted operationally. Transfer to Reservoir B, a depletion-drive carbonate (8 producers) with cross-reservoir injection support, required only bounded, calibratable adaptations, indicating that the workflow is transferable across contrasting carbonate reservoir-management regimes; quantitative validation on Reservoir B is preliminary and remains in progress. The framework is browser-deployed with monthly refresh and engineer-in-the-loop governance, providing a scalable path to VOI-optimized surveillance across carbonate portfolios.

title: Physics-Governed Agentic AI for Production Diagnostics: A Transferable Process Validated Across Operational Domains
container-title: ADIPEC
df761479d0502b1063a0d9545bed1176612a34a8.abstract: Abstract Production surveillance at fleet scale runs into two constraints. No operations team can review thousands of wells at diagnostic depth every week, and the data for an optimal decision often lives across several source systems. This paper describes a production AI surveillance system built to address these constraints. The system analyzes approximately 6,100 wells each week across four artificial lift types in five operated basins and delivers a prioritized set of recommendations to each engineer. Three concurrent development cycles convert expert diagnostic reasoning into versioned rules, fragmented source data into governed contracts, and engineer corrections that update both the reasoning and the data contracts. The system applies deterministic physics and economic calculations before any AI reasoning. Nodal analysis, production decline evaluation, and lift-specific diagnostics are computed programmatically for the fleet, refreshed on a schedule, and injected into each analysis as governed data. Specialist LLM analyses reason over the evidence without seeing the deterministic conclusions, a synthesis reconciles the two views, and deterministic gates hold correction authority over the output. Engineers individually reviewed more than 950 insights in the first five months. Agreement between engineers and the model exceeded 70 percent across more than 900 reviews that carried a documented reason and a determinable outcome, and it held as the depth of written critiques grew. One in five actioned insights converted to directly confirmed same-well field work within seven days. Twenty-four confirmed-diagnosis wells showed more than 750 BOE/d of combined decline-adjusted improvement. Engineers validate prepared recommendations rather than investigate from scratch. The process was implemented four times, once for each lift method, each build faster and with increased scope over the last, with each lift incorporating its own physics, rules, and source bindings. What carried the system to fleet scale was the rigor of the process, and what kept it there was the engagement of the engineers who review its output each week. The paper presents the development process, the runtime governance, and the attribution standard behind these results.

title: Edge AI Vision Camera Intelligence and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) for Real-Time Industrial Safety Monitoring in Oil & Gas Facilities
container-title: ADIPEC
630a0ebf0bea077cef165c6fb1574bb2581950d2.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Oil & gas operations require continuous monitoring of safety compliance and high risk anomalies; however, conventional supervision and manual CCTV monitoring are constrained by limited coverage, delayed detection, and inconsistent enforcement. This paper presents an AI-based industrial safety monitoring framework for edge computer vision analytics and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to enable real-time detection of safety violations and hazardous conditions. Methods, Procedures, Process The proposed solution integrates deep learning-based video analytics with existing CCTV infrastructure and AMR-mounted cameras to extend monitoring into blind spots and dynamic work zones. AI inference is performed on edge GPU servers to ensure low latency, reduce cloud dependency, and support uninterrupted site operations. The platform detects over 100 industrial safety anomaly types, including PPE non-compliance, restricted zone intrusion, work-at-height violations, fire/smoke indicators, spill/leak anomalies, housekeeping deviations. Temporal tracking and Multi-frame validation is applied to improve event confidence and reduce transient false triggers. Rule-based escalation workflows generate real-time alerts with timestamped evidence frames, which are stored in an auditable event database for compliance reporting, trend analytics, and continuous improvement. Results, Observations, Conclusions Performance evaluation across operational deployments indicates a detection accuracy of 90-95% depending on use case complexity and environmental conditions. End-to-end alert latency from detection to notification was measured at approximately 3 seconds, enabling near real-time intervention by EHS teams. The combined CCTV + AMR monitoring approach improved coverage in areas where fixed cameras had occlusion limitations, particularly in large fabrication yards, laydown zones, and high-traffic operational corridors. Observed deployment constraints included low-light sensitivity, PPE partial visibility and false triggers caused by reflections and steam. These were mitigated through site-specific confidence threshold tuning, improved zoning logic, and periodic model refinement using operational datasets. The system also enabled automated reporting outputs such as violation heatmaps, repeat violation identification, shift-wise compliance scoring, and incident categorization. The paper concludes that integrating edge AI vision with existing CCTV infrastructure and AMR-based mobile sensing provides a scalable and measurable approach to proactive industrial safety monitoring, improving response time, compliance governance, and data-driven EHS decision-making. Novel/Additive Information This paper presents additive field evidence on deploying a low-latency (~3 seconds) edge AI vision system integrated with existing CCTV networks and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to monitor 100+ industrial safety anomalies. It contributes practical deployment methodology, performance benchmarking (90-95% accuracy), and mitigation strategies for real operating constraints such as occlusion, low-light, reflections, and steam. The work advances scalable, audit-ready AI safety intelligence for petroleum operations.

title: Recent Advances in Semi-Automated Stratigraphic Framework Building and Ai-Assisted Reservoir Evaluation of the Habshan Formation, Southeast Abu Dhabi, U.A.E.
container-title: ADIPEC
7f1b2711cd45225ac922ccf3b94a6e9d4f95febf.abstract: Abstract An ongoing exploration campaign in southeast Abu Dhabi (UAE) uses a model-driven stratigraphy workflow on high quality seismic data to enhance the interpretation of the stratigraphic framework of the Lower Cretaceous Habshan carbonate succession. AI assisted seismic interpretation, integrated with newly acquired well, core, and petrophysical data, is then used to refine reservoir evaluation and update the regional geological model and associated play concepts. A semi-automated seismic interpretation workflow was applied to a high-quality PSDM seismic volume to extract depositional surfaces and build a 3D chronostratigraphic framework. As part of the stratigraphy analysis, AI-based geobody extraction was applied on stratal slices and seismic attributes to delineate shoal or reworked bodies and clinoform geometries. Interpreted horizons were converted to a chronostratigraphic domain to quantify stacking patterns, interpret platform evolution, and predict reservoir/seal distribution. Newly drilled wells provided geological and petrophysical control to calibrate stratal slices and constrain facies interpretation. Updated well correlations, depositional profiles, and gross depositional environment (GDE) maps were generated to validate the revised model and guide future exploration. Model-driven, semi-automated seismic interpretation shows an evolution from dominantly aggradational stacking, represented by subparallel reflectors interpreted as vertical platform growth during relative sea-level rise, to northeastward progradation, represented by dipping clinoforms formed by lateral accretion during reduced accommodation and sustained sediment supply. A regionally continuous, low-angle high-amplitude reflector is interpreted as a key late highstand surface associated with onset of relative sea-level fall; it may represent exposure and a diagenetically altered boundary that generates a strong impedance contrast and may include karstified or reworked reservoir intervals that remain unproven. Overlying packages show aggradational–progradational parasequences culminating in oolitic shoal facies, which form the main reservoir fairway and exhibit hydrocarbon indications in all wells. Additional porosity and hydrocarbon evidence occur at other Habshan levels within transgressive, early highstand, and lowstand deposits. Reservoir distribution is controlled by depositional architecture and diagenesis, while trapping is largely stratigraphic with limited structural influence. These results refine play risking and highlight the need for stratigraphic model updates to target diverse, subtle reservoirs in this complex carbonate succession. This study delivers a refined, chronostratigraphically constrained framework for the Habshan in SE Abu Dhabi through semi-automated seismic stratigraphy, highlighting overlooked stratigraphic and diagenetic play elements and revising reservoir fairway distribution. It also demonstrates the added value of AI-based geobody extraction integrated with stratal attributes and new well control to reduce uncertainty and unlock subtle carbonate plays in a mature basin.

title: Engineering Bolting Remanufacturing Using Automated AI-Based Inspection for Sustainable Asset Integrity
container-title: ADIPEC
53bf2d2d5cec4edce19b2da79f5895fc4d4e5a7d.abstract: Abstract The proposed methodology is based on the principle that used bolting can be safely reused when compliance with material integrity and dimensional standards is verified. Inspection criteria are aligned with ASTM F788 for detection of surface discontinuities and ASME B1.1 for thread profile acceptance. An automated inspection system, InsX-B 2.0, was developed to enable high-throughput and repeatable assessment of used bolting. The system integrated various techniques including machine vision and AI-based defect detection for identifying surface cracks, dimensional deviation, and marking inconsistencies. High-resolution imaging in combination with low-distortion optical systems and laser distance sensors were used to capture precise thread geometry and dimensional conformity. Inspection results were processed through a standardized acceptance framework, enabling objective classification of reusable versus reject components. The system was designed for industrial-scale operation, ensuring consistency, traceability, and reduced dependency on human-based inspection. Field application of the system demonstrated its capability to inspect stud bolts up to 3 inches in diameter and 36 inches in length. The evaluation results obtained from used bolting representatives (2,095 samples) indicated that approximately 45% of the used bolting samples met applicable standards and were suitable for safe reuse. This outcome translates to up to 45% reduction in replacement cost compared to procurement of new bolts. Based on an annual servicing volume of approximately 20,000 units, the approach yielded an estimated reduction of 23.1 tons (CO2) per year, reflecting approximately 75% lower emissions compared to new manufacturing. The implementation confirmed that automated inspection enables reliable, repeatable, and efficient remanufacturing of mechanical fasteners, supporting both operational efficiency and sustainability objectives. This work introduces a scalable, AI-enabled inspection framework specifically designed for reuse qualification of industrial bolting. The integration of automated defect detection, dimensional verification, and standards-based acceptance criteria provides a consistent and auditable alternative to conventional manual inspection practices. The approach establishes a practical pathway for circular material utilization in oil and gas operations, bridging asset integrity requirements with sustainability goals. The developed system has been protected through multiple-filed intellectual property applications and offers potential for broader implementation across asset-intensive industries.

title: Scaling AI-Enabled Drilling Optimization Solution for Drilling Activity in the United Arab Emirates: Advisory Workflow Field Validation Toward Closed-Loop Drilling Automation
container-title: ADIPEC
fc80fa8eaea2f4d69e88498d4633ed283cf44d94.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the field validation of a machine learning (ML)-enabled rate of penetration (ROP) optimization solution deployed in advisory mode across five onshore wells in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (UAE). The solution was developed through a collaboration between the operator, an in-country AI technology partner, an international energy services company, and a drilling analytics provider. The paper shows how real-time recommendations generated by an ML engine were translated into live operations to improve on-bottom drilling performance and accelerate digital adoption, and it evaluates the transfer of the methodology to Middle East drilling operations using operator-specific models, an advisory execution workflow, and an in-country cloud deployment that satisfies data residency requirements, establishing a scalable pathway toward drilling automation. Predictive ROP models for positive displacement motor and rotary steerable assemblies were trained on high- and low-frequency drilling data from 70 offset wells and qualified in a proof of concept against an acceptance criterion of median absolute percentage error below 15%; blind testing returned 6.5% offline and 3.8% online, confirming readiness for deployment. Following shadow-mode validation on live data streamed into an in-country cloud environment, five wells comprising 16 hole sections were drilled in advisory mode on two rigs. The campaign met all pilot success criteria, delivering more than 142 hours of on-bottom drilling time savings, a 23% reduction in on-bottom drilling time across the 13 of 16 sections that met or exceeded the top-quartile (P75) offset benchmark. Higher adherence to recommended setpoints was generally associated with higher section-level ROP improvement, proving the advisory concept under live operating conditions, while trajectory control and downhole vibrations constrained the achievable gains in build-dominated and dense intervals. These results validate advisory-mode deployment as a structured qualification stage toward closed-loop drilling automation in UAE onshore operations.

title: Virtual H2S Sensing and Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Enable Sustained Autonomous Control of Refinery Acid Gas Removal
container-title: ADIPEC
61e20a8c974f17e41caaa76d5d84642c691cf06b.abstract: Abstract Amine-based acid gas removal is an energy-intensive operation, and in many refineries, it is run with a deliberate safety margin because the one measurement needed to optimize it — the treated-gas hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) concentration — is often not reliably available online. This paper describes how we deployed reinforcement-learning (RL) autonomous control on an Off-Gas methyl-diethanolamine (MDEA) acid gas removal unit that had no dependable online H₂S analyzer, and kept it running in closed loop for months rather than days. Two elements made this possible. The first is a virtual H₂S sensor, checked against laboratory samples, that turns the intermittent lab result into a continuous quality signal the controller can act on. The second is a hybrid training method that combines about two years of plant history with a dynamic process simulator, so the controller also learns how to behave in conditions the historical data never contained. Three controllers — one on the absorber and one on each of the two regenerator trains — were switched to autonomous operation in January 2026 and held their manipulated variables without operator input under normal conditions. On the absorber, lean amine circulation dropped by roughly 23% (about 10 m³/h) while treated-gas H₂S stayed inside specification; on the regenerators, reboiler steam fell by 4.7% (about 1,656 kg/h). Together these gains are worth on the order of roughly 180 to 200 kUSD a year with an average feed flow of 19 to 21 KNm3/hr. The wider point is that the two problems most often blamed for keeping autonomous control in the pilot stage — a missing analyzer, and training data that does not cover the full operating range — are both solvable.

title: Knowledge Organization Matters: How Graph Design and Temporal Structure Shape Agentic AI Performance on Drilling Activity Reports
container-title: ADIPEC
7753ce5507f72bb75a481fb1d0f6dc135a833ca7.abstract: Abstract Agentic AI over drilling reports can automate analytics that today take hours per question, from non-productive-time trending to offset-well lookup. Published systems typically commit to a single graph design without testing it: most studies in literature perform multi-method comparisons and evaluate whole pipelines and do not evaluate individual design decisions. We compare five ways of organizing a corpus for an agent (a vectorless reasoning tree, an open-vocabulary graph, that graph with community post-processing, a domain-schema graph, and a fine-grained quantitative graph) against a shared flat-vector baseline, on two public corpora: 1,681 Daily Drilling Reports from Equinor's Volve field (North Sea, 1992–2016) and 1,888 Weekly Activity Reports from Shell Offshore operations in the Gulf of Mexico (BSEE eWell archive, 2022–2024). We benchmark a ReAct agent that runs the full matrix at four capability tiers: two successive frontier versions, a fast-tier cloud model, and an open-weights 26B model on a 16 GB consumer GPU. Under frontier agents the vectorless tree leads relevance on both corpora, while hybrid retrieval leads completeness against machine-verified answer keys, with the domain-schema hybrid the strongest graph configuration. A blinded pair-preserved scoring of all 1,080 frontier cells confirms the BSEE architecture effects: hybrid retrieval beats vector-only (+0.040, Holm-corrected p=0.0004), the schema step over the open-vocabulary control is the largest effect measured (+0.068), and community post-processing alone does not contribute anything. The architecture ranking reproduces at every capability tier, and the spread widens as the agent weakens. A bi-temporal fact table with a point-in-time query tool raises as-of accuracy to 1.00 on both corpora, correcting all nine static errors with no regressions (96 paired queries, exact McNemar p=0.004). A schema audit shows the cost of a hand-designed ontology: named storms present in 30 reports were invisible to schema-graph retrieval, producing confident false negatives that open-vocabulary and vector retrieval avoided.

title: Operationalising Generative AI in Subsurface Operations: A Low-Code Well Passport Skill Built by the End User
container-title: ADIPEC
aab9948c7028a0fb292a71ed9113a2556d304a22.abstract: Abstract Subsurface teams in mature, high-well-count fields routinely spend 30 to 60 minutes per well gathering data before any technical evaluation can start. Across an inventory of more than 2,000 wells, that custodial work pulls scarce petrophysical and engineering time away from interpretation and decision-making. This paper describes the deployment and early field validation of a suite of AI-driven workflow automations on a mature onshore carbonate field. A domain petrophysicist authored them, not a central digital team, and they run on an enterprise generative-AI platform that the organisation had already deployed. The automations are grouped into five operational domains: (1) well intelligence, covering automated retrieval of formation tops, casing configuration, H₂S and CO₂ classification, saturation history and pressure records, together with on-request assembly of well documents; (2) cement integrity, covering automated bond-log interpretation across all casing strings with isolation-risk flagging; (3) petrophysical quick-look, covering real-time logging-while-drilling (LWD) processing from any service provider on the asset, with composite-log and interpretation-software-ready output; (4) logging-program generation for saturation and production programs, annotated with live-condition safety information; and (5) intervention reporting, which consolidates multi-contractor performance into a single management view. In field use, well-data retrieval time fell by more than 90 percent. Logging-program preparation dropped from one to three hours per well to under five minutes. Real-time petrophysical evaluation is now produced automatically at each drilling cycle to support landing decisions. Every output follows the corporate documentation standard, which removes the variation between engineers, and every value can be traced back to the source file it came from. The framework recovers an estimated four or more engineering hours per well event, needs no new infrastructure or software licences, and works with any logging service provider active on the field. It offers a practical and immediately replicable route to AI adoption for operations-intensive subsurface teams.

title: Clean Firm Power for the AI Age: Geothermal Pathways to Data Center Decarbonization Across the Energy Trilemma
container-title: ADIPEC
cc6d8e58073e31067a91b019c40b86fd18b9b127.abstract: Abstract The evolving development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence (‘AI’) is driving unprecedented 24/7 data center energy demand. A single generative AI query consumes roughly ten times the electricity of a conventional internet search, and one planned US data center has requested 1.4 GW of continuous power. This will exceed the total demand of some small states. These loads reframe the energy trilemma, highlighting the need to simultaneously deliver reliability, low carbon impact, and cost-effective energy, and expose the limitations of intermittent renewables for mission-critical digital infrastructure. Geothermal energy, with capacity factors exceeding 70–90% and very low lifecycle emissions, offers a reliable "clean firm" power and thermal management solutions. This study examines how the United States, UAE, and Saudi Arabia deploy geothermal solutions to decarbonize data centers while advancing all three trilemma pillars. The methodology adopts a three-case comparative analysis. In the United States, we assess Utah's Operation Gigawatt, aiming to double capacity from ∼4 GW, and Ormat Technologies’ long-term Power Purchase Agreements (‘PPAs’), including contracts supplying up to 150 MW of geothermal electricity to hyperscale operators. In the UAE, we evaluated ADNOC's G2COOL geothermal district cooling pilot at Masdar City, using ∼90°C water from ∼2.6 km depth to provide ∼10% of cooling demand with ∼50% lower electricity consumption. In Saudi Arabia, we analyzed KAPSARC resource mapping (Alsuwailem et. al, 2024) and KAUST's 2024 pilot at Thuwal targeting geothermal cooling applications. Each case is systematically assessed against trilemma metrics of reliability, carbon impact, and cost-effectiveness. This study evaluates geothermal applications for power generation and thermal management across three stages of market maturity. The United States case demonstrates reliability through baseload geothermal electricity for hyperscale computing; the UAE delivers carbon impact reduction through operational district cooling in extreme climates; and Saudi Arabia explores cost-effectiveness through early-stage geothermal-exchange systems optimizing cooling-intensive demand. The assessment identifies distinct contributions to reliability, carbon impact, and cost-effectiveness. For reliability, geothermal provides continuous baseload power and long-term PPAs that reduce supply volatility. For carbon impact, geothermal systems emit approximately 90% lower lifecycle CO2 than combined-cycle gas (≈40 against ≈500 gCO2e/kWh) and up to ∼99% lower operational CO2 against the same baseline while materially reducing cooling-related emissions in high-demand regions (IPCC 2011). For cost-effectiveness, for the right application, geothermal cooling and geo-exchange solutions can reduce electricity consumption by up to ∼50%, particularly in markets where cooling accounts for 65–70% of power demand. Across all three jurisdictions, geothermal solutions reconcile accelerating AI-driven electricity demand with system resilience, decarbonization objectives, and cost optimization. By positioning geothermal within the energy trilemma framework, this study demonstrates its strategic role in supporting sustainable large scale digital infrastructure.

title: Interdisciplinary Agentic AI Deployment: A Success Story from the Malay Basin, Malaysia
container-title: ADIPEC
b47c293a97591dffd00ec3af985e81ae3731d271.abstract: Subsurface professionals working in the oil and gas exploration and production industry are routinely exposed to a wide and diverse array of specialized software packages, digital tools, and sophisticated applications. These have been developed by various international technology companies, service organizations, and independent software vendors from around the world to help geoscientists, engineers, and technical analysts conduct their complex geological studies, detailed reservoir interpretations, and comprehensive data analysis tasks with greater efficiency and accuracy. The selection of one particular software solution over another competing alternative in the marketplace is primarily driven by several key factors. These include the software's comprehensive technical capabilities, its specific functional features, and perhaps most importantly, the individual user's personal proficiency, accumulated hands-on experience, and overall comfort level with the tool developed over months or years of regular use. When the technical capabilities and available features appear to be roughly equivalent or comparable between different software options, professionals naturally and instinctively gravitate toward the software platform with which they are most familiar and have the greatest operational experience using in their daily work activities. This well-established and understandable preference for familiar and well-understood tools, however, inevitably introduces significant operational friction across different workflows. This is particularly problematic when technical teams need to transition between various disconnected tools from different software vendors, which frequently results in operational delays, increased inefficiencies, potential data loss or corruption, and considerable frustration among team members who must constantly adapt to new interfaces and workflows.

title: Real-Time AI-Based Prediction of Stuck Pipe Events to Minimize Non-Productive Time in Drilling Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
6beab8a0dac09b280b7359b0333fbcf9e5ee0548.abstract: Abstract Stuck pipe remains a major drilling challenge, causing significant non-productive time (NPT), increased costs, and operational risks. This paper presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework for early prediction of stuck pipe events using real-time drilling data to enable proactive risk mitigation. The solution utilizes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network trained on refined WITSML data from multiple wells. Key drilling parameters, including hookload, torque, standpipe pressure, flow rate, rotary speed, and rate of penetration, were combined with engineered features to identify precursor patterns associated with stuck pipe incidents. Real-time inference workflows were developed to support field deployment. The model achieved 96.1% accuracy, 0.991 ROC-AUC, 83.3% precision, 87.5% recall, and an F1-score of 85.4%. It successfully predicted 7 of 8 confirmed stuck pipe events while maintaining a false alarm rate of only 2.1%. An average Early Warning Time of 2.9 minutes allowed drilling crews to implement preventive actions before conditions became irreversible. Deployment analysis indicated the potential to reduce stuck pipe-related NPT from 142.5 hours to 31hours, representing a 78.2% reduction. The results demonstrate that AI-driven prediction can improve drilling efficiency, reduce operational costs, and support digital transformation through reliable, actionable early-warning alerts.

title: Propose-Validate-Correct Shadow-Plant Architecture for Safe AI Agents in Process Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
0c41a406387415d7bed6a516d78d35033d6a7bf3.abstract: Abstract Large-language-model (LLM) agents are increasingly explored for autonomous process-plant operations, yet they can propose physically unsafe control actions due to hallucination and imprecise numerical reasoning. We introduce the Propose-Validate-Correct (PVC) architecture, a framework-agnostic safety layer in which every agent-proposed action is first simulated in a shadow plant, a lightweight physics-grounded process simulator, before reaching the real process. When the shadow simulation detects constraint violations, the proposal is rejected and the agent receives structured feedback for correction. PVC is an advisory safety layer and does not replace certified safety instrumented systems (SIS). Experiments are conducted on OpsEnv, an open-source continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) benchmark featuring mass and energy balance ordinary differential equations (ODEs), Arrhenius reaction kinetics, and proportional-integral cooling control. Four agent configurations (ReAct and Plan-and-Execute, each with and without PVC) are evaluated on four LLMs: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (cloud), Alibaba Qwen 2.5 32B, Meta Llama 3.1 8B, and Mistral 7B (all three local via Ollama). The evaluation spans 440 experiment cells organized in four tiers covering eleven scenarios, with three feedback granularity levels (binary, descriptive, suggested fix) for shadow-equipped agents. Both shadow-equipped setups record zero actual violations in all 282 PVC cells, while react_direct accumulates 10.4 mean violations per episode (Tiers 1–3) and plan_exec_direct incurs 0.2. Across all tiers, PVC intercepts 1,552 proposals that would have violated safety constraints, predominantly in upset scenarios where every agent proposal at every timestep triggers a constraint violation. In optimization scenarios (A-series), the correction loop salvages 40.3% of rejected proposals (Self-Correction Success Rate, SCSR), with descriptive per-variable feedback improving SCSR 3.0× over binary reject/accept for matched Gemini Flash cells (50.9% vs. 16.7%). In upset scenarios (B-series), SCSR is 0% under the current stability threshold; PVC acts as a conservative safety gate during disturbed states. Completion scores show a negligible trade-off (Cohen's d = −0.053, 95% CI [−0.283, 0.174]): no statistically significant performance cost is observed, though formal equivalence remains undemonstrated at the current sample size. Plan-and-Execute with PVC runs 31× faster than ReAct with PVC (60 s vs. 1,835 s for Gemini Flash). Shadow-plant validation is a viable safety mechanism for deploying LLM agents in safety-critical process environments; structured physics-based feedback markedly improves self-correction in optimization scenarios. AI-assisted tools were used in the experimental evaluation; all outputs were reviewed and validated by the authors.

title: Real Time Optimization of Gas Separation Cynara Membrane Through AI & ML for Adaptive CO2 Removal and Maximum CH4 Recovery Under Variable Feed Conditions
container-title: ADIPEC
c6cfd536b349f3833ba9d2761dcd4e1414008326.abstract: Abstract Gas processing facility that processes sour feeds, CO2 removal is required to meet pipeline specifications for the natural gas transmission pipeline. The separation is particularly challenging when high CO2 streams must be to processed. The present study does not consider alternative separation technologies, but rather systematically optimizes an existing membrane type process to optimize the removal of CO2 so as to avoid the production of off specification gas, which is costly to be generated. It is based on the commercially available hollow fiber membrane commercial cellulosic triacetate (CTA) modules, nominal capacity of 12T 0.72 MMCFD/membrane module as per Simulation. Deployments and optimizations to these modules will be explained in real time thus pressure of about 600 psi is applied to the membrane feed for optimum separation, furthermore it is mandatory to maintain a minimum CO2 concentration of the Nonpermeate within regulatory requirements (3 mol % set by Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, OGRA Pakistan) for feeds containing approximately 22 mol % CO2. In line pressure, flow rate and temperature data are measured, while composition data are measured simultaneously from an online gas chromatograph sampling the feed, Nonpermeate and permeate streams. This data is fed to a supervisory machine learning layer which predict the behavior of the Nonpermeate CO2 concentration and provide appropriate set point values for required feed pressure, flow rate and temperature. If an excess of CO2 is detected, the controller provides predictive value for the CO2 rich stream thus decreasing the CO2 concentration in the stream prior to exceeding the Nonpermeate specification by controlling the flowrate. On the other hand, a decrease CO2 in the feed provide an operational slack that will allow a safe increase in throughput. This has resulted in a closed-loop, human in the loop configuration with significant improvements in process stability, hydrocarbon recovery, and significant reduction in off specification events using Artificial Intelligence. The study thereby presents a feasibility of real time sweetening of natural gas by machine learning & Artificial Intelligence in an industrially viable way.

title: A Case Study of Seismic Geomorphology Analysis of Post-MMU Carbonate-Clastic Systems in Central Luconia Using Seismic Attributes and AI-Assisted Relative Geological Time (RGT)
container-title: ADIPEC
