00ce053ee1c65f0ed357fb21fa1391ad7c7cc4f7.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming disability support in higher education by enabling personalization, predictive analytics, and systemic change. This chapter explores AI tools—such as adaptive learning platforms, NLP assistants, early-alert systems, and automated accommodations—used to address barriers faced by students with diverse disabilities. Grounded in Universal Design for Learning and the social model of disability, it reframes AI as a means to enhance student autonomy rather than just improve services. It also examines risks like algorithmic bias, surveillance, and data misuse. The chapter proposes a governance framework emphasizing equity, transparency, and student agency, and outlines key directions for future research.</jats:p>

title: A Critical Exploration of How Artificial Intelligence Enhances Accommodation for Learners With Learning Barriers
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
2b033bfd9e3d57fefca89685cea1b21c53f84a3a.abstract: <jats:p>The purpose of this chapter is to critically explore how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning. The chapter identify sources and types of barriers to learning, pointing out the relevance of AI to teaching and learning as research studies have shown that it can personalize instruction, automate timely feedback, generate formative assessment and identify learning achievement and challenges. The chapter shows the readers how AI can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning by using planned Individual Educational Programme (IEP), data-driven analysis, adaptive learning platforms that dynamically adjust content difficulty, sequencing, and presentation formats in real time. Also, AI-powered tools are used such as speech-to-text, text-to-speech, to establish flexibility, personalization and promotes equitable participation for all learners to uphold equity, ethics, and human values in education.</jats:p>

title: Solar Thermal District Heating and Cooling for Smart, Sustainable, AI-Optimized Cities
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
5fb7b6f93a03dabd2aadb285a6f2da9c7a9936b8.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid urbanization and climate imperatives place cities at the center of energy transformation, yet thermal demand roughly half of urban energy end-use remains under addressed by electricity focused renewable strategies. This chapter, per the authors, examines solar thermal district heating and cooling (STDHC) systems as foundational infrastructure for sustainable smart cities. It reviews collector technologies and seasonal thermal storage configurations, then analyzes integration across the physical, cyber, and application layers of smart city architecture, emphasizing digital twins, IoT sensing, and machine-learning optimization including model predictive control and reinforcement learning. International case studies from Canada, Denmark, Croatia, and China demonstrate solar fractions above 50% and substantial carbon reductions. Lifecycle, cost, and energy-justice analyses benchmark performance and equity, while the closing sections identify deployment barriers and propose a research agenda spanning compact storage, federated learning, and policy alignment with SDG 7 and SDG 11.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Smart Microgrids and Electric Mobility Integration for Sustainable Urban Energy Systems in Smart Cities
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
b5fbd81ff64d56f595d8b18611cc2706c6345a69.abstract: <jats:p>For the development of sustainable urban energy systems in smart cities, this chapter focuses on the integration of electric mobility systems with AI-driven smart microgrids. It demonstrates the contribution of electric vehicles (EVs) through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities and variable demand, while smart microgrids enable effective management of dispersed energy resources and dispersed energy generation. The role of Artificial intelligence towards energy distribution optimization, real-time decision-making, and demand forecasting is emphasized along with identifying major obstacles including consumer acceptance, regulatory restrictions, interoperability problems, and discussing worldwide policy trends, the chapter provides an integrated conceptual framework offering insights into how the sustainability, dependability, and energy efficiency might improve urban settings through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), EVs, and microgrids.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Federated Learning Frameworks for Privacy-Preserving Smart Urban Energy Management
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
eadd50d14a20212bca5c4790316df5a2305aab8d.abstract: <jats:p>The growing complexity of urban energy systems with smartness requires intelligent solutions that are privacy friendly to manage the distributed energy resources efficiently. This chapter introduces a federated learning model that is AI-powered and in this system, model training is performed in an intelligent grid, micro grid, and IoT-based devices, without the exchange of raw data. The strategy improves accuracy in load forecasting, efficiency of energy use, and lessens the amount of overhead in communication besides maintaining data privacy and security. The framework combines edge computing and state-of-the-art AI to promote scalable and adaptive energy management to add to sustainable, resilient, and human-centric smart city ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Green Promises
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
f771357c6994b1b3d1a5a4ea4db933888583f4ae.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and sustainability in tourism within the broader context of Industry 4.0 and ongoing digital transformation processes. While AI-driven technologies are widely recognized for their capacity to enhance operational efficiency, optimize resource utilization, and support sustainable development goals, they simultaneously introduce significant conceptual, ethical, and governance-related challenges. Drawing on a socio-technical perspective, this study moves beyond purely technological or outcome-oriented approaches and explores how artificial intelligence reshapes not only the operationalization of sustainability but also its meaning, representation, and lived experience within tourism systems. The chapter introduces the concept of rehumanizing sustainability as a conceptual and practical framework for addressing these challenges. This approach emphasizes the reintegration of human values, agency, and experiential dimensions into AI-driven systems.</jats:p>

title: ОЛМА ДАРАХТИНИНГ ТАНА ЗАРАРКУНАНДАЛАРИ БИЛАН ЗАРАРЛАНИШ ДАРАЖАСИНИ ЎРГАНИШ
container-title: Agro ilm
07be934a2e74e07030e9c7b81718258441cfd2eb.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents the results of observations conducted to study the level of damage caused by body pests to apple trees grown in the conditions of Surkhandarya region. During the research, it was found that, depending on the conditions, from 9 to 28 percent of apple trees were heavily damaged by body pests, and the level of damage to damaged trees was 10-100%.</jats:p>

title: АРЧАНИНГ УНСИМОН ҚУРТИ БИЛАН ЗАРАРЛАНИШ ДАРАЖАСИНИ ЎРГАНИШ
container-title: Agro ilm
3f834e9920d6c830e9a187564564a5afa633d71c.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents the results of a study on the infestation levels of *Pseudococcus* (mealybug) pests on Virginian juniper (*Juniperus virginiana* L.) trees cultivated in the Surkhandarya region. Analysis of observations revealed that the incidence of severe infestation by this pest ranged from 21% to 36% depending on the location, while the degree of damage to individual trees varied between 10% and 100%.</jats:p>

title: AFRIKA TARIGʻIDA JOʻXORI PASHSHASI (ANTHOMYIIDAE)GA QARSHI KURASHNING BIOLOGIK SAMARADORLIGI
container-title: Agro ilm
e5acdeb20d729b725992dc8343811299e03d8c4b.abstract: <jats:p>The corn moth overwinters primarily in the soil in the pupal stage. In the spring, as temperatures rise, the adults emerge and lay eggs on newly sown plots. Upon hatching, the larvae penetrate the soil and feed on germinating seeds, root collars, and young stems. As a result, seedling growth ceases or the plants wither. Development takes 20—40 days, depending on climatic conditions. Most species produce 2—4 generations per year. This article examines the development of the corn moth (Anthomyiidae) and the biological efficacy of control measures against it.</jats:p>

title: СИММЕНТАЛ ЗОТЛИ СИГИРЛАРНИНГ ПУШТДОРЛИК ХУСУСИЯТЛАРИ
container-title: Agro ilm
18cd92c73dac5749719c45c1bd85abd95a604d36.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents information on the characteristics of Simmental cows belonging to different production types. The study found that the age at first calving was 789.5 days for cows of the dairy type and 795.1 days for those of the dairy-beef type; these figures were 11.1 and 5.5 days lower, respectively, than the age at first calving for cows of the beef-dairy type. Additionally, the service period lasted 78.3 days for dairy-type cows and 81.2 days for dairy-beef-type cows—4.2 and 1.3 days shorter, respectively, than the service period for beef-dairy-type cows. Research findings regarding the duration of the service period indicate that the cow itself is a primary factor determining reproductive performance; this highlights the importance of effectively utilizing cows of dairy and dual-purpose (dairy-beef) types for milk production.</jats:p>

title: TURLI ZOT ECHKILAR YELININING MORFOLOGIK KOʻRSATKICHLARI

98e848880df63ba98ca2e56f8de2bb1390a0aefa.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of a study on the morphological characteristics of the udder in local goats and first-generation (F1) crossbreds obtained by crossing local does with imported purebred Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks, as well as with locally bred Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks.</jats:p>

title: TURLI ZOTDAGI ECHKILARNING SUT MAHSULDORLIGI
container-title: Agro ilm
372cb4c69dc68f61038297f6ed9d9f1ebba38b16.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of a study of milk productivity in local goats and first-generation (F₁) crossbred goats obtained by crossing local does with purebred Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks imported from abroad, as well as with Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks produced through local selection. The study examined lactation performance indicators and the chemical composition of milk, including the contents of protein, fat, lactose, dry matter, and mineral substances. A comparative analysis of these indicators was conducted between local goats and F₁ crossbreds.</jats:p>

title: ТЎҒОНСИЗ СУВ ОЛИШ ШАРОИТИДА МАГИСТРАЛ КАНАЛ КИРИШ ҚИСМИДА ЛОЙҚА ЧЎКИНДИЛАРИ ДИНАМИКАСИНИ ТАҲЛИЛ ҚИЛИШ ВА ЗЕМСНАРЯДЛАР ИШЛАШ САМАРАДОРЛИГИНИ ОШИРИШ
container-title: Agro ilm
5f254fc5f7b7f246b8ec58bd1d3b1fca692abe1d.abstract: <jats:p>The article examines the dynamics of sediment deposition at the intake section of the Qarshi Main Canal (QMC) under damless (free) water intake from the Amudarya River, together with the role of dredgers in the overall volume of cleaning works. Based on field monitoring data, the distribution of sediment along the canal length, as well as the technical condition and placement of the fleet of 17 dredgers along the canal, were analysed. It was found that the PK 0-40 segment of the canal intake accumulates more than 85% of the total sediment volume, making it the most heavily loaded section. Recommendations are proposed for the rational placement of dredgers along the canal and for adjusting the cleaning schedule to seasonal sediment inflow.</jats:p>

title: ШЎРЛАНМАГАН ТУПРОҚЛАР ШАРОИТИДА КУЗГИ БУҒДОЙНИ СУҒОРИШ МУДДАТЛАРИНИ БЕЛГИЛАШДА БАРГ ҲУЖАЙРА ШИРАСИ КОНЦЕНТРАЦИЯСИ ВА ТУПРОҚ НАМЛИГИ ДИНАМИКАСИ
container-title: Agro ilm
f9b8de5eb1f617501ce4215003adb91c374cb193.abstract: <jats:p>The article evaluates the pre-irrigation soil moisture regimes (70-70-70, 75-75-75, and 80-80-80% of FC) and the dynamics of leaf cell sap concentration (CSC) in winter wheat grown on non-saline soils during 2020–2021. The results indicated that as pre-irrigation soil moisture increased, leaf CSC values proportionally decreased (13.82–16.31%), whereas toward the end of the growing season, values rose to 17.36–19.50% due to physiological tissue senescence. The study substantiates the high efficacy of using a refractometric method for rapid determination of irrigation timing based on CSC to enhance water-use efficiency. </jats:p>

title: EFFICIENCY OF SPRINKLER IRRIGATION FOR CARROT PRODUCTION ON TYPICAL GREY SOILS OF THE TASHKENT REGION
container-title: Agro ilm
379586c39b8fc86fe6bcbc1041c1fd88ba0b9658.abstract: <jats:p>This study evaluated sprinkler irrigation for carrot production on typical grey soils in the Tashkent region of Uzbekistan. Field experiments with the “Mirzoyi kizil” variety compared furrow irrigation with sprinkler intensities of 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 mm min⁻¹. The highest yield, 29.2 t ha⁻¹, was obtained at 0.4 mm min⁻¹, compared with 22.7 t ha⁻¹ under furrow irrigation.</jats:p>

title: СУҒОРИШ УСУЛЛАРИНИ ТАНЛАШ ВА РАЙОНЛАШТИРИШНИНГ ТАКОМИЛЛАШТИРИЛГАН УСУЛИ

7707643f49ec6b66f6b8c042879406a317a9807e.abstract: <jats:p>The paper proposes an improved approach for selecting irrigation methods by jointly assessing relief, reclamation conditions, soil and hydrophysical properties, agroclimatic conditions, and water source and quality. The final suitability class is determined by the most limiting factor. Separating current and potential suitability and using GIS zoning makes it possible to select irrigation technologies that better match local conditions.</jats:p>

title: SUGʻORILADIGAN BOʻZ - OʻTLOQI TUPROQLARNING AGROKIMYOVIY XOSSALARI VA SANOAT CHIQINDILARI TA’SIRIDA OGʻIR METALLAR BILAN IFLOSLANISHI
container-title: Agro ilm
ba0ed90ab84fabb0583adc409521ff67536ed2c8.abstract: <jats:p>This article highlights the agrochemical properties of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils of Sharaf Rashidovsky district of the Jizzakh Free Economic Zone (JEZ), reserves of humus, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and potassium. There is a high probability of heavy metal pollution in the region near industrial zones, free economic zones, and irrigation networks. Since these soils have a relatively humic layer, as well as a unique water-retaining structure, heavy metals can accumulate in the soil and negatively affect its agrochemical properties. Heavy metals adhere to soil colloids and retain their activity in the soil for a long time. In the soil under study, the lead content of Pb is 40-80 mg/kg (the norm is 32 mg/kg or more), cadmium CD is 0.5 - 2.0 mg/kg (the norm is 0.5 mg/kg or more), zinc Zn is 150-220 mg/kg (the norm is 100 mg/kg or more). This situation indicates an increase in the level of pollution combined with salinization and carbonate content of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils.</jats:p>

title: BUXORO VILOYATI SUG‘ORILADIGAN TAQIR-O‘TLOQI TUPROQLARIDA SHO‘RLANISH TIPI VA DARAJASINING FERMENTATIV FAOLLIKKA TA’SIRI
container-title: Agro ilm
74fd749e6cdb63ff6b1f078186b551a0953dd860.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigated the effects of soil salinity, soil depth, and seasonal conditions on catalase and dehydrogenase activities in irrigated takyr-meadow soils. The research was conducted in non-saline, slightly saline, moderately saline, and strongly saline soil variants at depths of 0–25, 25–50, and 50–80 cm. Enzymatic activity was determined during spring, summer, and autumn, and seasonal dynamics were comparatively assessed. </jats:p>

title: BUXORO VILOYATI SUG‘ORILADIGAN TAQIR-O‘TLOQI TUPROQLARDA SHO‘RLANISH TIPI VA DARAJASIGA BOG‘LIQ HOLDA BAKTERIYALAR SONINING O‘ZGARISHI

f369aff6eef59d13be3e1b1277792d4c20caeeb6.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigated the effect of salinity degree on bacterial abundance in irrigated meadow-takyr soils of the Ziyorat massiv, Karakul district, Bukhara region. Non-saline, slightly saline, moderately saline, and strongly saline soils were examined at depths of 0–25, 25–50, and 50–80 cm during spring, summer, and autumn. The results showed a consistent decline in bacterial abundance with increasing soil salinity and depth. </jats:p>

title: ПУШТА ТЕПАСИГА МИНИМАЛ ИШЛОВ БЕРАДИГАН РОТАЦИОН ЮМШАТКИЧ ПАРАМЕТРЛАРИНИ МАҚБУЛЛАШТИРИШ

65a93a7f82067fdd2ecf892897cc1eedeff7a339.abstract: <jats:p> The article presents research on optimizing the design and operating parameters of a rotary ripper for minimum tillage of the ridge top using mathematical planning methods. The effects of the number of ripper discs, vertical load, and travel speed on the degree of soil crumbling and draft resistance were studied. Based on the obtained regression equations, the optimal values for the working organs were determined, ensuring high-quality tillage of the ridge top in accordance with agrotechnical requirements.</jats:p>

title: LEGUME CROP PRODUCTION IN UZBEKISTAN: AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS OF DETERMINANTS
container-title: Agro ilm
b7f635d6999751960d8ed769b449e51e02d7f0e9.abstract: <jats:p>This paper examines factors affecting legume production in Uzbekistan using cross-sectional data from 1,225 farmers across 12 districts in the UzFarmBarometer 2024 database. A probit model identifies factors associated with the probability of legume adoption. Results show that older farmers are less likely to cultivate legumes, while larger households and more experienced farmers are more likely to adopt them. Earlier-established farms also show lower adoption. Distance to input markets is positively associated with adoption, whereas distance to output markets is negatively associated with it, reflecting differences in input dependence and transaction costs. We suggest that improving rural market infrastructure, extension services, and stable labor arrangements could support legume cultivation.</jats:p>

title: AI adoption in purchasing and supply management: how institutional voids rewire the UTAUT framework
container-title: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications
fd976dc156551128de71dc829f70972275c8141d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study investigates how institutional voids and behavioral factors jointly drive artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in purchasing and supply management (PSM) within emerging economies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Survey data from 200 PSM professionals in Morocco were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test an integrated UTAUT–institutional theory framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Performance expectancy (PE) (ß = 0.530) and social influence (ß = 0.453) primarily drive behavioral intention (BI), while coercive pressure is non-significant (ß = 0.050, p = 0.260). Facilitating conditions (FC) (ß = 0.472) and (BI) (ß = 0.497) exert near-equal direct effects on actual use, confirming an “infrastructure imperative”. Post-hoc multi-group analysis reveals that PE dominates predictive AI adoption, whereas effort expectancy dominates Generative AI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Organizations in emerging economies must pair AI software procurement with dedicated infrastructure, data governance and peer-led change management rather than relying on unsupported mandates.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study demonstrates that institutional voids modify the UTAUT nomological network by elevating FC to a primary co-determinant of technology use, proving infrastructure readiness equals user intention in driving adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Future of work in the era of AI: how technology strategy shapes daily job roles
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
aafce7fbea450e0f9f9a750ed043c623a0abe324.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to explore the impact of organizational technology strategies, particularly in the context of artificial intelligence (AI), on employees’ daily job activities. It also looks at the extent of the transformation and the role of leadership, supportive of innovation and cultural change, in reinforcing the transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The researcher adopted a quantitative research design based on the survey data collected from employees in various industries in Pakistan. The researcher used structural equation modeling to analyze the relationships among technology strategies, organizational facilitators and the transformation of job roles.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research shows that organizations that implement AI and automation alongside digitized processes and advanced data analysis capabilities will experience fundamental changes in their employees’ work functions, skills and job duties. The implementation of digital strategies enhances operational efficiency, but their impact extends beyond this benefit, as they completely transform how work is executed. The presence of an innovation-supportive culture together with strong leadership commitment creates an enhanced effect. The combination of encouragement of organizational experimentation and active leadership support for technological change results in more visible and positive changes in job responsibilities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research findings demonstrate that organizations need to combine technology investments with operational changes to achieve successful digital transformation outcomes. Organizations must establish supportive cultures together with proactive leadership to assist employees throughout the process of organizational change. Organizations need to develop their employees’ skills and build adaptable workforces while maintaining open communication to implement meaningful job role changes that last over time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research contributes to the future of work literature by examining how workers change their job functions at the individual-employee level rather than observing outcomes at the organizational level. The research describes how organizations use technology strategies and organizational enablers to create distinct work environments for the AI age by integrating Job Demands–Resources and Socio-Technical Systems perspectives.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The copilot paradox: configurational pathways to human-AI symbiosis in knowledge work
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
d03a8a16163a5dff3dc0337613cac6bcfc891866.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine the “Copilot Paradox” in safety-critical operations, offering insights into how the chronic tension between the algorithm’s increased efficiency and operational vulnerability is subdued through socio-cognitive configurations across time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>With the use of a two-wave longitudinal fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), the paper explores the changing dynamics of human–artificial intelligence (AI) symbiosis in the oil and gas industry.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Analysis of necessity shows that there is no single condition required in all cases. Sufficiency analysis reveals three distinct, equifinal pathways: buffering, synergy and substitution. At early adoption, institutional re-skilling coupled with psychological safety acts as a buffering mechanism against job insecurity induced by AI. As integration progresses, synergy (fuelled by empowering leadership) and substitution (where team resources fill the gaps in leadership) come to dominate.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Team psychological safety and capability building are structural safeguards for managers in high-reliability sectors, not optional cultural flourishes. These lessons point to pathways for realising AI copilots while preserving human agency and operational resiliency.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper contributes to paradox theory by developing a socio-cognitive infrastructure that highlights its dynamic, temporal configuration and causal asymmetries. Methodologically, it showcases the new promise of longitudinal fsQCA to model dynamics in algorithms’ infusion by capturing their embeddedness through time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: From risk management to AI-enabled governance: five intellectual orientations in EPC and infrastructure project risk governance
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
f4579817be9ece0d7a59e47c0bcdf23a0cb3d236.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to synthesise the intellectual development of engineering–procurement–construction and infrastructure project risk governance and examine whether bibliometric evidence supports five overlapping intellectual orientations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study combined bibliometric analysis with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and a scripted workflow to examine 173 Scopus-indexed publications (1999–2026). The analytical corpus was derived through relevance validation of 678 candidate records, with provenance checked against an 801-row master ledger. Fifteen provisional 2026 records were excluded from temporal comparisons.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The analysis identified five orientations: risk analysis and control (53 documents), performance and overrun (80), governance and relational mechanisms (52), digital information integration (7) and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support (18). The share of period publications addressing performance and overrun increased from 34.7 % in 1999–2018 to 59.7 % in 2023–2025, whereas the digital and AI orientations remained comparatively limited. These patterns concern the published literature and do not establish organizational maturity or realised capability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Scopus coverage, title/abstract-based relevance validation, citation lag, analytical thresholds and interpretive coding delimit the findings. Project-level research is required to test the proposed relationships.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The orientations provide structured review prompts for risk processes, outcome linkage, decision rights, information integration and human oversight of predictive systems; they are not intended as a diagnostic maturity instrument.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study connects construction risk, megaproject governance and construction AI through an auditable corpus and an evidence-bounded conceptual framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Digital and AI tools in informal care: understanding caregivers’ experiences in rural Nigeria
container-title: Working with Older People
9193766175c91a5d0c22308aaadf2db77e3cb6ef.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although informal caregiving for older adults is well-researched, a significant gap exists in understanding how informal caregivers navigate their caregiving roles with the help of digital technologies, especially in rural Nigeria, where internet connectivity is poor and access to digital devices is limited. This study aims to explore how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support care for older adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study adopted a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected from 10 informal caregivers, using semi-structured interviews. The data were further analysed thematically using NVivo 14.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Results identified that caregivers use digital technology for communication and care coordination, learning and self-empowerment, responding to emergency situations, improving efficiency, reducing stress and maintaining contact between older adults and their diaspora family members. The study also found poor access and limited internet infrastructure as barriers to the use of digital technology to improve caregiving.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Only caregivers in rural areas were interviewed. This excluded the experiences of caregivers in urban areas, who may face urban economic stressors that shape their overall caregiving experience and their use of digital technology for caregiving.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings highlight the potential of digital technology to support informal caregiving in rural Nigeria. Improving access to affordable digital devices, reliable internet connectivity and digital literacy can enhance care coordination, caregiver support, emergency response and communication with older adults and their families.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study is important because it provides new insight into how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support older adults despite limited connectivity and access to digital devices. It highlights both the potential of digital tools to strengthen caregiving and the infrastructural barriers that must be addressed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Librarians' perspectives on AI for environmental sustainability in Ghanaian academic libraries
container-title: Library Hi Tech
28538e5061d8e0fb3cd3fccd00568859e1336fb5.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined academic librarians' perspectives on the potential of artificial intelligence to advance environmental sustainability through sustainable library practices and efficient service delivery.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A qualitative approach was adopted, drawing on semi-structured interviews with 21 academic librarians and guided by the Technology Acceptance Model. Thematic analysis was used to identify key patterns and perspectives on AI adoption for environmental sustainability in academic libraries.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study found that academic librarians recognize AI's potential to advance environmental sustainability through intelligent energy management, predictive maintenance, environmental monitoring, and sustainability planning, yet its practical implementation remains limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The qualitative design and small sample limit generalizability; however, the findings provide contextual insights and a basis for broader research across diverse library settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings recommend that universities and library management integrate AI into sustainability planning through effective governance, improved digital infrastructure, and continuous AI literacy training, supported by national policies and investment in responsible AI innovation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Social implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study highlights the value of AI in advancing environmental sustainability in libraries, emphasizing the need for educational initiatives, institutional policies, and responsible technology adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study provides timely empirical insight into AI-enabled environmental sustainability in Ghanaian academic libraries, highlighting the critical gap between librarians' awareness and perceived potential of AI and its limited practical implementation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double‐Blind, Placebo‐Controlled Trial
container-title: Journal of the American Heart Association
846efcdec7a0d643412f19c49d820ad87b1db98b.abstract:
<jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">In this single‐center, randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound‐guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">
                      A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention‐to‐treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46–2.15], adjusted
                      <jats:italic toggle="no">P</jats:italic>
                      =0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross‐clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06–0.80]; adjusted
                      <jats:italic toggle="no">P</jats:italic>
                      =0.022), lower postoperative high‐sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: −2562 ng/L [95% CI, −4301 to −45];
                      <jats:italic toggle="no">P</jats:italic>
                      =0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06–0.98]; adjusted
                      <jats:italic toggle="no">P</jats:italic>
                      =0.046).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high‐sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Capabilities shaping institutional adoption: modeling generative AI adoption in higher education
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
0a3e7ad7e64c8e41dfe6295d2e612b4350cccdc6.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet its successful institutional adoption extends beyond technological capability to require effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. This study aims to structurally model the CSFs for GenAI adoption in education using an integrated interpretive structural modeling (ISM)–DEMATEL approach. The authors frame GenAI adoption explicitly as a knowledge management problem, analyzing how governance, infrastructure and privacy conditions enable or inhibit institutional capabilities for creating, sharing and governing GenAI-empowered knowledge.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The authors identified ten CSFs through a structured literature review and classified them as enablers, capabilities or outcomes across governance, infrastructure, data privacy, analytics, user experience and academic integrity. To analyze the causal and hierarchical relationships among CSFs, an expert validation was conducted through DEMATEL analysis by 20 experts, followed by ISM modeling, which involved 16 experts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>DEMATEL identifies technical infrastructure and scalability (CSF-V), data privacy and security (CSF-VII) and integration with LMS/SSO/enterprise systems (CSF-IX) as prominent causal factors. ISM further positions CSF-V at the deepest foundational level, followed by AI governance, policy and ethics (CSF-III), while assessment integrity and academic honesty (CSF-X) occupies the terminal dependent level. The findings identify assessment integrity (CSF-X), prompt literacy (CSF-IV) and user experience (CSF-VI) as dependent factors, confirming that they emerge from structural readiness rather than acting as independent adoption determinants.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Results are restricted to expert judgment and defined CSFs, which can reduce generalizability across diverse educational settings. Future research must involve larger samples, validate empirically and use longitudinal designs to study changing relations while also testing the knowledge governance mechanisms revealed in this research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The model enables phased prioritization of CSFs for optimal implementation of GenAI. Foundational readiness requires infrastructure, system integration and data governance, followed by governance policies and faculty capacity development, before addressing user experience and academic integrity as dependent outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research provides a systems approach to GenAI adoption in education by presenting an integrated ISM–DEMATEL framework based on TOE and DOI, grounded in knowledge governance theory. It aids authors’ understanding of how technological, organizational and knowledge governance dimensions must be sequentially aligned to enable better implementation of GenAI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The relationship between AI awareness and thriving at work: exploring the moderated mediation model
container-title: European Journal of Training and Development
2197f659428e01b99695470828484314d3e05f60.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on the socially embedded model of thriving and the conservation of resources model, this study aims to investigate the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) awareness, seen as a hindrance stressor, and thriving at work. In particular, it explores how AI anxiety mediates this relationship and how self-efficacy moderates the mediating effect.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To securitize the study hypotheses, data were obtained from banking employees via an electronic questionnaire, yielding 320 valid responses. The proposed model relationships were assessed through partial least squares structural equation modeling and process analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results uncover that while AI awareness is not significantly linked to vitality, it is negatively correlated with learning. Furthermore, AI anxiety mediates the direct influence that AI awareness has on dimensions of thriving at work. In addition, self-efficacy acts as a buffer, mitigating the adverse indirect influence of AI awareness on thriving at work through AI anxiety.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and digital literacy programs, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and revise their role descriptions, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Demystifying generative AI adoption in higher education: an integrated GRAI–AKM framework
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
5b17f041234a3c97cd5c9dc9ec71d868739c3eab.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet successful institutional adoption requires effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. Existing studies have predominantly relied on individual-level technology acceptance models, providing limited insight into organizational and knowledge management capabilities for sustainable implementation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A qualitative research design was employed using open-ended written responses from 20 academic professionals recruited through Prolific. The qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis, and the resulting themes were mapped onto the proposed graphs with results and actions interconnected (GRAI) and active knowledge models (AKM) framework (GRAI–AKM).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Six themes were identified: (1) professional training and AI literacy, (2) ethical governance and academic integrity, (3) structural capital flexibility and knowledge processes, (4) trust, transparency and relational capital, (5) platform maturity and technological infrastructure and (6) human–AI complementarity. Professional training and AI literacy emerged as the most-discussed themes. The findings suggest that Gen AI adoption depends on the interaction of human, structural, technological, and knowledge resources rather than technology acceptance alone.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although based on a qualitative sample and self-reported written responses, the study advances knowledge management research by integrating Intellectual Capital (IC) and the Knowledge-Based View (KBV) into a comprehensive framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy, ethical governance, organizational learning and human–AI collaboration for sustainable adoption of Gen AI in higher education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides qualitative empirical support for the GRAI–AKM framework, offering a multidimensional perspective on knowledge management for sustainable adoption of Gen AI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Organizational AI orientation, AI self-efficacy and value co-creation: a human-AI collaboration perspective in healthcare
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
3448621767455431dc4f953005dbeb9a4aab7448.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital to healthcare system transformation. Existing research mainly focuses on the macro-level technological empowerment of AI, yet insufficiently explores how healthcare organizations’ strategic commitment to AI translates into better medical service outcomes through individual psychological mechanisms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>From the perspective of human-AI collaboration, we utilize survey data collected from medical staff working in Chinese medical institutions to examine the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions linking organizational AI orientation and AI value co-creation outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on social cognitive theory, the results reveal that healthcare organizations’ AI orientation is positively related to medical staff’s AI value co-creation outcomes, and AI self-efficacy mediates this relationship. Moreover, their creative self-efficacy positively moderates the relationship between AI self-efficacy and AI value co-creation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study clarifies the micro-level transmission paths between organizational AI orientation and medical staff’s value co-creation outcomes. It provides new insights for hospitals to enhance medical service quality and optimize human-AI collaboration during AI-driven healthcare organizational transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation: a cybernetic perspective
container-title: Kybernetes
2b2a2584eeba12477d60849925f24bde6a805644.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In the AI era, digital transformation has become essential for enterprises to adapt as complex systems to uncertain business environments. In this work, we aim to analyze the evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation (EDT), focusing on its evolution and impact on enterprise performance from a system cybernetics perspective.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We employ evolutionary dynamics analysis grounded in game theory to model the EDT process, and perform an econometric and empirical analysis on a sample of Chinese A-share-listed enterprises from 2009 to 2023. The approach encompasses heterogeneity analysis, moderation effect models, such as testing enterprise environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors and market concentration, and threshold effect analyses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The evolutionary dynamics analysis finds that increasing the risk-averse benefits of traditional enterprises and reducing the additional benefit coefficient would hinder EDT. Increasing the investment of technology enterprises in internal resource restructuring accelerates the transformation process. Empirically, AI significantly contributes to EDT. ESG positively moderates the relationship between AI and EDT, while market concentration exerts a negative moderating effect. Furthermore, AI and EDT show an inverted U-shaped trend when R&D intensity exceeds a specific threshold, while a U-shaped trend is observed when enterprise performance exceeds a specific threshold.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this work, we uncover the complex, non-linear cybernetic feedback loops, such as U-shaped and inverted U-shaped, and boundary conditions, such as ESG and market concentration for AI-driven EDT, offering systemic strategies for enterprises adapting to the digital ecosystem.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
0bb98e6ca3b6e4203d765fe27185ba4340bcd31d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic constraint on the posterior mass attributable to the critical state (talert = 70.0%), the model outputs Bayesian probabilities alongside LLM-extracted textual evidence, yielding an anticipation interval of 1.33 reporting cycles relative to the documented administrative response.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The neuro-symbolic framework bridges the gap between deep learning perception and causal inference in construction management. By coupling LLM-driven zero-shot ordinal extraction with DBN causal reasoning, the research establishes an auditable framework for risk documentation. The integrated framework transitions AI from an opaque prediction model into an accountable decision-support tool, providing stakeholders with transparent explainable AI diagnostics and supporting a shift from reactive mitigation to proactive, evidence-based risk prevention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: NO‘XATNI SUG‘ORISHNING ILDIZ TIZIMIDAGI TUGANAK BAKTERIYALARI SHAKLLANISHIGA TA’SIRI

22654f13fe8ecff21c01ce7e566cc2154ca9fce9.abstract: <jats:p>The article investigates the effect of irrigation on the formation and accumulation of nodule bacteria in the root system of the chickpea varieties “Yulduz” and “Milyutin-6” under meadow sierozem soil conditions in the Samarkand region. Field experiments were conducted using non-irrigated control and irrigated treatments. In the irrigated treatment, three irrigations were applied during the growing season at rates of 700, 1200, and 1200 m³/ha, respectively. The results showed that irrigation had a positive effect on the formation and accumulation of nodule bacteria in the chickpea root system. In the “Yulduz” variety, the mass of nodules on the roots of 10 plants was 3.2 g in the non-irrigated treatment and 10.3 g in the irrigated treatment, while in the “Milyutin-6” variety, the corresponding values were 3.2 and 10.1 g. Irrigation maintained an optimal soil moisture level, contributing to better root system development and increased activity of nodule bacteria. It was also established that a soil temperature of approximately 18 °C is favorable for active nodule development.</jats:p>

e6ff33139217c01fd9c7182b2bb3870876c0d144.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents a comprehensive scientific analysis of the viability dynamics and the proportion of defective cocoons across various silkworm breeds, lines, and their inter-family hybrid combinations. The study confirmed the complete absence (0%) of pathogens causing highly dangerous diseases—such as nosemosis and nuclear polyhedrosis—in all samples. title: ОСАЖДЕНИЕ НЕОДНОРОДНЫХ ПО КРУПНОСТИ НАНОСОВ ПРИ ДЕЙСТВИИ ВЕТРОВЫХ ВОЛН

525533ec181b1bc66d8a49f6c4b0aad4ebbfac1f.abstract: <jats:p>A mathematical model of the settling of non-uniform sediment particles in water under wind-wave action is considered. Using the momentum and continuity equations for the solid and liquid phases, relationships are obtained for the variation of particle concentration with depth and time. Accounting for wave action makes it possible to refine the sequential settling behavior of sediment fractions. The resulting relationships can be applied to hydraulic calculations of settling basins and reservoirs by jointly considering flow parameters, wind velocity, and wave characteristics.</jats:p>

9529c2568333a1d06b4d72d97c3b703ffa056e1b.abstract: <jats:p>The paper examines the effect of combined pre-sowing ultraviolet (UV) irradiation of soil and seed tubers on potato emergence. Five irradiation variants at 10–50 cm from the source (0.42–0.76 mJ/cm²) and an untreated control were tested on cv. Santa in three replications. On day 15 after planting, emergence in all UV variants exceeded the control (56.7 %), reaching 63.3–83.3 %. title: MONITORING OF SOURCES OF INDUSTRIAL TECHNOGENIC HAZARDS IN THE SAMARKAND REGION, ASSESSMENT OF THEIR TERRITORIAL DISTRIBUTION AND IDENTIFICATION OF HAZARDOUS OBJECTS BASED ON GIS
container-title: Agro ilm
5ab7c621c6c7dcf1e6b7d59f3e2151a19856d3e4.abstract: <jats:p>This study is devoted to monitoring the sources of industrial techno genic risks in the Samarkand region, assessing the features of their territorial distribution and identifying dangerous objects based on geographic information technology (GIS). As part of the research, information about industrial enterprises and facilities that pose a potential anthropogenic hazard in the region is being collected, systematized and entered into a geoformation database. A comprehensive analysis of the spatial location of sources of danger, their technical condition, the likelihood of accidents, population density, environmentally sensitive areas and other factors is carried out. GIS technologies are used to map man-made risk zones and identify objects with a high level of potential danger. The results obtained can be used to assess territorial risks, prevent emergencies, ensure environmental safety and improve the management of sources of anthropogenic hazards.</jats:p>

title: O‘ZBEKISTON RESPUBLIKASI IQTISODIYOTI VA AGRAR SEKTORINI KLASTERLI MODERNIZATSIYA QILISH

title: Academic librarians' perceptions of new skills, competencies and professional development needs in the AI age
container-title: Library Hi Tech
6feab49e9ca40c398417d9ba6085cbacfde84c66.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined academic librarians' perceptions of new skills and competencies, use of AI tools and professional development needs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An online survey was distributed via professional networks, and data were collected and analysed from 155 valid respondents across Australia, European countries and the USA.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings demonstrate that the highly ranked new skills needed by academic librarians included AI tools and output evaluation, application of data governance and management, AI literacy instruction and integration of AI into curricula. The new competencies consisted of ethical implementation and governance, critical analysis and evaluation of AI tools and AI literacy and conceptual understanding of AI. AI tools could be used to improve information service provisions through responsible and ethical information management and discovery. Key training and knowledge areas included critical evaluation of AI-generated content. Hands-on tutorials with case studies and in-person or hybrid workshops were the most suitable training formats.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings are helpful and practical for academic librarians to develop new skills and competencies and support professional development and curriculum renewal.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The new contribution of this study lies in the identification of important new skills and competencies that academic librarians need to utilise AI tools in a successful way, mitigate associated potential risks and adapt to changing professional roles.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Beyond the laggard myth: time-series analysis of AI job market dynamics in construction
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
1f94dbb69ad21caf664f34c48c749bebc9978575.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study presents one of the first time-series, cross-industry analyses of the artificial intelligence (AI) job market for the construction sector. It benchmarks construction against both digital and traditional industries to interrogate prevailing assumptions of linear diffusion and temporal catch-up in AI workforce adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on 51 months of Lightcast job postings (January 2021–March 2025), with construction defined as ANZSIC Division E, the study employs an interpretable analytical toolkit comprising Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess decomposition (period = 12), month-of-year bootstrap tests on detrended series, cross-correlation analysis with bootstrap confidence bands, Newey–West trend estimation on sectoral share ratios and conservative one-step Exponential Smoothing State-Space (ETS) forecasts. All results are re-estimated excluding the partial final month (March 2025) as a sensitivity check.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Construction's AI hiring is very sparse, accounting for under 1% of AI postings and is more volatile than hiring in peer sectors, but it grew fastest: annual construction postings rose more than fourfold between 2021 and 2024, against increases of 13% and 9% in the digital and traditional sectors, whose postings peaked in 2022. Construction's share of AI postings relative to both comparators therefore rises (converges) rather than falls. No delayed-follower pattern is detected: no lag at which the comparator sectors lead construction is statistically reliable, and the short-run associations that are detected are weak, near-contemporaneous and sensitive to the sample end. Unlike the comparator sectors, construction shows no statistically significant within-year seasonality and short-horizon ETS forecasts do not improve on a seasonal-naïve benchmark. These findings are robust to the exclusion of the partial final month of data. Construction thus appears as a low-base, fast-growing entrant with its own hiring dynamics, not a “laggard” following digital-sector cycles with a delay.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings suggest that construction firms should prioritise internal capability building and domain-specific AI skills where external hiring is thin, support flexible, year-round upskilling, and design policy and vendor strategies tailored to the sector's operational realities rather than importing digital-sector playbooks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study provides among the first data-driven, time-series evidence that qualifies the dominant “late adopter” narrative in construction. It shows that construction's low level of AI hiring coexists with the fastest growth and a rising share, without a delayed-follower timing pattern, distinguishing a low starting point from a lagging trajectory and offering an empirically grounded alternative to technologically deterministic accounts of cross-industry AI adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Combined imaging of myocardial scar and fat using AI-guided dual bright- and black-blood late gadolinium enhancement
container-title: European Heart Journal - Imaging Methods and Practice
6fa1177f8d76bb4113d740b4286f2eba98181081.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Aims</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Characterization of myocardial scar and fat is clinically important for diagnosis, risk stratification, and procedural planning in cardiomyopathies. While black-blood late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) improves scar conspicuity, fat remains hyperintense and may confound interpretation. We aimed to develop and evaluate SPOT-DIXON, a dual bright- and black-blood LGE sequence with Dixon water-fat separation and artificial intelligence (AI)-guided analysis, enabling simultaneous and co-registered quantification of myocardial scar and intra- and extra-cardiac fat.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>SPOT-DIXON alternates bright- and black-blood LGE preparations on consecutive heartbeats while acquiring dual-echo data for Dixon water-fat separation. Simulations, phantom experiments, and validations in a prospective cohort of 36 patients referred for cardiac MRI were performed. An AI model automatically segmented the left ventricular (LV) wall on bright-blood water images, with contours propagation to scar and fat images.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Simulations and phantoms confirmed preserved bright- and black-blood contrast and accurate water-fat separation. In patients, AI-based LV wall segmentation showed excellent agreement with manual delineation (global DICE=84.4 ± 4.0%). SPOT-DIXON yielded higher scar volume, burden, and transmurality measurements than reference sequences, while LV wall volume was similar between sequences. Novel quantitative metrics, including intramyocardial fat burden expressed relative to scar mass, were feasible only with SPOT-DIXON. Acquisition times were comparable across sequences (5min55s ± 2min17 s), while AI-based analysis substantially reduced post-processing time to 2.1 ± 0.7 seconds.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI-guided SPOT-DIXON enables simultaneous, co-registered assessment of myocardial scar and fat within a single LGE acquisition. This approach overcomes key limitations of current workflows and introduces novel quantitative markers of fibrofatty remodelling with potential clinical relevance in cardiomyopathies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Water footprint of large AI models: risks to global water security and sustainable optimization strategies
container-title: Water Policy
7bc4d996ef1e8d7d275c67c8a8741273c4f6cf4e.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Diagram linking AI model training and inference to lifecycle water use, estimated at 4.2–6.6 billion m³ annually by 2027, and showing water reuse, efficient cooling, smarter workloads, and standardized reporting as strategies to protect global water security.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models has introduced a significant yet underexamined environmental challenge: freshwater consumption. This narrative review synthesizes scientific literature, industry sustainability reports, and case studies to quantify the water footprint of AI systems across their full lifecycle, from semiconductor fabrication and data center operations to electricity generation and supply chains. Direct water use occurs primarily through evaporative and liquid cooling in data centers, where a single large facility can consume 11,000–19,000m3/day. Indirect water use is embedded in electricity generation and chip manufacturing, with advanced fabrication plants drawing 10,000–37,000m3/day. Major technology companies, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta, collectively consume billions of cubic meters in 2022–2024, with consumption rising alongside accelerating AI deployment. Critically, over 52% of the world's top 100 data centers are projected to be located in high water stress regions by 2030, where AI infrastructure increasingly competes with agricultural, municipal, and ecological needs. Sustainable alternatives, including immersion cooling, nonpotable water reuse, and AI-driven workload optimization, offer measurable reductions but remain inconsistently adopted. The direct and indirect water footprints of AI models during their entire lifecycle are reviewed. Two of the main direct water usage sources are semiconductor manufacturing and data center cooling. Clip manufacturing and electricity generation significantly increase the indirect water footprint of AI. In areas with scarce freshwater supplies, the growth of AI technology may worsen water stress. Standardized reporting frameworks and lifecycle-based water accounting are urgently needed to safeguard global water security.</jats:p>

title: University students' disciplinary perspectives on generative AI after two years of its widespread use
container-title: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
5cfc2677f2ff083e2ccefb422d4ee92c351ab20c.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study explores how university students use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) across various disciplines, including STEM, Business, Education Futures, Clinical & Health Sciences (CHS), Creative and Allied Health & Human Performance (AHHP). It aims to identify discipline-based perspectives, perceived benefits, ethical boundaries and the support needs required for responsible use of GenAI tools.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A survey was conducted approximately two years after the widespread use of GenAI, by which time participants were expected to be familiar with its use. Students were categorised based on their discipline, English fluency, mode of learning and level of study. Their responses were analysed to compare usage patterns, satisfaction levels and ethical considerations across disciplines.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results highlight that student perspectives on GenAI tools are discipline-dependent. STEM and Education Futures showed the highest acceptance, while CHS and Business students were more cautious and sceptical about accuracy and ethical issues. Non-native English speakers rated GenAI tools more favourably as aids for writing and comprehension. Novice users expressed enthusiasm, while expert users showed dissatisfaction due to errors and false information.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study relied on self-reported perceptions and represents a single institutional context. Broader investigations are recommended, with a particular focus on equity groups such as students with disabilities, low-SES students and remote learners.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Different approaches were suggested for integrating GenAI into learning. STEM students favoured comparative tasks; CHS recommended support for diagnostic reasoning; Allied Health preferred role-playing simulations; Education Futures highlighted lesson planning; and Business students suggested case-based and productivity uses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides cross-disciplinary analyses of GenAI use by students and proposes approaches for ethical and discipline-specific integration into university curricula.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Teacher Monitoring Strategies for AI-Aided Student Writing Outputs Toward Policy Guidelines

<jats:p>This study examined the extent to which senior high school teachers monitor AI-generated written outputs, focusing on the use of AI detectors, manual review, and cross-checking results. The study respondents were teachers from the Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) strand of Philippine Christian University-Dasmariñas. The researchers collected data through a structured questionnaire and analyzed it using descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation. Results showed that teachers used AI detectors and cross-checking to a moderate extent, while they used manual review to a high extent and found it significant. Teachers faced challenges such as limitations in AI detection tools and time constraints in manual evaluation and cross-checking. These findings highlight the importance of a layered monitoring approach, where teacher judgment remains central, and AI tools serve as supplementary aids. The study provides evidence for developing clear guidelines and practices that balance ethical assessment, professional discretion, and responsible integration of AI in student writing evaluation.

 Keywords:  Artificial intelligence, AI-generated text, teacher monitoring strategies, manual review, cross-checking</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality–Emotional Attachment–Loyalty Pathway in 2025–2026
container-title: Revista Cultura Científica
98edd2a46835569f3a396f1f1c13e49d3436f00c.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although online-shopping participation should not be interpreted as a direct measure of AI adoption or retailer-specific investment. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect  = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). The study considers a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.</jats:p>

<jats:p>Abstract :
This study aims to analyze the challenges of using Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) to understand the Qur’an and Hadith among undergraduate Islamic Education (PAI) students, their practices of information verification and academic integrity, and the application of Islamic ethics of seeking knowledge. This qualitative study employed a case study design. Data were collected through an online questionnaire comprising open-ended and closed-ended questions administered to 13 informants and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that Generative AI helps students understand learning materials and access information efficiently. However, its use presents risks, including inaccurate information, unclear sources, and reduced learning independence.
