title: Digital Revolution in Coiled Tubing Operations: Pioneering a Remote Operations Center Framework that Redefines Intervention Efficiency, Asset Reliability, and Sustainability Across a Large-Scale CT Fleet
container-title: ADIPEC
41f76fd9cd9c133d5eddd6c981bdc5b9dc53e0c1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Coiled tubing (CT) interventions have traditionally required significant field presence, intensive personnel deployment, and reactive decision-making. A Remote Operations Center (ROC) framework, integrating real-time asset health monitoring, live operational parameter surveillance, and remote expert engagement, fundamentally challenges this model. Deployed across a long fleet of CT units and validated in more than 100 jobs, this framework redefines how interventions are monitored, managed, and optimized by reducing well-site personnel dependency.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The framework operates through two integrated digital layers and three synchronized pillars. An asset health and monitoring platform delivers real-time visibility across injector head performance, pressure control equipment supply pressures, hydraulic readings, engine diagnostics, maintenance status, and operational parameters for each CT unit. A remote screen access and communication interface enables live data viewing, direct supervisor engagement, and real-time technical intervention without physical presence. Three pillars govern execution: a Field Team responsible for on-location job execution, a ROC Team providing live monitoring, engineering oversight, and technical decision support, and a Reliability Team managing equipment anomaly detection, alarm generation, and notification workflows.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Deployed across a fully digitalized fleet of CT units, the ROC framework consistently demonstrated its ability to detect and resolve critical deviations before escalation—including job design, treatment execution, equipment performance, tubing force verification, injector head chain behavior, and BOP supply conditions—interventions that conventional field-only execution models would have missed or delayed.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Operational efficiency increased by 80% year-on-year. Pipe failures were eliminated entirely in the first full deployment year. CT pipe life extension reached 39% in underbalanced operations and 78% in conventional operations, delivering combined maintenance savings exceeding 20% of the annual cost in supplies. Injector head chain twist incidents dropped 64% year-on-year. Sustainability outcomes proved equally transformative: diesel consumption fell 45% year-on-year, saving over 2.6 million liters, with reductions of 27 metric tons CO2e in Scope 1 and 545 metric tons CO2e in Scope 3 emissions. These combined results establish remote operations not as a support function, but as a core enabler of safer, smarter, and more sustainable coiled tubing intervention delivery.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Remote monitoring concepts exist broadly across oil and gas, yet a purpose-built ROC governing an entire CT fleet through integrated asset health surveillance, live parameter monitoring, and synchronized three-pillar expert engagement represents a step change in how coiled tubing interventions are managed. This framework establishes a new operational benchmark for the industry, offering a scalable and replicable blueprint to elevate CT intervention performance, asset reliability, and sustainability through structured digital transformation</jats:p>

title: Comprehensive Monitoring of a Macro Grid Through Digital Tools in a Secondary Recovery Process
container-title: ADIPEC
d13cd9f9dc85cdac40992acf99233a36ee43d86c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>After more than 40 years of production, Field A faced reservoir energy depletion in Reservoir B, as evidenced by declining pressure and low recovery. This work addresses the implementation of secondary recovery through water injection, based on a large-scale grid of horizontal producer and injector wells. The objective is to increase ultimate recovery and sweep efficiency, focusing on the evolution of the strategy, the monitoring of injection distribution, and well performance from 2017 to 2026.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The methodology combined workover and strategic conversion of wells, drilling of new horizontal producers and injectors, and the implementation of a multiscale monitoring system for the Macro-grid (field, sector, pattern, well, flow unit) that evaluates pressures, production, and incremental oil. Dynamic simulation models and advanced digital analytical tools were employed, calibrated with real data and comparative analysis of pressure and production before and after water injection. Flow unit correlations and pattern adjustments allowed for optimized efficiency considering the heterogeneity and dynamic behavior of the reservoir.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The original reservoir pressure (3,600 psi) decreased to approximately 900 to 1,100 psi before injection, very close to the bubble point pressure (874.7 psi). Upon implementation of the project, the current average pressure increased to 1,524 psi in the optimized areas. Between January 2017 and April 2026, 12 injection wells and 37 active producers were completed in the B sandstone. The average daily injection rate in April 2026 was 57,395 BWIPD, generating an average production increase of 10,506 BOPD associated with secondary recovery, with a total fluid production of 47,445 BFPD. The incremental reserves by waterflooding developed at December 2025 are estimated at 27.64 MMSTB. The response time was short (1–3 months), with water breakthrough occurring 90–180 days after each injection, and the voidage replacement ratio is 1.1. Continuous monitoring has allowed for pattern adjustments and maximized sweep efficiency, keeping field production above 18,000 BOPD even with increasing water cut, and maintaining it above the bubble point pressure.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This work introduces an innovative methodology for the monitoring and optimization of secondary recovery in mature fields, integrating a macro-grid composed of multiple injection patterns and horizontal wells, along with multiscale monitoring systems and advanced digital tools. Unlike traditional approaches based on simple injection patterns, this strategy enables adaptive, continuous control tailored to real reservoir complexity. It demonstrates not only the technical effectiveness of secondary recovery through water injection, but also continuous optimization based on data and analytical/dynamic simulation, highlighting an adaptable approach to maximize reserves and efficiency.</jats:p>

title: Integrated Flare Energy Reduction and Emissions Mitigation at Oman LNG: Low-Capital Operational and Digital Solutions
container-title: ADIPEC
56aba0650cb8375e1d092dfc54a624378fb7b647.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Liquefied natural gas (LNG) facilities are under increasing pressure to lower greenhouse gas emissions while preserving the safety margins required for continuous, high-reliability operation. Flaring will remain necessary for process protection during abnormal or emergency conditions; however, routine or avoidable flaring represents lost hydrocarbon value, unnecessary fuel consumption, and additional carbon emissions. Within the Oman LNG complex, flare management was therefore treated not as a single environmental project, but as an operating discipline linked to energy efficiency, production planning, marine coordination, and Oman LNG's broader Net Zero Emissions roadmap.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper describes an integrated flare energy-reduction program built around practical changes that could be implemented with existing assets and internal technical capability. Implemented or operationally established initiatives include fuel-gas-to-nitrogen flare purge optimization, comprehensive flare quantification, nitrogen monitoring and consumption, warm ship handling improvements, and Cold Gas Recovery. The Direct Cooldown Method is presented as a trial-demonstrated concept with optimization ongoing.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Engineering calculations based on restriction-orifice design flows estimated that substitution of continuous fuel-gas flare purging with nitrogen reduced fuel-gas consumption by approximately 7.05 t/d, equivalent to more than 2,500 t/year of avoided hydrocarbon consumption. Digital quantification improved identification of individual flare contributors, event duration, cause classification and emissions reporting. Warm ship handling improvements delivered an observed operational result: zero cooldown-related flare events in 2022 and 2023 despite 20 cooldown activities in 2023 compared with 17 in 2019.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The Direct Cooldown Method eliminated the conventional gas-up stage, corresponding to approximately 12,000 MMBtu of avoided gas-up energy and a calculated gross emissions-reduction potential of approximately 793 tCO2e per applicable operation. The trial also identified an important limitation: elevated nitrogen concentration in the ship vapor return prevented the intended fuel-gas-system recycling and resulted in approximately 500 t of flaring. Further optimization is therefore required before the gross emissions-reduction potential can be considered a net achieved benefit. Cold Gas Recovery has been completed and implemented, with an estimated annual reduction potential of approximately 3,303 tCO2e/year based on the recovery of shutdown-related cold gas through the BOG/fuel-gas system. Overall, the case study shows that low-capital engineering, operational and digital interventions can materially reduce routine and avoidable flaring while preserving the safety function and availability of the flare system.</jats:p>

title: Lightweight Digital Twin Fabric: Scaling Asset Intelligence via Progressive Fidelity and Reduced-Order Intelligence
container-title: ADIPEC
7f51899ef5bbc9f1801580afe67bc6db3aa9d8f8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives/Scope</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite significant capital investment, industrial digital twin initiatives frequently fail to scale across large brownfield portfolios due to unsustainable modeling costs and lifecycle overhead. This paper introduces the Lightweight Digital Twin Fabric(LwDT-Fabric)—a decision-centric architecture that decouples actionable insight from full-physics model dependency. By prioritizing decision relevance over exhaustive fidelity, the framework enables enterprise-scale deployment aligned with ISO 55000 and API 580/581. The objective is a "Right-Sized" digital transformation delivering maximum asset integrity with minimum computational and human overhead.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods, Procedures, Process</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The LwDT-Fabric utilizes a progressive, event-driven architecture built on open-standard schemas, including CFIHOS and ISO 15926, to ensure cross-platform interoperability and long-term data sustainability. The architecture is structured across three core pillars: Standardized Twin Templates: Utilizing asset-class libraries to enable rapid instantiation with consistent data models, significantly reducing initial configuration time.Reduced-Order Modeling (ROM): Implementing hybrid physics-informed models that capture decision-critical behaviors—such as vibration anomalies and corrosion progression—while functioning reliably in "noisy" or incomplete brownfield data environments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Progressive Fidelity & Expert Governance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A dynamic resolution system where model complexity escalates only when risk thresholds are breached. High-fidelity simulations are activated for complex analysis and routed through an Expert-Validation Layer for human-in-the-loop arbitration.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results, Observations, Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The LwDT-Fabric architecture is engineered for rapid scaling across extensive asset portfolios, providing a defensible blueprint for autonomous enterprise orchestration. Key strategic results and benefits include: Decision-Centric Intelligence: Shifts the operational goal from a "Visual Replica" to a "Decision Engine," prioritizing actionable intelligence over mere model fidelity.Deployment Acceleration: Achieves a projected 4× acceleration in setup speed, reducing deployment from 12-16 weeks to just 3-4 weeks per asset.Engineering Optimization: Projected to reduce engineering effort by approximately 50–55% through reusable Intelligence Templates and decision-focused intelligence.Integrity Velocity: Compresses RBI re-ranking cycles from weeks to hours, moving from static "post-mortem" reporting to live, dynamic governance.Accuracy & Resilience: ROM outputs maintain a projected 85% correlation with observed degradation trends, even in data-sparse brownfield environments.Computational Efficiency: Reduces high-performance computing(HPC) demand by &gt;60%, significantly lowering the digital carbon footprint of the asset estate.Proactive Risk Management: The "Right-Sized" approach ensures that computational and human resources are mathematically aligned with asset criticality, preventing "Pilot Purgatory" and ensuring that high-risk assets receive the necessary analytical depth while maintaining baseline visibility across the entire portfolio.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Novel/Additive Information</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The principal contribution of this work is the transition from model-centric digital twins to intelligence-centric asset decision support. By decoupling model complexity from business value and aligning intelligence depth with asset risk, criticality, and decision value, the Lightweight Digital Twin Fabric (LwDT-Fabric) provides a practical and scalable framework for extending asset intelligence across brownfield industrial facilities. This framework provides global operators with a scalable, open-source blueprint to achieve true digital maturity, ensuring every computational watt and engineering hour is weaponized to protect the facility's bottom line while maintaining uncompromising safety standards.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The Digital Divide in Global Communication: Inequality, Governance, and the Contest for Narrative Power
container-title: Financial Economics Research
13321ff411b3489426d04c8f4244913a81332f38.abstract: <jats:p>The spread of information and communication technologies has made connectivity central to global communication, yet the benefits of this transformation are distributed unequally. This article examines the digital divide as a structural feature of contemporary global media rather than a mere gap in hardware access. Drawing on scholarship that treats the divide as a complex and dynamic phenomenon, it argues that the divide operates on at least three intersecting levels: access, usage and skill, and algorithmic and infrastructural power. It then traces how the divide is deepened by the politics of platform governance and by asymmetric control over digital content, and considers how these asymmetries become acute in armed conflict, where the ability to generate, moderate, and frame information is itself a weapon. The article concludes that bridging the divide requires not only connectivity and digital literacy but a redistribution of the power to produce and govern the global media environment.</jats:p>

title: Is mental fatigue a nonlinear accumulation process? Evidence from field EEG-based brain network analysis
e0de6443eadd3930fce88c525ea233b9d919aeff.abstract: Mental fatigue is a difficult to detect risk state in high-risk industries and is closely associated with sustained cognitive load and prolonged work duration. To overcome the limitations of post-incident management, research has introduced wearable EEG technologies, promoting a shift in safety management from passive response to feedforward warning. However, most existing studies are based on laboratory experiments, treating cognitive load and work duration as independent variables and inducing fatigue over short durations, which limits the characterization of fatigue under extended work periods. To address these issues, this study conducted a field experiment at a drilling site, combining wearable EEG functional connectivity and brain network analyses with a PCA Transformer framework for automated fatigue recognition. The results show that as task duration increased, functional connectivity analysis indicated that mental fatigue generally increased and then decreased; meanwhile, brain network analysis revealed a transition from local strengthening to global integration, accompanied by reduced network stability. The Transformer model demonstrated excellent classification performance, achieving recognition accuracies of 90.7% and 91.0% under low and high load conditions, respectively. Overall, these findings indicate that shift scheduling should not rely solely on cumulative work duration but should instead pay closer attention to changes in risk across different work periods. Based on this, safety management practices may consider reducing the concentration of high cognitive load tasks and critical decision making activities during later stages of work, while machine learning based fatigue state recognition offers feasible technical support for feedforward safety management.

title: Consumer Protection in the Digital Economy Era: A Literature Analysis of E-Commerce Regulation in Indonesia
container-title: SKYHAWK : Jurnal Aviasi Indonesia
51734a8a6818bfc4ae0c92ab9da7eb1c8b5f2551.abstract: <jats:p>The growth of Indonesia’s digital economy has driven a significant transformation in transaction patterns while posing new challenges regarding consumer protection. Although the Consumer Protection Law and Personal Data Protection Law have been passed, they are not considered optimal in responding to the complexity of the digital ecosystem.  This research uses a descriptive qualitative approach based on a structured literature review combined with doctrinal legal analysis and thematic synthesis. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of consumer protection regulations in e-commerce transactions in Indonesia by examining legal studies, consumer behavior, and international regulatory comparisons through a literature review approach.  The study’s results show that regulatory implementation weaknesses, low digital literacy, insufficiently standardized online dispute resolution mechanisms, and institutional enforcement and supervisory gaps remain important obstacles. Additionally, an overly rigid ex-ante regulatory approach has the potential to stifle digital innovation. Therefore, adaptive, participatory policy reformulation based on the principle of equitable consumer protection is needed.</jats:p>

title: Penguatan Literasi Keuangan Digital melalui Pelatihan Mobile Banking bagi Mahasiswa STEBIS IGM Palembang
container-title: ASPIRASI : Publikasi Hasil Pengabdian dan Kegiatan Masyarakat
9f7a35a06d60db177376efc6e5e9fcb3512b1ab9.abstract: <jats:p>This community service activity aimed to strengthen digital financial literacy among students at STEBIS IGM Palembang through mobile banking training for personal financial management. Conducted on October 12–13, 2026, the program involved 122 students and employed presentations, demonstrations, guided practice, assignments, and interactive discussions. The evaluation used a descriptive qualitative approach, collecting data through participatory observation, semi-structured interviews, and assignment documentation, which were analyzed thematically. The findings indicated that participants gained insights into using mobile banking transaction histories to identify spending patterns, monitor expenses, and understand the importance of financial records for personal budgeting. However, several challenges emerged, including cash transactions that were not automatically recorded, limited internet connectivity, and concerns regarding the security and privacy of financial data. These findings highlight the potential of practical mobile banking training as a contextual approach to improving students' understanding of digital financial management. Nevertheless, improvements in financial competence and sustained behavioral changes cannot be conclusively established without structured measurements and long-term follow-up evaluations.</jats:p>

title: HelloTalk as a Digital Communication Space for Korean Language Learning among Indonesian Users: A Qualitative Study
container-title: Jurnal Komunikasi dan Bisnis
7211c7a037ffadb4c89a904e25ac985b992b9a32.abstract: <jats:p>Digital media have become important communication spaces in which people learn foreign languages beyond formal classrooms. However, research on HelloTalk has largely concentrated on English learners and on pedagogical outcomes such as speaking skills and learner autonomy, and limited attention has been given to how Indonesian users experience HelloTalk as a communication space for learning Korean. This study examines how Indonesian users experience HelloTalk as a digital communication space for Korean language learning, using New Media Theory and Computer-Mediated Communication (CMC) as its analytical framework. A qualitative approach with a post-positivist paradigm was applied. Five Indonesian HelloTalk users who actively learn Korean were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation, and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, with source and technique triangulation. The findings show that informants experience HelloTalk as an interconnected, accessible, interactive, and open-ended space that enables them to communicate with native speakers, receive peer correction, share content, and learn flexibly across time and place. Within the CMC dimensions, informants emphasized wide access to information, fast message exchange, varied learning input, and motivation, while the perceived usefulness of the application depended on the intensity and purpose of use. Informants also reported constraints related to VIP features, time differences, and device limitations. The study argues that HelloTalk functions as a participatory digital communication space in which Korean language learning takes place through interpersonal interaction, peer correction, and user-generated content. The study does not measure language proficiency.</jats:p>

title: Digital Fraud and Psychological Blackmail Strategies: An Analysis of Scammers' Communications toward the Elderly via Social Media and Instant Messaging Apps
container-title: Jurnal Komunikasi dan Bisnis
6b23de3485dc7e026052ce411cddbd7c01178cd9.abstract: <jats:p>Online fraud targeting the elderly is one of the many types of cybercrimes that have emerged as a result of the expansion of digital media, which has also created a large communication area. This study examines the psychological blackmail and communication strategies employed by scammers in fraudulent activities involving phony lottery schemes through Facebook and the instant messaging software WhatsApp. To instill fear, trust, and cooperation in their victims, scammers use images of popular personalities or celebrities, stories of large lottery winnings, and threats of police involvement. This study employs a case study methodology and qualitative techniques, including data from interviews with senior victims and screenshots of online interactions. To find trends in message manipulation, the use of authority symbols, and fear-based persuasion strategies (fear appeals), data analysis is done through communication discourse analysis. The findings reveal that scammers employ a sequential communication strategy consisting of trust building, emotional engagement, authority construction, fear appeal, and psychological blackmail to manipulate older adult victims. These strategies are reinforced through Facebook and WhatsApp interactions, enabling scammers to create perceived legitimacy and urgency. The urgency and credibility of messages are reinforced by digital media. Understanding the communication weaknesses of older adults and the significance of digital literacy techniques in thwarting online fraud are two areas in which this research advances communication science and digital media studies.</jats:p>

title: Reorientasi Pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam di Era Digital: Membangun Etika Media Sosial Sejak Pendidikan Dasar
container-title: JUDIKDAS: Jurnal Ilmu Pendidikan Dasar Indonesia
da3b6f2cd5d1c360626b902d25443b9f5ed12c43.abstract: <jats:p>Perkembangan teknologi digital menghadirkan tantangan baru bagi pembentukan etika dan karakter murid sekolah dasar, terutama dalam komunikasi daring, penyebaran informasi yang belum terverifikasi, perlindungan privasi, dan respons terhadap perundungan siber. Kondisi ini menunjukkan adanya kesenjangan antara pemahaman nilai-nilai moral dalam pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) dan penerapannya dalam kehidupan digital sehari-hari. Penelitian ini bertujuan merumuskan kerangka konseptual reorientasi pembelajaran PAI yang mengintegrasikan nilai-nilai keislaman dengan pengembangan etika bermedia sosial pada murid sekolah dasar. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kepustakaan (library research). Data diperoleh dari lima buku dan 34 artikel jurnal yang diterbitkan pada 2021–2026, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan metode sintesis tematik melalui tahapan pengodean teks, pengembangan tema deskriptif, dan perumusan tema analitis. Hasil kajian menghasilkan empat dimensi reorientasi pembelajaran PAI, yaitu reorientasi tujuan, konten, metode, dan ekosistem pembelajaran. Reorientasi tujuan menekankan aktualisasi akhlak dalam interaksi digital; reorientasi konten mengintegrasikan nilai tabayyun, kejujuran, amanah, tanggung jawab, kesantunan, dan penghormatan terhadap privasi; reorientasi metode mengutamakan keteladanan, studi kasus, diskusi, refleksi, dan pembiasaan; sedangkan reorientasi ekosistem menekankan kolaborasi antara guru, sekolah, dan orang tua. Kerangka ini menempatkan etika digital sebagai bagian integral dari pengamalan nilai-nilai Islam, bukan sekadar keterampilan menggunakan teknologi. Penelitian ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan landasan konseptual pembelajaran PAI yang kontekstual dan adaptif terhadap perkembangan teknologi. Namun, kerangka tersebut masih bersifat konseptual sehingga memerlukan pengujian empiris untuk mengetahui keterlaksanaan dan efektivitasnya dalam membentuk perilaku digital murid sekolah dasar.</jats:p>

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
container-title: Digital Technologies Research and Applications
9846cab94a199e2bda9d30d406a36d92a6eb9deb.abstract: <jats:p>In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. Issues like management support, information accuracy, and departmental integration have a major impact on implementation. This study contributes to the theory of human-machine collaboration by proposing the concept of asymmetric algorithmic accountability, which captures the uneven distribution of organizational consequences for following versus overriding AI recommendations and shapes practitioner behavior in ways that extend beyond individual trust or algorithmic transparency.</jats:p>

title: Digital inventory management systems and the growth of agro farms in Cross River State, Nigeria
container-title: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
a953d89a1326db1f50a178d73681c34356685068.abstract: <jats:p>Digital technologies are increasingly promoted as a way to improve stock handling and coordination on farms, yet evidence from Nigerian agro farms is limited. This study examines how digital tools, mobile applications, and software systems for inventory control relate to the productivity, profitability, and market expansion of agro farms in Cross River State, Nigeria. A cross sectional survey was conducted between February and August 2025 under a positivist, hypothetico deductive approach. A structured questionnaire with five point Likert items was administered to owners and managers of registered crop, livestock, and mixed farms selected through stratified random sampling, yielding 364 valid responses from 450 distributed. Reliability and construct validity were assessed, and hypotheses were tested using multiple regression at the 5 percent level of significance. The results show that IoT systems and digital monitoring systems are positively associated with productivity, with a reported indirect effect through inventory accuracy. Mobile stock tracking applications, cloud based farm inventory systems, and barcode and QR code applications are positively associated with profitability. Web based inventory platforms and enterprise level digital supply chain software are positively associated with market expansion. The study concludes that digital inventory control systems can support agro farm growth and recommends regular staff training and reliable internet connectivity at farm locations. Because the design is cross sectional and relies on self reported measures, the findings indicate association rather than causation.</jats:p>

title: Can digital infrastructure construction promote the synergy between pollution and carbon reduction? A quasi-natural experiment based on the “Broadband China” pilot policy
container-title: Digital Economy and Sustainable Development
4e33fc9fce5e9f0a5c1119a81ddda5e0d312e71d.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Digital infrastructure (DI) presents a critical opportunity for China to address the dual challenges of climate change and environmental pollution. In this study, we empirically investigate the effects and mechanisms of DI on the synergy between pollution and carbon reduction (SPCR) using balanced panel data from 273 Chinese cities during 2011–2023. The results reveal that DI significantly reduces CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    and SO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    emissions, thereby promoting SPCR. The mechanism analysis shows that DI facilitates synergistic governance by limiting the entry of heavily polluting enterprises and increasing government expenditure on environmental protection. Heterogeneity analysis suggests that the synergistic effects of DI are more pronounced in cities with small and medium size, high digital innovation capacity, advanced economic development, and greater government digital attention. This study clarifies the micro- and macro-mechanisms through which DI empowers cities to achieve SPCR, and provides empirical evidence and policy implications for improving DI construction and promoting urban green transformation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Overstimulasi Digital dan Impulsivitas Verbal pada Anak Generasi Alpha: Analisis Pembelajaran Observasional
container-title: Jurnal Obsesi : Jurnal Pendidikan Anak Usia Dini
ec06fd276287e34323bd3ae6cf98e3180378edc3.abstract: <jats:p>Paparan media digital yang intens pada anak usia dini sering dikaitkan dengan lemahnya pengendalian diri, tetapi kajian tentang cara anak bertutur, khususnya tuturan spontan yang kurang terkendali, masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis keterkaitan overstimulasi digital dengan impulsivitas verbal pada anak Generasi Alpha melalui pembelajaran observasional dalam teori belajar sosial. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan desain studi kasus tunggal di sebuah lembaga pembelajaran anak usia dini. Informan anak, orang tua, dan guru dipilih secara purposif. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi terstruktur, wawancara semiterstruktur, dan dokumentasi, lalu dianalisis melalui reduksi, penyajian, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Ditemukan pola sulit mengendalikan respons saat penggunaan gawai dibatasi, tuturan tergesa-gesa, sulit menunggu giliran, menyela, suara meninggi, dan peniruan kata serta gaya bicara dari media digital. Pola tersebut lebih kuat pada akses mandiri atau pendampingan yang tidak konsisten dan lebih ringan pada akses terbatas yang diawasi. Keterkaitan itu bersifat kontekstual, bukan deterministik, dan dijelaskan oleh proses atensi, retensi, reproduksi, dan motivasi dimoderasi respons orang dewasa. Kebaruan penelitian ini terletak pada penghubungan paparan media sehari-hari dengan empat proses pembelajaran observasional, bukan dengan durasi layar semata. Temuan ini berkontribusi pada perluasan teori belajar sosial dan menjadi dasar pendampingan digital oleh orang tua dan guru.</jats:p>

title: ANALYSIS OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TUBE CURRENT-TIME (MAS) AND EXPOSURE INDEX IN DIGITAL CHEST RADIOGRAPHY
container-title: JHN: Journal of Health and Nursing
94ce1c92316108b4fe9a8e5c9424efa73580c4c0.abstract: <jats:p>Chest radiography is one of the most frequently performed radiological examinations, requiring optimization of exposure parameters to achieve adequate image quality while minimizing unnecessary radiation exposure. Milliampere-second (mAs) is an important exposure parameter that affects the quantity of X-ray photons reaching the detector and consequently influences image noise and Exposure Index (EI). This study aimed to analyze the effect of mAs variations on image noise and EI in digital chest radiography and to determine an appropriate mAs setting based on the relationship between these parameters. This quantitative experimental study used an anthropomorphic chest phantom and a digital radiography system. Seven mAs variations of 4, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, and 25 mAs were applied while maintaining a constant tube voltage of 80 kVp. Image noise was measured as the standard deviation (SD) of pixel values, while EI was recorded from the digital radiography system. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, normality testing, and simple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. The results showed that EI increased consistently with increasing mAs, from 285.44 at 4 mAs to 1,709.81 at 25 mAs. Regression analysis demonstrated a statistically significant positive effect of mAs on EI (F = 1009.928; p < 0.001), with a regression coefficient of 68.609, indicating an increase of 68.609 EI units for every 1 mAs increase. In contrast, noise values fluctuated across the mAs variations, ranging from 456.882 at 4 mAs to 170.658 at 16 mAs and increasing to 331.297 at 25 mAs. The effect of mAs variation on noise was not statistically significant (F = 2.782; p = 0.156).</jats:p>

title: Capitalization effects of digital infrastructure in Chinese cities: agglomeration, accumulation and technovation
container-title: Digital Economy and Sustainable Development
5011fa7dd1186dbbc5cfe62ef13d904862d0e626.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The construction of digital infrastructure requires substantial capital investment from both the government and private sector. A key question arises: to what extent do these investments contribute to economic growth and welfare? This paper investigates this issue through the lens of the capitalization effect. Specifically, we leverage China’s “Broadband China Pilot Policy” as a quasi-natural experiment in digital infrastructure development and employ panel data from 298 cities between 2010 and 2021. Using a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) approach with two-way fixed effects (TWFE), we empirically establish the presence of a significant capitalization effect. Furthermore, we examine several potential mechanisms associated with the capitalization effect, focusing on population agglomeration, capital accumulation, and technological innovation. The results provide suggestive evidence that these factors are potential channels through which digital infrastructure may affect urban housing markets. To quantify welfare implications, we construct a partial equilibrium framework and integrate an LSTM-based deep learning model for predictive analysis. Furthermore, our partial-equilibrium analysis provides a model-implied monetary assessment of the potential welfare implications of digital infrastructure investment, while acknowledging the limitations of interpreting housing-price capitalization as direct welfare gains. This study provides valuable insights for digital infrastructure investment decisions in developing countries.</jats:p>

title: PENGUATAN BRANDING DAN STRATEGI KOMUNIKASI DIGITAL PADA UMKM ARLIN GORDYN
container-title: PUBLICA: Jurnal Pengabdian Kepada Masyarakat
10f85344010615153de5766e29c521567da33f5d.abstract: <jats:p>Arlin Gordyn, an MSME (Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise) engaged in the sale and installation of curtains and interior products in Tanjung Mulia Village, Medan Deli District, has been in operation since 1998. However, its marketing has relied solely on customer recommendations and word-of-mouth. The business lacked an Instagram or TikTok presence, the skills to create promotional content, and an understanding of digital marketing communication strategies. This Community Partnership Service (PKM) initiative aimed to enhance the partner's capacity in digital branding, social media management, and the creation of promotional content. The implementation method included surveys and observations, outreach and hands-on training, mentoring, as well as monitoring and evaluation. The training covered setting up Instagram Business and TikTok Business accounts, developing a business profile and visual identity, designing content using Canva, and editing videos with CapCut. The project resulted in the establishment of Instagram and TikTok accounts (@arlin.gordyn), featuring 15 Instagram posts, 8 TikTok videos, and 5 Canva templates. At the time of evaluation, the Instagram account had 21 followers and the TikTok account had 7 followers; the partner was able to manage both accounts independently, with only limited ongoing support required for using Canva. This initiative demonstrates that hands-on, practice-based mentoring—utilizing the partner’s own product documentation—can effectively help an MSME build a digital identity. As the impact on the number of customers and total revenue has not yet been measured, further mentoring is recommended.</jats:p>

title: Digital Agency and the Preservation of the Banggai Language Among the Younger Generation in Banggai City
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
203e0b7e16a8585e4f923fc710185b1ccbabb730.abstract: <jats:p>Regional languages are essential components of cultural identity, serving not only as means of communication but also as vehicles for transmitting values, knowledge, and local wisdom across generations. Banggai, spoken in Banggai Laut Regency, has shown signs of declining use among younger generations in family and educational settings. Meanwhile, digital technology offers new opportunities for regional language use and dissemination. This study examines the forms, functions, and factors influencing Banggai language maintenance among young people in Banggai City through the perspective of digital agency, which views youth as active and creative users of digital technology. This qualitative case study involved 29 respondents who completed open-ended questionnaires and three informants who participated in in-depth interviews. Participants aged 15–30 years were purposively selected. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, with source and methodological triangulation. The findings show that 19 respondents use Banggai on social media, primarily in informal conversations with fellow speakers. However, none reported producing Banggai-language content or collaborating on content creation, while digital resources, such as dictionaries, were rarely used. Digital spaces help maintain language use and strengthen linguistic identity and pride, although their contribution to broader language use, learning, and intergenerational transmission remains largely potential. Key supporting factors include preservation motivation and family and school support. Major barriers include limited language use in families and communities, the influence of Indonesian and other languages, restricted vocabulary, social stigma, and scarce digital content and learning resources. Limited device and internet access were not reported as barriers. This study refines digital agency by distinguishing language-use agency from content-production and collaborative agency, highlighting the need for youth-driven digital resources supported by families, schools, and local governments.</jats:p>

title: The influence of FinTech adoption on sustainability performance: the mediating roles of financial inclusion and digital transformation
container-title: Future Business Journal
08facf143f3eca59ce0751c9634b06b3dd98fbf4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This research aims to analyze how FinTech adoption (FA), mediated by digital transformation (DT) and financial inclusion (FI), influences sustainability performance (SP) in Jordan’s commercial banking sector. The study focuses on bank managers as participants because they play key roles in managing FA, DT, and SP. Study collected 395 questionnaire responses sufficient for analysis using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in Smart PLS 4.0. The results showed that DT positively influences SP, suggesting that banks’ digital initiatives are important for advancing sustainable business practices. The study confirms that FA significantly drives both DT and FI. This indicates that integrating financial technologies improves banking services and supports the digital transformation of banking operations. The study confirms that FA directly and positively determines a bank’s SP. Moreover, the study highlights significant mediation, showing that both FI and DT positively affect banks’ SP and validating multiple pathways through which FinTech supports sustainable outcomes. The results also show that FA and FI cross multiple dimensions, enhance an institution’s SP, which is particularly relevant to managers and policymakers seeking to advance sustainable development through digital finance innovations.</jats:p>

title: Digital Technologies and Climate Change Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Emerging Trends and Research Directions
container-title: F1000Research
a13895b184d19495b5abce0182286be1aa3f7d28.abstract: <ns3:p>Abstract* Background Digital technologies offer new opportunities to support climate change education, yet the intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, and relationships between technological approaches, pedagogies, and educational objectives remain insufficiently characterized. This study maps the development of research on digital technologies for climate change education and identifies priorities for future investigation. Methods A bibliometric analysis was conducted using Scopus-indexed publications retrieved on 18 August 2026. The search strategy combined terms related to climate change education, climate literacy, and digital technologies. Following screening and eligibility assessment, 323 documents published between 2006 and 2026 were included. Bibliometrix and VOSviewer were used to examine publication characteristics, influential contributors, institutional and country contributions, scientific collaboration, keyword co-occurrence, thematic structure, and temporal research trends. Results The dataset comprised 323 documents from 179 publication sources, involving 1,141 authors. The analysis identified contributions from diverse institutions and countries, reflecting the interdisciplinary and internationally connected nature of the field. Keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed seven thematic clusters encompassing climate literacy and public understanding; technological and experiential learning; computational and interdisciplinary learning; adaptation and sustainability; communication and place-based applications; technology-supported pedagogy; and curriculum and teacher capacity. The thematic and temporal analyses highlighted connections between digital technologies, pedagogical approaches, and climate-related educational objectives. However, the network structure indicates conceptual associations rather than demonstrated educational effectiveness. Potential research priorities include integrating digital technologies with systems thinking, strengthening pedagogical frameworks for immersive learning, investigating artificial intelligence in climate literacy, and evaluating learning transfer and sustained climate-related action. Conclusions This study provides a bibliometric overview of digital technology research in climate change education and identifies opportunities for more theoretically grounded and empirically robust investigation. Future research should combine explicit instructional designs with multidimensional learning assessments, longitudinal evaluation, and attention to teacher readiness and equitable technology access.</ns3:p>

title: Strategic integration of business intelligence tools to enhance business management efficiency
container-title: Journal of Innovative Digital Transformation
f77e28ca3e93ad443c3d332c42ebba3bca186cc6.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how data and business intelligence (BI) systems support procurement decisions and strategic execution. It aims to improve the efficiency of business management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A five-stage implementation framework is proposed for integrating BI into strategic business execution. The methodology includes technical validation and a case study that assesses the impact of digital transformation and BI adoption on tracking strategic execution and key performance indicators (KPIs). We frame BI adoption within the broader digital transformation (DT) agenda, aligning data, processes and governance to strategic objectives.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Research shows that aligning digital transformation initiatives with an organization’s specific operational needs is the most cost-effective path to achieving efficiency. Analysis suggests that a successful digital transformation must be closely linked to the management requirements. Selecting appropriate BI tools is critical to delivering substantial business value.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The proposed framework offers managers a structured approach to implementing BI systems aligned with strategic goals. The case study provides actionable insights for professionals aiming to improve operational and management performance through data-driven strategies and digital transformation.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research contributes to the literature on digital transformation by presenting a structured, stage-gated framework for integrating BI tools into strategic management. It offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to enhance performance through data-informed decision-making, differentiating itself through a detailed implementation model developed and illustrated in a procurement context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: A Multi-Agentic Digital Twin Framework for Human-in-the-loop Workflows
33c4112ce8f41376749518d5fbcc523be8b8f15f.abstract: Traditional robot task planning struggles to recover from failures and changing requirements because it relies on predefined rules, labelled datasets, and limited state awareness. Digital twins provide real-time virtual representations of physical systems, while multi-agent systems support collaborative, stepwise reasoning. However, their integration for failure evaluation, requirement adaptation, and state-aware robot planning remains underexplored, particularly at the architectural level. This study proposes a multi-agentic digital twin framework for human-in-the-loop workflows, enabling bidirectional communication between machines, digital twins, and multi-agents. The framework is validated through robot task planning for an aerospace product-qualification metrology process. Results show that digital-twin integration adds 885-1,149 milliseconds to communication between robots and agents because continuous state updates are required. Multi-agent workflows need more human feedback than single-agent workflows to align outputs with predefined goals and mitigate hallucinations, highlighting the importance of human-in-the-loop orchestration. Datasets, logs, code, videos, results, and deployment instructions are available on GitHub 1 .

title: Digital health misinformation in Southeast Asia: a systematic review of susceptibility, public health consequences, and intervention evidence
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
00ce89db318a37339b109c74210ace406b59f2c2.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Digital health misinformation forms part of the information environment in which people assess health risks and act on health advice. We systematically reviewed participant-level studies from Southeast Asia addressing susceptibility, public-health consequences, and intervention evidence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We searched PubMed, Europe PMC, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus, supplemented by known reports from the original manuscript and publication-version checks. Prespecified eligibility criteria required primary empirical research involving Southeast Asian populations, an explicit health-misinformation focus, a documented digital connection, and participant-level outcomes. The search and selection process was reported according to PRISMA 2020. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT 2018). Heterogeneity in study designs, measures, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized narratively.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The searches identified 2,210 database records; 1,142 remained after deduplication. Including supplementary identification, 282 reports were sought, 147 were assessed in full text, and 77 reports were included, representing 74 conservatively grouped study populations. Country-attributable evidence came from Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, and Lao PDR; two further reports provided regional findings. Fifty-four reports concerned COVID-19. Appraisal and belief were associated with cognition, literacy, trust, identity, emotion, and social context, although measures and sampling differed considerably. Findings linked misinformation-related constructs with sharing, vaccine attitudes, preventive behavior, distress, and accounts of delayed care. Correction, inoculation, digital education, chatbots, and community responses produced heterogeneous findings; most interventions did not isolate a misinformation-specific behavioral effect.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Interpretation is limited by 135 unretrieved reports, a single assessment workflow without independent duplicate human screening, and predominantly observational evidence. The regional literature supports context-sensitive interpretation of exposure, appraisal, belief, and action; it does not establish a uniform causal pathway or a preferred intervention transferable across all settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Urban digital twins and digital twinning as a continuing planning practice
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Cities
30720abe2667b7e2067aff54baf12ff6d94a0e6a.abstract: <jats:p>Urban digital twins are increasingly used to support planning, policy, and urban governance, yet cities cannot be fully captured as stable digital representations. Building on existing understandings of digital twinning, this article argues for conceptualizing urban digital twinning as a continuing institutional planning practice. We distinguish the digital twin as a configured representational and analytical system from digital twinning as the broader practice connecting digital representation with interpretation, deliberation, governance, planning decisions, urban interventions, monitoring, institutional learning, and model revision across successive planning cycles. This perspective emphasizes the role of human judgment and institutional knowledge in responding to evolving urban conditions and planning uncertainty, offering a basis for more adaptive, transparent, accountable, and context-sensitive urban planning and governance.</jats:p>

title: Integrating digital financial solutions into MSME business models: assessment of MSME readiness for digital financial integration
container-title: Frontiers in Human Dynamics
c3fd986a83e2850542810b8550893597b8743b51.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital financial solutions has become essential for enhancing the sustainability and competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), especially in developing economies. This study examined MSME readiness in terms of digital capability, financial literacy, infrastructure readiness, and strategic orientation in relation to the integration of digital financial systems. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional research design, data were collected from 189 MSMEs in Surigao del Sur, Philippines, and analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation, and regression techniques. The findings revealed a strong positive relationship between MSME readiness and the level of digital financial integration. MSMEs with higher levels of readiness demonstrated greater improvements in business performance, operational efficiency, and financial stability, whereas those with lower levels of readiness gained only limited benefits. The results also indicated that full and systematic integration produced better outcomes than partial adoption. Overall, the study highlights that readiness is a key driver of successful digital transformation among MSMEs and emphasizes the need for targeted interventions to strengthen their capabilities and support sustainable digital finance adoption.</jats:p>

title: Navigating boundary-less work: how family-supportive leadership reshapes the impact of work-family blurring on professional women’s job engagement and taking charge in the digital transformation
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8b3dd731c66d9daf41a7cfb503ae5e2d2731352f.abstract: <jats:p>In the context of a digital transformation that is fundamentally refining the nature of work and leadership dynamics, this research examines the mediating role of job engagement and the moderating role of family supportive supervisor behavior in the relationship between work-family role blurring and taking charge. A moderated mediation model is constructed using boundary theory and work-family border theory as foundational frameworks. The data were collected from 275 professional women in China. Moreover, family supportive supervisor behavior which is a key manifestation of supportive leadership in the modern, boundary-less workplace moderates the relationship between work-family role blurring and job engagement. Additionally, moderated mediation results confirm that a higher level of family supportive supervisor behavior increases professional women’s taking charge level through the indirect effect of work-family role blurring via job engagement. The findings highlight that in an era of pervasive digital connectivity, cultivating family supportive supervisor behaviors is a crucial strategy for management to mitigate role blurring and enhance professional women’s proactive workplace behaviors. This study enriches our understanding of the underlying processes of taking charge by developing a more comprehensive model that integrates the challenges of digital-era work design with the resource-providing function of leadership.</jats:p>

title: P2-VGAN: a lightweight velocity-weighted graph attention network for privacy-conscious edge anomaly detection
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
fac05ecbc490866159a715e5c7029d4aa7f01789.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Two persistent challenges hinder intelligent video surveillance in public spaces: dense pixel-based models incur heavy computational costs on edge infrastructure, and continuous capture of identifiable imagery creates substantial visual privacy liabilities. Skeleton-based pipelines, which abstract each video frame into articulated landmark coordinates, support visual data minimization by discarding appearance information. However, conventional graph backbones weight joint trajectories uniformly across time, frequently confusing benign high-speed locomotion (such as sprinting for transit) with violent anomalies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper presents the Privacy-Conscious Velocity-Weighted Graph Attention Network (P2-VGAN; the prefix “P2” is retained as a legacy identifier designating privacy-conscious representation rather than a cryptographic guarantee), an efficient framework engineered for desktop-class CPU edge gateways. The pipeline decouples motion analysis from visual appearance by extracting 33 planar body landmarks via a single-shot pose estimator; the application does not intentionally store or transmit decoded RGB frames after pose extraction, ensuring downstream processing operates strictly on appearance-reduced pose coordinates. The primary contribution is the Velocity-Weighted Attention Mechanism (VW-AM), an ultra-lightweight gating module requiring only two shared parameters that converts inter-frame coordinate displacements into a bounded squared-displacement motion proxy. This proxy modulates node features prior to multi-head graph attention, directing message passing toward rapidly moving limbs while damping near-stationary joints. Trained under a weakly supervised Multiple Instance Learning objective with temporal smoothness and sparsity regularizers, P2-VGAN is evaluated across five random seeds on the ShanghaiTech Campus and a human-centric subset of UCF-Crime.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      On ShanghaiTech, the model achieves a frame-level AUC of 84.72 ± 0.28% with 1.81 M downstream trainable parameters (pose-extractor parameters excluded) and sustains 34.01 frames per second (FPS) on an Intel Core i7-10700 CPU without hardware acceleration. When compared directly with an identical Vanilla GAT backbone without gating (83.14 ± 0.39%), VW-AM provides an unconfounded +1.58% absolute AUC gain (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      = 0.00096). On the human-centric UCF-Crime subset (215 test videos), it attains 77.88 ± 0.35% micro-average AUC, with high-motion categories (Fighting, Assault) exceeding 82% AUC. Stepwise ablations document an incremental +2.52% gain from VW-AM over an adaptive ST-GCN baseline.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We position P2-VGAN as a Pareto-efficient framework for lightweight CPU surveillance, acknowledging that coordinate streams reduce visual surface exposure but do not eliminate biometric gait re-identification.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Self-efficacy and job burnout among early childhood physical education teachers: exploratory indirect associations through the negative compassion-fatigue domain and professional identity moderation
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
45e33cf99965e3fd1d8af976d0d050c0bcc225d3.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Early childhood physical education teachers work at the intersection of early childhood education and physical education, yet psychological factors associated with job burnout in this group remain underexamined. Guided by the Job Demands–Resources model, this study examined associations among self-efficacy, an exploratory negative-domain composite, professional identity, and job burnout, including an indirect association and moderation of the direct association.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional online survey using snowball sampling included 588 early childhood physical education teachers in Chengdu, China (555 women, 33 men; mean age = 26.12 years, SD = 5.77). Participants completed the Chinese short-form Teachers’ Sense of Efficacy Scale, an adapted 15-item Chinese compassion-fatigue questionnaire, the Chinese Maslach Burnout Inventory-Education Survey, and the Teacher Professional Identity Scale. An exploratory 10-item negative-domain composite was constructed from five burnout-related and five secondary traumatic stress (STS) items, excluding the five compassion-satisfaction items. Pearson correlations and PROCESS Models 4 and 5 were estimated, adjusting for age and gender. Indirect associations were evaluated using 5,000 bootstrap resamples.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Self-efficacy was negatively correlated with job burnout (r = −0.38,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001) and positively correlated with the negative-domain composite (r = 0.16,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001), which was also positively correlated with job burnout (r = 0.19,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001). The adjusted indirect association through the composite was positive (ab = 0.081, 95% CI [0.034, 0.143]) and opposed the negative direct association (B = −0.778,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001). Professional identity moderated the direct association (interaction B = −0.263,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001; ΔR
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      = 0.018), which was nonsignificant at low professional identity (B = −0.086, 95% CI [−0.260, 0.088]) and strongest at high professional identity (B = −0.422, 95% CI [−0.610, −0.234]).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Higher self-efficacy was associated with lower job burnout, and this negative association was stronger at higher levels of professional identity. The positive indirect association through the exploratory negative-domain composite was small and sensitive to its operationalization. Given the cross-sectional design and measurement limitations, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory statistical associations rather than evidence of causal mechanisms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: A Deepfake Detection Framework for Securing Facial Biometrics Using Attention-Based Deep Learning and Blockchain
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
5d91e2fc92d65212a87fa5d1bd630e1bbbdd24cf.abstract: <jats:p>Facial biometric authentication is widely deployed for identity verification, yet it is increasingly exposed to deepfakebased presentation and injection attacks and to large-scale breaches of centrally stored biometric templates. This paper proposes a deepfake-resilient facial biometric security framework that combines attention-based deep learning with blockchain technology. At registration, face images are pre-processed, augmented with a generative adversarial network (GAN), encoded by a convolutional neural network (CNN) with self-attention, and classified as real or fake by an artificial neural network (ANN). Only images classified as real are encrypted, bound to a unique user identifier and committed to a private blockchain through a cryptographic hash, whereas fake attempts are written to an immutable event log. At authentication, a fresh probe passes through the same pipeline and is verified by smart contracts that check the integrity of the registered commitment and the template similarity using zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), so that raw biometric features are never disclosed. We formalise the threat model, specify the architecture, the smart-contract interface and the security properties, and define an evaluation protocol based on the CIPLAB Real and Fake Face Detection and UTKFace datasets that covers detection accuracy, authentication error rates, adversarial robustness, demographic fairness and system overhead. The framework provides a basis for privacy-preserving, auditable and scalable facial authentication in digital identity management, financial services, healthcare and e-governance.</jats:p>

title: NuTwin: A Zero-Trust, Confidential Cloud Architecture for Real-Time Nuclear Reactor Digital Twins Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
635269ce8b16bf9071393a701bcaf2cf0b2e45a0.abstract: Real-time telemetry diagnostics and predictive anomaly tracking in nuclear reactor cores present a fundamental computational dilemma: high-fidelity numerical neutronics and thermal-hydraulics solvers are too computationally prohibitive for sub-second edge evaluation, whereas conventional black-box deep learning architectures violate physical conservation bounds and lack operational determinism. Simultaneously, transmitting safetycritical nuclear operational data to public cloud infrastructure introduces acute cyber-physical security vectors that breach strict operational air-gaps. This paper introduces NuTwin, a zero-trust, confidential cloud architecture designed for real-time nuclear reactor core digital twins. NuTwin couples a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) surrogate model—constrained directly by point reactor kinetics equations (PRKE) with six delayed neutron precursor groups and coupled thermal-hydraulic reactivity feedback—with hardware-enforced cryptographic isolation. Live operational telemetry, simulated via Python Point Reactor Kinetics (PyRK), is streamed over unidirectional mutual TLS (X.509) connections into AWS IoT Core and processed exclusively inside an ephemeral, attestation-verified AWS Nitro Enclave via an internal virtual socket (vsock) channel devoid of persistent storage or external network interfaces. Experimental validation demonstrates that NuTwin bounds the physical residual loss below 1.4 × 10−4 , achieves sub-second inference latency (42.8 ms per step), and guarantees zero data-leakage surface under zero-trust operational constraints. Index Terms—Digital twins, physics-informed neural networks, confidential computing, AWS Nitro Enclaves, point reactor kinetics, nuclear cyber-physical security, real-time anomaly detection.

title: Mapping the knowledge domain of internal control and information technology: a bibliometric analysis using CiteSpace
container-title: Digital Transformation and Society
4216d7d8e3fe5a7360a1fe1f90315b9d627104da.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study maps the knowledge domain of internal control and information technology (IC-IT) and traces how the intellectual foundations, thematic evolution and future research agenda of IC have evolved alongside digital technologies. The theoretical implications of these descriptive patterns are discussed for future theory development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using CiteSpace, the study analyses 1,222 publications and 43,092 cited references from the Web of Science Core Collection for 2005–2025. It conducts reference co-citation, author, country and institutional collaboration, cited journal, keyword co-occurrence and subject category analyses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings show that IC-IT research has evolved from compliance-oriented IC, risk management and internal audit toward technology-enabled and intelligent control systems. The field is grounded in accounting, auditing, information systems and management, with emerging themes including artificial intelligence, machine learning, blockchain, cloud computing, access control, audit automation and real-time monitoring.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study conceptualizes IC-IT as an integrated interdisciplinary domain and provides the first full-domain bibliometric mapping that crosses four traditionally isolated research streams. It identifies a three-stage evolution from compliance-oriented control toward technology-embedded and intelligent governance, showing how digital technologies are reorienting internal-control research toward new objectives, mechanisms, audit evidence and accountability systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Examining the digital divide for persons with aphasia: an evaluation of the accessibility of Australian health and government websites
container-title: Universal Access in the Information Society
54c45febd0b70afb165e91c60308c7d222570f00.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The Internet has transformed the way we access healthcare and information, yet barriers to digital inclusion remain for persons with disabilities. Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) promote equitable digital access for persons with disabilities, however, guideline adherence is inconsistent, and standards do not fully address the needs of individuals with communication disabilities. This study aimed to investigate whether high-use Australian health and government websites meet: (1) minimum (WCAG 2.2 Level AA) and comprehensive (WCAG 2.2 Level AAA) web accessibility standards, and (2) Novel Level of Success Criteria for persons with aphasia (communication disability).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Eleven Australian healthcare and government websites were selected based on usage. The homepage and one internal webpage of each website were evaluated using Accessible Web RAMP™. Each website was assessed for: (1) compliance with WCAG 2.2 Level AA and Level AAA standards, and (2) performance against Novel Level of Success Criteria for persons with aphasia.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>At WCAG 2.2 Level AA, 7 (64%) homepages and 8 (73%) internal webpages were not fully compliant. At Level AAA, 10 (91%) homepages and 11 (100%) internal webpages demonstrated violations, presenting potential accessibility challenges for persons with aphasia. Performance on the Novel Criteria demonstrated a similar trend in non-conformance. However, some websites demonstrated a reduced total number of violations. The majority of issues were concentrated within the perceivable principle.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A high proportion of selected high-use Australian health and government websites presented accessibility non-compliances across all levels of criteria, including the Novel Criteria. Despite some websites demonstrating fewer violations against the Novel Criteria, accessibility barriers remain prevalent. This highlights the importance of improving inclusive practices, strengthening regulatory compliances, and integrating cognitive and communication disabilities into digital accessibility standards.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: An attention-enhanced CNN-BiLSTM framework with confidence-gated inference for arrhythmia detection using ECG signals
container-title: Discover Computing
943d73a84a877a6a9c79f159c4c6fea324279df3.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Automated arrhythmia detection from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for early diagnosis and continuous cardiac monitoring. However, accurate classification remains challenging due to complex temporal dependencies in ECG waveforms and severe class imbalance, where clinically significant arrhythmias are underrepresented. To address these challenges, we propose an Attention-Enhanced CNN–BiLSTM framework with a Confidence-Gated Inference mechanism for ECG-based arrhythmia detection. The proposed model integrates a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to capture local morphological features with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to model long-range temporal dependencies in ECG signals. A temporal attention mechanism is employed to focus on diagnostically relevant segments of the signal. Additionally, a confidence-gated inference strategy is introduced to improve prediction reliability, particularly for minority classes. An extensive ablation study across 18 configurations is conducted to evaluate the contribution of temporal modeling, attention, and inference strategies. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 96.58% and a macro-F1 score of 86.05%. To ensure an unbiased evaluation free of test-set leakage, we further adopt a strict protocol in which all hyperparameters (
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$\gamma$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ,
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$\tau$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ) are selected exclusively on a held-out validation set; under this leakage-free protocol the model attains an accuracy of 96.74% and a macro-F1 score of 86.54% on the untouched test set. These findings demonstrate that integrating attention-driven temporal modeling with calibrated inference yields efficient arrhythmia classification on the MIT-BIH benchmark.
