AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
0cea04df1f33891ac6e61332b69e78c30652b6e1.abstract: <jats:p>News gathering, production, verification, and distribution have been reshaped—sometimes profoundly, sometimes quietly—by the growing presence of artificial intelligence and machine learning in broadcast operations. This chapter surveys the main areas where these technologies operate: automated news production, deepfake detection, audience analytics, recommender systems, and voice synthesis. It also examines ethical questions emerging in each domain. Drawing on recent scholarship across journalism studies, computer science, media ethics, and communication research, the chapter explores tensions between operational efficiency and journalistic integrity, between personalization and information diversity, and between AI-assisted verification and its vulnerability to synthetic content. A key theme is that productivity gains, though real, are not self-sustaining. Responsible deployment requires editorial oversight, effective governance, and transparent disclosure to audiences. The chapter concludes by outlining a research agenda for an information environment increasingly shaped by AI.</jats:p>

title: The Digital Transformation of Television Broadcasting Supported by Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
35b7dc9c798c6869d6eeb6921fd0c44c284f95bc.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the digital transformation brought about by artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in television broadcasting within a conceptual and critical framework. It discusses how processes such as content production, automation, scheduling, audience measurement and personalisation have been reorganised through data-driven systems. Furthermore, by assessing the impacts of algorithmicisation on editorial independence, public accountability, transparency, privacy and accountability, the study argues that the future of television broadcasting is shaped not only by technical innovation but also by institutional and ethical choices.</jats:p>

title: The Future of Television
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
bff6f50e054390e2c139c80e7fb45824d6ff514a.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are transforming the television and broadcast media industry by reshaping production workflows, distribution models, and audience engagement strategies. Intelligent systems are increasingly applied in automated content creation, smart studio operations, personalized recommendation services, and predictive audience analytics. These innovations enhance efficiency, reduce operational costs, and enable broadcasters to deliver more adaptive and customized viewing experiences across digital platforms. However, the growing integration of AI also raises important challenges related to ethical accountability, algorithmic bias, transparency, and workforce transformation. Human creativity, editorial judgment, and trust remain essential elements in ensuring responsible media practices. The future of television will depend on balancing technological innovation with human-centered values to build sustainable and socially meaningful broadcast ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Television Platforms
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
054cd1bab132b082e3e6a31810c1cc1a1ff38db7.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how artificial intelligence–driven algorithms on digital television platforms transform the processes of cultural production, distribution, and consumption within the media ecosystem. Focusing on Netflix as a case study, it analyzes how algorithmic recommendation systems structure content visibility, shape user preferences, and reorganize audience behavior through data-driven mechanisms. Drawing on sociological theories of power and cultural production, the study conceptualizes algorithms not merely as technical tools but as socio-technical actors that establish new regimes of visibility and control. In this context, the notion of the “algorithmic field” is proposed to explain how platform-based systems redefine power relations, mediate cultural hierarchies, and reproduce structural inequalities. The findings suggest that digital platforms operate as influential intermediaries that both organize and govern cultural circulation in contemporary media environments.</jats:p>

title: From Broadcast to Platform Power
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
0039e4646b5f12e04840a5816064712c21fdb48a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the transformation of Turkish television from a broadcast-centered system into a platform-based, datafied media ecology shaped by Netflix, BluTV, Exxen, and related streaming services. It argues that streaming in Turkey cannot be understood as a simple technological shift, because platforms entered a media system already defined by dizi exports, RTÜK regulation, broadcast scarcity, censorship pressures, and audience dissatisfaction with long-form television. Through case studies of The Protector, Ethos, BluTV, and Exxen, the chapter analyzes how platform commissioning, personalization, metadata, recommendation systems, and AI-assisted workflows reshape cultural visibility, editorial authority, and creative labor. The chapter also considers how state regulation and media capture complicate platform governance in Turkey. It concludes that Turkish television's future depends on balancing algorithmic efficiency, cultural specificity, regulatory pressure, and editorial responsibility.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence, Local Broadcasting, and the Logic of Innovation From the Periphery
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
993d09fe2a97e708c317641849a351071457e373.abstract: <jats:p>Drawing on a qualitative case study of Radio Kepulauan Seribu, this chapter examines how these tensions unfold within Indonesia's small-island broadcasting context. Rather than framing AI as a disruptive force that automates editorial work, the chapter advances the concept of guided augmentation, in which AI supports preparatory cognitive tasks while ethical judgment, contextual interpretation, and public responsibility remain human-centered. Through interviews and non-participant observation, the study demonstrates how AI adoption emerges from structural constraints, limited resources, and public service mandates rather than technological ambition. The findings challenge dominant, Global North–centric narratives of AI-driven media transformation by presenting small islands as sites of adaptive innovation and relational accountability. By reframing hybrid broadcasting as a stable, context-sensitive media configuration, the chapter contributes to broader debates on AI, ethics, and the future of broadcasting in community-oriented media ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Television
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
857bae5718eff00351eeae246d5c2a40314cac99.abstract: <jats:p>With the process of digitalization, television broadcasting has evolved into a data-driven, algorithmic structure through digital platform services. In this context, the use of artificial intelligence is regarded as a tool that increases efficiency in television broadcasting. However, gaining competitive advantage through algorithmic infrastructures and the commodification of viewer data create forms of algorithmic management. This study examines the transformation created by artificial intelligence in the field of television broadcasting through platformization shaped by data ownership, the reshaping of labor processes through automation, and algorithmic governmentality as the outcome of these processes. The fact that artificial intelligence produces transformations in relation to capital accumulation, labor regimes, data ownership, and ideological control makes it necessary to evaluate television broadcasting from a political-economic perspective.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Curatorial Shift
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
1559be582d93ad91c2a432d936327ea610496ff5.abstract: <jats:p>Television program scheduling has long been an exercise in editorial authority: decisions regarding which programs to air, when, and in what order have shaped viewer behavior, structured the revenue logic of commercial broadcasting, and reproduced the broader ideological and economic conditions of the broadcasting system. The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into broadcasting operations is restructuring this framework. Algorithmic tools are increasingly shaping audience forecasting, ad placement, content performance evaluation, and recommendation systems. Drawing on Raymond Williams' flow theory, gatekeeping theory, and platform capitalism, this chapter examines this transformation through the concept of algorithmic curatorial shift, the redistribution of editorial authority from human planning experts to algorithmic systems.</jats:p>

title: Personalized Broadcasting and Algorithmic Recommender Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
45211ebcedbc6bad1d33a282df18d35a0dac1227.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the digital transformation of television broadcasting through personalized broadcasting and algorithmic recommender systems. It aims to explain how television has evolved from a linear medium into a data driven, platform centered, and algorithmically organized environment. The study discusses the conceptual foundations of personalized broadcasting and the main types of recommender systems, including content based, collaborative, and hybrid models. The findings show that these systems are not merely technical tools for content discovery, but socio technical mechanisms that shape audience experience, engagement, content visibility, and cultural circulation. The Netflix case further demonstrates that algorithmic personalization has become a strategic force that restructures media economies, influences user preferences, and redefines contemporary broadcasting practices.</jats:p>

title: Watching What You Want
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
d1ff86b30e4ee238eb295d1fbf660002d7278fc2.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how algorithmic recommendation systems have become central to television broadcasting. Drawing on critical media theory, platform studies, and research, it argues artificial intelligence and machine learning reshaped relationships between broadcasters and audiences by shifting curation from human programmers to automated systems. It situates collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, and deep learning within debates on filter bubbles, cultural fragmentation, editorial responsibility, and the political economy of digital media. Treating recommendation as a categorical transformation, it addresses ethics, including transparency, bias, and viewer autonomy, reviews regulatory and self-governance frameworks, and outlines future trends such as emotion-aware AI and cross-platform personalization.</jats:p>

title: AI, Television News, and the Future of Democratic Gatekeeping
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
3ee3b8c7e6d4280704c4999714e0509349e034cd.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is increasingly shaping television news production by influencing how stories are selected, prioritized, and targeted to audiences. While AI offers efficiency and data-driven decision-making, it also raises concerns about democratic gatekeeping in broadcast journalism by challenging traditional ideas of editorial judgment, accountability, transparency, and pluralism. This chapter examines how AI reshapes gatekeeping in television news by shifting decisions from human editors to hybrid human-AI systems. Drawing on gatekeeping theory and journalism studies, it explores issues such as algorithmic opacity, automation bias, and reduced diversity in news coverage. The chapter argues that without proper governance, AI-assisted gatekeeping may weaken the democratic role of television news. To address these concerns, it proposes a framework for democratic gatekeeping in AI-assisted television news based on transparency, human oversight, editorial responsibility, and pluralism, offering guidance for integrating AI into news workflows.</jats:p>

title: The Transformation of News Discourse in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
8e94f02ed0fdcf254c98a1451e802610a07e5039.abstract: <jats:p>In the digital media ecosystem, AI-based text generation systems, particularly large language models, have become increasingly influential in news production processes. These systems are viewed not only as technical tools but also as new mechanisms of discourse production that reshape how news content is created. This development has made the comparative examination of human-produced and AI-generated news texts increasingly important. In this context, the study comparatively analyzes news texts selected from international news organizations such as Al Jazeera and Reuters alongside texts generated by ChatGPT. The research focuses on military interventions and violent incidents in Palestine. Using document analysis as a qualitative research method, the study evaluates the texts through Teun A. van Dijk's Critical Discourse Analysis approach and identifies major differences between human-produced and AI-generated news texts in terms of discourse structure, framing strategies, linguistic choices, and meaning production practices.</jats:p>

title: The Role of Socially Responsible Marketing in the Context of Sports Management
container-title: Creative Advantage of Cultural Diversity in Global Business
b8a75b6c08f33c388a3b0280b3d2f7cae4a5bb6b.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the role of socially responsible marketing within sports management through a case study of Vitória Sport Clube, analyzing the effects of social responsibility initiatives on supporters' perceptions. The main objective is to understand how Vitória SC's socially responsible marketing practices influence pride, identification, reputation, and intentions to support, while clarifying the mechanisms through which these effects occur. A qualitative, exploratory–descriptive approach is adopted, supported by an integrative review of the literature and a semi-structured interview with a former executive responsible for the social domain, employing thematic analysis and documentary integration of the data. The findings highlight the strategic centrality of social responsibility in the club, expressed through alignment with community and environmental causes.</jats:p>

title: AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: “Friendship” and “Love” With Companion Robots
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
022fceef735cce777f0d8dacf51096f466dfc905.abstract: <jats:p>The emergence of companion robots introduces profound questions about the nature of human relationships, specifically regarding friendship and love. Unlike conventional machines, these robots are designed to provide emotional support, social interaction, and even intimacy, blurring the boundaries between human and artificial companionship. This paper explores the psychological, ethical, and societal implications of forming such bonds. It investigates the drivers behind these attachments including loneliness, accessibility, and advances in AI realism and examines whether these relationships can be considered authentic. The study also assesses potential benefits, such as improved mental well-being, alongside challenges like dependency, ethical concerns, and broader societal acceptance. By analyzing theoretical frameworks, real-world applications, and future trajectories, this work offers a holistic understanding of how companion robots are reshaping fundamental human experiences like friendship and love in contemporary life.</jats:p>

title: Human Socialization (and Dis-Socialization) by AI and Robotic Companions in Educational Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
21e354c94bb2573462d54359bd698db08de31a01.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter interrogates how AI chatbots, social robots, and ambient agents function as companion technologies that reconfigure human socialization and dis-socialization in educational ecosystems. Drawing on socialization theory, ecological systems, sociocultural mediation, sociomaterial assemblages, and posthuman subjectivity, it constructs a multi-level lens spanning micro interactional dynamics, meso institutional architectures, and macro political economies. The chapter develops typologies of companion configurations, maps learner needs to companion affordances, and analyses interactional quality through constructs such as social presence, parasociality, and epistemic justice. It then articulates normative, rights-based, and governance frameworks that distribute responsibilities across learners, educators, institutions, vendors, regulators, and civil society. The chapter positions humane companionable education as an agenda that seeks to harness machine companionship for inclusion and flourishing while resisting surveillance, stratification, and civic erosion.</jats:p>

title: Aesthetics of Robotic Digital Pets
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
7e635f747fbbe5476f902f978891bbe7c498f00f.abstract: <jats:p>Robots designed to replace pets are being developed to meet the emotional, social and cognitive needs of different age groups, from children to seniors. This chapter analyzes the factors that influence people's perception of robotic pets as companionable and socially present, focusing on shape aesthetics and motion quality, sound quality and textural effects and behavioral patterns. By examining the history of how humans have created and used artificial beings, it also becomes possible to understand how aesthetics has been viewed in the past and how it continues to shape expectations for the future. User expectations regarding the design of artificial pets, as well as the personalization of these products, are shown to influence acceptance and engagement. Understanding the role of aesthetics in the development of artificial pets therefore supports the creation of ethical and meaningful companions within contemporary and global society.</jats:p>

title: Emotional and Social Intelligence in AI Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
6a2e01dfa5708795013bf97dce0351890b7ec891.abstract: <jats:p>As artificial intelligence increasingly engages emotional and social dimensions of human life, its ability to recognize and respond to emotion raises important ethical and philosophical concerns. This chapter examines the development of emotional and social intelligence in AI, highlighting the shift from rational computation toward affective interaction. Drawing on cognitive psychology, affective computing, and moral philosophy, it explores whether machine empathy reflects genuine understanding or performative simulation. The discussion addresses risks such as emotional surveillance, manipulation, dependency, and cultural misrecognition, while acknowledging benefits of emotionally responsive AI in education, healthcare, and assistive contexts. To address ethical gaps, the chapter proposes a Computational Compassion Framework (CCF) integrating moral intentionality, transparency, human oversight, and contextual sensitivity into AI design. It argues that the future of emotional AI lies not in humanizing machines, but in embedding ethical responsibility within technological systems.</jats:p>

title: Iron Man or Tin Man?
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
739e5ce062b70ab12c4e4d9faa2f7e77bf9b8104.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence and robotics are no longer distant technologies but intimate infrastructures of everyday life, shaping how humans think, decide, feel, and relate to time, data, and one another.Drawing on cultural allegories (the Tin Man as the loss of emotional agency, Iron Man as the promise and peril of augmentation, In Time as a warning about the commodification of time, and the contemporary data economy where habit itself becomes a product) this chapter argues that the central challenge of AI is not technological capability, but human capacity. Through interdisciplinary perspectives from communication studies, psychology, and critical AI ethics, the analysis reveals how persuasion, efficiency, and optimization quietly reshape human behavior without overt coercion. Rather than asking whether machines can become more human, this chapter reframes the question: can humans remain reflective, empathetic, and morally responsible in systems designed for speed and prediction?</jats:p>

title: The Human Side of Robotic Warehousing
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
49ef72dbd7010ac0048e4e4ae894fc8d134c1a59.abstract: <jats:p>The chapter explores the perceptions of employees working in Amazon's Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems (RMFS). We used a netnographic approach to uncover employees' perceptions related to the use of this technology, as well as the social and ethical considerations related to the topic. The results of the study show several advantages perceived by the employees in terms of flexibility, improved picking rates, and ergonomics at work. Nevertheless, numerous risks and challenges emerged from the qualitative analysis conducted specifically in relation to job security and human-machine interaction. The results and analyses offer us several perspectives regarding the automation and robotization of workspaces in relation to employees' perceptions and social considerations.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Emotion, Social Intelligence, and Culture in Robotic Companions
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
11b5a43f16d9978c902b26af103395a866acf26f.abstract: <jats:p>The chapter discusses how emotional, social and cultural intelligence can be integrated into the design of robotic companions and their importance in promoting authentic, empathetic and adaptive human-machine relationships. It explores theoretical assumptions, technology methods, and examples of the application of emotional recognition, social adaptability, and cultural sensitivity. The most notable challenges mentioned in the discussion include ethical dilemmas, trust, and cross-cultural differences, as well as determine the way forward as influenced by affective computing, cultural AI, and large language models. Finally, the chapter encourages an integrated system that incorporates human compassion and machine predictability to increase emotional resonance, inclusivity, and universal acceptance in human socialization with AI.</jats:p>

title: Ethical Dimensions of Companion Bots, Intelligent Devices, and Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
3244f1bc2f7abb55a5b6321434f09e48bbe95961.abstract: <jats:p>Companion bots and emotionally responsive AI systems integrate deeply into daily life, managing social interactions, emotional support, learning, and care. Unlike standard computational tools, they maintain ongoing relationships and mimic empathy, transforming perceptions of companionship, autonomy, and moral responsibility. They deliver key benefits like alleviating loneliness, advancing healthcare, and customizing education, but raise ethical issues around authenticity, dependency, privacy, manipulation, and accountability. This chapter explores these ethics through philosophy, human-computer interaction (HCI), psychology, and policy lenses. It contends that evaluations must go beyond utility to examine effects on human dignity, moral agency, and social values. Principles for ethical design, governance, and deployment follow, emphasizing human well-being amid AI companionship's moral stakes .</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Quality Assurance in Higher Education
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
fb5843c135ec13caf51a5f619643fd47db8d0fec.abstract: <jats:p>In today's dynamic landscape of higher education, institutions must prove to society the societal benefits of their teaching, learning, and research. Many organizations are embracing AI-enabled quality assurance (QA) to foster a mindset of constant growth and outstanding performance inside their institutions. This approach aims to enhance education, cater to the requirements of students and communities, and ultimately help them stay competitive. The complex quality assurance system is open to multiple interpretations and potential improvements due to the interconnected nature of technology in higher education. Excellence requires continuous institutional growth. It is common for stakeholders to see quality assurance as too bureaucratic. To prioritize institutional change and ongoing improvement, modern QA frameworks should use organic and dynamic operating methods.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Digital Platforms for Learning-Centred Quality Assurance in Higher Education
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
2e6b9dfed2d61a7b891e8850e05ec19839ab8002.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter theorises AI-enabled digital platforms as socio-technical quality infrastructures that orchestrate learning, accountability, and equity in higher education. It fuses constructs from quality theory, learning sciences, organisational studies, and critical datafication to recast quality as holistic capability formation rather than performance compliance. The chapter outlines competing quality lenses, sketches platform typologies and algorithmic logics, and shows how governance architectures and stakeholder attitudes co-produce datafied regimes of merit and risk. It then advances design principles for learning-centred, justice-responsive AI ecosystems that foreground equity-sensitive analytics, participatory governance, and reflexive professional judgment. The chapter contends that AI must be treated as pedagogical and civic infrastructure, with human actors retaining epistemic primacy in steering quality work toward rigorous, inclusive higher education.</jats:p>

title: Quality by Design
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
99a02b8d40ae031ce9afe816538422b86464b6b0.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter focuses on how AI and digitalisation are affecting assurance and improvement activities within Higher Education and how the concept of Quality by Design (QbD) can help integrate AI technologies, automated governance, and advanced analytics into institutions' processes and workflows. It contends that the digital university must undergo both a technological and cultural transformation, moving away from a compliance-driven model of quality evaluation and moving toward a model focused on intelligent, seamless assurance. The AI-Enabled Quality Ecosystem Model is designed and offered as a means of accomplishing this aim as it integrates the appropriate data infrastructure, AI-augmented human supervision, and mechanisms for continuous improvement. The chapter draws on ethical, digital, participatory governance frameworks and on the role of AI as a complement to human judgment to advance the argument that AI enhances institutional quality and integrates the key institutional elements of leadership, inclusiveness, and collaborative, adaptive learning.</jats:p>

title: Digital Assurance Ecosystems
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
ea5f0137283fa7bf65376788b0b0b8d6da893fc2.abstract: <jats:p>The high pace of digitalization of higher education has changed the quality assurance to a standard data-based institutional process instead of a long-term and compliance-based process. The chapter focuses on the digital assurance systems based on artificial intelligence, analytics, and integrated platforms as the means to facilitate the continuous quality improvement within the higher education sector. It discusses the role of AI-driven dashboards, learning analytics, predicting models, and feedback loops in the process of coming up with good decisions in the areas of teaching, learning, governance, and accreditation. Quality by Design is highlighted in which quality is actively incorporated by tracking on time, detection of risks at early stages, and remedies. It discusses the stakeholder involvement, institutional benefits, ethical issues, and case studies of AI-based quality monitoring and student success management in the near past, and hence digital platforms would be the solution providers of quality assurance systems in the future.</jats:p>

title: Next-Generation AI Architectures for ECG Arrhythmia Detection
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
c06f20ff59b2a1a32fbb1574e77b84f20954089e.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized cardiac healthcare by enabling rapid, accurate, and automated arrhythmia detection using electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. This chapter explores advanced AI-driven arrhythmia classification techniques that integrate deep learning (DL), preprocessing, and explainable model interpretation. Emphasis is placed on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent networks, and hybrid architectures capable of learning morphological and temporal ECG features. The proposed framework covers data acquisition, filtering, segmentation, feature extraction, model training, and validation. Ethical challenges, interpretability, and clinical deployment frameworks are discussed. By bridging computational intelligence with clinical expertise, AI systems have demonstrated near-cardiologist-level diagnostic accuracy, making them vital in next-generation cardiac care.</jats:p>

title: Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: Governing AI-Driven Universities in Cambodia
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
1c876c30e971c0906955347a760678450910f5f3.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter focuses on Cambodian higher education institutions to explain the pillars of Trust-Centred AI Governance for responsible AI and how AI can support services and functions currently burdened by demand and under-resourced in the Cambodian higher education sector, which is rapidly growing and flexible in enrollment. Without governance, the Threats to Educational Equity caused by algorithmic bias, Data Breaches, Digital Exclusion, and Breaches of Trust will dangerously flourish. This chapter presents a Trust-Centred AI Governance Framework built around seven principles: ethical leadership, transparency, and data privacy. It is supported by core ideas such as algorithmic accountability, inclusive access, human oversight, and public-sector innovation, and guides partner institutions on fostering ethical innovation ecosystems. It presents, through analyses and the implementation of proposed strategies, case studies, and policy frameworks, a model that balances technological efficiency with human-centred principles, empowering global competence and leadership in the south.</jats:p>

title: From Knowledge Transmission to Democratic Transformation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
14a3b3c15207f76fff58adce5bfb961062efee1c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapidly evolving context of digitalisation, democratic fragility, and educational inequality has highlighted the need to change conventional teacher education practices that focus on transmission of knowledge and skills. Although teacher identity is a key concept in contemporary educational reform discussions that focus on inclusion, digital innovation and democratic citizenship, the concept is still fractured in policy, curriculum and governance. This research faces this challenge and critically explores the changing landscape of teacher education in terms of reconstructing the teacher identity as a multidimensional and transformative professional construct to support democratic transformation. In this study, the doctrinal and analytical research methodology is used, which systematically reviews and synthesizes the current educational theories, international policy instruments, governance models, and scholarly debates on inclusive education, digital pedagogy, democratic citizenship and professional development.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Internet of Things and Artificial Intelligence for the Development of Sustainable, Intelligent, and Efficient Physical–Digital Learning
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
26c5b42ef86ad41f27f523603793d198bf2cb6ce.abstract: <jats:p>The application of the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) is driving towards a new era of intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable smart campus ecosystems in higher education institutions. This research aims to examine the potential of IoT-powered physical–digital learning environments and AI systems in the fields of personalized learning, intelligent campus management, predictive analytics, and sustainable resource optimization. The study also explores the opportunities and challenges associated with the application of AIoT technologies for enhancing operational efficiency, learner participation, and environmental sustainability, as well as those of cybersecurity, data privacy, interoperability, and ethical governance. The results emphasize the need to implement human-centered, secure, and sustainable technological frameworks to empower future-ready universities and foster inclusive, efficient, and resilient educational ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Shadows in the Lecture Hall
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
66561a07cf91a6cd744b035edb6f73babf583b22.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence has rapidly transitioned from a supporting tool to a central force in academic research, teaching, and institutional governance. Its capacity to process vast datasets, generate scholarly content, and enhance decision-making offers unprecedented opportunities for innovation. Universities now employ AI to streamline administrative operations, improve academic workflows, and enable personalized learning experiences. In research, advanced algorithms and large language models facilitate literature synthesis, data interpretation, and even hypothesis generation, thereby accelerating scholarly output. This chapter advances the argument that the future of academia depends on striking a careful equilibrium between embracing AI's transformative power and preserving the foundational principles of truth, fairness, and accountability. It proposes a framework for “Responsible AI in Academia” grounded in transparency, inclusivity, and continuous ethical evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Responsible AI Governance Frameworks for Intelligent Higher Education Management and Creative Public Sector Innovation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
99d99fa7c05bdbaa0acde5b32467be06597babd5.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines responsible AI governance for intelligent higher education management and public-sector innovation. It highlights the importance of ethical AI, governance transparency, institutional readiness, stakeholder AI literacy, and sustainability-oriented governance in AI-enabled ecosystems. The study proposes a conceptual governance framework integrating ethical oversight, intelligent decision-support systems, governance interoperability, and adaptive governance mechanisms. The chapter also discusses governance challenges associated with generative AI, including algorithmic bias, explainability, misinformation, and compliance risks. The findings emphasize that responsible AI governance supports sustainable institutional transformation, public trust, accountability, and human-centred innovation across higher education and public-sector environments.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Adaptation and Leadership in AI-Augmented Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
a5612c037c0c5391ee895bba1a4fc5ae65f530b1.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI poses pressing governance challenges regarding the future of human-AI interaction and how it enhances or diminishes the cognitive capabilities, professional role, and leadership of academic professionals. Three cognitive adaptation patterns emerge from the analysis of the qualitative data (retrieved from the interviews) and the quantitative data (PLS-SEM survey): AI Augmentation, AI Dependency, and AI Co-construction. The positive relationship between adaptation outcomes and AI trust is supported by PLS-SEM, with the cognitive load change as a mediator and the organisational learning orientation as a moderator, the most significant institutional factor influencing adaptation outcomes. The chapter suggests embedding metacognition and AI literacy in workforce governance, institutional reflection in HR and L&D processes, and complementarity guardrails. For practical governance tools for adopting responsible AI in higher education, a validated diagnostic instrument and a Human-AI Capability Convergence Model are provided.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Academic Governance in the AI Era
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
e49d653e589a416eb7de0e2ea2a3cdd823c5f09a.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI (GAI) has rapidly become an integral part of higher education, significantly reshaping the teaching, learning, assessment, and research experiences of institutions around the globe, thereby creating unprecedented moral, legal, and governance dilemmas. Academic honesty and honour codes, which typically aimed to combat cheating and plagiarism in human-powered settings, are no longer adequate to deal with the challenges of AI-enabled environments. The study critically reviews the current paradigm of academic governance in the context of the emergence of generative AI and addresses the interplay of institutional honour codes, ethical responsibility, accountability systems, and regulatory compliance in higher education institutions. The research is done by a doctrinal, interdisciplinary and policy-oriented approach, analysing new institutional polices on AI, international ethical guidelines, university governance frameworks, data protection laws, and current academic discussions on responsible use of AI in academia.</jats:p>

title: AI Governance in Academia
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
82978771df486b7a50f02bfe7e3688784c7559c6.abstract: <jats:p>The ability to add artificial intelligence (AI) to higher education institutions in the entire public sector has opened up never-before opportunities to personalised learning, administrative efficiency and evidence-based policy-making. However, such opportunities are kept in company with serious governance issues that relate to transparency, fairness and institutional accountability. The chapter examines ethical strains that are inherent in utilisation of AI systems in the evaluation of students, collection of admission details, and distribution of resources, and argues that without the presence of robust governance architectures these systems have a risk of entrenching the existing inequalities and also eroding democratic educational values. The chapter is based on a multi-layered governance model which incorporates regulatory compliance, stakeholder participation, algorithmic auditing, and continuous ethics oversight.</jats:p>

title: Plant-based natural products against multidrug-resistant cancers: mechanisms of apoptosis induction and cell cycle modulation with a focus on breast cancer
container-title: Comptes Rendus. Chimie
ef54d246b98269416642f8936b151f50d7397197.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Breast cancer (BC) is a frequently diagnosed cancer in women worldwide and imposes a significant burden on healthcare systems. Although chemotherapy remains a primary treatment modality, its efficacy is often compromised by multidrug resistance (MDR), leading to poor clinical outcomes and treatment failure. Multidrug resistance in BC arises through multiple mechanisms, including decreased apoptotic activity, overexpression of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters, alterations in the tumor microenvironment, enhanced DNA repair capacity, and epithelial–mesenchymal transition. Conventional chemotherapeutic agents such as doxorubicin and paclitaxel are effective against BC cells; however, their clinical utility is limited by MDR, severe side effects including cardiotoxicity and neuropathy, and reduced efficacy in resistant tumors. To address these challenges, natural products interfere with resistance mechanisms through diverse pathways, inhibiting efflux pumps such as P-glycoprotein, restoring apoptosis, and modulating signal transduction pathways, including PI3K/Akt and NF-
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>κ</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    B. Furthermore, they induce autophagy, inhibit unregulated cell growth, and modify the tumor microenvironment to enhance therapeutic response. Compounds such as curcumin, silybin, apigenin, berberine, matrine, and
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>β</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    -elemene have been shown to improve the effectiveness of chemotherapy, whether used as monotherapies or in combination with conventional drugs, while exhibiting minimal side effects compared to synthetic medicines. In conclusion, secondary metabolites derived from plants possess significant potential to overcome MDR in breast cancer. Their ability to attack resistance-related mechanisms through multiple pathways not only enhances the effectiveness of current therapy but also offers a promising source of safer and more effective anticancer agents.
                  </jats:p>

title: Improving CommonGround, an Online Peer Support Intervention for People Living With Long-Term Physical Health Conditions and Subthreshold Depression: Theory of Change–Informed Qualitative Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
590525e4319b41b895c89aaf36dad4b53e1e076e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>People living with long-term physical health conditions who are also experiencing subthreshold depression are at risk of developing major depression. In partnership with lived experience experts, clinicians, and software developers, we co-designed CommonGround, an online peer support and psychoeducation platform. CommonGround’s Theory of Change (ToC) was also conceptualized to outline the intermediate outcomes (and associated indicators of whether such outcomes are achieved) needed to improve the mental health of the target population.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This qualitative study, informed by the ToC, aimed to examine the acceptability, usability, and intervention mechanisms of CommonGround and ultimately refine the ToC and corresponding intervention design ahead of definitive evaluation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A nested qualitative study was conducted within a remote, 12-week feasibility randomized controlled trial comparing CommonGround (intervention group) to signposting to National Health Service (NHS) web pages (control group). Thirty-nine participants were purposively sampled and interviewed within 6 weeks postintervention about their experiences of CommonGround and trial participation. The interview schedule and thematic framework analysis were rooted in a pretrial ToC while being responsive to emergent themes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Evaluating the assumptions and intermediate outcomes (via their indicators) refined our understanding of how CommonGround may support mental well-being. Overall, participants viewed CommonGround as an appropriate, safe space to access self-management information and support from others with a unique shared understanding of chronic illness. However, many participants felt more time was needed for genuine social relations to form and community culture to evolve. Anonymity helped foster a sense of safety but, for some participants, limited the formation of genuine connections. Other factors contributing to low engagement included personal circumstances (eg, limited time). Key suggestions for future development included creating a mobile app that would be easier and more intuitive to access and navigate.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CommonGround was considered an acceptable and appropriate space to access peer support, with the potential to positively impact psychological well-being by fostering shared understanding, support, and knowledge exchange. Beyond informing the future evaluation of CommonGround in a definitive trial, the refined ToC identifies the key preconditions, intermediate outcomes, and associated indicators, and assumptions that may underpin the acceptability and usability of digital peer support interventions in achieving their intended outcomes. We also demonstrate how evaluating and refining components of the ToC after the intervention had been implemented in the trial enabled a more nuanced understanding of how and why the intervention may work, for whom, under what circumstances, and informed changes to improve the co-designed intervention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Evaluation of the Clinical Utility of Circulating Tumor DNA in the Management of Patients With Nonmetastatic Head and Neck Cancer: Protocol for a Prospective Bicentric Study (CIRVAD)
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
b1976b53ee2bea23d592bc1ffbc200075b05520c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Human papillomavirus (HPV)–negative head and neck cancers, often linked to tobacco and alcohol exposure, have a poor prognosis and high recurrence rates. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a promising biomarker for detecting minimal residual disease and monitoring treatment response. Recent studies show that ctDNA can detect recurrence earlier than clinical or radiological methods. Prospective trials are needed to validate its clinical utility.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The primary objective is to assess postoperative ctDNA as a predictor of 28-month progression-free survival. Secondary objectives include evaluating ctDNA levels before and after treatment as predictors of recurrence, studying ctDNA dynamics during follow-up in relation to survival, and exploring their association with tumor characteristics and surgical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This prospective, bicentric study evaluates ctDNA in patients undergoing surgery for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Plasma ctDNA concentrations will be measured quantitatively in ng/mL before and 1 to 2 weeks after surgery, with or without adjuvant radiotherapy or chemotherapy. Progression-free survival is defined as the time from surgery to disease progression or death, and recurrence-free survival as the time to clinically confirmed recurrence. Overall and disease-specific survival will also be assessed. Changes in ctDNA levels over follow-up and clinical characteristics will be compared between patients with and without progression at 28 months. Absolute and relative variations in ctDNA preoperatively and postoperatively will be described, and surgical quality will be evaluated according to resection margins (R0, R1, R2).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As of August 2026, study preparation, including protocol development and methodological validation, has been completed. The study is currently entering the implementation phase, with regulatory procedures, funding applications, and site initiation activities underway. No participants have been recruited at the time of manuscript submission, as recruitment has not yet begun. Recruitment is expected to start following regulatory approval and funding acquisition. The funding status remains pending as of August 2026, with funding applications underway. Participant recruitment and data collection are projected to take approximately 24 months, followed by a 28-month follow-up period. Data analysis has not yet started and will be conducted after completion of the follow-up period. The first study results are therefore expected to become available after the completion of data collection and follow-up, although a precise publication timeline (season/year) cannot yet be determined.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to provide key data on the potential of ctDNA to detect early recurrence in HPV-negative cancers and could inform personalized patient monitoring and management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy–Based Digital Interventions for Illicit Substance Use Disorders: Scoping Review of Intervention Design, Efficacy Indicators, and Methodological Gaps
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
9d1858cff34c91ccfc45c7d996e799804ca90d99.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Illicit substance use disorders (SUDs) are escalating globally; yet, social stigma and legal barriers restrict access to conventional treatment, and existing research remains skewed toward alcohol and nicotine. Digital interventions incorporating cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) offer a discreet, scalable alternative.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review maps how CBT-based digital interventions for illicit SUDs are designed and delivered across platforms, identifying their theoretical frameworks, functional components, outcome indicators, and reported methodological limitations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) scoping review methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews). Six databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycINFO, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL) were searched from inception to June 28, 2026, without language, date, or study design limits, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching (July 3, 2026). Eligible studies were empirical primary studies quantitatively evaluating digital interventions incorporating CBT for illicit or nonprescribed substance use; alcohol- or nicotine-only populations were excluded. Three reviewers independently screened and charted all studies, with disagreements resolved by consensus or adjudication. Data were synthesized narratively, with tables, figures, and an evidence gap map.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Fifty-six studies published between 2008 and 2026, drawn from 47 distinct participant samples, met the eligibility criteria. Most were conducted in North America (40/56, 71.4%) and used randomized controlled designs (39/56, 69.6%). Polysubstance-using populations were most frequently targeted (32/56, 57.1%), followed by cannabis (13/56, 23.2%), opioids (6/56, 10.7%), and stimulants (5/56, 8.9%). Interventions were delivered mainly via web (24/56, 42.9%) or app (24/56, 42.9%) platforms, and most (49/56, 87.5%) were grounded in traditional CBT, most often combined with contingency management (18/56, 32.1%) or motivational interviewing (17/56, 30.4%). Core functional components included therapeutic intervention (55/56, 98.2%), self-tracking and notification (25/56, 44.6%), reward (24/56, 42.9%), and support and feedback (21/56, 37.5%). Primary outcomes focused on substance use and abstinence (41/56, 73.2%), retention/feasibility (16/56, 28.6%), and mental health status or coping skills (14/56, 25%). Author-reported limitations were predominantly participant-level (52/56, 92.9%), measurement-level (43/56, 76.8%), study-level (34/56, 60.7%), and intervention-level (25/56, 44.6%) domains.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Unlike previous reviews confined to a single substance or delivery platform, this review is innovative in mapping CBT-based digital interventions across the full spectrum of illicit substances, including polysubstance use, and in linking their functional components to intended therapeutic mechanisms. It thereby contributes to the development of these technologies and, by synthesizing author-reported limitations, proposes methodological improvements for their future evaluation. At present, CBT-based digital interventions are best positioned as adjuncts that extend the reach and continuity of existing addiction care rather than as stand-alone substitutes for it; substance-specific customization, objective outcome measures, and modular trial designs are needed to establish them as scalable clinical tools.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

17c3410fca5d52334564908f9163fcfe7cb92222.abstract: <jats:p>This research addresses predictive analytics for proactive risk identification and management across sectors. Using time series analysis, ML algorithms, and Chi-square testing, the study found that financial forecasting models are accurate, with credit scoring models being 85% accurate. The study reveals that predictive analytics-based frameworks considerably improve an organization's resilience. To boost forecast accuracy, businesses should integrate real-time data, use adaptive algorithms, and customise models for their sector. ML-based predictive analytics can forecast, plan for, and reduce these issues. This chapter discusses ML in predictive analytics and how firms may leverage data-driven insights to become more resilient and ready for anything. ML approaches including supervised learning, unsupervised clustering, and DL architectures are examined for disruption prediction. Real-world examples demonstrate how things work, and discussions of challenges and trends encourage research and industry use.</jats:p>

title: AI Crisis Simulations for Strategic Supply Chain Resilience Engineering

efa3bdd3f378e0abf94485b4112923a7db9e1877.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the integration of Scenario Intelligence (SI) in supply chain resilience engineering, leveraging AI-powered simulations for crisis management. Traditional risk management approaches are increasingly ineffective at addressing modern, unpredictable disruptions, whereas SI, through dynamic AI-driven simulations, enables proactive, real-time decision-making. Theoretical frameworks like complexity theory and resilience engineering—evolving from robustness to antifragility—are central to understanding the adaptability of supply chains in crises. The chapter covers practical applications of AI simulations in predicting and managing natural disasters, pandemics, and geopolitical risks, demonstrating how AI enhances decision-making in volatile environments. It also highlights the role of policy frameworks, industry innovations, and global governance in fostering AI adoption for resilience. Despite its potential, challenges such as data privacy, integration complexities, and governance issues remain significant barriers.</jats:p>

title: AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility Health Crises, Geopolitical Strife, and Cyber-Sabotage

4614f38b11f4dc792498ad9446a4ebd70c22f00e.abstract: <jats:p>The threat of unparalleled disruptions of international supply chains caused by health crises (example, COVID-19), geopolitical and geo economic tensions, and an increase in the risk of cyber-sabotage is growing. The conventional risk management strategies are not sufficient in handling the multi-dimensional nature of supply chains today. This chapter explores the potential uses of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in securing, stabilizing and future-proofing supply chains in the face of volatile conditions. By combining predictive analytics with blockchain, machine learning-driven anomaly forecasting, and the use of AI-driven decision-support tools, companies can also ensure resilience against uncertainty, cyberattack, and breakdowns in logistical operations. The chapter also examines how the incorporation of AI and supply chain governance connect in terms of ethics, and how to protect data security. By integrating a set of conceptual frameworks, real-life industry case studies and best practices within global supply chains</jats:p>

title: Cybersecurity in Digital Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
a2d591ae29b63d49c8f5b0f24754dec3ea764c2d.abstract: <jats:p>With ever-increasing exposures of interconnected networks to threats and complex vulnerabilities, the cybersecurity of digital supply chains acquires importance. The principle of zero-trust architecture is, never trust always verify. An implication of this is that stringent authentication must be validated, real-time acknowledgment and monitoring must be ensured at all points, and the least-privilege access must be granted to all the users and devices. An undeniable fact is that blockchain guarantees security in transactions through its decentralized and tamper-proof record. Thus, building a truly trust less infrastructure in logistics and supply chain, blockchain and smart contract-based applications can be employed to automate business processes, remove intermediaries, and prevent fraud. For a quantum computer, post-quantum cryptography becomes an answer to preserve secrets in view of any threat of decryption; it thereby replaces classical ways of encryption with one that resists quantum attack.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Supply Chain Security

AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
a9fac601cba8221d0a0ca6b6ee0491173add368e.abstract: <jats:p>Supply chains are the backbone of global trade, yet they face unprecedented risks in the digital era. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into supply chain security has emerged as a transformative strategy to manage complex risks, enhance cyber defenses, and build resilient networks. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of how AI is reshaping supply chain risk management, from predicting disruptions to automating responses. It discusses how AI-driven tools bolster cybersecurity in increasingly digital supply chains, identifying threats and safeguarding critical links. The chapter also examines the ethical challenges—such as data privacy, bias, and accountability—arising from AI integration, along with governance measures to ensure responsible use. Policy and international cooperation aspects are explored, recognizing that global supply chains require harmonized regulations and collaboration.</jats:p>

title: Architecting Antifragile Supply Chains With AI, Digital Twins, and Zero Trust Architecture
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
633ea892d6852074e94cf9336e159d7797152a41.abstract: <jats:p>In an era defined by perpetual disruption, traditional supply chain models have proven dangerously fragile. This chapter introduces the “Sentient Shield,” a novel framework for architecting antifragile supply chains that benefit from disruptions rather than merely withstanding them. The framework integrates three critical technologies: AI driven predictive analytics for precognition, Digital Twins for hyper realistic visualization and simulation, and Zero Trust Architectures as a foundational security posture. Through detailed case studies of the COVID 19 vaccine distribution, semiconductor trade wars, and the SolarWinds cyberattack, this chapter demonstrates how the Sentient Shield creates supply chains that learn from disruption. The chapter concludes with practical implementation principles and discusses governance challenges, providing a comprehensive blueprint for C suite leaders, government strategists, and researchers seeking to build self-improving supply networks in an increasingly volatile global environment.</jats:p>

title: Securing Supply Chain Data Integrity

AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
6ae06d7ba4e33764ea4e2c6baf465dcb9f47235f.abstract: <jats:p>The digitization of global supply chains has enhanced efficiency but simultaneously expanded the attack surface for cyber-sabotage and insider manipulation. Ensuring data integrity across interconnected entities has become a strategic necessity for operational resilience. This chapter presents an AI-driven multi-layered framework integrating machine learning, deep learning, federated learning, and explainable AI to strengthen data authenticity and transparency. The framework detects behavioral and contextual anomalies, preserves privacy through decentralized intelligence, and supports auditability via interpretable decision outputs. Analytical case studies from pharmaceutical and semiconductor domains demonstrate adaptability across heterogeneous supply environments. The study further outlines future research directions involving quantum-safe architectures, sustainable AI, and ethical governance, positioning artificial intelligence as a cornerstone for secure, trustworthy, and resilient supply chain ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: The Convergence of National Security and Supply Chain Sovereignty

44cb6bda4d1590b2dfc8114ac6a80fe1ec18625f.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in global supply chains has reshaped how organizations and governments predict, detect, and respond to security threats. Yet, this transformation has produced both notable successes and critical failures. This book explores real-world adoption cases, best practices from multinational corporations and defense agencies, and the regulatory, ethical, and technological challenges influencing AI integration. It also projects the future of supply chain sovereignty in 2040 and beyond, highlighting risks such as technological dependency, data monopolization, and geopolitical fragmentation. By combining insights from policy, industry, and technology, the book offers a comprehensive framework for securing supply chains and provides guidance for academics, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to align AI innovation with resilience, ethics, and long-term security.</jats:p>

34de16ba31a98b6ca3895143b1aa9ee703bcb69c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines three technology families that have drawn attention from supply chain researchers and practitioners: blockchain, augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR), and edge computing. The argument is not simply that each yields operational benefits, but that their significance lies in addressing complementary problems within a single domain. Blockchain addresses trust and information integrity in multi-party networks; AR/VR addresses human interface challenges in complex environments; edge computing provides distributed computation enabling real-time responsiveness at scale. Drawing on recent work, the chapter traces how these technologies support the industrial metaverse. Sustainability, resilience, human-centred design, and infrastructure scalability are key themes. It also examines challenges—interoperability, governance gaps, cost barriers, and security exposures—and offers a coherent view of their convergence and implications.</jats:p>

title: Industrial Metaverse in Supply Chain Management

Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
09f40adbf7cb76bff382bbf6d92aec1c8a0bac82.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the concept of the industrial metaverse in supply chain management, highlighting its role in enabling AI-driven virtualization, collaborative decision-making, and sustainable transformation. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, digital twins, IoT, and immersive interfaces create integrated, real-time, and interactive supply chain ecosystems. The study emphasizes the shift from reactive to predictive and autonomous supply chains through simulation, optimization, and data-driven intelligence. It further discusses the role of the industrial metaverse in enhancing multi-stakeholder collaboration, operational efficiency, and environmental sustainability through circular economy practices. A comprehensive framework is proposed to integrate technological, organizational, and strategic dimensions. The chapter contributes by offering insights into building resilient, intelligent, and sustainable supply chain systems.</jats:p>

d99b6055016f0e8c84e8e502fe276ebb105bc5e1.abstract: <jats:p>The major gap that still exists is the operationalization of the application of the concept of digital twist in the supply chain management although more research has been done on the area. This is more so in the emerging countries where its adoption is impeded by infrastructural and fragmented logistic ecosystems and limited capital. This chapter addresses that gap by introducing digital twin architectures within supply chain processes through a structured conceptual framework to support adaptive governance, anticipate risks, and intelligence in decision-making. Three basic mechanisms are discussed in the chapter such as (1) bi-directional data synchronization in real-time among supply chain nodes; (2) predictive simulation modeling of demand volatility and disruption; and (3) cross-tier visibility as an architecture requirement of coordination. These processes rest on a critical review of the literature, industry experience and systems-thinking concepts.</jats:p>

800c4603905b0b481af418f93c27b335627b538c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops an architecture for combining cognitive digital twins with blockchain ecosystems to deliver predictive business intelligence in the industrial metaverse. It argues that digital-twin initiatives create value only when operational telemetry, semantic context, decision models, and human governance are connected through trusted data-sharing and executable coordination mechanisms. Drawing on research in digital twins, industrial metaverse design, blockchain-enabled provenance, smart contracts, human-centric manufacturing, and explainable AI, the chapter proposes a layered reference architecture, performance metrics, implementation logic, and governance controls. It also examines persistent challenges, including semantic fragmentation, model drift, latency, privacy, interoperability, energy cost, and the oracle problem. The chapter concludes with design recommendations and a research agenda for resilient, trustworthy, and economically useful industrial intelligence systems across networked industrial-metaverse platforms and ecosystems.</jats:p>

6cae48cda77d8a51b8ca2bc4b94e05b4a9e8c301.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, we explore the process of achieving supply chain resilience in Industrial Metaverse environments by embedding digital twin technology and blockchain-based distributed trust mechanisms. No single technology is sufficient to address the triple crises of disruption, opacity, and accountability in contemporary supply chains. The chapter makes its case through trans-disciplinary scholarship spanning supply chain management, digital transformation, blockchain governance, and Industry 4.0. They introduce a 5-layer conceptual framework to illustrate how these physical operations, data connectivity, simulation, distributed verification, and governance layers are interdependent among each other via the Digital Twin–Blockchain Trust Framework, which allows us to visualize how such Human-centric smart systems can lead towards Visibility, Traceability, and Adaptive Resilience eventually. Investigates sustainability implications, ethical risks, and cyber vulnerabilities, as well as concrete pathways for managerial adoption.</jats:p>

d1b522f79a68031ab548219a1152e6dfcb83f336.abstract: <jats:p>The study presents the earliest effort to conceptualize SCM integration with quantum computing principles, providing dynamic capabilities for SCM. It proposes a unique interdisciplinary framework that demonstrates where hybrid quantum-classical approaches can realise value, and specifies the conditions that organizations must meet to adopt such methods. In this article, a conceptual framework has been proposed for HQCSCO. This framework facilitates key decision-making areas such as inventory optimisation, production scheduling, and logistics routing, where quantum-enhanced algorithms could supplement classical models to enhance performance. At the managerial level, the framework helps manufacturing leaders to determine viability, prioritize high-impact use cases, and develop future-ready digital capabilities that enhance cost efficiency, agility, and resilience. The research provides a conceptually-based baseline of quantum-facile supply chains and offers a research agenda to investigate the strategic, ethical, and operational implications thereof.</jats:p>

title: Immersive Stock Control for Virtual Depots via Process Digital Twins and Topological Data Analysis

181d6ce5803b6924cc02dfd46f21bf24456d4579.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents the development of an advanced inventory management model for virtual warehouses. By combining process digital twins with Topological Data Analysis, this model strives to support supervisors in pinpointing bottleneck formations that standard performance indicators are unable to reveal. The methodology describes how IoT-like intralogistics events are interpreted as augmented point clouds. The methodology also describes how persistent homology is computed through Vietoris-Rips and Alpha-complex filtrations, and how topological indicators are transformed into an immersive decision layer through the framework's comprehensive approach to bottleneck and Wasserstein distances. The computational case interprets fragmentation, routing loops, and volumetric cavities as congestion, vulnerability, and latent capacity indicators. The results show how the persistent topology of the model offers a candidate articulate layer for the process digital twins. The model still needs additional empirical calibration, for operational interventions in a physical warehouse.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Smart Ports and Sustainable Maritime Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

fb27937fd6ed5b67a638e8b71b2617dfc041ff66.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming maritime logistics by improving operational efficiency, sustainability, and digital integration. At the same time, the Industrial Metaverse is reshaping supply chain management through real time data, digital twins, and intelligent decision environments. However, the linkage between these developments remains underexplored. This study conducts a bibliometric and thematic review of 208 Scopus indexed journal articles published between 2013 and 2025 using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix. The analysis identifies key trends and four thematic clusters: smart ports, green shipping, digital transformation, and governance. Findings indicate that existing research is technologically advanced but fragmented, with limited focus on system integration, human interaction, and economic feasibility. The study highlights critical gaps and provides insights for advancing next generation, Industrial Metaverse based maritime supply chains.</jats:p>

title: Challenges of Industry 4.0 Adoption in Malaysia's Ship Repair Industry
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

a5c2578bb1ed98f301ea6bb9016c9962fd028ba1.abstract: <jats:p>The adoption of Industrial Revolution 4.0 (IR 4.0) technologies in Malaysia's ship repair industry presents significant opportunities to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and global competitiveness. However, the transition toward digital transformation remains constrained by multiple structural, technological, and organizational challenges. This study aims to identify and analyze the key barriers to IR 4.0 adoption using a mixed-method approach that integrates literature review and empirical data collected from 175 industry experts. The findings reveal five critical challenges, namely technological infrastructure and investment, data management and integration, workforce skills, cybersecurity, and regulatory frameworks. Among these, infrastructure and data-related challenges emerged as the most significant. The findings contribute to both academic literature and industry practice by offering a comprehensive understanding of IR 4.0 adoption in a developing maritime context.</jats:p>

title: Industrial Metaverse and AI-Driven Food Supply Chains

47d3e0515c13fda1af2da5950b7c6fa396315d15.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores how agriculture and food logistics are being transformed through artificial intelligence and Industrial Metaverse-enabled supply chain systems in emerging economies. It examines the shift from traditional linear food systems toward immersive, data-driven, and phygital ecosystems integrating digital twins, blockchain, IoT, and AR/VR technologies. Using a qualitative multiple-case study approach, the research analyzes India, China, Brazil, and Russia to understand how policy reforms, technological adoption, and infrastructure development influence food security and resilience. Findings show that AI-enabled forecasting, real-time monitoring, and immersive simulation improve supply chain efficiency, reduce food waste, and enhance sustainability. However, challenges such as infrastructure gaps, digital inequality, and limited workforce readiness persist. The study emphasizes the importance of integrated policy frameworks and education systems to enable next-generation resilient food supply chains.</jats:p>

title: Sustainability and the Circular Economy in Virtualized Settings

ebe6f0b34ee1b19fb405906ddf6f10d2270baad4.abstract: <jats:p>Supply chains are under mounting pressure to reconcile operational performance with environmental responsibility — a tension that conventional efficiency tools and isolated green initiatives have not resolved satisfactorily. This chapter examines how the industrial metaverse, as an integrative platform encompassing digital twins, extended reality interfaces, and AI-enabled analytics, can embed circular economy principles within supply chains. Drawing on recent scholarship, it traces alignment between closed-loop material flows and the informational closure enabled by metaverse environments. Attention is given to enabling conditions and persistent barriers — organisational, technological, and regulatory — shaping adoption. The chapter situates these developments within the digital economy, considering how financial digitalization and platform economics affect viability, and offers practical guidance followed by a research agenda.</jats:p>
