title: Implementation strategies for integration of evidence-based caries management approach in dental education: a scoping review
container-title: Caries Research
742b8ba1781e73c57ec54fd70039950550d931bc.abstract: Abstract Introduction: The adoption of Evidence-Based Caries Management (EBCM) approach, introduced over two decades ago, has been slow and inconsistent in dental education and practice. There is a need for enhancing the implementation of EBCM in dental educational settings. This scoping review aims to map and summarizing evidence on EBCM implementation strategies and implementation outcomes in undergraduate dental schools. Methods: A comprehensive search strategy was conducted using MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and ERIC databases along with gray literature, and hand searches. Studies looking at implementation strategies for the EBCM approach in dental education were included. Data were screened, selected, and extracted by two independent reviewers. Qualitative content analysis was performed. Findings were reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Results: One webinar and 25 studies, published between 2007 and 2023 across dental faculties in America, Europe, and Asia were included in the scoping review. Seven studies focused on developing comprehensive cariology curricula tailored to specific contexts, corresponding to the exploration/preparation phase. In the implementation phase, caries detection was the most frequently reported component of EBCM (n=7), followed by caries risk assessment (n=3), caries risk assessment and management (n=4) or multiple components of EBCM (n=4). According to ERIC classification, 22 out of 73 implementation strategies grouped in seven clusters were identified. The most frequent ERIC strategies were “make training dynamic” and “promote adaptability”, and the most frequent ERIC strategies’ cluster was “train and educate stakeholders”. Among the most frequent implementation outcomes identified were “acceptability”, “appropriateness”, “fidelity” and “adoption”. Less frequent outcomes were “sustainability” and “implementation cost”. Only three evidence sources reported about the implementation of the whole EBCM approach withing all graduate years of the undergraduate dental education. Conclusion: Overall, the findings underscore the need for more comprehensive and coordinated approaches to effectively integrate EBCM into dental curricula. The EBCM approach in undergraduate dental education remains in its early implementation stages and characterised by inconsistent adoption, as many institutions focus on isolated components rather than the entire framework within all Cariology curriculum. More studies focusing on the implementation of the whole EBCM approach in dental education using implementation science methodology are needed.

47c83c8edddcf3f80554e658fd45b7249b6122ed.abstract: This paper presents the findings of a multi-year study evaluating the effects of convective drying temperatures and processing durations on the dried product yield of six promising fig cultivars — Uzbekskiy zheltiy, Krym 9, Krym 29, Krym 43, Karshinskiy cherniy, and Dalmatskiy, grown under the subtropical conditions of Surkhandarya region. The experimental data revealed that increasing both drying temperature and exposure duration led to a consistent and substantial reduction in fruit yield due to intensive moisture evaporation, ranging from 68.7–77.9% at 40°C after 20 hours down to 8.7–13.7% following profound dehydration at 60°C after 80 hours. Distinct cultivar-specific dehydration kinetics were observed, governed by pericarp thickness, tissue density, and initial dry matter content. Uzbekskiy zheltiy (average yield of 42.04%) and Dalmatskiy (39.17%) exhibited notable technological stability and uniform moisture release, whereas Krym 29 and Krym 43 demonstrated rapid desiccation, achieving target moisture levels 10–15 hours earlier than the other cultivars. title: When traditional culture meets digital games: pathways and boundary conditions linking cultural identity to purchase intention

b737bf9f158dd7fe1115790c35d9a3290a8b2095.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how cultural identity is associated with purchase intention for paid digital games featuring local cultural elements. In the context of Black Myth: Wukong, it further investigates whether perceived value and immersive experience explain this relationship and whether price sensitivity conditions these associations. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 1,167 mainland Chinese and international gamers were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) and cross-sample model comparisons were used to examine group differences. Findings Cultural identity was positively associated with purchase intention, with significant indirect effects through perceived value and immersive experience. In the full sample, price sensitivity weakened the links between cultural identity and both mediators and their indirect effects. Mainland Chinese gamers showed higher cultural identity and perceived value, and stronger direct and indirect effects of cultural identity, than international gamers. The moderating effect of price sensitivity was not significant in the international subsample. Practical implications Managers can strengthen culturally grounded digital products by embedding culturally resonant narratives, symbols and aesthetics into product design, communicating their relevance to target consumers and adopting differentiated value-framing and pricing strategies for consumers with varying levels of price sensitivity. Originality/value This study applies cultural identity theory to paid digital game consumption by integrating perceived value and immersive experience as two distinct mechanisms linking cultural identity to purchase intention and examining price sensitivity as a boundary condition of these relationships.

58666eea94c350bdfa7261dba276440be363cb70.abstract: The work is devoted to the study of the legal regulation of public administration of tertiary education in branch systems using the example of the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs. The article identifies the issues of legal regulation of the administrative-legal status of the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs as a departmental governing body for higher education, and substantiates the expediency of expanding the ministry's competence in the field of higher education in law enforcement-related specialties to universities implementing these programs, regardless of departmental affiliation. The shortcomings of legal regulation have been identified, measures have been proposed to eliminate them, as well as to improve the management of migration processes using modern digital technologies.

title: Self-attention-aided multi-layer CNN-LSTM for non-uniform 4-level differential amplitude modulation and detection with atmospheric turbulence for OWANs

1922c9e0cb34b13e5ea74df3c48f83317a5531ed.abstract: This paper proposes an environment-aware four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation and detection scheme assisted by self-attentive multi-layer CNN-LSTM (SA-CNN-LSTM) for optical wireless access networks (OWANs) under atmospheric turbulence, to mitigate severe distortions induced by atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Relying on four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation (NUADM-4) and a self-attention-aided detection algorithm at the receiving terminal, the proposed scheme can effectively suppress both multiplicative turbulence fading and additive Gaussian noise simultaneously. Numerical results reveal that the proposed scheme achieves remarkable bit error rate (BER) improvements compared with conventional detection frameworks for NUADM-4, and it substantially outperforms the classical uniform four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) across diverse turbulence strength regimes. Moreover, the tailored architecture integrating self-attention with multi-layer CNN-LSTM maintains high transmission efficiency, reduces the dimension of the fully-connected layer at the receiver to a certain extent, and accelerates the computation speed compared with the CNN-based algorithm. In comparison with conventional detection-aided algorithms such as vanilla CNN, LSTM, and MLP, the presented scheme delivers a universal BER performance gain. Furthermore, the machine-learning-aided design philosophy for different modulation systems offers a practical design paradigm and implementable solution for the engineering deployment of high-speed OWC systems serving OWANs operating in volatile atmospheric turbulence environments.

title: Social Justice in Education
Bridging or Widening the Gap? AI Policies and Social Justice in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
9e13e6e7f3a42906186f831be85e28f41f88c8fe.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as a means to improve educational quality, efficiency, and equity. However, when introduced into systems already shaped by inequality, AI risks reproducing rather than reducing social injustice. This chapter examines whether AI policies in education bridge or widen existing gaps, drawing on Nancy Fraser's framework of redistribution, recognition, and representation. Through a comparative analysis of supranational frameworks and national strategies in the United States, China, India, and Türkiye, the chapter identifies persistent tensions between innovation-driven agendas and justice-oriented goals. The findings suggest that equity is often framed in technocratic terms, while issues of power, participation, and accountability remain marginal. The chapter concludes by proposing a justice-centered policy evaluation framework that emphasizes democratic governance, cultural responsiveness, and the right to contest or refuse harmful AI systems.

title: Cultivating Pre-Service EFL Teachers' Social Justice
container-title: Social Justice in Education
a002f3a0d9d2e35aa4b5b72098861ea596ef4433.abstract: This autoethnographic study investigates the mystories of three English as Foreign Language (EFL) teacher educators' respective implementation of social justice-oriented procedures in their teacher education programs with a distributed leadership lens. Data for this study came from autoethnographic reflections and autoethnographic conversations. Together with these, we built our own mystories that capture our total experiences in our attempts to cultivate pre-service EFL teachers' social justice awareness and practices. Findings indicated that we acted based on a sense of distributed leadership and highlighted the importance of preparing teachers to navigate the emotional and social aspects of learning while promoting critical and socially aware pedagogies.

title: Factories of Sadness
container-title: Social Justice in Education
e81bdafb57e30a783e40155efcfda801bb30326f.abstract: Authoritarian leadership in South African higher education institutions (HEIs) has reshaped collegial academic spaces into compliance-driven environments, described here as factories of sadness. Line managers often exercise control through micromanagement, manipulation, and opaque decision-making, a governance regime conceptualised as darkocracy. These practices erode academic freedom, undermine morale, and replace collaboration with fear and conformity. Drawing on literature and autoethnographic insights, this chapter examines toxic leadership as a systemic outcome of neoliberal and managerial governance rather than isolated managerial failure. It highlights the emotional and professional consequences for faculty, including burnout, disengagement, and loss of academic identity, and calls for ethical, transparent, and participatory leadership models that restore academic autonomy, psychological safety, and democratic engagement.

title: Inequality and Discrimination in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
83e3576767390bf5240a404bb35dc18dbc4a13ec.abstract: The multifaceted dynamics of discrimination and inequality in education have attracted growing academic interest in recent years, leading to the development of an increasingly interdisciplinary and conceptually diverse research field. Despite this expanding body of literature, there is still a limited number of studies that systematically map the evolution, major trends, leading research networks, and intellectual structures of this field. The present study aims to map the position, intellectual structure, and direction of development trends in discussions of inequality and discrimination in education by conducting a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. To provide a comprehensive map of the research field focusing on inequality and discrimination in education between 2000 and 2025, academic publications indexed in international databases (Web of Science, Scopus, etc.) are analyzed in temporal, geographical, and thematic dimensions. This study provides a systematic perspective on the fundamental research orientations of this field, the themes that emerge, and the future trends.

title: Leading with Inclusion
container-title: Social Justice in Education
1a7cfbf684b92ec753491daad36e2097fb76e2a6.abstract: This chapter views neurodiversity as a social justice issue in English language education from the leadership perspective. Despite a growing emphasis on diversity, equity, and inclusion, neurodivergent learners continue to encounter institutional practices restricting their meaningful participation and access. Drawing on narrative accounts from four English language educators in K-12 and higher education contexts, the chapter explores how leadership practices shape inclusivity. The educators' reflections reveal tensions between institutional policies and teachers' efforts to support neurodivergent learners in the face of curriculum and assessment-related restrictions. These narratives highlight the importance of teachers' role as informal leaders and advocates. From a social justice lens, the chapter argues for an inclusive leadership beyond policy statements to foster flexible, collaborative, and dignity-affirming practices. It displays the pivotal role of neurodiversity in equitable educational leadership and underscores lived experiences for inclusive institutional change.

title: Mapping Inclusive Practices in English Language Teacher Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
6033410d4a72f78561e790674716af4e46de64e6.abstract: Teachers are not only facilitators of learning but also agents of change, capable of shaping educational systems to become more equitable and responsive to learner diversity. Their preparation within teacher education programs is therefore critical in ensuring that inclusivity moves from being a stated value to a lived reality. This study examines how inclusive education is represented in an English Language Teacher Education Program (ELTEP) and ELT department's artifacts. Data were collected through systematic document analysis of the program framework, mission, vision and goal statements, and program competency framework of the department. Analysis revealed that inclusivity is acknowledged but unevenly embedded, primarily through a single compulsory course and several electives of limited reach. These findings suggest that while inclusivity has some fragmented curricular presence, there is a need for structural revisions to embed it as a systematic, ELT-specific competency.

title: Polycentric Leadership for Justice and Epistemic Inclusion as Institutional Design in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
c3bded076c6ad636a7bd0da039f3919e672fde7c.abstract: This chapter proposes a polycentric institutional design that turns equity into routine educational practice. It integrates reflexive coaching, affective leadership, arts-infused curriculum and governance, epistemic inclusion, emotional sustainability, and semiotic pluralism. A systems map links micro-level instruction, meso-level governance, and macro-level accountability to outcomes in access, fairness, belonging, and staff vitality. The framework combines improvement science, realist evaluation, arts-based inquiry, calibrated moderation, and mixed-method scorecards with clear thresholds, review cycles, reciprocal accountability, and retire-to-add rules. It offers a portable operating grammar that distributes authority with coherence, broadens legitimate forms of knowledge without weakening rigor, and supports equitable practices that can survive leadership transitions and adapt to changing institutional conditions.

title: Social Justice Leadership in Practice
container-title: Social Justice in Education
db419fbd1fb801d6c3234298fc7483a39d22530a.abstract: This chapter presents a practitioner-scholar playbook for institutionalizing equity in the management systems that shape higher education: staffing, budgeting, promotion and tenure, safety/care, and accountability. Using a Social Justice Leadership lens informed by cross-sector accountability practice, we translate equity commitments into governance-ready tools that administrators can implement and evaluate. We present workload-equity bylaws and crediting schemas, need-weighted budgeting and transparent trade-off protocols, promotion and tenure criteria that recognize community-engaged and public scholarship, a student-facing support protocol, employee-facing restorative supervision scripts and coordinated referral procedures, and an equity accountability dashboard with KPIs and a review cadence. The chapter clarifies how Social Justice Leadership shifts equity from aspiration to measurable practice while strengthening institutional performance.

title: Teacher Educators as Justice-Oriented Leaders in Multilingual Higher Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
61825cf85bcbfa9cbc588fef55660f73c241628a.abstract: This chapter explores the enactment of social justice-oriented leadership within English Language Teacher Education (ELTE). Adopting a critical collaborative dialogic autoethnographic approach, the authors examine how leadership for justice manifests through pedagogical rather than administrative means. The text analyzes how teacher educators navigate institutional and linguistic exclusions, such as native-speakerism and cultural misrecognition, which persist beneath celebratory discourses of internationalization. Through reflexive dialogue, the study theorizes leadership as a relational, ethical, and political practice across micro, meso, and macro levels. Findings suggest that justice-oriented leadership is realized through micro-level decisions; such as reframing student contributions or interrupting exclusionary norms, which carry significant emotional labor. The chapter argues for a grounded understanding of leadership that prioritizes sustained ethical attentiveness and the refusal of quiet erasures in multilingual spaces.

title: Trauma Sensitive Schools Creating Conditions for Resilience and Post Traumatic Growth
container-title: Social Justice in Education
22aaa6edbf54398f5ded8815364ce37f57e94a73.abstract: This chapter examines how schools can integrate trauma-informed principles with support for resilience and posttraumatic growth while addressing structural inequities. It clarifies the distinctions among adversity, trauma-related responses, and clinical diagnoses, and considers their developmental, relational, and educational implications. Critical and intersectional perspectives inform an analysis of how school practices can reproduce harm or support safety, belonging, and participation. A multilevel framework identifies universal, targeted, intensive, and organizational responsibilities. A student scenario illustrates observation, support, qualified assessment when needed, and follow-up. The chapter argues that schools can support recovery and learning without diagnosing students, requiring trauma disclosure, or treating growth as a required outcome.

title: Women Leading Social Justice Movements in an Era of Backlash
container-title: Social Justice in Education
2f7e50667971a4eb2a67e60157b77209758b2513.abstract: This chapter examines how women leaders sustain moral integrity and transformative vision amid escalating backlash against social justice movements. Drawing from global empirical research across educational, healthcare, and community contexts, it advances a moral-ecological framework linking fortitude, resilience, and justice. The analysis integrates intersectional, feminist, and decolonial perspectives—highlighting Latina superintendents' pláticas, African Ubuntu leadership, Arab women's contextual resilience, and Appalachian educators' relational fortitude. Findings reveal that resilience is relational rather than individual, and rooted in networks of care, mentorship, and collective healing. The chapter proposes a five-pillar framework emphasizing moral clarity, relational infrastructure, institutional reciprocity, collective healing, and joyful sustainability. Implications extend to leadership education, policy, and organizational design, urging systems that reward empathy and reflection as strategic assets.

title: The impact of the demise of department stores on the geography of UK retailing
container-title: Property Management
03f928301f0ff786416b6651b79fad4b14373eaf.abstract: Purpose The article examines the impact of the closures of department stores on the geography of retailing in the United Kingdom and the supply of shops in different types of shopping centres. Design/methodology/approach A three-step process was adopted to address the task. First, a list of closed department stores was identified. Second, the analysis draws on the CoStar database that provides information on real estate transactions from property agents. For each of the closed stores information was collected on what had happened since the store ceased trading, so whether the unit had been relet, sub-divided, use changed or remained vacant or a combination of these. A third step was the supplementation of this information with searches of news outlets such as the BBC and local newspapers to provide more detail. Findings The findings from the empirical analysis show that large regional centres have coped reasonably well with the demise of department stores, as have retail parks and large out-of-town centres. Nevertheless, there have been some changes of use for these vacant stores, notably to residential and leisure in city centres. Offices have also offered an alternative use. The long-term decline of small centres over decades has been amplified by the closure of their department stores that were probably the largest store in the locality. A high percentage remain empty while others have been converted to other uses, so that a significant majority of former department stores have been lost to retailing in these localities. Given that these stores acted as core attractions to shoppers in these small towns who then also visited other retail businesses, there is an existential crisis of local retail function unfolding for small centres. Originality/value This is the first article that assesses the impact of the widespread closure of department stores on the retail hierarchy. While the research is based on the United Kingdom, the findings almost certainly have a resonance for other countries.

title: Integrated risk management framework for international civil engineering projects
container-title: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Management, Procurement and Law
23cfd10aee7cfbf019a3f36dfcb937ee06bea5f8.abstract: International civil engineering projects are exposed to political, financial, technical, environmental, and organisational risks that frequently interact and evolve throughout the project lifecycle. Existing risk-management approaches, including the Integrated Project Risk Assessment (IPRA) tool, fuzzy logic, structural equation modelling (SEM), and resilience engineering, are typically applied independently, limiting their ability to support integrated decision making. This study develops an integrated conceptual framework that combines these complementary approaches within a unified risk-management process. A structured literature review guided by PRISMA 2020 covered publications from January 2000 to March 2024, supplemented by a targeted literature update through August 2026. The review identified and synthesised studies addressing structured risk identification, uncertainty modelling, risk interdependencies, and resilience-based management. Within the evidence identified through these searches, no publication explicitly integrated IPRA, fuzzy logic, SEM, and resilience engineering within a single framework for international civil engineering projects. The proposed framework links structured risk identification, uncertainty-aware risk evaluation, interdependency analysis, and adaptive management through iterative information flows and feedback mechanisms. The framework provides a structured basis for supporting risk-informed decision making and establishes a foundation for future empirical validation and implementation in the management of complex international civil engineering projects.

title: Family bricolage in family-managed agribusinesses
container-title: Management Decision
bb39fc6b075a2b7080a68b49bce0fab6782e335c.abstract: Purpose This study explores bricolage in mature, multigenerational family-managed agribusinesses and develops family bricolage to explain how family managers reproduce, regulate or reject inherited ways of making do. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative, abductive design based on 42 interviews with 29 participants from 26 family-managed agribusinesses, and one with a farming support organisation, in England, analysed iteratively alongside secondary evidence. Findings Family bricolage is a family-embedded process in which accumulated stories, knowledge, experience and intergenerational relationships shape how family managers recognize, mobilize and recombine resources at hand. It comprises family symbolic resources, family resourcefulness and family tinkering. Senior members regulate successors' tinkering, and negative cases show that inherited bricolage may be rejected when it inhibits renewal or professionalization. Research limitations/implications The context-specific findings are not statistically generalizable. Future research should compare industries and resource conditions and develop and validate measures of the three dimensions. Practical implications Family managers can use narratives, tacit knowledge and existing resources to address constraints, but should reassess inherited practices when self-reliance discourages external expertise or tinkering consumes resources without producing dependable, scalable solutions. Succession offers a natural point for this reassessment. Social implications Family bricolage may support continuity and adaptation in resource-constrained rural settings while enabling successors to reconsider inherited practices that inhibit renewal. Originality/value The study challenges the view that firms outgrow bricolage by showing how it is reproduced, regulated or rejected across generations in mature family firms. Family bricolage is conceptualized as an enabling and constraining process rather than a uniformly beneficial resource.

title: Evaluation of Biological and Synthetic Fungicides for Management of Watermelon Anthracnose in Indiana, 2025
container-title: Plant Health Progress
c1caaf9490263e12fb8dc8d686fd19fee047d399.abstract: Anthracnose, caused by Colletotrichum orbiculare , is a major disease of watermelon in the United States. Symptoms include irregular dark brown leaf spots that may coalesce and produce a shot-hole appearance, as well as sunken lesions on fruit rinds. A field trial was conducted in Indiana in 2025 to evaluate biological and synthetic fungicides for management of watermelon anthracnose. Anthracnose severity was significantly reduced by several treatments at the final assessment compared with the nontreated control. Results from this study provide information to support fungicide selection for anthracnose management in Indiana watermelon production.

title: Towards sustainable construction: a roadmap for aligning BES6001 with the UN SDGs
container-title: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Management, Procurement and Law
6237367d64176f4023aada30212be2a1065d8c68.abstract: The architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector has grown significantly over recent decades, sparking ongoing debate about its environmental impact. While advancing sustainability is essential, the sector’s role in meeting housing needs, upgrading infrastructure and restoring biodiversity remains critical to delivering safe and resilient communities. Responsible sourcing and green supply chains are increasingly recognised as key mechanisms for delivering sustainable construction. BES6001 is a certification standard for responsible sourcing, offering a structured and transparent framework for AEC organisations producing materials. However, its potential contribution to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remains insufficiently explored. This study examines the alignment between BES6001 and the SDGs, through the development of a conceptual roadmap. The roadmap was subject to expert review and identified strongest contributions to SDG-8 and SDG-12, although findings are based on preliminary validation (n = 7). By analysing BES6001’s scoring criteria and principles, the roadmap illustrates how UK organisations may support the operationalisation of SDG commitments through BES6001 certification. Recommendations include revising BES6001 to strengthen SDG alignment and holistic review of SDG targets for developed regions where current goals may lack relevance. This combined approach aims to improve uptake and drive meaningful sustainable procurement within the AEC industry.

title: Evaluation of Humic Acid and Chitosan Additives for Corn Diseases Management in West Lafayette, Indiana in 2025
container-title: Plant Health Progress
5b86553902858733167d9563778e2d66f3c12ee6.abstract: Corn diseases such as tar spot ( Phyllachora maydis ), gray leaf spot ( Cercospora zeae-maydis ), northern corn leaf blight ( Exserohilum turcicum ), Curvularia leaf spot ( Curvularia lunata ), southern rust ( Puccinia polysora ), and Physoderma brown spot ( Physoderma maydis ) are frequently found in Indiana corn. Tar spot, gray leaf spot, northern corn leaf blight, and southern rust are the main foliar diseases and have been causing significant yield loss. This report evaluates the efficacy of humic acid and chitosan additives in corn ( Zea mays ‘P0035AM’) compared to a standard fungicide product. The trial was conducted in 2025 in West Lafayette, Indiana. Disease incidence and severity, canopy greenness, lodging, harvest moisture, test weight, and yield were collected for each treatment. Low disease pressure was observed in central Indiana. Treatments with Impact SIX chitosan (1.0 pt.) and Monty's Liquid Carbon (1.0 qt.), both alone and combined with generic azoxystrobin + propiconazole (10.5 fl. oz.), applied at VT/R1 or Monty's Liquid Carbon at V5, led to significantly lower lodging percentages than the nontreated control. title: Gcn5 and mTORC1 mediated regulation of autophagy controls Drosophila blood cell homeostasis
container-title: eLife
700db83f75519837e25d45ca5d0f3b8c17d2c4a4.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Blood progenitors are regulated by a variety of systemic and nutritional cues from their environment. In the
                    <jats:italic>Drosophila</jats:italic>
                    lymph gland (LG), the Posterior Signaling Center acts as a stem cell niche striking a balance between progenitors and differentiated blood cells. Autophagy is a vital cellular process that maintains homeostasis by removing unnecessary or dysfunctional cell components through autophagic degradation and recycling. Here, using genetic perturbation analysis, we show that autophagy plays a critical role in regulating LG blood cell homeostasis. General control non-derepressible 5 (Gcn5), a histone acetyltransferase, is expressed in the primary LG lobe, and modulation of Gcn5 levels perturbs LG homeostasis. Our results show that hemocyte-specific Gcn5 modulation controls autophagic flux in the hemocytes. Furthermore, we show that modulation of mTORC1 activity can perturb hematopoiesis. Our results indicate that organismal Gcn5 levels respond to dietary shifts and are modulated by mTORC1 signaling. Chemical intervention shows that mTORC1 overrides the effect exerted by Gcn5 in regulating LG hematopoiesis. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that Gcn5 and mTORC1 regulate autophagy to maintain blood cell homeostasis in
                    <jats:italic>Drosophila</jats:italic>
                    .
                  </jats:p>

title: Beyond Belief Updating: A Framework for Self-Belief Formation
3796862ab71587287fb46c3bdf9532408a32202a.abstract: From early childhood, we form self-beliefs about where we belong, what we are good at, or who loves us. Despite extensive psychological research on self-beliefs, the fundamental question of how they initially form has received surprisingly little attention. Existing work on self-belief updating overlooks two critical limitations. First, it treats self-related learning as arising from isolated events, ignoring that self-beliefs typically emerge from sequences of meaningfully connected experiences. Second, because updating paradigms operate in familiar domains, participants already hold precise prior beliefs intertwined with established motives and emotional states making it impossible to study belief formation from a genuinely uninformed starting point. We propose that studying novel experiential domains addresses both problems: individuals enter such domains with neutral, imprecise self-beliefs, enabling formation of “artificial” self-beliefs through repeated feedback in a controlled setting. As a concrete implementation, we introduce the Learning Of Own Performance (LOOP) task, in which participants form beliefs about their abilities in a novel performance domain. Extensions of this approach could illuminate broader aspects of self-belief formation, including personality and identity. This Perspective bridges psychology, computational neuroscience, and sociology around a foundational question: how do we come to think about ourselves the way we do?

title: Decentralized Finance and Digital Assets: A New Perspective on Financial Management and Risk
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
13b14090a5c64d7c3224b43ae85f72408e707dbf.abstract: <jats:p>Financial services are being transformed, how they are designed, accessed, and managed, by the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi) and digital assets. These innovations via blockchain networks, smart contracts, and tokenization offer alternatives to existing models for payments, lending, investment, and asset exchange. But the economic, institutional and operating risks of financial intermediation are not eroded when transactions are automated. In this conceptual study, the impact of DeFi and digital assets on financial management is explored, including capital allocation, treasury operations, risk management, and the governance of digital assets. It assesses what could be gained from this technology, alongside its potential technological vulnerabilities, market instability, regulatory uncertainty and inability to provide meaningful financial inclusion. An analysis approach is built to present a managerial perspective, which considers digital financial arrangements from an economic function, dependency and accountability standpoint. It points out that sustainable adoption requires coordination of technology with financial management, strong rights, organizational efficiency and appropriate governance. DeFi is therefore a reorganization of financial management and not the automatic replacement of existing financial institutions.</jats:p>

title: Blockchain Technology in Management: Opportunities, Risks and Governance Challenges
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
37cc95f3465e4e0fb32f40a5e9c5644d70c42fdc.abstract: <jats:p>The idea of using blockchain seems to be gaining support as a way to facilitate transactions between organizations which don't have a shared database or administration. The importance of its management, however, is subject to debate. This article provides a critical assessment of the opportunities, risks and governance issues of organizations taking up blockchain technology. Research is synthesized into a focused narrative organized by three themes—Organizational Value, Implementation Constraints and Institutional Governance Responsibilities—that are grounded in the foundational research, further developed by management and information-systems scholarship, and then extended by institutional guidance. Several potential benefits are suggested in the literature: record reconciliation, traceability of the supply chain, auditing and rule-based transaction processing. This is only achievable by partner willingness to share, the validity of the source information and the appropriateness of blockchain over traditional databases. Potential gains might be offset by technical risks, privacy issues, organizational challenges, and uncertainties regarding regulations. In arguing this, the article does not suggest that you can forgo identifiable decision responsibilities, human responsibility or good dispute resolution when you decentralize record validation. Strategic fit, network design, accountability, information stewardship and performance review are the elements of an integrated governance framework. The paper provides an action-oriented consideration of blockchain adoption, considering benefits not as inherent properties of blockchain but rather possibilities that are likely to occur when blockchain is adopted.</jats:p>

title: Managing Investment Decisions and Risk in Decentralized Financial Markets: Evidence from Blockchain-Based Platforms
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
5970dbe0d163fa1f2d86a6ee377a5277f5d7e7c5.abstract: <jats:p>Decentralized finance (DeFi) has provided alternative investment, lending, trading, asset management and other methods via blockchain on both public and private platforms. Unlike traditional financial institutions, DeFi protocols rely on smart contracts for transactions, collateral, and financial returns and do not depend on the entire reliance of the centralized intermediaries. The innovations provide access, transparency and operational efficiency but also financial, technological, liquidity, and governance risks to the investor. This study adopts a structured literature review approach of academic studies, institutional reports and documented platforms mechanisms and investigates the investment decision making and risk management in decentralized financial markets. The cases of platform Uniswap, Aave, Compound, and MakerDAO are not meant to represent an empirical sample, but instead serve as examples to illustrate the platforms. Thematic synthesis take account of the concepts of portfolio theory and information asymmetry, highlighting the centrality of factors like expected return, collateral management, security of smart contracts, the reliability of oracles, concentration of governance, and regulatory uncertainty. It concludes that transparency of record and liquidation automation can enhance transaction discipline, but will not be enough to prevent losses in stressed markets all on its own. The study suggests an integrated decision-making approach that incorporates elements of financial, technological due diligence, governance appraisal, Exposure limits and ongoing monitoring. The results offer a basis for future transaction level tests of the effectiveness of risk adjusted investment strategies.</jats:p>

title: A Survey of Learning-based Method Name Prediction
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
48b81eddcf90694d4fefcd0a971c62e474bcae45.abstract: <jats:p>The choice of method names significantly influences code comprehension and maintenance, posing a considerable challenge, especially for novice developers. Automating the prediction of appropriate method names based on the method code body has emerged as a promising approach to address this challenge. In recent years, numerous Machine/Deep Learning (ML/DL)-based Method Name Prediction (MNP) techniques have been proposed. However, a systematic review of these techniques is currently lacking, hindering future researchers from understanding the research status, development trends, challenges, and opportunities in this field. To fill this gap, in this article, we conduct a systematic literature review on learning-based MNP studies. Specifically, we first perform a thorough review of the literature concerning publication venue, publication year, and contribution types. This analysis enables us to discern trends in studies related to MNP. Second, we depict the general workflow of learning-based MNP techniques, which involves three consecutive subprocesses: context extraction, context preprocessing, and context-based prediction. Subsequently, we investigate contemporary techniques/solutions applied in the three subprocesses. Third, we scrutinize the widely used experimental databases, evaluation metrics, and replication packages utilized in MNP studies. Moreover, we summarize existing empirical studies on MNP to facilitate a quick understanding of their focus and findings for subsequent researchers. Finally, based on a systematic review and summary of existing work, we outline several open challenges and opportunities in MNP that remain to be addressed in future work.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The time course of neural activity predictive of self-initiated movement
6bb29c0fa61a9bb6f281a6f43aa6ce014a54e928.abstract: <jats:p>Decades of research have shown that early ramping activity is a very reliable antecedent of self-initiated movement. However, the dominant paradigm has been to only analyze data epochs culminating in movement, which discounts how often slow ramping might occur when no movement follows. To address this, we introduced a matched control condition that did not culminate in movement. We recorded electroencephalography data and compared these two conditions using a variety of powerful machine-learning classifiers. Although early ramping activity was present, it was not useful in predicting movement. Instead, classification accuracy rose abruptly about 100 ms before movement. By contrast, the traditional approach reproduced the spurious impression of early predictability. Our results substantially constrain the interpretation that early EEG antecedents, including the RP, reflect a commitment to act, instead indicating that EEG-detectable evidence consistent with such a commitment emerges closer to movement onset, in line with the timing of conscious intention and the capacity for late movement inhibition. More broadly, our results show that a reliable antecedent is not necessarily a good predictor, underscoring the need for proper control conditions in time series analyses.</jats:p>

title: Feasibility Analysis of Education in Indonesian Provinces: A Machine Learning Clustering Approach for Regional Classification
container-title: Engineering and Technology Journal
1b5bd0dfe6cab0a4e4dc5dc25d573208b2fdac15.abstract: <jats:p>Education system feasibility varies significantly across Indonesian provinces due to geographic, socioeconomic, and infrastructural disparities. This study applies unsupervised machine learning clustering algorithms (K-Means, Hierarchical Clustering, Gaussian Mixture Models, and Self-Organizing Maps) to classify Indonesian provinces into homogeneous groups based on education feasibility indicators. Using 39 provinces and special territories, we evaluated clustering quality through internal validation metrics (Silhouette coefficient and Davies-Bouldin index) and inter-algorithm agreement measures (Adjusted Rand Index and Normalized Mutual Information). Results demonstrate that Hierarchical Clustering achieves the best Davies-Bouldin index (0.782), while K-Means and GMM produce identical partitions (ARI = 1.0, NMI = 1.0). Self-Organizing Maps identified nine distinct regional education feasibility profiles, with provincial distributions revealing significant heterogeneity in education conditions. These findings provide a quantitative framework for targeted policy interventions and resource allocation to improve education feasibility across Indonesia’s diverse regions.</jats:p>

title: Entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills, and self-esteem in students participating in sports programmes in Colombia
container-title: Journal of Human Sport and Exercise
7487e0e532b00ca3a9d308c88e1fc9fc09e90f2f.abstract:
<jats:p>This research presents the results of a systematic review that analyses the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills and self-esteem in students enrolled in sports programmes in Colombia, with the aim of identifying the factors that influence their positive attitude towards entrepreneurial capacity. In the literature review, 100 articles and academic research papers were selected between 2019 and 2025, prioritised from 42,958 results from different resources such as reference databases, multidisciplinary databases, academic repositories and academic journals. The databases with the highest number of results were Scopus, Web of Science, Wiley, Springer Nature, Science Direct, Ebsco Host, among others such as (COnnecting REpositories), Taylor & Francis, and Google Scholar. The results showed an interest in academia to research and reflect on the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, emotional skills, and young people. However, in most studies, entrepreneurial culture is associated with variables such as emotional intelligence and social skills in university contexts, leaving the field of the relationship between these variables and the field of sports somewhat lacking in studies. Studies that explore this relationship in depth conclude that athletes develop socio-emotional skills that make them strong candidates for entrepreneurship. However, there are limitations in the implementation of mechanisms that promote an entrepreneurial culture ( ) in university contexts for young people studying sports programmes.

The authorship information, affiliations, author contributions (CRediT), and related statements have been updated accordingly. The scientific content and conclusions of the article remain unchanged.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
7e6b65fd0eceaed8ad891218da9c81d3f193d863.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)—executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention’s effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Multi-omic integration using interpretable machine learning reveals genetic mechanisms of trait variation and phenotypic plasticity in switchgrass
d5ecaf8e9c0ab25f0f77449121b30e109d87be40.abstract: <jats:p>Uncovering the genetic architecture of quantitative traits is challenging because polygenic control yields small individual gene effects and because gene–gene and genotype-by-environment interactions add further complexity. To understand the genetic basis of polygenic traits and their plasticity across environments, we integrated genome-wide SNPs and RNA-seq transcript data with interpretable statistical and machine learning models in a switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) diversity panel grown at contrasting field sites in Michigan and Texas. Notably, in addition to single environments, our trait prediction models were able to predict phenotypic differences, across environments i.e., plasticity. By interpreting trait prediction models with explainable machine learning methods, we identified genes that are the most predictive of flowering time and annual biomass production across environments, based on their associated gene expression levels and nearby SNPs. This approach recovered canonical flowering regulators and revealed novel, environment-specific candidate flowering genes. Further, transcriptome models consistently recovered more switchgrass genes homologous to experimentally validated genes in Arabidopsis and rice than SNP-based models. Feature interaction scores from the models also allow the identification of trait- and environment-dependent gene–gene interactions, where flowering time showed stronger and more abundant interactions than biomass. While some of the interactions identified are consistent with the link between flowering time and yield, most are novel predictors that need to be further evaluated. These findings provide insight into the genetic basis of trait variation and plasticity across environments and help prioritize candidate genes for functional validation and cultivar improvement.</jats:p>

title: Endoscopic ultrasound-based deep learning for predicting chemotherapy response in unresectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
container-title: World Journal of Gastroenterology
1f6a560325fb967b8d7fb19fd1972b99328cdc40.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal malignancies, and chemotherapy remains the main treatment option for patients with unresectable disease. Reliable prediction of chemotherapy response is therefore critical for individualized treatment planning. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) provides high-resolution, tumor-specific imaging that may be well suited for deep learning-based prediction of chemotherapy response.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To develop and validate an EUS-based deep learning model for predicting first-line chemotherapy response in patients with unresectable PDAC, and to evaluate its prognostic value for overall survival (OS) stratification.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In this retrospective, single-center study, 190 patients with histologically confirmed PDAC diagnosed between February 2016 and March 2025 were included. All patients were deemed ineligible for upfront surgical resection based on formal multidisciplinary team evaluation, including those with locally advanced or metastatic disease and those considered medically or personally unsuitable for surgery. Patients diagnosed in 2023 or earlier were assigned to the training and internal validation cohort (n  = 152) using five-fold cross-validation, whereas patients diagnosed from January 2024 onward at a separate campus of the same institution constituted a temporally independent test cohort with site separation (n  = 38). Tumor regions of interest were manually annotated on pre-treatment EUS images. Four convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures (VGG19, VGG19-BN, ResNet50, and ResNeXt50) were trained to predict progressive disease, as defined by RECIST version 1.1 after first-line chemotherapy. Model performance was evaluated at the patient level using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and accuracy, and model-derived risk stratification was assessed for OS.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In the independent test cohort, ResNeXt50 demonstrated the best discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.848; sensitivity, 65.38%; specificity, 84.19%), followed by ResNet50 (AUC = 0.844), whereas VGG19-BN (AUC = 0.775) and VGG19 (AUC = 0.614) showed lower performance. Model-predicted probabilities enabled effective risk stratification, with high-risk patients exhibiting significantly shorter OS compared with low-risk patients (log-rank P  < 0.01; hazard ratio = 1.77). In contrast, baseline carbohydrate antigen 19-9-based stratification did not significantly discriminate survival, and CNN-based models demonstrated higher discriminatory performance compared with the conventional serum biomarker.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CNN models based on region-of-interest-level EUS imaging can predict chemotherapy response and provide clinically meaningful prognostic stratification in PDAC. Among the evaluated architectures, ResNeXt50 demonstrated the most consistent and robust performance across independent testing and sensitivity analyses. This noninvasive imaging-based approach shows potential for integration into clinical workflows to support personalized treatment planning.</jats:p>

title: Towards Realistic Project-Level Code Generation via Multi-Agent Collaboration and Semantic Architecture Modeling
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
2e98affb75fe6b1c9fa0a80bf39cb6bb48af6b14.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In recent years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in automated code generation. In real-world software engineering, the growing demand for rapid iteration and continuous delivery underscores the importance of project-level code generation, where LLMs are expected to generate complete software projects directly from complex user requirements. This task, however, presents greater challenges due to larger input scales, multi-modal information, and the need for holistic architectural reasoning. Although existing studies have made initial explorations, they still face key limitations, including unrealistic datasets and unreliable evaluation metrics that fail to reflect real-world complexity, the semantic gap between human-written requirements and machine-interpretable structures, and difficulties in managing hierarchical dependencies and maintaining quality throughout the generation process. To address these limitations, we first introduce
                    <jats:sc>CodeProjectEval</jats:sc>
                    , a project-level code generation dataset built from 18 real-world repositories with 12.7 files and 2,388.6 lines of code per task on average, supplemented with documentation and executable test cases for automatic evaluation. We further propose
                    <jats:sc>ProjectGen</jats:sc>
                    , a multi-agent framework that decomposes projects into architecture design, skeleton generation, and code filling stages with iterative refinement and memory-based context management. Within this framework, we introduce the Semantic Software Architecture Tree, a structured and semantically rich representation that effectively bridges user requirements and source code implementation. Experiments show that
                    <jats:sc>ProjectGen</jats:sc>
                    achieves state-of-the-art performance, passing 52/124 test cases on the small-scale project-level code generation dataset DevBench, a 57% improvement over the baseline approaches, and 310 test cases on
                    <jats:sc>CodeProjectEval</jats:sc>
                    , representing an improvement of roughly tenfold compared to the baselines.
                  </jats:p>

title: Wine, Politics, and Markets
a1477911e3f6fe9d8e457d1b117363ace5c1f507.abstract:
<jats:p>Wine has been at the heart of human civilization for thousands of years, and for centuries governments around the world have regulated wine production, consumption, and trade for reasons ranging from consumer protection and quality assurance to tax revenue and the protection of vineyard owners’ rents. The European Union (EU) alone has introduced more than two thousand wine regulations. Some of today’s regulations date back hundreds of years; others are more recent; and there is considerable variation over time.

The rich history of wine regulation offers fascinating insights into the political economy of public policy and the ways in which such policies persist and evolve. This book examines specific historical developments involving wines that are well known today, such as Champagne, Port, Chianti, and Burgundy. Drawing on original historical sources and multilingual archival research, it provides the first comprehensive analysis of global wine regulations from an integrated political, economic, and historical perspective.

It will appeal to a wide range of readers, including academics and students across disciplines, and anyone interested in wine and wine markets around the world.</jats:p>
