The present study does not consider alternative separation technologies, but rather systematically optimizes an existing membrane type process to optimize the removal of CO2 so as to avoid the production of off specification gas, which is costly to be generated. It is based on the commercially available hollow fiber membrane commercial cellulosic triacetate (CTA) modules, nominal capacity of 12T 0.72 MMCFD/membrane module as per Simulation. Deployments and optimizations to these modules will be explained in real time thus pressure of about 600 psi is applied to the membrane feed for optimum separation, furthermore it is mandatory to maintain a minimum CO2 concentration of the Nonpermeate within regulatory requirements (3 mol % set by Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, OGRA Pakistan) for feeds containing approximately 22 mol % CO2. In line pressure, flow rate and temperature data are measured, while composition data are measured simultaneously from an online gas chromatograph sampling the feed, Nonpermeate and permeate streams. This data is fed to a supervisory machine learning layer which predict the behavior of the Nonpermeate CO2 concentration and provide appropriate set point values for required feed pressure, flow rate and temperature. If an excess of CO2 is detected, the controller provides predictive value for the CO2 rich stream thus decreasing the CO2 concentration in the stream prior to exceeding the Nonpermeate specification by controlling the flowrate. On the other hand, a decrease CO2 in the feed provide an operational slack that will allow a safe increase in throughput. This has resulted in a closed-loop, human in the loop configuration with significant improvements in process stability, hydrocarbon recovery, and significant reduction in off specification events using Artificial Intelligence. The study thereby presents a feasibility of real time sweetening of natural gas by machine learning & Artificial Intelligence in an industrially viable way.</jats:p>

title: The Whole Worker: Integrating Occupational Health Risk Management and Mental Wellbeing in the Middle East Energy Sector
container-title: ADIPEC
a255ed38d9ea3bbbaadc6633f6f1aaf3764b8fdc.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Energy sector workers in the Middle East face a dual burden that conventional health, safety, and environment (HSE) frameworks have historically addressed in isolation: physical occupational health risks, including non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and chronic conditions, and mental health challenges, including burnout, psychosocial stress, and rotational isolation. This paper presents an integrated Occupational Health and Mental Wellbeing (OHMW) model developed by a global health and security risk management organisation and field-validated across Gulf energy operations between 2021 and 2025.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The methodology integrates operational data, electronic medical record (EMR)-derived health surveillance, and workforce wellbeing programme outputs from energy sector clients across the region, applying a dual-track analytical approach within a governance framework aligned to ISO 45003:2021. The OHMW model comprises four interconnected elements: workplace health risk assessments covering physical hazards and psychosocial stressors; structured pre-deployment medical screening addressing NCD burden and psychological vulnerability; integrated digital health surveillance monitoring physical and psychosocial key performance indicators (KPIs); and continuous remote clinical and psychological support services.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Results demonstrate that the integrated model produces outcomes exceeding those achieved through siloed programmes: a 38% reduction (relative to pre-programme baselines within the same operations) in medical evacuations driven by early NCD detection and structured chronic disease management; a 28% reduction (against the same pre-programme baselines) in sick leave and absenteeism among cohorts receiving integrated wellbeing support; and clear evidence of convergence effects, whereby workers with unmanaged chronic physical conditions exhibit elevated psychosocial risk and workers with poor mental health show higher rates of NCD complications and occupational injury. These findings confirm that the conventional separation of occupational health and mental health management represents a critical governance gap in the energy sector, and that a unified, clinically co-governed model is more effective, more efficient, and directly supportive of Duty of Care obligations in the region's most demanding operational environments.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Stealthy Fraudulent Data Injection Attacks in Modern Digital Energy Systems
container-title: ADIPEC
87902d4f95f676b6e97c16c32a196f67158ddc60.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The increasing digitalization of modern energy systems through Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and smart metering technologies has significantly enhanced operational efficiency, monitoring capabilities, and system automation. However, the widespread adoption of interconnected digital devices has also expanded the cybersecurity attack surface, exposing energy systems to sophisticated cyber threats, including Fraudulent Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs). These attacks manipulate energy measurement data in transit, compromising data integrity and potentially leading to incorrect operational decisions and fraudulent billing. Traditional detection techniques, including Bad Data Detection (BDD), have proven ineffective against stealthy FDIAs that can evade conventional validation mechanisms. This paper presents a machine-learning-based framework for detecting stealthy fraudulent data-injection attacks in digital energy systems. A realistic AMI simulation testbed was developed using virtualized digital energy meters, communication protocol simulators, and a controlled attack environment to generate both benign and malicious datasets. Network traffic was captured using Wireshark, and a dataset comprising selected communication and protocol features was constructed through preprocessing, feature selection, encoding, and normalization procedures. A total of 33 network- and application-layer features were used to develop the FDIA detection model. Four unsupervised machine learning algorithms, namely Isolation Forest (IF), One- Class Support Vector Machine (OC-SVM), Local Outlier Factor (LOF), and Elliptic Envelope (EE), were trained exclusively on benign operational data and evaluated using a test dataset containing both normal and FDIA-generated malicious samples. Comparative performance analysis was conducted using confusion matrices, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), balanced accuracy, and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC). Experimental results demonstrate that the Local Outlier Factor algorithm achieved the best overall performance, achieving 95.8% accuracy, 97.2% balanced accuracy, 92.2% F1-score, an MCC of 0.899, and perfect recall and AUROC of 1.000, successfully detecting all fraudulent data-injection attacks without any false negatives. The findings confirm that density-based anomaly detection techniques provide superior capability for identifying stealthy FDIAs in digital energy communication networks. The proposed framework offers an effective and scalable approach for strengthening cybersecurity, preserving data integrity, and enhancing the resilience of modern smart energy infrastructures</jats:p>

title: Tech-Enabled Recruitment Architecture for the Digital Energy Workforce
container-title: ADIPEC
229b5a01feaa5fffa5a46a8d60af5c8adca654ca.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Energy sector organizations face persistent speed, accuracy, and fairness challenges in recruiting digitally skilled professionals, placing them at a disadvantage against technology firms competing for the same talent pool. At nuclear power generation organizations, this challenge is compounded by workforce scale and heterogeneity: recruitment must simultaneously serve high-volume outage staffing, safety-critical license-gated roles, specialized engineering and maintenance functions, and a large managed-service contractor population, often within a single hiring cycle.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper proposes the architecture and implementation roadmap for a tech-enabled recruitment platform designed to accelerate identification, assessment, and selection of digital and specialized talent at a UAE nuclear energy organization. The proposed platform comprises four integrated components: a natural language processing (NLP) pipeline for semantic skills extraction using domain-specific entity recognition trained on energy sector role taxonomies, including verification screening for regulatory-gated roles; adaptive technical assessments calibrated to demonstrated capability across architecture, cloud, data engineering, and AI/ML competency areas; a structured interview scoring model using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) attribution designed to make cross-evaluator inconsistencies detectable and auditable; and end-to-end workflow automation integrated with the organization's HRMS. Candidate data governance is designed around a privacy-by-design framework with consent management, data minimization, and a full audit trail.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Industry-wide benchmarks indicate the scale of efficiency gain such platforms can plausibly deliver: recent survey data from SHRM and LinkedIn indicate that organizations using AI in recruiting report material time and workload reductions in screening and administrative tasks, while independent academic literature on explainable AI demonstrates that SHAP-based attribution is a validated method for detecting bias in automated hiring decisions. This paper uses these external benchmarks, together with the organization's recruitment volumes and role diversity, to establish anticipated outcome ranges and a proposed evaluation framework for the platform, rather than reporting outcomes from a completed deployment.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The paper concludes that tech-enabled recruitment is a strategic operational capability for nuclear and broader energy organizations, and that designing governance transparency, including algorithmic explainability and candidate data rights, into the platform from the outset positions transparency as a talent attraction differentiator rather than a compliance cost.</jats:p>

title: Pore-Scale Prediction of Apparent and Relative Permeability in Continental Shale Using Deep-Learning-Enhanced Digital Rocks
container-title: ADIPEC
a06e0bed7fa85a83e7d4a70861adc9888cb70ded.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate characterization of multiphase flow in continental shale remains challenging because of ultra-low permeability, nanoscale confinement effects, and the difficulty of conducting representative core-flooding experiments. This study presents a pore-scale simulation framework that integrates deep-learning-enhanced digital rock reconstruction with pore network modeling (PNM). The framework is applied to investigate nonlinear single- and two-phase flow behaviors and to quantify the effects of boundary-layer phenomena, wettability, and fluid properties on apparent and relative permeability.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A three-dimensional digital rock model was reconstructed from focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) images with an initial resolution of 9.4 nm. To overcome the tradeoff between field of view and imaging resolution, a deep-learning-based super-resolution algorithm was employed to enhance the image resolution to 4.7 nm prior to PNM extraction. To simulate nonlinear flow behavior, an open-source PNM simulator was modified by incorporating upscaled molecular-simulation results to capture nanoscale boundary-layer effects. The enhanced model dynamically evaluates apparent permeability and two-phase relative permeability under varying pressure gradients, fluid viscosities, interfacial tensions (IFT), and mixed-wettability conditions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The extracted pore network exhibits a highly compact structure dominated by pores ranging from 5 to 25 nm and throats ranging from 15 to 40 nm, with limited connectivity. Single-phase flow simulations demonstrate pronounced nonlinear flow behavior, where apparent permeability increases with pressure gradient because of the progressive weakening of boundary-layer effects. In addition, fluids with higher viscosity require disproportionately larger pressure gradients to achieve effective transport. For two-phase flow, incorporation of boundary-layer effects slightly increases oil relative permeability while decreasing water relative permeability, primarily because water adsorption along pore walls reduces the effective flow volume available to the aqueous phase. Mixed wettability also strongly influences displacement behavior, and a lower oil-wet fraction preferentially distributed in larger pores is found to enhance shale oil recovery. Furthermore, increasing oil viscosity shifts the crossover point of the relative permeability curves toward the lower-left region, indicating greater resistance during waterflooding. In contrast, higher IFT shifts the crossover point toward the upper-right region, suggesting enhanced capillary-driven displacement during imbibition.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study establishes a multiscale workflow that links molecular-scale boundary-layer effects with pore-scale flow evaluation in continental shale reservoirs. By enabling dynamic prediction of apparent and relative permeability without reliance on costly and time-consuming physical core-flooding experiments, the proposed method provides a practical and physics-informed foundation for optimizing shale oil development and evaluating displacement efficiency.</jats:p>

title: An Operator-Configurable Digital Twin of Multiphase Flow Metering: PVT Configuration Impact and a Physics-Featured Neural Networks Estimator
container-title: ADIPEC
bd2293e89c51c695aed5973e6f5bf2544e689523.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Physical multiphase flow meters calculate phase rates in vendor firmware using a configuration unknown to the operator: a fixed pressure-volume-temperature description, assumed water salinity, measured attenuation coefficients, mixing rules and separator conditions. Fluids evolve and characterizations are revised, but the configuration is on the vendor's schedule, and an operator with several hundred metered wells cannot check if an upcoming change will be beneficial or confirm after the fact except by asking the vendor. This paper describes how to create an operator-configurable digital twin of the meter. A parallel version of the same measurement chain reads raw historian signals, re-solves the phase holdups independently, and uses the operator's own equation of state. The twin reproduces vendor phase fractions to better than one percentage point and total mass rate to about two per cent, when run with the vendor's fluid model on identical raw signals for seven wells spanning electrical impedance and multi-energy gamma attenuation. Using the operator's own equation of state shows how much the fluid description is worth. The effect is technology-dependent: it shows up on impedance meters at the line-to-standard conversion (moving oil rate 5 to 6 per cent, water cut up to 1.5 percentage points) and directly in the holdup inversion for gamma meters. Most significantly, gas-oil ratio moves 5 to 15 per cent overall. Water salinity is shown to be a first-order factor driving water cut on gamma meters and negligible on impedance meters on permittivity mode. Finally, we use a small neural estimator, driven by features generated by a mechanistic choke model, to extend availability through meter outages, matching total mass rate to about 7 per cent on a past-to-future forecast. The contribution is that the vendor computation chain can be reproduced outside vendor firmware and its configuration items quantified, returning configuration control to the operator at asset scale.</jats:p>

title: From Diagnosis to Digital Execution: AI-Enabled Materials Management for High-Intensity Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
b468ba2461e8600618ede202ccc9794aa34ad6c9.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In high-intensity energy operations, material availability depends on more than the accuracy of an enterprise resource planning inventory balance. A component may be recorded as available and still be unusable because its location, condition, certification or readiness for the work cannot be confirmed. The resulting searches, expediting, emergency purchasing and workarounds create a form of operational friction that is often managed locally until the cumulative effect appears in maintenance delay, lost productivity, excess working capital or avoidable logistics activity.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A diagnostic-led transformation method is presented using practitioner evidence from energy and other asset-intensive operations. The method combines site engagement, benchmarking, value stream mapping, direct process observation and data analysis to identify where material flow is breaking down. Critical-to-quality requirements are then translated into a future-state operating model before the digital architecture is selected. Typical execution controls include master-data remediation, barcode or Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) identification, mobile warehouse tasks, two-way Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) integration, automated exception workflows, supplier-performance visibility, risk-based inventory policy and AI-enabled optimisation where the data and decision are suitable for probabilistic modelling.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Across the case evidence, digitally controlled execution produced material improvements in processing speed, traceability, training burden, inventory performance and logistics flow. The strongest results did not come from technology deployed in isolation. They came from removing process variation, clarifying ownership and decision rights, improving data quality and then using digital tools to enforce the redesigned flow. The approach is particularly applicable to Middle Eastern operations, where large-scale energy investment, complex contractor ecosystems, remote and offshore logistics, localisation objectives and high expectations for uptime increase the cost of material uncertainty. Materials management is therefore treated here as an operational assurance discipline supported by digital and AI capability, rather than as a transactional warehouse function.</jats:p>

title: Digital Optimization of Hoist Scheduling to Improve Workover Efficiency in Mature Fields: A Case Study from PDO's Nimr Cluster
container-title: ADIPEC
a667c90abbc65d3fb8ab2a889fec76f6751dc694.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Nimr Cluster, located in southern Oman and operated by Petroleum Development Oman (PDO), is the largest producing asset in the country, comprising 23 oil fields and more than 3,000 drilled wells. As a mature asset, sustaining production relies heavily on well intervention activities to address increasing water cut, aging infrastructure, and integrity-related challenges. More than 1,200 hoist interventions are executed annually, making efficient planning and deployment of intervention resources essential for minimizing production deferment and reducing Restoration Cycle Time (RCT).</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Historically, hoist planning relied on spreadsheet-based workflows requiring manual consolidation of operational, production, integrity, and logistical data from multiple independent systems. This fragmented process was time-intensive, susceptible to human error, and limited the ability to optimize intervention priorities in response to rapidly changing field conditions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents the development and deployment of the Hoist Sequence Optimizer (HSO), an end-user-driven digital decision-support platform developed to transform hoist planning through automated data integration, standardized prioritization, and optimized intervention sequencing. The platform consolidates information from multiple corporate databases and applies structured ranking logic based on production impact, integrity urgency, operational readiness, and logistical constraints to generate dynamic workover schedules that support daily operational decision-making.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Field implementation of HSO reduced planning effort by approximately 90%, significantly improved planning transparency, and enhanced collaboration between production, well engineering, and operations teams. The optimized planning process also contributed to an approximate 20% reduction in Restoration Cycle Time by improving resource utilization, minimizing hoist idle time, and accelerating the restoration of deferred wells.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The results demonstrate that field-developed digital solutions can deliver substantial operational and business value without reliance on commercial optimization software. The HSO framework provides a scalable and transferable approach for modernizing well intervention planning and supporting digital transformation initiatives across mature oil and gas assets.</jats:p>

title: Pore-Scale Guided Particle-Size Selection for Multistage Profile Control in Porous Carbonate Reservoirs Using CNN-Assisted Digital Rock Modeling
container-title: ADIPEC
5fdc869a094825562c21e67834524e3178054074.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Carbonate reservoirs commonly exhibit complex pore architectures and strong heterogeneity, which promote the formation of preferential flow paths during waterflooding. As a result, injected water may circulate through highly conductive channels, thereby reducing sweep efficiency. To quantitatively optimize particle sizes for profile control and water plugging in horizontal wells, this study proposes a pore-scale multistage profile-control method based on convolutional neural network (CNN)-assisted digital rock modeling. Sequential micro-CT images were processed using a CNN to enhance image quality and reconstruct a three-dimensional digital rock model that captures pore structure and connectivity. Waterflooding simulations were then conducted to locate dominant water-flow paths, followed by statistical characterization of pore-throat radius distributions within these channels. Based on the characteristic pore-throat sizes controlling preferential flow, a matching relationship between plugging-particle size and pore-throat scale was established to guide multistage particle selection for channels of different sizes. The results show that CNN-assisted reconstruction improves the representation of pore geometry and connectivity, while the pore-throat size distributions of preferential channels provide a quantitative basis for particle classification and matching. A graded particle system applied in a large-to-small sequence can progressively block highly conductive channels at multiple scales, redistribute the injection profile, and suppress ineffective water cycling. The proposed workflow integrates digital rock reconstruction, preferential-channel detection, pore-throat analysis, and multistage particle-size optimization, providing quantitative guidance for particle-based profile control in waterflooded horizontal wells in porous carbonate reservoirs.</jats:p>

title: Lessons from the Collaborative Adoption of Digital Pressure Testing Technology to Improve Offshore Drilling Efficiency and Barrier Assurance
container-title: ADIPEC
dee697dbc7d14247996c42cda5bde03e33598879.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper shares lessons learned from a successful deployment of advanced digital pressure testing technology aboard a jack-up rig for a major operator. It covers best practices for integrating real-time, physics-based pressure test analytics into offshore drilling workflows, and shows how the approach improves operational efficiency and strengthens well barrier assurance without compromising technical integrity.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The digital pressure testing platform was integrated into existing rig workflows to support real-time analysis of BOP testing along with positive and negative well barrier pressure tests. The system used live data streaming and automated, thermally compensated leak detection to evaluate pressure behaviour against objective, physics-based criteria, replacing conventional time-based or subjective interpretation methods. Over 150 pressure tests were conducted across a seven-month period.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Successful implementation relied on close tri-party collaboration between operator, drilling contractor personnel, and in-house technical advisors. Early crew engagement, familiar user interfaces, clearly defined operational thresholds, and iterative feedback loops drove sustained adoption.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The deployment delivered measurable operational gains while improving confidence in barrier verification. Critical-path BOP test duration fell by nearly 50%, high pressure hold times dropped by more than 40%, and non-productive troubleshooting time was reduced through the campaign. These benefits came without any trade-off in technical assurance, actually sharpening integrity evaluation as it identified cases where tests passed conventional decline-rate thresholds but failed thermodynamic analysis, revealing barrier weaknesses that traditional methods would have missed.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A critical finding from this case history is that adoption success wasn't dependent on technology performance alone. The human-technology interface, integration with existing rig software, and alignment between operator, drilling contractor, and service provider proved equally decisive. Rig personnel and technical advisors worked closely to optimise system performance, so the digital tools supported established operational routines rather than disrupting them.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The paper concludes that real-time digital pressure testing offers a replicable, field-validated model for offshore drilling operations looking to reduce critical-path time, minimize troubleshooting, and strengthen well integrity management. Drawing on the perspectives of operator, drilling contractor, and service provider, it sets out a practical tri-party adoption framework for digital technologies in offshore well operations, centred on human-machine interaction as the deciding factor in deployment success.</jats:p>

title: Scaling the Outcrop: An Integrated Cross-Scale Correlation Engine Bridging 3D Geological Outcrop Digital Twins with Subsurface Wellbore Analytics
container-title: ADIPEC
889197ed16c34f0f36e9ae61db1a028b494a4e7d.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives/Scope</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In complex hydrocarbon exploration, particularly within ultra-deep or frontier plays, the scarcity of offset well data often leads to significant geological uncertainty during drilling deployment. Field outcrop studies supply the analogs used to close that gap, but an interpreted outcrop section is rarely registered to the same spatial and depth reference frame as the wells it informs. This paper reports the third development stage of a 3D geological outcrop digital twin platform — a cross-scale correlation engine that places an interpreted outcrop section onto a well's true-vertical-depth axis. It is deliberately positioned as a validation-framework contribution, not an applied field-validation study: it defines, freezes, and audits the geometry-level registration workflow and establishes the numerical control a later field campaign can test against. No paired outcrop-and-well field dataset is reported here.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods, Procedures, Process</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The engine sits on an established foundation — UAV oblique photogrammetry, structure-from-motion reconstruction, RTK ground control, lithofacies segmentation — none of it claimed as new. Three elements are specified in full. A three-dimensional bedding-normal projection converts interpreted contacts to cumulative true stratigraphic thickness without assuming a section perpendicular to strike. A weighted multi-horizon affine model registers cumulative thickness to true vertical depth subsea, fitted on declared anchor horizons only. An auditable composite score ranks candidate outcrop-to-formation pairings on stratigraphic name, lithology, relative position, and marker-bed evidence. Lacking a paired field dataset, numerical behavior was examined through a disclosed synthetic benchmark: a nested ablation over 1,000 Monte Carlo realizations with ten held-out horizons, and a 4,000-trial semantic-mapping stress test with an 80-variant weight-sensitivity grid. Every parameter, equation, weight, and random seed is reported.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results, Observations, Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Under the declared synthetic uncertainty model, the ablation reduced mean held-out-horizon RMSE from 4.67 m for apparent thickness tied to a single datum, to 2.01 m after three-dimensional bedding-normal projection, and to 0.27 m after four-anchor affine registration, with 98.96% empirical coverage against a nominal 95% prediction interval. The deliberately ambiguous stress test raised top-1 matching accuracy from 42.45% for name similarity alone to 91.68% for the composite score, which stayed above the name-only baseline in all 80 weight variants. These figures establish synthetic self-consistency: the equations recover a truth the generator itself constructed. They are explicitly not measurements of field accuracy, geological predictive skill, or operational efficiency. Prototype runs on a marine pilot block confirm only that the pipeline executes end to end inside a standard multi-well correlation panel.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Significance/Novelty</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The novelty lies in integration and auditability rather than in the underlying technologies. UAV photogrammetry, SfM processing, RTK positioning, and pseudo-well construction are established practice; what is new is the reproducible chain binding them — explicit three-dimensional thickness formulation, multi-anchor depth registration, traceable semantic mapping, and a stated boundary between synthetic verification and field validation. Publishing that chain in full makes the workflow transferable rather than site-specific. A preregistered paired field campaign using these frozen equations and metrics is the declared next step.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Adaptive Microbubble Hull Lubrication for Fuel and Emission Reduction in Offshore Fleets
container-title: ADIPEC
9df0246a03237698082df9d6ebe25ac6c9f5ac12.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Offshore construction and support vessels operate across transit, standby, maneuvering, dynamic-positioning, and port modes. This variable duty makes a constant-flow air-lubrication system inefficient: compressor demand can consume the hydrodynamic benefit when speed is low, draft or trim changes, or bubbles escape from the treated bottom area. This paper develops an engineered, vessel level method for adaptive microbubble hull lubrication that controls air flow by zone to maximize measured net power reduction rather than gross drag reduction. The method combines a resistance decomposition, an isentropic compressor model, a bounded optimizer, and an on/off verification protocol. It is applied to a non-confidential reference offshore vessel (75m length between perpendiculars, 18 m beam, 5 m draft, 1,700 m2 wetted area, and 1.6 MW baseline shaft power at 10kn). All case results are simulation, not our sea-trial claims. At 10 kens, a base design assumption of 60% frictional share,55% treated-area fraction, and 35% local friction reduction give 185 kw gross propulsion power reduction. After 90 kw air-system demand, the modeled net reduction is 95 kw, or 5.9%. Across a representative 6,000-h annual duty cycle, the adaptive controller runs mainly above 8 and produces about 349 MWh/y net energy saving corresponding to 68 t/y marine diesel oil and 218 t/y CO2 at 195 g/kwh and 3.206 t-CO2 /t- fuel. Sensitivity analysis identifies achieved local drag reduction, transit hours, and treated area as the dominant variables. The contribution is a practical retrofit architecture and a falsifiable measurement plan: alternating system-on/system – off trial legs, direct shaft and blower metering, environmental correction, uncertainty reporting, and acceptance based on net-not gross- power. The analysis supports a gated pilot; it does not justify fleet deployment without full-scale validation.</jats:p>

title: Digital Twin-Driven Optimization in Natural Gas Processing: Methodology and Applications
container-title: ADIPEC
9186c5a36dfb1249daa1541085ea0eb32d434c2b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper aims to develop a practical methodology for digital twin-driven optimization in natural gas processing plants, addressing key practical challenges of low process efficiency, high energy consumption, and heavy reliance on operator experience. Focusing on two core processes—LPG recovery and gas decarbonization-dehydration—the study demonstrates the framework's adaptability across diverse unit operations. It seeks to validate the methodology's capability to boost product yield and reduce energy use, thereby improving operational stability and sustainability in the natural gas industry.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>SLB digital twin technology implements an integrated Real-Time Optimization (RTO) and Advanced Process Control (APC) system on an industrial Edge IoT platform at the terminal. A high-fidelity, first-principles model built with Symmetry™ was executed locally on the Edge device, leveraging real-time data. It carried out continuous optimization to minimize total energy consumption while meeting all process and product constraints. The resulting optimized operating conditions were generated and directly applied at the Edge through the APC system. The comprehensive implementation, involving data analysis, rigorous modeling, and validation, ensured the solution's accuracy, robustness, and reliable performance under variable conditions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The methodology delivered significant, validated results in two distinct application cases. In Gaolan natural gas terminal, the digital twin system increased the LPG recovery rate from 93.5% to over 95%, generating estimated annual economic benefits on the order of tens of millions of Chinese Yuan (RMB) while concurrently reducing specific energy consumption. In the decarbonization and dehydration unit of a Yanchang Petroleum CPF facility, the system effectively lowered the unit's energy consumption per volume of gas processed by optimizing amine circulation rates and regenerator operation. Key observations from both deployments include the system's consistent high model convergence rate (exceeding 95%), good robustness, and its notable contribution to enhanced process stability and reduced reliance on operator practical judgement.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In conclusion, this work successfully establishes a verifiable, replicable, and economically impactful universal Edge-enabled digital twin methodology for the continuous optimization of core natural gas processing operations. This study presents an industrial application of an Edge-deployed digital twin for real-time optimization in China's natural gas processing. Combining first-principles simulation with real-time data at the Edge enables immediate decision-making and reliable, cloud-independent optimization. The achieved gains in efficiency and stability demonstrate the solution's scalability, establishing a practical reference for improving economic and operational performance across the industry.</jats:p>

title: Adaptive Operating Strategy: Future-Proofing Helico-Axial Multiphase Pump Reliability and Efficiency Under Evolving Operating Conditions
container-title: ADIPEC
afee3dc27e4137485fb54c8aa6faaaaff9a43cf4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Helico-axial multiphase pumps have played an important role in sustaining production from remote and maturing onshore assets by boosting unseparated well fluids, reducing dependency on additional surface separation facilities, and supporting efficient hydrocarbon evacuation. As reservoir and process conditions evolve across the asset life, however, pump duty can progressively shift from the original design assumptions. Variations in gas volume fraction, water cut, total flow, fluid properties, suction pressure, discharge backpressure, slug severity, and solids loading can affect hydraulic stability, mechanical loading, auxiliary-system performance, and overall package reliability. This created a clear need to move beyond a fixed operating philosophy and time-based overhaul approach toward a cost effective, condition-driven strategy aligned with reliability, production assurance, lifecycle-cost optimization, and operational excellence.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a practical case study in which an adaptive operating and maintenance strategy was developed for a critical Helico-axial multiphase pumping service. The approach integrates operating-envelope surveillance, process and machinery trend reviews, failure-mode assessment, lubricant and seal-system monitoring, inspection evidence, condition-based overhauling, maintainability improvements, critical-spares planning and procurement, and qualification of competent in-country repair capability under defined technical and quality controls. The strategy converts changing field conditions into clear operating responses and lifecycle maintenance scheme.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The case demonstrates measurable value creation through disciplined asset management. The major-overhaul interval was safely extended by 40% above the original planning basis following structured condition assessment and multidisciplinary governance. Post-overhaul workshop inspection provided important validation of the condition and performance monitoring approach. The findings reinforced the need for continuous tracking of process conditions, vibration levels, lubrication sample analysis, seal-system performance, reviewing alarms and trips history. Technical issues were addressed through structured review and support from a qualified independent service provider with relevant capability in multiphase pump repair and mechanical seal systems. In parallel, critical spares and specialized services were managed through a competitive tendering process to secure technically acceptable solutions, optimize maintenance cost, and reduce dependency on long-lead repair options. This integrated approach helped avoid extended downtime during repair and maintenance activities while supporting production assurance, maintainability, and lifecycle-cost optimization. The revised execution model also achieved a significant reduction in overhaul cost by 60% through qualified in-country repair capability, supporting broader objectives for operational resilience, cost efficiency, industrial value creation, and sustainable lifecycle management. The revised maintenance approach also incorporated laser scanning and dimensional verification of critical components during overhaul to improve the accuracy of inspection, reverse engineering, manufacturing, repair, and refurbishment decisions. This capability supported precise assessment of material specification, dimension, clearances, fit-up conditions, and design tolerances for the parts, enabling technically controlled restoration rather than default replacement. By integrating repair and refurbishment of mechanical seals and associated components directly with original manufacturer of the seal system having local service center. This enhanced readiness helped optimize maintenance repair and overhaul duration, avoid unnecessary production impact, reduce dependence on long-lead replacement parts, and support extension of the overhaul interval through a condition-based maintenance strategy aligned with production assurance, cost efficiency, and sustainable asset lifecycle management.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The outcome of this shows that future-proof reliability and efficient operation can be achieved through practical lifecycle-management framework for Helico-axial multiphase pumps that links reservoir and process evolution to operating-envelope control, degradation mechanisms, condition-based maintenance, supply-chain resilience, and production assurance. This approach supports strategic priorities to maximize asset value, enhance equipment availability, strengthen local capability, and deliver safe, reliable, and efficient operations.</jats:p>

title: Predictable Execution Through Quantitative Evidence of Digital Unification Across a Multi-Billion-Dollar LNG Megaproject
container-title: ADIPEC
88445bbe4d4f4472a5f36e16ff1d3778ac3adae7.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Large LNG megaprojects continue to experience schedule overruns and execution variability due to fragmented workflows, disconnected engineering and construction information, and inconsistent visibility of evolving execution conditions. This study evaluates how a Digital Construction Block-enabled execution framework can connect project information across hierarchical work packages and support more context-rich execution management within a live LNG construction environment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods, Procedures, Process</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study examined operational reporting populations and historical analytical records generated at different stages of execution. The retained evidence included more than 4,000 Installation Work Packages spanning Civil, Mechanical, and Piping scopes, together with wider Construction Work Package reporting, engineering-release information, IWP status, piping and material records, and planned and forecast schedule information.</jats:p>
                    <jats:p>Digital Construction Blocks were used as structured execution units connecting Engineering Work Packages, Construction Work Packages, and Installation Work Packages with associated engineering, package-status, material, and schedule information. The analysis examined whether aggregated management indicators retained traceability to identifiable work packages and whether planned and forecast schedule conditions could be interpreted in relation to the engineering and construction scope potentially affected.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results, Observations, Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The case-study results demonstrate that the digital execution environment established hierarchical visibility across substantial engineering and installation work-package populations. Engineering-release and IWP-status information could be consolidated into management and leadership views while retaining relationships with underlying areas, disciplines, Construction Work Packages, Installation Work Package types, and individual packages. Discipline-specific piping analytics also connected line-level scope with bill-of-materials, procurement, delivery, and allocation information.</jats:p>
                    <jats:p>Planned-versus-forecast schedule reporting associated engineering forecast timing with planned and forecast Construction Work Package execution dates, enabling potential schedule exposure to be examined against identifiable scope. However, differences between live operational populations and retained historical datasets, together with incomplete actual dates and man-hour records, prevented defensible project-wide normalization of planned-versus-actual performance or causal attribution of execution outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Novel Information</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper provides field-based evidence of a Digital Construction Block-enabled information architecture operating at LNG-megaproject scale. Unlike approaches focused primarily on standalone dashboards or consolidated reporting, the framework preserves relationships between engineering information, hierarchical work packaging, package status, material information, and planned and forecast schedule conditions. The case demonstrates how this connected structure can support execution traceability and context-rich management visibility while identifying data governance as a prerequisite for reliable advanced analytics. The architecture also provides a foundation for future readiness assessment, package-centric constraint management, quality analytics, mobile field reporting, and machine-assisted decision support, although these additional capabilities were not deployed or evaluated on the case-study project.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Adaptive Geosteering in Tight Heterogeneous Clastic Gas Reservoirs- A Case Study from the Mandapeta Formation
container-title: ADIPEC
d8751c8c516d12c09851aa52d489e1170c0b79bb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Mandapeta (MDP) Formation of the Krishna-Godavari (KG) onshore Basin represents a challenging tight-gas reservoir characterized by significant geological heterogeneity, rapid lateral facies variations, stratigraphic pinch-outs, and structurally compartmentalized fault closures and mineral digenesis. Even though sands are characterized by the medium-coarse grained wit</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>h average effective porosity leads to good storage capacity; micro pore throat, pore filling and pore lining minerals imposing limitation on flowing capacity. Hence permeability is the great delimiting factor in MDP sands to be exploited in conventional methods. Exploitation strategies in the field have largely relied on hydraulic fracturing (HF) to improve reservoir contact and stimulate production. However, the presence of numerous thin shale intercalations within the reservoir interval frequently compromises fracture containment, resulting in undesirable vertical fracture growth and sub-optimal stimulation effectiveness.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents an alternative reservoir exploitation strategy focused on maximizing natural drainage through precise horizontal well placement enabled by Ultra-Deep Azimuthal Resistivity (UDAR) inversions and advanced geosteering workflows. Real-time UDAR measurements provided extensive look-ahead and look-around capabilities, allowing accurate mapping of reservoir boundaries, identification of approaching shale barriers, and proactive trajectory adjustments within the most productive sand units.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The integrated workflow combined the feasibility modelling with offset wells' Log data along with formation tops, pre-drill geological uncertainty assessment, real-time inversion interpretation, and geosteering decision making to maintain optimal reservoir exposure across complex heterogeneous intervals. The results demonstrated that accurate placement of horizontal wells within high-quality reservoir compartments significantly increased reservoir contact, enhanced production potential, and reduced dependence on hydraulic fracturing. The successful placement of the well, highlights how modern geosteering technologies can transform and development strategies in highly heterogeneous tight-gas reservoirs and turn them into tangible barrels of hydrocarbon.</jats:p>

title: Advancing Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) Plant Decarbonisation Through Extra High Voltage (EHV) Electrification, Digital Control, and Commissioning Excellence
container-title: ADIPEC
ae478a6457485c108897714f123537791de982d5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This project is a strategic initiative advancing the Company's energy transition agenda by decarbonising power supply to Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) facilities through integration with grid‑based renewable energy. By replacing conventional Gas Turbine Generators (GTGs) with a 275kV Extra High Voltage (EHV) grid connection delivering up to 90 MW, the project directly accelerates Net‑Zero Carbon (NZC) ambitions through significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and carbon intensity produced by the conventional Gas Turbine Generators (GTGs) by reduced direct combustion of fuel gas and reduce GHG emissions (CO2e) from the combustion in PLANT which generates a GHG index of 0.916 tCO2e/MWh. Beyond emissions reduction, it delivers substantial operational and economic value through optimized fuel gas utilisation, reduced reliance on carbon‑intensive generation, and enhanced energy efficiency. The transition strengthens system reliability and resilience via diversified power sources, while enabling a seamless and sustainable conversion within a brownfield environment—positioning the facility as a benchmark low‑carbon LNG operation.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The project adopts an integrated power system engineering approach covering engineering design, procurement, construction, installation, and commissioning of 275 kV EHV substations and its utilities, transformers, switchgear, protection relays, and Energy Network Management Control Systems (ENMCS). Key processes include integration with existing facilities, grid‑plant synchronization, protection coordination, dynamic load transfer, and stability validation under multiple operating scenarios. Execution is anchored on a risk‑based commissioning methodology, strengthened by the Smooth Start‑Up Program (SSP) and Operations Readiness Assurance (ORA) framework to ensure disciplined sequencing, operational readiness, and safe transition. Digital monitoring, real‑time control, and advanced simulations further optimize system performance, enhance energy efficiency, and minimize emissions, aligning execution with Net Zero Carbon (NZC) and sustainability objectives.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The project delivers significant environmental, operational, and strategic impact. Through systematic displacement of few gas‑based generation with imported grid power, implemented via controlled synchronization and phased load ramp‑up, it achieves substantial reductions in fuel gas consumption, flaring, and reduce CO2 emissions. This transition lowers overall carbon intensity while improving energy efficiency and stability of operations. Operationally, it enhances reliability, optimizes fuel gas utilisation for higher‑value use, and improves energy resilience. The integration of Smooth Start Up Programme (SSP) and Operation Readiness Assurance (ORA) ensures controlled energization, minimizes inefficiencies, and enables a seamless transition without disruption, delivering consistent, low‑emission performance.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The project establishes a benchmark for grid electrification in brownfield LNG facilities whereby conventional downstream plant is using Gas Turbine Generator for providing electricity. Its novelty lies in combining advanced EHV engineering, digital control systems, and commissioning‑led execution within a live operating plant and smooth load transfer without interrupting plant operation. Key differentiators include early interface alignment, strong technical assurance governance, and zero‑downtime integration. It demonstrates how disciplined electrification and execution can accelerate sustainable energy transition while maintaining operational integrity, reliability, and long‑term low‑carbon performance.</jats:p>

title: The Invisible Pivot: Forensic Identification of Digital Cascade Triggers in Port and Maritime Logistics Infrastructure
container-title: ADIPEC
8de159a964b180d19ca040ca771946befbee3489.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Conventional resilience audits of port and maritime logistics infrastructure concentrate on physical assets: cranes, quay walls, breakwaters, and berths. This paper argues that the assets most likely to trigger a systemic cascade are frequently invisible to that inventory: digital command systems, financial clearing rails, and single-operator authority nodes that carry no tonnage, yet determine whether a terminal can continue to function once a shock arrives. This framework paper develops a structured vulnerability-mapping methodology across six infrastructure layers (physical, digital, human, institutional, geographic, financial), illustrated through two applications of different evidentiary character rather than a single audited case study.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Application I is hybrid: a national port authority scenario whose design draws on documented precedent, including the 2021 Transnet ransomware attack and the CSB's investigation of the 2022 BP-Husky Toledo incident, with scoring and cascade outputs generated using an AI-assisted simulation tool. It identifies the digital customs clearance ledger, not cranes, fuel systems, or vessel traffic management, as the systemic Pivot Domino. A pre-positioned, air-gapped clearance server accepting asset-backed physical collateral sustains cargo discharge for a full 72-hour autonomous window under simulated total digital network denial, and a targeted USD 90 million hardening investment is modelled to avoid USD 6.21 billion in cascade losses, a scenario projection subject to the sensitivity assumptions in Section 2.3. A companion proposed maritime resilience design framework extends these prescriptions to compound cyber-and-climate disruption, a combined threat class absent from current IMO, BIMCO (2024), and offshore logistics resilience frameworks.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Application II, an extension beyond the paper's proposed scope (Section 5), is empirical throughout, applied using only public data to a real-world free-zone and port ecosystem. It identifies two Tier-0 nodes, an external maritime chokepoint and an internal digital command hub, and quantifies a USD 299.3 billion Sentinel Risk Value (SRV) and a five-action hardening programme, costing USD 3.785 billion, projected to compress that exposure by approximately 60 % under the modelling assumptions in Section 2.3. A live regional crisis in the following months saw two of its core prescriptions independently adopted in practice; since both are standard responses to a chokepoint closure rather than distinctive predictions, this is offered as corroborating context, not a claim of demonstrated predictive validity.</jats:p>

title: Adaptive K-Value Tables with Temperature Smoothing for Robust Isenthalpic Flash Calculations in Thermal Enhanced Oil Recovery Processes
container-title: ADIPEC
2116586cfbde722b9e3ed33840e93b5b19122b5c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate and computationally efficient determination of phase equilibrium is critical in thermal reservoir simulation of enhanced oil recovery processes such as steam flooding and Steam-Assisted Gravity Drainage. The K-value table approach, as the industry standard for thermal simulators, faces two fundamental limitations that compromise both accuracy and numerical stability. First, when the reference oil phase is absent and only gas and water coexist in equilibrium, the conventional two-table framework based on gas-oil and water-oil K-values provides no thermodynamic basis to describe the phase equilibrium, leading to misidentification of the phase state. Second, wherever negative flash calculations fail to extend K-values beyond phase boundaries, the conventional practice of setting K-values to unity introduces sharp discontinuities in both K-values and their temperature derivatives. These discontinuities directly destabilize the Newton-based isenthalpic flash, which relies on smooth K-value temperature derivative terms in the Jacobian for convergent temperature iteration.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study proposes a unified adaptive K-value table framework that addresses both limitations. To resolve the reference-phase inconsistency, a supplementary gas-water K-value table with the water phase as reference is introduced and activated adaptively in P-T regions where the oil phase is absent. A computationally efficient simplified variant is also proposed, in which the phase identification criterion is modified at supercritical hydrocarbon conditions so that the dense hydrocarbon phase in equilibrium with water is retained as oil-like, eliminating the need for a separate gas-water table while preserving phase continuity. For K-values beyond phase boundaries where negative flash fails to converge, a temperature-direction extrapolation constrained by the convergence temperature concept is applied, guaranteeing smooth and differentiable K-value surfaces across the entire P-T domain.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The framework is validated against direct Peng-Robinson EOS flash calculations for three multicomponent benchmark mixtures spanning heavy oil, bitumen, and solvent injection systems. Pressure-temperature and pressure-enthalpy phase maps are constructed using isothermal and isenthalpic flash, respectively. Results demonstrate that the adaptive reference selection correctly recovers two- phase gas-water boundaries that the fixed-reference framework misidentifies entirely, and that temperature-direction extrapolation is the decisive factor enabling stable isenthalpic flash convergence near phase boundaries, eliminating the vertical discontinuities that persist without smoothing. The simplified adaptive framework achieves comparable P-T accuracy and superior P-H stability, making it particularly suitable for practical thermal simulation workflows. The proposed framework is further evaluated through a thermal compositional simulation case study, where the full adaptive and fixed adaptive approaches are compared in terms of phase distribution, recovery profiles, and reservoir average thermodynamic conditions.</jats:p>

title: Decision-Centric Energy Operations: Integrating Edge Intelligence, Operational Digital Twins, Industrial Work Surfaces, and Agentic AI
container-title: ADIPEC
bf6c1d54d7cad07b1d55bab5937476edd48befb8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Energy operators are not short of data. Most assets already have sensors, historians, supervisory systems, engineering tools, dashboards, digital twins, and a growing number of AI pilots. The harder problem starts after an event is detected. Engineers still have to bring together operating trends, work history, procedures, constraints, and approval requirements from several systems before they can make a safe decision.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper proposes a decision-centric operating architecture that connects edge intelligence, an operational digital twin, an industrial work surface, and agentic AI within a human-in-the- loop model. The layers are intentionally separated. Edge intelligence qualifies events near the asset. The digital twin adds asset context, operating state, constraints, and history. The work surface places the case into investigation, approval, and execution workflows. Agentic AI supports the engineer by retrieving evidence, invoking approved tools, checking rules, and preparing an explainable recommendation.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The pattern is intended for workflow-level deployment rather than unconstrained automation. A representative implementation pattern shows how a qualified trigger initiates context retrieval from live data, engineering documents, maintenance history, procedures, prior events, and constraint models. The agent prepares a recommendation package that exposes evidence, assumptions, alternatives, constraint checks, confidence levels, and required human approval before action.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The contribution is a practical reference pattern for moving from data visibility to decision execution. The paper emphasizes bounded AI use, evidence traceability, workflow ownership, auditability, and human authority. It does not argue for transferring accountability to autonomous systems. Instead, it shows how AI can reduce investigation effort, improve decision consistency, and give engineers and operators a clearer basis for action.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Brownfield Subsea Assets into Standardised Digital Tieback Hubs
container-title: ADIPEC
29ea8f89de105258cfb4b13763ead82a46c930d6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Future offshore subsea developments will increasingly consist of satellite wells and marginal field tiebacks connected to existing brownfield production assets rather than new standalone infrastructure. While this development model improves project economics and reduces carbon intensity, it also introduces major technical and operational challenges when integrating new subsea wells into ageing host facilities.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Many brownfield assets operate with legacy subsea control systems, proprietary OEM communication protocols, ageing umbilicals, limited communication bandwidth and constrained topside control capacity. Integrating new satellite wells into these environments often requires bespoke engineering, extensive system modifications and production shutdown windows, introducing significant cost, schedule and operational risk.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a configurable software subsea control extension architecture developed to simplify and standardise the integration of new satellite wells and marginal tiebacks into existing subsea production systems while minimising the impact on ongoing operations.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The proposed solution transforms brownfield hosts into standardised digital tieback hubs capable of supporting multiple incremental subsea developments through reuse of existing infrastructure and industrialised integration methods. The architecture combines modular retrofit-friendly subsea control units with a standardised digital integration concept that enables new subsea wells to coexist safely alongside existing subsea and topside control systems. A gateway-based software abstraction layer bridges proprietary and modern communication protocols while maintaining operational segregation, cybersecurity and system integrity.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The solution builds on practical implementation experience integrating communication interfaces across multiple subsea OEM systems and the development of a Universal Master Control System (MCS) architecture for mixed-vendor subsea environments. Lessons learned from these activities demonstrate the operational feasibility and scalability of standardised protocol abstraction and software-defined integration methods for brownfield subsea assets.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>By standardising operational data access across multiple OEM subsea systems, the architecture also establishes a unified data layer that improves visibility into equipment condition and infrastructure performance across ageing subsea assets. This creates a practical foundation for condition-based maintenance, predictive maintenance planning and future deployment of advanced operational analytics capabilities using contextualised data from mixed-vendor subsea environments.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The architecture maximises reuse of existing infrastructure, including umbilicals, hydraulic distribution systems, power supply and available communication bandwidth wherever technical margins allow. Standardised software templates, reusable integration patterns and modular control building blocks can reduce project-specific engineering, testing scope and commissioning complexity compared with traditional bespoke tieback implementations. Project experience indicates that the approach can narrow the required integration scope while avoiding major host control-system upgrades.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents: Standardised integration methods for satellite wells into brownfield subsea systemsLessons learned from multi-OEM protocol integration and communication abstractionExperience from development of universal MCS architectures for mixed-vendor subsea environmentsIndustrialised deployment concepts using standardised software templates and modular control building blocksOperational and schedule benefits associated with reduced integration complexity and avoidance of major shutdowns during tieback executionHow standardised multi-OEM operational data access can support predictive maintenance and lifecycle management strategies for ageing subsea infrastructure</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The proposed approach demonstrates how software-defined integration architectures can simplify future subsea tieback developments, unlock stranded marginal resources and extend the productive life of existing offshore infrastructure while supporting continued asset utilisation.</jats:p>

title: Digital Fracturing: Fast-Tracking UAE Unconventional Development Through Integrated Fracturing Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
75c1fb282870c5ceae85bd591766cd68c0e3f574.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents an integrated digital-fracturing methodology developed to accelerate unconventional resource development in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) by improving completion efficiency and reducing drill-to-production cycle time. It evaluates the impact of integrating digital stimulation workflows on execution consistency, operational efficiency, improved confidence in stage-level diagnostics and uncertainty reduction during early-stage hydraulic fracturing campaigns.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A two-year high-intensity fracturing campaign was monitored to evaluate operational performance and identify execution variability. A digital workflow integrating real-time data acquisition, centralized monitoring, automated stage-level diagnostics, and execution with predefined operational fences was implemented, enabling closed-loop stimulation operation control. All data were standardized across all stages and wells to enable consistent key performance indicator (KPI) tracking, automated diagnostic and post-job analysis. The approach emphasized process standardization, reducing manual intervention, and enable data-driven decision-making. Performance improvements were assessed through comparisons of operational efficiency, stage execution consistency, and non-productive time before and after implementation.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The digital workflow delivered measurable improvements in operational efficiency, execution contingency, and subsurface understanding. Standardized real-time enabled improved control of job parameters, reduced variability between stages, and enhance responsiveness to dynamic well conditions. Operational performance increased significantly, achieving sustained high-intensity operations of approximately 20 pumping hours per day, driven by reduced non-productive time, Stage-transition efficiency also improved progressively, with average time between stages decreasing from 0.80 to 0.36 hours between stages and 50 individual transitions completed in less than 10 minutes, and improved equipment utilization across fracturing fleet. Beyond operational gains, the integrated data analysis provided enhanced subsurface insights. Synchronized treatment and offset-well monitoring also improved visibility of subtle inter-well pressure responses. In an offset well monitoring case, the observed response was interpreted as consistent with stress redistribution and formation-compressibility effects rather than direct hydraulic communication. This helps to fine-tune the lateral distance and effective stimulation volume. Improved visibility of treatment behavior also supported continuous optimization of fluid and sand placement. Overall, the implementation reduced execution risk, increased efficiency, and accelerated the field learning curve, enabling faster optimization of scalable unconventional development for UAE.</jats:p>

title: Governing Citizen Development to Scale Digital Delivery and People Capability in Petroleum Engineering
container-title: ADIPEC
7c294f6d090db92022c94079914d8d1ae5dd3a01.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Digital delivery in Petroleum Development Oman's (PDO) Petroleum Engineering function had come to rest on a small central team of IT specialists, and that team could not keep up with the pace and volume of business demand. Requests for process and workflow automation, advanced analytics, visualisation and reporting, and data solutions all queued behind the same few developers. Adoption lagged where the eventual user had no hand in the build, and teams filled the gap with manual workarounds and personal spreadsheets.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In 2024, the function set up the Petroleum Engineering Digital Factory: an integrated ecosystem of technologies, competency development and process optimisation that lets domain professionals from the business, citizen developers rather than the small central team of IT specialists, build governed production solutions on approved low-code and no-code platforms. The Digital Factory came first, and PDO's corporate Digital AI Journey of Transformation (JoT) launched in 2025; the Digital Factory was then integrated into it as Petroleum Engineering's model for business-led digital delivery. Citizen developers are enabled through PDO's corporate, IT-enabled Business Enablement Programme and Unified Citizen Developer Framework, which provide governance, training, platform access and managed data access. A governed demand-routing process sends each use case either to the Digital Factory or, where enterprise-scale IT delivery is required, to the corporate IT pathway.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Delivery spans four technology capabilities: intelligent process automation, advanced analytics and machine learning and AI, data visualisation and reporting, and workflow automation, supported by data engineering and data management. Every use case runs through one governed Standard Operating Procedure, from alignment and initiation through sprint-based development to handover and sustainment, regardless of whether a citizen or professional developer builds it. Capability is developed on real, registered use cases, under coaching, against a common review standard.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The Digital Factory began in 2024 with a pilot that delivered 3 digital solutions. By mid-2026, it had delivered 30 Petroleum Engineering digital solutions, saving close to 40,000 hours of annualised capacity, close to 20 full-time equivalents (FTE), and about USD 650,000 in cost savings and avoidance. Over the same period, the function grew its citizen developer population from 1 in the 2024 pilot to 31 by mid-2026, and citizen developers built 19 of the 30 delivered solutions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Registered demand, meanwhile, grew to double the annual commitment, leaving a funnel of further use cases carrying an estimated 20,469 hours of potential annual capacity. The case shows that people's capability becomes a measurable performance lever when it is governed, embedded directly in delivery and tied to real business outcomes rather than run as a training activity. The proposition transfers: existing business staff, given digital skills and applying their domain expertise under governance, can deliver high-value solutions at scale and reduce a function's reliance on a central team.</jats:p>

title: From Integrity Challenges to Resilience: Digital Leak Detection and Innovative Repair Methodologies for Aging Pipeline Networks
container-title: ADIPEC
a90ce707e4aee907aa288d7e023aa650f43db7cb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Aging pipeline networks are a persistent integrity challenge for mature oil and gas assets because localized corrosion, pinhole defects, and through-wall leaks can rapidly progress into production deferment, HSE exposure, asset availability losses, and potential loss of primary containment. In a large onshore producing asset, flowline leaks have historically required conventional cut-and-replace repairs that involve depressurization, flushing, cutting, welding, hydrotesting, radiography, and reinstatement. This paper presents an integrated asset integrity methodology that combines real-time digital leak detection with rapid, non-intrusive clamp-based repair. The approach uses Distributed Temperature Sensing, Distributed Acoustic Sensing, and Distributed Strain Sensing to identify thermal, acoustic, and mechanical anomalies along pipelines. Detected weak points are localized, risk ranked, and connected to a standardized intervention workflow using engineered band-type clamps and split-style clamps with PTFE gaskets. In 2025, twenty-six flowlines were repaired using the clamp methodology, avoiding estimated production losses of USD 11.86 million. Historical analysis from 2023 to March 2026 shows sixty-three leak incidents with potential financial exposure exceeding USD 26.55 million. Compared with conventional repair, the clamp-based method reduced typical repair duration from approximately five days to two hours and lowered direct repair cost by approximately 85 percent. The results demonstrate that digital monitoring delivers maximum value when linked to immediate physical intervention. The methodology improves integrity assurance, supports Field Sustainable Oil Production Rate, reduces exposure to LOPC events, and provides a scalable blueprint for extending the life of aging pipeline networks.</jats:p>

title: Real-Time Digital Twin Model for Optimizing Drilling Performance and Support Intelligent Decision Making
container-title: ADIPEC
4f4599e4f35cfff5576017d8d10a556782e1441b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Maintaining efficient and sustainable drilling performance is a key challenge in well delivery, particularly in deciding whether drilling dysfunctions can be corrected through parameter optimization or require pull-out-of-hole (POOH) and run-in-hole (RIH) operations. This paper presents a real-time digital twin model using Mechanical Specific Energy (MSE) analytics to optimize drilling performance, reduce non-productive time (NPT), and improve well delivery efficiency across multiple fields in Oman.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A real-time digital twin workflow — a continuously updated virtual model of the drilling process that stays synchronized with live rig data and closes the loop with an operational recommendation, as distinct from a static or periodically refreshed decision-support review — was developed to continuously monitor drilling performance using live rig sensor data integrated with MSE analysis. The model processes key parameters — weight on bit, rotary speed, torque, rate of penetration, flow rate, standpipe pressure, and drilling fluid properties — to build a continuous picture of downhole conditions. MSE is dynamically benchmarked against offset-well performance to evaluate efficiency. Combined physics-based and rule-based logic classifies drilling states as stable drilling, optimization required, or critical failure requiring POOH and RIH, while generating real-time operational recommendations and supporting integration with rig surveillance systems.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The model was validated using data from more than 500 wells across 15 fields in Oman, achieving 99.1% accuracy — measured as agreement between the model's recommended action and the independently recorded operational outcome of each bit run — in identifying inefficient drilling conditions and recommending the appropriate corrective action. Field implementation demonstrated improved decision consistency and operational efficiency in real drilling environments. In Well A case study, the reservoir section was drilled in three bit runs compared with eight in an offset well, significantly reducing drilling time and tripping frequency. The system effectively differentiated between conditions requiring parameter optimization and those requiring BHA replacement, enabling timely interventions and avoiding unnecessary POOH operations. Overall, the approach reduced drilling time by up to 17% and well cost by approximately 6%. In addition, fewer tripping operations and more efficient drilling contributed to lower rig energy consumption, improved operational performance, and better well delivery outcomes across multiple field applications.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This work introduces a digital twin-based drilling decision framework that extends conventional MSE analysis into real-time operational intelligence. Its novelty lies in integrating MSE with structured decision logic to classify drilling states and enable proactive interventions, supporting more autonomous, efficient, and lower-carbon drilling operations in complex field environments.</jats:p>

title: From Data to Decisions: A Closed Loop Digital Reliability Ecosystem for Predictive Maintenance in Stimulation and Coiled Tubing Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
3c7612bc39bb7b36086da4284505d97548df7876.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydraulic fracturing and coiled tubing operations rely on mechanically intensive equipment operating under highly variable loads across global environments. Conventional maintenance strategies are often constrained by fragmented data, delayed diagnostics, and reactive interventions, limiting asset utilization and spare parts planning.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents the deployment of an integrated digital ecosystem enabling the transition from reactive to condition-based maintenance. By integrating real-time surveillance, Prognostics and Health Management Models (PHMs), and advanced analytics, the ecosystem improves equipment reliability, maximizes asset availability, and reduces operating costs.</jats:p>
