2a025665591d9f73aa5b70d0d1678ce57aa9a287.abstract: Penetrasi gawai di wilayah pedesaan memunculkan dinamika baru dalam pengasuhan anak. Literasi digital orang tua tidak selalu sejalan dengan praktik pengasuhan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis tingkat literasi digital orang tua dan disonansi antara literasi digital dengan praktik penggunaan gawai sebagai digital pacifier pada keluarga pedesaan. Penelitian menggunakan desain kuantitatif deskriptif dengan survei cross-sectional terhadap 25 orang tua di dua desa Kabupaten Mojokerto, Jawa Timur, dengan rata-rata usia anak terkecil 5,48 tahun. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert yang mengukur literasi digital dan praktik pengasuhan, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif dan inferensial menggunakan uji Wilcoxon, Spearman’s Rho, dan Fisher’s Exact. Hasil menunjukkan tingkat literasi digital teknis tinggi (>80%), tetapi kesadaran keamanan siber dan pemahaman kritis terhadap informasi masih terbatas. Tidak terdapat korelasi maupun perbedaan signifikan antara literasi digital dan status pekerjaan orang tua dengan praktik pembatasan akses gawai (p>0,05). Temuan menunjukkan paradoks antara pemahaman normatif dan praktik pengasuhan, ketika kelelahan pengasuhan (parenting burnout) mendorong penggunaan gawai sebagai digital pacifier. Intervensi digital parenting perlu menekankan mediasi aktif yang aplikatif dan peka budaya, bukan sekadar pembatasan waktu layar.

title: SAGE-AIP: A Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for Predicting AI Adoption and Productivity Across Multiple Data Scales
5358271a89a3a9d9de2f5155abb8bccaa93cc9ce.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is frequently associated with productivity improvement, yet empirical conclusions depend on where AI exposure is measured, how productivity is defined, and which model is used. This study develops a multi-scale comparative framework using three datasets: 145,000 AI-adoption records from 10 countries and eight industries; 2,074 observed country-year records from 233 country or regional units (2015–2023); and 150 employee-level observations. Robust regression, country fixed effects, dynamic fixed effects, and difference-GMM sensitivity analysis are combined with a proposed Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for AI Adoption and Productivity (SAGE-AIP), which is benchmarked against six established regressors using temporal holdouts for the two longitudinal datasets and a train–test split for the employee data. The adoption dataset shows almost no systematic structure (R2 = 0.00018), and SAGE-AIP does not improve on simpler models there (test RMSE 28.976 vs. 28.900 for Elastic Net). In the global panel, automation intensity is strongly associated with AI-attributed productivity (β = 19.882, SE = 0.434), and SAGE-AIP attains the lowest test RMSE (4.448; R2 = 0.544). At the employee level, recorded AI-tool information remains positively associated with productivity (β = 0.905, SE = 0.220), but Random Forest outperforms SAGE-AIP (test RMSE 0.435 vs. 0.583). SAGE-AIP is therefore not uniformly superior; its value is scale-specific, which supports evaluating models across data scales rather than relying on a single dataset or model class.

title: Hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch Inference Acceleration for Attention-Based CNNs with Dynamic ROI Sampling: A Case Study on Jetson Nano
2356aca907e0d5b1b6084ccaae24703cb4766568.abstract: Edge AI deployment requires low-latency inference on devices with tight constraints in size, weight, power, and cost. NVIDIA TensorRT accelerates inference through layer fusion, precision reduction, and kernel auto-tuning, but a model containing even one unsupported operator cannot be compiled into a single engine. This paper presents a hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch deployment in which the supported subnetworks run as TensorRT engines while the unsupported operations fall back to native PyTorch, and applies it to an attention-based convolutional neural network (ACNN) whose region-of-interest sampling operators are unsupported. On an NVIDIA Jetson Nano, the hybrid approach reduced the end-to-end latency of ACNN-dsc, the fastest native PyTorch model, from 38.37 ms to 20.40 ms (1.88×) under FP32. Under FP16, the hybrid ACNN-k3 achieved the lowest latency of 17.78 ms, a 2.23× speedup over its PyTorch FP32 counterpart and 2.16× over the fastest PyTorch model. Stepwise profiling of the image preprocessing pipeline showed that transferring raw images and performing most conversions on the GPU more than halves preprocessing latency. Further analyses across devices, precisions, and frameworks show that practical latency on edge AI accelerators depends on hardware and runtime factors beyond FLOPs and model size.

title: Gate-Road Geomechanics in LTCC and Thick-Seam Longwall Mining: A Critical Review and Proposed Adaptive Framework for Indian Gondwana Coalfields
983cf270c3609750bcbd845ff4b3257b26ff2b21.abstract: Gate roadways provide access, ventilation, transport and services throughout longwall panel development and retreat. Their stability depends on stress orientation, roof-bed structure, discontinuities, pillar geometry, support response and extraction sequence. In longwall top-coal caving (LTCC), the deliberate fracture and rear-window drawing of upper coal add load-transfer interactions that are not represented by bottom-slice extraction or by high-cutting single-pass longwall. This critical narrative review synthesises published field studies, case histories, numerical analyses and technical literature relevant to LTCC and thick-seam gate-road behaviour, with particular attention to Indian Gondwana conditions. Adriyala is treated as a bottom-slice comparator: its retained upper coal informs roof behaviour and monitoring, but it is not evidence of deliberate LTCC top-coal drawing. The review proposes a six-stage adaptive framework linking site characterisation, extraction geometry, layout comparison, support design, installation verification, and monitoring-led updating. A TARP response logic is presented as a site-specific management tool. The framework is a structured synthesis of the reviewed evidence, not a validated design standard; numerical dimensions and support values from individual cases are not transferable without mine-specific analysis. Instrumented prospective studies in Indian thick-seam and LTCC panels are needed to test and refine the framework.

title: Deep Looking in Digital Pathology: An Explainable Federated Learning Framework for Lung Cancer Classification
df0244c17fa3418f5d06a31ae1ff5398bf9eaacb.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and growing slide volumes add to pathologists’ cognitive load. Deep learning can assist histopathological diagnosis, but two obstacles limit its clinical use: privacy regulations keep patient images in institutional “data silos”, and the “black-box” behavior of neural networks undermines clinical trust. Inspired by Topol’s Deep Medicine, we aimed to build a diagnostic platform that preserves privacy and explains its decisions. Methods: We developed the Lung Cancer Analysis System (LCAS), which combines federated learning (FL), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and a locally deployed medical large language model (LLM). Three public H&E datasets (LC25000, HistoSet-5×14, and CLID; 18,000 images; adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, benign tissue) acted as three hospital nodes with source-induced non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, and MobileNetV3-Small were trained centrally and with FedAvg/FedProx for 20 rounds. Grad-CAM produced visual evidence, and MedGemma 1.5, served offline through LM Studio, converted predictions and heatmap descriptors into structured reports. Results: Centralized training reached 99.50% ± 0.21% accuracy with DenseNet121. Under non-IID federated training with FedProx, DenseNet121 and EfficientNet-B3 achieved 96.97% and 97.49% accuracy on an independent external blind test set of 958 images, whereas MobileNetV3-Small reached 91.23%. Accuracy remained 99.78% under Gaussian blur. t-SNE showed that global features clustered by tissue class rather than by hospital, and Grad-CAM highlighted glandular and tumor-nest regions consistent with histopathological criteria. Conclusions: FL, XAI, and on-premise LLM reporting can be integrated into a single workflow that keeps raw images within each institution while giving pathologists numerical, visual, and textual explanations, providing a practical path toward trustworthy cross-institutional computational pathology.

title: A Critical Analysis of the Legal and Ethical Challenges of Digital Lending Applications in Tanzania: A Doctrinal Analysis with Comparative Reference to Nigeria
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
d4469acbb0a82dfd1bad9a53f87d3b9f93ff3070.abstract: App-based digital lending has changed how Tanzanians borrow: a loan can be applied for, scored and disbursed on a handset within minutes, with an algorithm in place of the loan officer and the borrower’s phone data in place of collateral. This article asks whether Tanzanian law has kept pace with that change. Using doctrinal legal research, it examines the Microfinance Act, Cap 407, its 2019 Non-Deposit Taking Regulations, the Bank of Tanzania’s 2024 Guidance Note on Digital Lenders, the Financial Consumer Protection Regulations as amended in 2025, the 2025 Complaints Guidelines and the Personal Data Protection Act, Cap 44. The analysis draws on information asymmetry theory, the vulnerability theory of the consumer, informational self-determination and contextual integrity, and algorithmic accountability. It finds that the reforms of 2019 to 2025 have filled most literal silences in the law, but that the framework retains one legal gap, the absence of any standard for authenticating a guarantor’s consent on a mobile interface; four normative gaps, concerning informed guarantor consent, a flat penalty ceiling, the timing and comparability of cost disclosure, and weak explanation and reconsideration rights for automated decisions; two implementation gaps, in unaudited debt recovery and in-app redress; and one coordination gap among the Bank of Tanzania, the Personal Data Protection Commission and the newly designated self-regulatory associations. Nigeria’s move from interim guidelines to binding regulations, upheld by its Federal High Court in 2026, shows that converting guidance into enforceable rules is achievable. The article recommends a binding guarantor-verification standard, scaled penalties, pre-application cost disclosure, specified algorithmic disclosure, joint sampled audits and a formal inter-agency memorandum of understanding.

title: Evidence-Aware Adaptive Recognition for Intelligent Traffic Sign Systems with Calibrated Uncertainty under Distribution Shift
346089f0eb8c5381e07c68a4d733f167228308b1.abstract: Abstract Traffic-sign recognition under image shiftraises two related questions: which label is supportedand whether the crop still contains the visual evidenceon which that decision is based. Adaptive signconditionedrecognition (ASCR) keeps these quantitiesseparate. A temperature-calibrated classifier withregularized adaptive prediction sets (RAPS) returnssemantic probabilities and label sets; a label-free monitormeasures preserved color, area, shape, and componentstructure. Track-disjoint traffic-sign data andcontrolled corruptions reveal a high-confidence/lowevidenceregime: the lowest-evidence group retains 0.913confidence at 0.162 error. The evidence–error slopealso changes sign across the evaluated environments,indicating that a single global evidence coefficient canbe misleading under these shifts. ASCR therefore actsat the decision stage: semantic ambiguity expands thelabel set, while evidence departure triggers intervention.Within the evaluated settings, this separation providesa transparent decision interface for calibrated classifiersand visual-evidence monitors.

title: An Application of the Self-Determination Theory Model for AI-Enhanced, Digital Psychosocial Interventions for Pediatric Disabilities
container-title: Western Journal of Nursing Research
6a353330c39f733eb7e369612f893bac2e52174c.abstract: Background: Youth with developmental disabilities (DDs) experience elevated psychosocial challenges, including difficulties with emotion regulation, self-concept, and access to timely mental health support. Pediatric nurses are well-positioned to address these needs; however, time constraints, limited training, and restricted access to specialty services often impede the provision of consistent psychosocial care. Digitally delivered psychosocial interventions enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities for individualized, accessible support, but these approaches frequently lack a clear theoretical foundation. Purpose: This paper applied Self-Determination Theory (SDT), specifically Basic Psychological Needs Theory, to guide pediatric nurses’ use of AI-enhanced, digital psychosocial interventions for DDs in practice. Methods: A theory-driven synthesis mapped SDT needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) to AI-enabled intervention features: conversational agents, neuro/adaptive feedback, and emotion-recognition tailoring. Results: The framework specifies how these features can promote volitional engagement, optimal challenge with timely feedback, and supportive interactions for youth with DDs. It also notes evidence gaps (small, heterogeneous samples; limited comparisons and follow-up) and barriers involving payment/workload, equity and access, and data protection, transparency, and bias. Conclusions/Implications: SDT offers a coherent, testable foundation for designing, evaluating, and integrating AI-enhanced psychosocial supports for pediatric DDs. Nurses can screen for support, coach families, monitor risks, and advocate for ethical deployment and rigorous research.

title: Adaptive optimization of large-margin learning for physics-informed time–frequency maps for the diagnosis of rotating components
container-title: Structural Health Monitoring
054ff56cd7bc0512b0025c9a721179018133bf56.abstract: This article introduces a novel physics-informed large-margin learning framework for diagnosing rotating component faults, addressing the limitations of traditional methods and “black-box” artificial intelligence models in handling complex, noisy vibration data. The methodology integrates feature mode decomposition and short-time Fourier transform to generate physics-informed time–frequency maps, from which interpretable features are extracted. A large-margin learning model then utilizes these features, with its five critical hyperparameters adaptively optimized using the slime mould algorithm to ensure robustness and optimal performance. Evaluated on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and intelligent maintenance systems (IMS) bearing datasets, the proposed framework achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 88.75% on CWRU and 96.67% on IMS, outperforming seven state-of-the-art classification baselines implemented under identical experimental conditions. This approach enhances interpretability, diagnostic accuracy, and generalization, offering a more reliable solution for machine health monitoring.

title: CRYPTOASSETS, MONEY LAUNDERING AND CRIMINAL LIABILITY: ECONOMIC AND LEGAL CHALLENGES OF THE DIGITAL FINANCIAL SYSTEM
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
901258ca194ab2bcdb518837960e5e0962b75d34.abstract: The present article provides a comprehensive economic and legal analysis of the use of cryptoassets in mechanisms for the legalisation (laundering) of proceeds of crime. In addition, it examines the specific features of criminal-law responses to such practices within the digital financial system. The study's relevance is determined by the rapid expansion of the global cryptoasset market, the growth in the volume of illicit cryptocurrency transactions, and the increasing use of stablecoins, P2P and OTC channels, cryptocurrency mixers, and other technologies in schemes designed to transfer and conceal criminal proceeds. It is also determined by the need to adapt national financial monitoring and criminal justice systems to the technological transformation of financial relations. The purpose of the study is fourfold: to identify the economic mechanisms through which cryptoassets are used for money laundering; to assess the applicability of Article 209 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine to digital forms of economic value; to pinpoint the primary challenges of criminal law qualification and evidentiary assessment; and to provide recommendations for enhancing the national economic and legal mechanisms for combating illicit financial flows in the digital environment. The study establishes that, while cryptoassets do not alter the economic essence of money laundering, they do significantly transform the architecture of the financial trail. This is achieved by increasing transactional complexity, fragmenting financial flows, enabling the repeated conversion of digital value and combining decentralised and traditional financial infrastructures. It is argued that the current wording of Article 209 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine is sufficiently technology-neutral to encompass transactions involving cryptoassets. However, the main challenges lie in establishing the link between a digital asset and a predicate criminal offence, identifying the beneficial or actual controller of the asset, proving that the individual is aware of its criminal origin, and ensuring effective procedural control over virtual assets. The study also shows that the FATF's standards and the European Union's regulatory framework provide the conceptual basis for integrating crypto assets into the wider system of risk-based AML/CFT regulation. The study's scientific novelty lies in substantiating an integrated model of economic and legal counteraction to money laundering involving cryptoassets. This model incorporates technology-neutral criminal law, specialised criminal procedural mechanisms for dealing with digital assets, risk-based financial monitoring, blockchain analytics and international co-operation. The findings have the potential to improve law enforcement practice under Article 209 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine by developing procedures for the detection, seizure, custody, valuation and confiscation of cryptoassets. They could also strengthen the analytical capacity of financial intelligence and criminal justice authorities and harmonise national regulation with FATF standards and European Union law.

title: A CONCEPTUAL MODEL OF ADAPTIVE MECHANISMS IN INNOVATION-ORIENTED AGRICULTURAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
7b84fefbaca664a28306eee312949b0c9f8af8ea.abstract: The war in Ukraine has presented the agricultural sector with an unprecedented combination of risks, including the loss of production assets, climate volatility, supply chain disruption and institutional instability. In such circumstances, traditional models of entrepreneurial resilience, which are primarily designed for peacetime or isolated natural or economic shocks, lose their adaptive capacity. Meanwhile, there is virtually no comprehensive theoretical synthesis of the mechanisms by which agribusiness adapts to multiple simultaneous threats. This article aims to substantiate a conceptual model of adaptive management mechanisms for innovative agribusiness by integrating the theories of dynamic capabilities and adaptive management with institutional economics. The subject of this study is the processes through which agro-industrial enterprises adapt to conditions of institutional instability and armed conflict. The study is based on the systematic organisation and critical analysis of scientific literature on dynamic capabilities theory, classical adaptive management, and institutional economics. It also draws on a synthesis of empirical studies on agribusiness adaptability under various types of shock. As a result, a four-level conceptual model has been developed. This model sequentially combines an exogenous shock in the form of armed conflict with a reinterpreted triad of dynamic capabilities—sensing, seizing and transforming—for wartime conditions. It also incorporates an institutional moderator and the final outcome of 'bounce forward' adaptive resilience. The practical value of the model lies in its potential use as an analytical tool for assessing the preparedness of agricultural enterprises for multiple crises, developing state policy to support the agricultural sector during wartime and the post-war period, and for formulating enterprise management strategies that take into account the quality of the institutional environment.

title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL BANKING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON PRIVATE BANKING IN SWITZERLAND: ARE CHANGES AHEAD?
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
fbee2638caf8a4913086b40b3e787ce2544b774d.abstract: Subject of Research. This study focuses on the digital banking landscape and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in private banking and wealth management in Switzerland. More specifically, it examines how technological innovations – ranging from process automation and generative AI to advanced data analytics – alter the operational dynamics, customer relations, and structural competitiveness of Swiss private banks in the context of shifting client expectations and rigorous regulatory environments. Methodology. The research employs a qualitative analytical research design that uses triangulation of secondary evidence. It systematically integrates and cross-checks academic literature on digital finance, fintech adoption and robo-advisory trust, alongside empirical data, regulatory frameworks and market insights from reputable Swiss and international organisations. The primary data sources analysed were supervisory guides from the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA), reports from the Swiss Bankers Association, digital maturity benchmarks from Deloitte Switzerland and private banking market profitability assessments from KPMG and PwC Switzerland. Purpose. The main objective of this paper is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the impact of digital transformation and the deployment of AI on the traditional Swiss private banking model. By analysing seven key dimensions – technological progress, customer expectations, process optimization, data analytics, risk and security, regulation/compliance, and market trajectories – the study aims to clarify the economic mechanisms driving digital adaptation, identify the structural barriers preventing rapid technology adoption, and evaluate the strategic options available to Swiss banks facing intense global competition and margin compression. Findings and Conclusion. The study reveals a significant discrepancy between Switzerland's position as a global leader in asset management, with CHF 9.3 trillion under management, and its digital banking maturity score of 39 out of 60. Although private banking clients continue to establish relationships based on traditional factors such as reputation, trust and personal referrals, they are also demanding friction-free digital execution, personalised dashboards and virtual investment simulations. AI has been proven to have high economic value when acting as a productivity layer centred around advisors, optimising processes such as client onboarding, document extraction, compliance screening and portfolio monitoring. However, it is not as effective when acting as an autonomous replacement for human relationship managers. Ultimately, the integration of digital banking and AI is causing a clear market polarisation. Large-scale institutions are successfully absorbing the substantial fixed costs associated with technology, data governance and regulatory compliance under the frameworks of FINMA and the European Union (such as DORA and the EU AI Act). Conversely, smaller Swiss private banks are under severe pressure to increase their profitability and consolidate, unless they adopt highly focused niche advisory models. The paper therefore concludes that urgent regulatory attention and strategic repositioning are necessary to preserve the overall image and international attractiveness of the Swiss private banking ecosystem.

title: Impact of Video-Based Educational Content on Middle School Students’ Earthquake Knowledge and Attitudes
container-title: Journal of Learning and Teaching in Digital Age
de01ad28f6af818fef06cb0c9c06c7406a364fa3.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of video-based educational content developed within the scope of earthquake education on middle school students’ earthquake-related knowledge and attitudes. The study employed a one-group pretest–posttest pre-experimental design and was conducted during the 2024–2025 academic year with 481 students enrolled in public middle schools. The video-based instructional materials were designed to enhance students’ cognitive understanding and affective responses to earthquakes. Data were collected using the Let’s Understand Earthquakes Test and the Attitude Toward Earthquakes Scale. Paired-samples t-tests and one-way ANOVA were used for data analysis. The findings of this study indicated that the intervention did not produce a statistically significant improvement in students’ overall earthquake knowledge, although a significant gain was observed in the protective behaviors dimension. In contrast, students’ attitudes toward earthquakes improved significantly with a large effect size. The results suggest that video-based educational materials developed within the scope of earthquake education are particularly effective in influencing affective outcomes such as attitudes, risk perception, and value-oriented motivation, while being less effective in fostering abstract conceptual knowledge. The study provides design implications for developing more cognitively supportive digital disaster-education materials.

title: Single-sensor acoustic emission source localization in blade local region based on an interpretable wavelet attention network
container-title: Structural Health Monitoring
ede9793d57cf20866e46b892aa7f92f49bbf6016.abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) technology is suitable for monitoring wind turbine blades because of its high-frequency response and sensitivity. However, existing damage localization approaches rely on multi-sensor arrays, which limit their engineering applicability. Moreover, deep learning models for single-sensor localization remain constrained by insufficient time-frequency representation and limited interpretability. To address these issues, a novel single-sensor AE source localization model, the Large-kernel dual wavelet attention network, was proposed. First, pencil lead break tests on real blade structures were conducted to investigate AE signal propagation, revealing strong nonlinear behavior and multi-scale attenuation characteristics. On this basis, a Large-kernel dual wavelet convolution layer was developed using Morlet and Mexican hat wavelets. With a mechanism-guided large wavelet kernel design, the arbitrariness in hyperparameter selection and the Gibbs phenomenon associated with incomplete truncation were mitigated, enabling the effective extraction of multi-scale time-frequency features. A time-grouped frequency attention mechanism module was introduced to adaptively recalibrate convolutional kernel weights through the fine-grained perception of localized time-frequency features, thereby improving the discrimination of critical features. Experiments on a real blade specimen demonstrated that the proposed method outperformed existing models in localization accuracy, achieving a minimum mean distance error of 20.29 mm. Furthermore, the model exhibited advantages in terms of feature interpretability and noise robustness. These results provide a promising and interpretable framework, laying the foundation for single-sensor damage localization in structural health monitoring of wind turbine blades.

ad9bb49b42ea91ebaba306a3f2d02182dfe91257.abstract: Mazkur maqolada fuqarolik sud ishlarini yuritishda raqamli dalillarning maqbulligi vaishonchliligini baholash bilan bog‘liq protsessual-huquqiy masalalar tadqiq etiladi. title: Film Criticism and Analysis in the Digital Era: Role of Online Platforms
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
fc7f185d7413cac784e5be88d5856368afd6d6f6.abstract: The digital era has revolutionized numerous facets of contemporary life, and film criticism is no exception. Traditionally confined to the pages of newspapers and specialized journals, film criticism has found new life on the internet, where online platforms have democratized and diversified the field. Today, anyone with a keen eye for cinema and an internet connection can publish reviews and analyses, challenging the dominance of established critics and broadening the discourse around film. This shift has not only expanded the audience for film criticism but also transformed the ways in which films are analyzed and discussed. The advent of the digital era has profoundly transformed film criticism, shifting the landscape from traditional print media to dynamic online platforms. Anchored on the technological determinism theory, this paper explores the role of these platforms in reshaping film criticism and analysis. Online platforms such as blogs, social media, and dedicated film websites have democratized the field, allowing a diverse array of voices to participate in the discourse. These platforms provide immediacy and interactivity, enabling rapid responses to new releases and fostering vibrant discussions. Furthermore, the integration of multimedia elements like video essays and podcasts offers a more immersive critique, enhancing traditional written reviews. However, this democratization also presents challenges, including the proliferation of content, the difficulty of discerning credible voices, and the polarization of online discourse. Despite these issues, the influence of online platforms is undeniable, representing a significant evolution in film criticism. This paper examines the opportunities and challenges presented by these digital mediums, highlighting their impact on how films are reviewed, interpreted, and appreciated in the contemporary era.

title: Continuous glucose monitoring, automated insulin delivery, and remote care in adolescents with type 1 diabetes: advances toward integrated digital management
container-title: Frontiers in Endocrinology
58f95259b2343193e59a2556b35816e8cb201993.abstract: Type 1 diabetes management in adolescents remains challenging due to physiological and behavioral factors. This review summarizes recent advances in three interconnected technologies: continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), automated insulin delivery (AID), and remote care. CGM provides real-time glycemic data with time in range (TIR) as the core metric, improving glycemic outcomes when implemented with structured education. AID systems, particularly hybrid closed-loop devices, consistently increase TIR, reduce glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lower risks of severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) across randomized trials and real-world studies, with validated efficacy in children as young as 1-year-old. Remote care models leverage continuous data streams to enable individualized follow-up, showing glycemic outcomes approaching those of traditional visits in comparative studies while improving access and psychosocial support. Despite proven benefits, barriers remain, including socioeconomic inequities in technology access, alarm fatigue, and implementation gaps across healthcare systems. Future priorities include fully closed-loop systems, dual-hormone approaches, algorithm optimization for exercise and illness, long-term psychosocial outcomes, and equitable implementation strategies. Clinical practice should integrate these technologies through multidisciplinary teams, early initiation, and patient-centered support to transform adolescent diabetes care from intermittent visits to continuous digital management.

title:
Etiquette in the Malay Archipelago Digital: A Comparative Study of Digital Media Self-Regulation and Cultural Values in
Indonesia and Malaysia
1bf1fd0aa628507ec41f945ce9838973faff20fa.abstract: Abstract This study explores the ethical frameworks, cultural values, and self regulation mechanisms that underpin social media governance in Indonesia and Malaysia. Each country operates within distinct legal, political, and socio-cultural contexts, resulting in varied approaches to regulating digital communication. Utilizing document analysis and in-depth interviews, this research examines how ethics, normative values, and foundational principles of media freedom are operationalized in accordance with the 1984 Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which upholds freedom of speech and expression as fundamental rights. Findings reveal that while both countries recognize the importance of media freedom, they also emphasize the need for responsibility and regulation. Self regulation has emerged as a strategic model for aligning state laws, community norms, and platform standards. In particular, the study highlights how religious values, cultural traditions, and institutional frameworks shape ethical media practices in each nation. This research underscores the importance of fostering digital literacy that is deeply rooted in local ethical and cultural values. It recommends a participatory approach that strengthens collaboration among governments, digital communities, and platform providers to ensure a balanced and responsible digital ecosystem in Southeast Asia.

title: Adaptive Robust Fading Memory Filter for Tracking Maneuvering Spacecraft with Heavy-Tailed Measurement Noise
container-title: Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics
a6ab171e049ff994fc2fa9d6529fae0430234d02.abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive robust fading memory filter (ARFMKF) to accurately track impulsively maneuvering spacecraft under heavy-tailed measurement noise. The ARFMKF is capable of simultaneously suppressing the adverse effects of measurement outliers, heavy-tailed measurement noise, and impulsive maneuvers. First, the Huber robust M-estimation methodology is investigated to mitigate the influence of measurement outliers and heavy-tailed measurement noise, enhancing the filter’s robustness to measurement model uncertainties. Then, an adaptive fading factor is incorporated to improve the maneuver detection sensitivity of the proposed filter and is used as a weighting coefficient for covariance inflation to compensate for the dynamics model errors caused by impulsive maneuvers. In addition, a discrimination index is designed to effectively distinguish impulsive maneuvers from measurement outliers, ensuring appropriate covariance inflation in the presence of maneuvers. Simulations show that the proposed ARFMKF outperforms the comparison filters in terms of maneuver detection sensitivity, discrimination capability, and overall tracking performance, particularly in scenarios involving multiple impulsive maneuvers and frequent measurement outliers.

title: Efektivitas Sistem Informasi Haji dan Umrah (SIHU) sebagai Media Dakwah Digital dalam Pembinaan Jamaah Haji dan Umrah di Aceh
container-title: Khulasah : Islamic Studies Journal
22042beb7db666a7f65d804c87816c026cffb21a.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis efektivitas Sistem Informasi Haji dan Umrah (SIHU) sebagai media dakwah dalam pembinaan jamaah haji dan umrah di Provinsi Aceh. Perkembangan teknologi informasi telah mendorong transformasi metode dakwah dari pendekatan konvensional menuju dakwah digital yang lebih interaktif, efektif, dan mudah diakses oleh masyarakat. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan mixed methods dengan desain sequential explanatory, yaitu mengombinasikan metode kuantitatif dan kualitatif secara bertahap. Data kuantitatif diperoleh melalui survei terhadap 120 responden calon jamaah haji dan umrah, sedangkan data kualitatif diperoleh melalui wawancara mendalam terhadap 15 informan yang terdiri atas pengelola SIHU, pembimbing ibadah haji dan umrah, serta ulama Aceh. Teknik pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi, wawancara, angket, dan dokumentasi. Analisis data kuantitatif menggunakan statistik deskriptif, sedangkan data kualitatif dianalisis menggunakan model Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña yang meliputi reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa SIHU berperan efektif sebagai media dakwah modern yang mampu meningkatkan kualitas pelayanan administrasi, pembinaan keagamaan, komunikasi, dan pengawasan jamaah secara terintegrasi. Tingkat pemahaman jamaah meningkat dari 60% menjadi 85%, retensi pesan mencapai 70%, dan tingkat keterlibatan (engagement) jamaah mencapai 65%. Namun, perubahan perilaku keagamaan jangka panjang masih berada pada kategori sedang dengan persentase 45%. Hambatan utama yang ditemukan meliputi keterbatasan akses internet di beberapa daerah, rendahnya literasi digital, serta dominasi jamaah lanjut usia yang membutuhkan pendampingan khusus. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa efektivitas SIHU tidak hanya ditentukan oleh kecanggihan teknologi, tetapi juga oleh kemampuan sistem dalam mengintegrasikan nilai-nilai lokal, memperkuat pendampi-ngan, dan mengembangkan personalisasi konten yang sesuai dengan karakteristik jamaah Aceh. Oleh karena itu, optimalisasi SIHU dapat menjadi strategi dakwah digital yang berkelanjutan dalam meningkatkan kualitas pembinaan jamaah haji dan umrah di Aceh.

title: Students' Interest in Mathematics during the Digital Age: Impact of Online Learning, Self-efficacy, and Self-regulated Learning Using Structural Equation Modeling
container-title: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
7d894f3c2ded748f3bf2ea7063b49de7cbe2984b.abstract: Background: The rapid digital transformation of higher education, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, has increased students' engagement with mathematics through online learning platforms. While online learning offers flexibility and broader access to educational resources, its influence on students’ interest in mathematics remains unclear. Self-efficacy and self-regulated learning are considered important factors that may explain how online learning shapes students’ motivation and interest in mathematics. Purpose: This study examined the mediating role of self-efficacy and self-regulated learning in the relationship between online learning and students’ interest in mathematics. Methodology/Design/Approach: This study adopted a cross-sectional survey design. The study was conducted at a public university in Ghana. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire with a sample of 350 students. Participants were selected through stratified random sampling. Data were analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM) in Amos (version 23). Findings: The analysis indicated that online learning significantly predicted students’ interest in mathematics, self-regulated learning, and self-efficacy. Additionally, self-efficacy and self-regulated learning also predicted students’ interest in mathematics. Furthermore, self-efficacy partially mediated the relationship between online learning and students' interest in mathematics. Finally, self-regulated learning partially and significantly mediated the link between online learning and students’ mathematics interest. Research Limitations: This study focused on the mediating role of self-efficacy and self-regulated learning without examining moderating effects. However, these factors might be crucial in analysing the moderating influence of perceived digital literacy on the relationship between online learning and students’ interest in mathematics. Originality: The principal contribution of this study is the examination of the mediating roles of self-efficacy and self-regulated learning in the relationship between online learning and students’ interest in mathematics.

title: Translation as pedagogy: strategic hybridization and multimodal equivalence in Indonesian–English digital storybooks for character education
container-title: Qualitative Research Journal
7982edbc8aa0658d831c0eae0d76ea0d7f261c5c.abstract: Purpose This study examines how translation strategies, equivalence, and multimodal resources interact to construct cultural, moral, and pedagogical meanings in an Indonesian–English bilingual digital storybook for character education. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a qualitative descriptive approach, the study analyses 112 purposively selected translation units from an interactive digital storybook. Translation strategies are examined using Molina and Hurtado Albir's framework, while equivalence is analyzed at functional, linguistic and pragmatic levels. Multimodal analysis explores the alignment of verbal, visual and auditory elements. Findings Three patterns emerge: strategic hybridization combines literal translation with pragmatic adaptation to maintain narrative clarity and pedagogical relevance; dynamic equivalence involves cultural and ideological reframing to make culture-specific expressions and moral values accessible to young readers; and multimodal reinforcement distributes moral and educational meanings across verbal, visual and auditory resources. These patterns demonstrate that translation involves negotiating linguistic accuracy, cultural specificity and pedagogical purpose rather than simply transferring meaning between languages. Originality/value The study integrates translation strategies, equivalence and multimodal discourse analysis to conceptualize translation as a pedagogical and trans-semiotic practice. It extends text-centered approaches to equivalence by demonstrating how linguistic choices interact with multimodal resources in representing cultural knowledge and character-education values in digital children's literature.

title: Plastic and adaptive mitochondrial responses help face hypoxia events in a freshwater fish
container-title: Functional Ecology
41f245595823c4129268fe54692535bf712df8d5.abstract: Abstract Hypoxic events (i.e. reduction of dissolved oxygen in water) are natural events, which intensity and frequency have been amplified by human activities. As oxygen fuels aerobic metabolism, species unable to avoid those events must maintain their functions through phenotypic adjustments, that could occur both at the individual level (plasticity) and population genomic level (adaptation). To examine the adaptative and plastic responses to hypoxia, we exposed two generations of three‐spined sticklebacks, Gasterosteus aculeatus , from wild populations historically exposed to different oxygen levels, to two different experimental oxygen conditions (normoxia or intermittent hypoxia with 12 h normoxia: 12 h hypoxia; with nighttime O 2 level at 20% for wild‐caught F0 during 4–6 weeks and at 35% for F1 throughout their entire 19‐month lifetime). By comparing the two generations, early‐life programming of the mitochondrial aerobic metabolism was revealed, conditioning the adult‐stage phenotypic and plastic response: F0 fish from the wild hypoxic environment had elevated pectoral muscle mitochondrial respiration and were able to increase their mitochondrial OXPHOS control efficiency under normoxia conditions at the adult stage. Signs of adaptations towards mitochondrial suppression were found in F1 hypoxia population fish livers while no differences were observed in their pectoral muscle, suggesting a downregulation of the hepatic, but not the pectoral muscle, aerobic activities through generations. In opposition to the adaptative trend, the plastic responses to experimental hypoxia were a decreased mitochondrial respiration in the pectoral muscle and an elevated liver mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation of the F1 fish, suggesting that inherited divergence rather countered than reinforced plastic responses. While both signs of adaptation and plasticity were found in the antioxidant defences of F1 fish, the absence of significant differences between experimental groups in terms of oxidative damage revealed that these fish were able to maintain oxidative balance. Our findings highlight that plasticity to hypoxia depends on the full organism life‐cycle, with the adult ability to face hypoxia depending on their early‐life environmental experience and provides valuable information on the potential evolutionary process of fish facing hypoxia. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

title: Corporate Asset Allocation under Economic Policy Uncertainty: Avoidance Behaviour and the Conditional Value of Digital Economic Assets
container-title: Financial Economics Research
d438ce920bf8fb44ecc0cd38900fcdb44bdc9349.abstract: Economic policy uncertainty has become an important factor affecting firms’ investment decisions in recent years. When uncertainty increases, firms may become more cautious about long-term investment and prefer to hold safer assets with higher liquidity. This paper studies how economic policy uncertainty influences firms' allocation between traditional safe assets and digital economic assets. It also examines whether this allocation affects firms' short-term performance differently under uncertain conditions. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed companies between 2014 and 2023, this study applies fixed-effects regression models for empirical analysis. The results suggest that firms tend to increase traditional safe asset holdings and reduce digital asset investment when economic policy uncertainty rises. In addition, digital economic assets are negatively related to short-term return on assets (ROA) on average. However, the interaction results show that the negative effect becomes weaker under higher levels of uncertainty. These results may indicate that firms become more conservative during uncertain periods, but reducing digital investment too much could also weaken firms' ability to adapt to changing environments in the long run.

title: ‘I think it's a rebrand…’: Pre‐service teachers' conceptualisations of adaptive teaching and differentiated instruction
container-title: Journal of Research in Special Educational Needs
320c2a9c8a5db403e4234e12ecc81459007232c0.abstract: Abstract This paper explores how pre‐service teachers (PSTs) conceptualise adaptive teaching in relation to differentiation within the contemporary policy landscape in England. Drawing on qualitative focus group data and informed by Bourdieu's theory of practice, the study examines how pedagogical understandings are shaped by social justice concerns, institutional constraints and emerging professional identities. The findings introduce pedagogical cynicism as a significant lens through which PSTs interpret reform alongside nuanced forms of teacher agency. The study offers original insight into how ambiguous pedagogical concepts are constructed in practice, highlighting implications for Initial Teacher Education and the development of socially just teaching.

title: Social Mobilisation and Social Marketing for Pastoral and Agro-Pastoral Wellbeing in the Horn of Africa: A Narrative Review
container-title: IRASS Journal of Multidisciplinary Studies
a19032f48ea229d188279937cd235ca57de677f0.abstract: Pastoral and agro-pastoral communities in the Horn of Africa face interconnected climatic, economic and institutional pressures that undermine livelihoods, food security and wellbeing. This narrative review examines how social mobilisation and social marketing can jointly strengthen collective agency, improve access to services and markets, and support sustainable use of livestock, environmental and cultural assets. It synthesises 25 purposively selected publications issued between 2020 and 2025, comprising empirical studies, scholarly literature, institutional guidance and regional policy documents. The thematic synthesis identifies six interconnected priorities: community ownership and accountable governance; audience insight and differentiated inclusion; feasible behavioural objectives and valued exchange; integrated services and fair commercial relationships; environmental and cultural stewardship; and livelihood, nutrition and risk protection. The findings indicate that knowledge and communication alone are insufficient to sustain beneficial practices where affordability, service reliability, mobility, resource rights and decision-making authority remain constrained. Collective organisation can strengthen coordination and bargaining power, but requires safeguards against exclusion and elite capture. Similarly, increased livestock sales cannot independently demonstrate improved wellbeing because livestock also support nutrition, breeding, savings and social security. The review proposes an iterative framework linking participatory diagnosis, accountable organisation, co-design, voluntary piloting, evidence-based expansion and continuous evaluation. Success should be assessed through sustained practice changes, net income, dietary outcomes, resilience, equitable control of benefits and resource condition. However, geographically uneven evidence and limited evaluation of combined interventions prevent causal conclusions about the framework’s effectiveness. Sustainable pastoral development therefore requires locally adapted testing that connects community influence with reliable services, fair markets and responsive institutions while protecting mobility, productive assets, cultural choice and voluntary livelihood diversification.

title: Technology-push risk screening for sustainable digital health adoption at the Uganda Cancer Institute: a design-stage research note aligned with SDG 3.8
ab189434bf60af0df2261b706fc82387852654ec.abstract: Abstract Objective Digital health can contribute to stronger and more equitable health services, yet technologies introduced because they are externally funded, vendor-promoted or administratively driven may be poorly aligned with local need, user participation and institutional readiness. This research note describes a design-stage Technology Push Mitigation Framework for pre-deployment digital-health decision-making at the Uganda Cancer Institute (UCI) and positions its intended contribution against Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3, particularly target 3.8 on universal health coverage. Results Evidence was triangulated from global digital-health guidance, Uganda policy and standards, UCI-specific studies, and recent LMIC implementation literature. The resulting artefact has three layers: a technology-push risk screen, a four-domain readiness assessment, and a decision/escalation pathway. Six technology-push indicators and four readiness domains are operationalised, leading to three provisional decisions: proceed, revise/mitigate, or defer/escalate. The framework has not yet been empirically validated and does not demonstrate improved adoption or SDG outcomes. A staged validation pathway is specified for future empirical research.

title: THE ROLE OF EDUCATION AND DIGITAL LITERACY IN WOMEN’S EMPOWERMENT: A DATA-BASED ANALYTICAL STUDY
container-title: EPRA International Journal of Research & Development (IJRD)
bae2e549e83ec235d9fb3b0e5c3046967ee18fa6.abstract: Women’s empowerment is an important foundation for inclusive, equitable, and sustainable social development. Education serves as a means of developing knowledge, awareness, self-confidence, decision-making ability, and social participation among women, while digital literacy strengthens access to modern technological resources, expands economic opportunities, and enhances the possibilities for independent expression. In the present digital era, the integration of education and digital literacy has become particularly relevant for the personal, social, economic, and political empowerment of women. The primary objective of the present study is to analyse the status of education, digital access, financial inclusion, and labour force participation in the context of women’s empowerment in India on the basis of secondary data. The study is based on the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), the All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE 2021–22), the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS 2023–24), and related government publications. Descriptive statistical techniques, such as percentages, percentage-point differences, comparative analysis, and trend analysis, have been used for the analysis. According to the available data, the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of women in higher education in India increased from 22.9 per cent in 2014–15 to 28.5 per cent in 2021–22. Similarly, the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) of women aged 15 years and above increased from 23.3 per cent in 2017–18 to 41.7 per cent in 2023–24. On the other hand, NFHS-5 indicated a substantial difference between women and men in internet usage. The study makes it clear that, despite the expansion of educational opportunities, ensuring equal access to digital resources, technical proficiency, and economic autonomy remains essential. In conclusion, education and digital literacy are complementary means of women’s empowerment; however, their actual impact is also influenced by social circumstances, resource availability, economic opportunities, and women’s independent decision-making capacity.

title: Adaptive gain sliding mode observer based on recursive least square for ultra-local model estimation in model-free predictive control of brushless DC motor drives
container-title: Electrical Engineering & Electromechanics
34d886b8de4214b3ae17172968ce60d65f221002.abstract: Introduction. Accurate current estimation is essential for high-performance brushless DC (BLDC) motor drives, especially in finite control set model predictive control (FCSMPC), where prediction accuracy directly affects control quality. Problem. Sliding mode observers (SMOs) are widely adopted for this purpose due to their robustness against modeling uncertainties. However, the performance of conventional SMO strongly depends on proper gain tuning, which is typically fixed and may lead to degraded performance under parameter variations and changing operating conditions. Goal. To develop an adaptive SMO gain strategy that automatically adjusts the observer gain online using recursive least squares (RLS) approach to improve robustness and estimation accuracy of the ultra local model without manual tuning. Methodology. The proposed method proposes the SMO gain adaptation as an online regression problem, where the RLS algorithm is used to recursively update the observer gain at each sampling instant. The adaptive SMO is integrated into an FCSMPC scheme. Its performance is evaluated through simulations under nominal conditions and parameter mismatches and compared with static-gain and PI-based adaptive SMO approaches using dynamic and steady-state performance metrics. Results. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RLS-based adaptive gain SMO achieves faster convergence, reduced chattering, and improved robustness against parameter variations. Scientific novelty. The main contribution of this work is the use of RLS to adapt the SMO gain rather than directly estimating system parameters, providing a stable and statistically grounded gain adaptation mechanism. Practical value. The method reduces the integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) of the sliding variable by 5.8 % compared to the static-gain approach and provides faster settling time and lower steady-state error in speed response. The settling time is reduced by 33 % and decreasing steady-state error by 58 % compared to the conventional static-gain approach. In addition, the adaptive mechanism enhances robustness under parameter mismatch and load disturbance conditions. References 34, tables 3, figures 6.

title: Real-time geometric complexity of language is associated with global functioning across psychosis and major depression
container-title: NPP—Digital Psychiatry and Neuroscience
ee08bfc20a1e8522bf808ddfca0c5483a2a2c406.abstract: Abstract Language disturbances are prominent across psychiatric disorders, yet their underlying organization and relationship to clinical functioning remain poorly understood. We conceptualized spontaneous speech as a temporally evolving sequence of contextual representations through semantic space, in which successive concepts define transitions between large-language-model embeddings. We characterized the local dynamics of these representations using Lyapunov-inspired measures of sensitivity to perturbation and anisotropy—the extent to which nearby neighboring contextual representations diverge differently depending on direction in representational space. We applied this approach to picture descriptions from 129 German-speaking participants with major depressive disorder (n = 43), schizophrenia spectrum disorders (n = 42), or no psychiatric diagnosis (n = 44). Individual differences in local geometric dynamics predicted multiple clinical dimensions, with the strongest association observed for global functioning, for which the geometric measures explained 51% of the variance. Clinically informative geometric structure was already detectable within the first three sentences of speech, where distinct dynamical profiles were associated with differences in negative and positive symptoms, anxiety, depression, and global functioning. These associations suggest that the dynamics of local representational divergence and contraction during speech reflect broad variation in cognitive and social functioning rather than diagnosis alone. Together, these findings suggest that psychiatric variation is reflected not simply in what people say, but in the dynamics by which semantic representations evolve during ongoing language production. A dynamical-geometric analysis of language may provide a compact, transdiagnostic marker of clinically meaningful variation in psychopathology.

title: Analisis Fitur dan Alur Kerja AIO Class untuk Mendukung Manajemen Pembelajaran Digital Terintegrasi
container-title: Jurnal Nasional Teknologi Komputer
8d9e6eda03dfac01f6842e7825e5ef7a62fa2465.abstract: Digital transformation in education encourages the use of platforms that integrate learning activities, academic administration, assessment, and communication among users. AIO Class is a digital learning management platform that provides various features to support teachers, students, and parents. This study aims to analyze the features and cross-actor workflows of AIO Class in supporting integrated digital learning management. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed through direct observation of the system using a demo account in 2025. The analysis covered user roles, system features, interactions among users, and learning and academic administration processes. A Use Case Diagram was used to map functions based on actors, while workflow modeling was applied to describe the sequence of activities and the involvement of each actor. The results show that AIO Class provides interconnected learning, assessment, academic administration, and communication features based on user access rights. The workflows demonstrate the involvement of teachers, students, and parents in assignment management, attendance, and Computer-Based Test (CBT) processes. The findings provide a mapping of features and cross-actor workflows that illustrates the interconnected functions of AIO Class in supporting integrated digital learning management.

title: Redundant attention fails to replicate as sustained engagement: Information quality in early review cohorts and long‐run popularity of books
container-title: Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology
29df535d6eda70428b375dc2ca2def53f85d92de.abstract: Abstract Early reviews on social reading platforms are an important clue for book buyers. However, research has so far focused on their volume and average rating rather than their informational content. To address this gap, we scraped nearly one million reviews of 25,000 books across five genres from lubimyczytac.pl, Poland's largest social reading platform. We modeled the long‐run accumulation of reviews attracted after a book's 30‐day initial launch window. Conditional on early review volume and book characteristics, reviews with greater semantic similarity and stronger solicitation cues predict less subsequent engagement. In contrast, early reviews with more linguistic perplexity and more diverse reviewer portfolios predict more engagement in the future. Furthermore, a text sentiment classifier we fine‐tuned to this specific domain added predictive signal beyond the raw star ratings, consistent with ratings being a coarsely discretized projection of the evaluative signal carried by review text. We frame these results within information quality theory: the informational profile of an early review cohort contributes to the prediction of sustained platform engagement beyond review volume and rating.

title: Hybrid Reliability-Based Control Optimization for Piezoelectric Structures via Adaptive Sequential Decoupling
container-title: AIAA Journal
6200c15a03facbce4d48271838a80c2b2f9c0c4c.abstract: Piezoelectric structures are widely used in active vibration control, but various uncertainties in practical engineering may lead to system failure. In this paper, a hybrid reliability-based proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controller design optimization framework is proposed for piezoelectric active control systems considering both interval and fuzzy uncertainties, taking the most widely used PID controller as an example. First, the fuzzy uncertainty is transformed into interval uncertainty by the cut-set strategy, and the adaptive dichotomy is used to select membership sample points intelligently to calculate the response boundary of the system. Then, the reliability index is defined in a nonprobabilistic way (the area ratio of the safety region of the limit state function to the total region) to quantify system safety. Next, a sequential decoupling strategy is adopted to optimize the PID parameters efficiently. This strategy updates the displacement constraints iteratively to meet the reliability requirements. Finally, the advantages of the proposed framework in terms of calculation accuracy and efficiency are verified by a piezoelectric plate example, and the influence of various uncertainties on the optimization results is analyzed by a piezoelectric shell example.

title:
Mimosa-Mimicking
Adaptive Dual-Mode Thermal Management
Device for Personal Moisture and Thermal Management
container-title: ACS Applied Polymer Materials
727750f7952cc4df93482c12134a6f968b9f8729.abstract: Abstract Adaptive dual-mode thermal management systems, which intelligently switch between heating and cooling based on environmental or physiological needs, hold transformative potential across multiple domains. Herein, a wearable mimosa-mimicking passive thermal management device (MTMD) is presented. The MTMD integrates a radiative and unidirectional water transportation Janus silk fabric as the cooling component and a flexible graphene film with photothermal, infrared-blocking, and moisture-blocking properties as the heating component. A modified wet-responsive Nafion membrane is employed as a switcher, which dynamically flattens/curls to enable/mute heating and cooling components. Experiments on human subjects demonstrate superior adaptive PPTM capability, with a maximum warming effect of 6.4 °C and a cooling effect of 2.9 °C compared with traditional cotton fabric, and a wide working range from 14 to 26 °C. The MTMD shows outstanding potential in personal thermal-moisture management, especially in sports scenarios, in seasons with significant temperature variations such as spring and autumn.

title: PAPR Control in Digital Predistortion Systems Using PC-CFR and RLS Forgetting Factor Adjustment
d551f9d0cde044113f400faf987650166c8a8e69.abstract: Abstract The high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals presents a challenge for power amplifier (PA) linearization. Cascaded crest factor reduction (CFR) and digital predistortion (DPD) suppress signal peaks and compensate for PA nonlinearity, but unsuitable parameter settings can cause excessive waveform distortion or peak regrowth after predistortion. This paper investigates the joint adjustment of peak-cancellation CFR (PC-CFR) and recursive least-squares (RLS) identification to control DPD-output PAPR while preserving linearization performance. The PC-CFR threshold determines the distortion introduced before predistortion, whereas the RLS forgetting factor influences coefficient adaptation and subsequent peak regrowth. A sequential procedure first determines the target PAPR immediately before normalized mean-square error (NMSE) first worsens and then selects the lowest-NMSE forgetting factor satisfying the PAPR constraint. Experimental results show that joint adjustment reduces DPD-output PAPR from 12.985 to 11.593 dB and improves PA feedback NMSE from -34.877 to -38.537 dB. The adjacent-channel power ratio (ACPR) in the upper and lower channels improves from -49.370/-50.332 to -51.923/-52.747 dBc. These results demonstrate coordinated peak suppression and improved linearization for the measured operating condition.

title: Effects of AI-Empowered Digital Inclusive Finance on the Income Growth of County-Level Farmers in Yunnan Province: An Empirical Test Based on County-Level Panel Data
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
26e7a2e0132358e730771e71c9a3dc17eac1b00e.abstract: {'en': "Using panel data of 119 counties (cities, districts) in Yunnan Province from 2015 to 2022, this paper constructs an AI-empowered digital inclusive finance index and examines its effect on county-level farmer income growth and the underlying channels with a two-way fixed-effects model. The results show that AI-empowered digital inclusive finance significantly promotes farmer income growth: a one-unit increase in the index raises rural residents' per capita disposable income by about 0.12% on average, and this conclusion remains robust after instrumental-variable estimation, replacement of the dependent variable, winsorization, and system GMM estimation. Mechanism tests indicate that AI-empowered digital inclusive finance mainly works through three channels—easing credit constraints, popularizing digital payment, and expanding e-commerce channels for agricultural products—whose combined mediation contribution exceeds one half. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the income effect is more pronounced for farmers in poverty-stricken and mountainous counties, and mainly manifests as growth in operating and wage income. Accordingly, policy recommendations are proposed, including deepening county-level intelligent risk control, improving rural digital infrastructure, developing e-commerce for plateau-featured agricultural products, and strengthening county-level financial risk monitoring."}

9b32e8ead5a930134b7e183251bc57cfcb45b344.abstract: In an increasingly volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous (VUCA) global environment, organizations face dual pressures to optimize existing operational capabilities while aggressively deploying digital innovations. This study investigates the structural mechanisms through which ambidextrous leadership drives sustainable organizational resilience via the mediating role of dynamic enterprise agility within emerging-market business enterprises. Anchored in the Dynamic Capabilities Framework and the Resource-Based View (RBV), we posit a structural model examining exploratory and exploitative leadership behaviors, process agility, market responsiveness, and multifaceted resilience (operational, financial, and strategic). Employing a cross-sectional, quantitative survey design, empirical data were gathered from N=412 senior executives, general managers, and chief technology officers across technology-enabled, manufacturing, and financial services firms in India. Structural Equation Modeling via Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM) was utilized to test the hypothesized paths and mediation effects. The results demonstrate that ambidextrous leadership exerts a statistically significant positive effect on organizational resilience (=0.342,p<0.001) and enterprise agility (=0.584,p<0.001). Furthermore, enterprise agility significantly mediates the relationship between ambidextrous leadership and organizational resilience (=0.286,p<0.001), accounting for a substantial indirect effect. The findings provide practical and theoretical frameworks for enterprise leaders navigating digital transformations under UGC-CARE and global research benchmark criteria, highlighting that structural ambidexterity without dynamic process adaptation yields suboptimal long-term stability.

title: Cold stress in fish: global mechanisms, adaptive strategies, and translational solutions for climate-resilient aquaculture
container-title: Frontiers in Marine Science
7756188024f260a6cc5790f75030244ca05be558.abstract: Water temperature is a fundamental abiotic factor that governs fish physiology, behavior, and survival. Although anthropogenic climate change is characterized by long-term warming and an overall decline in the frequency and intensity of cold extremes, regional climate variability and episodic cold events can still expose wild and farmed fishes to abrupt or physiologically stressful low-temperature conditions. This review synthesizes research on cold stress responses in fish from tropical, temperate, and polar environments from physiological and molecular perspectives. Using a structured literature search of major scientific databases for studies published between 1976 and 2026, we synthesized evidence across species and thermal environments. Building on earlier reviews, this cross-species synthesis links physiological, cellular, and molecular mechanisms of cold response with their implications for aquaculture management. Tropical fishes possess narrow thermal tolerance coupled with high vulnerability, whereas temperate species rely on metabolic and behavioral adjustments, and polar fish mostly depend on antifreeze proteins (AFPs) and cold-adapted enzymes. Exposure to low temperatures can elicit both detrimental stress effects and compensatory acclimatory responses, with their relative importance depending on the magnitude and duration of cooling, species-specific thermal limits, and prior thermal history. When cold exposure exceeds physiological tolerance, it may result in metabolic disruption, oxidative stress, osmoregulatory disturbance, immune suppression, and alterations in the gut microbiota. In contrast, modulation of MAPK and FoxO signaling, non-coding RNAs, and epigenetic regulation may participate in compensatory cellular responses that support physiological acclimation and, where demonstrated across generations, potentially contribute to longer-term thermal adaptation. Environmental management, dietary supplementation, selective breeding, pre-winter conditioning, and disease control represent potential strategies for mitigating cold-related losses in aquaculture, although the strength of supporting evidence and practical applicability vary among interventions, species, and production systems. We further identify critical knowledge gaps concerning long-term acclimation, transgenerational epigenetic inheritance, and interactions among multiple stressors. A key translational priority is to convert mechanistic indicators of cold tolerance into experimentally validated nutritional, breeding, and husbandry interventions that account for species-specific thermal biology and production conditions.

title: Task-dependent timing admissibility in digital seismology: forward propagation of structured timing errors into phase, polarisation, and array measurements
2b53ff39884b00e7c1f0a8819696dffc950ac151.abstract: Abstract. Accurate timing is essential in digital seismology, yet a single clock-accuracy specification does not determine whether a recording system is adequate for a given seismic measurement. Here I formulate timing quality as a task-dependent admissibility problem in which the temporal evolution, spatial or channel topology, and covariance of timing errors are propagated through the measurement operator of the observable of interest. Analytical and numerical formulations are developed for spectral phase, differential delay, three-component polarisation, array slowness and backazimuth, and coherent beamforming. The framework distinguishes absolute, differential, intercomponent, spatially structured, and common-mode timing errors and expresses admissibility through deterministic or probabilistic performance criteria. Controlled synthetic experiments, a perturbation benchmark using a public three-component seismic waveform, and a controlled benchmark based on a public compact-array geometry demonstrate that nominally identical timing uncertainties can produce markedly different measurement errors. At 10 Hz, a 95 % single-path phase criterion of 15° admits a timing standard deviation of approximately 2.13 ms, whereas corresponding representative benchmark limits are approximately 6.44 ms for intercomponent polarisation and 2.99 ms for compact-array backazimuth; an independent-error beam-coherence criterion CB ≥ 0.90 gives approximately 5.17 ms. These values are not interchangeable specifications because they act on different timing-error variables. Timing covariance is equally important: common-mode errors can cancel from relative observables, whereas differential errors remain observable, and spatially linear timing gradients can be indistinguishable from slowness perturbations under a plane-wave model. Extension to empirically estimated, non-Gaussian, and non-stationary clock processes would allow the same framework to support operational task-specific timing assessment. The results show that timing performance should be evaluated forward from the structured timing process to the intended seismic observable, rather than inferred from a universal millisecond threshold.
