                      <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05701956">NCT05701956</jats:ext-link>
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Mixed Reality
container-title: Environmental Justice in Digital Worlds
e04323502a4b153b2e9de555a487f931fc1a6812.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter looks at the ways in which Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Mixed Reality are inextricably linked. To do that, this chapter first looks at what is meant by current “Artificial Intelligence” and argues that in some ways it is best thought of as being neither artificial nor intelligent. The chapter then discusses the various ways in which Mixed Reality is the “eyes and ears” of AI, including using data collected via MR to train AI, using AI to create or improve MR elements in real time, and using AI to process MR data for users to allow a more minimally virtual mixed reality. Ultimately, the chapter argues that AI and MR work in concert to alter our experience of the environment and people’s roles in it.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Financial Decision-Making
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
9804e231d1b385dde790b1cf795ea7aaec80b1c1.abstract: <jats:p>Financial decision-making is being revolutionized by the use of artificial intelligence (AI). Whereas traditional statistical methods may be limited by the scope and complexity of contemporary financial datasets, AI technologies such as machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) permit companies to analyze not only structured but unstructured datasets efficiently. As such, there have been significant improvements in financial decision-making processes related to portfolio management, risk analysis, fraud detection, and algorithmic trading. However, the use of AI in the financial industry is also associated with issues such as lack of model transparency, algorithmic bias, and high reliance on past data, which create certain problems when it comes to transparency and reliability.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Decision-Making
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
478d0167085f2f271218a60ba78cf0ed82a89eb2.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping financial decision-making by enhancing analytical accuracy, speed, and strategic insight across corporate finance and financial services. The primary objective of the study is to evaluate how AI applications support strategic and operational financial decisions, while also assessing associated risks related to transparency, accountability, and decision control. A qualitative case study methodology is adopted, drawing on secondary data sources including corporate reports, financial disclosures, technology implementation documents, and industry publications. The findings indicate that AI significantly improves forecasting accuracy, real-time financial monitoring, and scenario analysis, leading to more informed and timely financial decisions. The study offers original value by providing practical, case-based evidence on how AI transforms financial decision-making processes beyond theoretical models. The implications are relevant for stakeholders seeking to leverage sustainable financial performance.</jats:p>

title: Evaluating the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Supply Chain Resilience of Goods Transportation
container-title: Auditing and Measuring Supply Chain Success and Sustainability
0f13c500235813cb1b24d53993c3fde254735b7c.abstract: <jats:p>In an era marked by heightened uncertainty and frequent disruptions, building resilient supply chains for goods has emerged as a strategic imperative for organizations. This study evaluates the role of Artificial Intelligence in enhancing supply chain resilience while transporting goods within a context of heightened disruption frequency by examining patterns of AI adoption, its practical applications, and the resulting organizational outcomes. Based on survey data from 160 industry professionals across various goods industries, we analyze the current state and perceived impact of AI integration. Findings indicate significant AI adoption, predominantly leveraging Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics. Significant statistical associations were found linking AI adoption to cost savings, specific resilience outcomes, and benefits. This research provides empirical validation of AI's positive influence on Supply Chain Resilience of goods transportation highlighting its capacity to improve organizational efficiency.</jats:p>

title: Attention Trap? How Visual Motion Shapes Children’s Screen Time and Engagement on Video Platforms
container-title: Information Systems Research
3836bd62e72740b25fd59c7e03808cdae1f4dd40.abstract:
<jats:p>Children spend considerable time watching online video, yet we know relatively little about which features of video content shape their engagement. This research examines one measurable feature: visual motion. Analyzing more than 32,000 videos from popular children’s channels on YouTube, we find that videos with greater visual motion receive more views, even after accounting for other visual, audio, and content characteristics. A randomized YouTube advertising experiment using professionally produced educational videos confirms this relationship; adding motion to the background increased view rates by about 2% at essentially no additional cost.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>An eye-tracking study with children aged 6–10 helps explain why. Visual motion does not prevent children from looking away. Instead, it reduces the duration of longer attentional lapses by bringing their gaze back to the screen more quickly. The additional attention is directed primarily toward the moving background rather than the instructor. The findings show how a measurable design feature can shape children’s attention and provide creators and platforms with a way to assess and design children’s video content more systematically.</jats:p>

title: Reconnoitring Yogic Peace of Mind and Transient Happiness With Their Perceived Psychological Correlates
container-title: The Neuroscience of Happiness
2a08909a0d86148aae4b34a85733003e4a4fe6d2.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter discusses yogic peace of mind as a complex, self-reported psychological construct and looks into its linkages with perceived cognition, emotional regulation, meditative consciousness, and well-being. The empirical part of the research is a pilot cross-sectional study conducted only using data collected via questionnaires; it did not include measurements of brain activity, neurotransmitter levels, the autonomic nervous system, or any other biological parameters. Consequently, all neurological hypotheses are discussed as interpretations based on existing neuroscience literature and not on the findings of this particular research. Some preliminary findings of factor, regression, and structural modeling analyses will be used to evaluate the proposed theoretical links between the concepts. There is evidence of correlations between long-term yogic practice, reported peace of mind, and positive psychological outcomes; however, there is no proof of causation or physiological changes. Further large-scale longitudinal studies are required to verify the hypothesis.</jats:p>

title: The application of an artificial intelligence–enhanced virtual reality cognitive behavioral therapy tool is feasible and acceptable in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: A multicenter mixed methods pilot study
container-title: Inflammatory Bowel Diseases
34e53c5af6594279fbcef7d176c277418b8c6c44.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently experience anxiety, pain, and reduced quality of life. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is effective for anxiety, but access may be limited. We evaluated the feasibility and explored the potential clinical impact of an artificial intelligence–powered virtual reality CBT-based application (XAIA [eXtended Reality Artificially Intelligent Ally]) in patients with IBD.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This was a multicenter, mixed-methods pilot study recruiting adults with IBD from the University of Chicago and Cedars-Sinai medical centers. Participants completed a single 30-minute session with the XAIA conversational avatar. Pain and anxiety were measured before and after the session using a visual analog pain scale and State–Trait Anxiety Inventory, respectively. Semi-structured interviews were conducted after the session to assess acceptability. Quantitative analysis was completed using paired t tests, and interview transcripts underwent thematic analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thirty-four participants (median age 34 years, 71% women, 59% with Crohn’s disease) participated in this study. Qualitative analysis revealed high acceptability, with participants reporting feelings of safety, validation, and improved coping. Participants valued the immersive environment, conversational avatar, and ability to discuss sensitive topics without judgment. As an exploratory outcome, participants reported a statistically significant improvement in pain (−0.46; P = .011) and anxiety (−10.65; P &lt; .001) immediately following a single session.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A single artificial intelligence–driven virtual reality CBT-based session in patients with IBD was feasible and well accepted and demonstrated preliminary evidence for acute reductions in pain and anxiety scores. Immersive digital behavioral health interventions may represent a scalable adjunct to traditional mental health support among adults with IBD.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Immersive Virtual Reality Cognitive Stimulation for Delirium Prevention in Older Surgical Intensive Care Unit Patients With Cognitive Impairment: Protocol for a 3-Arm Randomized Pilot Trial
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
6a0305024bfe7ca8c2a7ec25512ab1521c9d9887.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Postoperative delirium is common among older adults after major surgery, especially those with cognitive impairment, and is associated with prolonged hospitalization, functional decline, mortality, and subsequent cognitive deterioration. Nonpharmacologic delirium-prevention strategies are recommended but are difficult to deliver reliably in high-acuity environments because they require repeated staff-intensive interactions, consistent patient engagement, and integration into complex intensive care unit (ICU) workflows.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to evaluate the feasibility, usability, safety, acceptance, and adherence of ReCognitionVR 2.0, an immersive virtual reality (VR)–based cognitive stimulation intervention designed for older surgical ICU patients with mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This is a single-center, 3-arm, parallel-group randomized pilot trial. Ninety adults aged 65 years or older undergoing major surgery with expected postoperative ICU admission and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores of 15 to 24 will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to ReCognitionVR 2.0 cognitive stimulation, passive VR control exposure, or standard-of-care nurse-led reality orientation. VR sessions will be delivered once daily for up to 20 minutes on postoperative days 1 through 3 when participants are calm and alert. The primary outcomes are feasibility metrics, including recruitment, outcome completion, safety and tolerability, usability, acceptance, and adherence. Secondary outcomes estimate preliminary changes in attention and executive function using the Months Backward Test and NIH Toolbox Flanker Inhibitory Control and Attention Test. Postoperative delirium incidence is an exploratory clinical outcome.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study was funded in September 2025. Participant recruitment and data collection are currently ongoing. Preliminary data quality assessments and exploratory reviews of the collected data are underway. Formal statistical analyses of the trial outcomes will be conducted after participant enrollment is completed and the study database has been finalized and locked. As of July 29, 2026, we had enrolled 18 participants. Early operational experience informed the refinement of exploratory VR performance metrics and the documentation of protocol deviations. Following an oxygen-connection near miss, we added a preintervention oxygen/readiness checklist as an operational safety safeguard. Enrollment of 90 participants is projected to be completed in 2027 if the current recruitment pace is sustained. Results are expected to be published in winter 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This protocol will generate data on feasibility, safety, usability, adherence, digital performance, cognitive assessment, and delirium measurement, all needed to optimize ReCognitionVR 2.0 and to design a future multicenter efficacy trial of VR-enabled delirium prevention in critical care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Irresponsible regional future-making: fast forward as if there were no crises?
container-title: Cambridge Journal of Regions, Economy and Society
0e1287016d1aad62bdab34f124d9d1d4357d5d3d.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Although the current era is one of multiple global crises that call for more sustainable solutions, the futures imagined in many regions do not seem to address these crises adequately but are marked by irresponsibility, that is, the shifting of negative effects in time, space or within the population. These futures can be irresponsible in regions whose imagined future is a continuation of the past, as well as in regions whose imagined futures involve radical transformations. The article uses the discursive-institutionalist concept of ideational power to discuss how irresponsible futures emerge in these regions and which role power relations play in these imagined futures.</jats:p>

title: Safeguarding Democracy in the Age of Artificial Intelligence Warfare
container-title: Reframing Democracy Through International Relations, Strategy, and Governance in a Fragmented World
a76d47ff83e1035fea0593c859a1f74dd1205877.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has transformed the contemporary information environment, creating new forms of digital influence capable of shaping political narratives and public perception. While artificial intelligence offers significant benefits for governance, innovation, and communication, it also introduces complex risks for democratic societies. One of the most pressing challenges is the emergence of AI-driven disinformation, where automated systems are used to generate and disseminate misleading or fabricated content at unprecedented scale. Such developments threaten electoral integrity, institutional trust, and the credibility of public information systems. This chapter examines the relationship between artificial intelligence–enabled information warfare and democratic governance from a global perspective. It explores how disinformation campaigns operate within digital ecosystems and evaluates policy responses aimed at protecting democratic processes.</jats:p>

title: Should quantum physics be approached with mathematical formalism in school? Effects of instructional approach on functional understanding under cognitive and affective controls
container-title: Physical Review Physics Education Research
6493f05b70eb976685bab6227f1a5b655fc3ff28.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Evidence from physics education research suggests that the introduction of mathematical formalism in quantum physics instruction can support the development of students’ conceptual understanding, particularly by promoting functional ways of reasoning about quantum phenomena. However, empirical findings on the effectiveness of such approaches at the secondary school level remain inconclusive, and little is known about the extent to which learning outcomes are shaped by instructional design as opposed to learners’ affective and cognitive characteristics. This study addresses this gap by investigating the relative influence of instructional approach on students’ understanding of single-photon states, while controlling for prior knowledge, cognitive load, situational interest, and physics self-concept. A quasiexperimental pre-post design was implemented with
                    <a:math xmlns:a="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <a:mi>N</a:mi>
                      <a:mo>=</a:mo>
                      <a:mn>172</a:mn>
                    </a:math>
                    upper secondary students, comparing a qualitative instructional condition with an approach supplemented by a reduced Dirac formalism. Learning outcomes were assessed using the framework of Functional Fidelity and Fidelity of Gestalt. A multivariate analysis of covariance, followed by univariate analyses of covariance, was conducted to examine the contributions of instructional and learner-related variables. The findings indicate that affective variables emerge as strong predictors of functional understanding and suggest that learning in quantum physics is driven less by instructional format than by learners’ affective and cognitive prerequisites. In particular, fostering interest appears to be a key mechanism for supporting the development of functional understanding. The results highlight the importance of integrating affective dimensions into instructional design and provide a basis for future research on the interaction between instructional approaches and learner characteristics in quantum physics education.
                  </jats:p>

title: Retracting Attention
container-title: Seeing and Subjectivity
3a0cc0cdb516ebbc09d01859d15f1425d1efc074.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Further insight is at hand in a text Bhattacharyya does not discuss, but might have, Manu’s Code Law. Here we find a description of the lived experience of the wandering ascetic (yati), depicted as consisting in a state of ambient perceptual awareness; the experience of the ascetic is one of full attentional retraction. When Kalidas Bhattacharyya writes that ‘negative attention [is] a sort of concentrated withdrawal from, rather than positive fixation of, the content whose truth is sought to be discovered’, it is negative attention as attentional retraction that he has in mind, rather than either as absential attention or apophatic attention. The ascetic’s ambient awareness consists of a field of purely marginal consciousness, and it is here alone, Gurwitsch insists, that the sense of self (the dative of presentation) is to be found.</jats:p>

title: CL-GGD: Cross-layer Semantic Geometry Distillation for Lightweight Text Embedding Reconstruction
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
c056e1f76834c570bfad1b62f317100538dd3eb1.abstract: <jats:p>Lightweight sentence embedding models are critical for large-scale retrieval and semantic matching, yet aggressive compression often disrupts the semantic geometry learned by powerful teachers. Existing distillation methods primarily rely on point-wise feature matching or task-specific supervision, which fails to preserve fine-grained relational structure across samples. In this work, we propose Cross-layer Gram Geometry Distillation, a geometry-centric framework that transfers semantic structure by aligning pairwise similarity relations across teacher and student layers. By projecting multi-layer representations into a unified hyperspherical space and matching their Gram matrices under a cross-layer weighting mechanism, the student is optimized to reconstruct the teacher’s neighborhood geometry. An additional covariance regularizer is introduced to mitigate representation collapse and anisotropy. Extensive experiments on sentence embedding benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing distillation baselines under strict parameter and latency constraints. Theoretical analysis further establishes that minimizing Gram discrepancy yields explicit guarantees on nearest-neighbor preservation, providing a principled foundation for retrieval-oriented lightweight embedding reconstruction.</jats:p>

title: PGP-FD: A Lightweight Phase-Guided Generative Graph Process for Resource-Efficient Edge Fault Pattern Recognition in Fire-Protection Valve Sensing Systems
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
e8c77c8dfb0acb232d4d72b81bf0990419bebb53.abstract: <jats:p>Edge fire-protection sensing systems must recognize latent valve faults under limited computation, memory, and energy budgets, although fault samples are scarce and operational responses are strongly phase-dependent. This paper proposes PGP-FD, a lightweight phase-guided generative graph process for event-driven edge fault pattern recognition. Each valve operation or inspection is represented as a compact response window. A depthwise temporal encoder captures local dynamics, a monotonic phase gate models the ordered evolution of standby, actuation, transient, recovery, and settling phases, and a compact measurement graph learns hydraulic-mechanical coupling among pressure, valve motion, and event context. To reduce class imbalance, a fault-conditioned stochastic process generates rare events during training under range, phase-order, and valve-pressure consistency constraints. The training-only posterior and offline synthesis branches are removed during deployment, while confidence-uncertainty prefix inference avoids unnecessary continuous computation and retains full processing for difficult cases. Experiments on real fire-protection valve data show that PGP-FD improves recognition quality, response speed, and online model compactness over representative baselines. The results demonstrate a practical integration of lightweight pattern recognition and mechanism-consistent generative learning for resource-efficient industrial edge intelligence.</jats:p>

title: Optimized Emergency Sign Language Recognition with Large-Kernel Attention Graph Convolutional Network for Accurate Gesture Classification
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
3737bdb37c2afdac92e2c8a956436c9b57e10253.abstract: <jats:p>Sign Language Recognition (SLR) plays a significant role in improving communication accessibility for hearing-impaired individuals, particularly in emergency scenarios where fast and reliable gesture interpretation is required. However, emergency Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition remains challenging due to rapid hand movements, visually similar gestures, and complex spatial–temporal relationships among hand components. This study proposes an SLR-HIE-LKAGCN framework that integrates topology-aware spatial representation, spatial–temporal feature learning, graph-based gesture modeling, and optimization-based parameter adaptation for emergency ISL recognition. Initially, input gesture frames are processed using a Simplicial Convolutional Filter (SCF) to preserve higher-order spatial relationships among hand regions and enhance gesture representation. The refined gesture sequences are then provided to a Spatial–Temporal Knowledge-Embedded Transformer (STKET) to capture temporal dependencies and contextual movement patterns. The extracted features are further analyzed employing a Large-Kernel Attention Graph Convolutional Network (LKAGCN), which models relationships among hand landmarks and learns discriminative gesture representations. In addition, the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (SBOA) is employed to optimize critical network parameters and improve model convergence. The proposed framework is evaluated on emergency ISL gesture categories, including accident, call, doctor, help, hot, lose, pain, and thief. Experimental outcomes establish that the proposed technique achieves superior recognition performance with 98.82% accuracy, 98.57% precision, and 98.53% F1-score, outperforming existing approaches. The obtained results indicate that SLR-HIE-LKAGCN provides an effective and computationally efficient solution for real-time emergency ISL recognition.</jats:p>

title: Time-Series Load Prediction and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient-Based Task Scheduling Optimization for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Networks
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
4426ee3d8d3e458e60b0b22081da6f21626d3046.abstract: <jats:p>Cloud-edge collaborative networks have become an important computing paradigm for latency-sensitive and resource-intensive applications, but dynamic workload variation makes efficient task scheduling difficult. Existing scheduling methods often rely on current system states and cannot proactively respond to future load fluctuations, leading to congestion, delayed execution, and unbalanced resource utilization. This paper proposes PL-DDPG, a prediction-enhanced load-aware deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm for cloud-edge task scheduling. The method first predicts multi-horizon edge load trajectories from historical workload sequences, then integrates predicted loads, current observations, task features, and prediction residuals into an augmented reinforcement learning state. A deterministic actor–critic scheduler generates continuous task assignment, CPU allocation, and bandwidth allocation decisions, while a feasibility projection layer and risk-aware reward improve constraint satisfaction and service reliability. Experiments on four public workload datasets show that PL-DDPG consistently improves delay, energy efficiency, SLA satisfaction, load balancing, and scheduling stability. These results demonstrate that prediction-enhanced continuous control provides an effective solution for proactive cloud-edge resource orchestration.</jats:p>

title: ATT-SV2-ES Net: Hybrid Deep Learning Features and Lightweight Attention-Based Model for Early Glaucoma Detection
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
bc275378bb5009d7f256155d09bb39b3c0bf9888.abstract: <jats:p>Glaucoma is one of the main causes of permanent blindness. Timely intervention is ensured by its early and precise identification. This paper proposes a new hybrid approach, integrating handcrafted features with Deep Learning (DL), for reliable glaucoma identification and prediction on the G1020 dataset. Initially, pre-processing is conducted, which includes data augmentation to increase the diversity of images, Gaussian filtering to reduce image noise, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to enhance local retinal contrast and then grayscale conversion to simplify retinal image representation. After pre-processing, the enhanced images were given to Depthwise Dilated Spatial Attention Mechanism (DDSAM)-based Glau-SegNet for optic disk (OD) and optic cup (OC) segmentation. From the segmented images, handcrafted features, such as Local Binary Patterns (LBPs) and fractal analysis, which describe complementary texture and structural information, are extracted. In parallel, the segmented images are processed by the Attention ShuffleNet V2 with Echo State Network (Att-SV2-ES Net) to obtain high-level deep feature representations. Then these deep features and handcrafted features are concatenated and fed to a fully connected layer with sigmoid activation to classify into the class for the prediction of glaucoma. This combined approach achieves a balance between high accuracy and scalability, addressing the growing need for accessible and reliable glaucoma screening solutions. The experimental results demonstrate the proposed system’s superior performance in detecting and predicting glaucoma. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the proposed model, which integrates DL features, outperforms all other models in terms of key performance metrics, including achieving 99.32% specificity, 99.43% sensitivity, and 99.37% accuracy.</jats:p>

title: Toward Lightweight Fine-Tuning of YOLO via Guided Optimization for Cross-Domain Remote Sensing Object Detection
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
5932f2f56a4def2ac4f225db5167f427ca7ef859.abstract: <jats:p>Deep learning has advanced remote sensing object detection, yet prevailing detectors are tailored to individual datasets, generalize poorly across domains, and rely on large labeled corpora and heavy computation ill-suited to on-device platforms. This paper presents RMoE-YOLO, a lightweight fine-tuning framework that adapts a pretrained YOLOv8n detector to new remote sensing domains under tight label and compute budgets. Its core component is an object-oriented mixture-of-experts (OMoE) module placed before the detection head, where lightweight expert subnetworks learn object-category-conditioned representations and an image-level gating network selects the most relevant experts for each input. A saliency-aware sparsity term and a phased hierarchical fine-tuning schedule guide the adaptation, balancing retention of pretrained knowledge against adaptation to the target domain. On NWPU-VHR-10, RSOD, and SIMD, together with cross-domain transfer, RMoE-YOLO improves low-label cross-domain detection while remaining efficient. Under a controlled multi-seed protocol on a 5% label single-class adaptation setting, its multi-expert configuration significantly outperforms the YOLOv8n baseline by 1.7[Formula: see text]mAP[Formula: see text] points ([Formula: see text]), while its single-expert configuration matches the baseline accuracy at only 19.5 active GFLOPs, below YOLOv8n, and a comparable frame rate. RMoE-YOLO offers a practical route to accurate, generalizable, and efficient detection in low-resource remote sensing.</jats:p>

title: An Enhanced RT-DETR with Selective Boundary Aggregation and Tri-Focal CIoU Loss for Real-Time Object Detection
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
8fe4d107db20a206822cedf0a8fc129f1135e150.abstract: <jats:p>Real-Time Detection Transformer (RT-DETR) is the first detection transformer-based model to achieve real-time performance. However, the concatenation operation treats all scale features equally without adaptive weighting, leading to insufficient multi-scale feature fusion. In addition, Generalized Intersection over Union (GIoU) does not explicitly consider the center distance and aspect ratio between the predicted bounding boxes and the ground-truth boxes, leading to slow convergence. To address the above problems, this paper proposes Tri-Focal DEtection TRansformer (TriDETR) by replacing the GIoU loss function with the Tri-Focal Complete Intersection over Union (CIoU) loss to optimize overlap and assign weights, allowing the model to focus on difficult patterns. Additionally, TriDETR uses Selective Boundary Aggregation (SBA) to better fuse multi-scale features. Experiments were conducted on PASCAL VOC 2007, Foggy Cityscapes, and ACDC datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Specifically, in terms of [Formula: see text], TriDETR outperforms RT-DETR with the same backbone by 0.80-0.98 on PASCAL VOC, 0.20-1.23 on Foggy Cityscapes, and 0.30–0.95 on ACDC (snow, rain, and nighttime). Additionally, TriDETR outperforms the best-performing YOLO26 variant while maintaining approximately the same frames per second.</jats:p>

title: Application of Digital Health Interventions for Cognitive Management in Children With Cancer: Scoping Review
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
488230a323f4a1db95fece744265b1e2765b04ec.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Advances in the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer have substantially improved survival, resulting in a growing population of survivors of childhood cancer who may experience long-term treatment-related sequelae. Cognitive late effects are an important long-term consequence of childhood cancer and can affect cognitive functioning, psychosocial well-being, and quality of life. Digital health interventions offer accessible and flexible approaches to managing cognitive difficulties among children with cancer. However, the existing evidence has not yet been comprehensively synthesized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to map and synthesize the existing evidence on digital health interventions for cognitive management among children with cancer; characterize intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components; and identify evidence gaps and priorities for future research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Arksey and O’Malley framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) checklist. Six academic databases, including PubMed, Embase (Ovid), CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, were systematically searched for relevant studies published between January 2010 and August 2026. Eligibility criteria were developed using the population-concept-context framework. Two reviewers independently performed study screening and data extraction. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Screening was performed independently at the title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved through discussion and, when necessary, consultation with a third reviewer. Descriptive statistics and thematic content analysis were used to synthesize the findings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 5371 records were identified through the literature search. Following screening, 19 publications representing 14 independent study samples and involving 566 children with cancer were included. Four digital health modalities were identified: computer-based interventions, internet-based interventions, mobile apps, and neurofeedback training. Computer-based interventions were the predominant modality. Across these modalities, working memory and attention were the most frequently targeted cognitive domains, while feasibility, acceptability, and adherence were the most commonly assessed implementation-related outcomes. However, relatively few interventions incorporated coach support, telephone-based communication, or educational components, and none evaluated economic outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although digital health interventions show promise for supporting cognitive function in children with cancer, substantial gaps remain in the current evidence. This scoping review mapped the field according to intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components, rather than focusing solely on the efficacy of individual technologies. Future research should prioritize the development of multidimensional, personalized, and functionally integrated digital health interventions that combine cognitive training with supportive care, education, monitoring, and communication. Multicenter randomized controlled trials should subsequently evaluate these interventions using clinically meaningful outcomes, with comprehensive assessments of safety, adherence, implementation, and health economic outcomes to establish their effectiveness, feasibility, and sustainability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: EAS-Cap: Event-Aware Semantic-Enhanced Video Captioning
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
ee1cf5cdb0937cd336fa911362ad8aee9803609f.abstract: <jats:p>Video captioning faces significant challenges in balancing global semantic consistency with fine-grained syntactic accuracy, particularly in complex multi-event scenarios. Existing global alignment methods often suffer from semantic dilution, while fine-grained approaches based on Part-of-Speech tagging frequently encounter compositional failures. To bridge these gaps, we propose Event-Aware Semantic-Enhanced Captioning (EAS-Cap), a novel framework that redefines the fundamental learning unit as Atomic Events — indivisible Subject-Verb-Object triplets extracted via syntactic analysis. EAS-Cap decomposes the captioning task into three synergistic objectives: atomic event extraction, cross-modal semantic distillation, and global-local consistency optimization. Specifically, our Event Module employs learnable queries to distill textual priors into visual encoders, enhancing sensitivity to specific actions, while a Visual-to-Event constraint ensures local features remain consistent with global context. Extensive experiments on the MSVD and MSR-VTT datasets demonstrate that EAS-Cap achieves excellent performance, notably leading in CIDEr scores. These results confirm our method’s superior capability in preserving syntactic integrity and accurately describing complex temporal dynamics without relying on noisy global signals or explicit grammatical constraints.</jats:p>

title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
Designing Memorable Guest Experiences in the Experience Economy
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
7af8d5867cc8acf296fc5b100303d5193e099db4.abstract: <jats:p>The hospitality industry has transitioned from service delivery to experience orchestration, where value is created through memorable and emotionally engaging guest experiences. This chapter develops an integrated conceptual framework that explains how experience design influences customer outcomes. Drawing on a structured review of hospitality and tourism literature, the study identifies key inputs—personalization, servicescape, and storytelling—along with mediating mechanisms such as emotional engagement, co-creation, and psychological immersion. These factors collectively shape outcomes including memorable tourism experiences, customer satisfaction, loyalty, and destination competitiveness. The findings highlight the importance of balancing technological innovation with human interaction to enhance experiential value. By integrating fragmented research streams, this chapter provides both theoretical and managerial insights into designing meaningful and competitive hospitality experiences in the experience economy.</jats:p>

title: From Transactions to Transformations
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
615fdb83bc7fe603873e78b64b013c17947f7156.abstract: <jats:p>The hospitality industry is abandoning transaction-based service models and moving towards experience-driven and transformation-oriented value creation. This chapter investigates the changes in hospitality experiences through customer interaction, co-creation, emotional engagement, and technology integration. Utilizing service-dominant logic and experience economy perspectives, it emphasizes that customer experience is a continuous and evolving process throughout the entire journey. Emotional engagement affects satisfaction, loyalty, and behavior. The research also focuses on Generation Z, whose inclination for personalized and technology-enabled experiences is significantly influencing expectations. In order to fill the gaps, the chapter introduces the Transformative Hospitality Experience Model (THEM) which illustrates the transition from transaction to transformation.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Experience Economics on Hospitality Towards a Human-Centered Approach 5.0
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
86cc9dbe157a833a386f866d103fa6cc227f9792.abstract: <jats:p>This paper is about how the hospitality industry has been changing into a human-centric model through digital technologies and human interactions to create a better customer experience within the Experience Economy. This evolution will focus on providing 'emotional satisfaction' for guests, increasing the level of personalization throughout all aspects of service and creating something new for each individual guest. Additionally, this study will investigate how the combination of 'technology' and 'innovation' will impact current hotel practices to meet the increasing expectations of today's consumers. To this end, qualitative methods were used to gather data from two groups, hotel managers and professionals who specialize in digitization, through interviews to gather information on the role of personalization, artificial intelligence, and interaction of systems on the guest experience in the hospitality industry.</jats:p>

title: Place-Based Hospitality 5.0
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
cd4e8af466a7e9f7c6d834d7e0c3fd9ffda7d92c.abstract: <jats:p>Hospitality has traditionally been shaped by the experience economy, where service is staged as performance and guests are treated as audiences. While this model creates value, it often commodifies culture, place, and human interaction, reducing hospitality to spectacle and weakening authenticity, reciprocity, and care. At the same time, Hospitality 5.0, inspired by Industry 5.0 and Society 5.0, introduces a human-centered approach focused on dignity, collaboration with technology, and societal well-being. This paper argues that these paradigms are not conflicting but can be meaningfully integrated through a place-based ethos. Such an ethos centers hospitality on the cultural, relational, and ecological uniqueness of local contexts, redefining the host's role from performer to steward. In this perspective, Hospitality 5.0 becomes not just a technological shift but a deeper commitment to people, communities, and place. The paper contributes to hospitality theory and offers practical insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers seeking more sustainable and ethical models.</jats:p>

title: Neuro-Tourism
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
c6b53e96792a0ceed61271512cc85e440fae763b.abstract: <jats:p>The foundations of neuro-tourism and experiential neuroscience represent an emerging interdisciplinary frontier that integrates insights from neuroscience, psychology, tourism studies, and technology to understand and enhance how individuals perceive, experience, and remember travel. At its core, neuro-tourism seeks to apply principles from Neuroscience and Cognitive Psychology to analyze tourists' emotional, cognitive, and sensory responses to destinations, attractions, and experiences, thereby enabling the design of more engaging, meaningful, and memorable journeys. This approach moves beyond traditional tourism research, which often relies on self-reported data and observational methods, by incorporating neuroscientific tools and methodologies such as brain imaging, biometric tracking, and psychophysiological measurements to capture real-time at a deeper, objective level. Experiential neuroscience, a closely related concept, focuses on how the brain processes and encodes lived experiences, emphasizing the role of perception.</jats:p>

title: Neuro-Tourism in Hospitality 5.0 to Optimize Emotional Experience
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
8d60129c07710b9b8e1f7b8968216e2cfe78640e.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter proposes a biometric-driven mathematical framework to optimize emotional experiences within Hospitality 5.0 through neuro-tourism applications. Addressing limitations of traditional post-experience evaluation methods, the study integrates real-time biometric signals, including heart rate variability, facial emotion recognition, and gaze tracking, to model guest emotional states. A quantitative optimization function is developed to dynamically align service environments with predicted emotional responses. Using experimental design and machine learning techniques, the framework enables proactive personalization and adaptive service delivery. Findings demonstrate the potential to enhance guest satisfaction, operational efficiency, and decision intelligence, contributing a novel interdisciplinary approach to data-driven, human-centric hospitality systems.</jats:p>

title: Insights on Neuro Tourism in Hospitality 5.0
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
35db32d389fca3d52b3a6c767b7f0267abffdc9c.abstract: <jats:p>Tourism marketers can examine their traveler's brain waves and how different stimuli affect them through using neuroscience in tourism, also referred as “neuro-tourism”. Neuro-tourism allows access to travelers' minds, giving us real-time insight into what they consciously and unconsciously feel. Neuromarketing methods such as brain–computer interface (BCI), eye tracking, galvanic skin reaction have been implemented in neuro-tourism for purposes of designing tourism products and services that increase visitors happiness and experience. Since neuro-tourism is relatively new and there are few studies on the topic, this chapter offered an indepth investigation of peer reviewed journal papers published within neuro-tourism research during the past years in order to highlight possible trends in this line of research and present implications for researchers.</jats:p>

title: Emotional Intelligence and Mental Well-Being in AI-Driven Hospitality
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
53a8b9399dccecdf1d6c3cc1543b58d05b5ccf4c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and digital service systems within the hospitality sector has ushered in an era known as Hospitality 5.0. While these advancements enhance efficiency, personalization, and guest satisfaction, they also increase emotional labor, psychological strain, and occupational stress among employees. This chapter analyzes, using major theories and frameworks, how emotional intelligence and mental well-being mediate sustainable workforce outcomes in AI-intensive hospitality. An original conceptual model, the Emotionally Sustainable Hospitality Workforce Model (ESHWM), is introduced, highlighting sustainable HRM as critical for maintaining emotional and psychological health amid digital disruption. The chapter summarizes empirical evidence linking AI adoption to increased workplace stress and shows how high emotional intelligence protects and boosts frontline hospitality worker performance. Practical implications are offered for managers, HR practitioners, and policymakers, aligning with UN SDGs 3, 8, and 9.</jats:p>

title: Designing Regenerative Guest Experiences in Hospitality 5.0
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
5cc0cb59040fbb71fe95e38a5c9191ae45f73cc3.abstract: <jats:p>The emergence of Hospitality 5.0 has intensified the need to balance technological innovation with human-centered value creation. Simultaneously, regenerative hospitality is gaining prominence as a paradigm that seeks to generate positive social, cultural, environmental, and economic outcomes beyond conventional sustainability practices. This study explores how human capital contributes to the design and delivery of regenerative guest experiences within technology-enabled hospitality environments. Drawing on Experience Economy Theory, Service-Dominant Logic, and Regenerative Tourism Theory, the study adopts a qualitative approach based on semi-structured interviews with 22 stakeholders. Thematic analysis reveals that human capital mediates the relationship between advanced technologies and regenerative outcomes through experience curation, human–technology collaboration, and stakeholder co-creation. The study proposes a Human-Centric Regenerative Hospitality 5.0 Framework and identifies competencies needed to foster transformative and regenerative guest experiences.</jats:p>

title: Leading in the Algorithmic Hospitality Era
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
dc853f3918a8efbb04a94e84950cf2028afdd896.abstract: <jats:p>The algorithmic transformation of hospitality is fundamentally reshaping the conditions under which service leaders create, sustain, and differentiate meaningful guest experiences. As artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and smart service technologies become embedded across operational and strategic functions, a defining tension emerges: how to preserve human warmth and relational authenticity within increasingly automated service ecosystems. Drawing on experience economy theory, service dominant logic, and emerging Hospitality 5.0 scholarship, this chapter develops the Human Centric Algorithmic Leadership model, a four dimensional conceptual framework that anchors leadership practice in human values while deliberately leveraging algorithmic capabilities. Through theoretically grounded propositions and analytically framed mini cases, the chapter offers both scholarly contribution and practical guidance for hospitality leaders navigating the algorithmic era.</jats:p>

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence and Technological Innovations for SDG 9
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
4291b1d07c6c301ea5093a1541103751eefcaea7.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The accelerating advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and technological innovations presents transformative opportunities for achieving Sustainable Development Goal 9 (SDG 9), which emphasizes building resilient infrastructure, promoting inclusive and sustainable industrialization, and fostering innovation. Despite growing global attention, the integration of AI and emerging technologies into industrial development strategies, especially in developing economies, remains limited and uneven. As AI and emerging technologies transform industries and economies, their potential to advance SDG 9 is still largely untapped. This chapter explores the transformative impact of AI and technological innovations on the three pillars of SDG 9 through a series of case studies. The findings indicate that AI-driven solutions such as predictive maintenance for infrastructure, smart manufacturing systems and data-driven innovation ecosystems greatly improve efficiency, minimize resource waste and broaden access to industrial opportunities. However, several challenges remain, including the digital divide, ethical dilemmas associated with AI deployment and inadequate policy frameworks to ensure equitable benefits. The research emphasizes the necessity of collaboration among governments, industries, and civil society to scale AI applications while addressing inequalities in technological access and promoting sustainable practices. By recommending actionable strategies for integrating AI into national industrialization agendas and innovation policies, this study aims to bridge the gap between technological potential and the implementation of SDG 9. Ultimately, it advocates for a balanced approach that harnesses AI’s capabilities to create resilient systems, empower marginalized communities, and drive sustainable industrial growth, ensuring that technological advancements align with the inclusive and environmentally conscious principles of the 2030 Agenda.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Innovation EdTech Startups: A Bibliographic Review of Industry 5.0’s Implications for Sustainable Growth
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
65db5ccadd16a00e3aac401ac37197f7b011310f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter presents a systematic bibliographic review, investigating the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in fostering innovation within Educational Technology (EdTech) startups, contextualized within the human-centric and sustainable framework of Industry 5.0. Analyzing 42 scholarly works published between 2014 and 2024, this chapter explores the alignment of AI-driven entrepreneurial ventures in education with the core tenets of sustainability, resilience, and inclusivity. The findings reveal a complex landscape where technological innovation, while promising personalized learning and operational scalability, often exacerbates ethical dilemmas, regulatory gaps, and the digital divide. This chapter identifies a critical tension between rapid, profit-driven technological adoption and the deliberate, value-led innovation advocated by Industry 5.0. It concludes that for AI-powered EdTech startups to truly contribute to sustainable growth, a fundamental shift is required, from a paradigm of disruptive techno-solutionism to one of responsible innovation. This necessitates collaborative governance, ethically conscious design, and entrepreneurial models that prioritize equitable access, thereby ensuring that AI acts as a catalyst for building smarter, fairer, and more resilient education systems.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Talent Management and Acquisition for Small-Scale Handicraft Business in an Emerging Economy
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
94bfd2c739a06e30731f8df298b2a74d22dc2558.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The purpose of this study is to identify and investigate human resources (HR) challenges for SME-based handicraft businesses in the context of an emerging economy, which is one of the most critical and expanding industries for both the domestic economy and the global market. The study was conducted by following a qualitative approach to gather data through in-depth interviews and industry observations with 15 handicraft business owners from the Dhaka division in Bangladesh. It enabled the identification of transient and permanent operational patterns, as well as HR challenges, policies, and procedures in the industry. Results showed that typical HR procedures have essential flaws. Trusted recruitment approaches, primarily social media, promoted trust but limited diversity and innovation. Recruitment, especially for rural craftsmen, was a major logistical obstacle that hampered efficiency, as their items needed to be pure and genuine to preserve cultural authenticity. This chapter also found that informal incentives were used in the sector although low earnings and high personnel turnover caused motivation and retention to fluctuate. Inconsistent skill development due to poorly planned training programs affected product quality. Because most cultures undervalue handicrafts as a career, recruiting and retaining young people has become more difficult. Protecting proprietary designs hampered sector scalability. The report proposed a complete sustainable HR framework to solve these issues. Strategic ideas were valued, formal incentive systems were implemented, training programs were improved, and intellectual property protections were increased.</jats:p>

title: Strengthening Smart Cities Across Africa With Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
8e02c0a6e6a18bb2a312aa95986a867b545eef6d.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As the globe enters the machine learning era and the progress in smart systems, the ramifications for urban growth, especially in African cities, are significant. Utilizing artificial intelligence’s (AI’s) potential, African cities experience better infrastructure, more efficient resource distribution, and heightened resilience against urban issues like traffic congestion, insufficient services, internal security, conflicts, and environmental deterioration. Despite the benefits of sustainable cities in Africa, they encountered potential obstacles such as outdated infrastructure and limited resources. As such, this chapter’s objectives are as follows: (i) to scrutinize the task of AI in smart cities across Africa, (ii) to examine the success rate of African smart cities over the years, and (iii) to proffer pragmatic solutions to the identified challenges confronting smart cities in Africa. This chapter adopts a qualitative method of investigation to unravel what a smart city in Africa entails, its achievements, and possible challenges. This chapter argues that AI applications and innovations can be enablers and problem solvers for smart cities across Africa.</jats:p>

title: Rapid identification of porcine bacterial pathogens using an artificial intelligence Raman microbial analyzer for biology
container-title: Microbiology Spectrum
111991356aa6915a44792218f705c3ee62f8317c.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      Rapid and accurate identification of bacterial pathogens is critical for effective disease control in pig farms. Conventional bacterial culture-based and molecular diagnostic methods are time-consuming and often impractical for clinical decision-making. Raman spectroscopy, combined with artificial intelligence, offers a label-free alternative and provides isolate-level identification within approximately 2 min. The aim of this study was to evaluate the performance of the commercial Artificial Intelligent Raman Microbial Analyzer for Biology (AIRMAB) for the rapid clinical identification of swine bacterial pathogens. Bacterial isolates were collected from various tissues of diseased pigs between March and November 2025 at the Animal Disease Diagnostic Center, National Pingtung University of Science and Technology, Taiwan. The species-level identification of all the isolates was confirmed using species-specific polymerase chain reaction assays prior to Raman spectral acquisition, ensuring the accuracy of the reference labels. Overall, the AIRMAB system exhibited high performance in the identification of all 14 clinically relevant pig bacterial pathogens. Notably, perfect recall (100%) was achieved for clinically common species in the test set, including
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Pasteurella multocida</jats:italic>
                      (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                      = 30) and
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Salmonella enterica</jats:italic>
                      serovar Choleraesuis (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                      = 20). In addition, high recall (>90%) was observed for other important bacteria in the test set, including
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Escherichia coli</jats:italic>
                      (97%) (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                      = 33),
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Streptococcus suis</jats:italic>
                      (94%) (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                      = 35), and
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Glaesserella parasuis</jats:italic>
                      (93%) (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                      = 30). This study reports that the AIRMAB system provides rapid, accurate, and label-free identification of swine bacterial pathogens, delivering results within 2 min per isolate, and demonstrating practical value for timely decision-making in routine veterinary diagnostics, especially for common, and clinically important bacterial species.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>IMPORTANCE</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Bacterial infections pose a major challenge to global swine production, leading to growth retardation, elevated mortality, and substantial production losses. As several swine pathogens are zoonotic, they also pose direct and indirect risks to human health. Traditional diagnostic methods such as polymerase chain reaction are reliable but time-consuming and require well-equipped laboratories. This study introduces the Artificial Intelligent Raman Microbial Analyzer for Biology system, which utilizes Raman spectroscopy and deep learning to identify 14 major swine pathogens in approximately 2 min. This technology offers a highly automated, cost-effective alternative to traditional methods and matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry, facilitating rapid clinical intervention and large-scale screening to safeguard both animal and public health.</jats:p>

title: Multi-institutional Patient-Level Comparison of Decipher Genomic Classifier and Artera Multimodal Artificial Intelligence in Prostate Cancer
container-title: Clinical Cancer Research
d1076de8b8fd22d9d5f26b811c8b60d002ae17f0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The Decipher Prostate Genomic Classifier (GC) and ArteraAI Multimodal Artificial Intelligence (MMAI) platform are widely used prognostic tools for localized prostate cancer, yet no direct comparison has been performed within the same patient cohort.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Experimental Design:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We sought to evaluate the concordance and prognostic value of GC and MMAI across multi-institutional cohorts totaling 688 patients with localized and oligometastatic prostate cancer. These included populations enriched for African American and East Asian patients. GC and MMAI scores were stratified into risk groups based on specimen type [biopsy or radical prostatectomy (RP)]. The primary endpoint was distant metastasis–free survival, measured from diagnosis to last follow-up or event.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GC and MMAI scores were significantly correlated across multiple cohorts. In Moffitt RP, biopsy, and National Cancer Centre Singapore cohorts, both MMAI and GC were prognostic alone and after adjusting for clinical variables. Multivariable analysis, including both biomarkers and clinical variables, showed that MMAI was significant even when accounting for GC in Moffitt RP and borderline in Moffitt biopsy. Analysis of concordant/discordant cases showed that patients who were high risk for both GC and MMAI did qualitatively worse. In pathway analysis, concordance with GC and MMAI was high for Moffitt RP and oligometastatic patients. Across both biopsy cohorts, although most biological pathways were concordant, there were consistent discordant signaling, metabolic, and DNA repair pathways.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In the first direct patient-level comparison of GC and MMAI in prostate cancer, these biomarkers were found to demonstrate moderate correlation, and both biomarkers demonstrated prognostic value across diverse populations and disease states.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Defining Prompt Literacy in Higher Education and Faculty Development for Prompt Literacy
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
02732e64d99fbff87251316f3d9cd6bc3ce2f987.abstract: <jats:p>The current high rate of adoption of generative artificial intelligence in higher education has led to a sense of urgency in the need to come up with immediate faculty-level literacy development. The idea of prompt literacy described in this chapter is a conceptual extension of AI literacy, focusing on the skill of developing effective prompts to achieve meaningful results in teaching, learning and assessment. It explores the current gaps in faculty preparedness and points to the absence of systematic institutional strategies to promote this new competency. The chapter also suggests faculty developmental strategies that are based on experiential learning, ethical awareness and continuous skill improvement. It also gives a detailed institutional framework to inform the systematic incorporation of prompt literacy into the faculty development programs. The chapter, with its focus on pedagogical and organizational aspects, will also help create a sustainable, responsible and context-sensitive implementation of AI in higher education.</jats:p>

title: Typologies and Competencies of Prompt Literacy in Generative Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
013ea58d255cd2cb20230cf35206aa2e5da0de6b.abstract: <jats:p>This scoping review summarizes findings on an emergent area, “prompt literacy,” in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). It specifically maps key types identified in prompt literacy, including the competencies associated with each. Using a systematic approach to analyze recent literature on the types of prompts (e.g., instruction, exploration, iteration, and evaluation) used throughout GenAI's development provides insight into how they have shaped users' experiences and interactions with new AI-based systems. Additionally, this report provides a list of basic competencies to support effective development of prompt literacy skills, including linguistic accuracy/precision, context awareness, ethical reasoning, and iterative problem-solving—all of which help individuals become successful with their digital and information literacy skills but offer new challenges when people work with AI systems. In conclusion, this review revealed that prompt literacy is a technical/cognitive skill set that encompasses (but isn't limited to) flexibility and critical thinking at all levels.</jats:p>

title: Prompt-Based Cognitive Scaffolding
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
bf7bc1447e7ed3caf087f04fb77606d4e98c71c2.abstract: <jats:p>While research on AI literacy, prompt engineering, and prompt literacy has expanded rapidly, an integrated framework explaining prompt-mediated learning remains underdeveloped. We introduce the Prompt-Based Cognitive Scaffolding (PBCS) model, which conceptualizes prompts as regulatory mechanisms that coordinate cognitive, epistemic, and metacognitive processes during human–AI interaction. Building on cognitive scaffolding, distributed cognition, epistemic cognition, and prompt literacy, PBCS explains learning as a recursive coordination process in which human reasoning and AI-generated outputs are continuously refined. The model is operationalized through three interacting scaffolding dimensions and a functional prompt typology. Its explanatory scope is demonstrated across seminar-based learning, academic writing, collaborative learning, and research-oriented inquiry. We provide a theoretical foundation for understanding recursive human–AI knowledge construction.</jats:p>

title: Prompt Engineering as Distributed Cognition and Epistemic Infrastructure in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
d3ce7c75e5f8d37877d734c90b6dc48c96bd1c5b.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter theorizes prompt literacy as epistemic infrastructure in higher education, conceptualizing prompting as distributed cognition across learners, generative systems, artifacts, and disciplinary genres. It models prompting as a regulated workflow of specification, constraint-synthesis, iterative diagnosis, triangulated verification, uncertainty labelling, and accountable disclosure, reframing authorship as auditable process rather than polished output. Integrating mediated action, activity-system contradictions, pragmatics, genre theory, and epistemic cognition, the chapter translates construct logic into scalable pedagogies, evidence-centred assessment architectures, and integrity-by-design governance. It foregrounds equity as a capability condition, embedding culturally responsive prompting, multilingual burden reduction, accessibility-by-design, and privacy-security postures within institutional quality assurance. The result is a tool-agnostic blueprint for future-ready universities that stabilizes validity, trust, and learning under platform volatility.</jats:p>

title: Prompt Competence in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
d32288e5236e0a2532c8a3039cde17ecc97a0f14.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of artificial intelligence in higher education has changed how knowledge is accessed, created, and assessed. A key idea in this shift is prompt competence. It refers to the ability to design, refine, and interpret inputs for AI systems. This chapter explains the basic ideas behind prompt competence. It links the concept with digital literacy and critical thinking. It also discusses simple ways to include prompt-based learning in different courses. Teaching methods, assessment approaches, and real-life uses are explained. The chapter also looks at policy issues such as ethical use, academic honesty, data privacy, and institutional rules. It connects theory with practice and policy. It offers clear guidance for educators and institutions to use AI in a responsible way and support future-ready learners.</jats:p>

title: Prompt Literacy as a Pedagogical Resource
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
feb94f033fe2b7abcd2d34ab83cd576746ea93a7.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education is reshaping teaching, learning, and assessment practices. Within this evolving landscape, prompt literacy, the ability to design, refine, and critically evaluate prompts for AI systems, has emerged as a crucial yet underexplored competency. This chapter conceptualizes prompt literacy as a pedagogical resource within the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) framework. It argues that while AI introduces new cognitive, pedagogical, and ethical demands, prompt literacy functions as a key resource that helps mitigate these challenges and enhances engagement, teaching effectiveness, and learning outcomes. Drawing on insights from digital literacy, AI literacy, and educational theory, the chapter develops a multidimensional understanding of prompt literacy. It also highlights implications for curriculum design, faculty development, and institutional policy, positioning prompt literacy as a strategic capability for fostering responsible and sustainable AI-enabled education.</jats:p>

title: Designing Prompt Literacy
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
90eec376cccee410354ee6fd243510dd98fd84c6.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores prompt literacy in three interrelated aspects: theoretical, pedagogical, and institutional policy frameworks. Through a qualitative research design based on thematic analysis and systematic literature review, the study gathers the scholarly contributions from 2020 to 2026. The results show that prompt literacy improves critical thinking, learner agency, and academic achievement, while raising concerns about academic integrity, epistemic trust, and ethical use of AI. The chapter suggests an innovative interactive framework for incorporating prompt literacy in higher education curricula and emphasizes that it is time to be courageous in policy formation. It concludes by outlining future research directions and institutional strategies to ensure equitable and responsible integration of AI technologies in education.</jats:p>

title: Pedagogies of Prompting
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
8f0e6973756f9577bd3eeb5de26592a0529bcd79.abstract: <jats:p>The growing integration of generative AI in higher education has positioned prompt literacy as an essential pedagogical competency across disciplines. No longer confined to technical domains, prompting now shapes inquiry, learning, assessment, and knowledge production. This chapter argues for a shift from informal AI use to structured teaching grounded in constructivist, cognitive, and digital literacy frameworks. It explores how prompt literacy can be effectively taught across humanities, social sciences, sciences, and professional fields, emphasizing its role in problem framing, critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and reflective practice. A cross-disciplinary framework is proposed, integrating scaffolding, disciplinary alignment, and ethical engagement. Viewing prompting as dialogic interaction, the chapter highlights its potential to enhance creativity, inquiry, and responsible AI use while addressing risks of superficial learning and inequity.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI in Fashion Design Education

63247d82c461a4523c3e4a79b2e2ae1f0fd715d7.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter covers the transformative role of artificial intelligence in fashion design education, with particular attention to the creation of a framework for prompt literacy utilizing generative AI technologies, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Midjourney, and Newarc AI. This chapter also examines how second-year students in Amity University Kolkata's fashion design and fashion communication department generate virtual rapid clothing prototypes of their designs and develop print motifs using AI-powered tools, especially generative AI, which ultimately enhances the significance of these tools for the changing fashion landscape. Participants have created artwork in a variety of mediums, including Mahbubani art, terracotta, ceramics, and print motifs inspired by seashells, insect using mandalas art, Persian carpets, and other subjects like “Joy in Simplicity” and “The Harmony of Nature and Feminine Grace”. The AI-Augmented Fashion Design Education Framework (AI-AFDEF) was emphasized in this book chapter's discussion of traditional versus tech-driven approaches.</jats:p>

title: Prompt Literacy in Flipped Pedagogy

Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
b2f959206d0e0830e780ed1979a8107c445901f6.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter critically examines scholarly literature on prompt literacy and its relationship with flipped pedagogy in Economics education. It aims to establish conceptual clarity, identify dominant research trends, and highlight gaps in the emerging scholarship. A PRISMA-informed scoping review methodology was adopted to map the evidence, clarify key concepts, and identify research gaps. The findings conceptualize prompt literacy as a multidimensional competence encompassing pedagogical, cognitive, ethical, and disciplinary dimensions. In response, the chapter proposes a Flipped Pedagogical–AI-Mediated Learning Framework that positions prompt literacy as a mediating competence connecting AI-supported flipped pedagogy with students' cognitive, behavioural, ethical, and disciplinary learning outcomes. The framework provides a conceptual foundation for responsible and pedagogically purposeful AI integration in flipped Economics education.</jats:p>

title: Prompting for Academic Writing and Research
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
381b8ae3adf774d45c5ddbe6dc73d8a600b6339a.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming academic writing and research, creating an urgent need for prompt literacy as a core competency in higher education. This chapter develops an integrated framework that positions prompt literacy as a cognitive, pedagogical, and ethical capability supporting responsible human–AI collaboration. Drawing on contemporary scholarship, this chapter synthesises existing literature to examine prompt design, evaluation, research applications, instructional strategies, and ethical governance. It further proposes a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) verification framework to strengthen transparency, academic integrity, and the reliability of AI-assisted scholarship. This chapter contributes a structured conceptual model that informs curriculum design, research training, assessment practices, and institutional policy, enabling higher education institutions to foster responsible, critical, and future-ready AI-enabled scholarship.</jats:p>

title: Prompting for Academic Writing and Research
