title: Ambivalent close ties and cognitive functioning: Does coping play a role?
container-title: Innovation in Aging
3738dbe063f098bd707e9287333cbc2881dbfe03.abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Close relationships that are characterized by both positive and negative qualities (i.e., ambivalent ties) are common in later life and often give rise to interpersonal tensions with deleterious consequences for well-being. However, little is known about their effect on cognitive health. These effects may depend on seldom-studied interpersonal coping strategies that may either stimulate or deplete cognitive resources. This study tested whether ambivalent ties relate to lower cognitive functioning among older adults, and whether interpersonal coping strategies moderate these associations. Research Design and Methods As part of the Daily Experiences and Well-being Study (DEWS), participants (N = 271, ages 65-89) completed an in-person baseline interview assessing positive and negative qualities of their close social relationships and overall cognitive functioning (composite of four tests), followed by a self-administered questionnaire assessing three interpersonal coping strategies (engaged, avoidant, destructive). Results Linear regression models revealed that a greater proportion of ambivalent ties was associated with worse overall cognitive functioning, but this association was not moderated by any interpersonal coping strategy. Sensitivity analyses of the separate cognitive tests revealed, unexpectedly, that greater use of engaged coping strengthened the association between ambivalent ties and worse executive functioning performance. Discussion and Implications A greater proportion of ambivalent ties in one’s social network is associated with lower cognitive functioning among older adults, a link that may not easily be buffered through coping. Results suggest that ambivalent ties are an understudied important potential risk factor for adverse cognitive outcomes in later life.

title: Elite basketball athletes at rest: enhanced sensorimotor activity and reduced cognitive load
container-title: Brain Communications
a60db5de1caa2c93715e57f65cfc2f1acafe497c.abstract: Long-term sports training is associated with experience-dependent brain plasticity, but the core functional architecture of open-skill athletes remains unclear. As a representative open-skill sport, basketball requires rapid sensorimotor integration in dynamic settings. This study examined resting-state functional characteristics in elite basketball athletes, focusing on interactions between sensorimotor and advanced cognitive systems. Fifty-seven national first-class basketball athletes (mean age 20.17 ± 1.87 years, twenty-three males) and sixty-one healthy controls (mean age 20.33 ± 1.89 years, twenty-five males) underwent resting-state functional MRI. Fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF) and degree centrality (DC) were used to evaluate regional spontaneous activity and overall brain network integration, respectively. Group comparisons controlled for age, sex and head motion. Athletes showed a dual pattern of functional differences. First, athletes showed changed sensorimotor processing: significantly higher fALFF and DC in the superior temporal gyrus, cerebellum (anterior and posterior), parahippocampal gyrus, cuneus, and lingual gyrus, indicating stronger neural substrates for visuospatial integration and motor coordination. Second, athletes showed greater neural efficiency: lower fALFF and DC in the middle frontal gyrus, cingulate cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, and precuneus (parts of the default mode network), which may reflect enhanced cognitive control and reduced cognitive load. Notably, the insula and midbrain showed a distinct pattern (increased fALFF but decreased DC), indicating a specialized "high-readiness and low-redundancy" state for salience monitoring. Long-term basketball training is associated with distinct patterns of functional brain characteristics, marked by improved sensorimotor processing and greater neural efficiency within cognitive control networks. These training-related neural patterns may serve as biomarkers for athlete evaluation and selection. Abbreviated summary Wang et al. report that elite basketball athletes exhibit distinct resting-state functional brain characteristics, including enhanced sensorimotor-related activity and altered cognitive control network organization. These findings suggest that basketball expertise is associated with specialized neural organization supporting the demands of open-skill sports.

title: Joint associations of handgrip strength and chair-stand performance with motoric cognitive risk syndrome in older adults
container-title: The Journals of Gerontology, Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences
60e7025356494efec4a59e9b22df7d869545d7f5.abstract: Abstract Background Motor dysfunction is associated with cognitive vulnerability, but whether impairments across body regions jointly contribute to motoric cognitive risk syndrome (MCR) remains unclear. We examined the independent and joint associations of handgrip strength and chair-stand test (CST) with MCR. Methods This cross-sectional study included 6258 dementia-free older adults (mean age 71.5 ± 6.6 years; 63.1% women) from a community-based cohort. Handgrip strength and CST performance were used to define upper- and lower-extremity motor impairment. Participants were classified as normal, handgrip weakness only, CST impairment only, or combined motor impairment. Multivariable logistic regression was performed with adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Additive and multiplicative interactions were assessed. Results MCR was present in 10.4% of participants. Using the A/B CST cutoff as the primary definition, adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) for MCR, compared with normal function, were 1.84 (1.14–2.97) for handgrip weakness only, 4.17 (2.97–5.85) for CST impairment only, and 9.17 (6.56–12.81) for combined motor impairment. Associations were directionally consistent across alternative CST cutoffs. A positive additive interaction was observed at the A/B CST cutoff (relative excess risk due to interaction = 3.48; attributable proportion = 0.40; and synergy index = 1.83), whereas multiplicative interaction was not positive. Conclusions Combined handgrip weakness and poorer CST performance were strongly associated with prevalent MCR. A positive additive interaction at the primary CST cutoff suggests that joint motor impairment may help characterize MCR-related vulnerability in older adults.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Endocrinology: A Narrative Review from the Perspective of Early-career Clinicians and Researchers
container-title: Hormone Research in Paediatrics
b0cef863c0b132e90874cce2cb06d1dab86866f1.abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) use by early-career paediatric endocrinologists has started without waiting for the training and governance structures to develop. Since early-career physicians and researchers of today hold no pre-AI performance baseline against which to appraise the AI outputs, career stage-specific concerns regarding rapid adoption of AI use in the field have emerged. The goal of this review was to examine AI use in paediatric endocrinology from the early-career perspective. Summary: A narrative, non-systematic literature review regarding the AI use in paediatric endocrinology across the four professional domains (curricular coverage, clinical practice, teaching, and research) was conducted in January 2026 and updated through July 2026. 57 relevant publications were identified, with level of evidence differing significantly between domains, and inversely with how freely the AI tools are used: from randomised-trials data regarding specific clinical applications like closed-loop insulin delivery and automated bone age assessment, to no published data regarding use of large language models in the research domain. Greatest benefit of automated bone age assessment in the early career stage was reported, while no published studies examining AI use by early-career paediatric endocrinologists were found. Key Messages: While being most exposed to unsupervised AI use, early-career physicians are also the least studied group. Having in mind the lack of pre-AI baseline in this population, findings of this review emphasize the potential career stage-dependent risks regarding the AI use, and the need for subspecialty-specific AI competency frameworks.

title: Business Ukrainian in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Transformation of Language Norms, Professional Etiquette, and Communicative Culture
container-title: Revista Cultura Científica
fdb422e8c7735c4796f1afac776d44e6fd0922cf.abstract: The article develops a psycholinguistic account of how generative artificial intelligence changes professional Ukrainian-language writing, with particular attention to language norms, professional speech etiquette, communicative culture, and the educational workplace. A structured theoretical synthesis was conducted on a corpus of 29 peer-reviewed journal articles from 2022–2026. The corpus was organised into four evidence blocks: artificial intelligence in business and workplace communication; pragmatic behaviour of large language models; politeness and email communication in academic and workplace settings; and Ukrainian psycholinguistic and speech-etiquette contexts. Studies were coded for communication domain, speech act or genre, role of artificial intelligence, normative and pragmatic outcomes, relational perceptions, and contextual limitations. Because research designs and outcome measures were heterogeneous, the analysis used qualitative comparative synthesis rather than meta-analysis. The synthesis reveals three recurrent transformations. First, generative systems often strengthen formal correctness, structural coherence, and explicit politeness. Second, these gains can be accompanied by communicative conventionalisation: increased formality, formulaic organisation, reduced lexical or strategic variability, and weaker adjustment to the local interpersonal context. Third, artificial-intelligence mediation changes attributional and relational judgements: perceived authorship, authenticity, sincerity, trust, and willingness to maintain interaction may diverge from ratings of professionalism or clarity. These transformations are not uniform; their magnitude depends on communicative risk, status relations, degree of imposition, genre conventionality, source disclosure, and the extent of human revision. On this basis, a three-component model of normative optimisation, communicative conventionalisation, and attributional-relational shift is proposed. For Ukrainian professional communication, especially in higher education, generative artificial intelligence should be treated as a mediator of linguistic choice rather than a neutral editing device. The key research gap is the lack of direct empirical evidence on Ukrainian-language AI-mediated professional writing, which limits straightforward transfer of findings from English-dominant studies.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Religious Policy: Ethical Governance  in the Digital Public Sphere
container-title: AMUYA: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT REVIEWS
3e92be76556d313607d793a0624ba717c1fa41bd.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates religious communication, knowledge, and participation in the digital public sphere, yet research remains fragmented across digital religion, human rights, and AI governance. This study examines how AI-mediated religious communication shapes authority, visibility, and participation; identifies associated ethical and rights-based concerns; and analyzes the institutional conditions relevant to its governance. Using a qualitative, non-experimental, exploratory-analytical design, the study draws on academic publications, policy documents, regulatory instruments, institutional guidelines, human-rights reports, and documented analyses of digital religious practices. Materials were purposively selected for substantive relevance and examined through structured reading and extraction, open and focused coding, thematic synthesis, source triangulation, and iterative cross-source comparison. The analysis identified three interconnected domains: access, visibility, and religious authority; religious freedom, inclusion, and algorithmic risks; and accountability, contestability, and institutional responsibility. AI-mediated technologies can broaden access to religious resources while simultaneously shaping the visibility and perceived authority of religious actors and interpretations. Expanded access can coexist with unequal representation, privacy risks, profiling, and constraints on meaningful participation, while distributed responsibility can create accountability gaps when consequential outcomes are difficult to explain or challenge. These relationships are context-dependent rather than predetermined effects of AI. By integrating sociotechnical and algorithmic-governance perspectives, the study provides an analytical framework for understanding ethical governance as the intersection of technological mediation, religious pluralism, fundamental rights, participation, and identifiable institutional responsibility.

title: From Routine Fixed Schedules to Signals: A Condition-Responsive, AI-Augmented Pigging Intelligence Framework for Localised Internal Corrosion Control in Crude Oil and Water Injection Pipelines
container-title: ADIPEC
bb102d5cbb0ad65fc316c638ad53cb6149af8dab.abstract: Abstract Pigging plans in most operating companies globally are scheduled by calendar days. Pipeline segments are pigged every 30, 60 or 90 days based on the historical fixed maintenance schedules set during commissioning, regardless of the real time corrosion dynamics of the pipeline when in service. However, in most crude oil and water injection lines where the corrosion environment shifts with well stream composition, throughput and bacteria activity, the fixed schedule methodology of pigging does not prevent escalation of corrosion events. A five-year trending of several pipeline ILI data shows why 63% of anomalies deeper than 18% wall thickness were found in segments fully compliant with their pigging schedule. A 24-month study across 312 km length of pipelines compared condition-responsive segments against fixed 30-day controls showed that the mean maximum pit depth growth fell by 54.5% with over 80% drop in reactive integrity actions. Furthermore, the chemical inhibitor wetting efficiency increased by 18 points with 22.5% reduction in pigging runs. More so, 78% of the anomaly's clusters were located at the 5 to 7 o'clock orientation and concentrated in pipelines where inhibitor wetting had dropped below 69%. Sulphate Reducing Bacteria (SRB) and Iron Oxidizing Bacteria (IOB) counts proved the strongest leading indicators in the corrosion index, which is what should be expected in MIC-susceptible water injection systems. This paper proposes and validates the Pigging Intelligence Framework (PIF), in which pig runs are triggered by corrosion signals rather than fixed maintenance schedules. The PIF has three layers namely: the Corrosion Signal Index (CSI), supervised machine learning model and a root cause framework. The CSI combines flow velocity, BS&W content, microbiological activity, inhibitor residuals and ILI pit depth progression into a continuously updated risk score for each segment. Furthermore, the supervised machine learning model, trained on five years of pigging records and post-pig debris analytics from the pipelines, identifies the leading indicators of accelerated pitting. A root cause investigation tool anchored in NACE SP0106 ensures every unacceptable corrosion event produces a traceable corrective action, with outputs mapped to SAP PM and the integrity database. The study posits that pigging should be timed, based on the state of the pipeline and integrity condition of the medium rather than pigging as a historical norm. Therefore, it put forwards an A.I augmented framework in which pigging frequency, chemical dosing and inspection strategy recalibrate continuously from model output, closing the loop between detection, diagnosis and action.

title: The Skills Intelligence Engine for an AI-Ready Energy Workforce
container-title: ADIPEC
8f4721afded7a4529d81dc5465a5e908e8a7d7fd.abstract: Abstract As digitalization and AI reshape the energy industry, operators must transform large technical workforces without eroding core domain expertise. The challenge goes beyond training digital specialists; it requires evolving domain professionals into domain-plus-AI, domain-plus-digital, and domain-plus-business practitioners. This paper presents a framework of energy organization's Skills Intelligence Infrastructure, a single engine linking learning activity, curated curricula, skills maps, HR data, and a conversational AI agent (beta) that bridges HR and business to support upskilling, mobility, promotion readiness, and strategic workforce planning. The infrastructure was developed through a four-layer architecture. First, a unified data foundation integrates employee learning activity with HR data, enabling segmentation by role, organization, geography, seniority, and business area. Second, curated curricula and skills maps are designed with business owners to align with enterprise priorities across AI, machine learning, data, operations, sustainability, project management, safety-critical training, sales, and domain competence. These resources support aspirational and promotion-linked roles while clarifying expectations, gaps, and priorities. Third, persona-driven experiences serve employees and managers: employees pursue pathways, identify gaps and future requirements, and build T-shaped capability—deep domain expertise broadened by AI, digital, project, and business skills—while managers monitor development, assess the regional distribution of skills, and identify talent opportunities for mobility, promotion, and hiring. Fourth, a conversational AI agent lets employees ask which skills target roles require and which pathways to prioritize, while managers evaluate talent against skills, learning records, pathway completion, and readiness indicators. Deployed across approximately 8,000 professionals, the platform delivers curated curricula for more than 60 aspirational roles, including 12 promotion-linked roles, and hundreds of pathways across digital, AI, data, project management, safety, sales, and domain expertise. As the enterprise system of record for capability, it provides end-to-end visibility into the AI upskilling funnel: more than 3,000 employees advancing their skills, more than 1,500 certified data science practitioners, and early identification of domain data scientist candidates. It surfaces more than 150 AI-powered innovation projects across the E&P lifecycle and tracks participation in an enterprise's strategic development program. For managers, it reveals skills trends across regions, business lines, and disciplines, exposing hidden capability gaps and talent opportunities. By favoring internal development over hiring, it has reduced recruitment costs for scarce digital talent and improved satisfaction with learning and career development. Unlike commercial talent-marketplace platforms, this skills-based workforce intelligence solution is purpose-built for a large technical energy workforce. It links HR and business through manager-owned skills maps, integrates siloed domain certifications and critical pathways, and operationalizes the domain-to-domain-plus-AI transformation at scale. It supports upskilling, talent conversion, mobility, promotion readiness, compliance tracking, and build-versus-hire decisions. Future enhancements will infer skills from roles, projects, and experience and extend the AI agent into talent management. This provides a foundation on which the energy workforce can build as AI reshapes the industry.

title: Regulatory risk perception and corporate financialization: evidence from China
container-title: Digital Economy and Sustainable Development
37210d95e7db175200a50c91a1059d3435986b9b.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the effect of regulatory risk perception on corporate financialization in China. Using the method of keyword search, we quantify regulatory risk perception in China based on the text data of listed companies’ annual reports. With the sample of Chinese A-share companies from 2011 to 2024, we find robust evidence that regulatory risk perception significantly curbs corporate financialization. Meanwhile, our results also indicate that this effect is stronger in non-SOEs (non-state-owned enterprises), firms at the maturity and decline stages, and firms with lower risk preference and lower market position. Finally, we propose that easing financing constraints, reducing corporate tax avoidance and alleviating corporate credit mismatches are plausible channels through which regulatory risk perception decreases corporate financialization. Overall, we shed light on the real effects of regulatory risk perception and the determinants of corporate financialization.

title: Exceptionalising China knowledge: academic exchange, decisionism, and the securitisation of knowledge exchange with China in Australia
container-title: Asian Review of Political Economy
f06c9d6c1dd7f885fe388d5c6bc99a87dba7e01b.abstract: Abstract How does the securitisation of knowledge exchange cross the threshold from discursive reframing into the suspension of routine governance rules? This article examines the securitisation of Australia–China academic exchange between 2017 and 2025 and develops a three-layered analytical framework to answer this question. The first layer, discursive securitisation, captures the reframing of China knowledge as suspect knowledge through a securitising coalition of intelligence agencies, politicians, and media actors. The second, administrative securitisation, traces how this discourse was translated into institutional filtering through visa scrutiny, grant vetting, and compliance mechanisms, gatekeeping the evolution of China knowledge in Australian society and politics. The third layer identifies a qualitatively distinct step in increasingly intensified knowledge (re)production fields, where ordinary academic norms were displaced by anticipatory, category-based exclusion, while distributed decisionism disperses accountability and insulates exclusionary decisions from meaningful public deliberation. The article argues that the Copenhagen School accounts for the first two layers but cannot explain the decisive institutional acts that characterise the third. Drawing on Carl Schmitt’s logic of decisionism, it advances discussion around securitisation with a concept of “exceptionalisation” as a bridging concept that names the threshold at which securitised issues are removed from normal, routine and procedural governance. The Australian case reveals a paradox: exceptionalising China knowledge erodes the very expertise on which informed security policy depends. The article contributes to securitisation theory by specifying how and when securitisation becomes something else.

title: Edge AI Vision Camera Intelligence and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) for Real-Time Industrial Safety Monitoring in Oil & Gas Facilities
container-title: ADIPEC
630a0ebf0bea077cef165c6fb1574bb2581950d2.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Oil & gas operations require continuous monitoring of safety compliance and high risk anomalies; however, conventional supervision and manual CCTV monitoring are constrained by limited coverage, delayed detection, and inconsistent enforcement. This paper presents an AI-based industrial safety monitoring framework for edge computer vision analytics and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to enable real-time detection of safety violations and hazardous conditions. Methods, Procedures, Process The proposed solution integrates deep learning-based video analytics with existing CCTV infrastructure and AMR-mounted cameras to extend monitoring into blind spots and dynamic work zones. AI inference is performed on edge GPU servers to ensure low latency, reduce cloud dependency, and support uninterrupted site operations. The platform detects over 100 industrial safety anomaly types, including PPE non-compliance, restricted zone intrusion, work-at-height violations, fire/smoke indicators, spill/leak anomalies, housekeeping deviations. Temporal tracking and Multi-frame validation is applied to improve event confidence and reduce transient false triggers. Rule-based escalation workflows generate real-time alerts with timestamped evidence frames, which are stored in an auditable event database for compliance reporting, trend analytics, and continuous improvement. Results, Observations, Conclusions Performance evaluation across operational deployments indicates a detection accuracy of 90-95% depending on use case complexity and environmental conditions. End-to-end alert latency from detection to notification was measured at approximately 3 seconds, enabling near real-time intervention by EHS teams. The combined CCTV + AMR monitoring approach improved coverage in areas where fixed cameras had occlusion limitations, particularly in large fabrication yards, laydown zones, and high-traffic operational corridors. Observed deployment constraints included low-light sensitivity, PPE partial visibility and false triggers caused by reflections and steam. These were mitigated through site-specific confidence threshold tuning, improved zoning logic, and periodic model refinement using operational datasets. The system also enabled automated reporting outputs such as violation heatmaps, repeat violation identification, shift-wise compliance scoring, and incident categorization. The paper concludes that integrating edge AI vision with existing CCTV infrastructure and AMR-based mobile sensing provides a scalable and measurable approach to proactive industrial safety monitoring, improving response time, compliance governance, and data-driven EHS decision-making. Novel/Additive Information This paper presents additive field evidence on deploying a low-latency (~3 seconds) edge AI vision system integrated with existing CCTV networks and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to monitor 100+ industrial safety anomalies. It contributes practical deployment methodology, performance benchmarking (90-95% accuracy), and mitigation strategies for real operating constraints such as occlusion, low-light, reflections, and steam. The work advances scalable, audit-ready AI safety intelligence for petroleum operations.

title: Transforming the Future of Intermittent Wells: Predictive Computational Application for Dynamic Simulation and Artificial Lift Optimization Using a Surface Automatic Valve
container-title: ADIPEC
a874fa8b0df1be956c74573f05c2217ffed665e4.abstract: Abstract The Surface Automatic Valve (SAV) is a patented mechanism that automatically opens and closes hydrocarbon wells. However, the main challenge is not the valve action itself, but determining the proper timing to maximize hydrocarbon production without manual intervention. This study addresses that gap by moving from empirical methods and field testing to a software platform that simulates the SAV, reservoir, and well as an integrated system, defines optimal opening and closing cycles, and verifies whether formation gas is sufficient to lift the fluid column or whether external assistance is required. A computational platform was developed using an object-oriented architecture. The model iteratively solves time-dependent mass and energy balances to simulate gas-driven liquid lifting from bottomhole to surface. Liquid-column length is estimated using Zimmerman's (1976)1 transient-flow approach, modified for multiphase mixtures. A pressure balance is used to calculate flowing bottomhole pressure, and Vogel's correlation (1969)2 is incorporated to predict column growth based on actual reservoir inflow and reservoir pressure. Static reservoir pressure and production history were included in the simulation. Numerical trial-and-error methods were used to obtain convergence during each intermittent-cycle stage—pressure buildup, gas production, and liquid unloading—to estimate liquid and gas production, optimize the SAV operating range, select choke size, and define unloading time and cycle duration. Compared with manual operation, which depended mainly on operator judgment, the software predicted maximum liquid and gas unloading rates with more than 95% agreement with historical field data. For Well A, production after SAV installation reached 108.0 barrels of net production per day (BNPD), representing a 46% increase over the latest reference production test, with 95.4% agreement between predicted and measured liquid production. For Well B, a shut-in well, the model defined its intermittent-production potential. Using the software-recommended SAV operating range, the well produced 38.0 BNPD and 51.6 MSCFD, with 98.8% agreement for liquid and 98.6% for gas. For Well C, optimized SAV cycles converted an inactive well into a viable production opportunity. After SAV installation, gas production increased by more than 100%, and model agreement reached 97.8%, supporting the reliability of the software and the feasibility of recovering wells previously considered technically depleted. This work continues SPE-214961 and presents the first dynamic modeling development of a Surface Automatic Valve integrated with the well/reservoir system. Its main innovation is a multivariable optimization algorithm that performs sensitivity analyses on opening and closing pressures and choke sizes to characterize transient flow and optimize production. The development also includes a real-time monitoring module for SAV operation, enabling anomaly detection, better operational decisions, and a future basis for automated SAV adjustments.

title: SustainaDrill: Embedding Real-Time Emissions Intelligence into Drilling Operations at Scale
container-title: ADIPEC
103ca93797b7aac3b83d1b4f15c3e023027be30b.abstract: Abstract Drilling and well construction activities contribute an estimated 8–10% of total oil and gas industry emissions, with rig fuel consumption representing a major share. This paper proposes SustainaDrill, a real-time rig emissions monitoring and integration framework that will embed sustainability KPIs into drilling operations. The planned work will evaluate whether onshore drilling operations can reduce emissions, optimize energy use, and enhance operational efficiency while supporting Net Zero objectives. SustainaDrill will integrate automated rig-level emissions monitoring into the existing onshore real-time digital infrastructure. Real-time fuel consumption, power generation, and operational data will be captured, analyzed, and linked directly to drilling activities and non-productive time events. Emission-intensity metrics will be benchmarked against predefined sustainability targets and visualized for rig crews and operations teams. A controlled pilot will be implemented on selected drilling phases and sub-activities. The pilot findings will then inform optimization cycles, SOP development, and any phased scale-up across rigs. The proposed deployment of SustainaDrill is expected to enable systematic identification of fuel-intensive operational behaviours through real-time emissions visibility and integration into real-time operations workflows. By linking rig-level greenhouse gas emissions to operational activities and sub-activities, the framework is intended to convert emissions from a passive reporting metric into an active performance-management tool. The future pilot will determine whether the approach can deliver measurable operational and environmental improvements across drilling campaigns. SustainaDrill is projected to create value through reduced fuel consumption, improved rig power management, and shorter non-productive operating durations. Based on the current analytical model and portfolio assumptions, potential cumulative value creation is estimated at approximately USD 40–90 million per year across the full well portfolio. These figures are pre-pilot projections and will require validation using measured pilot data, documented calculation assumptions, the annual drilling programme, and the scale of operations. In parallel, the analytical model indicates a potential 5–7% reduction in Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions, proportional to the projected fuel-consumption savings. The planned pilot will test whether SustainaDrill can enhance Real Time Operations Center decision-making, embed sustainability into daily drilling operations, and improve environmental performance while creating economic value. The concept is designed to use existing operational infrastructure and is therefore expected to limit the need for major initial changes. SustainaDrill proposes a novel approach for transforming greenhouse gas emissions from a passive reporting metric into an active drilling performance KPI. Unlike conventional post-operation emissions accounting, the framework will be designed to support real-time emissions-driven operational decisions, behavioural change at rig level, and continuous improvement loops. Subject to pilot validation, integrating sustainability metrics into real-time operations workflows could provide an innovative, scalable, and low-cost pathway to decarbonizing well construction operations.

title: Electrifying Artificial Lift in a Remote West African Brownfield: Pilot Design, Power Scenarios, and Quantified Emissions Impact
container-title: ADIPEC
f8a8258359e401f0b417dc0b50f5f6b854051ca1.abstract: Abstract This study reassesses artificial lift strategy for a remote onshore brownfield in West Africa historically dominated by gas lift (GL). The question addressed is whether moving away from GL can materially increase drawdown and oil rate at late life while providing a credible, quantified pathway to lower greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions under diesel and grid power. The evolution of a candidate well is followed from GL, through hydraulic solutions like jet pump (JP) and hydraulic piston pump (HPP), to an electric submersible pump (ESP). Converting from other artificial lift methods to ESPs is common in the industry, but few operators have evaluated the emissions benefits of the same. Inflow and outflow models were calibrated for the candidate well, with sensitivities on reservoir pressure, productivity index (0.7–2.5 stb/d/psi), water cut (60–95%) and free-gas handling, to cover a range of well and reservoir performance scenarios, in the absence of direct measurements of certain key parameters such as reservoir pressure. ESP designs were engineered with gas-handler and separator configurations, motor derating, and a variable speed drive (VSD) strategy suited to high water cut and high gas volume fraction (GVF) conditions. For the baseline GL, JP and HPP cases and the proposed ESP cases, lift energy and Scope 1 emissions were estimated using IPCC Tier 1 stationary combustion methodology, taking the specific fuel consumption of each generating set from its certified fuel-consumption table at the load factor actually carried, with boundaries set by the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard. The International Energy Agency (IEA) emission factors database was used for Scope 2 emissions from imported grid electricity. Modelled diesel-powered ESPs increased oil rate from 91.9 bopd (GL) to 228.0 bopd, an uplift of approximately 150%, sustained at 76% water cut. Lift-related emissions depended strongly on the power source: absolute emissions fell from 696 tCO2e/yr (GL) to 239 tCO2e/yr (ESP–diesel) and 76 tCO2e/yr (ESP–grid), reductions of 66% and 89% respectively. Emissions intensity per 1,000 barrels of oil improved from 20.74 tCO2e (GL) to 2.88 tCO2e (ESP–diesel) and 0.92 tCO2e (ESP–grid) giving improvements of 86% and 96% respectively. These gains reflect both the higher lift capability and production efficiency of the ESP relative to compression-driven GL, and the comparatively low grid emission factor (0.24 kg CO2e/kWh) available in the host country. For remote, gas-constrained brownfields with rising water cut, ESPs can unlock meaningful production uplift alongside large, standards-aligned emissions reductions under both power scenarios. Because the intensity gain is driven by simultaneous rate uplift and lower specific lift energy, the case is compelling even before grid electrification. A staged pilot is outlined with KPIs on production, reliability and run life, interventions and emissions. Deployment-ready ESP engineering for a remote West African onshore field is coupled here with fully quantified emissions accounting across diesel and grid power scenarios, demonstrating that lift-method selection is a high-leverage, near-term decarbonisation lever for late-life brownfields. The wider and novel implication is that re-lifting mature wellstock is itself a low-carbon supply option. The 136 bopd of incremental production obtained here comes from a well that was drilled, completed and tied into existing facilities decades ago, so the barrels carry none of the drilling, construction and infrastructure emissions of an equivalent greenfield development, and are delivered with a fraction of its capital exposure and cycle time. Extending the productive life of old fields is therefore shown to be a route to meeting global demand at lower emissions and lower cost than developing new ones, and the accounting framework set out here allows that case to be demonstrated on a standards-aligned basis rather than asserted.

title: A Three-Tier Restart Framework for Shut-In Reservoirs by Coupling Drive-Mechanism Diagnostics, Artificial-Lift Integrity, and Surface-System Readiness to Quantify Recovery Risk Across Natural-Flow, Waterflood, and Mature Asset Classes Following Extended Curtailment
container-title: ADIPEC
83d2f443a0408eeadc3a36c4b674cdb3b0622423.abstract: Abstract Conventional supply-side disruption modeling treats producing assets as binary on/off systems, yet reservoir engineering fundamentals dictate that restart trajectories diverge sharply by drive mechanism, completion architecture, and life-cycle stage. This paper introduces a three-tier, parameter-driven framework to forecast field-level restart behavior, deliverability ramp profiles, and permanent-capacity-loss probability, calibrated against the 2026 Middle East Gulf supply disruption, in which shut-in crude and condensate volumes peaked near 11.4 MMbbl/d, 46% of the region's pre-conflict output base of ~24.9 MMbbl/d1 generating an estimated cumulative shortfall in the range of 1.4-2.0 billion barrels under extended-curtailment sensitivities. Curtailed production is segmented into three tiers using drive-mechanism and lift-system diagnostics scored across eleven parameters, feeding nodal analysis, material-balance decline curves, and pressure-transient diagnostics under Low/Base/High cases. Under the base case, Tier 1 volumes (natural flow) restore deliverability within one to two weeks; Tier 2 (waterflood/injection-supported) requires three to five weeks of managed restart; Tier 3 (mature, high-water-cut) faces windows of six weeks to six months and carries the highest probability of irrecoverable capacity loss. Aggregated through an S-curve, the tier-weighted profile rebuilds Gulf output from a trough near 12-14 MMbbl/d toward its pre-conflict plateau over roughly five to six months, with structural capacity loss of 0.4-1.1 MMbbl/d if curtailment extends past six months, widening to 0.6-2.5 MMbbl/d at twelve months. The framework offers a transferable, reservoir-engineering-grounded screening tool that operators and supply-side analysts can apply prospectively to future disruption scenarios -- hurricane outages, planned mega-shutdowns, sanctions-driven curtailments, or geopolitical events to pre-position workover rigs, ESP inventory, chemical packages, and intervention capital ahead of the event rather than reactively. Beyond the Gulf calibration, the framework is generalized for direct practitioner use: the scoring mechanics are laid out in full (parameter weights, thresholds, override rules, and tier cutoffs), and a decision-tree workflow and structured screening questionnaire allow the method to be applied to any operator or IOC portfolio as a field-development and restart-planning screening tool. The tier logic is additionally validated against a typical operational curtailment entirely outside the conflict setting: the 2014–2020 Partitioned Neutral Zone shutdown, in which the offshore Khafji and mature onshore Wafra fields followed exactly the divergent restart paths the framework predicts, and the 2020 Libyan blockade, which quantifies how infrastructure and logistics readiness dominate restart cost.

title: Autonomous Refinery Intelligence Architecture
container-title: ADIPEC
468ef9599b5e8cca4df21c522a21aaf982fc612c.abstract: Abstract Refinery decisions often require evidence that is distributed across plant historians, maintenance systems, work permits, incident records, management-of-change registers, audit actions, shift logs, engineering documents, and workforce-compliance records. Conventional search or dashboard solutions generally address one source type at a time and leave engineers to assemble the complete operational story manually. This paper presents the Autonomous Refinery Intelligence Architecture (ARIA), an on-premise, evidence-grounded architecture developed in-house at a public-sector refinery to unify structured plant records and unstructured operational knowledge while maintaining data sovereignty. The architecture is designed to connect 15 enterprise systems through governed tools and a Model Context Protocol integration layer. A refinery-wide source inventory contained 423,614 structured records and 6,898 shift-log records across 12 operational domains. The detailed case study evaluates eight operational source classes using controlled subsets from crude and vacuum distillation and hydroprocessing units. The method combines canonical equipment identity, deterministic source-quality checks, structured and chronological candidate generation, retrieval-augmented language-model synthesis, a refinery-specific qualification gate, and human review. Three domain patterns are supported: safety investigation, reliability investigation, and contractor-workforce compliance. The language model acts as a controlled reasoning and summarization layer; it is not permitted to authorize plant or workforce decisions. The evaluated crude-distillation pipeline assembled 52,664 evidence rows and reduced 124 candidate packs to 15 final cards, of which only three met the strongest machine qualification. The hydroprocessing pipeline assembled 81,313 rows and reduced 132 candidate packs to 15 cards, again with three receiving the strongest qualification. The deliberate rejection and review rates show that conservative evidence gating is more important than maximizing the number of generated insights. The evaluation also exposed material source-data limitations, including missing work-permit tags, invalid notification dates, and incomplete closure fields. These limitations were carried forward as confidence constraints rather than silently repaired by the model. An initial internal workflow benchmark for a representative incident investigation indicated approximately 80% less evidence-assembly time than the prior manual approach. This is a preliminary operational benchmark, not a controlled statistical trial. A 15-20% reduction in unplanned downtime remains a projected benefit to be tested through longer-term asset performance monitoring. The principal conclusion is that agentic artificial intelligence can support refinery operations only when identity, provenance, qualification rules, human accountability, and on-premise governance are designed as first-class system components.

title: From Data to Decision: A Field-Validated AI-Assisted Production Intelligence Framework for Opportunity Identification, Artificial Lift Optimization, and Surveillance in the Indus Basin
container-title: ADIPEC
682401dea7bf98f4681e69f40979ea43326f1efc.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope The increasing complexity of mature oil, gas, and condensate assets has expanded surveillance data volumes while making rapid identification of high-value production opportunities increasingly difficult. Conventional workflows rely on fragmented datasets, manual interpretation, and reactive assessments resulting in delayed intervention planning, suboptimal artificial lift performance, and inconsistent prioritization across large portfolios. This study presents a field-validated AI-assisted production intelligence framework to enhance opportunity identification, artificial lift optimization, and surveillance efficiency across a multi-well oil, gas, and condensate portfolio in the Indus Basin, Pakistan. Methods, Procedures, Process The framework integrates production, pressure, temperature, choke, gas lift injection, well testing, downtime, and intervention datasets from production databases into a centralized Python-based environment connected to business intelligence dashboards. Isolation Forest and gradient boosting-based anomaly detection algorithms were combined with petroleum engineering workflows including nodal analysis, liquid loading diagnostics using Turner and Coleman critical velocity models, gas lift performance diagnostics, and operating envelope validation to establish a physics-guided decision intelligence system. The framework screens wells across natural flow and artificial lift modes, diagnosing liquid loading, gas lift inefficiency, skin buildup, and choke instability, ranking opportunities by uplift potential and operational feasibility. Results, Observations, Conclusions Field deployment across 41 active wells including 4 gas lift producers reduced manual well review cycles from bi-weekly to daily automated anomaly alerts. Within 6 months, 29 anomaly flags were reduced to 16 physics-validated opportunities across four categories: 5 liquid loading remediation candidates drawn from 8 wells confirmed below Turner critical rate with deficits ranging from 12% to 78%, 2 gas lift optimization candidates, 4 choke and operating envelope deviations, and 5 rigless intervention candidates. Gas lift optimization contributed an incremental ~80 BOED, while aggregate uplift reached approximately 650 BOED (~3.9 MMSCFD) representing an ~18% improvement over the 12-month pre-deployment baseline. Decision cycle time was reduced by an estimated 55%, with full portfolio coverage achieved without additional engineering headcount. Novel/Additive Information This methodology demonstrates how AI-assisted surveillance integrates with petroleum engineering domain knowledge to create scalable production decision intelligence systems for mature assets. Unlike purely data-driven approaches, the framework combines machine learning with physics-based validation at every decision node preserving auditability, operational trust, and engineering accountability. This scalable, low-infrastructure model confirms that AI-assisted production intelligence is deployable without enterprise-scale investment across the Indus Basin and similar producing regions globally.

title: Preventing Major Road Transportation Incidents Through ADAS and AI-Enabled Fleet Intelligence: A Framework for Safer and More Resilient Energy Supply Chains
container-title: ADIPEC
9f5cdc164fe04e1f1f074f71895b4ac13038b5b4.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Road traffic crashes cause approx. 1.19 million fatalities and 20-50 million injuries globally each year (WHO 2023), while imposing economic losses approaching 3% of GDP in many countries. Transportation of fuels, chemicals, LNG, industrial gases, and other hazardous materials represents one of the most critical and risk-intensive links in global energy supply chains. Human factors—including fatigue, distraction, speeding, impaired judgement, and blind-spot errors—contribute to nearly 80-90%of severe transportation incidents. While telematics-based fleet monitoring has improved operational visibility, they remain largely reactive. This paper evaluates how Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) with AI-enabled fleet intelligence and Driver Monitoring System (DMS) can transform commercial fleet safety by shifting risk management from reactive monitoring to proactive accident prevention Methods, Procedures, Process This study utilizes a multi-evidence triangulation methodology integrating four streams: (1) forensic reconstruction of 60 severe tanker crashes (including 25 internal accident investigation); (2) physiological survey of 500 active drivers; (3) a 90-day pilot of 155 tankers using AI telematics and infrared DMS; and (4) Level 0–2 ADAS testing via an LCV-to-HCV validation bridge. The Safety Cocoon fuses forward 77 GHz radar, forward optical camera, and 24 GHz side radars with an in-cab DMS to continuously assess risk. Results, Observations, and Conclusions Forensic analysis identified rollovers (35%), rear-end impacts (28%), and sideswipes (18%) as dominant crash typologies, driven primarily by fatigue and distraction. The 155-tanker pilot revealed a 12-to-1 Detection Gap where DMS captured behavioral precursors invisible to passive GPS. Triangulated findings indicate the Safety Cocoon is projected to prevent 70–75% of forward and lateral collisions. Economic modelling projects a 17.12-month payback period on an upfront CapEx of ₹285.90 Lakh, generating ₹17.19 Crore in 10-year fleet lifecycle net returns. Novel Approach This paper presents an integrated Accident-to-ADAS Risk Mitigation Framework developed from real-world crash forensics, driver behavioural analytics, operational AI-enabled Fleet Intelligence pilot data, and an LCV-to-HCV ADAS Validation Framework. Rather than positioning ADAS as an optional vehicle feature, the research establishes an engineering and economic blueprint for integrating AI-enabled Fleet Intelligence, active ADAS, and Journey Risk Management 2.0 into a multi-layered Safety Cocoon for hazardous-material transportation. The proposed framework bridges the gap between passive behavioural monitoring and active physical intervention, providing energy executives, fleet operators, and regulators with a technically rigorous and economically justified pathway for strengthening the safety and resilience of global energy logistics

title: Closing the Loop: Connecting AI-Assisted HAZOP Analysis to Real-Time Operational Safety Intelligence
container-title: ADIPEC
af2ac320f8328df8414bc75a23c1510240f5ffe4.abstract: Abstract Process safety management in oil, gas and petrochemical facilities generates substantial safety knowledge through systematic Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) studies. That knowledge is, however, largely dormant in practice. Captured in static documentation, disconnected from operational systems, and unavailable to operators when needed. Simultaneously, control room operators face increasing volumes of data without real-time access to the structured safety reasoning developed during plant design. This paper presents an integrated approach to closing this loop, connecting AI-assisted HAZOP analysis to real-time operational safety intelligence through a shared knowledge representation framework based on Multilevel Flow Modelling (MFM). MFM is a deterministic, physics-based modelling methodology that represents a process plant as a network of functional goals, flows, and causal relationships. The same MFM model that enables automated HAZOP scenario generation can be deployed in a real-time decision support system to monitor plant operations, identify deviations, indicate likely root causes, and warn of potential consequences, all drawing from the pre-computed safety knowledge generated during HAZOP analysis. The paper describes the architecture of this dual-use safety model, the methodology for generating structured HAZOP outputs from MFM, the mechanism for deploying the same model in real-time control room assistance, and the approach for maintaining this connected safety knowledge base through plant lifecycle changes. Experience from AI-assisted HAZOP applications and control room decision support deployments demonstrates that the integrated approach improves hazard coverage, accelerates HAZOP execution, and provides operators with contextually relevant safety intelligence in real time. The paper also discusses the requirements for establishing a continuous Process Safety Management (PSM) evergreening cycle enabled by this technology integration.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Abnormal Situation Management: Field Performance Data from Oil and Gas Control Room Deployments
container-title: ADIPEC
30bbb89b3772ad5a2392ac8c19d2ca37f2e55ef5.abstract: Abstract Abnormal situations in oil, gas and petrochemical control rooms places extreme cognitive demands on operators. Time-pressured diagnosis, multi-source alarm interpretation, often result in decision-making under uncertainty. Artificial intelligence offers the potential to support this diagnosis and decision making, but the dominant machine learning approaches lack the transparency that safety-critical operational environments require. This paper presents field performance data from control room deployments of an explainable AI (xAI) system for real-time situational management, based on Multilevel Flow Modelling (MFM), a deterministic, physics-based knowledge representation that provides causal reasoning by design. The MFM-based system continuously monitors process data from the distributed control and safety system (DCS) or Historian, detects deviations against the plant production envelope, and presents operators with ranked potential root causes, related consequence that might happen and counter actions, each traceable to specific process model elements and P&ID´s. Unlike black-box AI systems, every indication can be interrogated, operators can examine the reasoning chain, cross-reference with P&IDs, and confirm or reject the system's assessment based on plant context. Field performance observations across multiple oil, gas and petrochemical deployments demonstrate consistent patterns. The system performs with high accuracy in root cause indication for abnormal events and multi-area scenarios, operators develop calibrated trust through demonstrated performance rather than blind reliance, explainability is identified by operators as the primary driver of adoption and the system provides measurable value in operator knowledge development, particularly for "new" personnel. The paper discusses the field evidence, the characteristics of MFM that enable xAI in this domain, the deployment architecture, and the implications for broader adoption of explainable AI in control rooms.

title: Reinventing Pipeline Shore Approaches on Artificial and Extended Natural Islands: A Cost- and Execution-Driven Strategy for Integrated Field Development
container-title: ADIPEC
d9c1bd6985dae1d24f4e5b37156bee3e1453822b.abstract: Abstract Optimizing pipeline shore approach design is a critical enabler for achieving sustainable production cost efficiency and long-term operational assurance in offshore gas developments, particularly within brownfield-constrained and environmentally sensitive environments such as extension of Das Island. For the SARB and NASR Gas Development Projects, the conventional shore approach involving rock revetment removal and reinstatement was initially adopted. However, one year misalignment in project execution timelines exposed significant inefficiencies associated with repeated island intervention, including increased CAPEX, environmental disturbance, constructability constraints, elevated risks to production continuity, and island integrity. This paper presents a techno-economic and execution-focused evaluation of alternative shore approach strategy, introducing a riser platform structure with bridge connectivity as a cost-optimized and future ready solution for integrated multi-project offshore developments. A structured, multi-criteria evaluation framework was applied to assess both conventional and alternative shore approach concepts. The baseline solution comprised island opening through revetment removal, sheet piling, excavation, dewatering, shore pull and full reinstatement of island. The timelines of SARB and NASR projects were not the same. To address inefficiencies arising from staggered project execution, an alternative offshore riser platform with bridge connection to Das Island was developed with evaluation as below with targeted market engagement and contractor expertise. Advanced engineering feasibility and constructability assessmentsOptimization of installation methodology, marine spread and dredging requirementsComparative analysis of CAPEX, execution duration and technical risksIntegration of a phased development strategy aligned with deferred NASR pipeline investment This approach ensured a holistic, execution-centric decision model balancing cost, schedule, risk, and long-term operability. The conventional beach pull approach, while technically proven, was determined to be operationally inefficient and cost-intensive, driven by repeated civil and marine interventions, extended schedule, and increased interface complexity. Moreover, staggered project timelines made it not feasible. In contrast, the riser platform solution enables single-instance infrastructure development, eliminating repeated revetment work and significantly reducing cumulative lifecycle cost. Despite higher upfront CAPEX, the solution delivers: Material reduction in total cost of ownership through elimination of reworkEnhanced constructability and execution certainly, with optimized schedule, minimizing offshore-onshore interface risksFuture-ready scalability, enabling seamless integration of the deferred NASR pipeline without reintervention This study conclusively demonstrates that adopting the riser platform provides superior lifecycle value, effectively aligning cost optimization with reliability, operability, strategic project delivery objectives and its more environment friendly This paper establishes a shift from project-specific optimization to integrated, cross-project infrastructure planning, introducing a lean, fit-for-purpose engineering approach for complex offshore developments. The proposed riser platform-bridge configuration offers a flexible, scalable, and replicable solution for scenarios involving multiple pipeline landfalls or constrained shore approach conditions. It demonstrates how early alignment of project interfaces, phased investment strategies, and innovative design integration can unlock significant value. This methodology enables reduced lifecycle costs, improved execution efficiency, and enhanced production assurance, and is directly applicable to ADNOC developments as well as global offshore assets facing similar constructability and landfall constraints

title: Objective Pre-Shift Cognitive Readiness as a Human Factors Barrier: Field Evidence from Offshore Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
f6494d7a443b791d77efca4dd5e7e864812b1ae9.abstract: Offshore operations depend on reliable performance in safety-critical functions, and the industry's human performance framework treats that performance as shaped by the conditions under which work is done, among them workload, sleep opportunity, rotation design, and supervision (IOGP 2026). When these conditions degrade, the effect reaches the operation as well as the safety record: in the deployments described in this paper, events whose investigations recorded reduced human performance among the contributing factors also carried production cost, in interrupted operations and deferred output. The controls that address these conditions, from fatigue risk management to competence assurance, primarily operate at the level of the schedule and the job category, and do not ordinarily provide a standardized, individual-referenced signal before the shift. In current practice, that space is covered by the supervisor's judgment and the pre-shift conversation. A standardized signal would give that judgment an instrument: an indication of when to offer support, and when to review the day's risk controls before critical work begins. The barrier literature offers a test for what a daily process built around such a signal would need to do. Sklet (2006) describes active safety barriers as realizing a sequence of functions: detect a deviation, decide on a response, and carry the response out. In the barrier models the industry applies across many domains, bowtie analysis among them, degraded human performance appears as one of several escalation factors that can erode the performance of other barriers, together with technical and organizational degradation. The controls that address the contributing conditions are set in advance and calibrated for groups: rosters, hours-of-service limits, training cycles. The growing use of leading indicators in operational safety follows a logic that applies here as well: monitor conditions relevant to barrier performance before the barrier is called on, instead of counting the events it failed to stop (IOGP 2023). A daily, individual-referenced readiness signal has not been routinely integrated with this set of controls, a gap discussed at greater length in the field study that precedes this paper. That field study showed the signal can be produced under routine offshore conditions. Before the shift, each operator in a safety-critical function completes a short cognitive task of under three minutes, delivered as a standardized digital application with the format of a game and the function of an instrument: the result is derived from measured performance on the task, not from a questionnaire. The task is calibrated to each function through an onboard neuroergonomic assessment, the application of neuroscience methods to the study of work (Parasuraman and Wilson 2008), which characterizes the cognitive demands the activity places on whoever performs it. The result is read against the operator's own accumulated baseline together with the cognitive demands of the function, so a deviation records a change in test performance relative to that combined reference, and it enters the day's risk assessment as an individual-referenced input, read much as a wind limit is read before work at height: the value is compared with a reference range, and an out-of-range reading changes how the task is conducted and which controls apply. A green result, within the operator's normal range, requires no further step. A yellow result opens a support conversation between operator and supervisor and activates predefined, graded, non-punitive risk controls, co-designed with the asset team, before critical work begins; the result is not a diagnosis and is not used for appraisal or discipline, and activation is used in this sense throughout the paper. Over a 22-month evaluation at one asset, the program was associated with a sustained reduction in events whose investigations recorded reduced human performance among the contributing factors, and in the production downtime attributed to those events (Baldassim et al. 2026, in press).

title: From Passive Video Surveillance to Scalable HSE Intelligence: Field Lessons from AI-CCTV Validation in a Harsh Desert Oil Field
container-title: ADIPEC
1d3a42bec17df281472c9ac2c9a57f24ae75f41d.abstract: Abstract At remote oil and gas facilities, closed-circuit television still relies on a person watching live views and searching stored footage after an event. As camera counts rise, that arrangement misses brief, distant, partly hidden, or visually ambiguous events more easily. This paper examines field validation of an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled closed-circuit television (CCTV) system, referred to here as AI-CCTV, in a large onshore field exposed to intense sunlight, glare, dust, long viewing distances, low-light conditions, sparse infrastructure, and a mix of fixed optical and moving infrared or pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras. The workflow combined secure video ingestion, computer-vision detection, multi-object tracking, context-preserving evidence, structured vision-language assistance, a monitoring interface, and human alarm disposition. Representative scenarios covered personnel presence, personal protective equipment compliance, portable gas-monitor recognition, liquid-like anomalies, falls, selected unsafe behaviors, and restricted-area monitoring. The evidence shows functional feasibility and recurring failure mechanisms, but it does not justify a universal accuracy claim. In many cases, the limiting factor was whether the scene made the target observable, not which model was selected. Small or distant targets required changes to imaging, camera position, tracking, and evidence capture; detector tuning alone rarely solved the problem. Moving cameras required a separate analytical contract for camera state, dwell time, target reacquisition, and return-to-route behavior. Generic models were useful starting points, but field use still required local hard negatives, controlled configuration, shadow-mode testing, and a release process that could be audited. Nuisance alarms were treated as a system cost and managed with temporal persistence, context, semantic checks, risk rules, and human review. These observations are organized into six scale-up gates covering operational value, observability, local evidence, infrastructure, controlled use, and lifecycle ownership. A three-wave rollout and a minimum metric set are also defined. The result is a governed health, safety, and environment (HSE) decision-support service, not an autonomous protection layer.

title: Circular Economy Approach to Drilling Fluid Additives: Sustainable Waste-Valorized CaO/MgO Nanocomposite for Rheology and Filtration Enhancement
container-title: ADIPEC
427c9419ea77cd3e12fbfd4c32524d77ed548dea.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the application of a waste-derived CaO/MgO (85:15 wt%) composite, synthesized from Sugar Filter Cake Waste (SFCW), as a multifunctional additive in KCl-Polymer water-based drilling fluids. Two synthesis routes were evaluated: a direct calcination route producing a microscale composite at 12.2 USD/kg, and a hydrothermal sol–gel route producing a nanoscale composite at 218.6 USD/kg. The primary objective is to determine whether the SFCW-derived material enhances the rheological and filtration performance of the base drilling fluid, and whether the microscale formulation can match or exceed the nanoscale equivalent — providing a cost-effective, industrially scalable alternative to conventional synthetic additives. KCl-Polymer base mud was prepared according to standard formulation protocols and used as experimental control. Both composites were added at 1,500 ppm and evaluated across a temperature range of 30–60°C. Measured properties included Plastic Viscosity (PV), Yield Point (YP), 10-second and 10-minute Gel Strength, full Fann viscometer flow curves (3–600 rpm), API 30-minute filtrate volume, and mud cake thickness. Performance improvement was quantified as percentage change versus the base fluid. Both composites significantly enhanced all measured drilling-fluid properties relative to the base mud. The microscale (Physical Method) composite produced superior improvements across every property: PV increased by 47.7% on average versus 35.6% for the nanoscale formulation; YP improved by 53.1% versus 30.4%; API filtrate volume decreased by 33.7% (to 6.9 cc from 10.4 cc base) versus 25.0% for the nanocomposite (7.8 cc); and mud cake thickness was reduced by 44.7% (0.83 mm) versus 33.3%(1.0 mm). The microscale composite demonstrated near-perfect thermal consistency in YP enhancement (+53–54% across 30–60°C), indicating superior thermal stability relative to the nanocomposite. This is the first study to demonstrate that a directly calcined, waste-derived CaO/MgO composite from sugar industry by-products delivers superior drilling-fluid performance compared to its nanoscale counterpart in a KCl-Polymer system at 17.9× lower production cost. The counterintuitive micro &gt; nano performance reversal is attributed to more uniform particle distribution and coherent filter-cake formation in the KCl electrolyte environment. The results highlight the potential of SFCW-derived CaO/MgO composites as sustainable drilling-fluid additives capable of improving operational performance while supporting circular-economy principles. Their low-cost production, scalability, and effective rheological and filtration enhancement make them attractive candidates for environmentally responsible drilling-fluid systems in future oilfield applications.

title: From Static Assumptions to Dynamic Intelligence: Next-Generation Gas Lift Optimization in Buhasa Field
container-title: ADIPEC
b30f7a6ee713630a957e159a3e816048a13093e3.abstract: Abstract Gas lift is widely used in mature oil fields to sustain production as reservoir pressure declines. In a large asset such as the Buhasa Field, Optimization involves more than selecting an injection rate for an individual well. A limited lift-gas supply must be distributed among wells with different production characteristics while honoring well targets, group controls, pressure limits, facility capacity, and field production objectives. Commercial reservoir simulators address this problem by dividing the lift-gas supply into discrete increments. At each optimization event, the simulator evaluates the production effect of adding or removing an increment from each eligible well. Gas is preferentially allocated to the wells offering the highest weighted incremental production response. A user-defined Minimum Economic Gradient (MEG) determines whether the incremental oil gained from an additional gas increment is sufficient to justify its use. The MEG provides a practical economic criterion, but the well response against which it is evaluated varies across the field and changes throughout field life. Reservoir depletion, increasing water cut, changing productivity, network backpressure, and operating constraints continuously alter the oil-versus-lift-gas response curve. Consequently, even when the user-input MEG remains unchanged, the economically justified injection rate for an individual well can change significantly with time. These variations are difficult to examine across hundreds of wells using standard simulator outputs alone. This paper presents an enhanced workflow that combines commercial reservoir simulation with custom Python-based analytics. The workflow extracts well-level oil and lift-gas response profiles, calculates the marginal oil response associated with successive injection increments, and compares the calculated gradients with the user-input MEG. Automated plots and diagnostic reports identify wells receiving gas in low-response regions and show how well performance changes through time. The workflow also supports separate review of wells that temporarily fall below the economic criterion but remain important for liquid unloading, production continuity, future potential, or other reservoir-management considerations. Application of the workflow to the Buhasa Field reduced gas lift injection rate by 25% and water production rate by 15%, this improved the Gas Utilization Factor by more than 35% at much lower infill wells required thus improving the overall economics of the field. The workflow does not replace the simulator's optimization algorithm; instead, it makes the basis of its well-level allocation decisions clearer and easier to review. The resulting framework improves lift-gas utilization, supports informed engineering intervention, and creates a structured dataset for future machine-learning applications.

title: Decision-Centric Energy Operations: Integrating Edge Intelligence, Operational Digital Twins, Industrial Work Surfaces, and Agentic AI
container-title: ADIPEC
1af45810d093a029724673a2f2c636ee47c2794e.abstract: Abstract Energy operators are not short of data. Most assets already have sensors, historians, supervisory systems, engineering tools, dashboards, digital twins, and a growing number of AI pilots. The harder problem starts after an event is detected. Engineers still have to bring together operating trends, work history, procedures, constraints, and approval requirements from several systems before they can make a safe decision. This paper proposes a decision-centric operating architecture that connects edge intelligence, an operational digital twin, an industrial work surface, and agentic AI within a human-in-the- loop model. The layers are intentionally separated. Edge intelligence qualifies events near the asset. The digital twin adds asset context, operating state, constraints, and history. The work surface places the case into investigation, approval, and execution workflows. Agentic AI supports the engineer by retrieving evidence, invoking approved tools, checking rules, and preparing an explainable recommendation. The pattern is intended for workflow-level deployment rather than unconstrained automation. A representative implementation pattern shows how a qualified trigger initiates context retrieval from live data, engineering documents, maintenance history, procedures, prior events, and constraint models. The agent prepares a recommendation package that exposes evidence, assumptions, alternatives, constraint checks, confidence levels, and required human approval before action. The contribution is a practical reference pattern for moving from data visibility to decision execution. The paper emphasizes bounded AI use, evidence traceability, workflow ownership, auditability, and human authority. It does not argue for transferring accountability to autonomous systems. Instead, it shows how AI can reduce investigation effort, improve decision consistency, and give engineers and operators a clearer basis for action.

title: A Master Well, Multilayer Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning (AI/ML) Framework for Scalable Porosity Permeability Prediction and Log Reconstruction in Carbonate Reservoirs
container-title: ADIPEC
dfaac0c94fde56ef5a3e7aa3ea031a204d0361e0.abstract: Abstract Carbonate reservoirs exhibit complex petrophysical behavior arising from heterogeneity, uneven core coverage and variable log data quality. These challenges significantly limit the scalability and repeatability of conventional petrophysical workflows, particularly when extended to large well populations. To address these limitations, this study presents a Master Well centric artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) framework for scalable prediction of porosity and permeability and log reconstruction with a focus on improving model generalization, validation robustness and operational efficiency across the field. Conventional petrophysical machine learning is bound to the well in which it was calibrated. This study shifts the unit of training from the well to the field by constructing a Master Well, a single core calibrated reference population assembled by randomized sampling across nine wells. Two advances underpin the approach. Pore aspect ratio is estimated from the fractional lithology curves of the multimineral solution, so the elastic properties follow the local calcite and dolomite volumes and stay consistent with theoretical endmember values. The soft and stiff pore endmembers defined by Kumar and Han (2005) and Xu and Payne (2009) provide the envelope within which each sample is placed, and the aspect ratio contours between those limits separate the pore classes. Each pore system is normalized within its class to decompose total porosity into comparable fractions, which enter the models as engineered features alongside the pore classes carried through training and testing as categorical classifiers. The secondary porosity index and the pore aspect ratio emerge as the strongest permeability indicators of those tested, and both outrank porosity alone. Seventy two models were developed across multiple algorithm families, with the best realization of each retained for comparison. Held out testing returns R2 between 0.71 and 0.95, the wireline responses being reconstructed most accurately and the rock properties limited by genuine reservoir heterogeneity rather than by model capability. Because the reference population spans the full multilayer succession rather than a single interval, the models carry that layered behavior into every well to which they are applied. Deployment to a new well requires only environmental correction and normalization to the Master Well reference distributions, with no additional core. Accuracy is expected to hold within the calibration envelope of approximately 20 km lateral extent defined by the present dataset, beyond which predictions should be treated as indicative until confirmed against local core.

title: Closing the Loop: Integrating QA/QC Intelligence with Advanced Process Control Across Oil & Gas Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
32e6a27e5c6085a6ef1bb18ab31efc8afd085a86.abstract: Abstract Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) activities in oil and gas operations generate high-value technical information through laboratory testing, inspection, calibration, audit, non-conformance and product-release workflows. In many operating environments, however, this information is mainly consumed after product movement, or process decisions have already occurred. Advanced Process Control (APC), process historians and digital optimization platforms are usually configured around continuously available variables such as flow, pressure, temperature, tank movement, online analyzer signals and process constraints. This separation creates a practical gap between verified quality evidence and real-time operating decisions. This paper presents a Quality Intelligence-to-Control Loop (QICL) framework that converts laboratory and QA/QC information into governed, predictive and actionable decision support for APC and operations. The framework is demonstrated using an anonymized petroleum distribution laboratory scenario covering lube/base oil, gasoline, Jet A-1, distillates of light-medium-heavy hydrocarbon samples. Routine parameters including appearance, density, kinematic viscosity, viscosity index, flash point, distillation profile, pour point, sulphur content, and others are transformed into critical quality variables, risk flags and advisory control constraints. The framework is designed around ISO/IEC 17025 principles including metrological traceability, measurement uncertainty evaluation, proficiency testing participation, and validation of laboratory data prior to operational use. Results generated through ASTM proficiency testing, instrument quality-control verification, and laboratory-approved workflows provide the governance layer required for reliable integration between quality intelligence and operational decision systems. Test result dataset of 120 demonstration records is used to illustrate product-family segmentation, quality-risk classification, escalation logic and normalized performance trends.
