The results show how QICL can support earlier quality-risk recognition, more consistent escalation, reduced decision latency and better alignment between laboratory assurance and operational control. The contribution of the paper is an original, template-ready integration model that makes QA/QC an active contributor to predictive process governance rather than a retrospective reporting function. The paper avoids commercial claims and presents the case as a generic petroleum laboratory application suitable for adaptation across oil and gas operations.

title: Strategy and Crisis Monitor: An AI-Enabled Autonomous Maritime Monitor for Disruption Intelligence and Operational Resilience
container-title: ADIPEC
58cade6d0892c7942bcb9842e0ff73b921a3b017.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the Strategy and Crisis Monitor, an agentic artificial-intelligence (AI) enabled executive dashboard conceived, built, and deployed end-to-end in days to track regional events, incidents, transport disruption, and energy-market signals during a live crisis. The work pursues three objectives: to demonstrate that autonomous AI agents can convert public maritime, energy, and trade data into always-on disruption intelligence; to replace the analyst-curated executive briefing with a live, evidence-linked signal layer operating under human oversight; and to compress executive decision latency from days to minutes. The architecture comprises three operational layers. An ingestion layer of autonomous agents continuously normalizes heterogeneous public sources, including multilateral chokepoint transit data, vessel-tracking feeds derived from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), international oil and gas statistics, and maritime trade and connectivity indicators, supplemented by market context as evidence layers. A classification layer maps incoming data against a rules-based event taxonomy covering chokepoint disruption, export-route stress, gas exposure, port-connectivity deterioration, and regional trade impact. A prioritization layer scores signals using a weighted composite risk index with exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) and cumulative sum (CUSUM) anomaly detection, and surfaces them through a 60-second executive scan pattern with full drill-down to underlying sources. Deployed live during the March 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption, when average daily transits collapsed by approximately 95% against the February baseline and the benchmark very large crude carrier (VLCC) rate reached an all-time high, the platform was used to brief senior leadership of a major national maritime and energy logistics operator in near real time. It reduced executive decision latency from a typical 24- to 72-hour analyst cycle to under five minutes per signal, a compression factor of roughly 290 to 860, while integrating more than 40 public indicators. The same detection logic was subsequently applied retrospectively to four historical chokepoint crises, in the Red Sea (2023 to 2024), the Suez Canal (2021), the Strait of Hormuz (2019), and the Panama Canal (2023 to 2024), confirming that the monitored public signals were available weeks to months ahead of official statistics in every case. Those case studies were reconstructed with knowledge of how each episode unfolded and therefore document signal availability and design generality rather than prospective detection performance. The contribution is twofold and is, to the authors’ knowledge, the first implementation of its kind in the maritime-resilience and energy-logistics literature. First, a decision-method contribution: passive public reporting feeds are converted into a structured, always-on resilience instrument fusing maritime, energy, and trade signals in a single operating view. Second, an operating-model contribution: the architecture is public-data-native, lightweight to sustain, and reproducible across operating companies, corridors, and risk domains, and is presented together with the governance, oversight, and control mechanisms required before agentic AI is admitted to a critical operational environment. Both are directly actionable for practicing engineers and planners in operations, strategy, and resilience roles.

title: From Incident to Intelligence: Preventing Major Accidents on Drilling Rigs Through Systematic Lessons Learnt Integration
container-title: ADIPEC
996e4e38ec939bc99377498ce6b4297937781e12.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope This paper presents a major study examining root causes and systemic failure patterns behind significant major accident events on drilling rigs across global operations, translating findings into a structured major accident prevention framework applicable across offshore and onshore drilling environments to reduce the recurrence of catastrophic events. Methods, Procedures, Process A structured review of publicly documented major drilling rig accidents was conducted, encompassing well control incidents, blowouts, fires, structural failures, and dropped objects. Root cause analysis and failure mode classification were applied using TRIPOD Beta methodology and bow-tie risk modelling, corroborated against ten years of independently published industry-wide causal factor statistics (IOGP 2026). Field validation was conducted through structured interviews with 28 drilling engineers, health, safety, and environment (HSE) specialists, well control instructors, and rig-floor supervisors across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. Results, Observations, Conclusions Analysis revealed persistent, recurring evidence of barrier degradation, inadequate risk perception, and organizational drift as primary contributing factors. Well control events were most frequently preceded by degraded primary barriers, insufficient monitoring discipline, and time-pressure-driven decision-making: 79% of surveyed practitioners (22 of 28) confirmed personally experiencing production pressure push an unsafe continuation decision, and 71% reported a bridging protocol that nonetheless failed in practice. The certification-to-competency gap was rated 3.46 of 5. TRIPOD Beta analysis identified maintenance management, communication, procedures, and training as dominant causal factors, independently corroborated by IOGP's industry-wide data. A proactive, lessons-learnt-driven safety culture is essential to breaking the cycle of recurring major accidents. Novel/Additive Information This paper introduces the Drilling Major Accident Prevention Framework (DMAPF) — a structured taxonomy of drilling rig accident causal factors organized by operational phase, barrier type, and organizational layer, validated through field ratings of 3.8–4.2 out of 5 across all 28 participants. The DMAPF enables drilling teams to systematically anticipate and proactively mitigate historically recurrent major accident pathways before they materialize.

title: Bounded Autonomy: A Budget-Constrained Framework for AI Agent Operations Toward Safety-Critical Process Environments
container-title: ADIPEC
218b63ba23b1023922dbb33dc33f93956e9f5161.abstract: Abstract Tight autonomy budgets improve safety for AI agents in process control with bounded completion cost: the pooled 95% CI for retention is 90.9 to 111.5%, admitting up to 9.1% loss in the worst case but centering on 100.8% (no net cost). For reactive architectures, safety-check rejections drop by 89% and token cost by 85% while completion change is negligible (Cohen's |d| &lt; 0.01). We introduce Bounded Autonomy, a framework that constrains AI agent autonomy along four coordinated dimensions (tool calls, cumulative process perturbation, simulation timesteps, and checkpoint intervals), all calibrated from a single tightness parameter derived from each scenario's estimated optimal action count. Pre-execution middleware, implemented as a LangGraph StateGraph, rejects over-budget actions before they reach the process. Four agent architectures (ReAct, Reflexion, Plan-and-Execute, Hybrid) are evaluated under four budget levels across 20 Continuous Stirred-Tank Reactor (CSTR) scenarios in the OpsEnv benchmark. The evaluation totals over 7,100 experiment cells: 1,680 core Tier 1 cells, 2,800 extended-seed cells, 1,260 cross-model cells, and 1,452 supplementary cells (sensitivity, ablation, rollback, and decoupled experiments). Under tight budgets (1.2× optimal), reactive architectures retain completion (Cohen's |d| &lt; 0.01; Bonferroni-corrected p &gt; 0.05; 95% CI for pooled retention: 90.9 to 111.5%) with 7× wall-time reduction for ReAct and 6.7× for Reflexion. Unconstrained agents take ∼5× more actions than necessary, and these excess actions are counterproductive: in the most pronounced case (scenario B04), a ReAct agent improves from 0.041 to 0.950 completion under budget constraints. Conversely, multi-step optimization tasks (e.g., A04 under ReAct) can lose up to 73 percentage points. Cross-model validation with Qwen 2.5 32B and Llama 3.1 8B (1,260 cells across up to 20 scenarios) confirms the directional violation-reduction effect at reduced magnitude (25% vs. 89% for Tier 1). AI-assisted tools were used in the experimental evaluation; all outputs were reviewed and validated by the authors.

title: From Broker Calls to Autonomous Chartering: How AI and Real-Time Market Intelligence are Reshaping Offshore Vessel Logistics
container-title: ADIPEC
df6a5f2e9db916cc0ed56d54fcca63a7da33ffa8.abstract: Abstract This paper explores how AI-powered vessel intelligence platforms and agentic systems are reshaping the way offshore energy operators and project managers identify, evaluate and engage with vessel owners. The objective is to demonstrate how consolidating real-time AIS tracking, vessel specifications, market availability and owner contact workflows into a single platform compresses the vessel sourcing cycle and reduces operational uncertainty in offshore logistics planning. The paper draws on the development and deployment of an offshore vessel intelligence platform aggregating data from 30,000+ vessels across 25+ countries, covering vessel specifications, live AIS positioning, ownership data and market availability signals. The methodology documents how agentic AI layers applied to this dataset enable project teams to move from initial vessel search to direct owner engagement within minutes rather than days. Case studies from European offshore wind and EPCI markets illustrate how consolidated market intelligence replaces fragmented, network-dependent sourcing processes with structured, data-driven workflows accessible to any operator regardless of existing broker relationships. The platform approach demonstrates measurable improvements across three dimensions of offshore vessel sourcing. Vessel identification cycles, traditionally dependent on broker networks and manual market canvassing, are reduced from days to minutes when real-time availability, technical specifications and ownership data are consolidated in a single searchable environment. Agentic AI systems enable operators to initiate contact with relevant vessel owners and receive preliminary availability confirmation within the same session, eliminating the sequential delays inherent to conventional brokerage. At the market intelligence level, aggregated fixture data and fleet movement analytics provide project teams with pricing benchmarks and availability forecasts previously accessible only to established brokers. These capabilities are particularly relevant for Gulf-based operators managing complex multi-vessel EPCI campaigns, where sourcing speed and market transparency directly impact project schedules and cost outcomes. This paper presents the first structured analysis of agentic AI applied specifically to offshore vessel sourcing workflows, demonstrating how real-time vessel intelligence and accelerated owner engagement compress commercial timelines without reliance on traditional brokerage intermediaries. This addresses a documented gap in digital transformation literature for offshore marine logistics.

title: An Award-Winning Reliability Transformation Program for Artificial Lift Wells: Applying Lean Six Sigma to Deliver 74% Failure Reduction and USD 125 Million Asset Value Creation
container-title: ADIPEC
96a6cb651871a60994601c93f439e3a968e48c83.abstract: Abstract Artificial-lift reliability in mature viscous-oil assets is governed by interactions among well trajectory, rod-string loading, solids, completion materials, operating practice, and execution quality. This paper presents a multi-year reliability-transformation program for beam-pump (BP) and progressive-cavity-pump (PCP) wells in South Oman. The program combined Lean Six Sigma DMAIC with reliability engineering, statistical validation, completion redesign, execution assurance, and closed-loop governance. Tubing failures increased from approximately 3% of all artificial-lift failures in 2014 to 9% by the first half of 2018 and reached 26% in the most affected clusters. Mean tubing run life in the focused population was approximately 187 days, below the 365-day lower specification. Analysis classified 91.5% of the tubing failures as wear-related. Contact load and local well deviation received the highest cause-and-effect scores, while failure position was strongly associated with distance from the pump. The improvement package addressed the complete failure system: glass-reinforced-epoxy (GRE)-lined tubing for selected recurrent-failure wells, rod-string and weighting-bar redesign to reduce buckling, solids and operating-envelope controls, standardized make-up and drift practices, and execution assurance through failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), checklists, and standard operating procedures. In a matched 12-well comparison, repeat interventions decreased from 43 to zero during the defined comparison window (two-sample Poisson rate test, p &lt; 0.001). Mean run life increased from 187 to 418 days in the early post-pilot dataset and to 459 days in the later controlled dataset. At project close, all 12 wells in the archived GRE surveillance chart were still running after 972-1,288 days, and 11 had exceeded three years. Later operational follow-up confirmed that many continued beyond the cut-off and some reached approximately five years of service. At portfolio scale, the operator's normalized reliability dashboard reported a 74% reduction in the defined tubing-failure key performance indicator (KPI) within the program population and deployment envelope. The approved five-year value-assurance model assumed 125 avoided tubing-failure interventions per year at USD 175,000 per event, giving USD 109.375 million of direct cost avoidance, plus USD 15.625 million of avoided oil deferment and USD 125 million of cumulative asset value. These portfolio outcomes rely on the operator's approved scorecard and value definitions and were not extrapolated from the 13-well pilot. Later fleet surveillance identified a rise in total and premature failure indices outside the stable pilot evidence, showing that durable hardware performance must be sustained by governance. The paper therefore contributes both a technical solution and a transferable management system based on evidence-tiered claims, risk-based deployment, and closed-loop control.

title: Red Palm Oil Administration in Undernourished Wistar Rats: Effects on Cognitive, Gastrointestinal, Skeletal, and Organ Parameters
container-title: An Idea Health Journal
d17d284aca06d0576a4bc881df0640faae01c668.abstract: Background: Malnutrition affects multiple physiological systems, including cognitive, gastrointestinal, skeletal, and organ functions. Red palm oil (RPO) contains bioactive compounds that may influence physiological responses to malnutrition. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of RPO on biomedical parameters in undernourished Wistar rats. Methods: This experimental laboratory study integrated several sub-studies using post-test-only and pretest-posttest control group designs. Male Wistar rats aged 3–4 weeks underwent 50% feed restriction for 14 days, followed by RPO administration at doses of 2, 4, or 6 mL/kgBW for 28 days. Groups included normal, negative, and selected positive vitamin A controls. Sample sizes varied across sub-studies. Data were analyzed using ANOVA, Kruskal– Wallis, post hoc tests, and correlation analyses, with p < 0.05 considered significant. Result: Significant differences were observed in Y-maze cognitive performance (p = 0.031), intestinal weight (p = 0.003), femur weight (ANOVA p = 0.037; Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.048), and heart (p = 0.010), liver (p = 0.002), and kidney (p = 0.004) indices. Femur length differed significantly using Kruskal–Wallis (p = 0.042), but not ANOVA (p = 0.052). No significant differences were observed in hemoglobin levels (p = 0.494),motor performance (p = 0.120), lung (p = 0.070), or spleen (p = 0.120) indices. Contribution for Practice: RPO administration produced variable responses across biomedical parameters, providing preliminary preclinical evidence for further nutritional research. However, inconsistent dose-response patterns and the absence of significant effects on several outcomes limit its clinical applicability. Further mechanistic and clinical studies are required before RPO can be recommended for nutritional rehabilitation.

title: Life-Of-Field Artificial Lift Strategy in Giant Fields with Varying Fluid and Rock Characteristics
container-title: ADIPEC
3940c2822085d6b85e4493e7549de9ed3fb29e0d.abstract: Abstract In medium-sized fields with more or less uniform rock and fluid properties, selection of the most appropriate artificial lift method is typically straightforward. In giant fields that exhibit substantial variation in both fluid and rock properties, many complicating factors play a role in the selection process. The aim of this paper is to document the thought process influencing the selection process for ADNOC's vast portfolio of giant reservoirs. The starting point is a simple vertical well model, which is subjected to a large variable sensitivity study involving depth, pipe size, reservoir inflow characteristics (reservoir pressure and productivity index, which will reflect a combination of average KH, skin, and effective well length), fluid properties (oil viscosity, solution GOR, saturation pressure, all of which are linked together leveraging ADNOC's large PVT database), and of course water-cut. Artificial lift methods, such as gas lift or electric submersible pumps, are then introduced, and the maximum liquid rate that they can deliver is then compared against the expected target production rate from the development plan. The methodology has identified four key domains in the parameter space. Domains 1 and 2 represent cases where the target rates can only be delivered by either ESP's or gas lift, respectively. Domain 3 captures situations where more than one artificial lift method applies and domain 4 highlights situations where existing methods currently appear to be technically unviable or require further R&D expenditure; this applies to low-GOR, high-PI wells where existing ESP solutions are unable to handle the required rates. The outcome of this first comprehensive screening step is then fed into the next stage of the selection workflow, which involves more practical aspects related to implementation, such as availability of gas, compression requirements, electricity requirements, ESP run-life, etc. We illustrate the methodology in a giant field with substantial variation in rock and fluid characteristics where a single method will not apply everywhere. Another complicating factor which will be covered describes the requirement to honor reservoir operational guidelines. This is to our knowledge the most comprehensive analysis method ever disclosed to the public and it covers situations which occur predominantly in giant reservoirs where the combined evaluation of technical applicability, infrastructure, and timing must all be considered.

title: Autonomous Well Startup and Control with AI-Based Decisioning for Measurable Production Outcomes and Operational Excellence Using Real-Time Wellhead Intelligence
container-title: ADIPEC
8db35cd131842310f9d5d4faf2dbfb30ea10108c.abstract: Abstract This paper details an innovative practice and adapted initiative implemented by Company Asset to ensure continuous measurement, monitoring, and control of oil flow from oil-producing well leveraging Artificial Intelligence. In addition to maintaining the specified oil flow target, autonomous gas flow control was also effectively managed to ensure comprehensive well control. This arrangement proved advantageous in achieving the well testing key performance indicators (KPIs) and eliminating the need for manual intervention, thereby saving man-hours. The need for real-time flow monitoring & control at individual wellheads led to evaluating various solutions. A Multiphase Flow Meter (MPFM) was installed, enhancing flow measurement and allowing configuration of oil flow rate signals to control valve. This setup enabled autonomous control of the well, managing both natural oil flow and artificial lift gas flow when needed. The design allows easy relocation based on well-activated needs. Steps taken included: Implementing management of change for new solutionsConducting risk assessmentsEvaluating vital GL well surface and subsurface parameters Developing safe operating procedures, scenarios, schematics, and a user-friendly control scheme The autonomous control of the well enabled comprehensive management of the lift gas well. It also significantly reduced the manual labor required for diverting the well into testing facilities. Additionally, it facilitated the optimization of the gas flow rate and ensured the continuous production of oil through the oil-producing wells. The observed well control behavior was smooth and adhered to the stipulated setpoints. By leveraging the capability to connect the MPFM with the piping connections available at the wellhead, the following benefits were achieved and will continue to be advantageous in the future: Optimization of manhours approximately 87 hours for 10 wells / 1,200 hours for 140 wellsProduction gain of 1,850,000 barrels of oil by preventing production loss from gas lift wellsOptimization of GL flow rate, leading to savings of lean gas (9,000 MMscf for 50 wells) valued at 133 MMUSDAchievement of 100% well testing KPIsEffective and timely dual-string well testing resulting in a 10 MMUSD production gainEnsuring compliance with subsurface parameter restrictions, thereby preserving reservoir healthEnhancement of well digitalizationFacilitation of autonomous well controlReal-time well testingAccurate representation of the well's behaviorAI-based decision-making ensuring adherence to restrictions and WH/reservoir guidelines The implemented solution is highly effective in ensuring continuous production, timely well testing, and reducing manhours by leveraging autonomous control integrated with artificial intelligence. This methodology can be replicated across other existing facilities within the company and globally for the following reasons: Real-time flow monitoring and controlWell testing complianceEffective reservoir management This implementation will enhance well availability with continuous production while ensuring the health of the reservoir and surface facilities.

title: Revolutionising Asset Performance Management Through Autonomous Robotics and Integrated Digital Platform Intelligence: First Deployment of an ATEX/IECEX-Rated Quadruped Robot in Kuwait
container-title: ADIPEC
20e5020536fed144a7648c14e0497064f0b39d4b.abstract: Abstract Reliability engineers in operating facilities are increasingly burdened by the manual aggregation of asset health data from disparate sources — process historians, ERP systems, and periodic inspection records — leaving limited capacity for higher-value analysis and decision-making. This paper presents the design and first deployment of an integrated autonomous inspection and asset performance management solution at a Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) facility, delivered through a tripartite collaboration between KOC, SLB and ANYbotics. The core objective was to demonstrate that continuous, robot-acquired inspection data — fused with existing ERP and DCS data on SLB's platform — could enable AI and physics-based models to autonomously generate asset health and maintenance actions, fundamentally augmenting the role of the reliability engineer. The solution architecture comprises three integrated layers. First, the ANYmal X quadruped robot — certified for Zone 1 and Zone 2 explosive atmospheres — was deployed to conduct autonomous inspection rounds across the KOC facility. The quadruped's terrain mobility across stairs, gratings, elevated structures, and confined walkways enabled coverage of approximately 70–80% of total inspection routes, including persistent monitoring of identified bad actor assets responsible for disproportionate unplanned downtime. The robot's multi-modal payload captures thermal anomalies, acoustic signatures, visual data with AI-based interpretation, and gas leak detection at frequencies unachievable through manual rounds. Due to the applicable explosive-atmosphere standards were written for fixed installations and manned mobile plants rather than for autonomous legged machines, the paper also sets the challenges in the design and realization of an Ex-product for such applications. Second, this continuous stream of inspection data is ingested into SLB's asset performance management platform; OptiSite - alongside existing asset health data — real-time process values from the DCS and equipment history and work orders from the ERP — creating a unified, continuously enriched data foundation for each asset. Third, SLB's AI models and physics-based models operate on this fused dataset to automatically generate prioritised maintenance recommendations, failure risk assessments, and asset health scores. The system was designed to take on a significant portion of the routine analytical workload traditionally performed by KOC's reliability engineers, allowing them to focus on complex exception handling and strategic decision-making. The deployment demonstrated that fusing autonomous robotic inspection data with ERP and DCS sources on a single intelligent platform produces a qualitative shift in asset performance management capability. Coverage of 70–80% of inspection rounds — with targeted monitoring of bad actor assets — provided reliability teams with a continuous, objective view of asset condition that manual inspection cycles cannot sustain. AI and physical model outputs translated this enriched data into actionable maintenance recommendations, measurably reducing the analytical burden on reliability engineers and shortening the time from anomaly detection to intervention. Personnel exposure in hazardous zones was also substantially reduced, improving HSE performance at the KOC facility. This paper presents the first deployment of the ATEX/IECEx-rated quadruped in an Ex-rated operational environment in Kuwait and the first documented implementation of a fully integrated solution combining quadruped robotic inspection — thermal, acoustic, visual interpretation, and gas detection — with ERP, DCS and AI-driven asset performance models on a single platform. The novelty lies not in any individual component, but in the end-to-end architecture: robot-acquired field data continuously enriching a digital asset health foundation, with AI and physical models closing the loop from data to action. This model represents a scalable blueprint for augmenting reliability engineering workflows across GCC operating facilities. The paper closes with a discussion of the deployment's limitations, challenges, and future work as the programme moves into its Expand and Commit phases.

title: From Tender to Total Depth: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI Agents Deployed Across Well Construction Planning and Execution
container-title: ADIPEC
d3e85950220b86d6b794d2c08b01b4de2c16e93a.abstract: Abstract Well construction projects face data and decision challenges across two distinct phases: pre-well planning and tender preparation, where manual offset analysis limits coverage and introduces bias; and active drilling execution, where non-productive time (NPT) events demand rapid, data-backed decisions. This paper describes an AI-driven platform that serves the full well lifecycle — automating time and risk estimation during tender preparation, and providing real-time generative AI agent support during drilling execution. The platform integrates 13+ AI and machine learning engines applied to Daily Drilling Reports (DDRs) across two workflow phases. For tender and planning: a transformer-based model classifying drilling activities from operational text in English and Spanish; Monte Carlo simulation for probabilistic time forecasting; a genetic algorithm adapted from multiple sequence alignment techniques to predict operational sequences from historical patterns; a Well Risk Index (WRI) for quantitative, data-driven risk scoring; and hierarchical aggregation from section to campaign level, enabling AFE and P&L scenario construction at tender scale. For drilling execution: a suite of generative AI agents that mine offset cases, rank hypotheses, and deliver remediation recommendations for NPT events including stuck pipe and loss circulation; a location-specific Optimum Fishing Time (OFT) model that replaces global cost rules of thumb with field-calibrated economic thresholds; and a generative AI agent that automates end-of-well report generation from DDR data. The platform is actively used by more than 250 engineers with 38% annual growth, supporting assessment of well construction tenders valued at $10-17 billion annually. Well classification time has been reduced from 8 hours to 20 minutes per well; offset coverage has expanded from the 10-20 wells an engineer can manually review to the full available dataset; data preparation effort has been reduced by 56%; risk assessment is 26 times faster than manual evaluation; and a MENA region tender involving 56 well architectures and 158 sections was completed in at least half the previously required time while evaluating all available offset wells. End-of-well report generation has been reduced from four days to two days. Automated technology identification has been estimated to recover approximately $34.7 million in value per year. P10 well time targets — previously aspirational — are now consistently achievable with actionable steps across the Integrated Well Construction (IWC) portfolio. This paper presents a field-validated, multi-component AI architecture structured around three operational phases — winning work, planning wells, and executing well construction programs — that links time estimation, AFE optimization by constructing scenarios, risk quantification, NPT classification, technology identification, local fishing economics, and real-time drilling event support within a single, data-driven ecosystem. Finally, this solution enables engineers to spend their time in high value activities than in manual excel intensive tasks.

title: Lightweight Digital Twin Fabric: Scaling Asset Intelligence via Progressive Fidelity and Reduced-Order Intelligence
container-title: ADIPEC
df64bf79b74ca58f3ef99d64c50b27057acdde97.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Despite significant capital investment, industrial digital twin initiatives frequently fail to scale across large brownfield portfolios due to unsustainable modeling costs and lifecycle overhead. This paper introduces the Lightweight Digital Twin Fabric(LwDT-Fabric)—a decision-centric architecture that decouples actionable insight from full-physics model dependency. By prioritizing decision relevance over exhaustive fidelity, the framework enables enterprise-scale deployment aligned with ISO 55000 and API 580/581. The objective is a "Right-Sized" digital transformation delivering maximum asset integrity with minimum computational and human overhead. Methods, Procedures, Process The LwDT-Fabric utilizes a progressive, event-driven architecture built on open-standard schemas, including CFIHOS and ISO 15926, to ensure cross-platform interoperability and long-term data sustainability. The architecture is structured across three core pillars: Standardized Twin Templates: Utilizing asset-class libraries to enable rapid instantiation with consistent data models, significantly reducing initial configuration time.Reduced-Order Modeling (ROM): Implementing hybrid physics-informed models that capture decision-critical behaviors—such as vibration anomalies and corrosion progression—while functioning reliably in "noisy" or incomplete brownfield data environments. Progressive Fidelity & Expert Governance A dynamic resolution system where model complexity escalates only when risk thresholds are breached. High-fidelity simulations are activated for complex analysis and routed through an Expert-Validation Layer for human-in-the-loop arbitration. Results, Observations, Conclusions The LwDT-Fabric architecture is engineered for rapid scaling across extensive asset portfolios, providing a defensible blueprint for autonomous enterprise orchestration. Key strategic results and benefits include: Decision-Centric Intelligence: Shifts the operational goal from a "Visual Replica" to a "Decision Engine," prioritizing actionable intelligence over mere model fidelity.Deployment Acceleration: Achieves a projected 4× acceleration in setup speed, reducing deployment from 12-16 weeks to just 3-4 weeks per asset.Engineering Optimization: Projected to reduce engineering effort by approximately 50–55% through reusable Intelligence Templates and decision-focused intelligence.Integrity Velocity: Compresses RBI re-ranking cycles from weeks to hours, moving from static "post-mortem" reporting to live, dynamic governance.Accuracy & Resilience: ROM outputs maintain a projected 85% correlation with observed degradation trends, even in data-sparse brownfield environments.Computational Efficiency: Reduces high-performance computing(HPC) demand by &gt;60%, significantly lowering the digital carbon footprint of the asset estate.Proactive Risk Management: The "Right-Sized" approach ensures that computational and human resources are mathematically aligned with asset criticality, preventing "Pilot Purgatory" and ensuring that high-risk assets receive the necessary analytical depth while maintaining baseline visibility across the entire portfolio. Novel/Additive Information The principal contribution of this work is the transition from model-centric digital twins to intelligence-centric asset decision support. By decoupling model complexity from business value and aligning intelligence depth with asset risk, criticality, and decision value, the Lightweight Digital Twin Fabric (LwDT-Fabric) provides a practical and scalable framework for extending asset intelligence across brownfield industrial facilities. This framework provides global operators with a scalable, open-source blueprint to achieve true digital maturity, ensuring every computational watt and engineering hour is weaponized to protect the facility's bottom line while maintaining uncompromising safety standards.

title: AI-Enabled Maritime Operations: Transforming Safety, Efficiency, and Decarbonization Through Real-Time Fleet Intelligence
container-title: ADIPEC
60f309ca54c33ce36234da56369dd71b92dc0693.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for improving safety, efficiency, compliance visibility, and decarbonization decision support in offshore maritime operations. Vessel daily reports, fuel and lube oil records, machinery hours, HSE observations, defects, inspections, certificates, crew and training data, and emissions indicators are often dispersed across applications, spreadsheets, emails, and document stores. The resulting problem is not lack of data, but difficulty retrieving and interpreting the right evidence when a decision is required. The framework converts verified vessel and company records into an access-controlled maritime knowledge base. For each natural-language question, the system applies validation, metadata filters, hybrid retrieval, reranking, deterministic calculations, grounded generation, source citation, and human verification. Representative questions include abnormal consumption, machinery hours inconsistent with activity, recurring defects, overdue or unverified compliance items, HSE themes, training gaps, and emissions variance. The demonstration indicates that RAG is valuable when it connects records that are normally reviewed separately. Consumption becomes meaningful when combined with activity, weather, machinery configuration, and comparable periods; safety observations become more useful when linked to actions, inspections, and training; and compliance queries can distinguish expiry from an approaching due date or superseded document. The process also reveals inconsistent units, duplicate entries, missing activity codes, and stale records. RAG can therefore provide traceable fleet decision support when it uses approved data, preserves lineage, enforces vessel- and role-based access, and permits a no-answer response where evidence is insufficient. It should reduce manual searching and support earlier intervention, while operational authority remains with competent maritime personnel. The evaluation approach therefore specifies quantitative measures—retrieval precision, citation coverage, calculation accuracy, end-to-end investigation and verification time, manual workflow steps, source-system switches, human correction rate, and user adoption—benchmarked against the same questions completed through existing reports and dashboards. Deployment success also depends on governed source quality, scalable indexing, integration controls, and maintained maritime metadata and taxonomies. Cross-industry controlled and field studies report AI-related productivity or task-time improvements ranging from approximately 15% to 55.8% [11–14]. Given the higher consequence of maritime decisions and mandatory human verification, this paper proposes benchmark-informed initial targets of 25-35% lower end-to-end investigation time and 25-30% lower manual workflow effort, with at least 90% retrieval precision and at least 95% citation coverage. These are acceptance targets for paired trials, not measured fleet outcomes.

title: AI-Driven Video Analytics and Behavioral Safety Intelligence: Enhancing Human-Centered Operational Adaptation in Offshore Support Vessels
container-title: ADIPEC
156e6d6192a3d2679989b73fff7135b74a8cfd47.abstract: Computer vision and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used in industrial Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) management to detect missing personal protective equipment (PPE), restricted-zone entries, and line-of-fire exposure. Early offshore and industrial deployments established the technical feasibility of real-time edge processing and automated safety monitoring (Almadhoun et al. 2020; Tamaazousti et al. 2022). A practical challenge emerges when these systems are scaled across multiple assets: large volumes of detections must be converted into operationally meaningful information. Real-time alerts can support immediate intervention, but isolated detections do not necessarily explain why a behavior recurses or whether the underlying procedure, equipment, or task design contributes to the observed deviation (Corallo and Spingardi 2024; Vukicevic et al. 2024). Traditional HSE responses may treat behavioral deviations primarily as individual compliance failures. Human Factors engineering instead recognizes that task demands, equipment interfaces, and environmental constraints shape worker behavior (Reason 1997). Safety-II similarly emphasizes the difference between prescribed work and operational practice, commonly described as Work-as-Imagined and Work-as-Done (Hollnagel 2014).

title: Consumer Protection in the Digital Economy Era: A Literature Analysis of E-Commerce Regulation in Indonesia
container-title: SKYHAWK : Jurnal Aviasi Indonesia
937ec062869aad0cc56986605e5cdb5b726f0a4b.abstract: The growth of Indonesia’s digital economy has driven a significant transformation in transaction patterns while posing new challenges regarding consumer protection. Although the Consumer Protection Law and Personal Data Protection Law have been passed, they are not considered optimal in responding to the complexity of the digital ecosystem. This research uses a descriptive qualitative approach based on a structured literature review combined with doctrinal legal analysis and thematic synthesis. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of consumer protection regulations in e-commerce transactions in Indonesia by examining legal studies, consumer behavior, and international regulatory comparisons through a literature review approach. The study’s results show that regulatory implementation weaknesses, low digital literacy, insufficiently standardized online dispute resolution mechanisms, and institutional enforcement and supervisory gaps remain important obstacles. Additionally, an overly rigid ex-ante regulatory approach has the potential to stifle digital innovation. Therefore, adaptive, participatory policy reformulation based on the principle of equitable consumer protection is needed.

title: The impact of sensorimotor and cognitive capacity on the kinematic performance of instrumental activities of daily living across the lifespan
dbe6069fe100492c67c43ff90f2b11ccfce543f9.abstract: Abstract Background With advancing adult age, sensorimotor and cognitive capacity (e.g., muscular strength) are declining and limitations in instrumental activities of daily living (iADL) are frequently reported. The translation of individual capacity to iADL performance represents a significant research object not only to better understand everyday life behavior but also to apply preventive measures in time. Due to the submaximal nature of iADL, we aimed to identify transition points, beyond which associations between capacity and performance appear, i.e., iADL stop to be submaximal. Methods A set of sensorimotor and cognitive capacity tests and kinematic analyses of hand movements in different complex kitchen tasks were conducted in a sample of 95 healthy adults with an age span of 18 to 93a. An iADL score was derived from the kinematics using a principal component analysis. Transition point segmented regression analyses were applied to examine the association of capacity and the iADL score. Results Most tests reacted to ageing and (negative) outlier frequencies in capacity and, to a weaker extent, in kinematics increased with advancing age. Transition points were identified in most tests and confirmed our hypothesis but were generally high. The best iADL performance was observed in persons between 42 and 58a despite decreased capacity. Discussion It appeared that iADL can be limited by impaired capacity, but profit from experience that can compensate capacity losses to a certain degree. The high transition points point towards the need for early interventions long before subtle alterations in iADL performance become subjectively observable.

title: Lenguaje, postautonomía y común en Facsímil de Alejandro Zambra
Language, Post-Autonomy, and the Common in Alejandro Zambra’s Facsímil
container-title: Cuadernos de Literatura
7572029dbe3e57062ffd39e9416aba66c1bdf219.abstract: This article examines Alejandro Zambra’s Facsímil through the lens of literary post-autonomy, within the context of informational capitalism and biopolitics. It argues that the work subverts the format of the Chilean university entrance exam, shifting from exchange value to use value through a situated writing that articulates the common. The study concludes that Facsímil reconfigures literature as a space of resistance and collective production.​

title: How artificial intelligence adoption relates to women’s entrepreneurial success in Tunisia
container-title: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
240839ff6fd82ea246285db461aade71b83f333c.abstract: This study examines whether adopting artificial intelligence tools is associated with entrepreneurial success among women entrepreneurs in Tunisia, which business capabilities carry that association, and under what conditions it is stronger. The study uses a cross-sectional survey of 350 women who own, jointly own or principally manage a business that uses at least one AI tool. Respondents were recruited through women’s business associations, incubators and entrepreneurial networks, with quotas by region and sector. The data were analysed with partial least squares structural equation modelling. Four capabilities (operational efficiency, market and customer capability, innovation capacity, and financial readiness) are tested as mediators. Digital skills and institutional support are tested as moderators. AI adoption has a positive direct association with entrepreneurial success (β = 0.200, p < .001). The four specific indirect effects are all positive and sum to 0.330, giving a total effect of 0.530 at mean moderator levels and indicating complementary partial mediation. Market and customer capability is the largest pathway (0.120). Digital skills (interaction β = 0.120, p = .003) and institutional support (interaction β = 0.100, p = .004) both strengthen the direct association. The model explains 62.0% of the variance in entrepreneurial success. Entrepreneurs should start with clearly defined tasks, especially marketing and customer service, and pair adoption with hands-on training. Support organisations can combine tool access with mentoring, practical skills programmes and guidance on responsible data use. The study offers gender-focused evidence on AI and business outcomes in Tunisia, a setting where earlier SME studies do not report results by owner gender. The findings are associations within a sample of AI users and need longitudinal testing before causal claims are made.

title: Can digital infrastructure construction promote the synergy between pollution and carbon reduction? A quasi-natural experiment based on the “Broadband China” pilot policy
container-title: Digital Economy and Sustainable Development
8e4dcb9cc4cf25002687788870cd9b49fc87f5c5.abstract: Abstract Digital infrastructure (DI) presents a critical opportunity for China to address the dual challenges of climate change and environmental pollution. In this study, we empirically investigate the effects and mechanisms of DI on the synergy between pollution and carbon reduction (SPCR) using balanced panel data from 273 Chinese cities during 2011–2023. The results reveal that DI significantly reduces CO 2 and SO 2 emissions, thereby promoting SPCR. The mechanism analysis shows that DI facilitates synergistic governance by limiting the entry of heavily polluting enterprises and increasing government expenditure on environmental protection. Heterogeneity analysis suggests that the synergistic effects of DI are more pronounced in cities with small and medium size, high digital innovation capacity, advanced economic development, and greater government digital attention. This study clarifies the micro- and macro-mechanisms through which DI empowers cities to achieve SPCR, and provides empirical evidence and policy implications for improving DI construction and promoting urban green transformation.

title: Brain Tissue Proportionality and General Cognitive Ability Across Three Adult Cohorts
a34e4de781115c698ea0e18eaae41c1c80102edd.abstract: Abstract General cognitive ability may relate to the proportional allocation of brain tissue beyond overall tissue volume. We examined five FreeSurfer compartments using compositional data analysis: cortical gray matter, cerebral white matter, subcortical gray matter, total cerebellum, and brainstem. Human Connectome Project Young Adult data (HCP-YA; N = 1,101) provided discovery estimates; the Dallas Lifespan Brain Study (DLBS; N = 418) and Amsterdam Open MRI Collection ID1000 (AOMIC; N = 926) provided independent cohort tests. Four isometric log-ratio coordinates represented composition, with age, sex, and log total analyzed tissue volume included separately. Composition explained additional cognitive variance in DLBS (partial R² = 4.20%, p = .00154) and AOMIC (partial R² = 1.35%, p = .014). The total-cerebellum-to-cerebral-white-matter contrast selected in HCP was positive in both replication cohorts: standardized β = 0.162 (heteroskedasticity-robust 95% confidence interval 0.072–0.252) in DLBS and 0.097 (0.024–0.170) in AOMIC. Participant-pairs bootstrap intervals supported both associations. Replacing total tissue volume with estimated intracranial volume attenuated the AOMIC association, whereas including both preserved it. Relative macroanatomical allocation is associated with broad cognitive ability conditional on analyzed tissue volume, with differing effect magnitudes across cohorts. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causal tissue trade-offs.

title: Peer Review Report For: Measuring and analyzing the impact of oil price shocks on domestic public debt in the Iraqi economy for the period (2004-2026) using the Nonlinear Distributed Slower Auto regression (NARDL) model [version 1; peer review: 1 approved, 2 approved with reservations]
Capitalization effects of digital infrastructure in Chinese cities: agglomeration, accumulation and technovation
container-title: Digital Economy and Sustainable Development
d9ba2633954e0bc32897f3e8233148214c4a38e9.abstract: Abstract The construction of digital infrastructure requires substantial capital investment from both the government and private sector. A key question arises: to what extent do these investments contribute to economic growth and welfare? This paper investigates this issue through the lens of the capitalization effect. Specifically, we leverage China’s “Broadband China Pilot Policy” as a quasi-natural experiment in digital infrastructure development and employ panel data from 298 cities between 2010 and 2021. Using a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) approach with two-way fixed effects (TWFE), we empirically establish the presence of a significant capitalization effect. Furthermore, we examine several potential mechanisms associated with the capitalization effect, focusing on population agglomeration, capital accumulation, and technological innovation. The results provide suggestive evidence that these factors are potential channels through which digital infrastructure may affect urban housing markets. To quantify welfare implications, we construct a partial equilibrium framework and integrate an LSTM-based deep learning model for predictive analysis. Furthermore, our partial-equilibrium analysis provides a model-implied monetary assessment of the potential welfare implications of digital infrastructure investment, while acknowledging the limitations of interpreting housing-price capitalization as direct welfare gains. This study provides valuable insights for digital infrastructure investment decisions in developing countries.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Spinal Diagnostics: Advances, Challenges and Future Directions
container-title: Journal of Orthopaedic Science and Research
700ffd496071a273b6b60d2ae041215542ea8886.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in spinal diagnostics, particularly through machine learning and deep learning applied to medical imaging and clinical data. These technologies may improve the detection and classification of spinal disorders, automate image interpretation and support clinical decision-making. This narrative review summarizes current applications of AI in spinal diagnostics, focusing on methods for detecting spinal cord injuries, spinal tumors, degenerative spine diseases and vertebral fractures, as well as predicting treatment outcomes and postoperative complications. It also examines convolutional and recurrent neural networks, automated image segmentation and other machine learning approaches for analyzing spinal images and clinical information. Available evidence suggests that AI models can perform comparably to conventional methods and expert assessments and may exceed them in some settings. However, implementation remains limited by challenges related to dataset quality and diversity, model generalizability and interpretability, data privacy and regulatory and ethical considerations. This review highlights both the clinical potential of AI and the major barriers to its integration into routine spinal diagnostic practice. Further prospective validation, external testing across diverse patient populations and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to establish the clinical utility and ensure the safe implementation of AI-based spinal diagnostic tools.

title: Predicting teachers’ intentions to implement bring your own device and take-home student device programs: a cognitive-affective-behavior framework with sem-ann analysis
container-title: BMC Psychology
c08c91f3c76828a754da5e52d4925d2b352b6979.abstract: Abstract Background Limited attention has been given to teachers’ intentions to implement Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) and Take-Home Student Device (THSD) as an integrated digital learning initiative, particularly from a psychological perspective. Accordingly, this study examines K-12 teachers’ behavioral intention to implement BYOD​ and ​THSD​ programs using the Cognitive–Affective–Behavior (CAB) framework. Methods A survey was conducted with 176 K-12 teachers in Taiwan. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN) analysis, and Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). Results Understanding, ability, and self-confidence were positively associated with behavioral intention. Self-confidence mediated the relationships between the two cognitive factors and behavioral intention. In addition, the IPMA results showed that ability had the highest importance value, followed by self-confidence, whereas understanding showed the highest performance but the lowest importance. Conclusions The findings suggest that teachers’ readiness to implement BYOD and THSD depends not only on their understanding of the programs but also on their perceived ability and confidence to manage the demands of implementation. The study extends CAB-based research on educational technology implementation and provides implications for teacher preparation and digital education policy.
