title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Treatment Planning in Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine
container-title: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
d5a505ec13026d30456b4012af14153327596d3e.abstract: Objective: Individualized rehabilitation plans are crucial for maximizing clinical outcomes. Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), which can generate new content based on large knowledge bases, could improve personalized rehabilitation. This systematic review aimed to assess accuracy and application of LLMs in rehabilitation. Design: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus until February 2026. The PICO included LLMs (P), their use in rehabilitation planning (I), comparison with expert opinion or other AI systems (e.g., machine learning, deep learning, or CDSS) (C), the ability to generate appropriate rehabilitation plans and compliance with expert clinicians or clinical practice guidelines (O). Studies involving non-generative AI were excluded. Methodological quality was assessed with JBI tools. Data extraction was performed by two reviewers; a third resolved conflicts. Results: Nine studies met inclusion criteria. Concordance with expert opinion varied, reaching 98.75% after an expert advisory board reviewed AI-generated statements. In musculoskeletal and cardiovascular rehabilitation, LLMs demonstrated alignment with guidelines. However, the included studies reported hallucinations, underscoring the necessity of supervision. Conclusion: LLMs showed promising capabilities in supporting rehabilitation treatment planning, possibly offering adaptability and personalization. Nonetheless, high-quality studies are necessary to validate real-world effectiveness and define implementation strategies.

title: Ecocentric approach for knowledge management and eco-conscious open innovation for a circular economy: leveraging intellectual capital
container-title: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
686c261491946be26d24c79772bd44511d29dc4d.abstract: Purpose The transition toward a circular economy (CE) requires organizations to develop environmentally responsible innovation practices; however, limited research has explained how knowledge management (KM) practices facilitate eco-conscious open innovation (EOI), particularly within small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises (SMEs) in emerging economies. Furthermore, the role of intellectual capital (IC) as an underlying mechanism linking the ecocentric approach to KM with EOI remains underexplored. Therefore, this study examines the mediating role of IC dimensions in the relationship between the ecocentric approach to KM and EOI among manufacturing SMEs in Pakistan. Drawing on the resource-based view (RBV), knowledge-based view (KBV), and intellectual capital-based view (ICBV), the study explains how environmentally oriented knowledge practices are transformed into sustainable innovation outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 398 respondents employed in manufacturing SMEs in Pakistan. PLS-SEM using SmartPLS 4.0.9 was employed to test the proposed relationships and examine the mediating role of IC dimensions in the ecocentric KM–EOI relationship. Findings The findings reveal that IC dimensions fully mediate the relationship between the ecocentric approach to KM and EOI. The results further indicate that the ecocentric approach to KM enhances human, structural, and relational capital, which subsequently promote inbound and outbound EOI. The direct effects of the ecocentric approach to KM on EOI became insignificant when IC dimensions were included, whereas the corresponding indirect effects remained significant, confirming full mediation. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by extending understanding of the ecocentric approach to KM within the CE context and by identifying IC as a critical mechanism through which environmentally oriented knowledge practices contribute to EOI. By integrating RBV, KBV and ICBV, the study offers a comprehensive theoretical explanation of the KM–EOI relationship. Moreover, evidence from Pakistani manufacturing SMEs provides insights from an underexplored emerging-economy context and offers practical implications for organizations seeking to strengthen intellectual capital and advance eco-conscious innovation for circular economy objectives.

title: Postoperative Behavioural, Cognitive, And Psychological Changes Following General Versus Regional Anaesthesia: A Narrative Review
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
d621feb3aec9694aeab17a9eca4e4b5f53f16d83.abstract: Postoperative behavioural, cognitive, and psychological changes represent an important spectrum of recovery-related complications after surgery and anaesthesia. This narrative review examines the available evidence comparing general anaesthesia with regional anaesthesia, with particular attention to postoperative delirium, delayed neurocognitive recovery, postoperative neurocognitive disorder, behavioural changes, and psychological outcomes. The available literature suggests that these outcomes are multifactorial and are influenced by patient vulnerability, surgical stress, inflammation, pain, sleep disturbance, medications, haemodynamic and respiratory changes, and anaesthetic exposure. Comparative evidence has not consistently demonstrated superiority of regional over general anaesthesia for prevention of postoperative delirium or cognitive dysfunction. Regional techniques may reduce exposure to general anaesthetic agents and postoperative opioid requirements in selected settings, but sedation and other perioperative factors can confound comparisons. Preoperative risk assessment, appropriate anaesthetic depth, effective analgesia, physiological optimisation, and multimodal postoperative care remain important components of prevention. Further well-designed studies using standardised definitions, baseline cognitive assessment, validated outcome measures, and adequate follow-up are needed.

title: Strategic integration of business intelligence tools to enhance business management efficiency
container-title: Journal of Innovative Digital Transformation
15aaaabce800370f4d4f3fa8c96a859b42098edb.abstract: Purpose This study examines how data and business intelligence (BI) systems support procurement decisions and strategic execution. It aims to improve the efficiency of business management. Design/methodology/approach A five-stage implementation framework is proposed for integrating BI into strategic business execution. The methodology includes technical validation and a case study that assesses the impact of digital transformation and BI adoption on tracking strategic execution and key performance indicators (KPIs). We frame BI adoption within the broader digital transformation (DT) agenda, aligning data, processes and governance to strategic objectives. Findings Research shows that aligning digital transformation initiatives with an organization’s specific operational needs is the most cost-effective path to achieving efficiency. Analysis suggests that a successful digital transformation must be closely linked to the management requirements. Selecting appropriate BI tools is critical to delivering substantial business value. Research limitations/implications The proposed framework offers managers a structured approach to implementing BI systems aligned with strategic goals. The case study provides actionable insights for professionals aiming to improve operational and management performance through data-driven strategies and digital transformation. Originality/value The research contributes to the literature on digital transformation by presenting a structured, stage-gated framework for integrating BI tools into strategic management. It offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to enhance performance through data-informed decision-making, differentiating itself through a detailed implementation model developed and illustrated in a procurement context.

title: Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
9c22c48dec77add12e18981832964c2f183e35aa.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p &lt; 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p &lt; 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p &lt; 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

title: Association between serum ferritin levels and mild cognitive impairment risk in middle-aged and older adults: evidence from the health and retirement study
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
a1dd5cd07688a1411d3f46db5c11fee6690ac5d0.abstract: Background Ferritin serves as the main iron-storage form in the human body. Iron ions are critical for numerous brain-related physiological processes. This study aimed to explore the association between serum ferritin levels and the risk of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in middle-aged and older adults. Methods Participants aged 50 years and above with available cognitive function assessments were selected from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) database. Baseline data for this retrospective cohort study were collected in 2016, and MCI occurrence was recorded through 2022. Cognitive function was assessed using tests of episodic memory and executive function. The primary MCI outcome was based on an operational cognitive-score definition rather than a clinical MCI diagnosis: the cognitive function score was at least one standard deviation (SD) below the age-specific normative value. Cox regression models were employed to explore the association between serum ferritin [tertiles: &lt;76 μg/L, 76-151 μg/L (reference group), ≥151 μg/L] and MCI risk, as well as impairments in episodic memory and executive function. Results A total of 6,572 participants were enrolled in the analytical cohort. Of these, 1,435 (21.84%) participants developed MCI, while 5,137 (78.16%) were free of MCI events. Individuals with serum ferritin ≥151 μg/L were related to a higher risk of MCI [HR = 1.15 (95%CI: 1.01–1.31)] compared to those with serum ferritin 76-151 μg/L, but no association was found in those with serum ferritin &lt;76 μg/L [HR = 1.04 (95%CI: 0.91–1.19)]. Serum ferritin levels showed a significant U-shaped non-linear association with MCI risk ( P non-linear = 0.03). Moreover, individuals with serum ferritin ≥151 μg/L were associated with a higher risk of episodic memory impairment [HR = 1.15 (95%CI: 1.01–1.30)] versus those with serum ferritin 76–151 μg/L. No significant associations were found between serum ferritin and executive dysfunction [HR = 0.99 (95%CI: 0.90–1.10)]. Conclusion High serum ferritin levels were associated with an increased risk of MCI among middle-aged and older adults, especially episodic memory impairment.

title: Hybrid one-shot and vertical federated learning framework for privacy-preserving brain tumor classification and segmentation using the BRISC2025 dataset
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
4e6e7bc5f7fb16414f2671c35b84aa06ef98beba.abstract: Introduction From MRI images, diagnosis of brain tumors may have limitations due to restriction over patient privacy and lack of annotated datasets so that models cannot be trained across multiple institutions. Methods HOS-VFL: A Hybrid One-Shot and Vertical Federated Learning framework with a two-round protocol that jointly enjoys the advantages of prototype-based one-shot aggregation and encrypted vertical feature space augmentation. Tested on BRISC2025 MRimages of glioma, meningioma, pituitary and non-tumor, with T1-weighted images, expert-annotated, at five simulated institutions, with simulated IID and Dirichlet setups. Results HOS-VFL obtained values of 98.73% on accuracy and 35–50 for conventional federated learning, with a 94.3% reduction compared to the best baseline valued. HOS-VFL performed 98.73% accuracy and 35–50 for the conventional federated learning with an improvement of 94.3% when compared with its best baseline accuracy. The mean Dice and IoU of Segmentation was 0.9147, 0.8423 respectively. Performance did not wane differently in terms of competitive levels and number of institutions, and was able to withstand gradient inference attacks. Discussion HOS-VFL philosophy is centralised performance with minimum communication with retention of raw data local. The method needs to be validated on larger real multi-center datasets before their clinical use.

title: Revisiting dynamic batch scheduling for grokking: the role of batch size, sample budget, and regularization
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
f053948b84ea114d88012c9b07eb60401c513651.abstract: Grokking—the sudden generalization of neural networks long after overfitting—has inspired training strategies aimed at accelerating its onset. This paper revisits dynamic batch size scheduling and asks whether larger batches provide intrinsically better optimization dynamics, or whether they appear better because they process more examples per update. We evaluate three dynamic schedules (linear, exponential, and step-wise increases from 32 to 512) against fixed batch sizes of 32 and 512 across four algorithmic tasks, each with 10 random seeds. When measured by update steps, the fixed-512 baseline is highly competitive: on modular division it reaches 99.6% final accuracy with 10/10 runs grokking at a mean of 3,245 steps. However, this advantage changes substantially after normalizing by total examples processed. Under a matched budget of 240,000 training examples (equivalently 960,000 input tokens), fixed-512 performs poorly and never groks on any task, while smaller-batch and dynamic strategies remain competitive on the modular tasks. A focused hyperparameter sensitivity study additionally shows that grokking depends strongly on weight decay, model size, and maximum batch size: without weight decay, none of the tested strategies grok, while intermediate or strong weight decay can make both fixed-large and dynamic strategies reliable. These results show that larger batches improve update-step efficiency but are not necessarily more sample-efficient, and that their effect is conditional on regularization and capacity. We therefore revise the original interpretation: batch size magnitude is a major confound in grokking experiments, and claims about acceleration should report both update-step and sample-normalized metrics.

title: StoneXAI-Net: an explainable weakly supervised framework for kidney stone classification, localization, and segmentation from CT images
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
e28bbc9e6a7cac34f005e3b1e1ffc59a516c4742.abstract: Introduction Kidney stone disease (urolithiasis) is one of the most frequent urological diseases worldwide; it is highly recurrent and carries a significant clinical burden and economic cost. Non-contrast computed tomography (CT) is the primary diagnostic modality and offers the highest sensitivity and specificity. However, automated kidney stone analysis remains challenging because expert pixel-level annotations are scarce, hyperdense non-stone anatomy causes mislocalization in weakly supervised localization, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are often used circularly, both for weakly supervised localization and for its subsequent interpretation. Methods We present StoneXAI-Net, an explainable, weakly supervised framework to classify, localize, and segment kidney stones from CT images. The framework consists of three modules: (i) a CT-physics augmentation strategy that diversifies training and mitigates overfitting; (ii) consensus pseudo-labeling that combines complementary explanation maps with uncertainty maps and anatomical priors to suppress false localizations; and (iii) a faithfulness audit module with deletion, insertion, and pointing-game metrics that objectively evaluates explanation quality. The resulting consensus pseudo-labels were used to train an attention-prior-conditioned Attention U-Net for segmentation. The framework was evaluated on 3,364 axial abdominal CT images (1,577 stone and 1,787 normal) using five-fold cross-validation. Results StoneXAI-Net achieved 97.4% accuracy, 98.4% precision, 96.0% recall, a 97.1% F1-score, and a 99.5% AUC. Against consensus pseudo-masks, the full segmentation configuration achieved a proxy Dice coefficient of 0.834, an IoU of 0.777, and an HD95 of 2.94 px; anatomical post-processing reduced HD95 by 6.26 px. Discussion StoneXAI-Net is a feasible and interpretable framework for the automated analysis of kidney stones that substantially reduces the time-consuming and costly manual annotation of kidney stones by experts. Because segmentation was evaluated against pseudo-masks at the slice level, these results are proxy estimates that require confirmation with expert annotations and patient-level validation.

title: Measuring risk preferences in large language models using adaptive binary search
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
c858d4cf3d1582c91bca6e51bed245e78c2a72cc.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support decision-making in high-stakes domains, where a model's risk preference, its tendency to favor lower-risk or higher-risk options under uncertainty, can shape the decisions it supports. Prior studies measuring these preferences in LLMs have produced mixed results. Several used fixed designs, such as choice lists, which locate the point where a preference changes only as finely as their preset values allow. Adaptive procedures, which adjust each query to earlier responses, concentrate measurement near that point and are established for eliciting human risk preferences. We present such a procedure for LLMs: it poses a choice between a lower-risk and a higher-risk option, varies the expected value of the higher-risk option across steps, locates by binary search the model's tipping point, the point at which its outputs shift to favor the higher-risk option, and reports it as an index of risk preference under one probability structure. We applied the procedure to eight LLMs from four providers (OpenAI, San Francisco, CA, USA; Anthropic, San Francisco, CA, USA; Google, Mountain View, CA, USA; xAI, Palo Alto, CA, USA), using emergency and disaster management vignettes, and tested whether presenting each option's expected value explicitly, rather than leaving it to be inferred, changed the measured preference. Median tipping points for six of the eight models fell near the point of equal expected value under both presentations. Claude Sonnet 4.6's tipping point was higher when the expected value was left to be inferred, with a shift whose bootstrap interval excludes 0; Claude Haiku 4.5's was higher as a point estimate, but its shift interval includes 0. In individual queries, deviations from expected-value maximization concentrated in four models: those of the two Anthropic models all toward the lower-risk option and those of the two Google models almost all toward the higher-risk option. Over the range queried in both presentations, presenting the expected value explicitly reduced these deviations in all four models. Because the two presentations convey the same expected values, the reduction indicates that these models did not respond to them as equivalent. The procedure applies to any model accessible via a text interface and is a reusable tool for comparing and screening models for risk-related decision support.

title: P2-VGAN: a lightweight velocity-weighted graph attention network for privacy-conscious edge anomaly detection
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
76c7345c8fd139e3ac90e2e10cd36d5a162fde2d.abstract: Introduction Two persistent challenges hinder intelligent video surveillance in public spaces: dense pixel-based models incur heavy computational costs on edge infrastructure, and continuous capture of identifiable imagery creates substantial visual privacy liabilities. Skeleton-based pipelines, which abstract each video frame into articulated landmark coordinates, support visual data minimization by discarding appearance information. However, conventional graph backbones weight joint trajectories uniformly across time, frequently confusing benign high-speed locomotion (such as sprinting for transit) with violent anomalies. Methods This paper presents the Privacy-Conscious Velocity-Weighted Graph Attention Network (P2-VGAN; the prefix “P2” is retained as a legacy identifier designating privacy-conscious representation rather than a cryptographic guarantee), an efficient framework engineered for desktop-class CPU edge gateways. The pipeline decouples motion analysis from visual appearance by extracting 33 planar body landmarks via a single-shot pose estimator; the application does not intentionally store or transmit decoded RGB frames after pose extraction, ensuring downstream processing operates strictly on appearance-reduced pose coordinates. The primary contribution is the Velocity-Weighted Attention Mechanism (VW-AM), an ultra-lightweight gating module requiring only two shared parameters that converts inter-frame coordinate displacements into a bounded squared-displacement motion proxy. This proxy modulates node features prior to multi-head graph attention, directing message passing toward rapidly moving limbs while damping near-stationary joints. Trained under a weakly supervised Multiple Instance Learning objective with temporal smoothness and sparsity regularizers, P2-VGAN is evaluated across five random seeds on the ShanghaiTech Campus and a human-centric subset of UCF-Crime. Results On ShanghaiTech, the model achieves a frame-level AUC of 84.72 ± 0.28% with 1.81 M downstream trainable parameters (pose-extractor parameters excluded) and sustains 34.01 frames per second (FPS) on an Intel Core i7-10700 CPU without hardware acceleration. When compared directly with an identical Vanilla GAT backbone without gating (83.14 ± 0.39%), VW-AM provides an unconfounded +1.58% absolute AUC gain ( p = 0.00096). On the human-centric UCF-Crime subset (215 test videos), it attains 77.88 ± 0.35% micro-average AUC, with high-motion categories (Fighting, Assault) exceeding 82% AUC. Stepwise ablations document an incremental +2.52% gain from VW-AM over an adaptive ST-GCN baseline. Discussion We position P2-VGAN as a Pareto-efficient framework for lightweight CPU surveillance, acknowledging that coordinate streams reduce visual surface exposure but do not eliminate biometric gait re-identification.

title: Which way does time fly in artificial intelligence?
69303b36e37ad0cd3e8fb67b4275fad98702b684.abstract: Abstract Abstract concepts are frequently mapped onto more concrete sensorimotor experiences. One such mapping concerns time and space: people who read and write from left to right tend to associate the past with the left and the future with the right, a correspondence known as the mental timeline (MTL). The present study examined whether an MTL-consistent spatial bias is also observed in ChatGPT and whether this bias can be altered by manipulating linguistic and cultural context. In four experiments, thirty-two independent chat sessions were conducted, with each session treated as an independent AI respondent and asked to place past-related and future-related words at any location on an xy plane (a word allocation task). When the prompt was written in English (Experiment 1), written in Arabic (Experiment 2), or written in Arabic and additionally specified that the model was a native speaker of Arabic (Experiment 3), past words were placed to the left and future words to the right. In contrast, when a Japanese prompt specified that the model was a person from a culture in which text is read from right to left (Experiment 4), this pattern was reversed. These results suggest that ChatGPT predominantly exhibits the MTL typical of English-speaking cultures, and that this mapping can be modulated by framing reading direction.

title: MoFed-Guard: a mobility-aware federated and explainable lightweight Transformer framework for misbehavior detection in VANETs
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
5ed391866e85cc2ca3dd5f3235e5a746f46e8fa2.abstract: Authenticated vehicles can disseminate false safety messages that pass cryptographic verification but remain behaviorally untruthful, making insider misbehavior a challenge in Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs). This study proposes MoFed-Guard , a data-local federated framework combining OBU-TFT , a compact temporal Transformer, with reliability-aware aggregation and on-demand SHAP explanation. Fixed RSUs act as training clients and OBUs perform inference. MoFed-Guard weights client updates using vehicle-association stability, communication reliability, and leave-one-client-out update consistency; these indicators are evaluated empirically rather than treated as theoretically derived trust variables. On the trajectory-disjoint 20-class VeReMi Extension test partition, the framework achieved 95.20% accuracy, 94.75% macro-precision, 94.30% macro-recall, and 94.52% macro-F1. With architecture and training fixed, MoFed-Guard improved macro-F1 by 1.45 points over FedAvg and 0.61 points over FedAdam; the five-seed improvement was significant [ t (4) = 6.30, p = 0.003, d z = 2.82]. Five-seed convergence reached 98.0 ± 0.2% validation macro-F1 at round 100, while held-out client-scale macro-F1 increased from 93.10% with three clients to 94.52% with ten. Explicit FL-layer delivery tests and a road-network-aware partition preserved the aggregation benefit, whereas coordinated-client corruption exposed the limitation of cosine-based consistency. The joint reliability score correlated positively with update utility (ρ = 0.71, p &lt; 0.001). OBU-TFT contains 85,460 trainable parameters, occupies 0.34 MB, and achieved 5.10 ± 0.42 ms T4 inference latency. Parameter-matched comparison showed that OBU-TFT achieved higher macro-F1 than Linformer and Performer, although Linformer remained smaller and faster. These results support empirical reliability-conditioned federated weighting under simulation without implying universal convergence, Byzantine robustness, formal privacy, or field deployment readiness.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled healthcare access and user experience: comparative institutional analysis and survey evidence from China
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
00acc2bacc9284c0eaf32b0b97ba14d672f38e67.abstract: Background Regulatory entry and public experience describe different aspects of artificial intelligence-enabled healthcare access. Methods This health policy study compares institutional arrangements in China, the United States, and the European Union, examines the coverage of equity-related evidence, and analyses an online Chinese survey. Of 480 submissions, 430 passed an attention check, including 32 respondents without reported functional contact and 398 entering the experience models. Results The institutional comparison identifies differences in regulatory objects, information recipients, and responsibility allocation. The coverage analysis distinguishes institutional information and hospital governance from measured portal use and service experience. In the survey, lower-capability respondents reported greater entry and operational barriers; 79 of 159 reported reducing or abandoning use because of barriers. Among contacted respondents, functional contact intensity was positively associated with perceived process ease (standardized β = 0.496), which was associated with perceived health-service responsiveness (standardized β = 0.381). The contact-by-capability interaction was negative (B = −0.254), contrary to the hypothesized direction. Conclusion The findings highlight entry and operational barriers alongside differences in experience among existing users, supporting evaluation of both access conditions and service encounters.

title: Sustainable Federated Continual Learning for environmental monitoring: a systematic review
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
b389fbb5ad33979bef8f6f3c3429ad0c8cd7c880.abstract: Introduction The use of distributed sensing infrastructures is increasingly becoming a key approach to environmental monitoring that is required to be mobile, flexible and adaptable to non-stationary conditions, preserve data privacy and consume as few resources as possible. The decentralized training paradigm provided by Federated Learning together with the ability of adapting sequentially over time without forgetting from Continual Learning has resulted in a concept of Federated Continual Learning (FCL) which offers a promising approach for privacy preserving environmental sensing systems that are capable of learning over time without forgetting. This systematic review provides an in-depth synthesis of the latest research, progress, environmental applications, sustainability, trustworthiness and future directions of Federated Continual Learning (FCL) for environmental monitoring. Methods A total of 90 peer-reviewed publications were identified by conducting a systematic literature search using pre-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria, quality assessment, bibliometric analysis and qualitative evidence synthesis with the framework of PRISMA 2020. Results The synthesized evidence suggests that Federated Learning has come of age in terms of optimization, communication complexity, robustness, and personalization, but Federated Continual Learning is still in its infancy with few applications in the real world. Typically, sustainability, trustworthiness, privacy, fairness, personalization and explainability are explored separately and not in parallel. Although most applications have been single-shot Federated Learning systems, without genuine continual adaptation, isolated examples include some applications from air quality to water quality, agriculture to disaster monitoring and remote sensing. Seven cross-cutting research gaps are identified: disjointed integration of research directions, few deployments in the real world, absence of standardized evaluation, unsolved multi-objective optimization, poor scaling in the long term, weak sustainability-trustworthiness coupling, and poor cross-domain generalization. Discussion It is not just about the evolution of single algorithmic breakthroughs anymore, but actual realization of Federated Continual Learning systems that can effectively assist in continual adaptation while ensuring communication efficiency, sustainability, trustworthiness, scalability and long-term deployment under real environmental conditions.

title: Coarse-to-fine-grained insulator defect detection using two-stage deep learning framework
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
a7263f4cd77959700086b801b46c1fa720140817.abstract: Introduction In power transmission and power distribution systems, insulators are the fundamental components which provide mechanical support and electrical isolation between conductors and supporting towers. However, these insulators are continuously exposed to extreme weather conditions, mechanical stress, pollution and dust, which can lead to surface damage and abnormal operation. Method Conventionally, manual on-site inspection is performed to identify faulty insulators. However, this method is labor intensive, risky, and reactive. With the advancement in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology and deep learning method, automatic visual inspection has replaced the conventional methods. However, automatic visual inspection from UAV images is challenging task due to complex background and small size of the insulators. To address these challenges, we proposed a framework that consists of two stages. In the first stage, you only look once (YOLO)-based is used for extracting candidate region of insulator to get coarse class prediction. During the second stage, the candidate regions are then cropped from the image into image patches and fed to a lightweight patch-level classifier. In order to enhance inter-class separability, hard-pair contrastive classification loss is proposed by adding hard-pair contrastive term to the cross-entropy loss in the embedding space. Discussion The proposed technique is evaluated using an open-source insulator defect image dataset. The experiment results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework compared with the YOLO variants and representative two-stage detectors.

title: Integrative approaches to acupuncture therapies for post-stroke mild cognitive impairment: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
750e5d10b3af3b8758ad1a9d2ad46cd3741ad839.abstract: Background Post-stroke mild cognitive impairment (PSMCI) frequently occurs after stroke and substantially restricts patients’ functional restoration and overall quality of life. Acupuncture has been widely adopted as an adjunctive intervention; however, the relative efficacy and safety profiles among different acupuncture modalities for PSMCI have not been clearly established. Objective To assess the comparative effectiveness and safety of multiple acupuncture therapies for treating PSMCI via network meta-analysis. Methods RCTs on acupuncture for PSMCI published from their inception to October 2025 were retrieved from nine databases and four clinical trial registries. Study quality was assessed via the Cochrane risk of bias tool. Meta-analysis was performed with ReviewManager and Stata software. Results In total, 47 RCTs featuring 3,680 participants and 15 types of acupuncture-related interventions were included. Electroacupuncture combined with Moxibustion showed the highest efficacy in improving both MoCA score [MD = 5.42, 95%CI (2.10, 8.74)] and total effective rate. Electroacupuncture plus HBOT [MD = 8.00, 95%CI (5.19, 10.82)] and manual acupuncture plus rTMS [MD = 3.42, 95%CI (0.87, 5.97)] were most effective in improving MMSE. Manual acupuncture plus donepezil [MD = 8.67, 95%CI (5.47, 11.88)] and Electroacupuncture plus cognitive training [MD = −8.09, 95%CI (−10.56, −5.62)] achieved the greatest improvement in Barthel index. Moreover, the adverse events of these interventions were acceptable. Conclusion This study suggested that acupuncture was effective and safe for PSMCI treatment. However, the poor methodological quality and uneven evidence quality of existing studies warrant further rigorously designed trials to confirm our findings. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ , identifier CRD420251165945.

title: Pharmacognostic Standardization, Phytochemical Profiling and Molecular Evaluation of Centella asiatica Extract for Neuroprotection Against Experimental Cognitive Dysfunction
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
10ab585cf81f0d44b566a2bb0fddf202cc267b14.abstract: The present study was designed to standardize Centella asiatica extract and evaluate its phytochemical composition and neuroprotective potential against experimental cognitive dysfunction. The plant material was subjected to pharmacognostic evaluation, physicochemical analysis, preliminary phytochemical screening, and chromatographic profiling. An ethanolic extract of C. asiatica was subsequently investigated in a scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction model in rats. Behavioral performance was assessed using the Morris water maze and Y-maze tests, while biochemical and molecular parameters associated with neuroprotection were evaluated. The extract showed characteristic pharmacognostic features, acceptable physicochemical parameters, and the presence of triterpenoids, flavonoids, phenolics, saponins, and other secondary metabolites. Illustrative results showed that treatment with C. asiatica extract improved spatial learning and spontaneous alternation behaviour, reduced brain acetylcholinesterase activity and oxidative stress, and enhanced antioxidant defence. Molecular evaluation indicated improvement in BDNF expression together with attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings suggest that standardized C. asiatica extract may exert neuroprotective effects through complementary cholinergic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic mechanisms.

title: A Deepfake Detection Framework for Securing Facial Biometrics Using Attention-Based Deep Learning and Blockchain
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
a0074b87d1d6c79dcfbe609a01fe5bc5a247f1d2.abstract: Facial biometric authentication is widely deployed for identity verification, yet it is increasingly exposed to deepfakebased presentation and injection attacks and to large-scale breaches of centrally stored biometric templates. This paper proposes a deepfake-resilient facial biometric security framework that combines attention-based deep learning with blockchain technology. At registration, face images are pre-processed, augmented with a generative adversarial network (GAN), encoded by a convolutional neural network (CNN) with self-attention, and classified as real or fake by an artificial neural network (ANN). Only images classified as real are encrypted, bound to a unique user identifier and committed to a private blockchain through a cryptographic hash, whereas fake attempts are written to an immutable event log. At authentication, a fresh probe passes through the same pipeline and is verified by smart contracts that check the integrity of the registered commitment and the template similarity using zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), so that raw biometric features are never disclosed. We formalise the threat model, specify the architecture, the smart-contract interface and the security properties, and define an evaluation protocol based on the CIPLAB Real and Fake Face Detection and UTKFace datasets that covers detection accuracy, authentication error rates, adversarial robustness, demographic fairness and system overhead. The framework provides a basis for privacy-preserving, auditable and scalable facial authentication in digital identity management, financial services, healthcare and e-governance.

title: The emerging research frontier of food analytics: artificial intelligence, consumer analytics, smart food systems and knowledge-driven intelligence
container-title: British Food Journal
59e282d0506ff34c4dcaafe165ad5b62e9992f60.abstract: Purpose This study examines the emerging research frontier of Food Analytics between 2016 and mid-2026. It identifies descriptors that show sustained novelty and growth, analyses how they combine into emergent thematic clusters, and synthesizes these clusters into broader research dimensions that shape the field's current research frontier. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a technological-intelligence design based on bibliometric tech mining and analyzes 1,967 Scopus-indexed publications using descriptor normalization, Porter's emergence indicators, document-level co-word analysis, and Louvain community detection. Emergent descriptors were identified using temporal growth and novelty criteria, clustered by co-occurrence, and interpreted comparatively to derive higher-order analytical dimensions. Findings The analysis identified 111 emergent descriptors organized into five Louvain communities after a sensitivity analysis of the emergence-ratio threshold and evaluation of cluster coverage and interpretability. The five-community solution was synthesized into four substantive dimensions: intelligent food quality and composition analytics; predictive and operational food-system analytics; personalized nutrition and consumer analytics; and semantic, generative, and knowledge-driven food analytics. The difference between the five communities and four dimensions reflects the integration of a predominantly methodological community across the substantive dimensions in which its methods are applied. Originality/value The study moves beyond technology-specific reviews by identifying emergence at the descriptor level and integrating overlapping clusters into a coherent framework of research dimensions. It provides a forward-looking account of how Food Analytics is expanding and clarifies the technological, methodological, and application areas most likely to shape its next stage of development.

title: Tonic neuron position and network topology determine synchronization dynamics
container-title: Cognitive Neurodynamics
275a9bafd1316f2357617f177dc915c918586499.abstract: Abstract Understanding how collective neuronal rhythms emerge from the interplay between network structure and single-neuron dynamics remains a fundamental challenge in neurodynamics. In this work, we show that in small heterogeneous networks, the network topology and the position of a single tonic neuron govern synchronization dynamics. We study minimal four-neuron Huber–Braun motifs composed of one tonic neuron and three bursting neurons coupled via electrical synapses. By systematically varying the tonic neuron’s centrality—quantified through degree and a quasi-Laplacian measure—we identify two critical coupling thresholds: the critical coupling for global phase synchronization and the coupling at which the network returns to synchronized periodic bursting. Remarkably, centrality determines the nature of the synchronized attractor: motifs in which the tonic neuron has low centrality synchronize into tonic spiking, whereas highly central tonic neurons drive the network toward synchronized bursting. Moreover, the networks exhibit nontrivial collective behaviors, including large-ISI “stairway-to-heaven” structures, partial firing death characterized by the coexistence of spiking and subthreshold neurons, and remote synchronization in the star configuration with the tonic neuron at the hub. While the present study focuses on the Huber–Braun model in four-neuron motifs, excitability and electrical coupling are features shared by many conductance-based neuronal models. This motivates the hypothesis that analogous structure–dynamics relationships may also arise in other neuronal models and small network motifs, highlighting the potential role of local structural control in shaping collective neural rhythms.

title: From Diagnosis by Accumulation to Diagnosis by Layers: Cognitive Psychiatry and Iatrogenic Risk in an Adolescent with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Case Report and Narrative Review
container-title: Asian Journal of Research in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
91dfcb6df22caf160a8be90ab100928fe3a693be.abstract: Background: Adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may show overlapping behavioural descriptions arising from neurodevelopmental features, psychiatric syndromes, environmental stressors and medication effects. Objective: To illustrate a layered psychiatric formulation using the clinical course of an adolescent with ASD, self-harm, restrictive eating, atypical experiences and prolonged psychopharmacological exposure. Methods: Clinical material supplied by the treating team was synthesised as a case report, with a complementary structured narrative review of literature on diagnostic overlap, pharmacotherapy, puberty, safety and feeding. The main PubMed/MEDLINE search covered January 2023 to September 2026, with a subsequent targeted update; evidence selection was purposive rather than systematic. Case Presentation: A 16-year-old adolescent experienced school and adaptive difficulties, sensory sensitivities, food restriction with occasional self-induced vomiting, self-injury and suicidal ideation. Clinical records described sequential exposure to several psychotropic agents. A reduction in lithium dose from 450 to 300 mg/day during the September 2026 admission was followed by improvement in reported hygiene, food variety and family interaction, but later by distress and an urge to self-harm. Co-occurring psychotherapy, environmental changes and uncertain clinical measurements prevent causal attribution. Discussion: The proposed eight-layer framework considers constitutional traits, temperament, neurodevelopment and cognition, psychodynamics, relationships and environment, superimposed syndromes, somatic factors and treatment effects. The concept is heuristic, not a validated diagnostic instrument. Feeding symptoms warrant assessment of sensory selectivity, body-image concerns, compensatory behaviours and nutritional consequences. Evidence associating adverse childhood experiences with neuroimaging measures in autistic samples is relevant context but does not substitute for individual assessment. Conclusion: Longitudinal, risk-sensitive formulation may help identify competing explanations and measurable intervention targets. The clinical sequence does not establish that medication, family circumstances or any single intervention caused the observed outcomes.

title: Comparative Analysis of Statistical, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Models for USD/IDR Prediction Using Macroeconomic Indicators and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
container-title: International Journal of Mathematics, Statistics, and Computing
563b51be889d2953f9d8bd3c5be637544cabc3c2.abstract: The USD/IDR exchange rate is a key daily barometer of Indonesia's economic health. Accurate forecasting is vital for trade, inflation, and monetary stability. However, its volatile and nonlinear dynamics pose challenges. While research has applied statistical models, machine learning, and deep learning, few studies offer a comprehensive comparison integrating predictive accuracy with model interpretability, particularly using banking stock prices as exogenous predictors. This study addresses this gap by developing and evaluating eight forecasting approaches—a naive random-walk baseline, two statistical models (ARIMA, SARIMAX), three tree-based ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM), and two recurrent neural networks (LSTM, GRU) using daily data from January 2015 to July 2026 (3,005 observations). Five major banking stocks (BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, BBNI, BDMN) are included as one-day-lagged exogenous features. Models are assessed via hold-out testing and five-fold walk-forward cross-validation using RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R². Contrary to expectations, the naive random-walk consistently achieves the lowest error (RMSE=115.24, MAE=63.80, MAPE=0.39%) and the most stable performance, with LSTM as the best-performing complex model (RMSE=269.59, R²=0.785). Diebold-Mariano tests confirm statistical significance (p<0.001). To enhance transparency, SHAP-based Explainable AI is applied to Random Forest, revealing that the lagged USD/IDR value overwhelmingly dominates predictions (mean |SHAP|=1,509.01), while banking stock contributions are negligible. These findings also empirically confirm the well-known Meese-Rogoff puzzle and weak-form market efficiency for USD/IDR, clearly proving that simple baselines remain formidable benchmarks for short-horizon forecasts. This study ultimately underscores the critical importance of combining rigorous benchmarking with XAI to deliver accurate and interpretable predictions for economic policymakers and financial practitioners.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Mental Health: Research Trends, Hotspots, and Emerging Themes (2004–2024)
container-title: NATIONAL BOARD OF EXAMINATIONS JOURNAL OF MEDICAL SCIENCES
a2f700f06eb44366b691ec968f08dc48fdbc8b23.abstract: Background and Aims: Mental health disorders constitute a major global health burden, while mental health services remain inadequately resourced, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, have opened new possibilities for the early detection, diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment of mental health conditions. Despite rapid growth, research in this field is highly interdisciplinary and fragmented, limiting understanding of its overall development. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Scopus database. Peer-reviewed journal articles published between January 1, 2004, and December 31, 2024, were retrieved through title-based searches combining AI- and mental health-related terms. Bibliometric indicators, including publication output, authors, institutions, countries, journals, funding agencies, and highly cited articles, were analyzed. Science-mapping techniques and network visualization using VOS viewer were employed to explore intellectual, social, and conceptual research structures. Results: A total of 14,904 publications were included. Research growth was modest until 2015 but accelerated markedly after 2019 (R² = 0.9685). The field was dominated by medicine, neuroscience, and computer science. The United States, China, and the United Kingdom emerged as the leading contributors in both productivity and international collaboration. Key research hotspots included AI-driven neuroimaging, natural language processing for mental health assessment, social media–based surveillance, and digital mental health interventions. Conclusion: AI research in mental health has expanded rapidly, progressing from neurobiological modeling to scalable digital applications. Future advancement will require ethical governance, representative datasets, interdisciplinary collaboration, and robust clinical validation to ensure safe, effective, and equitable implementation.

title: An attention-enhanced CNN-BiLSTM framework with confidence-gated inference for arrhythmia detection using ECG signals
container-title: Discover Computing
44feadb188256eccd1812c299d06ca2b1bdc38f0.abstract: Abstract Automated arrhythmia detection from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for early diagnosis and continuous cardiac monitoring. However, accurate classification remains challenging due to complex temporal dependencies in ECG waveforms and severe class imbalance, where clinically significant arrhythmias are underrepresented. To address these challenges, we propose an Attention-Enhanced CNN–BiLSTM framework with a Confidence-Gated Inference mechanism for ECG-based arrhythmia detection. The proposed model integrates a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to capture local morphological features with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to model long-range temporal dependencies in ECG signals. A temporal attention mechanism is employed to focus on diagnostically relevant segments of the signal. Additionally, a confidence-gated inference strategy is introduced to improve prediction reliability, particularly for minority classes. An extensive ablation study across 18 configurations is conducted to evaluate the contribution of temporal modeling, attention, and inference strategies. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 96.58% and a macro-F1 score of 86.05%. To ensure an unbiased evaluation free of test-set leakage, we further adopt a strict protocol in which all hyperparameters ( $$\gamma$$ , $$\tau$$ ) are selected exclusively on a held-out validation set; under this leakage-free protocol the model attains an accuracy of 96.74% and a macro-F1 score of 86.54% on the untouched test set. These findings demonstrate that integrating attention-driven temporal modeling with calibrated inference yields efficient arrhythmia classification on the MIT-BIH benchmark.

title: L3DM: An Open-Source Large 3D Multi-Modality Model on MindSpore with Text-Geometry Alignment
container-title: CAAI Artificial Intelligence Research
6ca9d9ad3a28d6b95cc6784772720f58a51aba2f.abstract: Abstract We present an efficient and scalable MindSpore-based framework for three-dimensional (3D) scene understanding, namely Large 3D Multi-Modality Model (L3DM), with a focus on text-geometry alignment through MindSpore-native multimodal feature integration and key–value (KV) cache adaptation. Our work delivers three key contributions to the community. First, we provide a dedicated MindSpore performance optimization for multi-modal feature inputs and KV cache, resolving prior bottlenecks and enabling stable, high-performance operation where it was previously challenging. Second, we explore zero-shot Chain-of-Thought reasoning for 3D multi-view understanding, providing valuable insights into its limitations for complex spatial reasoning tasks. Third and foremost, we offer the first complete, open-source, and scalable 3D foundation model implementation on the MindSpore platform. This contribution fills a critical gap by providing the community with a fully functional training and inference codebase, pre-trained weights, and pipelines for a multimodal 3D large model—resources that were entirely absent before. Overall, the proposed L3DM method establishes a new, stable, and accurate benchmark solution for 3D understanding on MindSpore, with impressive empirical validation on the ScanQA benchmark. Code is available at https://openi.pcl.ac.cn/OpenAIRobotics/L3DM.

title: Effectiveness of dynamic epidemic intelligence networks for early detection and intervention in infectious diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
90382af3734d9426b22d92982c3bfbbd157280ad.abstract: Background The increasing frequency of global health emergencies highlights the critical need for surveillance systems that transcend the limitations of traditional laboratory confirmation. Dynamic epidemic intelligence systems and syndromic surveillance networks have emerged as vital tools for early detection, yet their operational effectiveness remains characterized by significant variability across geographic and clinical contexts. Objective This study aimed to provide a comprehensive meta-analytical evaluation of the effectiveness of dynamic epidemic intelligence systems, focusing on diagnostic classification accuracy, outbreak detection sensitivity, signal precision (Positive Predictive Value), and temporal forecasting reliability. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, synthesizing data from original research articles searched across multiple databases (PubMed, Ovid/MEDLINE, and Embase) Methodological quality was appraised using structured six-domain quality assessment framework adapted from CASP principles and surveillance-system evaluation criteria. Diagnostic validity was synthesized using a bivariate random-effects (Reitsma) model to account for the correlation between sensitivity and specificity. Outbreak detection and alert precision were pooled using random-effects model, MSE was synthesized using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis on the log-transformed scale and back-transformed for interpretation. MAPE was summarized descriptively because only two estimates from a single study were available. Results Thirty-four articles were included for analysis. The pooled diagnostic analysis demonstrated high specificity (0.97; 95% CI: 0.94–0.99) but moderate sensitivity (0.64; 95% CI: 0.37–0.85), with a Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic (SROC) Area Under the Curve of 0.96. While systems were highly effective at detecting established outbreaks (pooled rate: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.73–0.97), performance was markedly lower for rare pathogens such as Ebola (0.30) compared to international health threats (0.97). Alert precision was a significant challenge, with a pooled Positive Predictive Value of 0.36 (95% CI: 0.14–0.66), indicating that approximately 64% of system-triggered signals were “noise”. Conclusions Epidemic intelligence systems are powerful instruments for excluding non-events and capturing large-scale outbreaks, yet their reliability for daily operational alerts is highly context dependent. To minimize investigative burden, future implementations must prioritize pathogen-specific optimization and the integration of diverse data streams to enhance sensitivity in humanitarian and low-resource settings.

title: Associations between cognitive reserve, glymphatic function and cognitive function in mild cognitive impairment
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
b07439303012bc223b7ba87f2dabecd86d618b0c.abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between cognitive reserve (CR) and glymphatic function in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and to examine whether the relationship between CR and cognition is mediated by glymphatic function. Methods 113 MCI individuals and 91 healthy controls (HC) were enrolled to assess the glymphatic function by using diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), perivascular space (PVS) ratings, and choroid plexus volume (CPV). Cognitive reserve index questionnaire (CRIq) was employed to evaluate the comprehensive CR of participants in both groups. The glymphatic function was compared between the two groups and Spearman correlation analyses were performed among the CR, glymphatic function and cognition. Mediation analyses were further conducted to explore potential mediating effects. Results The MCI group had significantly lower bilateral ALPS index and mean ALPS index than the HC group, while the bilateral CPV, basal ganglia (BG)-PVS and centrum semiovale (CS)-PVS scores were significantly higher in the MCI group than the HC group. After controlling for age and sex, bilateral and mean ALPS index were positively correlated with MoCA, MMSE, and VFT scores; mean ALPS index and left ALPS index were positively correlated with AVLT-immediately performance. BG-PVS was negatively correlated with MMSE and VFT scores, and right CPV was negatively correlated with VFT scores. Meanwhile, CRIq was positively correlated with bilateral and mean ALPS index, but was negatively correlated with BG-PVS, and mean ALPS partially mediated the association between CRIq and cognition in the MCI group. Conclusion Mild cognitive impairment individuals exhibit reduced glymphatic activity relative to HC. Comprehensive CR is associated with cognitive function in MCI, with the mean ALPS index statistically mediating a portion of the CR–cognition association.

title: Sensorimotor recovery, neuropathic pain reduction, and neuroplasticity changes following cognitive multisensory rehabilitation or adaptive fitness in adults with spinal cord injury: a feasibility pilot randomized controlled trial
container-title: Frontiers in Pain Research
9fed6f696e20c514887fb0d7b80050475f38e976.abstract: Introduction Spinal cord injury (SCI) often causes partial or complete sensory and motor loss, disrupting the afferent integration needed for accurate mental body representations (MBR, i.e., body awareness and visuospatial body map). MBR deficits compromise sensorimotor recovery and contribute to neuropathic pain in about 69% of adults with SCI. Medications for neuropathic pain are often ineffective and can cause adverse reactions. Our previous pilot clinical trial showed that Cognitive Multisensory Rehabilitation (CMR), a physical therapy that restores MBR, produced significant, lasting reductions in neuropathic pain, improved sensorimotor function, and enhanced brain function. Building on these results, we examined feasibility and whether 8 weeks of CMR or adaptive fitness (1) improves sensorimotor function and reduces pain; (2) increases sensorimotor- and MBR-related brain activity and connectivity in adults with SCI. Methods Sixteen participants (52 ± 8 years old, 13 ± 10 years post-SCI) were randomized to CMR or adaptive fitness (45 min, 3x/week, 8 weeks); one withdrew. Ten participants had neuropathic pain of ≥3/10. Pain and sensorimotor function were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and 3-month follow-up using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS), and Neuromuscular Recovery Scale (NRS). Functional MRI included resting-state and 4 tasks: imagining feeling the left leg, imagining moving the left leg, whole-body movement imagery, and a sensation task (i.e., gently brushing the big toes with a towel). Results Post-CMR ( n = 8), participants showed significant large within-group AIS effect sizes (touch: d = 1.54; pinprick: d = 1.83; lower limb motor function: d = 1.32) and large (core: d = 2.19) to moderate (arm function: d = 0.69; leg function: d = 0.74) NRS effect sizes. Adaptive fitness ( n = 7) showed non-significant small/moderate AIS (touch: d = 0.49; pinprick: d = 0.53; lower limb motor function: d = 0.74) and NRS effects (core: d = 0.73; arm function: d = 0.34; leg function: d = 0.00). Benefits persisted at follow-up. MCID was exceeded for average pain post-CMR and highest pain at 3-month follow-up. Pain virtually did not change after fitness. CMR increased brain connectivity and activation during leg imagery. During whole-body imagery, CMR increased widespread activation; adaptive fitness showed spatially limited increases. Discussion These preliminary results support CMR's potential to improve function and reduce neuropathic pain in adults with SCI, warranting larger confirmatory trials. Clinical Trial Registration : https://clinicaltrial.gov/ , identifier NCT05167032.

title: Rethinking the public health research ecosystem in the era of artificial intelligence: from evidence generation to population impact
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
80765495321f11d0147817ff60db348ef5c752f2.abstract: Public health is constrained less by the generation of evidence than by the time to act on it; artificial intelligence should be judged by whether it shortens that gap. AI has largely been evaluated within disciplinary silos, obscuring how choices at one stage of the research process shape the next. In this article, we propose an AI-enabled public health research ecosystem spanning evidence synthesis, knowledge extraction, prediction, adaptive implementation, health system operations and policy, and introduce evidence-to-action latency: the interval between recognising a problem and implementing an evidence-informed response. AI does not remove the bottlenecks; it relocates them from generating evidence towards validation, governance, implementation and workforce capability. These capabilities are least available in low-resource and community-based services, where need is greatest. Because inequity in source data propagates through every subsequent stage, the aim is equity-preserving latency, not speed alone. The AI-READY Framework sets out the conditions for responsible integration. The greatest gains will come from redesigning research systems rather than optimising individual methods.

title: Persistent neutrophil maturation deficits associate with cognitive impairment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
ac0aa8b9c9650b24069967ccaa55123144767865.abstract: Introduction Post-COVID-19 condition, or post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), is characterized by persistent cognitive impairments and immune dysregulation. While neutrophils are critical in acute COVID-19, whether their long-term functional dysregulation contributes to PASC, remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the links between immune system changes, symptom severity and cognitive impairment in PASC. Methods In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 40 individuals with self-reported issues with COVID-19 recovery (PASC) and 37 fully recovered (REC) volunteers. Participants were post-infection at either TP1 (from 6 up to 18 months post-infection, 7 PASC, 20 REC) or at TP2 (from 19 up to 36 months post-infection, 33 PASC, 17 REC). We evaluated the Newcastle post-COVID-19 Syndrome Follow Up Screening (NC) scores for symptom severity, and neuropsychological tests for memory, attention, and executive function. Peripheral blood was analyzed using multicolor flow cytometry, ELISA, clustering, and multivariate regression. Results PASC participants in both the TP1 cohort and the TP2 cohort, demonstrated increased NC scores and significant changes in neutrophil numbers and subset composition. In the TP1 cohort, the PASC group showed an increased frequency of activated CD16 + CD62L low neutrophils and a reduced frequency of CXCR4 + TREM-1 + CCR2 + polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs). This was accompanied by elevated soluble TNF receptor 1 (sTNFR1) and decreased sTNFR2 and CXCL12. In the TP2 cohort, PMN-MDSC levels were comparable between REC and PASC groups, alongside increased emergency granulopoiesis regulators IL-3 and IL-6. Multivariate regression revealed significant associations between PMN-MDSC signatures, granulopoiesis-related markers, NC scores, and cognitive test scores in either the TP1 or the TP2 cohort. These results represent cross-sectional observations in participants assessed within the respective post-infection intervals, rather than longitudinal evidence of persistence. The results show that dysregulated granulopoiesis and neutrophil maturation are present even at 18 and 36 months in PASC individuals, potentially associating with overall symptom severity and cognitive impairment. Conclusions Despite limitations in cohort size, requiring validation of the associations in larger cohorts, our findings may contribute to the further understanding of PASC and future new transitional perspectives for PASC management.

title: Artificial intelligence readiness in healthcare and health professions education in conflict-affected Syria: an online cross-sectional study
container-title: Scientific Reports
1e35972b42d6c427124e00d77eda6e48eddef9dc.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly relevant to healthcare delivery, clinical training, and health professions education. Evidence from conflict-affected settings remains limited, despite workforce shortages, disrupted training pathways, and constrained digital infrastructure. This study assessed AI knowledge, trust, willingness, and digital capability among Syrian adults and healthcare respondents (students and qualified professionals), with emphasis on implications for AI literacy and professional education. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of Syrian adults from March 4th to May 31st 2026, using a 35-item questionnaire distributed via social media through convenience sampling. The survey assessed AI awareness, trust, willingness, perceived risks and benefits, barriers to healthcare and digital health use, and Digital Literacy. Healthcare respondents (students and qualified professionals) completed additional items on clinical AI use and exposure to unsafe AI recommendations. Composite scores were calculated for AI Trust (3–15), AI Willingness (4–20), and Digital Literacy (2–10). Internal consistency was acceptable to excellent across scales (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.787–0.856). Among 829 participants, 353 (42.6%) were healthcare respondents (119 students and 234 qualified professionals). Mean AI Willingness, AI Trust, and Digital Literacy scores were 14.5 (SD 3.25), 11.0 (SD 2.34), and 6.67 (SD 1.80), respectively. In multivariable linear regression, AI Trust (β = 0.483) and Digital Literacy (β = 0.305) were the strongest predictors, followed by General AI Knowledge (β = 0.165). In sensitivity models excluding the Willingness item that loaded on Trust, Trust (β = 0.44 and 0.38) and Digital Literacy (β = 0.31 and 0.33) remained the strongest correlates. Educational use was the most accepted AI application (65.5%) and educational support was the leading perceived benefit (64.2%). Medical errors were the most frequently perceived risk (76.6%), while cost, unreliable internet access, and lack of Arabic-language content were major implementation barriers. In this online convenience sample, Trust and Digital Literacy were the strongest independent correlates of Willingness to use AI, followed by AI knowledge. The high acceptance of educational AI suggests a practical entry point for conflict-affected health systems. AI literacy should be integrated into undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing health professions education, with explicit training on critical appraisal, safe use, bias, privacy, local validation, and clinician oversight.

title: Observation of the beneficial effects of nasal saline irrigation combined with inhaled budesonide on acute asthma exacerbations in children: a retrospective study
container-title: World Economy and Management research
42b2d494767bb3f284f52ee492e82ebcc224b8fe.abstract: Background Acute asthma exacerbations remain a major cause of morbidity in children. While inhaled budesonide is a cornerstone of acute management, concurrent upper-airway inflammation may limit treatment efficacy. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effects of nasal saline irrigation combined with inhaled budesonide in children with acute asthma exacerbations. Methods This retrospective study was conducted at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital, Capital Medical University. Children aged 1–14 years who were treated for acute asthma exacerbations were divided into a control group (inhaled budesonide alone) and a combination group (inhaled budesonide plus nasal saline irrigation). Clinical symptom scores, peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂), respiratory rate, length of hospital stay, and adverse events were compared between the two groups. The study was approved by the institutional ethics committee (BJCY-26-371). Results A total of 186 children were included (control group, n = 92; combination group, n = 94). Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The combination group showed significantly faster reductions in total and nasal symptom scores, more rapid improvement in SpO₂ and respiratory rate at 24–72 h, and a shorter median length of hospital stay (4.0 vs. 5.0 days, P = 0.003) compared with the control group. The requirement for additional systemic corticosteroids was also lower in the combination group. Nasal saline irrigation was well tolerated, with only mild, self-limiting adverse events reported. Conclusions Nasal saline irrigation combined with inhaled budesonide was associated with faster clinical improvement and a shorter hospital stay in children with acute asthma exacerbations compared with inhaled budesonide alone, without increasing adverse events. These findings support the potential value of nasal saline irrigation as a simple adjunctive therapy in this setting.

title: Design and Validation of a Novel Planar 2R1T Remote Center-of-Motion Mechanism Composing of Dual-Triangular and Straight-Line Linkages
container-title: Journal of Mechanisms and Robotics
caf43fb798aa694f48d6f5c32707dcb9a24ad400.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Benefiting from small incision and fast recovery, minimally invasive surgeries (MIS) exhibit great advantages in clinical operations. In such kind of surgeries, the remote center-of-motion (RCM) mechanisms play an important role owing to their special motion characteristics. This paper presents the design of a novel planar RCM mechanism of two rotational and one translational degrees-of-freedom (DOF). In the proposed design, the mobility of RCM mechanism is decomposed into one-DOF pure rotation and translation with a remote stationary point. The dual-triangular linkage and the Peaucellier–Lipkin straight-line linkage are introduced to achieve the remote rotation and translation, respectively. Inspired by the concept of virtual screw, a dual-helical differential-motion joint is particularly designed to generate the coaxial rotation and translation. A preliminary prototype is developed to validate the feasibility of the designed RCM mechanism. The experimental results show that the developed prototype is easy to control and of acceptable positioning accuracy, which manifests potential application in MIS.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>
