The results showed that drip irrigation significantly reduces irrigation water use, improves water use efficiency, and increases cotton yield. The findings provide a scientific basis for the wider implementation of water-saving irrigation technologies in cotton production.</jats:p>

title: OQ AMUR (Ctenopharyngodon idella Valenciennes, 1844) OTA-ONA TO‘DASINING REPRODUKTIV-BIOLOGIK KO‘RSATKICHLARINI TURLI XO‘JALIK SHAROITLARIDA STATISTIK TAQQOSLASH
container-title: Agro ilm
945d92687c6d7953d19a14cadf41191d142af600.abstract: <jats:p>Morphometric and reproductive-biological traits of grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella Valenciennes, 1844) aged 3-5 years (n=540; 270 females, 270 males) reared in 2023-2025 at three farms (one monoculture, two polyculture) were studied. No significant differences in body size were found among farms (p>0.05), whereas gonadosomatic index (GSI) differed significantly among all three farms (Welch ANOVA, F=838.15; p<0.001; Games-Howell post-hoc). Compliance with the GSI≥12% criterion showed an absolute association with farm (100%, 0% and 100%; χ²=226.0; p<0.001). Most importantly, females selected by the GSI criterion significantly outperformed a traditional unselected control group on every reproductive measure ‒ relative fecundity (141.4 vs 111.8 thousand eggs/kg; p=0.023), fertilization rate (86.6% vs 78.0%; p<0.001), hatching rate (80.5% vs 74.1%; p<0.001), and survival to active feeding (75.7% vs 65.0%; p<0.001). These findings experimentally validate the practical effectiveness of GSI-based selection as a scientifically grounded method for forming a high-productivity broodstock.</jats:p>

title: Prevention before Therapy in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: The Clinical, Economic, and Human Case for Weighting Resources Upstream
container-title: Cancer Prevention Research
db55017995932d07ff27e004f693bacf40ed40f6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is projected to become the second leading cause of US cancer death by 2030, and survival is dominated by stage at diagnosis: roughly 44% at 5 years for localized disease versus about 3% with distant metastases. Only about 15% of cases are detected while localized, surgery reaches a minority of patients, and no validated screening test exists for average-risk adults. This topical review examines the biological, clinical, economic, psychologic, equity, and therapeutic evidence bearing on where scarce resources should be directed. The long interval between initiating mutation and invasive disease provides a mechanistic rationale for prevention and interception, and the modifiable exposures of obesity, tobacco, type II diabetes, and alcohol act largely within that window. We consider innovations that extend prevention beyond lifestyle advice—incretin-based weight management, risk stratification anchored in new-onset diabetes (NOD) and biomarkers, and immunoprevention—together with early-onset disease, implementation and policy, and the barriers and evidentiary limits that temper these arguments. We propose a three-tier framework of primary prevention, early detection in high-risk groups, and therapy and argue that research, policy, and clinical investment should be weighted upstream because every case prevented spares the cost, capacity, and suffering that the downstream tiers must otherwise absorb.</jats:p>

title: Human population dynamics as a Bayesian inverse transport problem
container-title: Physical Review E
a22f04ab6ddb828554991b611507f50b6aa1cd27.abstract: <jats:p>Many open problems across physical, biological, and engineered systems involve nonequilibrium transport processes where the governing conservation laws are known, but the underlying constitutive relations remain latent and time varying. Conventional data-driven approaches like deep neural networks capture statistical patterns but routinely violate fundamental mass conservation. Here I introduce a unified Bayesian inverse transport framework that resolves this by embedding Bayesian neural networks directly within exact partial differential equations in age-time space. By evaluating this framework on complex, real-world human cohort advection across China, Japan, and South Korea, I demonstrate that this physical constraint enables consistent uncertainty propagation and missing-data reconstruction from sparse observations. Beyond demography, this framework provides a generalizable foundation for observing and forecasting nonequilibrium boundary dynamics across various fields.</jats:p>

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Practice: How Should Rheumatologists Evaluate and Monitor Emerging Tools?
container-title: Arthritis Care & Research
3f160ed41d422ffb9dd3b8b7e40c689996ef000c.abstract:
<jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used in rheumatology practice, to assist with tasks such as documentation, record summarization, and clinical decision support. Rheumatologists need a practical approach to determining what evidence and oversight each application requires. This narrative review proposes a framework based on two dimensions: contextual complexity and influence on patient care. Greater contextual complexity can make errors harder to detect, whereas greater influence on care increases the potential consequences of an undetected error. We examine evidence for workflow benefits and clinical effectiveness within this framework and consider safety, equity, privacy, governance, and implementation. Existing evidence on the benefits, accuracy, and reliability of AI applications remains mixed. For example, studies of ambient AI scribes suggest reduced documentation burden, but evidence of improved patient outcomes from applications supporting clinical decisions is more limited. For applications with limited clinical influence, evaluation has initially focused on workflow, usability, and documentation quality. Tools that synthesize longitudinal information require additional assessment of completeness and source traceability. Those influencing diagnosis or treatment require prospective evaluation of clinical benefit and safety. Relevant vendor evidence should be assessed alongside proportionate local testing and ongoing monitoring. Safeguards should address risks such as hallucinations, automation bias, and propagating documentation errors, with attention to performance across patient groups. Changes in functionality or clinical use should prompt reassessment. The framework provides a structured basis for adoption decisions and identifies priorities for research on patient outcomes and feasible oversight in routine rheumatology care.</jats:p>

title: Evaluating Human-Robot Interaction With a Socially Assistive Robot in Pediatric Health Care: Mixed Methods Pilot Study
container-title: JMIR Nursing
40e81b1d6d1a4353ac306221b1b097058d049081.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Socially assistive robots are increasingly explored in health care, but evidence from routine pediatric outpatient settings remains limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined how contextual support and human facilitation shaped visitor interaction with the Temi V3 robot and which sociotechnical conditions were associated with practical acceptance according to staff.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A mixed methods pilot combined structured behavioral observation across baseline, poster support, and staff facilitation conditions with 4 staff focus group interviews. The observation unit was a visitor passage through the lobby zone; the qualitative sample comprised 12 staff members with direct exposure to the robot. Quantitative indicators were analyzed descriptively, and staff interviews underwent deductive-inductive qualitative content analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In total, 675 visitor passages (children: n=398, 59% and adults: n=277, 41%) were recorded (baseline: n=257; poster support: n=160; and staff facilitation: n=258). Looking at the robot increased from 8 (3.1%) passages at baseline to 30 (18.8%) with poster support and 80 (31%) with staff facilitation. Screen or app use increased from 2 (0.8%) passages at baseline to 4 (2.5%) with poster support and 14 (5.4%) with staff facilitation. Observer notes indicated stronger visible responsiveness among children, although age category was not linked to individual behavior codes. Staff emphasized role clarity, child and family value, human mediation, functional reliability, multilingual content, and organizational ownership.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Observed visitor interaction was higher with poster support and staff facilitation than at baseline. These descriptive findings and staff perceptions informed a provisional 4-domain framework comprising role clarity, interaction affordance, social mediation, and organizational embedding. The framework identifies potential implementation priorities; visitors’ own experiences and acceptance require direct assessment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: GutBiomeDB: an integrated human gut microbiome database of 168 464 samples
container-title: Nucleic Acids Research
6a4957f03a6eb2a887f369aa8be2cd2b5ff53fce.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The gut microbiome plays an important role in maintaining human health. Despite the rapid growth of literature and publicly accessible data on the gut microbiome, a large-scale, well-curated database integrating a unified matrix with multiple analytical tools is still lacking. Here, we introduced GutBiomeDB, a comprehensive database and analysis platform for the human gut microbiome. GutBiomeDB contains 168 464 samples from 482 BioProjects, spanning 72 countries, 224 disease conditions, and seven life stages. To improve the reusability and accessibility of data, the uniformly processed taxonomic profiles generated by Abdill et al. were reused without reprocessing to construct a matrix of 4680 taxa and 3142 genera, and disease, life-stage, sex, and geographic metadata were manually curated by our team. Additionally, GutBiomeDB offers four tools for in-depth analysis: “Differential Analysis” for comparing diversity and abundance of user-selected cohorts and performing random-effects meta-analysis across projects; “Interaction Network” for comparing disease and healthy-control co-occurrence networks; “Lifecycle Atlas” for visualizing genus trajectories across seven life stages; and “Health Index” for searching similar samples and scoring uploaded genus profiles. GutBiomeDB serves as a versatile and valuable resource for advancing a broad spectrum of gut microbiome research and clinical relevance. GutBiomeDB is freely accessed at https://gutbiomedb.online.</jats:p>

title: Design principle: a broadband achromatic metalens
container-title: Applied Optics
a512e6714105b08b4f090ce0a3c56525269060c9.abstract: We propose a design principle for broadband achromatic metalenses built from a single, simple meta-atom geometry in a dispersive material. The optical path length (OPL) of a meta-atom, rather than its phase, is used as the design criterion: a wavelength-independent OPL is equivalent to a constant group delay with vanishing group-delay dispersion, and it reduces the dispersion-engineering problem to a single scalar figure of merit, the OPL difference (ΔOPL) across the operating band, which can be evaluated directly from a phase library. Among circular and square rods, fishnets, and circular and square holes in a 600 nm thick GaN layer on sapphire, square air holes minimize (ΔOPL) over 450–700 nm. The aperture of the metalens is limited so that the required phase does not exceed 2 π at the longest wavelength, which removes phase wrapping. Metalenses with target focal lengths of 5, 7, and 10 µm and numerical apertures of 0.39–0.54 focus within 2.3% of the targets, suppress the chromatic focal shift of a conventional diffractive lens ( f ∝1/ λ ) by 80%–84%, produce focal spots within 1.12–1.20 times the diffraction limit, and reach absolute focusing efficiencies of 0.46–0.68 within the Airy disk. The design is robust against random critical-dimension variations and sidewall angles up to 6°. The principle can be applied to other transparent dispersive materials and spectral ranges.

title: Physical design of a high-charge beam injector for the on-axis swap-out injection scheme in an electron-positron collider
container-title: Physical Review Accelerators and Beams
43a9b59b54812a876ec0c47348c2aa687b47625d.abstract: The Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF), a next-generation electron-positron collider, adopts an on-axis swap-out injection scheme that demands high-charge electron bunches with exceptionally low emittance and minimal energy spread. This work presents a comprehensive and systematic beam dynamics design for the STCF electron injector. The bunching system, based on subharmonic bunchers and a traveling-wave buncher, is optimized using the nondominated sorting genetic algorithm III to efficiently explore the high-dimensional parameter space. Start-to-end simulations incorporating space-charge forces, wakefield effects, and alignment errors are performed, with beam-based alignment (BBA) applied to correct orbit deviations. The optimized injector delivers 8.5 nC bunches at 3.5 GeV with a normalized transverse emittance below 70 mm mrad and an rms energy spread below 0.5%, satisfying the stringent STCF requirements. The high transport efficiency achieved in simulations alleviates the design pressure on the electron source, while the excellent beam quality inherently suppresses beam halo effects. By integrating systematic multiobjective optimization with high-fidelity simulations, the proposed design overcomes the intrinsic limitations of thermionic cathodes while capitalizing on their proven stability, robustness, and cost-effectiveness, offering an efficient engineering solution for high-charge beam delivery in next-generation colliders.

title: Design criteria for a beam-driven resonant passive transverse deflector for longitudinal beam diagnostics
container-title: Physical Review Accelerators and Beams
940db001e2f0d4f59599bdece793503e9ebdcbcc.abstract: Conventional radio-frequency (rf) transverse deflecting structures provide high-resolution longitudinal beam diagnostics, but require externally generated high-power rf, waveguide distribution, synchronization, and input coupling at the operating frequency. We propose design criteria for a beam-driven resonant passive transverse deflector that does not require an external rf source. A leading drive bunch excites long-range wakefields in an off-axis periodic copper structure and a delayed witness bunch experiences the transverse wake near a zero crossing. The concept is based on the large temporal slope available from high-frequency wake components. A structure designed for installation after the second bunch compressor in the three-bunch-compressor layout of the European XFEL is optimized to place the zero crossing of the drive-bunch-induced transverse wake potential approximately one rf-bucket spacing of the 1.3 GHz linac behind the drive bunch. The selected geometry produces a multimode transverse kick dominated by TM-like modes. We use time-domain wake simulations, frequency-domain decomposition, cell-number scaling, mechanical-tolerance scans, orbit-offset studies, and uniform thermal scaling to determine the operating point and its sensitivity. For this geometry, the zero crossing occurs at s 0 ≃ 230.6 mm , with a per-cell temporal slope of S cell = 1.186 mV / ( pC fs cell ) . For a compact 1 m structure operated with a 250 pC drive bunch and a 700 MeV witness beam, the estimated temporal resolution is about 33 fs .

title: A multi-criteria framework for factor of change assessment to support climate-resilient infrastructure design across Tuscan cities
container-title: Environmental Research: Infrastructure and Sustainability
ede900a6634bf271f90aa2727cfe931120fe190f.abstract: Abstract Global and regional climate models (GCMs and RCMs) provide projections for climate change impact assessments. However, their performance may vary across locations and climate variables, introducing uncertainty into the estimation of future climatic actions on infrastructure. This study presents a multi-criteria framework for evaluating climate-model performance and adapting the factor of change (FC), which describes variations in characteristic values used in structural design. The framework combines extreme value theory, performance indicators, Shannon entropy, three multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods, and a game-theory approach based on the Shapley value. Model performance is evaluated using complementary accuracy and trend indicators against historical observations. Shannon entropy is used to derive indicator weights, while the preference ranking organization method for enrichment evaluation (PROMETHEE-II), the technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS), compromise programming (CP), and the Shapley value are combined to rank and weight the climate models. These weights are then used to calculate an adaptive FC that gives greater influence to models showing stronger historical performance. The methodology is applied to 12 GCM-RCM combinations from the European Coordinated Regional Climate Downscaling Experiment (EURO-CORDEX) across ten Tuscan cities in Italy, considering maximum temperature under the Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) scenarios RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. Model performance is assessed against the European gridded observational dataset (E-OBS). When the maximum adaptive FC across the analysed future time windows was applied to local reference characteristic values, the estimated increases ranged from approximately 3.3 ∘ C– 4.5 ∘ C under RCP4.5 and from 6.3 ∘ C to 7.4 ∘ C under RCP8.5. The adaptive FC preserves the ensemble warming signal while giving greater influence to models that more consistently reproduce historical observations and trends. The proposed framework supports the updating of climatic action maps and climate-resilient infrastructure design and can be extended to other climate variables and cities.

title: ACF-Net: design of an adaptive cross-modal fusion network for cross-subject wearable EEG-EMG gesture recognition
container-title: Journal of Neural Engineering
d6aed9f11ddb0cebe0aa4ff827de686fd733b4de.abstract: Abstract Objective . Cross-subject gesture recognition in wearable brain–computer interfaces is constrained by four structural deficiencies: symmetric cross-modal attention discarding cortical precedence over muscular execution, priors confined to post hoc analysis, invariance anchored on unimodal features, and adaptation requiring labelled target-domain data. This study closes these gaps by embedding corticomuscular coupling directly into the network architecture rather than recovering it from data. Approach . ACF-Net is a four-stage pipeline embedding neurophysiological priors directly into fusion. The corticomuscular coherence prior injection layer encodes time-lagged coherence and phase-locking values for every electroencephalography (EEG)-electromyography (EMG) channel pair as a learnable bias tensor. Granger-causality-inspired directed cross-modal attention uses a causal mask allowing only EEG-to-EMG influence within 30–120 ms. The fused embedding is projected onto a symmetric positive definite manifold with log-Euclidean triplet loss. Physiology-consistent test-time adaptation updates only batch-normalisation affine parameters, using EEG-precedes-EMG as unlabelled self-supervision, eliminating labelled target data. Leave-one-subject-out validation on WAY-EEG-GAL (12 participants) and WEE-Ges (20 participants, three days) used fold-wise priors and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests. Main results . ACF-Net reached 87.6% on WAY-EEG-GAL and 89.2% on WEE-Ges, exceeding the strongest baseline by 9.4 and 9.1 percentage points with all comparisons significant after correction. Ablation attributed gains of 6.3, 4.9, 3.4 and 1.8 percentage points to directed attention, prior injection, manifold embedding and test-time adaptation. Accuracy remained 77.5% under 20 mm simulated electrode displacement, adaptation reduced the cross-day loss from 6.8 to 2.1 percentage points, and a forward pass on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano took 32.4 ms within a 178 ms end-to-end response at 30.9 Hz. Significance . Learned coupling weights recovered central-to-forearm-extensor projection, and delays matched corticospinal conduction with motor-unit recruitment, suggesting physiological structure, not dataset-specific statistics. Yet healthy young adults, gel-based/semi-dry wired hardware, and simulated displacement make this methodological; clinical and wireless dry-electrode transfer remains unestablished.

title: Enhancing the structural integrity of 3D bioprinted urethral grafts for clinical applications using GelMA–fibrinogen bioinks infused with human primary cells
container-title: Biofabrication
6ab1e84134dc671b4681ae1a7e69d287a5e9efcb.abstract: Abstract The demand for organ transplantation continues to grow, while challenges remain, such as the shortage of organ donors and complications associated with existing treatments. A promising alternative to transplantation is the implantation of artificial organs, which can be produced using 3D bioprinting technology. This approach offers the advantage of patient-specific solutions tailored to individual needs. Patients with urethral stricture or hypospadias who are unable to urinate require urethral reconstruction, which carries risks of complications and restricture. These patients may benefit from a tissue-engineered urethra fabricated using autologous cells and 3D bioprinting.A printer setup for tubular structures was developed for a 3D-Bioplotter and a gelatin-fibrinogen-based bioink was supplemented with GelMA to enhance mechanical properties for clinical applications while maintaining cell compatibility. Evaluation was performed through tensile testing, printability, suturability and cell viability analyses. An artificial urethral graft was successfully fabricated, demonstrating the operational capacity of our rod-based printer setup and the GelMA-fibrinogen hydrogel exhibited an increase in Young’s modulus compared with the gelatin-fibrinogen hydrogel. The GelMA-fibrinogen hydrogel also exhibited good suturability and efficient cell recovery after 14 days of culture. Human urothelial- and smooth muscle cells developed characteristic morphologies within the print, and a 210% increase in burst pressure was observed for the urethral graft after 14 days of culture, compared with the acellular graft.This 3D bioprinted artificial urethra, containing human urothelial and smooth muscle cells, represents a significant step forward in developing new treatment options for urethral disorders.

title: UAE FININT Resilience using a Network-Based Framework for Countering Terrorist Financing: From AML Compliance to Financial-Hub Resilience, An Attempt to Design an Integrated Counter-Terrorist-Financing Architecture for the United Arab Emirates
container-title: Emirati Journal of Business, Economics and Social Studies
b67858b0b89802bc941627af7426722bb614c89b.abstract: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) occupies a distinctive position in the international financial system: its success as a global banking, trade, logistics and virtual-asset hub simultaneously generates economic value and creates a complex exposure surface for transnational terrorist financing. This article argues that institution-level anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing (AML/CFT) compliance remains necessary but analytically and operationally incomplete for a high-connectivity jurisdiction, and proposes a shift from a compliance-centred architecture to a Financial Hub Resilience Model (FHRM). The study adopts a doctrinal and conceptual research design, combining doctrinal legal analysis of primary instruments (Federal Decree-Law No. 10 of 2025 and Cabinet Resolution No. 134 of 2025), comparative institutional analysis of the United Kingdom, Singapore and United States frameworks, and conceptual synthesis of the regulatory-compliance, network-analytic and geopolitical literatures. The FHRM relocates the unit of defence from the individual regulated entity to the interconnected ecosystem. It rests on two original constructs: the Financial Hub Attack Surface (seven-layer interfaces across banking, informal value transfer, corporate structures, trade, real estate, digital finance and the non-profit sector); and Financial Convergence Risk (individually explicable transactions that form, across institutions, a coherent terrorist-financing pathway invisible to single-institution monitoring). The model yields an operational architecture centred on intelligence fusion, typology-led detection, a bidirectional public-private partnership, and two outcome metrics (Time-to-Disruption and Financial Network Containment). Its central claim is that the UAE’s financial connectivity can be converted from a residual vulnerability into a sustained comparative advantage in financial integrity and national security, provided the ecosystem, rather than the firm, becomes the object of defence.

title: Are Political Psychologists Doomed to Play Cassandra?
container-title: Pathways into Political Psychology, Challenges for the Future
3b318980121e3fb20f16e7c6fe2fc507aa4e350f.abstract: Abstract This chapter challenges political psychology’s reliance on natural science models and urges a shift toward a human science rooted in cultural context and relational ethics. Liu draws on his multicultural background and editorial role to critique the field’s Western-centric assumptions, power imbalances, and marginalization of non-Western scholars. He promotes critical realism as a more suitable epistemology, emphasizing mentorship, ethical relationships, and historically informed analysis to bridge global academic divides. He shows how political psychologists fail to predict human behavior because they overlook cultural complexity, and he calls for qualitative, case-based approaches that reflect real-world dynamics. Finally, the chapter urges scholars to act locally, invest in human connections, and adopt a philosophy that prioritizes ethical responsibility and inclusivity over scientific abstraction. We regret that James died before he could see this volume in print, and are grateful for his friendship and his contributions to the field of political psychology

title: Between Artifice and Enlightenment: Queer Critique, Insecurity, and the AI Large Language Model
container-title: Insecurity and the Eclipse of Enlightenment
5ea4098d32b460e0385913aad6336e3634f5a5d9.abstract: Abstract Over several decades, machine learning systems—often described with the double metaphor “artificial intelligence”—have become indispensable computational tools in the flow and mediation of economic and social capital. These systems can, on the surface, appear to deepen the dialectic of enlightenment identified by Horkheimer and Adorno by enabling ever greater domination over natural systems and human agency. They therefore generate widespread concern that computational advances endanger the security and autonomy of human subjects, especially in the sphere of production and exchange. Contemporary social theory offers conceptual tools that go beyond received categories of domination and autonomy, however, to provide a reanalysis of machine learning systems and their implication in social dynamics and economic relations. This chapter focuses on the ways large language model (LLM) systems demonstrate complex affinities with theories of mimesis and simulacrum, and therefore how such systems and require a rethinking of performativity and artifice. Recent queer critique—in which reflection on computational systems and simulacra is proliferating—and contemporary social theory, when read together, thus reveal how rhetoric about LLMs demonstrates slippages between agency, performance, reproduction, representation, and meaning that must be unpacked historically and conceptually before metaphors of the “artificial” and “intelligence” can carry analytical weight in addressing today’s socioeconomic relations. Ultimately, this theoretical-conceptual reading highlights the stakes of the problem of truth in systems where artifice manifests both socially and computationally.

title: From relative to absolute quantification of cytochrome c oxidase and hemoglobin in human tissue: a standalone broadband near-infrared spectroscopy (bbNIRS) framework
container-title: Biomedical Optics Express
90c0973d4b38dda75bac36236a062e8a9ddb53a5.abstract: Standalone broadband near-infrared spectroscopy (bbNIRS) is attractive for portable tissue monitoring but cannot directly separate absorption from scattering, limiting absolute quantification of weak absorbers such as cytochrome c oxidase (CCO). We present a standalone bbNIRS framework for model-constrained estimation of oxygenated hemoglobin ([HbO]), deoxygenated hemoglobin ([HHb]), reduced CCO ([CCOred]), oxidized CCO ([CCOoxi]), water volume fraction (fwater), scattering amplitude ( a ), and scattering power ( b ). The framework combines diffusion-theory forward modeling, analytical Jacobian sensitivity analysis, model-based spectral-window selection, and a four-stage derivative-domain fitting algorithm (termed ε-TetraDF) using first- and second-order spectral derivatives to reduce parameter cross-talk. Diffusion-theory-based simulations with 1-10% added noise showed <10% relative recovery error for most parameters across all noise levels, with [CCOred] reaching ∼14% relative error at 10% noise. Monte Carlo simulations resulted in mean relative errors <6% for recovered [HbO], [HHb], [CCOoxi], fwater, a , and b , and 7.9% for [CCOred]. Moreover, forehead measurements in vivo from healthy adults yielded physiologically plausible estimates: [HbO] = 41.7 µM, [HHb] = 19.3 µM, StO 2 = 68.3%, fwater = 76.0%, and [CCOtotal] = 5.3 µM. All these results support the feasibility of standalone bbNIRS for model-constrained recovery of tissue hemoglobin, CCO components, fwater, and scattering parameters.

title: Preliminary study on re–grounding strategies after membership change
Enhancing Virtual Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
ef4f0aaa09ae551d9c3e068f71a492e2fd205170.abstract: Applications of artificial intelligence (AI) are shaping new ways of teaching, including the creation of virtual teachers who can automate the teaching process. AI can combine text-to-image, text-to-speech, lip sync and gesture animation for the creation of virtual avatars who can present and teach. However, despite advancements in technology, there are still issues with the realism of avatars and the ability to synchronize all of these processes in real-time. This chapter discusses the main artificial intelligence technologies that have been used to build automated virtual instructors, including advancements, challenges, and applications. In addition, the author discusses the educational value of these technologies and the need for better algorithms and system designs to foster the reliable, safe, and effective use of artificial intelligence in virtual education.

title: Reassessing Faith and Facts in AI-Augmented Modern Higher Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
3098ae300a50b242ae5b282892b8c9c0aa1b6ebc.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into modern higher education has produced a dual impact: while AI has opened new opportunities for innovation in teaching, learning, and research, it has also introduced significant challenges for academic practice. This paper explores how AI reshapes epistemic boundaries by challenging traditional notions and examines how confidence in institutional traditions and technological promise intersects with empirical data and algorithmic reasoning, and the ethical implications for transparent decision-making frameworks. By combining theoretical perspectives with practical examples, this paper highlights how AI is redefining epistemological foundations by the need to strengthen the relationship between faith and facts. The paper argues for a human-centred approach that promotes adaptive learning cultures. It concludes by proposing a forward-looking framework to help modern universities remain grounded in an AI-intensive future.

title: Universal Design in Higher Education
container-title: Inclusion and Diversity in Business and Tourism Education
1f4cf1a6757ab0b79e1ef1cb38f6c6ddfdeab0f1.abstract: Universal design ensures products, services, and environments are usable by all, fostering equal opportunity and participation for individuals with diverse abilities. This chapter, stemming from an inter-university teaching innovation project, provides a pedagogical framework for integrating universal design and accessibility into university courses focused on customer interaction. The methodology involves designing competence-based teaching programs with specific accessibility contents. The suitability of this teaching proposal was tested through pre- and post-surveys with 117 university students across four courses. Findings revealed significant improvements in students' knowledge, awareness, and practical application of universal design principles in customer relationship management. This study underscores that embedding accessibility into university curricula is essential for preparing future professionals to create user-centered services and contribute to more inclusive societies.

title: Damage-growth performance in multilayer dielectric mirrors under 351-nm, 1-ns laser pulses: influence of design parameters
container-title: Optics Express
cf9b1b5a6945ff55570d90503e89e58f5571ab8d.abstract: Multilayer dielectric (MLD) mirrors are critical for next-generation, large-aperture, high-repetition-rate laser systems, such as inertial fusion energy drivers or directed energy systems. The performance of MLD mirrors must remain unaffected by laser-induced damage over their operational lifetime. This study investigates the material and design parameters that influence the damage-growth performance of fabricated Al 2 O 3 /SiO 2 and HfO 2 /SiO 2 MLD mirrors tested at 351 nm using nanosecond pulses. The study is based on the hypothesis that damage initiation can be considered unavoidable due to coating imperfections or contamination, but may not affect laser operation if damage sites remain stable with successive pulses. Modeling of damage-initiation sites revealed that the 3D electric-field intensity governs damage growth. Results show that high-index material significantly affects the damage-growth threshold. Using a high-index material as the outer layer helps confine damage growth to this layer, preventing catastrophic penetration into inner layers.

title: Regulation of the Use of AI in the Health Sector From a Human Rights Perspective
container-title: Innovation, Governance, and Resilience in Global Health Systems
5fb7dd0f3fd50c1495af258deb5479e3ef2287e2.abstract: The discussion for the use and regulation of Artificial Intelligence in the healthcare sector from a human rights perspective is much needed due to its intrinsic ethical, social, legal and non-jurisdictional implications. The fourth generation human rights core discourse is focused on the technological advancements, its impact on human lives. Though the fourth-generation human rights are not yet enlisted and explicitly codified through domestic or international legislative body, nevertheless; this is one of the socio-legal discourse after invention of AI. The European Commission has criticized AI systems for not adequately addressing patients' rights health-related risks such as discrimination, privacy concerns, and opaque decision-making processes, etc.

c3e35dc9cc6d6c3db481ba0234b0a9903939fd49.abstract: The article presents a comparative assessment of valuable agronomic traits in F₄ cotton hybrids studied in a first-year breeding nursery. The growing period, seed cotton weight per boll, plant productivity, fiber length, and fiber yield were evaluated in comparison with the Andijan-36 standard cultivar. The Bukhara-6 × 010888 combination achieved a plant productivity of 81.5 g and a fiber yield of 40.4%. The S-6524 × 011592 combination had the shortest growing period (114 days) and the greatest fiber length (34.5 mm). The Sulton × 011482 combination showed a plant productivity of 80.0 g and a fiber yield of 39.9%. These results identify the above combinations as valuable breeding materials for further evaluation based on a combination of economically important traits.

18a699872048aae257650763328c9a9eaa0f34f6.abstract: The article presents data on the impact of herbicide application against weeds simultaneously with sowing and during the 3–4 true leaf stages of cotton on the duration of the plant growing season. As a result of applying herbicides along with sowing and at the 3–4 true leaf stage of the plant, an extension of the cotton growing season by 1–4 days was observed.

bdc53edec3b08e5979205cd7592596da45af6845.abstract: This article presents data on the yield of cotton varieties from research conducted at the experimental fields of the Syrdarya scientific-experimental station. The study involved the regionalized “Guliston” variety and the promising "S-5727" variety, which were irrigated one to two times. Irrigation was applied at soil moisture levels of 70-70-60% and 75-75-60% relative to field capacity, with plant densities maintained at 100, 150, and 200 thousand plants per hectare. Taking the boll opening rate into account, it was determined that the cotton yield across the experimental variants averaged between 41.1 and 49.1 centners per hectare.

The growing season, calculated from emergence to full maturity, ranged from 225 to 232 days. Among the perennial samples, the earliest-maturing WHEAT-AGROPYRON INTERMEDIUM PARTIAL AMPHIPLOID6 had a growing season of 225 days, while the latest-maturing MADSEN//CHINESE SPRING/PI531718 had 232 days. These differences indicate phenological diversity in the development of perennial wheat genotypes.

b39a782935211bc85d4c9cb2bcbc690694c75c7a.abstract: The paper analyzes grate constructions used in cotton cleaners for removing large impurities. The aim is to systematize the advantages and limitations of stationary round, triangular and trapezoidal grate bars and to analyze the influence of grate design parameters on the cleaning process. The source material reports triangular grate dimensions of 19, 25 and 12 mm, a 1570 mm placement radius relative to the saw drum and a 40 mm spacing as an effective configuration. For the CHX-3 cleaner, trapezoidal grate bars with dimensions of 25, 16, 12 and 10 mm are reported, while a low efficiency is noted for the 12 mm working edge configuration in CHX-ZM. A grate with different grate-bar diameters and solutions aimed at increasing the degrees of freedom of grate bars are also considered. Since the source material does not contain sufficient quantitative results of a new experiment, numerical efficiency values were not fabricated; the analysis is based on the parameters and conclusions available in the source material.

0107d93e0c6265c326136b831716e2b85322e18a.abstract: The article investigates the effect of different rates of mineral fertilizers and the Moddus retardant on the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat varieties Krasnodarskaya-99 and Chillaki. The results showed that the application of mineral fertilizers in combination with the retardant had a positive effect on leaf area formation and the photosynthetic potential of plants. The highest values of photosynthetic activity were recorded when mineral fertilizers were applied at a rate of N210P105K70 in combination with Moddus at a rate of 0.4 L/ha. Among the studied varieties, Chillaki demonstrated higher leaf area and photosynthetic potential compared with Krasnodarskaya-99. The obtained results indicate that an optimal combination of mineral nutrition and Moddus retardant application can contribute to improving the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat plants.

title: Unsupervised detection of overshooting defects using hybrid generative and boundary classification models
container-title: Journal of Logic and Computation
5bd5611f5a7b62192ff0e5e55cf8165aac10e28e.abstract: Abstract Quality control in modern manufacturing increasingly relies on unsupervised anomaly detection to identify structural defects when abnormal samples are critically scarce. This study presents an evaluation of hybrid generative architectures designed to detect complex overshooting anomalies in industrial simple sub-assemblies base plates. We analysed eight distinct model combinations by pairing four advanced generative backbones, including a latent space resampling autoencoder and a denoising diffusion model, with two boundary classification strategies: the one class support vector machine and the deep support vector data description. The experimental results demonstrate that the configuration pairing the latent space resampling autoencoder with the one class support vector machine achieves superior detection capabilities, securing the highest mean area under the curve of 0.7870 alongside absolute statistical dominance. However, our findings reveal a critical architectural vulnerability, as pairing heavily regularized generative latent spaces with the rigid hyperspherical boundaries of the deep data description model invariably degrades detection, driving in the most strongly regularized configuration a systematic inversion of the anomaly score rather than a loss of discriminative power. Ultimately, this research establishes that flexible margin optimization is required to preserve anomaly detection accuracy in complex industrial topologies, providing a framework for deploying reliable automated quality assurance systems.

2c82404e59061d43e26831844193b6893fbcf292.abstract: The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.

title: Deep Learning for Adaptive Management of Renewable Hybrid Power Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
d578d62f03821803d57f6e8a397facef71850f2b.abstract: This study examines the problem of adaptive control for hybrid renewable energy systems combining photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and battery storage under conditions of generation uncertainty and price volatility. A control strategy based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, which does not require an explicit mathematical model and accounts for long-term consequences, including battery degradation. The control task is formalized as a markov decision process with an integral discounted reward combining economic costs, penalties for energy curtailment, and storage aging losses. Computational experiments on real meteorological data demonstrate that the trained regulator reduces operating costs by 12–15% compared to heuristic strategies, increases the share of renewable energy used by 18–22%, and extends estimated battery life by 15–20%. The results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach over classical methods, particularly under high uncertainty. Limitations and prospects for practical implementation are discussed.

title: Intelligent Energy Systems

Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
63395033ead6c334c44934c0c842fb3ccadf45ea.abstract: The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.

title: AI-Assisted Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Microgrids for Sustainable Rural Electrification

ea5cb44704ea7f5ca67dc3a9d789f030592a4484.abstract: This chapter reviews conventional optimization methods and AI-assisted approaches for hybrid renewable energy microgrids, highlighting their roles in system planning, sizing, operation, and control. It also explores emerging technologies, including reinforcement learning, explainable AI, digital twins, and edge AI, that are shaping the next generation of intelligent energy systems. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, the chapter presents a case study of a hybrid renewable energy microgrid in Muanda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, featuring solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, and blue-carbon bioenergy resources. The case study shows how optimization techniques can enhance techno-economic and environmental performance and discusses the potential of AI-based forecasting, intelligent battery management, and reinforcement learning to further improve system reliability, renewable energy utilization, and long-term sustainability.

a481d5d2ec22f7c57987bf6fb1f4d55e7e848167.abstract: The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.

dc3def60d826262ab21f0eea8c2fef98b5d58e72.abstract: Solar thermal systems encounter distinct operational challenges, which hinder their applicability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to solve them. The AI is more flexible and adaptable than traditional methods, which cannot deal with unpredictable factors, including changing weather and fluctuating energy demands. In this chapter, we introduced the solar thermal systems, and then the fundamentals of AI techniques used in solar thermal systems were provided. Subsequently, the application of AI in solar thermal systems was discussed. The advantages of the optimization process of the solar thermal systems were identified, supported by case studies from the real world. Then we identified the limitations and constraints that hinder the integration of AI into the solar thermal system. Finally, the economic benefits of using AI for the optimization of solar thermal systems were explained.

92ef05c8e2ba0949c3bf8f69974d39c51dc39e56.abstract: This chapter analyses the strategic incorporation of artificial intelligence technology into renewable energy systems to enhance energy security, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability. This chapter aims to examine how intelligent energy management systems, machine learning algorithms, smart grids, decentralized microgrids, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks can enhance the performance and resilience of renewable energy systems. This chapter places emphasis on predictive analytics, battery management, solar forecasting, digital twins, and autonomous energy optimization. The chapter examines the economic, environmental, and technological ramifications of intelligent energy systems, emphasizing their capacity to minimize energy losses, improve system reliability, facilitate decentralized electrification, and expedite sustainable energy transitions towards enhanced national energy independence.

974378bf655d4595a7410253b21e0ad381c1a368.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

a35056ead95e6546af494efa6e34c4e7ce0284ba.abstract: This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.

2488e9ed487b4765c71f38c4edb94b5b6290f2ae.abstract: Anaerobic co-digestion is an effective approach for biogas production, but optimizing operating parameters remains challenging due to the interaction of multiple variables. This study integrates ultrasonic pretreatment with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to enhance biogas yield from a mixture of dormitory food waste and pet animal dung. Batch digesters were operated at 37 °C, and daily biogas production was monitored. RSM evaluated the combined effects of ultrasonic temperature (25–65 °C), power (500–1,500 W), and treatment time (35–75 min). Biogas yield ranged from 35% to nearly 68%, with optimum conditions of 53.35 °C, 1,490.83 W, and 57.15 min, producing a predicted yield of 66.47%. The quadratic model showed excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9707; F = 110.33), confirming the importance of simultaneous optimization. The integrated ultrasonic–RSM approach provides a reliable and efficient strategy for maximizing biogas production in anaerobic co-digestion systems.

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability

Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
af88092a3405a3484f3caf6617dee2099625164e.abstract: This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.

title: Forecasting Electrical Load and Renewable Energy Generation Using Machine Learning Methods

b326566af7bfa615ecca304269db8b978877aabc.abstract: This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The purpose is to show why power systems need models handling nonlinear, non-stationary, and heterogeneous data. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.

title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys

bcafa941c82b95b48c33f91be24df91543e346ce.abstract: Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.

title: Towards theorising the normative agency of Central Europe: iterative identities and norms shaping from a Global East perspective
container-title: Pluriversal International Relations
2bab88b6b8efd5cb9648fabde86d60d4a0c7faa0.abstract: This article examines under what conditions actors operating through a semi-peripheral regional format can develop an emergent form of normative agency. It treats the Three Seas Initiative as an illustrative Central European case, viewed through the Global East as a relational and epistemic positionality rather than a fixed geography. The article introduces the constructivist model of iterative identities and norms shaping, a heuristic framework tracing how previously articulated norms, identity narratives and regional role claims re-enter later political and institutional contexts and are reinterpreted, contested, amplified or institutionalised. The model identifies identity alignment and norm localisation as the principal conditions of regional normative agency, distinguishing conditional norm co-creation from compliance, locally bounded autonomy and failed agency. Empirically, the article analyses Three Seas Initiative summit declarations from 2016 to 2025, supplemented by institutional documents and selected European Union and North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) materials examining external recognition and convergence. The analysis reconstructs three phases of the initiative’s development: initial identity formation and the search for recognition; institutionalisation and the localisation of connectivity norms; and the post-2021 reinterpretation of infrastructure through resilience, security and eastern-flank vulnerability. The findings suggest that the initiative has generated limited and conditional normative agency through the regionally grounded reinterpretation of broader Euro-Atlantic normative templates. The case does not demonstrate autonomous norm creation but shows how historically norm-receiving actors may contribute to norm transformation when regional institutionalisation combines with wider recognition.

title: Dual-band beam-steering metasurface design and analysis based on transmission line theory
container-title: Physica Scripta
87fafcd321245e95abcb974a90a3d45a386a929a.abstract: Abstract This paper presents an advanced design methodology for dual-band, all-dielectric metasurfaces based on transmission line (TL) theory. The proposed structure integrates two single-band metasurfaces placed back-to-back, enabling highly versatile dual-band functionality. By leveraging the TL framework, the design parameters are analytically derived to provide independent control over the steering angles at two distinct operating frequencies. This flexibility allows the deflection angle at the second frequency to be configured as either larger or smaller than that at the first, depending on the application requirements. The effectiveness of this theoretical framework is validated through multiple design scenarios, including cases with diverse angular relationships and anomalous transmission in opposite directions. Full-wave electromagnetic simulation results demonstrate excellent agreement with theoretical predictions, confirming the precision and robustness of the proposed methodology in achieving selective and decoupled wavefront control in dual-band environments.

title: Design for dynamic fitness: archetypes of urban water systems
container-title: Environmental Research: Infrastructure and Sustainability
81188f34d9a13d7171ac9a63ae9b442ff8609543.abstract: Abstract Infrastructure systems were largely designed for a world of environmental stationarity, and the Anthropocene—characterized by accelerating change that often produces more dynamic and extreme stressors—challenges infrastructure robustness. Urban water supply systems (UWSs) epitomize the pressures of socio-environmental change on infrastructure as they increasingly operate outside their physical design conditions, putting new pressure on their institutional designs to weather emerging challenges. Water management institutions must therefore be designed for ‘dynamic fitness,’ defined by anticipatory capacity and responsiveness. However, we do not yet understand the specific institutional design features enabling dynamic fitness and their relation to infrastructure and environmental (i.e. biophysical) characteristics. We advance research on dynamic fitness in UWSs by synthesizing theory and analyzing 35-year data sets of stressors and responses for 16 U.S. urban water utilities using archetype analysis. We find that institutional archetypes capable of coping with higher biophysical complexity invest in information processing capacity and response diversity. While these features of dynamic fitness come at a cost, balancing these promotes efficiency, which can be expanded through polycentric regional governance structures. Institutional designs for dynamic fitness must weigh tradeoffs in flexibility across governance levels and between quick responses and slow transformative changes.

title: Integrasi AI dalam Kurikulum Akuntansi Pendidikan Pesantren: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis tentang Kesiapan Teknologi, Pemahaman AI, dan Karakteristik Siswa
container-title: Business and Accounting Education Journal
9db92d2d3af48ff40caacdc975fdcbe142bb7929.abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong transformasi pendidikan akuntansi dan menuntut penyesuaian kurikulum agar sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia kerja digital. Namun, adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi masih dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor, khususnya pada konteks pendidikan pesantren yang memiliki karakteristik unik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kesiapan teknologi, pemahaman AI, dan karakteristik siswa terhadap adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi serta mengidentifikasi faktor yang paling dominan. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Data diperoleh dari 38 artikel ilmiah terindeks Scopus yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2015-2026 dan dianalisis menggunakan sintesis tematik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kesiapan teknologi merupakan faktor yang paling dominan dalam mendorong adopsi AI, diikuti oleh pemahaman AI dan karakteristik siswa. Ketiga faktor tersebut saling melengkapi dalam meningkatkan penerimaan dan pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran akuntansi. Temuan ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan model adopsi teknologi pendidikan serta menjadi dasar pengembangan kurikulum akuntansi berbasis AI di lingkungan pesantren.

title: Fertility rates across generations in twins and singletons: a total population study in Finland
container-title: Human Reproduction
0f08f59259ab0674c77bfff27b139d628691813b.abstract: Abstract STUDY QUESTION Does twin status and zygosity (monozygotic vs dizygotic; same-sex vs opposite-sex) predict fertility outcomes and intergenerational reproductive patterns compared with singletons? SUMMARY ANSWER Dizygotic female twins had a modestly higher number of biological children than singletons and monozygotic twins and were more likely to have a twin birth, but we did not observe differences for males or intergenerational differences. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY Dizygotic twinning is associated with heritable hyperovulation and higher natural fertility but less is known about whether being a twin or zygosity influences reproductive outcomes across generations. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION A population-based longitudinal cohort study using part of the Finnish Twin Cohort and national population registers. Participants included an Anchor Generation composed of monozygotic (MZ; N = 4068), same-sex dizygotic (SSDZ; N = 8890), opposite-sex dizygotic (OSDZ; N = 8474), unknown zygosity (XZ; N = 2320) twins, and singleton controls (N = 1 193 404) born between 1945 and 1957 (total N = 1 217 156; 49.1% female), their mothers, their children, and their grandchildren. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS Fertility outcomes (number of biological children, age at first birth, childlessness, multiple births) were derived from Finnish population registers. Analyses followed a preregistered plan (https://osf.io/qbwv3). MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE Differences in fertility between singletons and twins were modest and varied by sex and zygosity. Differences were observed generally in the mothers of twins and female twins themselves, with limited differences in the offspring of twins as compared to the offspring of singletons. Twins were slightly older at first birth, had fewer total biological offspring, but were more likely to have a twin birth. Dizygotic twins in particular differed from monozygotic twins and singletons. LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION Findings are limited to individuals born in mid-20th-century Finland and thus generalizability to recent populations or non-Nordic contexts may be restricted. Further, analyses are observational, and causal inference is limited due to alternative motivation behind fertility rates like social or cultural reasons. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS These findings suggest that zygosity and sex interact to shape reproductive outcomes, offering insight into genetic and environmental contributions to fertility. They highlight the value of large twin cohorts for studying intergenerational reproductive trends and the representativeness of twins in population-based fertility research. FUNDING As a supporting activity to ongoing research projects, funding for this project was provided by the Broad Trauma Initiative at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard. DISCLOSURES The authors declare no conflict of interest. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER N/A.

title: From prediction to design rules: explainable machine learning analysis of cryoprotectant effects in GelMA-based cryobioprinting bioinks
container-title: Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express
cba1d2360d45f4f2da517a4c0ec4ef34475e0fff.abstract: Abstract Machine learning has been used to predict cryoprotective-agent (CPA) effects in cryobioprinting, but prediction accuracy alone does not yield experimentally usable formulation rules. Here, we performed a secondary explainable analysis of Qiao et al ’s GelMA-HUVEC dataset using formulation-grouped validation, SHAP interpretation, stability metrics, and multi-objective ranking. A compact Random Forest model using permeable CPA identity, sugar CPA identity, permeable CPA concentration, sugar concentration, and storage day achieved MAE = 4.842%, RMSE = 6.106%, and R 2 = 0.649, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals of 4.418–5.274% for MAE and 0.585–0.710 for R 2 . SHAP analysis identified permeable CPA concentration and storage day as the strongest viability drivers, with directional patterns favoring balanced 15% permeable CPA and 15% sugar CPA rather than simple concentration maximization. Multi-objective ranking identified GL_15_RA_15 as the strongest individual formulation, whereas EG + trehalose showed the highest average CPA-family performance. Cross-domain tests showed limited transfer between EG and GL formulations, indicating that the extracted rules should be treated as local, data-supported design hypotheses rather than universal cryoprotectant principles. Together, these results show that explainable secondary analysis can convert small cryobioprinting datasets into experimentally testable CPA hypotheses while explicitly defining their transferability limits.

title: Tau hadronic decay channel reconstruction with a Lorentz-covariant graph attention network
container-title: Physica Scripta
7d7360eebe4f1102dd8fb23bb166025e3ac64c60.abstract: Abstract The reconstruction of hadronic decay modes of the τ lepton is a key task in high-energy physics experiments, directly impacting precision measurements and new physics searches. Conventional reconstruction approaches rely on handcrafted features and rule-based algorithms, which face challenges in handling complex decay topologies and detector effects. In this work, we propose LCGA-Net, a physics-informed deep learning framework for τ decay channel classification and four-momentum reconstruction. The method represents decay products as particle graphs and employs a multi-head attention mechanism to capture inter-particle correlations. To ensure physical consistency, Lorentz-invariant constraints are explicitly incorporated into the model architecture. A dedicated single- τ dataset is constructed from the simulation data of the Circular Electron Positron Collider, covering six major hadronic decay modes. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89.2% on the validation set, matching or slightly exceeding baseline models. More importantly, full physics constraints substantially improve the physical plausibility of reconstructed four-momenta—particularly the energy–momentum relation—without degrading classification performance. These results demonstrate that integrating physics priors with attention-based deep learning on particle clouds provides an effective approach for τ decay reconstruction, with potential applications in future high-energy physics analyses.
