title: Initial affect shapes risk-benefit information processing and public support for carbon dioxide removal technologies
container-title: Environmental Research Letters
1b65e208f3b196b83234cad4f22596ad08221a71.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Given the accelerating climate crisis, carbon dioxide removal (CDR) technologies are becoming increasingly important, while public support may play a relevant role in their implementation. This support is influenced by how citizens inform themselves about the technology. While prior research has examined public support under conditions of no or predefined information provision, little is known about the factors that shape how individuals actively select information about CDR and integrate it into their preferences about the technology. Here, we investigate how initial affect towards CDR shapes laypersons’ selection and evaluation of benefit-related versus risk-related information about the technology and how these processes influence subsequent policy support. In a preregistered study with 714 U.S. participants, we introduced a novel information-sampling task, in which participants could freely choose which information about CDR to attend to, followed by a policy choice experiment assessing public support of CDR technologies. In line with our hypotheses, participants’ initial affect influenced their information search: more initial positive affect towards CDR was associated with a higher likelihood to select benefit-related versus risk-related information about CDR. This confirmatory information search, in turn, was associated with immediate changes in affect towards the technology, especially when the information was perceived as persuasive. These affective changes across information search carried over to subsequent decisions to support climate policies in general and policy portfolios including CDR in particular. Overall, our findings highlight the reciprocal relationship between affect, endogenous information search, and support for CDR technologies.</jats:p>

title: BIRINCHI YILGI SELEKSIYA KO‘CHATZORIDA F₄ DURAGAY AVLODLARINING QIMMATLI XO‘JALIK BELGILARI BO‘YICHA BAHOLANISHI

5868f68ca821a8a3140ef8efb963d5a2d6a15df1.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents a comparative assessment of valuable agronomic traits in F₄ cotton hybrids studied in a first-year breeding nursery. The growing period, seed cotton weight per boll, plant productivity, fiber length, and fiber yield were evaluated in comparison with the Andijan-36 standard cultivar. The Bukhara-6 × 010888 combination achieved a plant productivity of 81.5 g and a fiber yield of 40.4%. The S-6524 × 011592 combination had the shortest growing period (114 days) and the greatest fiber length (34.5 mm). The Sulton × 011482 combination showed a plant productivity of 80.0 g and a fiber yield of 39.9%. These results identify the above combinations as valuable breeding materials for further evaluation based on a combination of economically important traits.</jats:p>

d55b438ea047efc4c7a110358eb03ad05e23e863.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents data on the impact of herbicide application against weeds simultaneously with sowing and during the 3–4 true leaf stages of cotton on the duration of the plant growing season. As a result of applying herbicides along with sowing and at the 3–4 true leaf stage of the plant, an extension of the cotton growing season by 1–4 days was observed.</jats:p>

title: SIRDARYO VILOYATI UCHUN RAYONLASHGAN G‘O‘ZANING GULISTON VA ISTIQBOLLI S-5727 NAVLARINING HOSILDORLIGI

5a53e05c64aff82600f4f8558413e6672eedd469.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents data on the yield of cotton varieties from research conducted at the experimental fields of the Syrdarya scientific-experimental station. The study involved the regionalized “Guliston” variety and the promising "S-5727" variety, which were irrigated one to two times. Irrigation was applied at soil moisture levels of 70-70-60% and 75-75-60% relative to field capacity, with plant densities maintained at 100, 150, and 200 thousand plants per hectare. Taking the boll opening rate into account, it was determined that the cotton yield across the experimental variants averaged between 41.1 and 49.1 centners per hectare.</jats:p>

title: KO‘P YILLIK BUG‘DOY SELEKSIYASIDA FENOLOGIK RIVOJLANISH VA VEGETATSIYA DAVRI DAVOMIYLIGI BO‘YICHA MANBALARNI TANLASH

3177fc183de9d9c0e409c1cddc46647aa5b359a0.abstract: <jats:p>The study investigated the phenological development and duration of the growing season of 11 perennial wheat collection samples. The growing season, calculated from emergence to full maturity, ranged from 225 to 232 days. Among the perennial samples, the earliest-maturing WHEAT-AGROPYRON INTERMEDIUM PARTIAL AMPHIPLOID6 had a growing season of 225 days, while the latest-maturing MADSEN//CHINESE SPRING/PI531718 had 232 days. These differences indicate phenological diversity in the development of perennial wheat genotypes.</jats:p>

69d9be549364767eb4cd15be7d3c8e10711b9280.abstract: <jats:p>The paper analyzes grate constructions used in cotton cleaners for removing large impurities. The aim is to systematize the advantages and limitations of stationary round, triangular and trapezoidal grate bars and to analyze the influence of grate design parameters on the cleaning process. The source material reports triangular grate dimensions of 19, 25 and 12 mm, a 1570 mm placement radius relative to the saw drum and a 40 mm spacing as an effective configuration. For the CHX-3 cleaner, trapezoidal grate bars with dimensions of 25, 16, 12 and 10 mm are reported, while a low efficiency is noted for the 12 mm working edge configuration in CHX-ZM. A grate with different grate-bar diameters and solutions aimed at increasing the degrees of freedom of grate bars are also considered. Since the source material does not contain sufficient quantitative results of a new experiment, numerical efficiency values were not fabricated; the analysis is based on the parameters and conclusions available in the source material.</jats:p>

title: КУЗГИ БУҒДОЙ НАВЛАРИНИНГ ФОТОСИНТЕТИК ФАОЛИЯТИГА РЕТАРДАНТ ВА ЎҒИТ МЕЪЁРЛАРИНИНГ ТАЪСИРИ

842147f8478a8792c0ff57ceb94f797caa0f8bcd.abstract: <jats:p>The article investigates the effect of different rates of mineral fertilizers and the Moddus retardant on the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat varieties Krasnodarskaya-99 and Chillaki. The results showed that the application of mineral fertilizers in combination with the retardant had a positive effect on leaf area formation and the photosynthetic potential of plants. The highest values of photosynthetic activity were recorded when mineral fertilizers were applied at a rate of N210P105K70 in combination with Moddus at a rate of 0.4 L/ha. Among the studied varieties, Chillaki demonstrated higher leaf area and photosynthetic potential compared with Krasnodarskaya-99. The obtained results indicate that an optimal combination of mineral nutrition and Moddus retardant application can contribute to improving the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat plants.</jats:p>

title: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor‐1 Deficiency Exacerbates Pressure Overload‐Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Mice
container-title: Journal of the American Heart Association
79ecebb2f41491829e41be60e3e4df5a684fc5a7.abstract:
<jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a key precursor to heart failure. PAI‐1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor‐1) is a recognized profibrotic mediator, yet its role in the heart remains paradoxical and incompletely understood.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">
                      Six‐week‐old male wild‐type (PAI‐1
                      <jats:sup>+/+</jats:sup>
                      ) and PAI‐1 knockout (PAI‐1
                      <jats:sup>−/−</jats:sup>
                      ) mice underwent sham or transverse aortic constriction surgery, followed by assessment of cardiac morphology, molecular markers, and function. In H9C2 cardiomyocytes, PAI‐1 was silenced or overexpressed before angiotensin II stimulation, with or without targeted signaling inhibitors, followed by coimmunoprecipitation, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">Pressure overload increased plasma and myocardial PAI‐1 levels. PAI‐1 deficiency exacerbated transverse aortic constriction‐induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, accompanied by JAK2/STAT3 (Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3) activation and collagen overexpression, whereas cardiac‐specific overexpression attenuated these maladaptive changes. Moreover, STAT3 inhibition reversed the adverse cardiac remodeling associated with PAI‐1 deletion. In vitro, PAI‐1 knockdown potentiated angiotensin II‐induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, an effect that was rescued by PAI‐1 overexpression. Mechanistically, PAI‐1 associated with JAK2 and STAT3, with reduced phosphorylation of both proteins and impaired STAT3 nuclear translocation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of STAT3 abolished the harmful effects of PAI‐1 silencing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">PAI‐1 acts as an endogenous cardioprotective checkpoint by negatively regulating JAK2/STAT3 signaling. These findings suggest a noncanonical cardiomyocyte‐associated function of PAI‐1 beyond its classical fibrinolytic role and identify the PAI‐1—JAK2/STAT3 axis as a potential therapeutic target for heart failure with hypertrophy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

36d6b77407653d455c80e2f500634a6232d7a5a9.abstract: <jats:p>The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning for Adaptive Management of Renewable Hybrid Power Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
8dbc26d9167ed7772f47b06f9aa8d0293cf7c8ac.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the problem of adaptive control for hybrid renewable energy systems combining photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and battery storage under conditions of generation uncertainty and price volatility. A control strategy based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, which does not require an explicit mathematical model and accounts for long-term consequences, including battery degradation. The control task is formalized as a markov decision process with an integral discounted reward combining economic costs, penalties for energy curtailment, and storage aging losses. Computational experiments on real meteorological data demonstrate that the trained regulator reduces operating costs by 12–15% compared to heuristic strategies, increases the share of renewable energy used by 18–22%, and extends estimated battery life by 15–20%. The results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach over classical methods, particularly under high uncertainty. Limitations and prospects for practical implementation are discussed.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
5f910b7c7ff3cc7a08791e8c37c348d51a9d359d.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Assisted Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Microgrids for Sustainable Rural Electrification
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
96ab7ef154dc58376a40cf75f589dc662f80d0d9.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter reviews conventional optimization methods and AI-assisted approaches for hybrid renewable energy microgrids, highlighting their roles in system planning, sizing, operation, and control. It also explores emerging technologies, including reinforcement learning, explainable AI, digital twins, and edge AI, that are shaping the next generation of intelligent energy systems. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, the chapter presents a case study of a hybrid renewable energy microgrid in Muanda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, featuring solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, and blue-carbon bioenergy resources. The case study shows how optimization techniques can enhance techno-economic and environmental performance and discusses the potential of AI-based forecasting, intelligent battery management, and reinforcement learning to further improve system reliability, renewable energy utilization, and long-term sustainability.</jats:p>

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ff36013178296736d6e2747d2c7e1830b32bd841.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Optimization of Solar Thermal Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
0860e093417810bedf80a8a8c80f3dec419bac99.abstract: <jats:p>Solar thermal systems encounter distinct operational challenges, which hinder their applicability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to solve them. The AI is more flexible and adaptable than traditional methods, which cannot deal with unpredictable factors, including changing weather and fluctuating energy demands. In this chapter, we introduced the solar thermal systems, and then the fundamentals of AI techniques used in solar thermal systems were provided. Subsequently, the application of AI in solar thermal systems was discussed. The advantages of the optimization process of the solar thermal systems were identified, supported by case studies from the real world. Then we identified the limitations and constraints that hinder the integration of AI into the solar thermal system. Finally, the economic benefits of using AI for the optimization of solar thermal systems were explained.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Solar Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
81ed3d5ef17a5775f35361935d09bc66b4b5cc4e.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyses the strategic incorporation of artificial intelligence technology into renewable energy systems to enhance energy security, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability. This chapter aims to examine how intelligent energy management systems, machine learning algorithms, smart grids, decentralized microgrids, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks can enhance the performance and resilience of renewable energy systems. This chapter places emphasis on predictive analytics, battery management, solar forecasting, digital twins, and autonomous energy optimization. The chapter examines the economic, environmental, and technological ramifications of intelligent energy systems, emphasizing their capacity to minimize energy losses, improve system reliability, facilitate decentralized electrification, and expedite sustainable energy transitions towards enhanced national energy independence.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning for Solar Thermal Energy Optimization and Smart Control
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
fb44f8ecb89dccb4a11eab978ce879fb41e44f26.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.</jats:p>

title: Energy Audits in Tanzanian Industrial SMEs for Methods, Barriers, and M&V-Linked Savings Prioritization
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
b85063b2e64cb2adf03e3a6fd9c4b42f3f347e50.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.</jats:p>

title: Biogas Production Optimisation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
3a1fabea3f97fb97115f71a9b24c656748b30ad4.abstract: <jats:p>Anaerobic co-digestion is an effective approach for biogas production, but optimizing operating parameters remains challenging due to the interaction of multiple variables. This study integrates ultrasonic pretreatment with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to enhance biogas yield from a mixture of dormitory food waste and pet animal dung. Batch digesters were operated at 37 °C, and daily biogas production was monitored. RSM evaluated the combined effects of ultrasonic temperature (25–65 °C), power (500–1,500 W), and treatment time (35–75 min). Biogas yield ranged from 35% to nearly 68%, with optimum conditions of 53.35 °C, 1,490.83 W, and 57.15 min, producing a predicted yield of 66.47%. The quadratic model showed excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9707; F = 110.33), confirming the importance of simultaneous optimization. The integrated ultrasonic–RSM approach provides a reliable and efficient strategy for maximizing biogas production in anaerobic co-digestion systems.</jats:p>

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
638e43b89445c1c4efd078d51246af0e90e11d12.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.</jats:p>

title: Forecasting Electrical Load and Renewable Energy Generation Using Machine Learning Methods
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ea63ae340e55dcd23a21c92099270e55640a1e65.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The purpose is to show why power systems need models handling nonlinear, non-stationary, and heterogeneous data. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
db14ec7802b2943f0f932ee90ef99812da7cac80.abstract: <jats:p>Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.</jats:p>

title: Integrasi AI dalam Kurikulum Akuntansi Pendidikan Pesantren: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis tentang Kesiapan Teknologi, Pemahaman AI, dan Karakteristik Siswa

e0f60edd89c8c829c91e27e2720ae59dca61591c.abstract: <jats:p>Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong transformasi pendidikan akuntansi dan menuntut penyesuaian kurikulum agar sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia kerja digital. Namun, adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi masih dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor, khususnya pada konteks pendidikan pesantren yang memiliki karakteristik unik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kesiapan teknologi, pemahaman AI, dan karakteristik siswa terhadap adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi serta mengidentifikasi faktor yang paling dominan. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Data diperoleh dari 38 artikel ilmiah terindeks Scopus yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2015-2026 dan dianalisis menggunakan sintesis tematik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kesiapan teknologi merupakan faktor yang paling dominan dalam mendorong adopsi AI, diikuti oleh pemahaman AI dan karakteristik siswa. Ketiga faktor tersebut saling melengkapi dalam meningkatkan penerimaan dan pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran akuntansi. Temuan ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan model adopsi teknologi pendidikan serta menjadi dasar pengembangan kurikulum akuntansi berbasis AI di lingkungan pesantren.</jats:p>

title: KUNJUTNING ODDIY VA BEKROSS CHATISHTIRISH NATIJASIDA OLINGAN F1  DURAGAYLARIDA O‘SIMLIK BO‘YI VA YON SHOXLARI SONI BELGILARINING IRSIYLANISHI

a1fc8d526224f83eedb1e34addc24c0a8e924a52.abstract: <jats:p>The study investigated the inheritance of important morphological traits, including plant height and the number of lateral branches, in simple and backcross F₁ sesame hybrids involving the local varieties “Onimdar”, “Qora Shahzoda”, “Tashkent-122”, and “Sadaf”. The experiments were conducted under field and laboratory conditions. The patterns of trait formation and the degree of heterosis in the hybrids were analyzed. The number of lateral branches ranged from 5.8 to 6.2 per plant in the local varieties, from 5.7 to 8.7 in simple F₁ hybrids, and from 5.6 to 9.2 in backcross hybrids. Positive heterosis for the number of lateral branches was observed in most of the simple hybrids. Positive inheritance of this trait was also recorded in several backcross combinations. Promising hybrid combinations with high values of plant height and the number of lateral branches were identified. The results indicate that the selected hybrid combinations can be used in sesame breeding to develop valuable initial breeding material with high productivity, stability, and adaptability to local environmental conditions.</jats:p>

title: SUG‘ORILADIGAN YERLAR UCHUN ARPA SELEKSIYASIDA OLIB BORILAYOTGAN TADQIQOTLAR

11f8545db76c4de11946113dd99d4f0d407be82d.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of research aimed at identifying valuable initial breeding material for barley breeding on irrigated lands. The studies were conducted in 2023–2026 at the experimental field of the “Farboma selekt” scientific seed-growing farm located in Jomboy district of Samarkand region. A total of 200 barley collection accessions obtained from the international centers ICARDA and CIMMYT, as well as the Institute of Plant Science and the Gallaorol Research and Experimental Station of the Research Institute of Grain and Legume Crops, were studied. The accessions were evaluated for productive tillering, number and weight of grains per spike, 1000-grain weight, yield, earliness, and resistance to diseases, winter conditions and lodging. The study identified valuable barley accessions with high productivity and yield potential. In particular, the Mirzacho‘l, K-22845, K-19985, Temur and K-566244 accessions demonstrated high yield performance. The selected accessions are recommended as valuable initial breeding material for developing new high-yielding, early-maturing and environmentally stress-resistant barley varieties for irrigated lands.</jats:p>

2ead1d54242c055a6be9b67d6bb932a0a527fc9a.abstract: <jats:p>The article studies the formation of plant density in chickpea varieties under different irrigation methods and irrigation regimes. The study examined the effects of furrow, drip and sprinkler irrigation, as well as irrigation regimes of 65–70–60%, 70–75–65% and 75–80–70% of field capacity. The results showed that plant density of the Zumrad and Malhotra chickpea varieties varied depending on the irrigation method and soil moisture regime. The highest plant density was recorded under drip irrigation with an irrigation regime of 75–80–70% of field capacity in the Malhotra variety, reaching 282.7 plants/m² at the beginning of the growing period and 275.3 plants/m² at the end. The obtained results demonstrate the importance of selecting an appropriate irrigation method and soil moisture regime for chickpea cultivation.</jats:p>

ea346533c1c20f87656be5bba609f0064e2f0e05.abstract: <jats:p>This article evaluates the seasonal growth dynamics of low-stem fodder mulberry plantations under the climatic conditions of Uzbekistan in 2025-2026 based on phenological and biometric indicators. The highest morphological and economically valuable traits were recorded during the summer period. The average shoot length was 136 cm in 2025 and 143.0 cm in 2026. Although 33.5% of the shoot length was damaged by frost in the spring of 2026 due to insufficient lignification following late autumn pruning, the plants demonstrated a high regenerative capacity during the summer period. The results indicate the necessity of optimizing pruning times, ensuring regular irrigation, and creating suitable conditions for the complete lignification of shoots before the onset of winter in order to achieve a high mulberry leaf yield.</jats:p>

title: Anisotropic Mamba-CNN Fusion Super-Resolution Network for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma MRI
container-title: International Journal of Information Technology & Decision Making
0bf41e7a8ee282cc3f91407fea1ea50880caa632.abstract: <jats:p>Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) MRI is important for lesion detection and radiotherapy planning. However, routine MRI is constrained by scan time, hardware conditions, and clinical acquisition efficiency, resulting in insufficient spatial resolution and 3D anisotropy. These limitations lead to blurred lesion boundaries, detail loss, and reduced inter-slice continuity. To address these issues, this study proposes an anisotropy-aware framework, termed Anisotropic Mamba-CNN Fusion Super-resolution Network (AMCF-SRNet). The proposed method adopts a dual-branch CNN-Mamba architecture to separately model local textures and long-range contextual dependencies. An explicit feature fusion mechanism is introduced to achieve adaptive integration of heterogeneous features. By these feature fusion operations, it can improve detail recovery, structural continuity, and overall consistency of the reconstructed images. Some typical frameworks, such as 3D Mamba, are selected as the competing methods. Experiments show that AMCF-SRNet provides the best performance, both verified by quantitative metrics and visual quality. Compared with the best competing method, AMCF-SRNet improves 2.55[Formula: see text]dB in PSNR and 0.0268 in SSIM. Meanwhile, ablation studies and computational cost analysis are conducted, proving the efficiency and contributions of each network component. All these results show that AMCF-SRNet can accomplish the reconstruction of NPC MRI and support subsequent diagnosis.</jats:p>

title: Interpretable Finger Vein Identification: Analysis of Fine-tuned Models with Explainable Artificial Intelligence
container-title: International Journal of Information Technology & Decision Making
28fb2182955c16ae0e2b0018164db6f7aebf61bf.abstract: <jats:p>Although convolutional neural networks report near-perfect accuracy in public finger vein datasets, their operational trustworthiness remains a critical, unevaluated blind spot. This study challenges the conventional reliance on accuracy as the primary metric for model viability. It is hypothesized that state-of-the-art models often achieve high scores not by learning robust vascular patterns, but by overfitting to spurious, nonbiometric cues in the dataset background. To expose this vulnerability, an explainability-driven audit is conducted using Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) on eight deep learning models across two benchmark datasets (SDUMLA and UTFVP). The results reveal a significant accuracy-reliability paradox. The highest-accuracy model, Densely Connected Convolutional Networks (DenseNet121-99.84%), is found to be functionally insecure, heavily relying on background artifacts for prediction. Conversely, Extreme Inception (Xception), despite lower raw accuracy, emerges as the most biometrically faithful architecture (Explainability Score: 89%), consistently targeting valid finger vein patterns. Unlike traditional performance-oriented studies, the primary novelty of this research lies in its explainability-driven audit approach, which systematically evaluates the trustworthiness of deep learning models in finger vein recognition, bridging the gap between high accuracy and model interpretability. This discovery demonstrates that high accuracy can mask significant security flaws, making models vulnerable to presentation attacks. Consequently, explainability is established not as a secondary feature, but as a mandatory security metric. It is proposed that future biometric evaluations must adopt interpretability analysis to ensure models characterize the biological trait rather than dataset noise.</jats:p>

title: Feature Interaction-Driven Machine Learning for Hotel Cancellation Prediction: Integrating Bayesian Networks and Gradient Boosting
container-title: International Journal of Information Technology & Decision Making
69e617336e21db9baf297cf5cfa05e723b2c17e6.abstract: <jats:p>Online travel platforms such as Trip.com and Agoda have made it easier to modify or cancel hotel reservations, increasing uncertainty for hotel revenue management. Cancellations can increase room vacancy, destabilize revenue, and raise operating costs. To address these challenges, this study proposes a feature-interaction-enhancement framework that enriches reservation data with interpretable cross-dimensional features designed to capture nonlinear relationships between booking behavior and cancellation risk. Unlike hybrid prediction models that jointly optimize a Bayesian network (BN) and a classifier, the proposed framework uses the BN solely as an auxiliary feature extractor. It generates two meta-features — the posterior cancellation probability and its entropy — which are concatenated with the original and interaction features for downstream prediction. We systematically compare several optimized machine-learning models, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost, and apply SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to the best-performing model to quantify feature contributions and derive operational insights. The experimental results show that the feature-enhanced framework outperforms baselines that rely solely on the original predictors. The resulting risk estimates can help hotels identify high-risk bookings and design targeted interventions, provided they are appropriately calibrated and operationally validated.</jats:p>

title: HMoEFormer: A source-aware heterogeneous mixture-of-experts network for music source separation
container-title: International Journal of Wavelets, Multiresolution and Information Processing
9cd7bd68e8c44577911cd6ef6f416144f47b20f9.abstract: <jats:p>Musical sources exhibit distinct acoustic patterns, motivating differentiated processing of the contextual representations learned by music source separation (MSS) models. This paper proposes a source-aware heterogeneous mixture-of-experts network for joint four-stem MSS. The model retains the band-split axial attention backbone of a transformer with rotary positional embedding and introduces heterogeneous expert transformations at the feed-forward stage following attention. Three expert pathways provide different architectural biases: grouped convolution for the drum-oriented expert, hierarchical convolution with feature-wise gating for the bass-oriented expert and bidirectional recurrent modeling for the vocal-oriented expert. A shared feature projection supplies a common representation, while a content-aware router combines all three expert outputs through dense soft weighting. Under the evaluated compact-backbone and joint four-source training configuration, the proposed model achieves an average signal-to-distortion ratio of 6.76 decibels on the 50-song test set of an uncompressed 150-song music separation benchmark after 200 epochs. This score exceeds that of the corresponding compact band-split transformer baseline by 2.32 decibels. Ablation studies support the heterogeneous expert design and multi-expert fusion, and routing analysis reveals input-dependent expert preferences consistent with the intended modeling biases. Evaluation on a selected 50-song subset of a separate multi-track music dataset containing 240 recordings yields an improvement of 1.84 decibels over the baseline without additional fine-tuning. These results support source-aware heterogeneous feature transformation as an effective design within the evaluated separation framework.</jats:p>

title: ChavacanoMNMT: Exploring Language Influences in the Multilingual Neural Machine Translation of a Spanish-Based Creole
container-title: ACM Transactions on Asian and Low-Resource Language Information Processing
a3a1301d07c5732d6b5509990d5ed258faad0bef.abstract:
<jats:p>Multilingual Neural Machine Translation (MNMT) enhances low-resource language translation by leveraging related languages, yet its application to Creole languages like Chavacano, a Spanish-based Creole spoken in the Philippines, remains underexplored. This study investigates the influence of Austronesian (Cebuano, Hiligaynon) and Indo-European (Spanish, English) parent languages on Chavacano MNMT performance.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>We fine-tuned an mT5-base model on the ChavacanoMT dataset, which comprises 1,044,185 samples spanning 20 language pairs involving Chavacano and related languages. Ablation experiments were conducted by excluding individual languages from training to evaluate their impact on model performance. Performance was assessed using BLEU, chrF++, and BERTScore metrics, with Paired Bootstrap Resampling applied to determine statistical significance.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study reports that Austronesian languages significantly influence Chavacano translation quality more than Indo-European languages (5 BLEU points,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">p</jats:italic>
                    =0.001). Cebuano and Hiligaynon enhance translation quality (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">p</jats:italic>
                    ⪋0.025), while Spanish contributes less due to structural divergence (VSO vs. SVO) despite Chavacano’s 77% lexical similarity with Spanish. Our model achieves a 17 BLEU point improvement in Chavacano-English translation over prior benchmarks.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>These findings highlight the role of structural similarity in MNMT and inform auxiliary language selection for low-resource Creole translation, contributing new benchmarks and insights for Chavacano NLP.</jats:p>

68b917fda5a9eff858671cf5df73d0cbcce02b1c.abstract: <jats:p>This article investigates the effectiveness of biological fertilizers and resource-saving agrotechnologies for potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) cultivation under the natural, climatic, and soil conditions of the Republic of Karakalpakstan. Based on field experiments, the effects of biological fertilizers on potato plant growth and development, tuber formation, yield, and product quality were evaluated. The results showed that, compared with the control, the application of biofertilizers increased plant height by 8-12% and the number of stems by 10-15%, while the number of tubers per plant increased from 7-8 to 9-11 tubers. Yield increased from 22-24 t/ha to 27-32 t/ha, corresponding to an approximately 21-36% increase compared with the control. The starch content of the tubers was 1,5-2,5 percentage points higher than in the control. In addition, the application of biological fertilizers enhanced soil biological activity and improved the uptake of nutrients by plants. The findings demonstrate that integrating biological fertilizers with resource-saving agrotechnologies is a promising agroecological approach for improving the efficiency of potato production under the conditions of Karakalpakstan.</jats:p>

ba2f8cb62b86caf4dd1d343ac5b4545c93d29a4a.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents the findings of a multi-year study evaluating the effects of convective drying temperatures and processing durations on the dried product yield of six promising fig cultivars — Uzbekskiy zheltiy, Krym 9, Krym 29, Krym 43, Karshinskiy cherniy, and Dalmatskiy, grown under the subtropical conditions of Surkhandarya region. The experimental data revealed that increasing both drying temperature and exposure duration led to a consistent and substantial reduction in fruit yield due to intensive moisture evaporation, ranging from 68.7–77.9% at 40°C after 20 hours down to 8.7–13.7% following profound dehydration at 60°C after 80 hours. Distinct cultivar-specific dehydration kinetics were observed, governed by pericarp thickness, tissue density, and initial dry matter content. Uzbekskiy zheltiy (average yield of 42.04%) and Dalmatskiy (39.17%) exhibited notable technological stability and uniform moisture release, whereas Krym 29 and Krym 43 demonstrated rapid desiccation, achieving target moisture levels 10–15 hours earlier than the other cultivars. While drying at 40–45°C required excessive processing times (>70–80 hours) accompanied by high energy expenditure, exposure to 60°C provoked rapid surface hardening (case-hardening) and sensory degradation.</jats:p>

0402454848d22af8452bc62a18a6a906a55f4943.abstract: <jats:p>The study investigated the technology for obtaining chitosan from the shell of the long-clawed crayfish (Pontastacus leptodactylus), which is widely distributed in the Tudakul Reservoir, as well as its antimicrobial activity. Chitosan with a molecular weight of 780 kDa and a degree of deacetylation of 84% was obtained and demonstrated high antimicrobial activity against Candida albicans and Escherichia coli. It was established that crayfish shells are a promising local raw material for chitosan production.</jats:p>

20621b086e6429a08ccd61738cb176ab180ed213.abstract: <jats:p>The dependence of stem height of sunflower hybrids KK-52 F1, Dushko F1 and Svetlana F1 on mineral fertilizer rates under meadow-alluvial soil conditions was evaluated by correlation, regression and covariance analysis. A very strong positive relationship (r = 0.998–1.000) was established and linear and quadratic regression equations were derived. Covariance analysis (ANCOVA) showed that 61.2% of total variation was attributable to sowing time, 25.6% to fertilizer rate and 13.1% to hybrid genotype.</jats:p>

dfc5711edf697ec31e1af016dd9653f9531d63e6.abstract: <jats:p>The study investigated the influence of agroecological factors on the growth, development, and bioproductivity of Silphium perfoliatum L. in the Samarkand and Andijan regions during 2023-2025. The highest germination rate under autumn sowing was 75.1%, while the optimal seed placement depth was 1,5-2,0 cm. Under the 90×90 cm planting scheme, plant height reached 310 cm, seed yield was 9,7 c/ha, and green mass yield reached 1237,8 c/ha.</jats:p>

title: Bridging or Widening the Gap? AI Policies and Social Justice in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
038583ab9446f69693d78ffd45b815c6af816060.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as a means to improve educational quality, efficiency, and equity. However, when introduced into systems already shaped by inequality, AI risks reproducing rather than reducing social injustice. This chapter examines whether AI policies in education bridge or widen existing gaps, drawing on Nancy Fraser's framework of redistribution, recognition, and representation. Through a comparative analysis of supranational frameworks and national strategies in the United States, China, India, and Türkiye, the chapter identifies persistent tensions between innovation-driven agendas and justice-oriented goals. The findings suggest that equity is often framed in technocratic terms, while issues of power, participation, and accountability remain marginal. The chapter concludes by proposing a justice-centered policy evaluation framework that emphasizes democratic governance, cultural responsiveness, and the right to contest or refuse harmful AI systems.</jats:p>

It looks into how human computer interaction, visual communication and information design together support healthy user experiences in clinical training scenarios. The chapter discusses immersive technologies such as VR/AR/MR/XR and simulation-based learning systems as environments for experiential and competency-based education. The ethical and social implications, including bias, accountability, trust, and the impact of AI on clinical judgment, are critically discussed. By integrating AI technologies with instructional design and technology-enhanced learning strategies, this chapter offers insights into building responsible, engaging, and future-oriented healthcare education ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: AI Universal Design for Learning and Inclusive Teaching Practices
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
96194347b26c0eee3dabcf71df528ca9f2951b64.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), universal design for learning (UDL), and inclusive teaching practices in higher education to enhance institutional performance. It examines how AI supports personalised learning, accessibility, and differentiated instruction aligned with UDL principles. Using conceptual analysis, the chapter shows that inclusive teaching improves engagement, retention, and equitable outcomes. It also situates inclusive pedagogy within social justice frameworks. Findings indicate that AI strengthens flexibility and responsiveness, while UDL promotes proactive accessibility for diverse learners. However, challenges such as algorithmic bias, data privacy, and unequal access remain critical considerations.</jats:p>

title: Agentic AI for Inclusive Assistive Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
64f993336be792d7c4b612d79a8d17390e1701fa.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming assistive technologies, yet many systems remain reactive, fragmented, and insufficiently personalized for individuals with disabilities and neurodivergent conditions. This chapter examines the architectural, design, and governance foundations of trustworthy agentic assistive systems. It synthesizes limitations of conventional approaches, including restricted adaptability, low interoperability, and weak support for user autonomy, and introduces a taxonomy of agentic architectures to guide scalable deployment. The chapter proposes a multi-agent framework integrating multimodal interaction, hybrid reasoning, explainable AI, and health-aware data to enable context-sensitive support. It further addresses privacy, ethical governance, and responsible institutional adoption while outlining future research directions. By bridging architectural innovation with human-centered design, this work advances a forward-looking vision for inclusive intelligent environments.</jats:p>

title: Empowering Visually Disabled Users Through Web Accessibility
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
e7b77c9fed0598c385d0917aa449f2d031fae972.abstract: <jats:p>The Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), often categorised as Institutions of Eminence (IoE) in India, are set as the standards of measurement for the rest of academia. In this regard, the purpose of this paper is to evaluate the accessibility standard of the IIT Library websites in terms of the perceivable guidelines of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (v. 2.1) using the Siteimprove Accessibility Checker. To improve the level of analytical precision based on the policy, technological, and user layers' conceptual frameworks, the study employs an artificial intelligence (AI)-based evaluation. The results indicate that there are considerable accessibility barriers in the various success criteria, such as non-textual content, information organisation, colour use, contrast ratio, and text images. Functional and visually organised designs notwithstanding, there are still critical gaps in ensuring the inclusion of visually impaired users. It also suggests the use of evidence-supported measures to enhance digital inclusivity and fair access in academic library settings.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Mindfulness-Based Mental Health Support for Mothers of Children With Autism
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
9d38710756c4d8e79d2247e02869d371d633cd4f.abstract: <jats:p>Mothers caring for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder often face ongoing stress, emotional challenges, and significant caregiving responsibilities. These factors can affect family dynamics and the quality of support services available for disabilities. Although traditional counselling can offer some psychological relief, it may lack personalization, scalability, or ongoing monitoring. This chapter presents a mindfulness-based intervention enhanced by artificial intelligence, utilizing established techniques like Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction to provide flexible and accessible mental health resources. By combining AI with structured mindfulness practices, this approach seeks to improve emotional regulation, promote increased caregiver engagement, and foster better collaboration with disability service organizations. The chapter emphasizes that AI-enhanced mindfulness can serve as a valuable resource to bolster caregiver resilience and facilitate more efficient and responsive delivery of disability services.</jats:p>

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Financial Accountability and Disability-Inclusive Resource Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
0d7a80fdfad7d743e38ff0f3aa9123c3f7b1ecd3.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming institutional financial management by improving transparency, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making. This chapter examines how AI strengthens budgeting, financial reporting, fraud detection, procurement, and performance measurement while advancing disability-inclusive resource management. It discusses the conceptual foundations of AI adoption, relevant theoretical perspectives, and practical applications that support equitable resource allocation and accessibility investments. The chapter also addresses governance, ethical considerations, data privacy, implementation strategies, emerging technologies, and persistent challenges affecting AI adoption. It concludes that responsible AI implementation, supported by effective governance, skilled personnel, quality data, and inclusive policies, can enhance financial accountability, optimise institutional performance, and promote sustainable disability-inclusive financial management across educational and public institutions.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Assistive Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
b83110c46123ad08d922ea8250e5266e1fe8dd02.abstract: <jats:p>Higher education institutions worldwide are increasingly prioritizing inclusive learning environments that accommodate the diverse needs of students with disabilities. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have introduced transformative opportunities for developing assistive ecosystems that support accessibility, personalized learning, and institutional efficiency. AI-enabled technologies—including intelligent tutoring systems, speech recognition, computer vision, and predictive analytics—can significantly enhance disability support services while improving educational outcomes and institutional performance. This chapter explores the concept of AI-enabled assistive ecosystems within higher education and examines how integrated AI technologies can support students with physical, sensory, cognitive, and learning disabilities. The chapter analyzes the potential benefits of AI-driven accessibility tools, institutional data analytics, and adaptive learning platforms for promoting inclusive education.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Early Identification of Learning Disabilities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
043143cf4cb7b04ac142cd26e901f7ca8ddd2099.abstract: <jats:p>Learning disabilities (LDs) need to be identified at an early age so that they can be addressed promptly so that they can utilize their academic performance and inclusive learning. Conventional diagnostic procedures are mostly reactive, time-consuming and subjective and rely on the use of standardized tests, teacher observations, as well as, clinical evaluations. The development of artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics allows active risk screening based on machine learning and deep learning, and explainable AI models. This chapter investigates predictive pipelines, benchmarking models (SVM) and random forests, (CNN and LSTM) and validation, ethics, privacy, and adaptive intervention frameworks in an attempt to encourage equitable, transparent, and scalable learning intervention systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Supported Inclusive Teaching, Learning, and Assessment Practices
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
f7d5b07d3572f89cb66a9323a13e52d04b0ad451.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming educational systems, offering innovative pathways for enhancing inclusive teaching, learning and assessment practices. In the context of disability support, AI-driven tools provide opportunities to personalize instruction, improve accessibility and strengthen institutional performance through data-informed decision-making. However, despite these potentials, some educational institutions face challenges in effectively integrating AI into inclusive education practices. This chapter therefore examines how AI-supported instructional strategies, adaptive learning systems and intelligent assessment tools can address diverse learner needs. It critically analyzes ethical concerns, implementation barriers and capacity gaps associated with AI adoption in education. The chapter proposes a conceptual framework linking AI integration, inclusive pedagogy and institutional outcomes. It further provides actionable suggestions for stakeholders seeking to leverage AI for sustainable disability support and improved institutional effectiveness.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Early Warning Systems for the Psychosocial Wellbeing of Students With Hearing Loss in Inclusive Educational Settings
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
129abc45062d56b3fbb0027ea16533ce2776036a.abstract: <jats:p>Students with hearing loss in inclusive settings frequently face psychosocial challenges including social isolation, communication fatigue, and emotional disengagement that develop gradually and evade conventional monitoring systems focused solely on academic metrics. This chapter proposes an AI-enabled early warning system (EWS) to proactively identify emotional distress and social withdrawal among deaf or hard of hearing (DHH) students. Integrating multimodal data streams, machine learning, transformer-based NLP, and explainable AI (XAI), the system generates actionable risk indicators for educators and counselors. Grounded in Social Inclusion Theory, Universal Design for Learning, Ecological Systems Theory, and Affective Computing Theory, it functions as a human-centered decision-support platform rather than a surveillance tool. Ethical dimensions including data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, and informed consent are critically examined alongside a roadmap for evidence-based implementation.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Assistive Technologies in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
7510ca4a3f66341f01e483ae97917d37a915e525.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education by enabling intelligent assistive technologies that enhance learning outcomes for students with disabilities. This chapter examines the landscape of AI-driven assistive tools—including speech recognition, adaptive learning platforms, natural language processing, and predictive analytics—and their role in advancing inclusive education. Drawing on recent systematic reviews and empirical studies, it critically evaluates opportunities such as personalized accommodation, improved accessibility, and universal design for learning (UDL) integration, alongside challenges including algorithmic bias, data privacy, and digital equity. Frameworks for ethical AI deployment and institutional policy recommendations are presented. The chapter concludes with future directions for sustainable, human-centered AI assistive ecosystems in higher education.</jats:p>

title: Assistive Tools to Intelligent Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
2d0c2eecb37bb3dc4dd370074acc4a5b42bfc597.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is changing how disability assistance systems work by combining personalized institutional services with proactive, data-driven methods. This chapter reviews the old support systems that often react slowly and create extra work and looks at how AI tools like predictive analytics, natural language processing, and intelligent decision-support systems can improve how institutions operate and provide help for disabilities. It discusses applications including automated management of reasonable accommodations, AI-powered virtual assistants, and accessible learning environments that enable earlier identification of support needs. The chapter also analyzes how institutions can use AI-generated insights to optimize resource allocation, strengthen regulatory compliance, and operationalize inclusive policies. Finally, it addresses key ethical challenges, including algorithmic bias, data privacy, and disability-inclusive design, and outlines principles for responsible implementation of AI in disability assistance.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Disability Support in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
00ce053ee1c65f0ed357fb21fa1391ad7c7cc4f7.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming disability support in higher education by enabling personalization, predictive analytics, and systemic change. This chapter explores AI tools—such as adaptive learning platforms, NLP assistants, early-alert systems, and automated accommodations—used to address barriers faced by students with diverse disabilities. Grounded in Universal Design for Learning and the social model of disability, it reframes AI as a means to enhance student autonomy rather than just improve services. It also examines risks like algorithmic bias, surveillance, and data misuse. The chapter proposes a governance framework emphasizing equity, transparency, and student agency, and outlines key directions for future research.</jats:p>

title: A Critical Exploration of How Artificial Intelligence Enhances Accommodation for Learners With Learning Barriers
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
2b033bfd9e3d57fefca89685cea1b21c53f84a3a.abstract: <jats:p>The purpose of this chapter is to critically explore how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning. The chapter identify sources and types of barriers to learning, pointing out the relevance of AI to teaching and learning as research studies have shown that it can personalize instruction, automate timely feedback, generate formative assessment and identify learning achievement and challenges. The chapter shows the readers how AI can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning by using planned Individual Educational Programme (IEP), data-driven analysis, adaptive learning platforms that dynamically adjust content difficulty, sequencing, and presentation formats in real time. Also, AI-powered tools are used such as speech-to-text, text-to-speech, to establish flexibility, personalization and promotes equitable participation for all learners to uphold equity, ethics, and human values in education.</jats:p>

title: Solar Thermal District Heating and Cooling for Smart, Sustainable, AI-Optimized Cities
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
5fb7b6f93a03dabd2aadb285a6f2da9c7a9936b8.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid urbanization and climate imperatives place cities at the center of energy transformation, yet thermal demand roughly half of urban energy end-use remains under addressed by electricity focused renewable strategies. This chapter, per the authors, examines solar thermal district heating and cooling (STDHC) systems as foundational infrastructure for sustainable smart cities. It reviews collector technologies and seasonal thermal storage configurations, then analyzes integration across the physical, cyber, and application layers of smart city architecture, emphasizing digital twins, IoT sensing, and machine-learning optimization including model predictive control and reinforcement learning. International case studies from Canada, Denmark, Croatia, and China demonstrate solar fractions above 50% and substantial carbon reductions. Lifecycle, cost, and energy-justice analyses benchmark performance and equity, while the closing sections identify deployment barriers and propose a research agenda spanning compact storage, federated learning, and policy alignment with SDG 7 and SDG 11.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Smart Microgrids and Electric Mobility Integration for Sustainable Urban Energy Systems in Smart Cities
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
b5fbd81ff64d56f595d8b18611cc2706c6345a69.abstract: <jats:p>For the development of sustainable urban energy systems in smart cities, this chapter focuses on the integration of electric mobility systems with AI-driven smart microgrids. It demonstrates the contribution of electric vehicles (EVs) through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities and variable demand, while smart microgrids enable effective management of dispersed energy resources and dispersed energy generation. The role of Artificial intelligence towards energy distribution optimization, real-time decision-making, and demand forecasting is emphasized along with identifying major obstacles including consumer acceptance, regulatory restrictions, interoperability problems, and discussing worldwide policy trends, the chapter provides an integrated conceptual framework offering insights into how the sustainability, dependability, and energy efficiency might improve urban settings through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), EVs, and microgrids.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Federated Learning Frameworks for Privacy-Preserving Smart Urban Energy Management
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
eadd50d14a20212bca5c4790316df5a2305aab8d.abstract: <jats:p>The growing complexity of urban energy systems with smartness requires intelligent solutions that are privacy friendly to manage the distributed energy resources efficiently. This chapter introduces a federated learning model that is AI-powered and in this system, model training is performed in an intelligent grid, micro grid, and IoT-based devices, without the exchange of raw data. The strategy improves accuracy in load forecasting, efficiency of energy use, and lessens the amount of overhead in communication besides maintaining data privacy and security. The framework combines edge computing and state-of-the-art AI to promote scalable and adaptive energy management to add to sustainable, resilient, and human-centric smart city ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Data Sovereignty and Algorithmic Governance in Developing Economies
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
6fdbeb58e96e829a460768ed1eba7412a41afc2e.abstract: <jats:p>Data is among the most contested resources of the twenty-first century. Citizens in developing and middle-income economies generate it constantly through mobile transactions, health services, and social platforms. Yet, the infrastructure that processes it and the governance frameworks that regulate it have largely been designed elsewhere. This chapter examines data sovereignty and algorithmic governance as twin pillars of an equitable digital transformation agenda, using South Africa as its primary lens. It argues that three connected interventions are essential: sovereign infrastructure architecture, algorithmic transparency and accountability, and genuine community participation in governance design. Drawing on socio-technical systems theory and institutional economics, the chapter demonstrates that data sovereignty cannot be achieved through any single instrument but requires deliberate alignment between technical architecture, governance institutions, and participatory process to produce inclusive Fourth Industrial Revolution outcomes in structurally unequal economies.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Green Promises
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
f771357c6994b1b3d1a5a4ea4db933888583f4ae.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and sustainability in tourism within the broader context of Industry 4.0 and ongoing digital transformation processes. While AI-driven technologies are widely recognized for their capacity to enhance operational efficiency, optimize resource utilization, and support sustainable development goals, they simultaneously introduce significant conceptual, ethical, and governance-related challenges. Drawing on a socio-technical perspective, this study moves beyond purely technological or outcome-oriented approaches and explores how artificial intelligence reshapes not only the operationalization of sustainability but also its meaning, representation, and lived experience within tourism systems. The chapter introduces the concept of rehumanizing sustainability as a conceptual and practical framework for addressing these challenges. This approach emphasizes the reintegration of human values, agency, and experiential dimensions into AI-driven systems.</jats:p>

title: AFRIKA TARIGʻIDA JOʻXORI PASHSHASI (ANTHOMYIIDAE)GA QARSHI KURASHNING BIOLOGIK SAMARADORLIGI
container-title: Agro ilm
e5acdeb20d729b725992dc8343811299e03d8c4b.abstract: <jats:p>The corn moth overwinters primarily in the soil in the pupal stage. In the spring, as temperatures rise, the adults emerge and lay eggs on newly sown plots. Upon hatching, the larvae penetrate the soil and feed on germinating seeds, root collars, and young stems. As a result, seedling growth ceases or the plants wither. Development takes 20—40 days, depending on climatic conditions. Most species produce 2—4 generations per year. This article examines the development of the corn moth (Anthomyiidae) and the biological efficacy of control measures against it.</jats:p>

18cd92c73dac5749719c45c1bd85abd95a604d36.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents information on the characteristics of Simmental cows belonging to different production types. The study found that the age at first calving was 789.5 days for cows of the dairy type and 795.1 days for those of the dairy-beef type; these figures were 11.1 and 5.5 days lower, respectively, than the age at first calving for cows of the beef-dairy type. Additionally, the service period lasted 78.3 days for dairy-type cows and 81.2 days for dairy-beef-type cows—4.2 and 1.3 days shorter, respectively, than the service period for beef-dairy-type cows. Research findings regarding the duration of the service period indicate that the cow itself is a primary factor determining reproductive performance; this highlights the importance of effectively utilizing cows of dairy and dual-purpose (dairy-beef) types for milk production.</jats:p>

98e848880df63ba98ca2e56f8de2bb1390a0aefa.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of a study on the morphological characteristics of the udder in local goats and first-generation (F1) crossbreds obtained by crossing local does with imported purebred Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks, as well as with locally bred Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks.</jats:p>

372cb4c69dc68f61038297f6ed9d9f1ebba38b16.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of a study of milk productivity in local goats and first-generation (F₁) crossbred goats obtained by crossing local does with purebred Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks imported from abroad, as well as with Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks produced through local selection. A comparative analysis of these indicators was conducted between local goats and F₁ crossbreds.</jats:p>

title: ТЎҒОНСИЗ СУВ ОЛИШ ШАРОИТИДА МАГИСТРАЛ КАНАЛ КИРИШ ҚИСМИДА ЛОЙҚА ЧЎКИНДИЛАРИ ДИНАМИКАСИНИ ТАҲЛИЛ ҚИЛИШ ВА ЗЕМСНАРЯДЛАР ИШЛАШ САМАРАДОРЛИГИНИ ОШИРИШ
container-title: Agro ilm
5f254fc5f7b7f246b8ec58bd1d3b1fca692abe1d.abstract: <jats:p>The article examines the dynamics of sediment deposition at the intake section of the Qarshi Main Canal (QMC) under damless (free) water intake from the Amudarya River, together with the role of dredgers in the overall volume of cleaning works. Based on field monitoring data, the distribution of sediment along the canal length, as well as the technical condition and placement of the fleet of 17 dredgers along the canal, were analysed. It was found that the PK 0-40 segment of the canal intake accumulates more than 85% of the total sediment volume, making it the most heavily loaded section. Recommendations are proposed for the rational placement of dredgers along the canal and for adjusting the cleaning schedule to seasonal sediment inflow.</jats:p>

title: ШЎРЛАНМАГАН ТУПРОҚЛАР ШАРОИТИДА КУЗГИ БУҒДОЙНИ СУҒОРИШ МУДДАТЛАРИНИ БЕЛГИЛАШДА БАРГ ҲУЖАЙРА ШИРАСИ КОНЦЕНТРАЦИЯСИ ВА ТУПРОҚ НАМЛИГИ ДИНАМИКАСИ
container-title: Agro ilm
f9b8de5eb1f617501ce4215003adb91c374cb193.abstract: <jats:p>The article evaluates the pre-irrigation soil moisture regimes (70-70-70, 75-75-75, and 80-80-80% of FC) and the dynamics of leaf cell sap concentration (CSC) in winter wheat grown on non-saline soils during 2020–2021. The results indicated that as pre-irrigation soil moisture increased, leaf CSC values proportionally decreased (13.82–16.31%), whereas toward the end of the growing season, values rose to 17.36–19.50% due to physiological tissue senescence. The study substantiates the high efficacy of using a refractometric method for rapid determination of irrigation timing based on CSC to enhance water-use efficiency. </jats:p>

title: EFFICIENCY OF SPRINKLER IRRIGATION FOR CARROT PRODUCTION ON TYPICAL GREY SOILS OF THE TASHKENT REGION
container-title: Agro ilm
379586c39b8fc86fe6bcbc1041c1fd88ba0b9658.abstract: <jats:p>This study evaluated sprinkler irrigation for carrot production on typical grey soils in the Tashkent region of Uzbekistan. Field experiments with the “Mirzoyi kizil” variety compared furrow irrigation with sprinkler intensities of 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 mm min⁻¹. The highest yield, 29.2 t ha⁻¹, was obtained at 0.4 mm min⁻¹, compared with 22.7 t ha⁻¹ under furrow irrigation.</jats:p>

title: СУҒОРИШ УСУЛЛАРИНИ ТАНЛАШ ВА РАЙОНЛАШТИРИШНИНГ ТАКОМИЛЛАШТИРИЛГАН УСУЛИ

7707643f49ec6b66f6b8c042879406a317a9807e.abstract: <jats:p>The paper proposes an improved approach for selecting irrigation methods by jointly assessing relief, reclamation conditions, soil and hydrophysical properties, agroclimatic conditions, and water source and quality. The final suitability class is determined by the most limiting factor. Separating current and potential suitability and using GIS zoning makes it possible to select irrigation technologies that better match local conditions.</jats:p>

title: SUGʻORILADIGAN BOʻZ - OʻTLOQI TUPROQLARNING AGROKIMYOVIY XOSSALARI VA SANOAT CHIQINDILARI TA’SIRIDA OGʻIR METALLAR BILAN IFLOSLANISHI
container-title: Agro ilm
ba0ed90ab84fabb0583adc409521ff67536ed2c8.abstract: <jats:p>This article highlights the agrochemical properties of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils of Sharaf Rashidovsky district of the Jizzakh Free Economic Zone (JEZ), reserves of humus, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and potassium. There is a high probability of heavy metal pollution in the region near industrial zones, free economic zones, and irrigation networks. Since these soils have a relatively humic layer, as well as a unique water-retaining structure, heavy metals can accumulate in the soil and negatively affect its agrochemical properties. Heavy metals adhere to soil colloids and retain their activity in the soil for a long time. In the soil under study, the lead content of Pb is 40-80 mg/kg (the norm is 32 mg/kg or more), cadmium CD is 0.5 - 2.0 mg/kg (the norm is 0.5 mg/kg or more), zinc Zn is 150-220 mg/kg (the norm is 100 mg/kg or more). This situation indicates an increase in the level of pollution combined with salinization and carbonate content of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils.</jats:p>

title: ПУШТА ТЕПАСИГА МИНИМАЛ ИШЛОВ БЕРАДИГАН РОТАЦИОН ЮМШАТКИЧ ПАРАМЕТРЛАРИНИ МАҚБУЛЛАШТИРИШ
