title: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
607e01bc517c5399388e06837788a54fe973b640.abstract:
<jats:p>The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) provides resolved stellar abundances and star formation histories  (SFHs) that can be used together to test models of dwarf-galaxy chemical evolution.
We investigated if the non-monotonic APOGEE $ Mg / Fe -- Fe / H $ sequence can be explained by a hybrid history that combines a second gas-infall episode with a temporary increase in star formation efficiency (SFE).
We selected 4933 LMC red giant branch stars from APOGEE-2 DR17. We fitted an adaptively binned median Mg sequence with the two-zone open-box code . The formal fitting objective contained only the Mg sequence. The metallicity distribution function (MDF), one-dimensional abundance distributions, SFH, present-day mass partition, star formation rate (SFR), and supernova (SN) rate were retained as posterior diagnostics. OMEGA+
The best-fitting model reproduces the Mg sequence with a root mean square (RMS) residual of 0.01 dex and also gives a close posterior match to O. It contains two delayed-tau infall episodes, with the second beginning at t_2=10.39 Gyr and with an integrated mass ratio of M_2/M_1=0.159, followed by a temporary Gaussian SFE enhancement centered at t=11.91 Gyr. The second infall is represented by a mixture of enriched and primordial gas. The model reproduces the timing of the late SFH enhancement and yields a present SFR within the adopted comparison range.
A hybrid second-infall and SFE enhancement history is a plausible scenario for reproducing the observed LMC Mg median sequence. Our fit explains the LMC evolution fairly well, but the remaining small MDF, mass, and SN rate discrepancies suggest that a selection-function-aware treatment of the stellar distributions is required for a stricter comparison.</jats:p>

title: A neural-network model for finding correlations in astrochemical space
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
421dace86fb494a31f092362923a0cee1c76d657.abstract: <jats:p>The detection of new interstellar molecules is a central objective of astrochemistry, and arguably the most transformative development in the field over the past decade has been the dramatic increase in both the number and diversity of detected species. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing models, we developed a machine-learning pipeline, in line with recent approaches reported in the literature, to establish relationships between molecular structures, encoded as chemical strings, and molecular column densities in the prototypical dark cloud TMC-1. The workflow generates astrochemically informed embeddings that can be employed in subsequent supervised learning tasks. In this work, these representations are used within a neural-network framework to perform column-density regression on both the original molecular inventory and out-of-distribution species. The resulting model achieves mean squared error values of 0.17 and 0.58 and mean absolute error values of 0.29 and 0.59, all expressed in logarithmic units of the column density, together with coefficients of determination of 0.88 and 0.51 for the train+validation and validation datasets, respectively. The latent vectors learned by the model represent a rich mathematical object that captures not only the underlying chemical relations but also the potential interstellar detectability of the molecule. Using these vectors in molecules obtained from systematic permutations of the TMC-1 inventory allowed us to identify several promising candidates for future detection in this cloud, together with a large number of apolar species. Furthermore, by training the model on datasets reflecting different historical epochs of molecular detections in TMC-1, we show that recent molecular detections have substantially reshaped our understanding of interstellar chemistry in a transformative, rather than incremental, way. Beyond the accurate prediction of column-density trends for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution molecules, the latent-space representations produced by the model provide a stepping stone for developing new forms of data-driven astrochemical intuition and exploration.</jats:p>

title: Towards a new model of the compact triple system łambda Tauri I. Improved periods and preliminary elements of the triple system
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
43cd7848f6594d5caa0166684f329b55f4e7bebb.abstract: <jats:p>We analysed our new radial velocity measurements and photometric observations (covering a time interval of 46838 days and 39100 days, respectively) as well as those from previous studies to derive accurate ephemerides for both orbits of the compact triple system łae. In the case of the inner eclipsing subsystem, we obtained a linear ephemeris of T_ ̊m min.I = ̊m HJD ,2440998.86069(35)+3 = E, improving the accuracy of the previous solutions by more than an order of magnitude. This allowed us to reproduce well all available light curve minima, including the first one recorded in 1844. Furthermore, the period of the outer subsystem, determined from radial velocity analysis, appears to be constant over the interval of available observations, with the corresponding linear ephemeris being T_ ̊m periast. ̊m HJD ,2456822.5(3.6)+33 E,. Assuming near coplanarity of the inner and outer orbits, we estimated the preliminary physical properties of the whole system. We found that the secondary of the inner subsystem is filling or nearly filling its Roche lobe. We used the long-term stability of the eclipsing subsystem period to place a strong upper limit on the rate of the proposed episodic mass transfer to its primary component. Our results constitute a preparatory step for a follow-up study that will also include an analysis of a rich collection of optical spectro-interferometric observations and use a full-fledged numerical model to describe the evolution of the orbital architecture of the system. Particular attention will be focused on determining the inner orbit forced eccentricity and understanding the absence of the apsidal advance of the outer orbit in our present solution.</jats:p>

title: A five-field mixed formulation for the fully dynamic Biot-Brinkman model
container-title: ESAIM: Mathematical Modelling and Numerical Analysis
daf3b1b47b687feb865f05abcf7a6127a66b4d05.abstract: <jats:p>We propose and analyze a mixed formulation for the fully dynamic Biot--Brinkman system, which models the coupled effects of internal viscous diffusion and deformation of the porous skeleton. The classical formulation is expressed in terms of displacement, fluid velocity, and pore pressure. In this work, we reformulate the problem in terms of the fluid velocity, pore pressure, and poroelastic stress tensor, together with two additional variables: the structural velocity and the rotation rate. In particular, we eliminate the solid displacement and the rotation tensor from the set of primary variables. Both quantities are subsequently recovered by a simple post-processing step. This yields a five-field mixed formulation. We establish existence and uniqueness of a weak solution and derive stability bounds based on the Babu\v{s}ka--Brezzi theory for perturbed saddle-point problems, as well as on the theoretical framework developed by Showalter for semilinear degenerate evolution equations. We then develop a semidiscrete continuous-in-time approximation based on stable mixed finite elements. Moreover, employing a backward Euler time discretization, we introduce a fully discrete finite element scheme. We prove that both schemes are well-posed, derive stability bounds, and establish the corresponding error estimates. Finally, we numerically verify the theoretical convergence rates and perform classical benchmark tests to illustrate the robustness and versatility of the method across different domains and parameter regimes.</jats:p>

title: CONCEPTUALIZING THE MULTIMODAL APPROACH IN FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING METHODOLOGY
container-title: Еволюція наукового знання: сучасні парадигми, методи та концептуальні засади досліджень: збірник наукових праць з матеріалами I Міжнародної наукової конференції (м. Чернігів, Україна; 10 листопада 2026)
d6aad0d99fe5718108ef56eab10bfeac152fb7da.abstract: <jats:p>The dynamic shift in the contemporary communication landscape underscores that alphabetic text alone no longer dominates meaning-making in foreign language education. Rooted in the foundational theoretical ideas of the New London Group, multimodality reflects how modern interaction relies on the interplay of two or more communication modes within a single text. When considering foreign language teaching methodology, a mode must be conceptualized as an organized set of semiotic resources-specifically en-compassing linguistic, visual, aural, gestural, and spatial dimensions. Recognizing how these distinct modes operate allows educators to move beyond traditional monomodal boundaries and design interactive learning environ-ments that reflect real-world language use. This changing nature of digital communication necessarily demands a broader understanding of literacy itself. Traditional definitions centered strictly on reading and writing printed words prove insufficient for navigating today’s textual world.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Model-Centric Object Detection: Mitigating Scale Bias Through Object-Size-Aware Dataset Partitioning
container-title: Iraqi Journal for Computers and Informatics
a2bffc37ee08bd944c965234a2e662b5685fd12c.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable object-detection evaluation is essential because reported performance depends not only on detector architecture but also on whether training, validation, and testing subsets adequately represent the object-scale characteristics of the data. However, conventional dataset partitioning often ignores object-size distribution, which can introduce scale bias and produce unstable or misleading estimates of model generalization. This study investigates whether object-size-aware dataset partitioning can improve the representativeness and reliability of detector evaluation without modifying the detector architecture. Two license-plate datasets were examined under four partitioning scenarios: natural unsorted splitting, descending size-ordered splitting, stratified size-descending splitting, and size-aware stratified sampling using strict quantized and hybrid semi-stratified variants. After partitioning, subset representativeness was assessed using Kullback-Leibler divergence and normalized Earth Mover’s Distance, while the nano variant of You Only Look Once version 11 was used as a fixed detector and trained under identical conditions at 640 × 640 resolution for 100 epochs. Performance was evaluated primarily using mean average precision over intersection-over-union thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, supported by mean average precision at 0.50, precision, recall, and F1-score. Size-ordered splitting reduced the primary metric to 0.124 in Dataset 1 and as low as 0.005 in Dataset 2, whereas size-aware stratification recovered competitive values of 0.523 and 0.477, respectively. These findings indicate that dataset partitioning is a consequential data-level design factor and can support more dependable benchmarking for automated license-plate recognition, intelligent transportation, traffic monitoring, and surveillance applications.</jats:p>

title: The challenge of AI dependence: exploring its impact on cognitive autonomy and elaboration in creative performance
container-title: Information Technology & People
5d10468ae5a26c2d8ac92ce1ad78fb5842569e0a.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As artificial intelligence advances and its application scenarios continue to expand, human–artificial intelligence interaction grows increasingly close. While artificial intelligence brings convenience, it also raises concerns that it may weaken users' cognitive autonomy. To investigate this issue. This study aims to explore the composition of AI dependence and its impact on cognitive autonomy and specific aspects of creative performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study draws on cognitive evaluation theory and the elaboration likelihood model to construct a dual-pathway model with instrumental dependence and affective dependence as core variables. The model explains the formation mechanisms of the two types of artificial intelligence dependence and their differential effects on cognitive autonomy. It also preliminarily examines their potential role in the elaboration dimension of creative performance. A two-stage mixed-method design was employed to test the model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Study 1 found that perceived trust mainly had a positive effect on instrumental dependence. Different dimensions of interactivity differentially affected affective dependence and cognitive autonomy. Mediation analysis further confirmed the core mediating role of Dependence. Study 2, a small-sample exploratory experiment, re-tested selected hypotheses and found a possible negative effect of instrumental dependence on the elaboration dimension of creative performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The main theoretical contribution of this study lies in revealing the dual-pathway formation mechanisms of artificial intelligence dependence and the reshaping effects of different types of dependence on cognitive autonomy. It also preliminarily explores the potential effects of dependence on elaboration performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The dual-pathway dependence model constructed in this study offers practical implications for understanding how long-term use of artificial intelligence affects cognitive autonomy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Crosslingual Writing in Language Teaching
9e6426d45d69c974bab1778b2c7e3cd8b90fece6.abstract: <jats:p>Writers who read, think, and write across languages need tailored support to navigate the complexities of crosslingual writing. Despite interest in pedagogical translanguaging and the rehabilitation of translation in language teaching, crosslingual writing remains underexplored as it stands at the margins of established disciplinary domains such as additional language instruction, writing pedagogy, and translator education. This Element argues that crosslingual writing is not only an essential skill for plurilingual communication, but also a powerful tool for language and writing development and deeper learning. Situating crosslingual writing within the trans/plurilingual turn and combining theoretical, empirical, and pedagogical insights from language (in) education, writing instruction, and translation studies, this Element identifies tools, strategies, and digital literacies for AI-powered crosslingual writing. It further explores how crosslingual writing can be systematically integrated into language curricula, offering practical strategies for pedagogical task design, scaffolding activities, and crosslingual writing assessment.</jats:p>

title: Pedagogic Tasks for The Language Classroom
fe4a22b649082c599359c568471c55f598d8057c.abstract: <jats:p>The purpose of this Element is to bridge research and classroom practice by presenting clear actionable strategies for how to design and implement pedagogic tasks from a task-based language teaching (TBLT) perspective. The Element is intended to benefit practitioners in English as a second language/foreign language (ESL, EFL) and world language classrooms as well as researchers who wish to use tasks or who wish to gain a better grasp of the interface between research and practice. We focus specifically on pedagogic tasks, which are approximations of real-world tasks that teachers can readily implement in their language classrooms. The Element is organized around a set of seven key principles that are supported by theoretical and empirical research in the field of SLA and illustrated through examples. Content covers fundamental concepts such as common task outcomes and task types, communicative gaps, task difficulty, scaffolding, focus on form, feedback, task engagement, and assessment.</jats:p>

title: BinauralLM: spatial prompted text-to-binaural audio generation with large language model
container-title: Journal on Audio, Speech, and Music Processing
19e57fa93b910b6cf942cda62ef61b5a1dc05797.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Binaural audio is a practical spatial audio format for headphone playback and is widely used in immersive media such as games, VR/AR, and interactive multimedia. Currently, binaural audio is still largely obtained either by specialized recordings or by spatializing pre-recorded monaural signals, which limits flexibility for controllable content creation. While recent text-to-audio models can generate the required audio, most of them target monaural output or unconstrained stereo. They provide limited control over spatial attributes such as direction and motion. To address these challenges, we propose BinauralLM, a spatial prompted text-to-binaural audio generation framework with large language model (LLM). BinauralLM adopts a two-stage pipeline. First, we use a Qwen2.5 LLM to autoregressively generate coarse binaural token sequences conditioned on text and spatial prompts. To effectively couple semantic content with spatial cues, we introduce a spatial prompt encoder and an attention fusion module to produce a unified conditioning representation for binaural token generation. Second, we employ a flow matching model that takes the coarse binaural tokens as conditions and reconstructs high-quality binaural waveforms in the continuous domain. Experimental results on the BEWO-1M dataset demonstrate that BinauralLM achieves superior performance on standard text-to-audio metrics and binaural spatial metrics, and achieves higher MOS scores in perceptual evaluation, especially on spatialization quality. These results indicate that our proposed method offers an effective route to controllable and high-quality text-to-binaural audio generation.</jats:p>

title: Innateness is (still) an orienting principle for language development
d94b3856e42e5d9a204d1345c69ca324c6794baf.abstract: How humans come to acquire language has been a persistent object of philosophical and scientific inquiry, in part because it bears on fundamental questions about the nature of human cognition.Classically, this field of inquiry has centered innateness as a critical component of language acquisition, traditionally characterizing innate capability in terms of richly specified, biologically endowed linguistic structure, such as Universal Grammar. Contemporary theories have evolved considerably from these earlier formulations and now present several differing candidates for innateness in language. Throughout this evolution, though, questions of innateness have remained central to theories of language acquisition, even as the nature of those questions has shifted in response to new sources of evidence. In this Perspective, we consider evidence from three complementary sources of evidence—linguistic diversity, human social interaction, and language models (LMs)—that together inform the question of what children must bring to the task of language learning. We conclude by identifying desiderata for theories of language acquisition that seek to specify the nature, scope, and explanatory role of innate contributions to language development.

title: Bayesian Treed Regressions for Estimating Heterogeneous Trajectories of Test Scores in Large-scale Educational Assessments
eff1fc6350d87a48be91231392d68074af4dbfa4.abstract: In large-scale educational assessment, students’ academic outcomes can evolve over time, due to various effect modifiers. For instance, parents’ education level, a common modifier, has been found to have time-varying effects on children’s test scores, leading to heterogeneous academic trajectories. To model these varying trajectories, parametric models like hierarchical linear models (HLMs) are commonly deployed. While these highly parametric methods are interpretable, their predictive capacities have not been rigorously compared to those of more flexible nonparametric approaches. We present the results of systematic simulation studies and empirical analyses comparing traditional parametric models to Bayesian nonparametric models based on Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART). Our findings indicate that BART-based alternatives can (1) achieve comparable out-of-sample prediction as HLMs, after accounting for individual variability over time; (2) provide a reasonable amount of interpretability and uncertainty quantification; and (3) do not incur much more computational burden. This work contributes to the existing social science literature by demonstrating that Bayesian treed regression methods are viable and feasible alternatives to conventional HLMs for predicting heterogeneous trajectories across time.

title: Peers link conflict-resolution reputation to social and cognitive capacities rather than the capacity to impose costs among Ethiopian forager-horticulturalists
b9ccdb38f6597ed3e62466f34e81e1c68972ba14.abstract: Leadership emergence in socially egalitarian contexts depends on the qualities of individuals and on how others perceive their capacity to use them. Multi-Capital Leadership theory proposes that leaders deploy material, social, somatic, and neural capital to solve problems of group living by providing benefits to group members or imposing costs. Conflict resolution is one important leadership domain. We reanalyse peer rankings of 60 adults in a relatively egalitarian community of Chabu forager-horticulturalists in southwest Ethiopia. Seven peer-raters ranked participants on twelve traits identified as relevant to leadership in contemporary evolutionary theories. A previous analysis averaged rankings before modelling, obscuring differences among raters and treating positions within an ordering as continuous measurements. Here, we fitted a multivariate Plackett–Luce model directly to the individual rankings. This accounts for dependence within rankings and incorporates uncertainty into estimates. It also allows us to estimate consensus orderings and systematic variation associated with rater sex. Male and female peer-raters produced broadly similar orderings, including for conflict resolution. This could reflect actual covariation in participants’ qualities, a shared evaluative schema, or both. Peer-ranked proxies for material, social, and neural capital covaried closely and did not form clearly separable perceptual domains. The clearest descriptive contrast was between benefit-related attributes, including conflict resolution, sound decision-making, and prosociality, and cost-related attributes, including being feared and fighting. Conflict-resolution reputation was most closely associated with decision-making, kin support, respect, and intelligence, and showed no clear positive association with fighting. In these rankings, a reputation for conflict resolution was more clearly distinguished from aggression and coercion than were measures capturing the three capital domains represented in the instrument.

title: Beyond Chemical Fingerprinting: Raman Photonics, Molecular Spectroscopy and  Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Palm Oil Authentication, Quality Assessment and  Transferable Optical Sensing
container-title: Journal of Advanced Physics and Interdisciplinary Science
84b8f03b843f3011a32eba7eff1136cea1cf4e7f.abstract: <jats:p>Authenticity verification and quality control in palm oil increasingly require rapid, defensible measurements across heterogeneous supply chains. This critical qualitative literature review examines the molecular physics, analytical performance, and interpretability challenges associated with Raman photonics and complementary optical spectroscopies. Drawing on journal evidence published between 2020 and 2026, it distinguishes chemically grounded measurement from statistical identification that may depend on correlated pigments, processing conditions, or instrument characteristics. Recent handheld Raman studies demonstrate geographical discrimination of West African palm oils, while machine learning-assisted Raman analysis has reported promising prediction of peroxide, iodine, and acid values. However, high within-study accuracy does not establish causal provenance markers, robustness across refining states, or transferability to new instruments and regions. The review compares Raman, Fourier transform infrared, near-infrared, fluorescence, and multimodal approaches; critically evaluates spectral preprocessing, variable selection, explainable AI, calibration transfer, and uncertainty management; and proposes an evidence-gated framework for deployment. Key recommendations include chemically verified band assignments, hierarchical out-of-domain validation, metrological controls, prediction intervals, standardized acquisition metadata, and reference-laboratory confirmation of consequential decisions. The resulting framework positions explainable spectroscopy as a powerful screening and process-monitoring capability while maintaining clear boundaries between compositional inference, product authentication, geographic attribution, and certified sustainability traceability.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence Assistance with CRISPR to Optimize Drug Development
container-title: Theoretical and Natural Science
d3a234a40b3f1788d998eef39dd6112dabcf3dea.abstract: <jats:p>Drug development remains a costly and time-consuming process since identifying therapeutic targets that are both biologically relevant and clinically effective remains challenging. New technologies including bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, CRISPR screens and AI are enabling new target discovery opportunities, but there are still a number of challenges in bringing the heterogeneous data sets together. This paper describes how AI-assisted integration of these three technologies can improve drug development. This paper explains in detail how Bulk RNA sequencing can detect differentially expressed genes, how Single-cell RNA sequencing can uncover cell-specific expression patterns, how CRISPR screening can identify dependencies of genes in disease-related phenotypes, and how AI models can recognize complex molecular patterns and prioritize targets for therapeutic intervention using these complementary datasets. With AI support and current technologies, researchers could decrease false-positive target identification and enhance drug sensitivity forecasting. This paper suggest a way to improve the precision-drug-discovery strategies. But there are still issues with data heterogeneity and with model interpretability. To address the remaining challenges, interpretable AI models that combine multi-omics, functional genomic, and patient-derived data should be developed in the future.</jats:p>

title: Neural Mechanisms of Willed Attention Control
6c47127d70f109a58cb6025488b9cb7e3e64f432.abstract: Cueing paradigms are commonly used to study the neural mechanisms of visual spatial attention control. In these paradigms, each trial starts with an external cue, which instructs the subject to pay covert attention to a spatial location in anticipation of an impending stimulus (instructed attention). Recent work has introduced a new type of cue which prompts the subject to spontaneously decide which spatial location to attend (willed attention). We studied the neural mechanisms of willed attention control by analyzing fMRI and EEG data recorded at two institutions (UF and UC Davis) using the same willed attention paradigm. The findings include: (1) both instructional cues and the choice cue activated the DAN, (2) the choice cue additionally activated a frontoparietal decision network consisting of dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC), anterior insula (AI), anterior prefrontal cortex (APFC), dorsal lateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), and inferior parietal lobule (IPL), (3) the decision about where to attend can be decoded in frontoparietal decision network in choice trials but not in instructional trials, and (4) EEG alpha oscillation patterns immediately preceding the choice cue, but not the instructional cues, predicted the postcue direction of attention and the frontoparietal decision network activity. Based on these findings we proposed a model of willed attention control suggesting how the direction of visual spatial attention was decided upon in the absence of external instructions.

title:
A Catalog of Compact High-velocity Clouds from the FAST All-Sky H
                    <scp>i</scp>
                    Survey (FASHI) DR2
container-title: Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
d3dde96f6c706676ad1d2e5636cb7668f5b8c69f.abstract: Abstract High-velocity clouds (HVCs)—especially compact HVCs (CHVCs)—are thought to serve as gaseous tracers of dark-matter-dominated subhalos, providing a crucial empirical link between the predicted dark matter substructure and observed satellite galaxies. In this paper, we present a new catalog of 192 CHVCs identified from the FAST All-Sky H i Survey Data Release 2. Among these, 108 are ultra-compact HVCs, the majority of which are new discoveries. We find that 185 of the 192 CHVCs are spatially and kinematically concentrated around the Andromeda galaxy (M31), with a median local standard of rest velocity of −296.1 km s −1 , suggesting physical association with M31. Adopting an M31 distance of 0.8 Mpc, we derive H i masses in the range 1.9 × 10 5 –4.0 × 10 6 M ⊙ and dynamical masses from 1.0 × 10 7 to 6.3 × 10 8 M ⊙ . Approximately half of the CHVCs follow the baryonic Tully–Fisher relation. No optical counterparts are detected in Pan-STARRS1 imaging down to a limiting magnitude of m g = 22.8. We conclude that these CHVCs likely represent a population of gas-rich, starless minihalos and provide an excellent sample for the search for dark galaxies.

The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain, and cloud computing has enabled governments, businesses, and regulatory institutions to improve financial transparency, automate compliance processes, strengthen decision-making, and enhance the efficiency of tax administration and accounting systems. 8d6566608fce521055ce1c29ae126198863c8d7f.abstract: In conclusion, this research demonstrates that artificial intelligence (AI) represents a genuine qualitative leap in the field of management in general, and in the administrative decision-making process in particular. The study's findings confirm a strong correlation and a significant positive impact of using AI technologies on improving the quality of administrative decisions in Iraqi Public Sector. title: Quality monitoring in extrusion-based bioprinting: From defect formation to AI-driven detection and correction
2497f27ecb0a80c081f637e0b5d2ad5b16be7901.abstract: Extrusion-based bioprinting is widely used to fabricate cell-laden three-dimensional constructs, yet its structural integrity remains difficult to ensure because interactions among bioink rheology, process parameters, hardware and construct design produce defects that compromise the dimensional accuracy and cell viability of the bioprinted samples. This review organizes the structural defects along a causal chain, from root-cause factors to nozzle-level failures (clogging and buckling-induced filament curling), filament-level defects (size inconsistency, fusion, delamination, sagging, collapse and breakage) and construct-level inaccuracy. It then maps each defect class to the sensing modalities that have been shown to observe it, spanning surface imaging (optical and machine-vision imaging, microscopy, thermography, video-based vibrometry and laser profilometry), volumetric analysis (optical coherence tomography, X-ray computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasound) and process sensing (dielectric impedance spectroscopy and flow sensing). The methods are compared in terms of processing stage, reported resolution and target object. The evidence linking each defect class to each method is also mapped. Machine learning is assessed as an interpretation layer on these data, distinguishing classification, segmentation, anomaly scoring, open-loop prediction, and assisting corrective measures in printing. Key open challenges include the scarcity of shared, standardized datasets, limited external validation and regulatory frameworks, the absence of standardized defect definitions and the coupling between structural fidelity and cell viability, which together define the requirements for quality-assessment frameworks that can support clinical translation. Collectively, this review aims to provide a structured foundation for developing quality assessment frameworks capable of supporting the translation of extrusion-based bioprinting from laboratory research toward consistent, clinically viable fabrication.

title: Consonant Articulating Errors in Khmer-Speaking Preschool Children: A Picture-Naming Task Analysis
container-title: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research
6c379abdd314406fd2cafae318b93ae5c2c9ef3a.abstract: Purpose: Consonant errors (mainly phonetic and phonological errors) as a phenomenon in speech development are frequently observed in preschool children's daily speech communication across languages. Since the Khmer language is a low-source language, consonant articulating error patterns of Khmer-speaking children have not been explored to date, leaving open the question whether the patterns are similar to those found in high-source languages such as English. To bridge the gap, this study investigated the on-spot speech of Khmer preschool children across three age groups (3;0 [years;months] to 5;11) using a picture-naming test with 203 pictures of varying complexity. Method: The naming data of 60 (34 girls and 26 boys) and 56 (34 girls and 22 boys) children, respectively, for two tests were recorded and transcribed for analysis, with errors categorized into (a) phonetic errors (substitution, deletion, addition, or distortion) and (b) phonological errors (regular and irregular). Results: The results showed that children aged 3;0–3;11 had the lowest speech sound accuracy among the three groups (3;0–5;11), with more frequent phonetic errors in substitution and deletion and more regular versus irregular phonological errors, including final consonant deletion, lateralization, initial consonant deletion, glottalization, and alveolarization substitution, but the errors did not reach statistically significant differences among the three age groups. The patterns are consistent with the developmental trends of speech sound error found in English and other high-source languages. Conclusion: These findings reveal the unique speech sound error patterns in Khmer preschool children, which may partly arise from linguistic universality during children's language development and partly be attributed to the typological features peculiar to the Khmer language. Supplemental Material: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33684361

title: Integrating multifunctional interfaces via chelation-driven chemical reconstruction enables efficient and durable perovskite solar cells
container-title: Materials Futures
3f8c2076c37d525da4e64e6e44f55252fefcdca1.abstract: Abstract Interfacial instability is a critical constraint for the practical deployment of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). It commonly arises from the metastable residual PbI 2 and deep-level defects like under-coordinated Pb 2+ . Herein, a benzeneseleninic acid (PSA)-enabled interfacial chemical reconstruction strategy, that simultaneously converts residual PbI 2 , mitigates interfacial defects, and stabilizes the perovskite lattice through synergistic bidentate chelation and hydrogen bonding, is reported to significantly improve the interfacial stability. Robust Pb–O–Se chelate structures can be formed via dual-site coordination between PSA with under-coordinated Pb 2+ and residual PbI 2 . This chelation-driven interfacial reconstruction not only eliminates detrimental defects at the interface but also induces ordered molecular self-assembly, in which outward-oriented phenyl groups form a hydrophobic barrier that blocks water/oxygen intrusion, while the interfacial dipole modulates the degree of energy-level matching, thereby markedly enhancing charge extraction efficiency. Meanwhile, PSA molecules stabilize the halide sublattice through hydrogen-bond interactions, suppressing ion migration and structural degradation. Consequently, PSA-treated PSCs exhibits markedly improved efficiency (from 23.68% to 26.56%) together with substantially enhanced stability, retains 87.8% of initial efficiency after 2000 h under 60% relative humidity.

title: Metabolic modeling: the link between AI and multi-omics data to accelerate the discovery of antibiotic-resistant traits in ESKAPE pathogens
container-title: Infection and Immunity
7ed95bf61237d995171ecce906cdf2fb609f6b80.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of predictive understanding of bacterial resistance to antibiotics is one of the greatest challenges of modern medicine. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) are mathematical representations of the metabolic network of a given organism assembled from genomic data that predict cellular activity across many environmental and genetic contexts. Because a single model can be solved under thousands of conditions, GEMs generate data at scales that support downstream analysis with artificial intelligence tools, helping to elucidate how pathogens adapt to host environments, evade immune responses, and acquire resistance. Here, we review how GEMs of ESKAPE pathogens are built, what data they require, and what they can and cannot do. We describe the reconstruction workflow from automated draft network through manual curation, gap filling, and experimental validation and the public and experimental data sources each stage depends on. We then describe how accessory genes and transcriptomic measurements are incorporated to yield strain- and condition-specific models and where machine learning contributes both in expanding functional annotation and in consuming model-generated flux distributions. Applications are illustrated with ESKAPE examples throughout, including conserved metabolic vulnerabilities identified across strain collections and flux rewiring observed under antibiotic exposure. Despite this progress, high-quality GEMs exist for only a fraction of ESKAPE species; many are constrained by incomplete annotation or limited experimental validation, and non-metabolic resistance mechanisms are captured only insofar as they impose a metabolic cost. Providing reliable tools to build new models from trustworthy templates, therefore, remains a priority for narrowing the gap between genotype and phenotype.

title: Physician Training for the AI Era
container-title: JAMA
d03b628dc014ee00d349104fd758959dd3bf4115.abstract: This Viewpoint discusses the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education, and how physician training should change in parallel with AI use including emphasizing skills that AI makes more valuable, cultivating those it makes newly necessary, and carefully de-emphasizing those it makes less important.

title: Sentence Completion Expressive Language Task–Preschool: Preliminary Evidence of Validity and Feasibility for the Neuroimaging Environment
container-title: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research
9f303726843cd3b42204158b419ee8d743e20ba9.abstract: Purpose: This preliminary investigation occurred across two studies and examined validity, discriminant accuracy, and feasibility of the Sentence Completion Expressive Language Task–Preschool (SCELT-P) for characterizing language production in a neuroimaging environment for typically developing (TD) preschoolers and those with developmental language disorder (DLD). Method: Two separate studies were completed. Study 1 (validity) included 82 preschoolers (50% female; 69 TD, 13 DLD) aged 4;0 (years;months) to 5;11 ( M age = 4;7). All children were assessed using standardized language measures (e.g., Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool–Second Edition), a play-based language sample (analyzed using Developmental Sentence Scoring), and the 30-item SCELT-P (outside the neuroimaging environment), later streamlined to 20 items (SCELT-P Revised [SCELT-PR]). Study 2 (feasibility) included 14 preschoolers ( M age = 4;9, 43% female; nine TD, five with DLD) that were assessed using the SCELT-P (inside the neuroimaging environment) and functional magnetic resonance imaging using a sparse acquisition approach with a “listen” (passive) and “listen + speak” (active) condition implemented using DirectRT software. Results: In Study 1, the SCELT-P and SCELT-PR demonstrated high reliability, including interrater (intraclass correlation coefficient = .99), test–retest ( r = .86 and .80, respectively), and internal consistency (Cronbach's α > .86 and .83, respectively), and similar strong criterion validity ( r = . 53–.84). Area under the curve analyses (.91) revealed both versions also evidenced fair sensitivity (.88 and .87) and specificity (.85) rates with a cutoff score of 15.5 and 9.5, respectively. In Study 2, 89% of TD preschoolers and 60% of preschoolers with DLD successfully completed the SCELT-P/R inside the neuroimaging environment, with activation maps illustrating relatively similar neurobiological characteristics across preschoolers in some brain regions. Conclusion: The SCELT-P, including its streamlined version, the SCELT-PR, holds promise as a reliable and valid task for including 4- to 5-year-olds in the neuroimaging environment to inform neural and cognitive systems involved in language development. Supplemental Material: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34543209

title: Berta, an Open-Source, Modular AI Scribe for Clinical Documentation: Implementation Report
container-title: JMIR Medical Informatics
f2df5d7b63b39635ad5f7aae8d112bd7749180cb.abstract: Abstract Background Clinical documentation is a major contributor to physician workload and burnout, particularly in high-acuity settings such as emergency departments. Ambient AI scribes have emerged as a response, but commercial products cost US $99 to more than US $600 per physician per month, operate as opaque systems, and often process data on vendor-controlled infrastructure. These characteristics limit organizational control over data sovereignty, quality improvement, and clinical workflows and create barriers to adoption in resource-constrained settings. Objective We aimed to develop an open-source, modular AI scribe platform that could be deployed entirely within institutional infrastructure, and to evaluate its real-world use across a provincial health system. Methods We developed Berta, an open-source, modular platform that pairs a Next.js front end and a FastAPI back end with configurable automatic speech recognition and large language model components. A closed-source implementation developed in parallel with Berta was deployed at Alberta Health Services (AHS), Canada’s largest provincially integrated health system at the time of implementation, and operated within AHS’s existing Snowflake AI Data Cloud infrastructure. All clinical audio and text remained within the secure AHS environment. Use and session metadata were automatically recorded during routine clinical use by emergency physicians across AHS between November 2024 and July 2025, and physicians were emailed an optional survey. Operating costs were estimated from Snowflake service consumption over the same period. Implementation (Results) During the 9-month study period, 197 emergency physicians registered at 105 urban and rural facilities used the system, generating 21,548 clinical sessions and more than 2700 hours of audio. Monthly session volume grew from 675 sessions in November 2024 to 5463 in July 2025. Mean recorded session length was 7.6 minutes, and 42% (82/197) of users customized at least 1 documentation template. Operating costs averaged less than US $30 per physician per month, representing a 70% to 95% reduction in cost compared with commercial subscription prices; this comparison excludes personnel costs for development and maintenance. Survey respondents (69-73 per item) rated user-friendliness as good (median 5, IQR 4-6), reported a median time saving of 16 to 30 (IQR 0-15 to 46-60) minutes per shift, and rated documentation quality the lowest. After the pilot, access was opened to other departments, and by September 30, 2026, approximately 2000 users had registered. Conclusions An in-house AI scribe can be deployed at provincial scale within existing health system infrastructure at a fraction of the operating cost of commercial alternatives while preserving data sovereignty and institutional control. The full cost of ownership and documentation quality require further evaluation. By releasing Berta publicly, we provide a reproducible foundation that health systems can adapt to evaluate and deploy AI documentation technology within their own secure environments.

title: Is AI the End of the DMA As We Know It?
container-title: GRUR International
06f29e15676b1c1246b131e4c599fff0a384cd12.abstract: Abstract The disruptive potential of AI-enabled applications for competitive dynamics and the core organisational forms of digital intermediation inevitably also has significant implications for the recent regulatory initiatives adopted to govern digital markets. Indeed, because these instruments were conceived without AI specifically in mind, they risk becoming outdated within a very short period of time. Notably, while they have been shaped by a Big Tech-centred conception of digital markets, the possible emergence of new gatekeepers in the age of AI marks a turning point that calls into question the very rationale and foundations of these regimes in their present form. As a result, only a few years after its enactment, the role of the DMA, its rationale and its claimed future-proof character are already under scrutiny. The deployment of AI applications raises the question whether policymakers should reopen the legislative framework in order to amend the Regulation. Against this background and in the context of the first review of the DMA, the paper argues that the rise of AI applications calls for a reconsideration of the DMA’s overall architecture and for the development of a distinct competition policy framework, rather than for a merely incremental fine-tuning exercise.

title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
9582d73b28887383a9b2b76978981d894f9ddb6a.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is rapidly reshaping the landscapes of education and business, driving innovation and redefining operational norms. The latest volume of the Advanced Series in Management brings together interdisciplinary perspectives to explore how AI technologies—from predictive analytics and automation, to adaptive learning systems—are enabling smarter decision-making, personalised experiences, and enhanced efficiency. At the same time, it critically examines the ethical, infrastructural, and skill-based challenges that accompany this digital shift, offering a balanced view of both promise and complexity. Bridging theory and practice, AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business presents empirical research, real-world case studies, and policy insights that illuminate the evolving role of AI in organisational and educational contexts. It contributes to global conversations around digital transformation and sustainability, aligning with key UN Sustainable Development Goals such as Quality Education and Responsible Management. Ideal for scholars, students, and practitioners, this volume offers a comprehensive guide to navigating the AI-driven future, especially in a post-pandemic world where hybrid learning and intelligent business models are becoming the norm.

title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business: Concepts, Contexts and Sustainable Pathways
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
12c7a41ee43b34016c4d1e1b96a121e36b341f8a.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a transformative facilitator for organizations in different industries, reshaping how organizations design processes, make decisions and aim for sustainable values. Though there have been intense examinations of AI and analysis tools and methodologies in past studies, there is a pressing need for a wide and competent understanding of the different dynamics of AI as a transformative tool in real-world contexts. To address this issue, this chapter develops a case study analysis of how AI is influencing education and businesses and develops definitions based on transformative analytics. In this chapter, real-life examples of how AI has or can transform big businesses, educational systems of a nation and college and university systems have been examined. In fact, examples of educational institutions illustrate how AI can impact teaching and governing as well as how it can be used at a systemic level for inclusion. In turn, examples of big businesses illustrate how AI can influence excellence in work processes and administration as well as innovation directed at environmental friendliness. This chapter does not only focus on AI adoption as an issue of technology adoption; it also emphasizes the transformative process as socio-technical in nature. This chapter conducts a cross-case analysis to identify common enablers, sector-specific obstacles and various patterns of transformations in both business and the education sector. These elements are further integrated to develop various sustainable AI-based pathways of transformation in relation to long-term institutional viability, ethical use of AI and social purpose.

title: Applications and Reflections on AI in the Field of Education
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
5365282d93a3257359ddc4184742a198fe075dab.abstract: Abstract The cognitive artificial intelligence (AI) radically transforms the educational ecosystem through data-driven thinking and algorithmic optimization, which focuses on precision, personalization and collaboration of the educational process, leading to significant changes in metacognitive development, human-machine cognitive synergy and ethical considerations. This technology overcomes the barriers of traditional standardized teaching by dynamically adapting learning paths through cognitive diagnosis, intelligent content adaptation and personalized goal setting. Regarding the development of metacognitive abilities, AI visualized abstract thinking processes and identified self-directed learning capabilities as skills that can be taught and learnt through strategic training and dynamic modification, ultimately redefining them as talents. Nonetheless, the use of technology raises ethical issues, including educational equity, algorithmic bias, data privacy and diminished cognitive autonomy, as overreliance on AI and instant feedback may hinder students’ ability to think independently. This means that a future development should strike a balance between technological advancement and humanism, base technological orientation in human concern and find synergy between tool empowerment and human leadership to build up education to a more fair and equitable evolution.

title: AI-Driven Learning Analytics for Outcome-Based Education in Higher Education Institutions
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
63f8a4644f6da71c2a6d76fa348694b1a741456d.abstract: Abstract With the recent emphasis on Outcome-Based Education (OBE), it has become even more essential that colleges and universities have excellent data-driven systems that are able to not only compile, evaluate and interpret learning evidence into measurable outcomes, but essentially do it accurately and comprehensively as well. The traditional way of implementing OBE tends to rely on imperfect assessment data, looking backward in time and lacking depth, which further handicaps it from being useful in executing continual enhancements and making rapid academic decisions as well. To address such a difficulty, there comes across a framework within this chapter that proposes needing data-driven systems that incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) into learning analytics as part of OBE systems as well. This chapter illustrates how AI is beneficial in increasing accuracy, monitoring, prediction and intelligent interventions regarding various types of institutional settings and is based on actual data and proves that primary data at an institutional level can be employed to reveal students’ actual engagement, their performance on tests and their success rates in accomplishing their goals within various programmes and academic cycles as well. To ensure that AI is used responsibly in the best interest of the institution and its stakeholders, the paper also addresses issues related to ethics, issues related to data governance challenges and readiness of the institution. This chapter offers a very useful and viable strategy for universities that are on a path of successful implementation of Outcome Based Education using AI learning analytics.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Marketing 5.0 in the South Asian Business Sector
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
e075d794091c0eb3faa3a951db8aae4619fcec56.abstract: Abstract This research explores the five core components of the revolutionary marketing phase of the ongoing era, Marketing 5.0, across diverse business sectors in South Asia. The study takes a qualitative, inductive approach to analyze primary and secondary data collected from exclusively picked marketing professionals’ opinions and insights, as well as published interviews on YouTube, blogs, academic papers, books focusing on relevant evidences in the context of South Asian business sectors. The research findings develop an integrated theoretical framework of the disciplines, applications and enablers of the concept ‘Technology for Humanity’ under artificial intelligence (AI)-powered marketing phenomena. The study upholds the synergistic value of the collaboration of humans and technologies complementing human cognitive skills with advanced technological skills in the post-pandemic world. The appropriate applications of AI-driven marketing approaches are evaluated in respect to close the widening generation gap, societal and digital polarization gap. The research concludes the foundational disciplines of the appropriate applications of AI-powered technologies for marketers, intended to create unique, yet inclusive and sustainable value that bridges these gaps while upholding the core value of humanity across the region.

title: The Future of Customer Experience: AI-Powered Personalization in Marketing 5.0
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
15a7fa8476e2fcc39c7dd08d32d0cf3a092c663d.abstract: Abstract In this era of cut-throat marketing campaigns, where every brand is devising strategies to stand out and grab attention, traditional methods are often unable to establish the required customer connections. The future of effective customer experience (CX) lies in personalization, and artificial intelligence (AI) is truly a revolution in marketing personalization. Personalized marketing campaigns definitely increase the conversion rate by fostering deeper customer connections. Natural language processing (NLP) powered by AI is used to understand the customer sentiment. AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants can provide personalized customer support. Huge data sets can be analyzed, and through predictive analytics, personalized campaigns can be created. This paper explores the potential of AI to develop personalized marketing experiences based on individual consumer preferences, behaviour and demographics.

title: AI Adoption in MSMEs: Opportunities, Barriers and Strategic Readiness in Emerging Economies
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
d9f15671226e32d94f4685ff1c7039687a6d1af1.abstract: Abstract The adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important tool for harnessing competitiveness, learning and results of performance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in emerging economies. Despite requiring greater policy emphasis and greater access to technology, little research data have been collected on emerging perceptions of AI opportunities, adoption challenges and strategic preparedness of MSMEs. In an endeavour to generate such research data, this chapter will examine AI adoption by MSMEs using data. The use of AI not only serves as an aid to organizations but also an innovation for organizations to acquire knowledge on data that influence performance outcomes on results. In this chapter, a survey-structured approach to the analysis is used, and a pragmatic and empirical method of data handling is used to describe MSMEs in operating crucial sectors of emerging nations. The descriptive and interpretational statistics, such as comparison of mean tests, correlation and regression, are used to spot trends in the adoption of AI, intensity of value creation sentiments, degree of constraint and readiness. These trends and patterns are spotted with the help of bar chart comparison, trend charts, scatter charts and heat maps, among others. The findings highlight that there is great potential for AI to make working more efficient for MSMEs, to help them make good decisions and to help them react better to the market.

title: Smart Supply Chains and Operations: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Understanding Smart Logistics
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
3a1efa1edc5ff915cf6ae21a3322f5d27b45e644.abstract: Abstract Smart Supply Chains is one of the evolving concepts in management. From making to procuring to sourcing products, everything is artificial intelligence (AI)-driven. The applications of AI, like warehouse optimization, real-time stock tracking and product optimization, are popular applications of AI. With the use and adoption of fuzzy models like artificial neural network (ANN) frameworks, the dependency on humans has eventually reduced, making smart AI ensure the best decisions for operations. The paper includes a case study and a study of a theoretical model known as Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) (Model), which is very popularly used in supply chain management and tracking logistics. The process includes plan, source, make, deliver and return. This is a good framework applied with AI in automation logistics for smoother functioning. It includes the use of fuzzy algorithms, genetic models and ANN networks to efficiently update and track product specifications as well as the delivery process without much human interaction. The ANN model is popular and widely used in data science as well as behavioural science.

title: Industry 4.0 and the Future of Digital Strategy: Pathways to Digital Value Creation
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
218150914ff06798dd0fe2d20c483286c0ae044d.abstract: Abstract The acceptance and addition of such progressive digital technologies into operational processes and decision-making platforms have totally redefined how businesses conceptualize strategy in Industry 4.0. This chapter explores how digital value creation (DVC), as a process, has been facilitated through Industry 4.0 technology, with digital strategy orientation (DSO) as the intermediary. For instance, employing a quantitative research strategy that focuses on theoretical constructs, the chapter integrates theories from dynamic capability theory, the resource-based view (RBV) and IT business value theory to explain how businesses achieve strategic and performance outcomes from their digital investments. Data collection entailed conducting surveys among managers whose business entities adopted Industry 4.0 technology. The examples given for Industry 4.0 technology were Internet of Things technology, artificial intelligence technology, analytics technology, automation technology and cyber-physical system technology. This chapter empirically explores Industry 4.0 technology and DVC and how Industry 4.0 technology influences DSO through structural equation modelling techniques. The results show that Industry 4.0 technology affects DVC both directly and through DSO. Digital strategy is an integral part of any business through which technology capabilities are actually linked with overall business goals. Organizations primarily benefit from the outcomes of a digital strategy by making their operations more efficient, starting new creative activities and gaining a competitive advantage in Industry 4.0. The findings quite clearly bring out that firms focusing on digital strategy are better positioned to achieve long-term value from their Industry 4.0 investments.

title: Building Resilient Supply Chains: Collaborative Approaches to Cybersecurity for Critical Infrastructure
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
69ef3b4bd98fa812b47926725f643b3bbca05bd0.abstract: Abstract Cybersecurity resilience has become a major factor in determining the strength of the supply chain, especially in sectors which constitute the national critical infrastructure, such as energy, transport and healthcare industries. This chapter examines the importance of collaboration to cyber resiliency in interdependent supply chains. The analysis is carried out through a conceptual literature review in which synthesis of 122 scholarly and policy papers published from 2014 to 2025 is made based on the concept of a network that brings into consideration theories of supply chain resiliency, resource dependency, collective action, socio-technological system and network governance. Cybersecurity resilience can be achieved only when more than one player is involved in the network. Through collaboration, information exchange concerning the nature of the threats, addressing such threats and public and private partnership will make the environment less vulnerable to cyberattacks and therefore more flexible. On the other hand, fragmented environments where there is very little cooperation are likely to be victims of system failure. This chapter outlines a framework called the Collaborative Cyber Resilience Framework, which is made up of components such as threat environment, actors, collaboration mechanism, governance and cyber resilience outcomes. One of the most essential things about collaboration according to the Collaborative Cyber Resilience Framework is that coordination will make collaboration better and sustainable. This study contributes to the existing literature in this field through offering a theory-based cyber security approach that focuses on the network aspect.

title: Sustainable Business Models and Artificial Intelligence for Handicraft Entrepreneurship: A Cross-Cultural Case Study
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
280c6ee15c3a60b7ae449cdd269f945d69496f05.abstract: Abstract Across the globe, handicrafts have been validating cultures, identities and traditions that have been present in the modern world. At the same time, the craftsmen who are a part of the process of manufacturing the product not only validate themselves on the capability of manufacturing the product but also sustain their culture, heritage and tradition. The case study would revolve around the process of preserving cultural heritage crafts with the aid of sustainable business practices with the help of advanced artificial intelligence (AI)-based explanations. The research would be carried out as compensation for the rigorous qualitative case study to perceive four different handicraft cultures. This would include Pattachitra paintings from India, Dokra metal casting from India, Moroccan carpets from Morocco and Talavera from Mexico. Based on the research carried out, it has been identified that with the aid of AI for design invention, quality declaration, prediction analysis and digital storytelling with sustainable business practices, companies can sustain their attractiveness.

title: Measuring What Matters: A Systematic Review and Future Agenda for Social Impact Assessment
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
bdf8ea266b44fc56f97e644ac31e64fd09230ecc.abstract: Abstract The use of Social Impact Assessment (SIA) is indispensable when considering the consequences of changes occurring in organizations, policies and initiatives to the society in which we live. Unfortunately, the present methods of SIA are fragmentary, instrumentally driven and lack a theoretical basis. To address these weaknesses, in this chapter, an extensive study of the current scientific literature on SIA methods is conducted based on the PRISMA approach and conceptual thematic analysis as well as the assessment of theoretical foundation of each tool. The most popular SIA methodologies, including Social Return on Investment (SROI), Theory of Change, environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles, Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) criteria and well-being measures, are examined. This chapter proposes Adaptive Social Impact Measurement (ASIM) as a methodological meta-framework aiming to reinterpret the notion of measurement through its adaptability, participation and educative dimensions. While the traditional measurement approach relies on indicators, ASIM values an interactive, dynamic process of assessment enabling it to tackle such challenges as standardization and context, accountability and learning, control and empowerment, and other problems. From the conclusions drawn from this chapter, it is possible to state that the current stage of development implies not one methodology of measuring social impact but several ones. Furthermore, some directions for future research are suggested by the author, such as the application of artificial intelligence and big data techniques, participation, hybrid valuation, ethics and decolonizing methods.

title: AI-Enabled Talent Management: Transforming Recruitment, Performance and Employee Engagement
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
9886b48584b8d91269b829bd1a85d226cfa82673.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the way organizations recruit, assess, engage and retain employees by transforming the way they do these in the organization. Although existing literature has deeply explored various AI-based tools and applications in the field of human resource management, there is a strong need for a theoretical understanding of how AI alters the basic principles of talent management as a practice. Addressing the need, in this chapter, a theoretical and integrative approach has been applied, applying various established theories in the realms of organization, human resource and behaviours as a way of reinterpreting talent management in the AI era. Counter to conventional thinking that regards AI as a mere technological advancement, in this analysis, AI-based talent management has been identified as a social, technical and strategic phenomenon that alters the way organizations recruit members, manage their performance and encourage them to work. This analysis has applied classical concepts such as Person–Job Fit Theory, Signalling Theory, Human Capital Theory, Goal Setting Theory, Expectancy Theory, Agency Theory, Job Demands–Resources Theory, Social Exchange Theory, Self-Determination Theory, Resource-Based View and Institutional Theory. This chapter develops these new viewpoints and constructs a conceptual framework for AI-enabled talent management. The framework describes how talent outcomes are impacted by AI capabilities via hiring, performance and engagement processes.

title: Ethical, Legal and Governance Challenges of AI Implementation in Education and Enterprises
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
7c0f5e366e46844378f9d457494688d59e3b288a.abstract: Abstract The rapid application of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools and organizations has impacted the process of decision-making, performance measurement and value addition. In post-secondary education, AI-powered learning analytics is increasingly being employed to support outcome-oriented education. In organizations, AI solutions are being employed to enhance organizational operation, employee management and organizational-level decision-making. Nevertheless, emerging parallel to these advances, ethical, legal and governance (ELG)-related challenges have appeared to have immense potential to become important considerations for systematic and evidence-based analysis, rather than simply normative discussion (Floridi et al., 2018; Mittelstadt et al., 2016). This chapter applies a data-driven model for analysis of ethical, legal and governance-related concerns emerging due to the employment of AI within schools and organizations. This research avoids literature-based discussion for its focus by applying hypothetical but realistic primary research data to test concerns regarding privacy, bias, transparency, regulatory compliance and maturity in a governed context. Based on business enterprises and colleges, the chapter applies structured synthetic data in the application of comparative, correlational and descriptive analytics to uncover quantifiable risk exposure and governance readiness scores (Kshetri, 2021; Raji et al., 2020). This chapter is an application of pattern identification in the quantification of ethical risk vulnerabilities, regulatory issues of compliance and governance inadequacies in sectors through the application of tables, analytics and text analysis (Jobin et al., 2019).

20ab3ed55c9eec8c5c7cff92eb971e6413e2ae68.abstract: 随着AI发展对软件开发与计算机教育的影响,地方工科高校的编译原理课程在课时压缩和学生基础差异明显。传统的从零手写完整编译器,学生容易感受到挫败,且实验成果仅停留于理论层面,学生学习兴趣不高。本文在原"课程实验+课程设计"的两阶段安排的基础上,探索面向工程应用和能力拓展的分层实践教学改革。改革中第一阶段开展AI协同的编译原理性实验,第二阶段保留编译系统集成的同时,增强编译理论的实际工程应用,相应地,实践考核改用编译系统集成保底,加应用拓展项目增值的组合方式。对比改革实施组与历史比较组的实验提交、代码相似度检测、答辩记录和归档作品,发现改革后完整编译流程完成率从70%多增长到99%,存在代码抄袭的作品比例从约20%降至约1%;课程设计作品类型也更加丰富。但是也存在着"程序能运行、代码难解释"、重度依赖AI整体构建和代码验证不足等问题。针对这些问题,本文提出编译各模块的接口约束、版本追溯、提示词记录与随机代码走查等手段,加强对学生学习过程的管理。由于本研究采用历史队列比较,相关结果主要用于呈现改革后的变化趋势,不能将其仅仅归因于AI工具使用的效果。

title: AI赋能民事诉讼法课程个性化学习路径的探索与思考
container-title: 教育发展论坛
46143faedda4629d8550ea202a220d616de22099.abstract: 以AI为代表的数智时代,对民事诉讼法的教学提出新挑战。传统的民事诉讼法教学存在着教学模式固化、学生被动学习、学情不客观、评价方式单一等问题,亟须进行全面而深刻的改革。AI赋能民事诉讼法个性化学习有现实的可行性,它符合国家教育教学改革政策导向,符合社会发展与学生培养需求,同时有强大的数智技术支持。AI可以从学情画像、学习资源供给、学习过程引导、学习评价反馈四个角度赋能,对前面提到的问题进行破冰,提供有针对性的措施,推动民事诉讼法课程个性化学习路径不断优化。

title: 生成式AI赋能的人才培养模式研究—基于数据计算及应用专业视角
container-title: 教育发展论坛
3e7a0248358a477fc0d098e23131f7b126d64ceb.abstract: 随着生成式AI的快速迭代,以生成式AI为代表的智能技术深度融入高等教育,已成为推动专业数字化转型、提升人才培养质量的核心路径。数据计算及应用专业作为新工科背景下的应用理科专业,具有理论性强、实践要求高、技术迭代快等特征。本研究立足生成式AI赋能教育的时代需求,明确数据计算及应用专业人才培养目标与能力定位,从课程体系、教学模式、实践平台、评价机制四个维度构建AI赋能人才培养路径,推动专业教学向智能化、个性化、实战化转型,为地方高校同类专业改革提供借鉴。

title: Minds Meet Machines: The Joint Role of Trust and Intellectual Humility in AI Persuasion
d8b7b16ca9c75a1deb3b83f3c4c11a9668b438b8.abstract: Research shows that AI models have a remarkable ability to change people’s minds following a short conversation, a notoriously difficult task for human communicators. Such persuasive paradigms provide a unique opportunity to examine which psychological characteristics predict receptivity to counter-attitudinal information. We focus on two characteristics: intellectual humility (IH), reflecting openness to revising one’s beliefs following new information, and trust in the information source (AI). To establish the role of a-priori dispositions that determine acceptance of new information, we ran two online studies, sampling British participants with a negative attitude toward legal immigrants (N = 294). We replicated previous findings showing significant and lasting attitude change following a brief exchange with GPT, but crucially, this effect was not uniform. In Study 1, attitude change was greatest among participants with higher initial trust in AIs and higher intellectual humility. Study 2 extended this finding by measuring both dispositions a week before the conversation with GPT, revealing the same pattern: opinion change was greatest among those who were both open to new information and trusting of its source. These findings highlight the centrality of recipient dispositions, suggesting that the relationship between source trust and persuasion depends on recipients' intellectual humility. More broadly, source trust may function as more than a heuristic cue, and its relationship with attitude change may depend on recipients' willingness to recognize the fallibility of their beliefs. Together, these findings extend perspectives on persuasion by highlighting the joint role of source trust and recipients' epistemic dispositions in belief revision.

title: Empowering the anesthesiologist: Navigating the future of AI-driven visualization and wearable technology in regional anesthesia
container-title: Perioperative Precision Medicine
b445412f8c53724ad77ef1c335303383faadf067.abstract: In current regional anesthesia practice, “visualization” typically refers to the real-time imaging and display of subcutaneous anatomical structures with ultrasound imaging, and “wearable technology” refers to hands-free, optical head-mounted displays (e.g., smart glasses) that can project digital information directly into the clinician’s field of view. The paradigm shift in the history of regional anesthesia from anatomical landmark techniques to ultrasound guidance has revolutionized the art of regional anesthesia and transformed a blind procedural technique into a visually guided intervention.

title:
Pedagogical Experiences, Challenges, and Ethical AI Use in Peer Writing Tutoring:
            Insights from the Azcapotzalco Writing Center (CEAZ)
