title: Integrating AI General Education with Digital Literacy Cultivation and Cognitive Construction in Industry-Specific Universities
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
fd9b89ad8c965d3d4be7255a513cbbde498f584e.abstract: Artificial intelligence has evolved into a general-purpose technology that permeates nearly every corner of knowledge production and social governance. This transformation is pushing college students' digital literacy far beyond the traditional "digitization" benchmark toward what this paper terms "intelligent-digital" literacy. For industry-specific universities—institutions committed to serving specific industries and cultivating application-oriented talents—the significance of AI general education is perhaps even greater than for other types of universities, because their graduates directly enter the industrial chain. Taking the practice of Moutai Institute as a concrete case, this paper elaborates on the internal logic, practical challenges, and feasible pathways for integrating AI general education into students' digital literacy cultivation and cognitive construction. The core argument of this paper is that such education should be anchored in industrial scenarios rather than abstract theory, and that cultivating compound talents equipped with digital literacy, industrial awareness, and social responsibility requires simultaneously grasping three main threads: technological empowerment, value guidance, and cognitive construction. On this basis, this paper proposes a trinity integration framework and offers actionable strategies from four dimensions: curriculum system, teaching model, faculty development, and evaluation mechanism. This paper aims to provide theoretical reference and practical insights for general education reform in industry-specific universities.

title: Ethical Risks and Normative Paths in Digital Communication in the AIGC Era
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
5573bba3e050f67e9a69ebdccbe4b10e2a1ee216.abstract: The rapid rise of generative artificial intelligence (AIGC) has profoundly reshaped the technical foundation and ecological structure of digital communication. From the combined perspective of communication studies and technology ethics, this paper examines four shifts that AIGC has brought to digital communication: the intelligent upgrading of content production, the multimodal expansion of representational forms, the pluralistic restructuring of production subjects, and the turn toward a precise and personalized communication logic. However, viewed along four dimensions—the erosion of authenticity, the illusion of neutrality, the loss of boundaries, and the rupture of rights and responsibilities—digital communication in the AIGC era faces serious ethical risks, including the spread of false information, algorithmic bias and value skew, data security and privacy leakage, disputes over content ownership, and the weakening of media responsibility. This study argues that a normative path combining "institutional constraint, responsibility strengthening, ethical shaping, and literacy improvement" is needed, so as to keep a dynamic balance between technological innovation and ethical order and to promote the healthy development of the digital communication ecosystem.

title: Visual Filters and Digital Subjectivity on Chinese Social Media: Platform Power, Beauty Labour, and Identity Negotiation
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
9387f9c074aafa6eb125ca75910420817a0cc956.abstract: In the digital presentation of the self, visual filters can have a huge impact in Chinese social media on identity construction and expression, emotional expression, and social expectation negotiation. In this research, we will look at the double effect of the visual filters on Douyin and Xiaohongshu (Rednote) and how they (re)produce aesthetic standards and offer possibilities for individual agency. Taking on the qualitative case study approach, the three types of filtering - beautification filters connected to the "bai-you-shou" aesthetic, crying filters for an expression of emotions, and cartoon distortion filters for concealment of identity - are examined based on the theory of disciplinary power and technologies of the self and the theory of emotional capitalism and the theory of everyday tactics. The analysis shows that beautification filters are suitable for the function of self-surveillance and beautification work in the online space, and the emotional filters have an influence on the presentation and perception of emotion in an online space. Filters for concealment, on the other hand, offer other ways to work on issues of visibility and negotiate privacy. These practices show visual filters to not only be about platform control, but also not solely about personal empowerment. Rather, they must be comprehended within the dynamic between platform architecture and cultural norms and uses of the platform. This study integrates the aspects of aesthetic control, emotional expression and identity management of digital subjectivity to social media in the modern China, which enriches the research on digital subjectivity in China with a more sophisticated dimension.

title: Research Review on Online Identity Construction and Personal IP Commercialisation in the Digital‑Media Era
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
8c6bfb2566828d37e61c6639e9b1987ebdb9cd2a.abstract: Against the backdrop of iterative mobile internet technologies and an increasingly mature social media ecosystem, the traffic economy has gained growing prominence. Ordinary internet users are no longer passive recipients of information, through sustained online content creation, they can proactively construct digital identities and cultivate personal intellectual property (IP) to achieve commercial monetization. As a representative phenomenon in the digital media sector, personal IP commercialization has reshaped employment patterns and content production logic within the new media industry. Taking Xiaohongshu as the research context, this paper employs literature review and case study methods. It synthesizes core theories of online identity construction, personal IP, and the attention economy, and unpacks the end-to-end monetization pathway of personal IP. The study further examines practical risks including fabricated personas, user privacy breaches, and interest conflicts within multi-channel network (MCN) institutions, and puts forward targeted optimization countermeasures across four stakeholder dimensions: creators, platforms, regulatory authorities, and consumers. The findings reveal that the commercial value of personal IP is anchored in stable online personas and trust-based relationships with followers. Nevertheless, fierce competition for platform traffic tends to breed problems such as persona fabrication and excessive marketing. This study enhances understanding of the operational logic of the self-media industry in the digital era and helps identify systemic industry risks, thereby providing theoretical references for the healthy and sustainable development of the new media sector.

title: Digital Marketing and Inclusive Finance: A Mechanism Analysis from the Perspectives of Cost Optimization, Efficiency Enhancement, and Resource Allocation
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
fda7008da5d52e7526e5c13b4045cf16e4eded21.abstract: Inclusive finance has long been limited by information asymmetry, insufficient physical branch coverage, and the "80/20 rule" mindset, which has left long-tail customer segments underserved. The spread of digital technology offers a possible way to ease these problems. Drawing on long-tail theory, market efficiency theory, and capital cost theory, this study employs a theory-driven literature review to examine how digital marketing supports inclusive finance, focusing on its pathways, main mechanisms, and practical limits. The review indicates that digital marketing changes traditional financial service models in three main ways: it reduces information asymmetry, extends service reach, and improves resource allocation. In practice, these effects come mainly from lower costs (reducing information costs, outreach costs, and customer acquisition costs) and higher efficiency (improving information matching, operational efficiency, and customer lifecycle management). Besides, the high initial customer acquisition cost (CAC), the structural mismatch between the cost and return when providing services to low-income groups (long-tail customers) on a large scale through low-profit products, as well as the weak business sustainability, still pose significant limitations to this model. This study has constructed a comprehensive theoretical framework to understand how digital marketing supports the development of inclusive finance, while also pointing out its practical limitations.

title: Free Digital Content Business Model: Value Creation Mechanisms and Sustainable Competitive Advantage
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
8cc8519fe1f0eddd078050493f14587269f442ef.abstract: Digital media's rapid development has changed how content platforms create, promote, and monetize content. In China, the free content plus advertising model has become increasingly important in the digital content industry. This study uses Fanjie Free Novel from ByteDance as the case, combining zero-price effect and two-sided market theory to analyze the value creation mechanism, structural challenges, and sustainability problems of free digital content business models. The study finds that a free business model can lower the entry barrier for users and rapidly scale the market, and a two-sided market model can help the platform turn users' attention into revenue through advertising. At the same time, large-scale behavior data can support content discovery, recommendation, and cross-media IP development. However, this model also faces three major challenges: conflicts among lower user commitment, advertising intensity, and user experience. And how creator incentives guided by immediate traffic will affect long-term content quality. To address these challenges, the study suggests a more flexible freemium model, dynamic advertising governance, and a redesigned creator incentive system. These strategies aim to help digital content platforms strike a more stable balance among user growth, monetization, creator incentives, and sustainable competitive advantage.

title: The Dual Effects of Digital Rhetoric on Firm Performance in the Electronic Equipment Manufacturing Industry: Evidence from ROA and Sales Growth Models
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
f5daeb6d07e7478885d02f300bec48a81b14558c.abstract: Digital transformation has expanded from actual investment to the way firms describe their digital plans in annual reports. This study examines whether digital rhetoric affects firm performance and whether its effects change over time. The sample contains 50 A-share firms and 150 firm-year observations from China's C39 industry between 2023 and 2025. Digital rhetoric is measured through selected keywords in the Management Discussion and Analysis section. Ordinary least squares models with standard errors clustered at the firm level are used to examine ROA and sales growth. The results show that digital rhetoric is positively and significantly related to ROA. Its relation with sales growth is positive but not statistically significant, and the effect becomes weaker in later years. The findings suggest that digital rhetoric may support current profitability without producing immediate sales expansion. This study adds a disclosure-based perspective to research on digital transformation and distinguishes substantive digital change from symbolic expression.

title: Existing Development Issues and Optimised Governance Strategies in the Digital Economy Era
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
379f1a8c197985c8c9101e52d4da8072d9caca32.abstract: Against the backdrop of the global wave of digital industrial transformation, the digital economy has become a key driver of high-quality economic development in China. In 2024, China's digital economy reached RMB 59.2 trillion, accounting for 43.8% of GDP. Yet rapid expansion has also generated multiple governance challenges. Drawing on industry reports, official regulatory documents, authoritative news cases, and Chinese and international academic literature, this paper systematically examines the practical constraints on the sustainable development of the digital economy from four dimensions: market competition, data security, balanced industrial development, and digital labour. It also analyses the underlying mechanisms of these problems through the representative case of the Ctrip antitrust penalty. The study finds that an incomplete legal framework, fragmented cross-departmental regulation, insufficient supporting industrial policies, and the absence of rules protecting digital workers have collectively contributed to disorderly operation by digital platforms. Accordingly, it proposes a comprehensive optimisation framework at four levels: legal reform, coordinated government regulation, industrial policy support, and protection of workers' rights and interests. The findings offer practical governance guidance for balancing the innovative dynamism of the digital economy with regulated development.

title: Low-Cost Experimentation in the Attention Market: Evidence from Short-Drama Platforms
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
0065405c5d496314070b363ae470f902432a1016.abstract: With the development of micro-short dramas, new forms of content creation and market experiments for digital entertainment have emerged. Micro-short dramas generally have a lower production cost than traditional television programs and a shorter production cycle, and thus can be quickly promoted by the platform. Therefore, the producer can test various content ideas and adapt to changes in the audience's desires. However, a more efficient market learning may also lead to the repeated production of successful genres and narrative patterns, thereby reducing content diversity. This paper studies the relationship among low-cost experimentation, platform feedback, attention concentration and content diversity in the Chinese market for micro-short dramas. Using the publicly available Top 20 recommendation ranking data from the Hongguo platform, a descriptive analysis of production formats, narrative genres, Recommendation Values, Heat Values, and new-release status was conducted in this study. Based on the above data, animated and AI-generated dramas have achieved remarkable results and are now popular entries in the ranking list. At the same time, the attention of the audience is not even, and some genres and narrative patterns appear repeatedly in the rankings. The results show that low-cost experimentation can enhance the efficiency of content testing and market learning, but the speed of platform feedback may also lead to a concentration of attention on already successful content models. A potential conflict exists between the efficiency of market learning and content diversity in the platform-based entertainment market.

title: Digital Transformation and Marketing Capability: The Moderating Role of Digital Marketing
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
af9f177791425843f1cee676819d3dac123aec42.abstract: Based on the resource-based view and contingency theory, this study investigates the impact of digital transformation on corporate marketing capabilities and examines the moderating role of digital marketing. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2024, the empirical analysis reveals that digital transformation significantly enhances marketing capabilities, while digital marketing further strengthens the causal relationship between them. Heterogeneity analysis shows that these effects vary across firms at different life cycle stages and with different pollution attributes. This study extends existing research on the microeconomic consequences of digital transformation and provides practical insights for firms in converting digital resources into competitive advantages in marketing.

title: Digital Collaboration‑Oriented Supply Chain Management for Fast‑Fashion Enterprises: A Case Study of UNIQLO
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
a519adc18d3bf02befa1d7c43dc95bb954645bbb.abstract: In the post-pandemic era, global supply chains have shifted from prioritizing efficiency to placing equal emphasis on efficiency, safety, and resilience. The push-based supply chain model in the fast fashion industry can easily lead to a series of problems, including stockouts and excess inventory, insufficient supply chain resilience, poor cash flow between upstream and downstream sectors, and an amplified bullwhip effect. This paper examines how fast fashion companies can match supply with demand across the chain and enhance chain-wide resilience through optimization of the chain network, digital collaboration, and digital financing. The paper analyses the SPA vertically integrated network of the company, the digitally enabled information-sharing mechanisms and the company's core-enterprise-credit-based "1+N" supply chain finance model by conducting a literature review and analysing one case study of UNIQLO (Fast Retailing Group). The findings show that integrating digital collaboration, network optimization, and supply chain finance enables fast fashion firms to better match supply with demand and build resilience.

title: Research on the Impact of Digital Inclusive Finance on Corporate Financing Cost: Theoretical Mechanism and Empirical Test
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
32da85f2bcf3ec50c906969f77ad069190e3c8de.abstract: Based on the data of A-share non-financial listed companies from 2011 to 2023, this paper matches the Peking University prefecture-level city digital inclusive finance index with corporate financial data, and empirically examines the impact of digital inclusive finance on corporate financing cost and its mechanism of action. Financing cost is measured by the financial expense ratio, and the industry and year fixed effects model is used for estimation. The study finds that the increase of the regional digital inclusive finance development level significantly reduces corporate financing cost; the mechanism analysis shows that digital inclusive finance plays its role by improving the external information environment of enterprises and raising analyst following and research report coverage. The heterogeneity analysis shows that this effect is more obvious in non-state-owned enterprises, the eastern region and larger-scale enterprises. The study provides an empirical basis for improving digital financial infrastructure, optimizing corporate credit information governance and differentiated credit pricing.

title: Attention Economy and Marketing Mechanisms: A Comparison of Low- and High-Involvement Products
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
71e7bd49a3887adf1a9cbd5ec351725206ea7f7d.abstract: In the era of the attention economy, consumer attention has become an increasingly scarce and valuable marketing resource. With the rapid development of digital platforms and algorithmic recommendation technologies, the way firms acquire and utilize consumer attention has undergone significant changes. This paper uses a conceptual analysis examines how attention-based marketing mechanisms differ across products with different levels of consumer involvement. By integrating insights from attention-based marketing theory and consumer decision-making literature, this paper analyzes two distinct pathways through which attention is transformed into purchase behavior: low-involvement products primarily rely on attention repetition and mental availability to stimulate purchasing, while high-involvement products require deeper information processing and trust formation after attention is captured. The study further discusses how firms can allocate attention resources effectively by adopting broad attention strategies for low-involvement products and deep attention strategies for high-involvement products in the digital marketing environment. This paper contributes to a better understanding of attention allocation in marketing and provides both theoretical and practical implications for firms seeking to improve marketing effectiveness in the attention economy.

title: Exploring How to Optimize Enterprise Marketing Strategies in the Digital Age
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
ac719b262846c02deee219bfab6283279e0b2197.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the proliferation of new media platforms are fundamentally transforming the retail landscape and reshaping consumer decision-making processes. In this evolving environment, conventional, mass-oriented marketing approaches are increasingly inadequate for sustaining competitive advantage in digital markets—evidenced by persistently low customer acquisition efficiency and diminishing brand resonance. This paper systematically examines enterprise-level digital marketing strategies through a dual-method approach: comprehensive literature review and in-depth case analysis. It first maps the current state of the digital marketing ecosystem, then identifies and analyzes critical implementation barriers—including organizational silos, data fragmentation, and capability gaps—that hinder effective digital marketing adoption, further clarifies the core strategic advantages of digital marketing (e.g., real-time responsiveness, audience precision, and iterative optimization) and its tangible business value, and finally proposes forward-looking, actionable recommendations aligned with emerging industry trajectories. Empirical findings indicate that sustainable marketing transformation hinges on three interdependent pillars: seamless cross-channel integration, granular data-driven operationalization, and audience-centric content innovation. These insights provide a rigorous, practice-oriented framework to guide traditional enterprises in navigating their digital marketing transformation.

title: The Impact of Digital Financial Inclusion on Household Consumption Upgrading: Empirical Evidence from Provincial Panel Data in China
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
c8c4fcb78abb98de64939657f64f0a3e6e15f4b6.abstract: Whether digital financial inclusion can push household consumption toward higher-quality categories, and through what channels, remains an open empirical question in the context of domestic demand expansion. This study combines the Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Index with provincial macroeconomic statistics to build a balanced panel covering 31 Chinese provinces over 2013-2022, and estimates two-way fixed effects models that identify the aggregate impact, its regional variation, and the underlying transmission channels. Three findings emerge. First, digital financial inclusion exerts a significant positive influence on consumption upgrading: raising the aggregate index by 1% is associated with an increase of roughly 0.23 percentage points in the share of development- and enjoyment-oriented spending, a result that survives alternative dependent-variable definitions and a one-period lag of the core regressor. Second, the effect is geographically uneven — clearly present in eastern provinces but not yet detectable in central and western ones — which indicates that turning financial supply into actual consumption behavior requires complementary conditions in income, logistics, and consumption scenarios. Third, channel tests lend preliminary support to the digital credit route but not to the payment convenience route, and coverage breadth proves to be the dominant sub-dimension. The evidence can inform more targeted digital finance policies aimed at expanding domestic demand and upgrading consumption.

title: Digital Infrastructure and Urban Green Productivity: Reassessing the Broadband China Pilot Programme
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
703309675c81bd177be9180531defa9ac611a082.abstract: Broadband expansion may support economic growth, but its green-productivity benefits remain uncertain. Establishing whether local designation delivers these benefits matters for evaluating digital investment. This paper assesses the Broadband China designation in 285 cities over 2008-2022, using cumulative green TFP and annual productivity change. A staggered difference-in-differences approach compares designation cohorts with never-designated cities. The average cumulative-productivity estimate is 0.0051 log points, or about 0.51%, with a 95% confidence interval of −0.96% to 2.00%. The annual-change estimate is also statistically indistinguishable from zero. With baseline adjustment, the cumulative estimate increases to 0.70% but remains statistically insignificant, and the joint pretreatment test no longer rejects. Non-rejection does not establish identification. Unadjusted pretreatment differences are concentrated primarily in the 2014 cohort. Removing that cohort, matching cities and excluding areas with partial treatment leave the average cumulative effect statistically insignificant. Resource-group contrasts remain exploratory because both groups exhibit pretreatment differences. The results do not establish automatic green-productivity gains from designation and emphasize the importance of outcome construction, sample selection and treatment geography.

title: Digital Islamic Literacy and Self efficacy in Shaping Santri Religious Behavior: Mediating Attitudes Toward Technology and Moderating Pesantren Culture
container-title: Berkala Ilmiah Pendidikan
a736d04dc6b81135d3d3f3a283f72b38887be08b.abstract: Digital transformation in pesantren education presents challenges in integrating technology use with the development of santri religious behavior, particularly in ensuring alignment with Islamic values and pesantren culture. This study examines the effects of Islamic digital literacy and digital self-efficacy on santri religious behavior, considering attitudes toward technology as a mediating variable and pesantren culture as a moderating variable. A quantitative approach was employed through a survey involving 200 Madrasah Aliyah students residing in traditional and modern pesantren in Kudus Regency, Central Java, Indonesia. Respondents were selected using proportionate stratified random sampling based on grade levels (X, XI, and XII) within each madrasah, with random selection following proportional allocation. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings reveal that Islamic digital literacy and digital self-efficacy have positive and significant effects on santri religious behavior. Both variables also significantly influence attitudes toward technology, which mediate the relationships between digital competencies and religious behavior. Furthermore, pesantren culture strengthens the relationship between attitudes toward technology and santri religious behavior. These findings indicate that religious behavior in digitally evolving educational environments depends not only on individual digital competencies but also on positive attitudes toward technology and institutional cultural values. The study concludes that managing digital transformation in Islamic education requires integrating digital competency development, positive technological attitudes, and the preservation of pesantren culture. Accordingly, pesantren administrators are encouraged to implement Islamic value-based digital literacy programs supported by institutional guidance and cultural reinforcement.

title: Telugu Handwritten Word Recognition Using an Autoregressive Transformer Decoder with Joint CTC-Attention Training
c1a3bfeb651c0560b822b8ee2fdeb51dd0fa2377.abstract: Abstract Telugu handwriting recognition remains difficult, largely because of the script’s syllabic structure. Consonants fuse with vowel diacritics and stack into conjuncts via the virama; the resulting compound glyphs bear little visual resemblance to their constituent characters. We compare a CNN-BiLSTM-CTC baseline with an autoregressive Transformer decoder trained under a joint CTC-attention loss on the IIIT-HW-Telugu benchmark (80,693 training images, 17,910 test images). Both decoders share a stride-modified ResNet-18 encoder that preserves horizontal resolution for sequential decoding. We also construct a character bigram transition matrix from the training labels and apply it as a soft constraint during inference. The best Transformer configuration achieves 3.66% character error rate (CER), a 6.4% relative reduction over the CTC baseline’s 3.91%. Two details proved critical for convergence: scaling token embeddings by √ d model and tying input–output embedding weights. An earlier decoder lacking both still trained but plateaued at 4.89% CER—below the CTC baseline—though that comparison confounds several hyperparameters and is not an isolated ablation. Error analysis reveals a practical trade-off: CTC scatters small substitutions across many samples , while the Transformer is more accurate on average but occasionally exhibits what we term autoregressive collapse, confidently emitting a valid Telugu word unrelated to the input image. Code and trained weights are publicly available.

title: Grandparental Involvement in Chinese Intergenerational Coparenting: A Digital Collage-Assisted Interview Study of Adolescents' Experiences
container-title: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
ca3bc872a176768ffdf8bce27a9192948dfb41c1.abstract: In multigenerational families in China, grandparents typically share child-rearing responsibilities with parents, but little is currently known about how adolescents experience this arrangement. Using the Process Model of Family Functioning (PMFF) in seven essential dimensions, this study observed how teenagers understood grandparental contribution in family interactions and connected it with family relationships and their experience of happiness. Seven participants who were being interviewed aged 15–18, all living with their parents and grandparents, took part in online interviews (Tencent Meeting). Thematic analysis mainly identified three themes: task accomplishment and role performance in daily care; communication and emotional expression during family conflicts; and teenagers' interpretations of how grandparental contribution how to impact their experience of happiness. Grandparents directly managed daily routines but had less authority over educational decisions. For instance, during conflicts they explained both sides and spoke for participants, though they could not always change parents' decisions. In addition, participants often experienced warmth from those caring and understood reasonable discipline as care. Finally, these findings suggest that interactions between grandparents and teenagers, as well as the teenagers' interpretations of these interactions, jointly shape the meaning of grandparental involvement.

title: Development of a Multidimensional Computerized Adaptive Testing Program for Measuring Digital Competency Level in Higher Education
container-title: Suranaree Journal of Social Science
50aa1bad152576982eb8989c05f149347267106e.abstract: Background and Objectives: Thailand has implemented policies to promote and develop digital competencies among students, which require all universities to assess students’ digital competencies prior to graduation. As a result, many small universities face resources shortages for conducting such assessments. Therefore, the development of an online testing system serves as a potential solution to this issue. This research aimed to develop a digital competency item bank and validate the effectiveness of a Multidimensional Computerized Adaptive Testing (MCAT) program. Methodology: This research employed a research and development (R&D) design. Participants consisted of fourth-year undergraduate students enrolled in higher education institutions in Thailand during the academic year 2023–2024, from the fields of Health Sciences, Science and Technology, and Humanities and Social Sciences. The results indicated that the digital competency item bank contained 211 items and 30 indicators. The item bank was developed using a three-parameter Multidimensional Item Response Theory (MIRT) model. The test demonstrated an EAP reliability of 0.865. Digital competency levels were interpreted using a Wright Map. Additionally, the MCAT program was developed using PHP and MySQL. Results: The quality of 211 items in the item bank was analyzed using three-parameter item response theory. The items demonstrated an average discrimination parameter of 1.44, an average difficulty parameter of 0.24, and an average guessing parameter of 0.13. The item bank was categorized into three modules based on the difficulty parameter. The digital competency model was developed in accordance with the between-items multidimensional item response theory with three parameters. Digital competency level cutoff scores were determined by defining a criterion zone on the Wright map at the mean ability threshold (θd) of -0.39. The results indicated that 69.27 percent of students met the digital competency criteria. The highest level of digital competency was observed in Component 1, Information and Digital Media Literacy, followed by Component 3, Adaptability to the Digital Transformation Era, while the lowest level was found in Component 2, Skill for using, developing, and problem-solving with digital tools. In addition, the findings demonstrated that the MCAT program accurately evaluated digital competency with only 22 items, using a variable-length termination criterion of SE(θ) < 0.30 (RMSE = 0.112). This approach provides an effective method to reduce the testing burden. Discussions: The MCAT program demonstrates the feasibility of implementing a reliable and efficient assessment tool in resource-constrained higher education institutions. At the same time, the study suggests a direction for future development in competency assessment on a web-based platform, which enhances the possibilities for implementing MIRT within an educational organization. Conclusions: The MCAT program demonstrated strong performance across all assessed dimensions, including content validity, indicators, and program structure. The MCAT program consists of an item bank, initial item selection, subsequent item selection, and a termination criterion. The MCAT approach requires less time and fewer items than traditional tests, with the optimal number of items for accurate ability estimation being 22. Overall, the MCAT program provides an appropriate and practical solution for equitable implementation across large, medium, and small universities.

title: Development and Content Validation of the YANR Digital Family Support Nursing Framework for Mental Health Care: A Modified Delphi Study
container-title: F1000Research
9b829a6afe274fa8e26ba864763133d21c09b608.abstract: Background Family caregivers play a vital role in supporting individuals with mental health conditions. Effective support requires competencies in mental health literacy, emotional support, caregiving, problem-solving, relapse prevention, and access to professional and community resources. Therefore, an integrated framework is needed to guide family support nursing practices. Methods A methodological framework-development study was conducted involving eight experts from mental health nursing, family nursing, and nursing research methodology. The framework was evaluated using a structured instrument comprising 48-items across eight assessment groups, including six framework domains and implementation-related components. Experts rated item relevance using a four-point scale and provided qualitative feedback. Ratings of 3 or 4 were classified as positive for content validity assessment. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize expert ratings, while qualitative comments were reviewed to inform revisions between rounds. Content validity was assessed using the item-level content validity index (I-CVI) and scale-level content validity index based on the average method (S-CVI/Ave). Results The overall mean rating increased from 3.779 in Round 1 to 3.883 in Round 2. The proportion of ratings assigned the highest score of 4 increased from 77.9% to 88.3% after the intervention. The mean ratings increased across all eight assessment groups after framework refinement. In both rounds, all 48 items achieved an I-CVI of 1.00 and an S-CVI/Ave of 1.00. These findings indicate complete expert agreement on item relevance under predefined dichotomization rules. Conclusion The two-round modified Delphi process supported the content relevance of the YANR Digital Family Support Nursing Framework for Mental Health Care and informed its refinement through expert feedback. The findings provide an initial basis for further framework development. Subsequent research should examine its comprehensibility, feasibility, and practical utility, followed by evaluation of its effectiveness in nursing practice. The findings should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical effectiveness.

title: When Digital Access Becomes Investment Capability: Financial Literacy and Portfolio Diversification Across Countries
ce1da44064707ee52911227159149d97f1ba2d4d.abstract: Abstract This study tests whether macro-level conditions corresponding to economic, functional, emotional and social value explain cross-country variation in a digital investment adoption proxy, whether adoption is associated with a broader portfolio-diversification environment, and whether financial-literacy capacity strengthens that conversion.A five-wave panel covering 82 countries and 291 country-year observations is assembled for the 2011, 2014, 2017, 2021 and 2024 Global Findex waves using open World Bank Development Indicators and Global Findex series. Entropy-weighted composite indices are estimated in two-way country and year fixed-effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors. K-means clustering, silhouette validation and ANOVA provide descriptive market typologies.Economic and social value-enabling conditions positively predict adoption, whereas functional and emotional proxies are negative in the within-country specification. Adoption is positively associated with diversification (β = 0.049, p = 0.008), and its interaction with financial-literacy capacity is positive (β = 0.088, p = 0.006). Cluster estimates require caution: the mature-market interaction has a larger point estimate but is statistically imprecise (p = 0.207), while the low-access estimate is smaller but significant.The paper moves beyond intention-based, single-country digital-banking studies by testing a macro analogue of perceived value, linking adoption to a consequential market outcome and identifying financial literacy as a conversion capability. It also shows where a simple monotonic transfer of micro perceived-value predictions fails under country fixed effects.

title: Assessing the attentional dynamics of Responding to Joint Attention in infancy via online webcam-based eye-tracking
container-title: Frontiers in Developmental Psychology
77866589d1bd517913c2a28ccae5a091111ff709.abstract: Responding to Joint Attention (RJA) is a foundational social-cognitive skill that unfolds through a sequence of distinct attentional processes: engagement with a social partner, orienting toward a referent, and sustained attention to a shared point of interest. Traditional assessments of joint attention often rely on aggregate behavioral scores that may not capture this fine-grained temporal structure. The present study developed and tested a remotely administered, webcam-based eye-tracking task, delivered via the Labvanced platform, to characterize the attentional dynamics underlying RJA in infants and toddlers aged 10 to 36 months ( N = 29). The task decomposed RJA into three sequential phases and included a gaze-contingent delay manipulation to probe how infants balance attention between the social partner and the cued object under varying temporal demands, quantified through dwell time and gaze re-engagement (entry rate) toward the face, the cued object, and an uncued object. Infants showed a clear attentional hierarchy, with the greatest engagement directed toward the face during the early phases, followed by a gradual reallocation of attention toward the cued object as the referent became identifiable. This temporal profile is consistent with theoretical accounts describing joint attention as an unfolding sequence, in which infants first anchor attention to the social partner before coordinating it with a shared referent. Age-related differences emerged selectively in later phases of attentional maintenance, with older infants showing reduced monitoring of the social partner's face after the partner's gaze had shifted toward the referent while attention to the target itself remained stable across age, although the wide age range relative to sample size may limit sensitivity to finer-grained developmental change. Together, these findings support the feasibility of remote, webcam-based eye-tracking for capturing fine-grained dynamics of early social attention, supporting progression to future pilot testing of developmental and clinical applications.

title: Comparative evaluation of ResNet-Based AI models for breast cancer detection in digital mammography and digital breast tomosynthesis
container-title: Frontiers in Systems Biology
b5cd32e8397df1843cd74bcffa6248924139b1ea.abstract: Introduction Early detection of breast cancer is crucial for better treatment options; however, physicians usually encounter challenges when reading breast mammograms because some tissues can overlap or look similar. New computer technologies can help by highlighting areas that may contain cancer. In this study, we assessed computer systems to identify whether a breast image is normal, benign or malignant and compared their performance on standard digital mammography (DM) and digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) images. Methods This retrospective study included 31 (100 after augmentation) images with malignant breast lesions, 175 with benign findings, and 475 normal images. We developed a deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) model to classify images using ResNet-18 and ResNet-50. We trained the model via 10-fold cross-validation and Holdout validation. Performance was measured for each model. We computed performance metrics on original (non-augmented) images from 10-fold cross-validated predictions, with 95% confidence intervals from a stratified patient-level bootstrap (2,000 replicates), precision–recall analysis with average precision (AP), and paired DeLong and exact McNemar tests with Holm correction. We increased the malignant class from 31 to 100 images in the training set via data augmentation for the stage-2 classifier. Validation used non-augmented images. Results In normal versus abnormal classification (679 original images per view; ResNet-18, 10-fold cross-validation), DM CC, DM MLO and DBT MLO achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.995 (95% CI 0.991–0.998), 0.984 (0.975–0.992) and 0.994 (0.989–0.998), sensitivity of 95.1%, 95.6% and 95.1%, and specificity of 96.6%, 94.1% and 98.5%, respectively. DBT had significantly higher specificity than DM in selected comparisons (ResNet-18 vs. DM MLO and ResNet-50 vs. DM CC; Holm-adjusted p ≤ 0.002), with no significant AUC-ROC differences between modalities or architectures (all Holm-adjusted p ≥ 0.13). In benign versus malignant classification (131 original images, 31 malignant), AUC-ROC ranged from 0.977 to 0.999 and AP from 0.946 to 0.996, with no significant differences between DM and DBT or between ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 (all Holm-adjusted p ≥ 0.50). The detection and classification of malignant, benign, and normal images in DBT and DM using an artificial intelligence (AI) training model achieved comparable performance to the medical field. Conclusion Computer systems can detect and classify breast findings with high accuracy, helping to reduce errors and support physicians’ decisions. The original number of malignant images was relatively small (n = 31), which may affect the model’s generalizability and highlights the need for validation on larger, multi-institutional datasets. These findings may encourage more use of computer-assisted detection in breast imaging and contribute to developing better tools for early breast cancer diagnosis.

title: Digital and media literacy of pre-service early childhood teachers in the context of digital education: a bibliometric analysis of research trends
container-title: Frontiers in Education
d30a7ab21a2572baebc484bf5f6c1f3ecb274a3d.abstract: The digital transformation of education is increasing the demands placed on the professional preparation of pre-service early childhood teachers, including the development of digital competence, media literacy, and emerging competencies related to the use of artificial intelligence. Despite the growing body of research in this area, the conceptual structure of the field and the relationships among these strands remain insufficiently systematized. This study aims to analyze the structure and development of international research on the digital and media literacy of pre-service early childhood teachers, identify the main thematic directions, examine the nature of their interrelationships, and determine existing research gaps. The bibliometric corpus was constructed using data from Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection through a refined search strategy, comparison of the results of two searches, and manual screening of non-relevant records. To avoid distortions associated with an incomplete calendar year, the analysis was limited to the period 2012–2025, resulting in a final corpus of 86 publications. The analysis was conducted using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and included descriptive bibliometric indicators, analysis of scientific collaboration and citation impact, structured content analysis of the most highly cited publications, frequency and network analysis of author keywords, and thematic mapping. The findings show that digital competence and early childhood education occupy central positions in the conceptual structure of the field, whereas media literacy represents a related but less integrated research strand. AI-related topics are present in the field but remain relatively infrequent and do not yet form an independent thematic cluster, indicating a limited degree of thematic consolidation. The identified structure points to uneven development and limited thematic integration among digital competence, media literacy, and AI literacy. Based on these findings, the Conceptual Continuity Model of Digital Competence, Media Literacy and AI Literacy in Pre-Service Early Childhood Teacher Education is proposed. The model conceptualizes these components as complementary dimensions of professional digital judgment, integrated at the level of responsible pedagogical decision-making concerning children's digital experiences. The model is conceptual, non-hierarchical, and non-causal in nature and requires further empirical testing.

title: Factors associated with fatigue in systemic lupus erythematosus: a cross-sectional structural equation modeling analysis of depressive symptoms as a potential mediator
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
f93b1db1c07e7d903eced787f7dbac6bb5cedb6b.abstract: Objectives This study examined physiological, psychological, and environmental factors associated with fatigue in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and assessed whether depressive symptoms statistically mediated the relationships between these factors and fatigue. Methods A convenience sample of 252 patients with SLE was recruited from the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University, between June 2023 and June 2024. Guided by the Theory of Unpleasant Symptoms (TOUS), candidate variables were classified into physiological (including disease activity on the SLEDAI-2K, anemia, biologic agent use, and sleep disturbance), psychological (anxiety and depressive symptoms), and environmental factors (including employment status and social support). Pain severity and other clinically recorded variables were entered as covariates. Validated measures included the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS), Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). Univariate analyses, Spearman correlation analysis, and multivariable linear regression were performed using SPSS 26.0. Structural equation modeling (SEM) and indirect-effect testing based on bootstrapping (2,000 resamples; percentile 95% confidence intervals) were performed in R (lavaan). Sensitivity analyses (robust estimation, a Bollen–Stine bootstrap, and covariate-adjusted and alternative mediator models) were also performed. Results Social support, depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, pain severity, biologic agent use, and employment status were found to be independently related to fatigue. Moreover, social support and sleep disturbance each had a significant indirect relationship with fatigue via depressive symptoms. The indirect associations persisted after clinical covariates were specified as predictors of both depressive symptoms and fatigue. However, social support was not independently associated with the binary fatigue outcome (FSS ≥ 4; OR = 0.96 per SD, P = 0.837). Conclusions In this cross-sectional sample, social support, depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, pain severity, biologic agent use, and employment status were associated with fatigue, and depressive symptoms showed a statistically significant indirect association with fatigue through pathways linking social support and sleep disturbance. Because the data are cross-sectional, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory indirect associations that are compatible with, but do not establish, a mediating mechanism, and as hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of causality or treatment effect. Systematic assessment of social support and depressive symptoms, together with dynamic evaluation of sleep disturbance and pain, may inform comprehensive fatigue assessment, while longitudinal and interventional studies are needed before firm clinical recommendations can be made.

title: STRATEGI BIMBINGAN DAN KONSELING DALAM PENGEMBANGAN LITERASI DIGITAL SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR
container-title: ELEMENTARY: Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Dasar
4e3d37b2b4783a91b1eeaf4c184a7f847f98e32d.abstract: The need for digital literacy is becoming increasingly important because elementary school students’ ability to utilize digital technology is not yet fully consistent across the board. Furthermore, guidance and counseling strategies aimed at developing digital literacy among elementary school students remain relatively limited. Therefore, a study is needed that not only examines the media or technology used but also maps out guidance and counseling strategies and the dimensions of digital literacy being developed. This study aims to analyze guidance and counseling strategies in the development of elementary school students’ digital literacy, identify the dimensions of digital literacy being developed, and examine the outcomes and factors influencing their implementation. The study employs a literature review method using a descriptive-qualitative approach. Literature was sourced from various scientific sources published between 2020 and 2026. Relevant articles were selected through a review of titles and abstracts, verification of full texts, data extraction, and thematic synthesis. A total of 20 articles were analyzed based on service strategies, dimensions of digital literacy, research findings, and supporting and inhibiting factors. The results of the study indicate that guidance and counseling strategies in the development of digital literacy can be categorized into preventive, developmental, remedial or curative, digital media-based, and collaborative strategies. The dimensions developed include information literacy and critical thinking, communication and collaboration, digital creation, digital safety and ethics, and self-regulation in the use of technology. The synthesis indicates that the contribution of guidance and counseling lies not only in enhancing digital competencies but also in fostering digital self-regulation through ongoing support and collaboration among counselors, teachers, parents, and schools. This study underscores the importance of strengthening the role of guidance and counseling in fostering digital behavior among students that is competent, critical, safe, ethical, productive, and self-regulated. ABSTRAK Kebutuhan terhadap literasi digital menjadi semakin penting karena kemampuan siswa sekolah dasar dalam memanfaatkan teknologi digital belum sepenuhnya merata. Lebih lanjut, bahwa strategi layanan BK dengan pengembangan literasi digital siswa sekolah dasar masih relatif terbatas. Oleh karena itu, diperlukan kajian yang tidak hanya melihat media atau teknologi yang digunakan, tetapi juga memetakan strategi layanan BK hingga dimensi literasi digital yang dikembangkan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis strategi bimbingan dan konseling dalam pengembangan literasi digital siswa sekolah dasar, mengidentifikasi dimensi literasi digital yang dikembangkan, serta mengkaji hasil dan faktor yang memengaruhi penerapannya. Penelitian menggunakan metode kajian pustaka dengan pendekatan deskriptif-kualitatif. Literatur ditelusuri dari berbagai sumber ilmiah dengan rentang publikasi 2020–2026. Artikel yang relevan diseleksi melalui penelaahan judul dan abstrak, verifikasi teks lengkap, ekstraksi data, serta sintesis tematik. Sebanyak 20 artikel dianalisis berdasarkan strategi layanan, dimensi literasi digital, hasil penelitian, dan faktor pendukung maupun penghambat. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa strategi bimbingan dan konseling dalam pengembangan literasi digital dapat dikelompokkan menjadi strategi preventif, developmental, remedial atau kuratif, berbasis media digital, dan kolaboratif. Dimensi yang dikembangkan meliputi literasi informasi dan berpikir kritis, komunikasi dan kolaborasi, kreasi digital, keamanan dan etika digital, serta regulasi diri dalam penggunaan teknologi. Sintesis menunjukkan bahwa kontribusi BK tidak hanya terletak pada peningkatan kompetensi digital, tetapi juga pada pembentukan regulasi diri digital melalui pendampingan yang berkelanjutan dan kolaborasi antara konselor, guru, orang tua, dan sekolah. Kajian ini menegaskan pentingnya penguatan peran BK dalam membangun perilaku digital siswa yang cakap, kritis, aman, etis, produktif, dan terkendali.

title: Community-based organizations’ experiences in using a digital resource referral platform (ConnectedNest) to support cancer patients
container-title: Supportive Care in Cancer
8b8bc9f1ee438ec793c57422da76f575cae6a514.abstract: Abstract Background Over 8 million US patients with cancer experience health-related social needs (HSRNs) (e.g., food, transportation). Despite the clear importance of addressing HRSNs, there remains a gap in the IT-infrastructure allowing providers to monitor and facilitate patient connections to external resources. We created a community resource referral platform (ConnectedNest) to help connect cancer survivors with community-based organizations (CBOs). The goal of this study was to better understand the feasibility of implementing CRRPs into cancer-focused CBOs. Methods After piloting ConnectedNest, we invited 13 CBOs to participate in semi-structured interviews to learn from their experience. Two qualitative researchers used a directed content analysis approach to identify insights and key recommendations for improving engagement based on constructs from the RE-AIM Framework. Results We identified barriers and facilitators describing their (1) adoption of the ConnectedNest technology, (2) reach of clients, (3) implementation of ConnectedNest, and (4) long-term maintenance of the technology. CBOs varied in both in their organization’s programming and target populations. Participants reported alignment between ConnectedNest workflows and organizational roles as key factors for implementation success. All CBOs expressed interest in continuing to use ConnectedNest. Key recommendations include improving data integration and enhancing the caregiver-user experience. Discussion CBO programming breadth and the size of their target client population largely determined their experience during the pilot study. Community resource referral platforms can support CBOs by clearly distinguishing unique programs and eligibility requirements within the platform. Conclusion Community resource referral platforms have potential acceptability among cancer-focused CBOs. Co-creators see the potential value of these tools.

title: Spatial Attention Mechanism for Improved Multi-Focus Satellite Image Fusion: SARA-Net Model
container-title: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
119f7b73f19f2e73145cc4f9e15a610ef3f19eb4.abstract: Multi-focus image fusion is crucial in various fields, particularly in satellite images, because it creates intricate images with augmented clarity. However, maintaining the original structure is challenging, leading to a reduction in performance. Therefore, this research proposes a Spatial Attention ResNet-50 Network (SARA-Net) model for fusing multiple satellite images. The proposed model utilizes an integration of ResNet-50 and Spatial Attention to effectively extract spatially significant features from actual images. Initially, satellite images from the publicly available SpaceNet datasets are preprocessed by normalization and grayscale conversion to provide consistency. ResNet-50 handles multi-scale feature extraction by residual learning, which addresses vanishing gradient issues, whereas spatial attention assigns adaptive weights to improve relevant spatial information within the feature map. The fusion layer combines these attention features to generate high-resolution and detail-preserving images. On the ten held-out test images, the proposed SARA-Net achieves a PSNR of 48.972 dB, an SSIM of 0.9953, and an entropy value of 8.4319, which is better than the existing methods.

title: ПЕДАГОГІЧНІ УМОВИ ФОРМУВАННЯ ІНФОРМАЦІЙНОЇ КУЛЬТУРИ ДІТЕЙ ДОШКІЛЬНОГО ВІКУ ЗАСОБАМИ ЦИФРОВИХ ТЕХНОЛОГІЙ
