415d8654a1d88d6080c956a763085d97a5f9a8f4.abstract: У статті актуалізовано проблему формування інформаційної культури дітей дошкільного віку в умовах цифрової трансформації освіти та стрімкого розширення інформаційного середовища, у якому з раннього віку перебуває дитина. Обґрунтовано необхідність переходу від розуміння цифрової компетентності дошкільника як сукупності елементарних технічних умінь до комплексного формування інформаційної культури, що охоплює здатність сприймати, розуміти, знаходити, оцінювати й використовувати інформацію відповідно до мети та вікових можливостей, взаємодіяти з різними її джерелами, дотримуватися правил інформаційної та цифрової безпеки, а також відповідально й творчо використовувати цифрові технології. Метою статті є теоретичне обґрунтування педагогічних умов формування інформаційної культури дітей дошкільного віку засобами цифрових технологій та визначення основних напрямів їх реалізації в освітньому процесі закладу дошкільної освіти. Методологічну основу дослідження становлять аналіз, систематизація та узагальнення наукових джерел і нормативно-правових документів, що дали змогу визначити сучасні підходи до цифровізації дошкільної освіти, уточнити зміст поняття «інформаційна культура дітей дошкільного віку» та обґрунтувати сукупність взаємопов’язаних педагогічних умов її формування. На основі теоретичного аналізу визначено інформаційну культуру дітей дошкільного віку як інтегровану характеристику особистості, що виявляється у сформованості позитивної мотивації до пізнання інформації, здатності її сприймати, розуміти, знаходити та використовувати у доступних видах діяльності, взаємодіяти з різними інформаційними джерелами, дотримуватися елементарних правил інформаційної та цифрової безпеки, а також відповідально й творчо використовувати цифрові технології. Обґрунтовано шість взаємопов’язаних педагогічних умов її формування: створення безпечного та педагогічно доцільного цифрового освітнього середовища; змістова інтеграція інформаційної культури з різними видами дитячої діяльності; організація педагогічного супроводу інформаційної діяльності дошкільників; формування навичок критичного та усвідомленого сприймання цифрової інформації; формування цифрової безпеки та відповідальної поведінки; підвищення цифрової компетентності педагогів і педагогічної культури батьків. Встановлено, що результативність формування інформаційної культури визначається не інтенсивністю використання цифрових засобів, а їх педагогічною доцільністю, вікововідповідністю, змістовою спрямованістю та включенням у різні види дитячої діяльності. Акцентовано, що цифрові технології мають доповнювати, а не замінювати гру, безпосереднє спілкування, рухову, художню, конструкторську та дослідницьку діяльність дітей. Визначено провідну роль педагога як організатора та медіатора взаємодії дитини з інформацією, а також значення партнерської взаємодії закладу дошкільної освіти із сім’єю у забезпеченні єдності вимог до цифрової поведінки дитини. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає в систематизації та теоретичному обґрунтуванні комплексу педагогічних умов формування інформаційної культури дітей дошкільного віку засобами цифрових технологій з урахуванням безпечного цифрового середовища, різних видів дитячої діяльності, педагогічного супроводу, критичного сприймання інформації та взаємодії основних суб’єктів освітнього процесу. Практичне значення результатів полягає у можливості їх використання педагогами закладів дошкільної освіти під час добору цифрових ресурсів, організації освітньої та ігрової діяльності дітей, розроблення дидактичних вправ і проблемних ситуацій, а також у роботі з батьками з питань цифрової безпеки та культури використання цифрових технологій.

title: ОСОБЛИВОСТІ ФОРМУВАННЯ ЦИФРОВОЇ КОМПЕТЕНТНОСТІ ВИХОВАТЕЛІВ ЗАКЛАДІВ ДОШКІЛЬНОЇ ОСВІТИ
PECULIARITIES OF THE FORMATION OF DIGITAL COMPETENCE AMONG EDUCATORS OF PRESCHOOL EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
container-title: Human Studies Series of Pedagogy
25535e3c95f331e1319df3b0855419f9bb7cb36d.abstract: У статті розглянуто проблему формування цифрової компетентності вихователів закладів дошкільної освіти в освітньому процесі. Обґрунтовано необхідність розвитку цифрових навичок педагогів як важливої передумови ефективного використання інноваційних технологій, електронних освітніх ресурсів та онлайн-інструментів у професійній діяльності. Проаналізовано наукові підходи до визначення понять «цифрова грамотність» і «цифрова компетентність» та уточнено їх співвідношення. Визначено, що цифрова грамотність є важливою основою формування цифрової компетентності, тоді як цифрова компетентність передбачає здатність педагога педагогічно доцільно, критично, безпечно та відповідально застосовувати цифрові технології у професійній діяльності. Охарактеризовано основні компоненти цифрової компетентності вихователя закладу дошкільної освіти: цифрові й технічні навички; використання цифрових ресурсів в освітньому процесі; цифрову дидактику; цифрову комунікацію; цифрову етику та безпеку; критичне мислення й інформаційну грамотність; безперервний професійний розвиток і самоосвіту. Розглянуто можливості використання сучасних цифрових ресурсів і платформ для професійного розвитку педагогів та організації освітньої взаємодії. Акцентовано увагу на особливостях цифровізації дошкільної освіти в умовах воєнного стану, зокрема використанні дистанційного та змішаного форматів освітньої діяльності. Наголошено на тому, що ефективне формування цифрової компетентності вихователів потребує належного цифрового інфраструктурного забезпечення, методичного супроводу, професійного навчання, доступу до якісного цифрового контенту, мотивації педагогів та можливостей безперервного професійного розвитку. Перспективи подальших досліджень пов’язано з теоретичним обґрунтуванням та експериментальною перевіркою педагогічних умов формування цифрової компетентності вихователів закладів дошкільної освіти.

title: <b>Digital Literacy dan Deep Learning Approach sebagai Determinan Utama Higher Order Thinking Skills Siswa SMK: Bukti Empiris dari Analisis SEM-PLS</b>
container-title: FASTABIQ: JURNAL STUDI ISLAM
b70b0729b39f7d71237e0eda589e569e3963ef22.abstract: Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) have become a fundamental competency in 21st-century vocational education to prepare graduates capable of critical, analytical, and creative problem-solving. However, students' HOTS remain relatively low, while previous studies have predominantly emphasized the effectiveness of instructional models, particularly Project-Based Learning (PjBL), with limited attention to learner capability as the primary determinant of HOTS. Consequently, it remains unclear which factors contribute most substantially to HOTS development. Furthermore, empirical studies integrating Digital Literacy, Deep Learning Approach, and PjBL within a single structural model are still scarce. This study employed a quantitative explanatory design involving 240 vocational high school students. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS), while the moderating role of Deep Learning Approach was examined through the Two-Stage Moderation approach. The findings reveal that Digital Literacy and Deep Learning Approach exert significant positive effects on HOTS, whereas Project-Based Learning does not significantly influence HOTS. In addition, Deep Learning Approach fails to moderate the relationships between Project-Based Learning and HOTS as well as between Digital Literacy and HOTS. These findings indicate that learner capability, represented by Digital Literacy and Deep Learning, plays a more decisive role in developing HOTS than instructional models alone. Therefore, strengthening students' internal learning capabilities should become a strategic priority for improving HOTS in vocational education.

title: From Human Capital to Circular Capabilities: Digital Transformation and Inclusive  Growth Tensions in a Brazilian SME
container-title: Advances in Earth and Environmental Science
ec7a07dab383d35ab20f7aab412ed964b014a0d1.abstract: The circular economy (CE) was popularized by the Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2013) as an alternative to the linear model of extraction, production, and discharge of resources, emphasizing the circularity of products and materials and the regeneration of natural systems. CE models can also be considered as a complementary strategy toward decarbonization. According to the latest report (Macarthur & Heading, 2019), the energy transition can address 55% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, while the remaining 45% are associated with the production of goods and land use. However, CE has primarily been framed in terms of its economic and environmental aspects, and social benefits are usually presented as expected outcomes rather than being systematically investigated. In their analysis of 221 CE definitions in the literature, Kirchherr et al. (2023) found that approximately one-quarter of these definitions contemplate social equity or related concerns such as human well-being, socioeconomic development, and employment.

title: CardioTwin-AI: development and internal validation of a digital twin-based adaptive risk-aware learning framework for heart disease prediction
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
ad124e367bd9776c8ecde4d8d57bbe7082beaa2f.abstract: Heart disease is one of the most common causes of death in the world and early identification of individuals at elevated cardiovascular risk requires reliable risk-assessment methods that can support clinical decision-making. Many conventional machine-learning models focus primarily on disease classification or risk prediction and do not explicitly provide patient-specific virtual representations. This study introduces CardioTwin-AI, a Digital Twin-based Adaptive Risk-Aware Learning Framework (ARLF) to predict the presence or absence of heart disease. We propose a data-driven, patient-specific Digital Twin representation based on clinical attributes, in which the patient state is mapped to a corresponding virtual state and evaluated using state-level synchronization measures, including Twin Simulation Error (TSE) and Twin Fidelity Score (TFS) to quantify representation consistency. The deep feature representations are generated by feature engineering process based on autoencoder, and then analysed by the ARLF prediction model to estimate the probability of the presence of heart disease. It achieved high patient-state representation consistency between the source clinical state and its virtual representation, with a Twin Fidelity Score of 99.76% and a Twin Simulation Error of 0.002402. The proposed ARLF model achieved accuracy of 90.21%, precision of 90.32%, recall of 94.11%, F1-score of 92.18%, and ROC-AUC of 95.13% in the fixed held-out evaluation. The results indicate the potential of CardioTwin-AI for predicting the presence or absence of heart disease and assessing patient-state representation consistency, subject to further external validation and prospective clinical evaluation.

title: A digital quality-improvement program to reduce mortality among intubated children in a public pediatric intensive care unit in Colombia: a pre–post study with interrupted time-series analysis and a protocol for multisite replication
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
cb6600cac1d79c2a54076ba2cc15bcc00e7218b0.abstract: Introduction Mortality among intubated children in public pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) in lowand middle-income countries remains high, driven in part by gaps in workforce training, team coordination, and standardized processes. We evaluated a low-cost, multidisciplinary digital education and team-based quality-improvement (QI) intervention—a multilingual online curriculum, telesimulationbased team training, standardized airway and handoff workflow tools, and on-site visits—in the PICU of a public pediatric hospital in Cartagena, Colombia. Methods In this single-center pre–post QI study, we included all intubated patients (&lt;18 years) admitted to the PICU of Casa del Niño during a baseline period (1 October 2023–30 April 2024), a washout period of near-complete nursing turnover (1 April–30 June 2025), and a post-intervention period (1 July–22 October 2025). The primary outcome, 30-day all-cause mortality, was analyzed by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and the logit of Pediatric Index of Mortality 3 (PIM3)-predicted mortality, calculated without diagnosis-risk terms for all patients because these were not recorded for later patients, supplemented by additional case-mix adjustment, an interrupted time-series analysis of all 272 intubated patients admitted between October 2023 and October 2025 (with the implementation period also modeled as a separate transition segment), and sensitivity analyses. Cost-effectiveness was explored as incremental cost per death and per disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) averted. Results Of 144 patients analyzed (95 pre-intervention; 49 post-intervention), age, sex, and median PIM3 were similar between periods, but mean PIM3-predicted mortality was twice as high before the intervention (10.7% versus 5.3%), reflecting 10 pre-intervention patients with bilaterally fixed pupils (none after). All-cause mortality was 28.4% before and 10.2% after the intervention (risk difference −18.2 percentage points, 95% confidence interval [CI] −29.6 to −4.1; relative risk 0.36, 95% CI 0.15–0.87; adjusted odds ratio 0.26, 95% CI 0.09–0.77). PIM3 under-predicted mortality in both periods (standardized mortality ratio 2.68 and 1.94, respectively). Findings were consistent in case-mix-adjusted analyses and in interrupted time-series analysis with implementation modeled as a separate transition segment (level-change odds ratio 0.24, 95% CI 0.07–0.82). Mortality was higher during implementation (35.9%) than at baseline (27.6%), which was not explained by measured severity of illness. Under the most conservative assumptions (the entire 5-year program cost attributed to the approximately two deaths averted when expected deaths were estimated with PIM3, with 3% discounting), the intervention cost up to approximately US$4,800 per DALY averted, below Colombia’s gross domestic product per capita but above half of it; less conservative scenarios gave lower estimates. Discussion Implementation of this program was associated with lower mortality among intubated children in one public Colombian PICU. Given the single-center, non-randomized design, small sample, and imperfect severity adjustment, these findings require confirmation in controlled multisite evaluations, for which we provide an implementation protocol.

title: Human factors shaping engagement with a digital treatment platform among individuals with lived experience of addiction
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
2797aa3d81395e392855e5dc4c2fc79eaa7166d3.abstract: Introduction Substance use disorders (SUDs) are highly prevalent, yet access to care remains limited. Digital interventions have been investigated as a means to expand treatment access, but individuals routinely disengage from them. We evaluated the acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and usability of a digital platform being tested as part of a collaborative care management-based intervention for SUD treatment in under-resourced areas to identify human factors influencing feasibility, usability, and accessibility. Methods Participants were adults with lived experience of addiction and related treatment. They engaged with the digital treatment platform for one week, then completed semi-structured interviews exploring their experience, followed by the Acceptability of Intervention Measure, Intervention Appropriateness Measure, Feasibility of Intervention Measure, and System Usability Scale. Template-based rapid analysis identified themes. Results 18 individuals ( n = 12 females) completed all assessments. Heavy text, lack of customization, and inconsistent notifications hindered usability. Participants felt assigned goals should match an individual's circumstances and resources available to them to support utilization. Participants desired personalization, integration with existing recovery supports, and features that encouraged routine use. Acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility had respective means of 3.4 (95%CI = 3.0-3.9), 3.3 (95%CI = 2.8-3.9), and 3.4 (95%CI = 2.8-4.0) on 5-point scales with a neutral midpoint of 3. Usability scores approached the commonly used benchmark of 68 (mean=67.6, SD = 15.0). Discussion Digital interventions suffer from heavy disengagement. These findings suggest that digital interventions should fit the end-user's needs and surrounding environment and be both person- and context-specific. Attention to these human factors may improve usability and accessibility, while also limiting additional barriers in under-resourced areas.

title: Preparing future rehabilitation professionals for virtual care: a community case study of Renace digital for telehealth education in Chile
container-title: Frontiers in Health Services
71f04def784a7033b13f29d058b94939719d4a99.abstract: Digital health literacy is increasingly relevant to preparing health professionals for telehealth and virtual care, particularly when digital technologies mediate interactions with people who may experience barriers to accessing and using digital health resources. This community case study describes Renace Digital for Telehealth Education (RD-TE), an educational experience designed to integrate digital health literacy into the preparation of Speech-Language Pathology students for telehealth within a community-based program for older adults. RD-TE used a progressive educational pathway that connected conceptual learning, guided exploration of digital needs, clinical simulation, and application with service users during telerehabilitation practice. Students developed strategies to identify digital barriers, adapt communication and educational approaches, and support users' autonomy in the use of digital technologies. The experience was supported by structured implementation materials for tutors, students, and simulation actors, designed to facilitate replication and adaptation. Complementary quantitative assessments using the eHEALS and the Digital Health Literacy Questionnaire showed higher post-training scores in both measures. However, the difference observed for the adapted 46-item questionnaire did not remain statistically significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.054). These exploratory findings should not be interpreted as evidence of intervention effectiveness. The contribution of RD-TE lies in its structured educational pathway and the availability of detailed implementation materials for tutors, students, and simulation actors, provided as supplementary materials to facilitate replication and adaptation to other rehabilitation education programs and populations. RD-TE offers a practical model for integrating digital health literacy into telehealth education through conceptual learning, clinical simulation, and situated application, with potential for adaptation to continuing professional education for clinicians working in telehealth.

title: SynForge-Cardio: a unified multimodal synthetic dataset generation framework for privacy-preserving cardiovascular AI
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
53d7a1f04e63b97105e6928eb46809e02c7207b9.abstract: Multimodal cardiovascular AI systems benefit from jointly available chest radiographs, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), and structured electronic health record (EHR) variables. In practice, multi-institutional model development is constrained by privacy regulations, institutional data silos, and class imbalance for less common findings. Existing open-source synthetic data tools are largely modality-specific: tabular libraries such as Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)/Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN), image generators based on latent diffusion, and time-series methods such as Time-series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) each require its own setup, configuration, and validation. This study presents SynForge-Cardio, a multimodality orchestration framework for prompt-driven synthetic dataset generation across chest X-ray (CXR), 12-lead ECG, and EHR modalities. Rather than introducing a new generative backbone, SynForge-Cardio coordinates established components—latent diffusion with optional low-rank adaptation for CXR; parametric and bounded morphology-preserving augmentation (with an optional TimeGAN path) for ECG; and size-aware routing among jitter augmentation, Gaussian copula, and CTGAN/Tabular Variational Autoencoder for EHR—behind a shared clinical prompt interface, a rule-based router, and a postgeneration quality/privacy reporting layer. The three modalities were generated independently from separate datasets; the framework does not perform patient-level joint synthesis and makes no claim of anatomical or physiological consistency across modalities. This system is implemented as a FastAPI backend with a React frontend and can run on a single workstation GPU. Herein, we formalize the orchestration objective, specify modality-wise models and metrics [Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), dynamic time warping (DTW), power spectral density similarity, Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, correlation preservation, and distance-to-closest-record privacy screening], and describe an evaluation protocol on public corpora (NIH Chest X-ray14, PTB-XL, and the UCI Cleveland Heart Disease dataset), including a four-regime train-on-synthetic/test-on-real (TSTR) utility analysis with five random seeds. On the framework alone, we measured 94.6% modality-routing accuracy, 100% direct-vs.-routed generation equivalence on the evaluated cases, 59 unnecessary generator calls avoided, and 100% validation/reporting completeness (1,105/1,108 tests pass, 3 skipped). Downstream-utility results were mixed: augmenting a 25%-real training set with synthetic data changed the held-out AUROC by −0.041 to +0.050 across three CXR tasks (none significant at five seeds); by +0.019 for ECG MI-vs.-NORM [produced by mode B (bounded real-waveform augmentation, whose synthetic samples can be matched to their true source recording at top-1 ≈ 42.7–43.4%, and hence, mode B is not an independently learned generative model)]; and by +0.017 for EHR heart disease classification, which is not evidence of benefit given the 61-record hold-out set (the test-set bootstrap 95% CI for the difference includes zero). Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV acquisition was not completed because credentialed access was unavailable; all reported EHR results were UCI-based. SynForge-Cardio is intended as a practical, reproducible research framework for privacy-conscious cardiovascular data augmentation and prototype development.

title: Statistical learning for RT-QuIC kinetics phenotyping in prion disease
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
db3bcb13a1e6d5818fec53a1dd0b0fdc56f1a517.abstract: Background Prion diseases, such as Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, are invariably fatal neurodegenerative disorders whose clinical heterogeneity makes early diagnosis challenging. The Real-Time Quaking-Induced Conversion (RT-QuIC) assay has revolutionized antemortem detection by amplifying the pathogenic prion protein (PrP Sc ) with near-perfect specificity. However, routine diagnostics typically reduce the continuous RT-QuIC fluorescence curve to just two metrics: the lag phase and the maximum fluorescence intensity. This two-parameter reduction discards the striking heterogeneity of the full temporal profile, erasing latent biological information regarding pathological burden and strain properties. Exploiting this hidden data requires new analytical methods that keep reaction kinetics biologically legible. Methods To address this, we propose an end-to-end statistical framework that captures the complete fluorescence distribution over time. We analyzed cerebrospinal-fluid RT-QuIC trajectories from 301 patients/samples; after exclusion of five patients/samples with consistently shorter recordings, 296 patient/sample-level profiles were included in the tensor modeling and clustering analyses. We then applied a three-way (Tucker3) tensor clustering approach to the unreduced time courses across all technical replicates. Results The proposed framework identifies distinct empirical RT-QuIC fluorescence profiles and provides a compact description of curve morphology. By modelling the complete trajectory, it captures differences in rise steepness, timing, baseline level, and late-phase attenuation that are not represented by conventional lag-phase and maximum-intensity summaries. Conclusions The identified profiles are cohort-specific empirical patterns of the RT-QuIC fluorescence reaction. The late-phase attenuation parameter provides an additional descriptor not included in standard sigmoidal models; however, its biological, clinical, and diagnostic interpretation requires independent validation. Future studies should assess associations between curve-derived parameters or profiles and clinical phenotype, PRNP genotype, molecular subtype, biomarkers, and survival.

title: Lightweight MFCC–SVM recognition of wheeze events in pediatric respiratory sounds: inter-patient evaluation on SPRSound and a software deployment proof-of-concept
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
f08757192416a997a850c854f6b218d243ef4aa8.abstract: Pediatric wheeze recognition can support the automated analysis of respiratory sounds and reduce dependence on subjective auscultation. This study develops and evaluates a lightweight machine-learning approach for event-level wheeze/no-wheeze recognition using the publicly available SPRSound pediatric respiratory sound database. Respiratory events were extracted exclusively from the expert-annotated temporal boundaries provided with the dataset, without automatic event segmentation. A total of 9,089 annotated respiratory events were represented using Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), delta, and delta-delta features summarized into a fixed 120-dimensional vector. Logistic Regression, Linear Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine with a radial basis function kernel (SVM-RBF) were evaluated under the same acoustic-feature pipeline. The operating threshold of the SVM-RBF classifier was optimized using the INTRA-2022 partition and subsequently applied to the inter-patient INTER-2022 partition. At this operating point, the model achieved a sensitivity of 0.935 (95% CI 0.901–0.957), specificity of 0.777 (95% CI 0.752–0.801), ROC-AUC of 0.930, PR-AUC of 0.772, and F1-score of 0.679; the positive predictive value was 0.534, reflecting a substantial false-positive burden. As a secondary software-level contribution, the trained preprocessing and classification components were integrated into an Android–Flask client–server workflow for audio submission, server-side feature extraction, inference, and result visualization. The software workflow was functionally implemented but was not quantitatively validated using respiratory recordings acquired through a smartphone microphone. Accordingly, the reported performance characterizes event-level classification under SPRSound conditions and should not be interpreted as mobile-acquisition, diagnostic, or clinical validation.

title: Beyond grades to learning enhancement: development, implementation and evaluation of a conversational AI agent in medical education
container-title: Education + Training
084b6523ad822ed6a663bd21d0cf5dfd788d527b.abstract: Purpose The integration of conversational artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education shows promise but lacks empirical evidence of effectiveness. This study evaluated a customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)-4-based conversational agent designed explicitly for a pharmacology block in undergraduate medical education. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods sequential explanatory design was employed in a four-week elective pharmacology block at the College of Medicine, Sulaiman Al-Rajhi University. Phase 1 involved a cross-sectional survey of enrolled students (n = 58) who used the AI tool, with a comparative analysis of their academic performance against historical cohorts without access to AI (2022–2023: n = 33; 2023–2024: n = 37). Academic performance was measured through mid-block quizzes, end-of-block examinations, and total block score. Phase 2 comprised semi-structured interviews (n = 9), transcribed and analyzed thematically. Findings The survey response rate was 89.6% (52/58), and 98.1% (51/52) reported using the tool. Among users, 74.5% engaged with the GPT tool daily. Students reported exceptionally high satisfaction: 92.2% found it more effective than traditional methods, 94.1% felt it made learning more engaging, and the likelihood of recommending it averaged 4.65 ± 0.73 (on a 5-point scale). Frequency of use was significantly associated with perceived improvement in learning (χ2 = 15.84, p &lt; 0.05). Academic performance showed marginal, non-significant improvements: total scores increased by 2.5% (75.52 vs. 77.40, p &gt; 0.05), with pass rates improving from 92.9% to 98.3% (p &gt; 0.05). Qualitative analysis revealed six themes: learning support and academic enhancement; efficiency and accessibility; GPT's supplementary role in learning; perceived strengths and unique features; limitations and challenges; and suggestions for improvement. Originality/value The disconnect between exceptional user engagement and minimal performance improvements challenges traditional evaluation paradigms. While conversational AI may not directly enhance examination scores, students' accounts suggest it may support metacognitive development, reduce cognitive load, and foster critical-thinking skills essential for modern medical practice, thereby necessitating multidimensional assessment frameworks.

title: Design, Implementation, and Empirical Evaluation of a Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model in Higher Education
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
c4fc7c2df67e25e958c78f59c8dc7e87340a3c13.abstract: AI-supported assessment increasingly enables adaptive tasks, automated analysis, and personalized feedback, yet their integration into coherent, human-supervised formative assessment remains insufficiently established. This study developed and evaluated the Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model (HA-CAAM) using Design and Development Research structured through the ADDIE framework. Implemented in a higher-education Media Education course, the model employed performance-responsive task adaptation using predefined thresholds, rubric-guided AI-assisted scoring, formative feedback, and instructor verification. Five experts validated the model, 148 students provided quantitative and qualitative implementation feedback, and 50 student responses were independently assessed by two human raters and AI. Expert validation provided initial evidence of content validity (mean Aiken's V = 0.818). Students reported generally favorable experiences, particularly regarding clarity and feedback usefulness, although Learning Support and Overall User Experience received comparatively lower ratings. AI-generated scores demonstrated strong agreement with human-reference scores (ICC = 0.898), despite individual discrepancies. These findings provide initial evidence of content validity, positive implementation experiences, and scoring agreement, rather than demonstrated improvements in learning outcomes or equivalence between AI and human assessment decisions. HA-CAAM contributes an empirically refined, seven-stage assessment framework that coordinates performance-responsive adaptation, AI-assisted analysis, formative feedback, and instructor-led quality assurance within a human-supervised assessment process.

title: Please Forward this Postdigital Feminist Chain-Letter on Living with AI in Higher Education
container-title: Postdigital Science and Education
97107e75549a7b1d23b73a701cdc9f4ca9237854.abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) enters higher education within established hierarchies of knowledge and expertise, becoming entangled with judgments about who sounds authoritative and which forms of writing carry weight. Those judgments were gendered, long before GenAI arrived. Drawing on feminist postdigital inquiry and collaborative, experimental approaches to knowledge production, this article reports a chain-letter experiment. Thirteen academics who identify as women or gender-diverse, from nine countries, write in relation to the letters preceding their own. The chain letter produces knowledge through response, so that each letter is partial and the argument accumulates between them. Read together, the letters describe a persistent need to defend expertise within a field shaped by masculine norms of authority, and the frustration and exhaustion this produces. Authors variously report work intensifying rather than easing, critique of GenAI tools being reframed as failures of individual users, and a sense that AI-assisted writing diminishes what makes teaching and research pleasurable. Their positions differ, with some refusing these tools while others work closely with them. At the same time, the exchange brings solidarity, hope and relief, and the discovery that these difficulties are structural as well as personal. The letters suggest that GenAI makes long-standing, gendered questions about expertise and working conditions more pressing, and that these remain shared and unfinished. The article closes with an open invitation to join a feminist and postdigital conversation about GenAI in research and education.

title: A study on the synergistic effects of teacher–student interaction patterns and an AI-based emotional feedback system in secondary school chemistry laboratory classes: an intervention experiment grounded in inquiry-based instruction
container-title: Frontiers in Education
96b6b86b3b878503d2576ece5930fa96e5fb585b.abstract: While prior research has examined how teacher-student interaction influences student learning in conventional chemistry laboratory instruction, few studies have systematically disentangled the synergistic mechanisms that connect dynamic patterns of teacher-student interaction with AI-driven emotional feedback systems-and, critically, how these interactions jointly shape educational outcomes in AI-integrated chemistry laboratory classrooms. This gap constrains the evidence-informed design of emotion-responsive, intelligent chemistry pedagogy. This study employed a mixed-methods design integrating a quasi-experimental intervention with qualitative thematic analysis. A semester-long intervention was implemented with two cohorts of ninth-grade students: an experimental group ( n = 40) receiving inquiry-based chemistry laboratory instruction augmented by an AI-powered emotional feedback system, and a control group ( n = 38) receiving equivalent inquiry-based instruction supported solely by conventional teacher-student interaction. The study comparatively analyzed students' emotional experiences across the two instructional conditions. Distinct emotional trajectories emerged between the groups. The AI-supported experimental group exhibited a statistically significant increase in chemistry laboratory anxiety over the semester, with no meaningful improvement in subjective achievement. In contrast, the control group maintained stable anxiety levels and demonstrated consistent growth in perceived achievement. Moreover, the control group outperformed the experimental group in procedural compliance and the rigor of hands-on laboratory operations. No statistically significant intergroup differences were observed for other affective indicators-including sense of accomplishment and willingness to collaborate. These findings advance the theoretical understanding of human-machine collaborative pedagogy within intelligent learning environments. Empirically grounded, they yield actionable insights for the design of chemistry laboratory instruction in AI-integrated settings-particularly in developing learner-centered, emotion-aware frameworks for human-AI co-teaching.

title: Designing the Future: Leadership and AI
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
48d1a912943fae642bf3d6ccadf6945742236023.abstract: This chapter explores the evolving, reciprocal relationship between leadership and augmented/artificial intelligence (AI) across individual, team, organizational, and societal levels. While we use the term AI throughout in recognition of its widespread usage, we acknowledge the growing preference for augmented intelligence – a framing advanced by leaders in human–machine teaming, such as Paul G. Kaminski (2020), which emphasizes cognitive extension and human–AI partnership. Just as leadership helped shape – and was reshaped by – the Agricultural, Industrial, and Information Ages, the emerging Age of AI demands a renewed focus on human values and moral courage. Far from a neutral tool, AI reflects the intentions of its designers and the integrity of its leaders, and in turn, transforms how we work, relate, and lead. Grounded in authentic and moral leadership theory, systems thinking, and sociotechnical design, we examine how leaders can engage AI in ways that safeguard human dignity, foster trust, and advance ethical innovation. Through a multilevel lens, we explore how AI influences self-awareness, interpersonal responsibility, team dynamics, and global leadership strategies. We extend prior work on efficacy-performance spirals to the AI context, showing how trust, learning, and adaptation can reinforce or erode across levels over time. Drawing on work published in Organizational Dynamics, this chapter also applies the TRUST, COACH, and CARES frameworks to AI leadership. As AI reshapes decision-making and connection, the defining force will not be technology itself, but the authenticity, trustworthiness, and moral imagination of those who lead it.

title: Digital Transformation 2.0: Integrating AI and Empowering People for Sustainable Growth in the Future of Work
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
cd295fcbb5cd4820a5d40948a004a94d7d35cbec.abstract: The digital era has reached a new inflection point, accelerated by artificial intelligence (AI) and organizations’ need to adapt to dynamic, technology-driven conditions. This chapter examines the legacy of Digital Transformation 1.0—highlighting failures and their causes—and defines the imperatives of AI-infused Digital Transformation 2.0. Drawing from relevant case studies, research, and executive interviews, it emphasizes the critical shift from episodic digitization to sustained AI-embedded digitalization. Leaders must enable systems-level transformation across people, process, and technology while aligning cultural, ethical, and operational domains. Digital Transformation 2.0 demands coordinated iterative design over monolithic strategy, requiring organizations to reimagine work as a fluid mix of tasks rather than fixed roles. Human–AI collaboration is a new reality that depends on psychological safety, AI literacy, and digital dexterity across the blended human-AI workforce. Successful transformation hinges on new leadership behaviors that elevate trust, agency, and adaptability while modeling and encouraging the use of new tools. The piece explores decentralized workforce models, the urgency of building AI-ready cultures, and a new social contract. It examines how agile frameworks, value mapping, and upskilling efforts create coherence amid complexity, making change tangible and participatory. The Future of Work is framed not as a fixed destination, but as a dynamic system requiring deliberate, ongoing leadership to combine machine capabilities with uniquely human capabilities. Ultimately, this work calls for defining or reframing organizational purpose and progress: AI can multiply what we value, but it is up to us to define what we value—and how we lead with it.

title: A Cautionary Tale: When AI Outpaces Character in Leadership Development
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
0b2e9c41561f67c0653a2cb28c371eb88152dc74.abstract: This chapter, A Cautionary Tale, explores the risks and unintended consequences of pursuing leadership development and organizational transformation without grounding efforts in ethical discernment, evidence-based practice, and human-centered design. Drawing from decades of experience in the military, higher education, and executive coaching, the chapter highlights how well-intentioned initiatives often falter when leaders prioritize efficiency, image, or short-term outcomes over trust, character, and sustainable growth. Through illustrative narratives and applied research, it examines how misplaced reliance on tools, trends, or unchecked authority can erode organizational culture, diminish performance, and compromise individual well-being. The cautionary perspective emphasizes that leadership is not merely the accumulation of skills or the exercise of influence but a continual process of reflection, humility, and responsibility. Practical insights are offered for leaders navigating high-pressure contexts, including the importance of aligning purpose with practice, cultivating resilience, and embedding feedback loops that elevate both performance and values. Ultimately, the chapter argues that the true cost of neglecting character in leadership is not only organizational inefficiency but also the erosion of human dignity and trust – resources far more difficult to restore than financial capital. By reframing leadership as a moral as well as strategic endeavor, A Cautionary Tale serves as both a warning and a guide for leaders committed to building organizations that endure and uplift.

title: Agents of Change: Teamwork and Collaboration with AI at the Table
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
dcfd8d7ff89f9b704d69b63c67897d2290b5f515.abstract: This chapter explores the transformative implications of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) technologies as a “teammate” in leading virtual and hybrid teams. The growing prevalence of GenAI tools and the shift toward remote and hybrid work create a critical need to reexamine how leaders demonstrate essential leadership competencies in these environments. Framed by discussions on GenAI as both a collaborator and a tool, this chapter considers the ethical dilemmas, pedagogical innovations, and practical strategies for integrating GenAI into team leadership. Building on the authors’ previous work in exploring leadership competencies for leading at the virtual table, it investigates how GenAI reshapes trust, collaboration, and productivity in diverse teams while balancing human agency and technological capabilities. Through critical questions, a case study reflection, and practical takeaways, the chapter offers a roadmap for fostering GenAI literacy (LeaderAIcy), managing ethical and technical considerations, and leveraging GenAI for meaningful leadership and teamwork in global, hybrid contexts.

title: Using AI Tools for Leader Development and Assessing Competencies
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
6670b996a20df16f557191ac8831733fc9abb418.abstract: This chapter explores how the United States Air Force (USAF) leader development course (LDC) used artificial intelligence (AI)/sentiment analysis (SA) for leader development and assessing leader development competencies that support learning objectives and course outcomes. A narrative format is first used to describe the engaged practice with key stakeholders and the staged approach process that underlaid the development of how innovation is driving change for leaders, assessing performance specific to selected competencies in mixed reality scenarios, and offering ways of strengthening leader development. A five-phased qualitative structure is used along with content analysis, design thinking, and a grounded theory approach. After coding data using thematic analysis from phases 1 to 4, a grounded theory approach is used to better understand the findings and discoveries with literature related to innovation development, AI technology associated with immersive learning environments, design thinking and change, performance and competency assessment, and leader development. A new theory (AI-augmented leader development theory) and a new model, emotionally tuned competency assessment model (ECAM), emerged as well as emphasis on the power of using dialogic development in virtual contexts to train, assess, and develop leaders. Theoretical and practical implications, as well as recommendations are provided for improving how AI tools can be used for leader development.

title: AI as a Catalyst for Change: Transforming Human Resources in Educational Institutions
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
93d2ee78452d2d36780fedbbf08d870e031b50d3.abstract: This chapter delves into the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and the human resources (HR) function within a public school district, offering a detailed case study of its implementation. It examines how AI tools were leveraged to streamline recruitment, enhance employee engagement, and support data-driven decision-making. The chapter highlights key challenges and opportunities, focusing on trust building and change management strategies essential for the successful adoption of AI tools. Ethical considerations are explored, including the need to mitigate algorithmic bias, ensure fairness in automated processes, and uphold data privacy and security standards. Recommendations emphasize the importance of transparent communication, reengaging employees through inclusive practices, and building trust in AI systems while reskilling and upskilling employees. By combining practical insights with emerging trends in digital transformation, this chapter provides a roadmap for educational leaders and HR professionals seeking to responsibly leverage AI in their organizations.

title: Leading Inclusively: Universal Design Principles in the Age of AI
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
ce20000e654b8aeff35b1155111a8b38d1312b8b.abstract: Modern organizational leaders increasingly encounter artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in their workplaces, creating both opportunities and challenges for inclusive leadership. This chapter introduces Universal Design for Learning (UDL) as a framework for navigating these technological changes while maintaining human-centered approaches to inclusion. UDL’s three core principles – multiple means of representation, engagement, and action/expression – provide leaders with practical strategies for creating flexible workplace systems that benefit all employees. When thoughtfully implemented, AI technologies can support these principles through personalized learning experiences, enhanced accessibility features, and improved communication tools. However, the chapter cautions leaders to ensure that technology is amplifying rather than replacing human judgment and cultural competence. The chapter addresses critical considerations for leaders, including the risks of algorithmic bias, the limitations of automated solutions in complex interpersonal situations, and the importance of maintaining employee agency and choice. It examines common implementation barriers – from cost concerns to misconceptions about technology as a cure-all for inclusion challenges – while demonstrating that UDL principles require minimal investment and generate significant returns. Through examination of both opportunities and pitfalls, leaders learn to distinguish between technological applications that enhance inclusion and those that may inadvertently create barriers. The chapter provides actionable guidance for implementing UDL principles in technology-enhanced environments, positioning inclusive leadership capabilities as essential competencies for organizational success regardless of technological context.

title: Generative AI Powered by Large Language Models for Leadership Development: Between Epistemic Responsibility and the Future of Innovation
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
2befe576d22df3abb8f03a51478516f11ce0d40c.abstract: This chapter examines language-based generative AI, particularly large language models (LLMs), as active epistemic agents in leadership development. Moving beyond their perceived neutrality, the authors argue that LLMs serve as mirrors of dominant assumptions, co-constructors of leadership meaning, and framing devices of legitimate knowledge. The sources highlight how these systems reinforce prevailing Euro-American managerial ideals, often marginalizing diverse leadership paradigms such as Indigenous, collectivist, or spiritual frameworks, thereby amplifying structural and cultural biases. Through epistemic feedback loops and personalization, LLMs can subtly shape leadership identity and constrain developmental horizons, leading to adaptive standardization or performative conformity. The chapter emphasizes the critical need for epistemic responsibility in innovation leadership, advocating for leaders to interrogate system framings, reflect on their influence, and cultivate design awareness. This involves fostering inclusive data practices, participatory design methodologies, and culturally responsive AI governance to ensure AI-mediated innovation ecosystems are just, inclusive, and reflect pluralistic worldviews. Ultimately, the chapter calls for leaders to reclaim framing power and engage AI dialogically to foster an innovation leadership that is reflexive, ethically grounded, and attuned to human complexities.

title: The Influence of Generative Artificial Intelligence on K–12 Educational Leadership
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
2e16eaf81aea3695e6f9f9b263f8c5764ccfa4cb.abstract: This chapter examines the transformative influence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) on K–12 educational leadership after the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. The rapid adoption of remote learning technologies created a tech-dependent educational environment, accelerating AI integration in both classroom instruction and school administration. As generative AI tools, such as large language models (LLMs) and chatbots, become increasingly accessible, school leaders face new opportunities and challenges in leveraging these tools to support instructional design, data-driven decision-making, and school governance. This chapter explores how AI is reshaping educators’ roles, enabling real-time feedback, streamlining administrative tasks, and personalizing learning experiences, while also requiring ethical oversight, digital literacy, and sustained professional development. Attention is given to the complexities of equity, access, and teacher readiness, emphasizing the need for thoughtful implementation and culturally responsive AI use.

title: Inverse design of terahertz metasurface polarization converters based on generative adversarial networks
container-title: Optics Continuum
739abe95c331ed3ee886745c2727c1c6332ce894.abstract: A reflection-type broadband terahertz metasurface polarization converter with a three-layer structure—comprising a patterned metal layer, a dielectric layer, and a metallic ground plane—is inversely designed based on a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP). By incorporating the Wasserstein distance and a gradient penalty term, the WGAN-GP effectively overcomes the training instability inherent in conventional generative adversarial networks, thereby enabling the construction of an end-to-end mapping model from target spectra to metasurface structural parameters. The results demonstrate that the WGAN-GP achieves efficient and high-accuracy inverse design, with a single inference time of only 30 ms and a mean absolute error of structural parameter prediction as low as 0.1263. The optimized metasurface polarization converter exhibits a consistently high polarization conversion ratio exceeding 0.8 over the 3–7.5 THz frequency range, corresponding to a relative bandwidth of up to 86%, and maintains excellent angular stability within an incidence angle range of 0° to 50°. This work not only verifies the efficiency and reliability of WGAN-GP in the inverse design of complex electromagnetic devices, but also provides an effective solution for the development of high-performance terahertz metasurfaces, with the potential to accelerate device innovation and applications of terahertz technologies in key fields such as communications, sensing, imaging, and spectrum security.

title: Generative structure-guided denoising diffusion probabilistic model for MR to CT image synthesis in radiotherapy planning
container-title: Physics in Medicine & Biology
cfa98f94b57aed8a928c9fb300f2a97663467510.abstract: Abstract Objective . Radiotherapy (RT) planning uses magnetic resonance (MR) imaging for soft tissue information, while computerized tomography (CT) imaging is necessary for dose calculation. Synthetic CTs generated from MR images (MRI) streamline the clinical workflow by reducing the need for an actual CT acquisition while minimizing radiation exposure, enabling adaptive RT workflows. The objective of this study is to propose a new RT planning model combining stable structure-guided denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) with MRI conditioning, for generating synthetic CT (sCT) images. Approach . The model combines a hybrid network architecture with a dynamic guidance mechanism, conditioned on MR images, to direct the reverse diffusion process and preserve structural details. The model integrates both a denoising and a refinement network: the denoising network predicts and progressively removes the noise added during the forward diffusion process, while the guidance strength adapts at each timestep based on the noise level. This adaptive guidance mechanism uses a non-linear formulation that satisfies noise constraints, optimizing the denoising process while preserving structural integrity. The training process includes a weighted structure-guided loss function that combines the DDPM noise loss with a dynamic guidance regularizer term for sCT image generation via noise prediction, along with a reconstruction loss for refinement. Main results . Evaluated on three paired MR/CT datasets (head and neck (HaN), as well as brain), our model outperforms recent MR to CT synthesis models, showing the best performance in image quality based on the mean absolute error in Hounsfield units, as well as improved peak signal-to-noise ratio, structural similarity index and gradient magnitude similarity deviation compared to other DDPM and generative adversarial network approaches. When comparing tumor segmentation quality, it achieves the best results in Dice score (0.76 ± 0.04), Hausdorff distance (7.9 ± 2.0), intersection over union (0.69 ± 0.04), geometric consistency index (0.84 ± 0.04) and precision-recall index (PRI) (0.88 ± 0.03) for segmented tumor regions in the generated sCT images. Finally, it achieves the best mean square error of 10.1 ± 2.6 Gray (Gy) in the head-and-neck cohort, when evaluating dose planning on sCT, with a conformity index of 0.61 ± 0.02 and a homogeneity index of 0.10 ± 0.02. Significance . Performance shows promise in integration for RT in HaN, as well as in brain cancers.

title: Critical Research, Inquiry, and Communication
55f48f04c80b22fd643567b61f598ef0665f7fe3.abstract: Developed by Oklahoma State University faculty, Critical Research, Inquiry, and Communication​​​​​​​: Writing Your Way into the the Disciplines introduces students to discipline specific discourse communities, exploring how knowledge is created, communicated, and evaluated by scholars and practitioners in their field. Through authentic examples, discipline-specific genres, and guided practice, students will learn to analyze audience expectations, rhetorical conventions, and professional standards that shape communication in their fields.A central feature of the text is a sustained research project that invites students to investigate a meaningful question currently being explored within their discipline. As they engage with scholarly literature, professional conversations, and disciplinary methods of inquiry, students develop the research, critical thinking, and communication skills essential for academic success and workforce readiness.By connecting writing instruction to students' academic majors and career aspirations, Critical Research, Inquiry, and Communication​​​​​​​: Writing Your Way into the the Disciplines prepares learners to participate confidently in the conversations that define their professions while supporting Oklahoma State University's commitment to student success and career readiness.

title: Trust Modulates Speech Entrainment: Enhanced Cortical Tracking for Low-trust Speakers
container-title: Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience
93efb8d8a2efd6ac00960e2f7910f482c84055f4.abstract: Abstract Trust is a critical component of human communication, providing a foundation for understanding, information exchange, and social coordination. Much of the research on trust in speech communication has focused on how vocal characteristics impact perceived trustworthiness. However, little is known about how trust in a speaker affects the neural processing of speech. Here, we demonstrate a two-stage experimental framework to study that question using noninvasive EEG. First, participants engage in a trust-building stage, where they play an investment game with fictional characters, each paired with a distinctive voice and trustworthiness level (i.e., frequency and magnitude of lies). Next, participants engage in a story-listening stage, in which they are presented with stories from the same characters. Data acquired from 20 young adults confirm a statistically significant correlation between the perceived and actual trustworthiness of the fictional characters. Cortical speech tracking was quantified using a temporal response function analysis on the EEG data. We found that the trustworthiness established during the trust-building stage influenced the cortical tracking of speech in the subsequent story-listening stage, with lower trustworthiness corresponding to a stronger cortical tracking of speech. Interestingly, trustworthiness selectively modulated tracking strength, with no statistically significant changes in the spatial and temporal temporal response function dynamics.

title: Distributed Neural Dynamics Underlie the Shift from Movement Preparation to Execution
container-title: Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience
7a79083e41e8564c05cef0c9e6a1179e83f26049.abstract: Abstract Understanding how neural population activity supports the transition from movement preparation to execution remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience. Invasive recordings in nonhuman primates indicate that motor preparation and execution occupy orthogonal subspaces within the primary motor cortex (M1), yet how these neural dynamics evolve across broader networks and support skilled, memory-guided action remains poorly understood. We used source-resolved magnetoencephalography during a memory-guided finger-sequence task to track population dynamics across a cortico-hippocampal network. Manifold trajectories and decoding revealed that preparation and execution of movement sequences occupy distinct, yet not fully orthogonal, neural subspaces—a separation that generalized across all regions but was most pronounced in motor regions. Crucially, we identified a hierarchical spatio-temporal transition across the brain: The state shift originated in the hippocampus via theta-band modulations and rippled through the pre-SMA, SMA, and lateral premotor areas before culminating in M1 via broadband activity. This progression follows the functional hierarchy of descending motor pathways, with M1 shifting last, 160 msec before the first button press. Although sequence identity could be decoded from all areas during execution, only the hippocampus and M1 maintained predictive representations of upcoming sequences during preparation. These findings demonstrate that the initiation of complex motor sequences relies on a well-timed integration of hippocampal memory systems with primary motor output, rather than being a process localized to the motor cortices alone.

title: Sequential Sampling from Memory Underlies Perceptual Decisions Unyoked from Actions
container-title: Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience
a917d6aa52f462098a3786e8e5c48f2839ba057f.abstract: Abstract Perceptual decision-making refers to the class of decisions in which sensory evidence is used to categorize percepts and guide actions. Conventionally, categorical decisions are thought to precede motor actions. However, recent studies in nonhuman primates challenge this assumption—when perceptual decisions were uncoupled from the actions they bear upon, animals postponed the decisions until relevant response options were revealed. To determine whether this postponement stems from cognitive limitations unique to nonhuman primates, we conducted a similar experiment with human participants. Naive participants viewed a random dot motion (RDM) stimulus that was difficult to categorize. After a delay period following the RDM, two choice targets were presented and participants decided which target lay closer to the perceived motion direction. Decision accuracy varied across participants, reflecting individual differences in ability to integrate motion evidence. Notably, participants with higher decision accuracy showed prolonged deliberation after choice-target presentation. Furthermore, the time they took to report their decisions depended on the strength of the motion evidence. This pattern of accuracy and decision reporting time could be accounted for by a bounded diffusion model in which participants sequentially sample stored sensory information from memory during the target selection phase. When the RDM was challenging to categorize, the subsequent appearance of the targets provided a framework to interrogate stored evidence and render a decision. Our results reveal a strategic feature of working memory of retaining information based on its future utility. This observation opens new avenues for investigating how memory and decision-making interact.

title: Confounds in Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging—Part III: Auxiliary Data
container-title: Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience
7ebbf91cc1104ca6a325a8fc4b3255a08d3c579e.abstract: Abstract In the first part of this series, we reviewed the pathways that bring about confounding nuisance signals in fMRI. Then, in the second part, we considered how human factors can modify these pathways. In this, the third and final part, we review auxiliary data that may allow researchers to identify and perhaps correct for nuisance signals and their modifiers. We consider three broad categories of data: (1) measures that can be collected synchronously with the fMRI, (2) other MRI scans that either capture trait information or attempt to define the state that exists during an fMRI scan in the same session, and (3) non-MRI measures that can be collected before or after the scan and that also capture trait or relevant state factors influencing the fMRI. We conclude with some recommendations on ways to improve fMRI experiments going forward.

title: Credibility displacement in algorithmic financial reporting: a critical review of AI, disclosure credibility and capital-market consequences
container-title: Journal of Accounting Literature
18243e89dcb911f6253cee203ff5a4e80cabeb04.abstract: Purpose This review examines how financial-reporting credibility is shaped when algorithmic systems enter the reporting chain. It asks where credibility is produced, tested and understood when artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, large language models, eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) analytics and related tools affect reporting information. Design/methodology/approach The paper combines a search and screening procedure informed by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) with a concept-centric synthesis. The evidence base comprises a 226-paper curated core and a 144-paper close-synthesis subset. Sensitivity analyses re-examine the 39-record outlet boundary and the close-synthesis threshold. Findings The evidence remains dispersed across research on textual disclosure and natural language processing (NLP), audit analytics and assurance, structured reporting using XBRL, market interpretation, accounting information systems (AIS) implementation and AI governance. Across these streams, algorithms can improve reporting processes but may also alter the grounds on which reporting assertions are accepted. We describe the latter possibility as credibility displacement: model-related output, provenance or validation partly substitutes for scrutiny of the underlying assertion or for identifiable professional and institutional safeguards. Originality/value The review defines algorithmic financial reporting as a reporting-chain phenomenon rather than a general label for technology adoption. It distinguishes four sites: preparation, assurance, machine-readable presentation and algorithmic interpretation. Governance operates across these sites as a cross-cutting condition, making the proposed displacement mechanism more focused and empirically testable.

title: Beyond grades to learning enhancement: development, implementation and evaluation of a conversational AI agent in medical education
container-title: Education + Training
084b6523ad822ed6a663bd21d0cf5dfd788d527b.abstract: Purpose The integration of conversational artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education shows promise but lacks empirical evidence of effectiveness. This study evaluated a customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)-4-based conversational agent designed explicitly for a pharmacology block in undergraduate medical education. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods sequential explanatory design was employed in a four-week elective pharmacology block at the College of Medicine, Sulaiman Al-Rajhi University. Phase 1 involved a cross-sectional survey of enrolled students (n = 58) who used the AI tool, with a comparative analysis of their academic performance against historical cohorts without access to AI (2022–2023: n = 33; 2023–2024: n = 37). Academic performance was measured through mid-block quizzes, end-of-block examinations, and total block score. Phase 2 comprised semi-structured interviews (n = 9), transcribed and analyzed thematically. Findings The survey response rate was 89.6% (52/58), and 98.1% (51/52) reported using the tool. Among users, 74.5% engaged with the GPT tool daily. Students reported exceptionally high satisfaction: 92.2% found it more effective than traditional methods, 94.1% felt it made learning more engaging, and the likelihood of recommending it averaged 4.65 ± 0.73 (on a 5-point scale). Frequency of use was significantly associated with perceived improvement in learning (χ2 = 15.84, p &lt; 0.05). Academic performance showed marginal, non-significant improvements: total scores increased by 2.5% (75.52 vs. 77.40, p &gt; 0.05), with pass rates improving from 92.9% to 98.3% (p &gt; 0.05). Qualitative analysis revealed six themes: learning support and academic enhancement; efficiency and accessibility; GPT's supplementary role in learning; perceived strengths and unique features; limitations and challenges; and suggestions for improvement. Originality/value The disconnect between exceptional user engagement and minimal performance improvements challenges traditional evaluation paradigms. While conversational AI may not directly enhance examination scores, students' accounts suggest it may support metacognitive development, reduce cognitive load, and foster critical-thinking skills essential for modern medical practice, thereby necessitating multidimensional assessment frameworks.

title: Dance choreography education: Socio-emotional and creative thinking skills development among primary school students in China
container-title: International Journal of Research Studies in Education
825666113242483fefb45462f14eac8f66bc861a.abstract: This study examined the perceived effectiveness of dance choreography in promoting the social skills and creative thinking of Chinese primary school children and served as the basis for an enhancement program. A quantitative descriptive-correlational research design was employed, utilizing validated survey questionnaires administered to dance teachers from selected Chinese schools. Descriptive statistics, tests of difference, and correlation analyses were used to interpret the data. The findings revealed that most respondents were young to middle-aged adults, predominantly female, bachelor's degree holders, and in the early stage of their teaching careers. Dance choreography was perceived to be highly implemented, with social and emotional growth receiving the highest ratings, while cognitive development obtained the lowest. The respondents also rated children's social skills and creative thinking as generally high. Among the social skills dimensions, cooperation ranked highest, whereas assertiveness ranked lowest. For creative thinking, imagination received the highest rating, while flexibility emerged as the area needing the greatest improvement. No significant differences were found across age, sex, and educational attainment in all dimensions, except for creativity when grouped according to years of service. Furthermore, no significant relationship was identified between most dimensions of dance choreography and the social skills of Chinese primary school children. Based on these findings, an enhancement program entitled “Creative Steps for Growth: An Enhancement Program for Cognitive Development, Creative Flexibility, and Assertiveness through Dance Choreography among Chinese School Children” was developed. The study recommends strengthening instructional strategies, institutional support, curriculum integration, guidance interventions, extracurricular dance activities, active student participation, and further research to maximize the educational benefits of dance choreography in fostering children's holistic development.

title: Queer inclusion in organizations: a critical review of methodologies and theoretical frameworks
container-title: Equality, Diversity and Inclusion: An International Journal
0b1aeb31913563bdd8ee76e1a90baf3a20127bf5.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to critically examine how queer inclusion in organizations has been studied, with a focus on the methodological approaches and theoretical frameworks that shape this body of work. Design/methodology/approach This paper is based on a critical review of peer-reviewed literature, drawing on databases such as JSTOR, Web of Science and Scopus for their comprehensive coverage of gender and sexuality studies within corporate and institutional settings. Fifty-eight peer-reviewed publications between 2007 and 2024 are included. Findings Among the dominant frameworks in the reviewed literature – queer theory, minority stress theory and intersectionality, none adequately explains how queer claims translate into organizational change across context. Qualitative approaches dominate (50%), followed by quantitative (20.7%), theoretical and conceptual (20.7%) and mixed methods (8.6%) studies. Geographically, the literature remains heavily concentrated in a small number of national contexts, particularly the United States. The review compares the literature across shared analytical dimensions such as legal protection and enforcement, family, kinship and disclosure, intersecting axes of disadvantage, organizational form and employment informality, movement infrastructure and organizational dependencies, and business case reasoning, showing that inclusion outcomes depend on the specific combination of these conditions present in a given context. Significant gaps persist in intersectional engagement, representation beyond a monolithic “LGBT” category and longitudinal analyses of organizational change. Originality/value By connecting politics of alignment with a global–local approach, this review offers a framework for understanding not only what shapes queer workplace inclusion but the conditions under which queer claims become consequential to organizations, for whom and when the results lead to real change rather than symbolic compliance.

title: Working towards gender equality in higher education and research: a critical review of unintended consequences
container-title: Equality, Diversity and Inclusion: An International Journal
7efbbe4db926d47b6fe364213cd05c509bd33c75.abstract: Purpose The critical review paper explores contributions on gender equality initiatives (GEIs) in higher education and research to understand how the unintended consequences of GEIs, and their implications, are discussed in the literature. While it is known that the application of GEIs might cause unintended effects, much of the literature often sidelines this aspect. Design/methodology/approach Review paper, adopting a critical literature review approach. Findings This review demonstrates that GEIs may have unintended consequences such as: perverse incentives, homogenisation of approaches, sidelining intersectionality, placing new pressures on women and the persistence of privileged subjects. These have negative implications for individuals (women and minorities) and equality work. Some instances of positive spillovers (beyond expected outcomes) were identified. Research limitations/implications The review calls for re-thinking the design of studies exploring the impact of GEIs in higher education and research. There is a latent need for additional evidence on the organisational conditions, societal norms and legislative context shaping the impact of GEIs. Practical implications This research highlights the unintended consequences of GEIs as an intersectional risk factor for consideration by practitioners and scholars alike. Practitioners are invited to raise awareness on the potential unintended consequences of GEIs and devise strategies to anticipate and manage these. Originality/value The literature privileges focusing on the expected and positive impact of GEIs. The study of unintended consequences significantly contributes to contemporary understandings of the organisational conditions underlying the success of GEIs, which in turn, holds the potential to foster more robust understandings of how GEIs may be improved.

title: Truth-telling in history education: confronting disinformation through critical historical consciousness
container-title: History Education Research Journal
3f046ba2622d5645218da4e2b741a1aa2671ba67.abstract: In an era increasingly characterised by disinformation and post-truth politics, history education faces renewed epistemic, ethical and societal praxis challenges. Historical narratives are frequently mobilised to legitimise exclusion, distort collective memory and undermine trust in scholarly knowledge, particularly within digital media ecosystems. This article examines truth-telling in history education as a critical educational and societal imperative, arguing that factual accuracy alone is insufficient to confront contemporary forms of historical disinformation. Drawing on interdisciplinary scholarship on disinformation, historical consciousness and philosophy of history, the article advances three interconnected arguments. First, it conceptualises historical disinformation as a narrative and epistemic problem that exploits the interpretative nature of historical knowledge rather than merely disseminating false facts. Second, it mobilises Jörn Rüsen’s theory of historical consciousness, with particular emphasis on the genetic type, as a powerful framework for fostering critical engagement with contested pasts while avoiding both dogmatism and relativism. Third, it challenges the enduring myths of neutrality and historicism in history education, arguing that claims of value-free history often conceal power relations and contribute to the sanitisation of injustice. The article further illustrates these dynamics through analytically selected contemporary contexts, including the conflict in Ukraine and memory politics in Portugal, demonstrating how historical narratives are weaponised in public discourse. It concludes by proposing a vision of history education oriented towards ethical responsibility, narrative plurality and epistemic vigilance, positioning the history classroom as a key site for resisting manipulation and strengthening an ethical and pluralist culture in the post-truth era.

title: AI Integration in Automotive Packaging Engineering for Multi-Constraint Component Optimization
container-title: International Journal of Sustainability and Innovation in Engineering
31c5e065257fd8076186c66a65576fe16420241c.abstract: This paper introduces a framework for the packaging of components in a vehicle's threedimensional structure that is grounded in evidence and reproducible when taking advantage of the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The public OSU–Honda CarHoods10k dataset provides over 10,000 3D hood-frame designs based on 109 parameterized designs, along with design parameters and finite element (FE) performance data. The data package is about 45.66 GB, including design parameters and finite-element (FE) performance data. This dataset is not a multi-component vehicle-layout dataset and can't be used for a complete validation of a vehicle packaging optimizer: thermal, service access, or assembly data of the vehicle are not available at the component level. The studies of published adjacent work have shown that an improved solution with 3 times less computational budget could be offered, a result specific to this study but not predicted for automotive packaging. The proposed framework formalizes the placement variables, geometric constraints, engineering constraints, a model of screening by an artificial neural network (ANN), and a genetic search by NSGA- II, where the two objectives change. It also defines a controlled validation protocol to manual and rule-based baselines. There are no new vehicle-program performance gains since no proprietary vehicle-program layout dataset, executable code, or experimental logs for auditing were provided. The applicable vehicle-program specifications and relevant standards should supply acceptance limits.
