e6da680fc1759bc57e2d45fbf53896760aadbd44.abstract: The performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for mammographic image classification needs to be evaluated using data that were not involved in model development to assess its ability to generalize to data from different sources. This study aims to analyze the performance of a CNN model through external evaluation on a local web-based mammographic image classification system. The method involved applying the previously developed EfficientNetB2 model to 15 clinical mammographic images as external data. Each image was entered into the system to obtain its classification result, which was then compared with the diagnostic label in the original data. During the model development stage, the EfficientNetB2 model achieved an accuracy of 72%, precision of 67%, recall of 96% and an F1-score of 79%. The external evaluation results showed that 13 out of 15 images produced predictions consistent with their diagnostic labels, while 2 images produced inconsistent predictions, resulting in a prediction agreement rate of 86.67%. Based on the confusion matrix, the model achieved an accuracy of 86.67%, precision of 80%, recall of 100%, and an F1-score of 88.89%. The external evaluation provides an overview of the model’s generalization capability when applied to data outside its development environment through a local web-based system.

title: Design, Implementation, and Empirical Evaluation of a Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model in Higher Education
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
c4fc7c2df67e25e958c78f59c8dc7e87340a3c13.abstract: AI-supported assessment increasingly enables adaptive tasks, automated analysis, and personalized feedback, yet their integration into coherent, human-supervised formative assessment remains insufficiently established. This study developed and evaluated the Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model (HA-CAAM) using Design and Development Research structured through the ADDIE framework. Implemented in a higher-education Media Education course, the model employed performance-responsive task adaptation using predefined thresholds, rubric-guided AI-assisted scoring, formative feedback, and instructor verification. Five experts validated the model, 148 students provided quantitative and qualitative implementation feedback, and 50 student responses were independently assessed by two human raters and AI. Expert validation provided initial evidence of content validity (mean Aiken's V = 0.818). Students reported generally favorable experiences, particularly regarding clarity and feedback usefulness, although Learning Support and Overall User Experience received comparatively lower ratings. AI-generated scores demonstrated strong agreement with human-reference scores (ICC = 0.898), despite individual discrepancies. These findings provide initial evidence of content validity, positive implementation experiences, and scoring agreement, rather than demonstrated improvements in learning outcomes or equivalence between AI and human assessment decisions. HA-CAAM contributes an empirically refined, seven-stage assessment framework that coordinates performance-responsive adaptation, AI-assisted analysis, formative feedback, and instructor-led quality assurance within a human-supervised assessment process.

title: JCOIN Dissemination and Stakeholder Engagement Core: Advancing the Translation and Use of Evidence in Criminal Justice and Health Settings
306349618e06bb7a7c85151762140f7a194eeed7.abstract: Abstract Background: Despite decades of research identifying effective approaches to prevent, identify, and treat substance use disorders (SUD), gaps persist between scientific discovery and utilization in routine practice, particularly within criminal legal systems (CLS). Contributing factors include: limited access to research findings, which are often published in technical and inaccessible formats; insufficient collaboration and trust between researchers and practitioners; research that is not relevant to real-world practice, where controlled studies don’t reflect the real-world context that practitioners face; and dissemination approaches to practitioners that are not tailored for the culture and climate of the organization or don’t match the skills of the staff. Practitioners and policymakers therefore need practical and tailored information that enables them to implement innovations while preserving the elements essential to their effectiveness. Methods: The Justice Community Opioid Innovation Network’s (JCOIN) Coordination and Translation Center (CTC) was established to address these barriers and accelerate the translation of research into policy and practice. During JCOIN 1.0, the CTC’s Dissemination and Stakeholder Engagement Core (DSEC) developed the stakeholder-engagement and dissemination infrastructure that supports this work. The Core cultivated networks of champions and trusted messengers through national practitioner and stakeholder advisory boards and maintained bidirectional communication channels connecting researchers and JCOIN leadership with practitioners, policymakers, community organizations, and people with lived experience. The DSEC identified field priorities, summarized research findings into digestible formats, co-developed educational products with community partners, and disseminated such products through various channels and networks. This article describes the DSEC’s stakeholder engagement, knowledge translation, and dissemination framework. Conclusion: By embedding stakeholder engagement, knowledge translation, implementation support, and dissemination within JCOIN, the DSEC strengthens the relevance, reach, and practical application of new research and evidence-based practices. This infrastructure advances JCOIN 2.0’s scientific and translational goals by sustaining feedback loops between research and practice, extending participation beyond the funded network, and supporting the adoption, implementation, and sustainment of evidence-informed policies, programs, practices, and treatments for people affected by SUD, overdose risk, and CLS involvement.

title: System Dynamics Modeling for Performance Optimization in a Pipe Manufacturing System: An Ethiopian Case Analysis
container-title: International Journal of Modeling, Simulation, and Scientific Computing
f159ad406e28320d5cc27f5ef78540c2144349d0.abstract: This study presents a system dynamics-based case study aimed at evaluating and enhancing the performance of a manufacturing system, with specific application to the Amhara Pipe Factory in Ethiopia. Manufacturing systems in developing economies often face challenges related to capacity utilization, operational inefficiencies, and human performance, which collectively limit their ability to meet customer demand and maintain competitiveness. To address these issues, a system dynamics model integrating human factors, process factors, and product and service factors was developed using empirical data collected through questionnaires, interviews, direct observations, and company records. Statistical analysis using IBM SPSS was applied to identify and prioritize key performanceinfluencing factors, which were subsequently incorporated into the simulation model developed in Vensim software. Three policy scenarios were evaluated to assess potential performance improvements: variation in customer demand, reduction of cycle time and downtime, and enhancement of employee training and experience. Simulation results indicate that increasing customer demand by 50% improves production performance by 0.457%, while reducing cycle time and downtime by 50% increases performance by 2.257%. The most significant improvement was observed under the human-factor-focused scenario, where enhancing employee training and experience by 50% resulted in a 26.6% increase in production performance, achieving up to 98.1% of the desired production capacity. Unlike conventional static performance assessment approaches, the proposed framework captures the dynamic interactions and feedback relationships among manufacturing system variables, enabling long-term evaluation of alternative operational policies. The findings highlight the critical role of human factors in manufacturing system performance and demonstrate the usefulness of system dynamics modeling as a decision-support tool for performance improvement in industrial and environmental engineering applications.

title: O (2)-Equivariant Hopf Bifurcation and Wave Selection in a Delayed Cross-Diffusive Predator-Prey Model: Theory and Simulation
container-title: International Journal of Modeling, Simulation, and Scientific Computing
4e948d06be0680251d03e014b27b9ee9157166d9.abstract: This study develops a modeling and simulation framework for wave selection in an O(2)-equivariant predator-prey model with general local kinetics and two delayed cross-diffusion mechanisms. We derive the mode-dependent characteristic equation and construct stability switching curves in the two-delay parameter plane, which provide computable criteria for delay-induced loss of stability. Center manifold reduction and O(2)-equivariant Hopf bifurcation theory are applied to obtain a normal form for the critical nonzero spatial mode, and the resulting coefficients determine the existence, bifurcation direction, and stability of the rotating and standing waves. A concrete fear-memory predator-prey model is used to illustrate the analytical results. The stability switching curves, normal form coefficients, and direct numerical simulations consistently identify the emergence of rotating- and standing-wave branches. The numerical scheme combines finite-difference spatial discretization, delayed-state interpolation, and a splitting time integrator. Moreover, simulations with multimode and random perturbations reveal mixedmode patterns associated with nonlinear interactions among spatial modes. These results show that behavioral memory, cross-diffusion, and spatial symmetry jointly organize stability switching, wave selection, and spatiotemporal pattern formation in delayed ecological systems.

title: Measuring Autonomous and Efficacious GenAI Use and GenAI Reliance in EFL Learning: Initial Scale Development and Validation
container-title: Applied Language Sciences
77ae85783ca0a3c588bf9186e455193a2953553b.abstract: This study developed and examined initial validity evidence for a scale assessing autonomous and reliant use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in English as a foreign language (EFL) learning. Participants were 416 students enrolled in required English courses at one Japanese university. The sample was randomly divided into an exploratory sample (n = 205) and an independent confirmatory sample (n = 211). Exploratory factor analysis of 10 initial items supported two factors: Autonomous and Efficacious GenAI Use (six items) and GenAI Reliance (three items). One of the ten items (REL4), which concerned worry about reliance, did not load meaningfully on either factor and was treated as an exploratory single item. The initial confirmatory factor analysis showed mixed fit. A post hoc model allowing a residual covariance between two autonomy items (AU1 and AU2) showed improved fit (robust CFI = .959, robust TLI = .940, robust RMSEA = .073, and SRMR = .060). Internal-consistency coefficients were .86 for Autonomous and Efficacious GenAI Use and .70 for GenAI Reliance, and the latent factor correlation was small and nonsignificant (r = .11, 95% CI [−.07, .30]). The heterotrait-monotrait ratio was .175, 95% CI [.132, .343]. These findings provide preliminary evidence that Autonomous and Efficacious GenAI Use and GenAI Reliance may represent distinct dimensions. Further validation with new, more diverse samples and external criteria is required.

title: Credit Default Risk Assessment of Listed Real Estate Firms Using the KMV Model
container-title: Risk and Financial Management
91b1aff0a7dafd489d54a7797dc24dcea1a56be3.abstract: This study examines the credit default risk of Chinese listed real estate firms using the KMV structural credit risk model, with particular attention to market-based risk assessment and the limitations of conventional credit ratings. Drawing on data from 261 real estate firms listed on mainland China's A-share markets and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange between 2010 and 2023, the study estimates distance to default (DD) from equity market information and financial statement data. A logistic regression approach is employed to translate DD into estimated default probabilities, while receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and firm-level case studies are used to evaluate risk discrimination and early-warning performance. The results reveal a substantial deterioration in the creditworthiness of mainland-focused property developers during the industry downturn, particularly in 2022–2023, alongside pronounced differences between mainland and non-mainland firms. The DD measure achieves an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.760, indicating moderate discriminatory ability within the evaluated sample. Comparative case studies further suggest that market-based risk indicators can provide more frequent signals of financial deterioration than conventional credit ratings, although their predictive reliability depends on appropriate calibration and validation. The findings highlight the potential of the KMV model as a supplementary instrument for credit risk monitoring while emphasizing the need for improved probability calibration, rigorous out-of-sample validation, and integration with firm-level and macroeconomic indicators.

title: Explainable Job Category Detection Using DistilBERT: A Three-Class Transformer Model for Classifying Real, Fake, and Invalid Online Job Offers
37f40912a931a9fd00d4853dc7c823643fbd3eff.abstract: Abstract Online job portals have widened access to employment, but they have also become a primary channel for Online Recruitment Fraud (ORF), in which fake job postings are used to extract money, harvest personal data, or recruit victims into illicit schemes. Most fake job detection systems treat the task as binary Real/Fake classification, which forces incomplete, nonsensical, or spam-like postings into the wrong class and makes them less reliable in practice. This study develops and evaluates an explainable, lightweight DistilBERT model that classifies online job offers as Real, Fake, or Invalid, and deploys it as a real-time web application. The distilbert-base-uncased classifier was fine-tuned on a corpus that combines the Employment Scam Aegean Dataset (EMSCAD), the job-scam domain of the DIFrauD benchmark, and a researcher-curated Invalid Token dataset. The combined corpus of 34,325 records was highly imbalanced (21.8:1), so it was rebalanced to 3,000 records per class through controlled undersampling and textual augmentation instead of SMOTE, and balanced class weighting was kept during training. The model was trained for four epochs with AdamW (learning rate 2 × 10⁻⁵) and a 256-token sequence length on a stratified 70:15:15 train–validation–test split, with the best checkpoint chosen by validation loss, and was then served through a FastAPI backend with SHAP-based token-level explanations. On a held-out test set of 1,350 samples, the model achieved 98.74% accuracy and 98.74% balanced accuracy and misclassified only 17 samples. It reached F1-scores of 0.98, 1.00, and 0.98 and one-versus-rest ROC-AUC values of 0.998, 1.000, and 0.998 for the Fake, Invalid, and Real classes, respectively, and the deployed system returned predictions in about 1.0 to 2.9 seconds. These results show that a distilled transformer can deliver accurate, efficient, and interpretable three-class fake job detection, and that the explicit Invalid category and SHAP explanations take automated job offer screening beyond conventional binary approaches.

title: Integrated analysis of ATAC-seq and RNA-seq in endometrial tissues between American and French large white pigs
container-title: BMC Genomics
6fb171ba061dd712fb3c49aa19b74b2d24a839de.abstract: Abstract Large White pigs are widely used as maternal lines, although reproductive performance varies among populations. The endometrium supports embryo implantation and development, and its molecular state may contribute to reproductive variation. This exploratory extreme-phenotype study compared endometrial tissues from nulliparous estrous gilts from French (FL) and American (AL) Large White source populations with different historical herd-level litter-size records. Uterine horn length was measured in five gilts per line, and the three FL gilts with the longest total uterine horns and the three AL gilts with the shortest were selected for ATAC-seq and RNA-seq. The left and right uterine horns were significantly longer in FL than in AL gilts ATAC-seq identified 11,502 exploratory candidate accessibility regions; these regions were linked to 6,867 unique genes. RNA-seq detected 4,078 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Integrated analysis identified 1,227 overlapping genes and highlighted oxytocin, calcium, PI3K-Akt, and related signaling pathways as candidate modules. ITPR1 , ITPR2 , PLA2G4A , and CACNA1C , together with several motif- and network-derived candidate transcriptional regulators, were prioritized for further study. These findings describe molecular differences observed in the selected extreme-phenotype gilts and provide hypotheses for validation in larger, unselected populations.

title: Multiple Methods for Visualizing Human Language: A Tutorial for Social and Behavioural Scientists
62e0c58fe1ca6fa551be699f926100d873c03d4d.abstract: Humans use language to communicate psychological experiences. Advancements in Natural LanguageProcessing have enabled researchers to quantitatively study and assess psychological states andbehaviors through language (e.g., well-being and mental health). Insights from language analyses areoften best conveyed through visualizations. Data-driven visualizations of how language statisticallyrelates to psychological dimensions can help interpret assessment scores, uncover meaningful patterns,and understand the intricate relationships between language use and mental states. Visualizations canbe used to differentiate between related constructs (e.g., How does language related to depression versusanxiety differ?), understand the validity of assessment tools (e.g., Does the language related to highdepression severity match with depression theory?), and explain language-based assessments (e.g.,Which language is indicative of higher depression severity in a language-based assessment?).This tutorial demonstrates how to transform language data into visual insights using the text and topicspackages in R. We provide practical guidance on creating four types of visualizations based on differentlanguage analysis techniques, examining how language use patterns are statistically associated with apsychological construct. We visualize 1) individual words and phrases (n-grams), 2) topics (wordclusters), 3) words in the word embedding space, and 4) relevant language examples. These differentvisualizations offer complementary perspectives, visualizing linguistic elements from individual wordsto overarching topics and text examples. The underlying methods range from correlations betweenindividual words to more advanced techniques, including topic modeling and Large Language Models.By making these methods accessible, this tutorial aims to empower researchers to use languagevisualizations for meaningful, data-driven insights.

title: Multilingualism WithOut Words: A non-lexicalist model of bilingualism
7df0e344224a244ebb0cf0008c863265adf9a4a5.abstract: Standard models of bilingualism are primarily concerned with how words in multiple languages are stored and associated in the mind. However, there is growing consensus in linguistic theory that language cannot be organized around words, given that meaning, syntax, and form do not always align at the word level. We propose the Multilingualism WithOut Words (M-WOW) model to realign models of bilingualism with current linguistic theory and account for a broader typology of languages. In contrast to other models, M-WOW allows more flexibility in how features are realized across languages and expands the possibilities for code-switching. Because the model does not rely on a word level, it accommodates a broader set of linguistic phenomena and provides new insights into bilingual language processing and the dynamic and variable processes of L2 acquisition and attrition.

title: THE IMPACT OF ENGLISH LOANWORDS ON THE VOCABULARY OF MODERN UZBEK LANGUAGE
container-title: Zamonaviy dunyoda ijtimoiy fanlar, Vol. 5, No. 32 (2026)
4890cf2ab79cc6c2428ce654468a748502ceb5ac.abstract: This article examines the linguistic influence of English loanwords on the lexical system of the modern Uzbek language. Driven by rapid globalization, technological advancement, and international integration, the inflow of English terminology into Uzbek has accelerated significantly. This paper analyzes the structural, semantic, and sociolinguistic aspects of these borrowings across key spheres such as information technology, business, economics, social media, and daily communication. Furthermore, it explores the mechanisms of phonetic and morphological adaptation of English loanwords into Uzbek, alongside the debate between linguistic purism and natural lexical expansion. The study relies on contemporary linguistic frameworks and empirical language samples from media and daily discourse.

title: An Improved EfficientNet-B0 Model for Facial Emotion Recognition
2c67da4fc77af46e65767156b1ef14045dacac17.abstract: Abstract Facial emotion recognition (FER) is increasingly built into interactive software, but reported accuracies are hard to compare because datasets, emotion sets and evaluation splits differ between studies, and few studies examine whether a larger backbone is worth its extra computational cost on the same data. This study develops and evaluates an EfficientNet-B0 model for five-class FER (happiness, sadness, anger, surprise and neutral) and compares it with EfficientNet-B1 and EfficientNet-B2 trained on the same images. FER2013 and the Real-world Affective Faces Database (RAF-DB) were combined, 1,470 duplicate or label-conflicting images and 19 unreadable files were removed, and a balanced set of 25,000 grayscale images (5,000 per class) was divided into 20,000 training, 2,500 validation and 2,500 test images, with no image shared between subsets. The model was fine-tuned in two stages from ImageNet weights using label smoothing, geometric and photometric augmentation, Mixup and CutMix. On the independent test set, EfficientNet-B0 achieved an accuracy of 78.68%, a macro F1-score of 78.83% and a macro-averaged ROC-AUC of 0.948, with class F1-scores ranging from 70.13% (neutral) to 87.78% (surprise). EfficientNet-B1 reached 79.76% accuracy, a difference that McNemar's test did not find significant (p = 0.107), while EfficientNet-B2, trained under a reduced schedule, reached 75.44% and was significantly less accurate (p < 0.001). EfficientNet-B0 used 36.6% fewer parameters than B1 (4.38 million against 6.90 million), needed 8.5 ms per image for single-image inference against 12.4 ms, required 40% less fine-tuning time and recorded the highest macro AUC of the three backbones. The trained model was deployed in a FastAPI web application that returns the predicted emotion with a confidence score. Within the conditions tested, EfficientNet-B0 gave the best balance between recognition performance and computational cost, while sadness and neutral remained the expressions most often confused with each other.

title: PLSTM-Reg v1.0: a regional physics-encoded LSTM model for simulating reservoir operations without site-specific training
container-title: Geoscientific Model Development
ac393b241f930546259e957374c2df728fe4f9ec.abstract: Representing reservoir operations in large-scale hydrological models remains difficult due to complex release decisions and scarce operational records. Here, we develop PLSTM-Reg v1.0, a regional physics-encoded deep learning framework that explicitly enforces mass balance and operational constraints to simulate reservoir operations across diverse systems. The framework is evaluated using 256 representative reservoirs across the Contiguous United States, focusing on three core capabilities: temporal generalization to unseen periods, spatial transfer to unseen reservoirs, and historical data reconstruction in data-scarce reservoirs. Under temporal testing, the regional model improves 1 d-ahead release forecasts from a median Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE) of 0.83 to 0.96 relative to local counterparts (i.e., models trained exclusively on site-specific records), and reduces poorly simulated cases (KGE<0.8) from 41.8 % to 2.3 %. For long-term simulation, storage performance reaches a median KGE of 0.79, a modest gain over local models (0.76) but with notable robustness for reservoirs with large capacity. When transferred to unseen reservoirs, the model substantially outperforms widely used rule-based schemes: median KGE rises from 0.55 (best benchmark) to 0.73 for release and from 0.22 to 0.59 for storage, and the proportion of usable simulations (KGE>0.5) increases from 56.6 % to 89.8 % for release and 14.4 % to 61.7 % for storage. In historical storage reconstruction, incorporating monthly satellite-derived surface area as a proxy for missing ground-based records enables reconstruction accuracy comparable to local models. These results demonstrate that cross-reservoir deep learning combined with physical knowledge provides a scalable scheme for representing human water management within large-scale hydrological and land surface models.

title: Peningkatan Kemampuan Berbicara melalui Model Problem Based Learning Berbantuan Permainan Ular Tangga Edukatif berbasis Kartu pada Materi di Iklan Kelas VIII A Smp N 7 Purwokerto
container-title: AKSARA: Jurnal Bahasa dan Sastra
880035f75a43f0c4edeb2efbe949a9d8480bb2d2.abstract: This study aimed to improve students’ speaking skills through the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model assisted by a card-based educational snakes-and-ladders game on advertising material in Grade VIII A at SMP Negeri 7 Purwokerto. The study employed Classroom Action Research using the Kemmis and McTaggart model, comprising planning, action, observation, and reflection. It was conducted in two cycles involving 31 students. Data were collected using a speaking skills observation sheet consisting of 20 indicators, interviews, and documentation, and were analyzed descriptively. The mean speaking assessment score increased from 75.32 in Cycle I to 90.65 in Cycle II. The number of students scoring above 75 increased from 16 (51.61%) to 31 (100%). In Cycle II, the separate game boards used by individual groups were replaced with one large shared banner and a turn-taking system. This revision aimed to organize the game flow and provide more structured opportunities for speaking. The findings showed an improvement in speaking assessment results across the two action cycles. The research success criterion, defined as at least 70% of students scoring above 75, was achieved in Cycle II.

title: Which Distortion gets confused? A Controlled Comparison of Language Models for Dominant Cognitive Distortion Classification
1d1b0a3f085f8bdcf519bf4317e10a7d572f9fef.abstract: Cognitive Distortions are unhelpful thinkingpatterns that Cognitive Behavioral Therapy(CBT) aims to identify and restructure, soclassifying cognitive distortions is a crucialprocess for reframing. The classificationbecomes difficult as the data is limited, andthe data are imbalanced most of the time. Westudy dominant distortion classification onthe publicly available Therapist Q&amp;A dataset(Shreevastava and Foltz, 2021) where the anno-tator agreement on the dominant distortion islow (34%). Using the annotated distorted spanas input, we compare TF-IDF baselines withRoBERTa, DeBERTa-v3 and MentalBERT(with and without focal loss) over three seeds,reporting accuracy, macro F1 and Cohen’skappa with significance tests. The encodersreach 0.39 to 0.44 accuracy, well above themajority-class baseline (0.15), the three cross-entropy encoders are not significantly differentfrom each other, while the weighted focal lossis worse. An error analysis shows that errorsconcentrate on a small group of overlappingdistortions, mainly All-or-nothing thinking,Magnification and Mental filter, whichsuggests that unclear category boundaries limitperformance more than model choice.

title: Differentiated Instruction in Grades 7 and 8 English Language Arts Inclusion Classrooms in Los Banos, California: A Qualitative Case Study
container-title: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice
65db89b67840e039c92b4f6d1dc7d00d7fbe220e.abstract: This qualitative single-case study examined how Grades 7 and 8 English Language Arts (ELA) inclusion teachers at Creekside Junior High School in Los Banos, California, used and appraised differentiated instructional strategies. Eight interview transcripts were available. Seven were provisionally analyzed as accounts of inclusive instruction, with grade assignments still to be verified for two interviewees. One transcript described a self-contained special education setting and was held separately. Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis generated six themes. Teachers reported maintaining grade-level learning objectives while varying modeling, organizers, prompts, and individual or group assistance. They described identifying the difficulty underlying a learner’s response, revising scaffolds that created or failed to resolve barriers, and using participation, student work, and independence to judge whether to continue or reduce assistance. Shared responsibilities created opportunities for support, while planning time, staffing, and competing classroom needs shaped which strategies teachers could sustain. The findings distinguish perceived instructional responsiveness from practical usefulness and informed the proposed Responsive Differentiated ELA Instruction Framework (R-DELA Framework). The interview accounts document teachers’ reasoning and perceptions. Independent classroom observations and instructional documents were unavailable for analysis, leaving implementation and learner outcomes unverified. The study recommends a school-approved pilot of the framework before wider use.

title: PENERAPAN MODEL ROLE PLAYING UNTUK MENGATASI MASALAH PERILAKU BELAJAR DI SMA NEGERI 1 JEMBER
container-title: TEACHING : Jurnal Inovasi Keguruan dan Ilmu Pendidikan
ae509300ca73f470e5c61f7613b56bbdae2bfb43.abstract: This study was motivated by the identification of student learning behavior issues that prevented classroom learning from achieving optimal conditions. These issues were reflected in limited student engagement, a less conducive classroom environment, and disrupted interactions between teachers and students as well as among students. This study aimed to describe changes in students' learning behaviors during the implementation of the Role Playing model and identify their drama appreciation achievements in Indonesian language learning. A qualitative approach with a case study design was employed, involving 35 students from Class XI Health 1 at SMA Negeri 1 Jember. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and documentation and analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings revealed observable changes in students' learning behaviors during the implementation of the Role Playing model, characterized by improved attention, greater participation in group discussions, increased responsibility for assigned tasks, and reduced off-task activities and misuse of permission to leave the classroom. Students also demonstrated strong drama appreciation achievements, with average scores of 96.89 on the listening worksheet and 98.29 on the reading worksheet, while all 35 students met the minimum mastery criteria in both assessments. These findings suggest that the Role Playing model, supported by teaching methods and learning media tailored to students' characteristics, may serve as an alternative instructional strategy for facilitating student engagement and drama appreciation. This study contributes empirical insights into changes in students' learning behaviors within the context of participatory and experiential drama learning. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh ditemukannya masalah perilaku belajar siswa yang menyebabkan dinamika pembelajaran belum menunjukkan kondisi yang ideal. Kondisi tersebut berdampak pada kurangnya keterlibatan siswa dalam pembelajaran, suasana kelas yang kurang kondusif, serta terganggunya interaksi antara guru dan siswa maupun antarsiswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan perubahan perilaku belajar siswa selama penerapan model Role Playing serta mengidentifikasi capaian apresiasi drama siswa dalam pembelajaran Bahasa Indonesia. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus yang melibatkan 35 siswa kelas XI Kesehatan 1 SMA Negeri 1 Jember. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui tahapan reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya perubahan perilaku belajar siswa selama penerapan model Role Playing, yang ditandai dengan meningkatnya fokus, partisipasi dalam diskusi kelompok, tanggung jawab terhadap tugas, serta berkurangnya aktivitas di luar pembelajaran dan penyalahgunaan izin keluar kelas. Capaian apresiasi drama siswa juga menunjukkan hasil yang baik, dengan rata-rata nilai 96,89 pada LKPD menyimak dan 98,29 pada LKPD membaca, serta seluruh 35 siswa mencapai ketuntasan pada kedua penilaian. Temuan tersebut menggambarkan bahwa penerapan Role Playing, yang didukung oleh pemilihan metode dan media pembelajaran sesuai karakteristik siswa, dapat menjadi alternatif strategi untuk memfasilitasi keterlibatan belajar dan apresiasi drama. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi berupa gambaran empiris mengenai perubahan perilaku belajar siswa dalam konteks pembelajaran drama yang partisipatif dan berbasis pengalaman langsung.

title: Chinese language studies in Malaysia: a systematic review on researchers, topical concerns, and methodological trends
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
68554b5daba63306862a77f4023568cdfed53b17.abstract: Introduction The tensions among language maintenance, language shift, and identity formation has long been discussed in Chinese Malaysian society. Against this backdrop, this review examines the researchers, topical concerns, and methodological trends on Chinese language studies in Malaysia. Methods Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, a total of 488 studies (269 in English journals and 219 in Chinese journals) on Chinese language studies in Malaysia were selected taken from China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), MyCite, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, Ebscohost, Scopus, and the Web of Science database (1981–2025). Results The results show that (1) the distribution of researchers, journals, and countries collectively demonstrates a long-tail effect in Chinese language studies in Malaysia; (2) language practice is the most frequent topic found within the studies indexed in the Chinese and English journals, followed by language management and the combination of language practice and language ideology; (3) approximately three-fourths of the studies are empirical, while the remaining are non-empirical research, review articles, and unidentifiable studies. Discussion Among the empirical articles, the most prevalent research approach was qualitative—followed by quantitative studies and mixed-methods research studies. The results of this study may serve as references for sociolinguistics and the psychology of language.

title: Longitudinal cognitive and functional outcomes after hemorrhagic stroke in patients with preserved consciousness: a prospective observational study
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
a6dcd096c328872c19fc7e51efbe7313a5031202.abstract: Introduction Cognitive impairment is a common consequence of stroke but may be underrecognized in patients with preserved consciousness. This study evaluated longitudinal changes in neurological, cognitive, and functional outcomes during the first 6 months after hemorrhagic stroke and identified baseline predictors of unfavorable outcomes. Methods A total of 74 patients with hemorrhagic stroke and preserved consciousness [Glasgow Coma Scale ≥13; mean age, 57.9 ± 10.1 years: 36 women (48.6%)] were prospectively enrolled between July 2020 and July 2024. Cognitive and functional outcomes were assessed at the initial assessment and at 1, 3, and 6 months using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR), Basic Activities of Daily Living (BADL), and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL). Longitudinal changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, and logistic regression was performed to identify predictors of unfavorable outcomes at 6 months. Results Cognitive measures improved significantly over time, with increases in MoCA scores ( p &lt; 0.001) and reductions in CDR scores ( p = 0.028). In contrast, BADL and IADL showed trends toward improvement without statistical significance. At 6 months, 25.7% of patients had unfavorable cognitive or functional outcomes. Older age, lower educational level, and previous stroke were independently associated with unfavorable outcomes. Conclusion Patients with hemorrhagic stroke and preserved consciousness showed gradual cognitive improvement over 6 months, although a substantial proportion experienced unfavorable cognitive or functional outcomes. These findings highlight the potential importance of early cognitive assessment even in patients with relatively mild neurological presentations. Given the modest sample size and exploratory nature of the analyses, larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings and further investigate predictors of post-stroke cognitive and functional recovery.

title: The effectiveness of AI-based cognitive behavioral therapy chatbots for anxiety and depression symptoms: a systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
12ee7b8b941ec1f9692a230d0f570c757b2ca9ce.abstract: Background AI chatbots are increasingly being used to provide accessible psychological support. However, the effectiveness of chatbot-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and depressive symptoms remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of artificial intelligence chatbot-based cognitive behavioral therapy on anxiety and depressive symptoms. Method A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wanfang, and CBM databases was conducted from their inception to July 8th, 2025. Updated search on August 25, 2026. Meta-analysis was conducted using Stata version 18.0 and RevMan version 5.4. The ES for the treatment effect was calculated using the SMD . Results Ten studies involving a total of 1,301 participants. The results of the meta-analysis showed that the CBT of AI chatbots could significantly improve depressive symptoms at the end of the intervention ( d = −0.40, 95% CI : −0.62 ~ −0.17, P = 0.0005). In contrast, the intervention did not significantly improve anxiety symptoms ( d = −0.029, 95% CI : −0.145 ~ 0.087, P = 0.623), with no substantial heterogeneity detected ( I 2 = 0%). The subgroup analysis for depressive symptoms indicated significant effects were observed in participant age stratification, intervention Duration, and Control group intervention. However, some subgroup estimates were based on a small number of studies, so the data should be interpreted with caution. Conclusion This meta-analysis emphasizes that AI-based chatbots for CBT may have great potential in contributing to the alleviation of depressive symptoms. Given the small number of included studies and the high heterogeneity, the results should be interpreted with caution. More high-quality RCTs are needed in the future to further validate these findings and explore their long-term benefits. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251089835 .

title: Latent profiles of teachers’ beliefs about drama pedagogy and children’s social–emotional, linguistic-communicative, and cognitive performance
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
fc22ad1429c406f8e34509d938a4185b73190323.abstract: Introduction Although drama pedagogy is widely used as a participatory educational approach, less is known about how teachers organize their beliefs about its developmental value. The present study examined teachers’ beliefs regarding the contribution of the drama-pedagogical approach to children’s social–emotional, linguistic-communicative, and cognitive functioning. More specifically, it examined the internal structure of these beliefs, the identification of latent belief profiles, and the association of these profiles with teachers’ demographic and professional characteristics. Methods The study involved 571 primary education teachers who had previous training and teaching experience with drama-pedagogical practices. Data were collected through an adapted online questionnaire designed to capture teachers’ perceptions of the developmental functions of drama pedagogy. The analyses included an examination of the factor structure, assessment of internal consistency, latent profile analysis, and investigation of the association between profile membership and demographic and professional characteristics. Results The results provided qualified support for a three-factor organization of perceptions into social–emotional, linguistic-communicative, and cognitive dimensions, with strong positive correlations among the dimensions and satisfactory internal consistency. The latent profile analysis identified three belief profiles: a strong developmental beliefs profile, a moderate profile, and a comparatively lower profile. The profiles differed mainly in the overall intensity of beliefs and less in distinct combinations of dimensions. Profile membership was associated mainly with teaching grade or educational setting and, to a lesser extent, with gender. Discussion The findings indicate that teachers make sense of drama pedagogy as a multidimensional developmental practice, with differences in the intensity of their beliefs. The findings may inform the design of more targeted professional development programs, adapted to the teaching context and to teachers’ belief profiles.

title: Time-dependent association between mean platelet volume and gynecological cancer risk in a large healthcare-based cohort
container-title: Frontiers in Oncology
9f56e2569247ad45bf8a1c9ab355c564969f8faa.abstract: Background Gynecological cancers remain a major public health concern worldwide, highlighting the need for accessible biomarkers for early risk assessment. This study aimed to investigate the association between routine clinical laboratory parameters and the risk of incident gynecological cancers in a large healthcare-based cohort. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 187, 861 women from the Clinical Center of the University of Debrecen between 2007 and 2023. Baseline laboratory parameters were defined as the median of measurements recorded in the entry year. Incident gynecological cancers were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models, incorporating time-varying coefficients to address violations of proportionality. Results During a median follow-up of approximately 10 years (IQR 6–14 years; maximum follow-up 16 years), 1, 036 incident gynecological cancer cases were identified, corresponding to a crude proportion of 0.55%. Higher baseline mean platelet volume (MPV) was significantly associated with increased cancer risk; however, this relationship was strongly time-dependent. MPV showed little or inverse association in early follow-up but demonstrated progressively increasing hazard ratios over time. This pattern remained robust after adjustment for age, red cell distribution width (RDW), and C-reactive protein (CRP). RDW exhibited a time-dependent association with stronger effects early in follow-up that attenuated over time, while age showed a consistent positive association with cancer risk. Conclusion In this large healthcare-based cohort, higher baseline MPV was associated with an increased long-term risk of incident gynecological cancer, and the association strengthened with longer follow-up. These findings represent adjusted epidemiological associations that may be affected by residual confounding and should not be interpreted as causal.

title: Cognitive load detection using hyper-learning dragonfly optimization for feature selection
container-title: Frontiers in Physiology
5a453798221500241d3cfe550feba897cab0c822.abstract: Introduction Cognitive load detection is essential for understanding brain responses to mental effort and cognitive demands. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals provide valuable information about neural activity and offer a non-invasive approach to identifying cognitive load. However, accurate detection and the identification of brain regions with superior discriminative capabilities remain important challenges. Methods This study proposes an EEG-based cognitive load detection framework using empirical Fourier decomposition (EPFD), entropy-based feature extraction, and the hyper-learning binary dragonfly feature selection algorithm (HLBDA). EEG signals recorded from each brain lobe over four-second intervals were decomposed into 10 intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). Entropy-based features were extracted from the IMFs, and the most informative features were selected using HLBDA. The selected features were classified using machine learning (ML) classifiers. The proposed framework was evaluated on the MAT, STEW, and MLR datasets. Additionally, lobe-wise cognitive load detection was performed on the MAT and STEW datasets to investigate the discriminative capabilities of five individual brain lobes. Subject-wise leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) was employed to prevent data leakage. Results The proposed framework achieved classification accuracies of 97.13%, 96.48%, and 98.2% on the MAT, STEW, and MLR datasets, respectively, using the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) classifier for MAT and STEW and the ensemble subspace KNN (ESSK) classifier for MLR. In the lobe-wise analysis, the frontal lobe demonstrated superior discriminative capability for cognitive load detection, achieving accuracies of 96.7% and 96.6% on the MAT and STEW datasets, respectively, using the ESSK classifier. Discussion The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed EPFD–HLBDA-based framework for EEG-based cognitive load detection across multiple datasets. The superior performance of the frontal lobe suggests its potential as a particularly informative region for distinguishing cognitive states. Furthermore, the use of subject-wise LOOCV strengthens the evaluation by reducing the risk of data leakage. Compared with recently reported methods, the proposed framework demonstrates competitive classification performance and highlights the potential of lobe-specific EEG analysis for reliable cognitive load assessment.

title: Coach leadership behavior and athlete engagement among Chinese competitive basketball athletes: the parallel mediating roles of sport confidence and team cohesion
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
d33780ad626dccbddab3faa323444dfadd00d999.abstract: Objective This study examined the association between coach leadership behavior and athlete engagement among Chinese competitive basketball athletes and assessed parallel indirect associations through sport confidence and perceived team cohesion. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 450 National Level I and II basketball athletes recruited from Sichuan, Chongqing, and Shandong, China. Participants completed validated or adapted measures of coach leadership behavior, athlete engagement, sport confidence, and perceived team cohesion. Descriptive statistics, group comparisons, Pearson correlations, and structural equation modeling were performed using SPSS 27.0 and AMOS 26.0. Indirect effects were evaluated using bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples and 95% confidence intervals. Results Coach leadership behavior was positively correlated with athlete engagement ( r = 0.561, p &lt; 0.001). Training and instruction, democratic leadership, positive feedback, and social support were positively associated with engagement, whereas autocratic leadership was negatively associated with engagement. In the structural model, the direct association between coach leadership behavior and athlete engagement remained positive ( β = 0.259, p = 0.010), alongside significant indirect associations through sport confidence (effect = 0.152, 95% CI [0.077, 0.232]) and perceived team cohesion (effect = 0.344, 95% CI [0.162, 0.559]). Although the latter estimate was numerically larger, the contrast did not reach statistical significance ( p = 0.051). Model fit was favorable for χ 2 / df (1.103), RMSEA (0.015), CFI (0.987), TLI (0.987), and SRMR (0.041), whereas GFI (0.863) and AGFI (0.854) were below 0.90. Because fit cutoffs are heuristic rather than absolute rejection criteria and several complementary indices were favorable, the model was retained for cautious interpretation rather than regarded as unequivocally well fitting. Conclusion Coach leadership behavior was associated with greater athlete engagement, with complementary indirect associations through sport confidence and perceived team cohesion, reflecting individual competence-related and athlete-perceived interpersonal pathways. Because the study was cross-sectional and based on self-report data, the indirect pathways should be interpreted as theoretically informed statistical associations rather than causal mechanisms.

title: Intranasal deferiprone delivery increases brain exposure and ameliorates abnormal open-field behavior in a mouse model of brain iron dysregulation
container-title: Frontiers in Pharmacology
f04d24c9ced22346d44352328e3151ceca64f3db.abstract: Introduction Although brain iron dysregulation has been implicated in neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders, its potential as a therapeutic target remains unclear. Deferiprone (DFP), an oral lipophilic iron chelator approved for systemic iron overload, has been explored for central nervous system (CNS) disorders, but its use has been limited by systemic toxicity and suboptimal brain distribution. In this study, we evaluated intranasal (IN) delivery of DFP as an alternative strategy to modulate impaired neurobehavior in a mouse model of brain iron accumulation. Methods Wild‐type and H67D mice (male, n = 6–10 per group) received IN or oral DFP daily for 7 days, followed by open field testing and hematological assessment. To determine whether the behavioral effects and hematological tolerability of IN administration were associated with route‐dependent exposure, we evaluated pharmacokinetics and compared tissue distribution of DFP following IN and oral administration. Results In contrast to high-dose oral treatment, IN administration of DFP produced behavioral effects at 20 mg/kg without detectable hematological changes, whereas high-dose oral DFP (100 mg/kg) reduced circulating leukocyte and neutrophil counts without producing comparable behavioral effects. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed increased drug distribution in the olfactory bulb and distinct brain-to-plasma distribution patterns after IN administration relative to oral dosing. Conclusion Collectively, our findings demonstrate that intranasal delivery alters regional CNS exposure to DFP and improves open-field behavior associated with brain iron dysregulation.

title: Endoscopic-assisted rotary cutter for axillary osmidrosis: high efficacy and safety in a large retrospective cohort
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
537c8e0f8a5f6b99c85aadf8ce7a34b0e5591e8e.abstract: Background Minimally invasive axillary osmidrosis surgery is limited by an efficacy-safety trade-off caused by blind visualization. This study evaluated intermediate-term outcomes of a novel endoscopic-assisted rotary cutter technique. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort enrolled 980 consecutive moderate-to-severe axillary osmidrosis patients undergoing the procedure between January 2022 and June 2024. Treatment success was defined as patient-reported marked improvement or complete odor elimination. We assessed complications, recurrence, and compared outcomes between the learning phase (first 100 cases) and proficiency phase. Results With a 13-month median follow-up, overall patient-reported success rate was 97.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 96.5–98.5%), recurrence rate 2.35%, and overall complication rate 3.27% (only 0.2% required hematoma intervention). After 100 cases, operative time and complication rate dropped significantly ( P &lt; 0.01), with consistently high efficacy (&gt;96%). Preoperative severity was an independent success predictor (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.45, P &lt; 0.05). Conclusion This technique appears to help reconcile the traditional efficacy-safety trade-off in minimally invasive axillary osmidrosis treatment, with outcomes improving over an estimated learning curve of approximately 100 cases; these promising intermediate-term results warrant prospective comparative evaluation.

title: Association between plasma homocysteine levels and post-stroke cognitive impairment: a pooled analysis of 564 patients from two independent cohorts
container-title: Frontiers in Nutrition
7c0af70c2e569550b83f2b9dcf508c44c859fffb.abstract: Introduction Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) affects one-third of stroke survivors, but early biomarkers are lacking. We tested whether plasma homocysteine (Hcy) independently predicts PSCI. Methods Two acute ischemic stroke cohorts were merged (564 patients). PSCI was defined as a Montreal Cognitive Assessment score ≤ 23 at 3–6 months. Associations were tested with multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline, sensitivity, subgroup, and mediation analyses. Results PSCI occurred in 36.9%. Hcy was higher in PSCI (21.99 vs. 15.87 μmol/L, p &lt; 0.001) and associated after adjustment (OR = 1.019 per μmol/L, 95% CI 1.002–1.037, p = 0.030); in Cohort B, where age, sex, education and infarct laterality were recorded, the association remained significant after full adjustment (OR = 1.034, 95% CI 1.011–1.057, p = 0.004). The association was graded, with the steepest relative increase at lower Hcy levels and a plateau at higher levels (restricted cubic spline; non-linearity p = 0.054, borderline), and was not statistically significant at Hcy ≥ 20 or ≥ 25 μmol/L. Combining Hcy with Lp-PLA2, NIHSS, and β2-MG improved discrimination (AUC = 0.748, an apparent estimate that was not externally validated). In an exploratory counterfactual mediation analysis the proportion mediated was small (≈ 4% via NIHSS and ≈ 2% via Lp-PLA2). Discussion Elevated Hcy is associated with PSCI in this pooled analysis, and the association persisted in Cohort B after adjustment for age, sex, education and infarct laterality. The relationship was graded rather than sharply thresholded. As an observational finding, and given the absence of folate, vitamin B12 and renal-function data and the neutral results of B-vitamin trials such as VITATOPS, Hcy is best regarded as a risk marker rather than a proven causal target; dedicated trials are needed before any clinical recommendation.

title: A dynamic nomogram for predicting early post-stroke disorder of consciousness among stroke patients: model development and temporal validation
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
c0f5bb2229d86bd49c942882b73dda93a73e6b02.abstract: Objective This study aims to develop and validate a dynamic nomogram for the early prediction of post-stroke disorders of consciousness, tailored for general ward settings where rapid risk assessment without reliance on laboratory results is urgently needed. Methods This study enrolled 502 stroke patients as the modeling cohort, which was randomly divided into a training set ( n = 354) and an internal validation set ( n = 148) at a 7:3 ratio. An additional 186 stroke patients were recruited as a temporal validation cohort. The Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression and multivariate logistic regression were applied to screen independent risk factors and construct the predictive model. The model performance was comprehensively evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, decision curve analysis (DCA), and the Youden index. The study further constructed a dynamic nomogram to enable real-time risk calculation. Results The incidence of disorder of consciousness was 20.52% in the modeling cohort and 24.19% in the temporal validation cohort. Four independent predictors were identified: age, smoking status, systolic blood pressure, and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score. The nomogram exhibited favorable discriminatory capacity, with area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of 0.860, 0.852, and 0.764 in the training, internal validation, and temporal validation sets, respectively. DCA demonstrated satisfactory clinical net benefit within the threshold probability range of 0.1–0.3. An illustrative threshold of 0.30 is presented for reference in general ward settings. Conclusion This dynamic nomogram, built on four readily available clinical indicators obtainable at admission without waiting for laboratory or imaging results, shows reasonable discrimination and calibration. This model may serve as an exploratory reference tool for early risk stratification of post-stroke disorders of consciousness in general wards. Further prospective studies are required to verify its clinical utility.

title: Fluctuation in China’s liquefied natural gas import prices and risk transmission mechanism: an empirical study from the perspective of the eco-environment-oriented development model
container-title: Frontiers in Environmental Science
a7331c886d168e63ef10a4fdc6a6731d27a5ce3a.abstract: Introduction This study is an exploratory analysis. From the perspective of the Eco-environment-oriented Development (EOD) model, this study constructs a three-dimensional transmission model of “international oil prices–geopolitical risk–environmental policy” to explore the drivers and risk transmission paths of China’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) import price fluctuations. Methods Using monthly data (September 2021 to September 2024) on China’s LNG import prices, international oil prices (Brent and WTI), the Geopolitical Risk (GPR) Index, and the Environmental Policy Index (EPI), we conduct a dynamic empirical analysis via a vector autoregression (VAR) model. Results The research findings indicate that, based on asymptotic standard error statistics, the bootstrap robustness check reveals that only the contribution of GPR (22.81%, 95% Bootstrap CI: 3.04%–42.59%) is statistically significant, making it the only robust driver of price fluctuations within the sample period. The contributions of international oil prices (Brent point estimate 13.54%, WTI point estimate 10.05%) and environmental policy (EPI point estimate 11.38%) do not reach statistical significance under bootstrap inference; their point estimates are provided only as directional references and require further validation with larger samples. Discussion The study suggests possible transmission pathways of “international oil prices–geopolitical risk–environmental policy” on China’s LNG import price fluctuations under the EOD model, providing directional policy implications for balancing energy security and low-carbon transition goals. We recommend carbon price-linked LNG long-term contracts, a diversified supply system, and enhanced geopolitical risk early warning and coordination.

title: Patient engagement and care pathway continuity in structured osteoporosis management: real-world evidence from routine practice
container-title: Frontiers in Endocrinology
be7bf936d3cac086e613a6f53ad6315aa43171ed.abstract: Background Osteoporosis carries a substantial clinical burden, yet underdiagnosis and care pathway discontinuity remain common in routine practice. Structured care models integrating primary care and specialists may optimize disease assessment and care coordination. This study presented a retrospective descriptive evaluation of the operational implementation, patient-engagement patterns, and disease burden within a structured Health Bone Network (HBN) dedicated to osteoporosis care in a real-world setting. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study of 1,631 individuals undergoing bone mineral density assessment by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) in 2021 within a coordinated primary care-specialist HBN. Care pathway continuity, report access rates, consultation attendance, clinical characteristics, and specialist management patterns were analyzed. Results Among 1,631 evaluated individuals (mean age was 64.6 ± 10.7 years; 92.5% female), 60.1% accessed their digital specialist report. Among those with an explicit recommendation for specialist evaluation, consultation attendance was 38.2%. Densitometric osteoporosis was diagnosed in 28.3% of participants with applicable criteria. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, female sex, advanced age, and personal history of fragility fractures emerged as independent clinical factors for osteoporosis (p&lt; 0.05). Vitamin D supplementation was also positively associated with an osteoporotic T-score, a finding likely reflecting confounding by indication and reverse causation rather than an etiologic determinant. Conversely, diabetes mellitus was inversely associated with a densitometric diagnosis of osteoporosis (aOR=0.56, p = 0.018), highlighting a densitometric paradox in this population. Conclusion This study provides a baseline description of the operational implementation of a structured healthcare network integrating DXA reporting with primary care. While characterizing its operational structure, the substantial attrition rates along the care cascade highlight that digital data integration alone is insufficient to guarantee care continuity, offering a benchmark for future effectiveness evaluations and proactive engagement strategies.

title: DEVELOPING SPEAKING SKILLS THROUGH REAL-LIFE COMMUNICATIVE ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE COMMUNICATIVE LANGUAGE TEACHING APPROACH
container-title: Zamonaviy dunyoda ilm-fan va texnologiya, Vol. 5, No. 33 (2026)
8cc152f3f1f2d221731fe4ca877a8635f5e12fd3.abstract: Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) is an approach to language education that emphasizes meaningful interaction and the practical use of language in real-life situations. The ability to speak a foreign language involves more than knowing grammatical rules and vocabulary; learners must also be able to express ideas, exchange information, respond to others and communicate appropriately in different social contexts. This article examines how real-life communicative activities within the CLT approach can contribute to the development of English speaking skills among intermediate-level learners. The article focuses on the characteristics and needs of B1-level learners, the theoretical foundations of CLT, appropriate speaking content and practical classroom techniques. Activities such as storytelling, interviews, information-gap tasks, group discussions, problem-solving tasks and everyday situation simulations are discussed. The article is based on established academic literature and the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). It argues that meaningful communication, learner participation, appropriate language support and constructive feedback are important elements of communicative speaking instruction. The article also considers possible classroom challenges and suggests practical solutions for teachers.

title: A Cognitive Predictive Model of Air Traffic Controller’s Mental States
ce05181c1ef1dba04d9ea2ac5526e526b2ee6786.abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of a psychological model aimed at predicting the mental states of air traffic controllers (ATCOs). The proposed model aims to advance human–machine collaboration in air traffic management by enabling the precise prediction of critical operator cognitive and affective states, including mental workload, fatigue, stress, and attentional engagement. By formally integrating core cognitive processes—namely perception, comprehension, and decision-making—within its architecture, the model provides a principled framework for the continuous monitoring and real-time adaptation of support systems. Such adaptive capabilities are intended to optimize the allocation of assistance provided by artificial agents, thereby strengthening human–system coordination and contributing to enhanced operational safety and efficiency within the complex and highly dynamic environment of air traffic control. To estimate the parameters of the model, several air traffic simulations were conducted with expert controllers. In these simulations changes to traffic situations were introduced. Those changes could affect the controllers' mental states. The results of these changes were observed in the measured verbal and psychophysiological dependent variables. This paper presents results that partially validate the initial parameters of the models. These results will contribute to a future improvement of the model by refining the parameters of the proposed formulas for calculating mental workload, fatigue, stress, and vigilance in the air traffic control task.

title: Oscillations of a Universal Plowing Tractor with a Transformed Drive System: Bibliometric Analysis Based on Scopus Data, Mathematical Model, and Experimental Verification
66c496d588e40ff3d27aa3a446be54ae0e4fcf23.abstract: Universal-plowing wheeled tractors are operated in two fundamentally different modes: in-ter-row machining, where driving precision and minimum turning radius are decisive, and transport operations, where stability and smoothness of movement come to the fore. The trans-formed driving system, which allows for changing the base, track, and clearance (and conse-quently, the agrotechnical or road clearance), allows for adjusting the geometry of the driving system to the operating mode; however, the influence of these parameters on the oscillations of the frame has been studied in fragments. The work analyzed an array of 545 publications downloaded from the Scopus database on September 21, 2026, on the topic of vibrations of tractors and off-road vehicles. It is shown that 73% of the documents were published after 2010, and the research focuses on operator vibration protection, seat and cabin suspension, and tire dynamics, while works where base, track, and clearance are considered simultaneously variable parameters are rare, and there are no publications on tractors with a transforming chassis in the sample. To fill this gap, a mathematical model of the tractor's plane oscillations was constructed based on Lagrange equa-tions of the second kind, taking into account the non-holonomic connections of wheel rolling, and characteristic equations and expressions for low-frequency and high-frequency components of natural oscillations were obtained. Modeling at 245 cm and 275 cm bases, corresponding to tractors for row tillage and transport work, showed that as the speed increases, the oscillation amplitude increases and the period decreases, while increasing the tractor base decreases the amplitude. Tests of the TTZ-1033M tractor prototype with ADXL345 accelerometers at a track gauge of 1200–2400 mm and a clearance of 650–870 mm confirmed these dependencies: the increase in clearance in-creases vertical vibrations, the increase in base decreases them, and the change in track mainly determines the difference in rear wheel vibrations. The practical conclusion is that it is advisable to have a short tractor base for row-crop cultivation and a long tractor base for transport work.

title: Positivity of Single-Centred Black Hole Indices in the <span class="math-tex">\( \mathbb{Z}_2 \) CHL Model
a41aa5c266d7ae8000d0b0e6d0cdec16e6c1fe68.abstract: We prove Sen's positivity conjecture for single-centred quarter-BPS black holes of the \( Z_2 \) CHL model for every charge with \( Q^2\le2 \) and for every charge of discriminant at most 800. For all charges we reduce the conjecture to an explicit level-two Rademacher expansion of the dyon partition function and prove it under that hypothesis.

title: Memory and Time-Varying Activity in Batch Microbial Growth: A <em>ψ</em>-Fractional Monod Model Tested on Substrate–Biomass and Open Growth Data
446b7c2a4e47663f693889137401f6d02236fc5a.abstract: Batch cultures often show features that the Monod model cannot reproduce: lag phases, residual substrate and loss of cellular activity. Fractional-order extensions are increasingly proposed to capture such effects, but they are rarely tested against data. We formulate a ψ-fractional Monod model in which the order θ represents memory of the cells’ physiological history and a parameter β represents a time-varying activity. The model conserves mass, keeps concentrations positive, contains Monod kinetics as a special case and, without cell decay, predicts residual substrate if and only if activity declines (β > 0). We compare it with the Monod, Baranyi–Roberts, Weibull and tailing models on synthetic substrate–biomass data, a tequila batch fermentation and 43 open growth and survival curves, using information criteria, profile likelihoods and forecasting. With joint substrate–biomass data, the model recovers memory and deactivation where the Monod model returns biased kinetic constants. In the tequila fermentation, which stalls with 5.5% of the sugar unconsumed, it reproduces the stall with an identifiable order (θ = 0.54; 95% interval 0.40–0.67), but Monod kinetics with ethanol inhibition is equally supported. With biomass data alone, the order is not identifiable and the Baranyi–Roberts model forecasts better. We conclude with practical guidelines for model selection.

title: Auditable Feasibility-Gated Command Admission for Language-Conditioned Robotic Task Allocation
container-title: Journal of Intelligent & Robotic Systems
325c4d316e4a33021ff7d0ec978dbf77a08d9459.abstract: Abstract Language-conditioned robotic systems can map natural-language instructions to plausible skills, yet a semantically matched skill may still be non-executable on a particular robot. This paper presents QER–HFV, an auditable command-admission layer for robotic task allocation under semantic uncertainty. The layer expands the top-ranked skill hypotheses into explicit skill–robot candidates, checks capability, resource, communication, workspace, policy, and interface constraints, and records admission, rejection, or escalation outcomes with blocking reasons before any soft ranking is applied. In a reproducible decision-layer benchmark, 4-bit semantic memory preserves the FP32 allocation-success proxy to the displayed precision while reducing normalized semantic-memory cost to 12.5%. Hard feasibility verification lowers the single-step non-executable allocation rate from 0.580 for semantic-only retrieval to 0.108 for Semantic+HFV and 0.084 for the full gate. In a 1200-step online replay, the post-gate resource-aware ranker improves the mission-success proxy from 0.651 to 0.821, while windowed strong baselines clarify that the ranker is not a general batched scheduler. Execution-facing tests further show 100/108 executable successes and 72/72 correct infeasible-command rejections in a controlled tabletop Hiwonder xArm 1S study; overall correct handling is 172/180 (0.956; 95% Wilson CI [0.915, 0.977]). The simplified Robot Operating System (ROS)/Gazebo comparison records no collisions or infeasible false executions for QER–HFV. Targeted boundary experiments additionally show 0.9942 mean cosine preservation for 4-bit embeddings, extend candidate-fleet scaling to 80 robots per task, improve correct handling of 300 ambiguous/vague commands from 0.6267 to 0.8600 (paired difference +0.233; 95% bootstrap CI [0.167, 0.300]) with an escalation policy, and complete a 72-hour Raspberry Pi 5 replay with 259,200 decisions, two recoverable events, and no crashes or restarts. The results support QER–HFV as a reusable pre-command admissibility interface rather than a formal safety certificate or global scheduling optimizer.

title: MODEL PEMBELAJARAN READ, ANSWER, DISCUSS, EXPLAIN, AND CREATE (RADEC) PADA PEMBELAJARAN ILMU PENGETAHUAN ALAM DAN SOSIAL (IPAS) DI SEKOLAH DASAR: KAJIAN PUSTAKA KUALITATIF
container-title: Pendas : Jurnal Ilmiah Pendidikan Dasar
692955df4b49ae8c212edbf1972294d7146a4f02.abstract: The Read, Answer, Discuss, Explain, and Create (RADEC) learning model is increasingly used in Science and Social Studies (IPAS) lessons in Indonesian elementary schools, yet qualitative evidence on how it works in classrooms remains scattered. This study is a qualitative library research that synthesizes 17 sources: eight sources on RADEC and nine qualitative or mixed-methods articles by Syafi’i and Mudayat on distance education, digital learning, and learning processes in elementary schools. Sources were selected purposively, coded inductively, and synthesized thematically. The synthesis shows three things. First, RADEC is described as a five-stage syntax in which Read and Answer prepare students before the lesson, while Discuss, Explain, and Create form collaborative classroom activity. Second, the only purely qualitative RADEC study in IPAS found in this review, a case study in a fourth-grade class, reports that students perceived RADEC as enjoyable and motivating and that teachers saw it as increasing engagement, while quantitative and classroom-action studies report gains in concept understanding and learning outcomes. Third, the studies by Syafi’i and Mudayat point to four conditions that shape implementation: timely feedback, a collaborative social environment, affective engagement and student agency, and teacher capacity with contextual resources. The article proposes a stage-by-stage mapping of RADEC onto IPAS activities as a working hypothesis for field-based qualitative research; it does not report new classroom data.

title: Influence of digital work platforms on working conditions in the tourism sector: a system dynamics model
container-title: Central European Journal of Operations Research
75134822585ee5ae1f6b7138bb73a3106676e8ed.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the System Dynamics (SD) model developed within a research project focused on the phenomenon of platformisation of services in tourism and its impacts on the labour market, i.e. wages, working conditions and unionisation of tourism workers. Through consultations with domain experts, we have developed a causal loop diagram representing the relationships between stakeholders and other influential factors and used it as the starting point for the development of a System Dynamics (SD) model. The SD model aims to provide insight into the tourism labour market dynamics in Slovenia through the interplay of a set of variables representing the tourists, employers and workers in tourism industry. The model is based on previous research, consultation with labour market experts, public data on collective bargaining coverage, public statistical data on labour market and tourism industry from SiStat, Eurostat and OECD, and reports from Hotels, Restaurants & Cafés in Europe association (HOTREC) and European Working Conditions Surveys (EWCS).

title: Evaluation of the Quran literacy program at Muhammadiyah Simpang Empat Junior High School using the CIPP Model
container-title: International research journal of management, IT and social sciences
00e8ffdfec8f1157062f6f61413340234c964984.abstract: Low Qur’an reading proficiency among junior high school students from general education backgrounds poses a unique challenge for Islamic-based schools. This study aims to evaluate the Qur’an Literacy Program at Muhammadiyah Simpang Empat Junior High School using the CIPP (Context, Input, Process, Product) evaluation model. This study used a qualitative approach, with data collection methods including in-depth interviews, structured observations, and document analysis. The evaluation results at the context stage showed that this program arose from a real need and is highly relevant to the school’s vision and mission. The evaluation at the input stage indicated that, despite limitations in the number of teachers and financial support, the program was designed and implemented efficiently, realistically, and collaboratively. The process stage revealed that program implementation was consistent with the plan, student participation was high, and regular monitoring and improvements were conducted. In the product stage, the program proved successful in improving students’ ability to read the Qur’an, fostering religious attitudes, and having a positive impact on students’ self-confidence. This program also has strong potential for replication in other schools.

title: Large Language Models In Auditing Assessments: Comparisons Between Human Learners, Model Scale, and Enhancement Techniques
container-title: ABIS: Accounting and Business Information Systems Journal
0559330dcb20d024c1a9baf906e4ff4969818418.abstract: This study examines whether large language models (LLMs) can perform audit work by comparing their performance with human learners, across model scale and under two enhancement techniques. Drawing on the audit-judgment distinction between declarative and procedural knowledge, the study evaluates seven publicly available LLMs on audit work in two forms of audit assessment. In the knowledge-based assessment, the LLMs answer four undergraduate auditing examinations previously sat by 352 accounting students, as a proxy of human learners. In the data-analytic case assessment, they plan and execute SQL-based substantive procedures to test the occurrence of revenue and the completeness of expenditures. On the knowledge-based assessment, LLMs outperform human learners where large LLMs typically fall between the 78th and 98th student percentiles, and large LLMs outperform small LLMs. On the data-analytic case assessment, no LLM scores above 50% of the rubric maximum, and large and small LLMs do not differ significantly. Meanwhile, two enhancement techniques: self-reflection and agentic workflow do not improve performance on the data-analytic case assessment. These results reveal a knowing–doing gap: LLMs display strong declarative audit knowledge but weak procedural capability, and self-correction without external feedback does not repair knowledge errors. This study discusses implications for audit practice, assessment design and standard setters.
