title: The effectiveness of AI-based cognitive behavioral therapy chatbots for anxiety and depression symptoms: a systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
12ee7b8b941ec1f9692a230d0f570c757b2ca9ce.abstract: Background AI chatbots are increasingly being used to provide accessible psychological support. However, the effectiveness of chatbot-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and depressive symptoms remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of artificial intelligence chatbot-based cognitive behavioral therapy on anxiety and depressive symptoms. Method A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wanfang, and CBM databases was conducted from their inception to July 8th, 2025. Updated search on August 25, 2026. Meta-analysis was conducted using Stata version 18.0 and RevMan version 5.4. The ES for the treatment effect was calculated using the SMD . Results Ten studies involving a total of 1,301 participants. The results of the meta-analysis showed that the CBT of AI chatbots could significantly improve depressive symptoms at the end of the intervention ( d = −0.40, 95% CI : −0.62 ~ −0.17, P = 0.0005). In contrast, the intervention did not significantly improve anxiety symptoms ( d = −0.029, 95% CI : −0.145 ~ 0.087, P = 0.623), with no substantial heterogeneity detected ( I 2 = 0%). The subgroup analysis for depressive symptoms indicated significant effects were observed in participant age stratification, intervention Duration, and Control group intervention. However, some subgroup estimates were based on a small number of studies, so the data should be interpreted with caution. Conclusion This meta-analysis emphasizes that AI-based chatbots for CBT may have great potential in contributing to the alleviation of depressive symptoms. Given the small number of included studies and the high heterogeneity, the results should be interpreted with caution. More high-quality RCTs are needed in the future to further validate these findings and explore their long-term benefits. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251089835 .

title: Application of inertial measurement units and machine learning for fatigue assessment in badminton athletes
container-title: Frontiers in Physiology
28910308e3b04040c11085a4c70390b4cfcc2df5.abstract: Objective To evaluate offline binary classification of recorded fatigue conditions using inertial measurement unit (IMU) acceleration features and five machine-learning algorithms. Methods The author-confirmed performance dataset contained 32 observations per condition. The revised primary IMU dataset comprised 70 recordings from 25 roster-linked athletes, with 22 non-fatigue and 48 fatigue labels after correction of four misclassified recordings. Seven-sensor and right-forearm configurations provided 231 and 33 candidate features. A newly reconstructed analysis retained five documented outer athlete-grouped folds and used three grouped inner folds for training-only preprocessing, sparse logistic feature selection and hyperparameter tuning. Results CMJ was 40.01 ± 8.51 and 30.27 ± 7.29 in the non-fatigue and fatigue conditions, respectively. Across classifiers, fold-mean AUC ranged from 0.655 to 0.846 for seven sensors and from 0.715 to 0.846 for the right forearm. Macro F1 ranged from 0.600 to 0.775 and from 0.655 to 0.775, respectively. Specificity ranged from 0.483 to 0.700 and from 0.550 to 0.650. Code, inclusion decisions, actual inner and outer assignments and held-out predictions are supplied for this new run. Conclusion The results support further investigation of IMU-based condition classification, but do not establish algorithm superiority, sensor equivalence, physiological validity of every recording label, or real-time monitoring performance.

title: An IoT-enabled environmental informatics framework for real-time crop disease detection using attention-driven deep learning
container-title: Frontiers in Environmental Science
90e6e8bd29434b2912cb190bf8bc0a9a88485b6a.abstract: Introduction Crop diseases are a major challenge in agriculture because their early and accurate identification is essential for reducing crop losses and improving productivity. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with deep learning provides an effective approach for automated crop disease monitoring by enabling the collection and analysis of environmental parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. However, accurate fine-grained disease identification remains challenging because of variations in disease symptoms, environmental conditions, and visual characteristics. Methods This study proposes an IoT-enabled deep learning framework for automated crop disease detection and classification. The collected crop images are pre-processed using scaling, normalization, and data augmentation techniques to improve image quality and model generalization. For efficient disease detection, a lightweight attention-driven convolutional neural network-based object detection approach, termed YOLO10-YSTs (You Only Look Once 10-Yield Surveillance Technology), is employed. The framework integrates the real-time detection capability of YOLO10 with an attention mechanism to emphasize disease-relevant regions and a stigmergy-based encoding strategy to enhance feature representation and extraction. In addition, a novel DBGU-LSTM (Dual-Bi-Gated Recurrent Unit with Long Short-Term Memory) architecture is developed for fine-grained crop disease classification. Results The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides effective disease detection, discriminative feature representation, and fine-grained classification. The DBGU-LSTM architecture achieves improved classification performance and training stability compared with the conventional deep learning models considered in the study. Overall, the proposed approach achieves a classification accuracy of 97.99%, demonstrating its effectiveness for automated crop disease recognition. Discussion and conclusion The results indicate that combining IoT-based environmental monitoring with attention-driven deep learning and recurrent feature-learning mechanisms can provide an effective solution for intelligent crop disease detection. The proposed framework enables accurate identification of disease patterns while supporting efficient and automated agricultural monitoring. Therefore, the approach has potential to assist farmers in early disease diagnosis, reduce crop losses, and improve agricultural productivity.

title: Simulation-based evaluation of a modified RRT algorithm for ground-robot navigation in 3D environments
container-title: Frontiers in Robotics and AI
37cf988259cc41c2b51715ebe278bf4c4b76af05.abstract: Autonomous robot navigation requires path-planning algorithms that maintain reliable performance in environments involving dynamic obstacles, changing goals, and complex terrain. This study extends the evaluation of a previously proposed Modified Rapidly-Exploring Random Tree (Modified RRT) algorithm from two-dimensional benchmark maps to robotic navigation scenarios in three-dimensional simulated environments. A simulation-based robotic navigation framework was developed using ROS 2 and Gazebo. Five scenarios were investigated: reconstruction of selected benchmark maps in 3D simulation, dynamic obstacle avoidance, dynamic goal adaptation, warehouse/campus navigation, and slope traversal. The framework incorporates synchronized RGB and depth sensing with point-cloud generation to characterize simulated environmental observations and support the analysis of perception and navigation performance. The global path planner operates in the horizontal x-y plane, while the robot, obstacles, and terrain are represented in the three-dimensional simulation environment. All four planners were evaluated under a common protocol using a shared costmap, collision checker, stopping budget, and parameter-tuning procedure. Modified RRT achieved success rates of up to 98%, reduced navigation completion time by up to 17.6%, and generated paths 10–15% shorter than standard RRT and 2–10% shorter than the next-best planner, Informed RRT* (IRRT*), at the cost of higher planning time than standard RRT in most scenarios. Under ideal sensing, Modified RRT reduced the near-collision rate by up to 74% in structured environments and 63% in unstructured environments relative to standard RRT. When depth noise, missing measurements, latency, and registration errors were introduced, the reductions were 45–61% and 40–52%, respectively. The results indicate that the Modified RRT sampling mechanisms can improve path-planning and navigation performance across the evaluated simulation scenarios. The findings also show that perception imperfections reduce the near-collision-rate improvements observed under ideal sensing. Overall, this study presents a simulation-based framework for evaluating planar global path planning, robot navigation execution, and simulated multimodal perception in three-dimensional robotic environments.

title: Clinical-priority task orchestration and verified safety supervision for a physician-directed ward-rounding robot: a simulation-based feasibility study
container-title: Frontiers in Robotics and AI
75e76a9638e56799c26399a950509379264bc348.abstract: Introduction A ward-rounding robot that accepts orders at the level of clinical intent becomes a shared clinical resource: several clinicians may hold outstanding requests of differing urgency, and execution is punctuated by confirmation gates at which the robot waits on a human and by engagement steps that cannot safely be interrupted. This paper formalizes the resulting scheduling problem together with the safety layer that it necessitates. Methods We present (i) a task model in which an intent-level order expands into primitives carrying resource locks, physician confirmation gates, and an explicit interruptibility partition; (ii) the Clinical-Priority Scheduler (CP-Sched), which combines urgency weighting, aging, travel awareness, and class-relative escalation and preempts only at safe interruption points; and (iii) a safety supervisor specified as a network of timed automata and verified exhaustively for a single robot serving one order at a time, with independent reproduction in the TLA+ model checker TLC. All task timings in the 1,590 discrete-event simulation runs are modeling assumptions, not hardware measurements. Results Across 1,080 runs spanning two ward sizes and three utilization levels, CP-Sched reduced the 95th-percentile time for urgent orders to bedside from 347 s to 215 s at moderate utilization, a 38% reduction relative to the strongest of four baselines; all comparisons survived Holm’s correction at p &lt; 0.0001 under both the paired Wilcoxon signed-rank and unpaired Mann–Whitney tests (rank-biserial effect sizes: 0.93–1.00 paired, 0.66–0.93 unpaired). A further 510 runs showed that aging alone cannot bound the waiting time and that escalation at a fixed absolute horizon restores a guarantee only by inflating the urgent tail at saturation. All five clinical invariants hold under the supervisor and each is violable without it, so none is vacuous. Runtime enforcement eliminated all 757 unsafe interruptions observed in the unshielded ablation at a cost of 2.1–35.4 s in the median urgent tail. Discussion The enforcement cost is small but systematic at light and moderate loads and undetectable at saturation, which supports keeping the safety layer independent of the scheduling policy. The formal guarantee covers a single-order model, and absolute timings require calibration on a physical platform.

title: AI-enabled talent analytics and workforce agility in manufacturing SMEs: the mediating role of human-AI collaboration and the moderating role of technostress resilience
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
7a00163c0cbc23dd1aec7c74b74a435e94d6dc53.abstract: Introduction Small and medium-sized enterprises increasingly use AI-enabled talent analytics (AITA) to support workforce planning and adaptive performance, yet the mechanisms linking AITA to workforce agility (WA) remain underexplored. This study examines human-AI collaboration (HAIC) as a mediating mechanism and technostress resilience (TR) as a psychological resource and boundary condition. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 334 owners, HR managers, and operations/production heads from Pakistani manufacturing SMEs actively using AITA. Exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling, 5,000 bootstrap resamples, and moderation analyses were used to assess the measurement and structural models. Results AITA was positively associated with WA, and HAIC showed a significant indirect association between AITA and WA, consistent with partial statistical mediation. TR was positively associated with WA and significantly strengthened the AITA-WA association. The exploratory TR x HAIC interaction was not statistically significant. Discussion The findings position AITA as a socio-technical work-design resource whose association with agility depends on human interpretation, collaborative routines, and psychological capacity to manage technology-related demands. Because the data are cross-sectional and based on one knowledgeable respondent per firm, the results should be interpreted as manager-perceived associations rather than causal effects.

title: Processing speed accounts for the discriminative power of a brief smartphone Go/No-Go task among individuals with multiple sclerosis
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
ddd8c4be6b87b29f19ee2f83cbf8531910f33374.abstract: Background Identifying and longitudinally measuring cognitive decline remains challenging because traditional assessments rely largely on episodic, in-person administration of analog scales by trained examiners. Smartphone technology offers a scalable alternative for extracting distinct digital biomarkers from continuous sensor and event streams. Following the integration of several cognitive modules into the self-administered Neurological Functions Test Suite (NeuFun-TS), this study evaluates the clinical utility and incremental validity of a final candidate module: a brief (30 s per hand) equiprobable (50/50) Go/No-Go (50/50GNG) choice-reaction task. Methods We analyzed 3,270 quality-controlled 30-s runs from 303 participants, with primary analyses focused on the first run per hand (488 observations; 18,650 stimuli) across 34 healthy donors (HDs) and 213 multiple sclerosis (MS) participants. From the raw event stream, we screened 16 candidate metrics and retained 10 based on their psychometric properties. Using these 10 metrics, we evaluated diagnostic group separation, test–retest reliability, correlations with clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) benchmarks, and incremental validity over existing digital modules: the randomized Symbol Digit Modalities Test (rSDMT) and the Motor Sequencing Test (MST), using paired observations. Results Although nine of the 10 outcomes significantly separated HD from MS and seven separated relapsing–remitting from progressive MS subtypes (all adjusted p &lt; 0.05), discriminative power was driven almost entirely by response latency rather than by commission errors or inhibitory metrics. Response latency accounted for the majority of its full-run separation within the first 12 s. Multi-predictor composite scores offered no diagnostic advantage over reaction time alone. Furthermore, the Go/No-Go task showed poor-to-moderate longitudinal test–retest reliability and did not provide incremental clinical value over existing modules. Conclusion In this brief implementation, the smartphone Go/No-Go task served as a choice-reaction-time measure reflecting processing-speed impairment in MS; however, its discriminative capability was redundant with reaction-time metrics already implemented on the platform, so the module was excluded from NeuFun-TS. These findings do not generalize to longer continuous performance tests, whose error-based measures require many more stimuli than a 30-s run provides.

title: From Learner Modeling to Human–AI Co-Regulation: A Systematic Scoping Review of Adaptive Generative AI in Personalized Learning
container-title: F1000Research
4aa94bffdc8347f6dcb33ca8bcd4a4f0a10bd6b5.abstract: Abstract* Background Adaptive generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to personalize learning, yet evidence remains fragmented across system design, human–AI co-regulation, self-regulated learning (SRL), sustained behavioral outcomes, and ethics. This systematic scoping review mapped these dimensions in a single synthesis. Methods We searched Dimensions, ERIC, IEEE Xplore, Lens, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science on 5 May 2026. Of 3,084 records identified, 95 journal articles published between 2023 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. Evidence was synthesized using descriptive mapping, form–function co-occurrence analysis, and qualitative comparative synthesis. Results Adaptive GenAI was most commonly instantiated as conversational tutors, generative content personalizers, and hybrid feedback systems, with adaptive feedback, content adaptation, diagnostic analysis, scaffolding, and progress tracking emerging as the dominant functions. Conceptualizations of human–AI co-adaptation were less mature: most studies framed AI primarily as a responsive regulator, with feedback-loop acceleration and metacognitive prompting more frequently articulated than internalization, behavioral reinforcement, or social modeling. Empirical effects were concentrated in proximal SRL outcomes, particularly forethought and performance, while evidence for self-reflection, affective regulation, transfer, stable self-efficacy, persistence, and learning habits was much thinner. Ethical evaluation likewise remained uneven, emphasizing feedback quality, pedagogical validity, well-being, autonomy, motivation, inclusivity, and agency, while transparency, data minimization, scaffold fading, developmental suitability, manipulation risk, and ethical nudging were addressed far less often. Conclusions Adaptive GenAI is more mature in technical personalization and proximal SRL support than in reciprocal co-regulation, durable behavior change, and integrated ethical governance. Future research should test whether regulatory gains persist beyond immediate AI support and develop stronger frameworks for governing learner influence and dependency.

title: Beyond AI Assisted Creativity: Digital Storytelling for Orchestrating Human AI Co-Creation in Higher Education
e99f30d7f1b28e01f3c862cdf7b7188266881f8c.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence is increasingly used to support creativity in higher education, yet its educational value may depend on how human and AI contributions are pedagogically coordinated. This study examined whether digital storytelling can orchestrate human–AI co-creation while preserving students’ creative agency. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design involved 180 higher education students assigned by intact cohorts to orchestrated human–AI digital storytelling or conventional AI-assisted digital storytelling. After controlling for baseline performance, the experimental group demonstrated significantly higher creative competency, F(1,177) = 10.95, p = .001, partial η² = .058, alongside stronger human–AI co-creation quality, creative agency, critical evaluation, and creative ownership. Regression pathways further linked co-creation quality and creative agency to creative competency. These findings position digital storytelling as a pedagogical orchestration environment that shifts AI-supported creativity from output generation toward intentional, evaluative, and human-directed co-creation.

title: Deepnude Forensics: Detection, Attribution, and Defense Against AI-Generated Intimate Image Abuse
0f4bb517c9bd7a8ccd6b1198894e4224f535566c.abstract: The commoditization of open-weight generative image models has collapsed the technical and eco- nomic barriers to producing non-consensual intimate imagery (“deepnudes”) and, in its most severe form, synthetic Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM). Unlike photographic abuse material, synthetic content is unbounded in volume, detaches from any specific victim-identification signal, and sys- tematically defeats the perceptual-hash infrastructure (PhotoDNA, Project Arachnid, INTERPOL ICSE) on which global child-protection operations depend. Building on our prior work on machine- learning deep nude detection, this paper first develops the theoretical foundations of deep nude detection techniques—decomposing the task into explicitness, manipulation, and subject-attribute factors with a decision- and information-theoretic account of multi-cue fusion—and then presents an end-to-end, defense-oriented framework with cybersecurity at its core that (i) formally charac- terizes the open “uncensored” generation ecosystem and the model-level mechanisms by which safety alignment is stripped, treated strictly as a threat model rather than a recipe; (ii) formalizes the reverse engineering of generative pipelines for attribution—tracing a synthetic artifact back to its originating model family through diffusion reconstruction error, latent and weight-space fingerprints, spectral forensics, membership inference, and foundation-model feature forensics; (iii) specifies a multi-stream detection architecture, with algorithms, designed to be trained without possessing illegal material, using a curated-benign public track with suspect material confined to accredited enclaves, benign adult/synthetic proxies, and a privacy-preserving federated protocol; (iv) analyzes preemptive defenses—adversarial immunization (PhotoGuard, Glaze, Nightshade), data poisoning, and prove- nance watermarking (C2PA, SynthID, Stable Signature)—together with their documented robustness failures under purification and adaptive attack; and (v) maps the whole to operational law-enforcement workflows (INTERPOL, NCMEC, Canadian Centre for Child Protection), to a multi-jurisdiction legal analysis, and to forensic-admissibility and chain-of-custody constraints. We contribute a layered risk taxonomy, a reproducible evaluation protocol and benchmark design with explicit ethical controls, a cybersecurity-hardening checklist for the model supply chain, an illustrative (benign) end-to-end walkthrough, and a prioritized research and policy agenda. Our central thesis is that durable defense requires shifting from post hoc content matching toward generative-pipeline forensics: detecting, attributing, and raising the cost of synthesis at the model and provenance layers. We position this work as a critical synthesis, a proposed reference architecture, and an evaluation protocol rather than an empirically validated system: the figures are illustrative of the protocol, not measured results, and we mark throughout what is established in prior work, what is proposed here, and what remains to be validated—particularly for the hashing, attribution, and privacy guarantees, whose scope we state conservatively.

title: Case Study on the Production Deployment of an AI Powered Data Warehouse Management Service
7f4b8016661c384910ba92d7a947a397d4c3a0b9.abstract: This paper assesses the performance of a big language model (LLM) driven agent for the data warehouse (DW) when used during production for five months. The service translates users' conversational requests to typed operation primalies, and deals with their execution via semantic constraints, static verification, cost estimation and staged execution, as well as automatic rollback. It performed 3, 870 operations, including 1, 260 pipeline creations (32.6%) and 2, 610 other management tasks (67.4%). Logistic regression revealed that for every added planning step, the odds of task success decreased (OR = 0.81: 95% CI: 0.76–0.87); and the 0.89 point estimate for each additional schema table and the 0.42 estimate for schema evolution vs. schema pipeline creation. The median was 6.4 minutes for agent tasks, and 2.1 business days for work orders handled by the engineer (412), but undocumented matching and time boundaries make it non-sensical to make a causal comparison. A total of 42 rollbacks were made, with 3.2-minutes average recovery time with no manual intervention. The actual resource saved from a downgrade or rejection of a plan is based on the number of slot-hours that are estimated to be used, which came to an estimated 210, 000 slot-hours. Of these, the completion rate was 87.1% with validation and 79.6% without and 23 (4.8%) were identified as possible unsafe operations in this offline 480 work order ablation study. The results can then be used for auditable execution controls, and schema evolution will still have to be audited manually.

title: Auditable Feasibility-Gated Command Admission for Language-Conditioned Robotic Task Allocation
container-title: Journal of Intelligent & Robotic Systems
325c4d316e4a33021ff7d0ec978dbf77a08d9459.abstract: Abstract Language-conditioned robotic systems can map natural-language instructions to plausible skills, yet a semantically matched skill may still be non-executable on a particular robot. This paper presents QER–HFV, an auditable command-admission layer for robotic task allocation under semantic uncertainty. The layer expands the top-ranked skill hypotheses into explicit skill–robot candidates, checks capability, resource, communication, workspace, policy, and interface constraints, and records admission, rejection, or escalation outcomes with blocking reasons before any soft ranking is applied. In a reproducible decision-layer benchmark, 4-bit semantic memory preserves the FP32 allocation-success proxy to the displayed precision while reducing normalized semantic-memory cost to 12.5%. Hard feasibility verification lowers the single-step non-executable allocation rate from 0.580 for semantic-only retrieval to 0.108 for Semantic+HFV and 0.084 for the full gate. In a 1200-step online replay, the post-gate resource-aware ranker improves the mission-success proxy from 0.651 to 0.821, while windowed strong baselines clarify that the ranker is not a general batched scheduler. Execution-facing tests further show 100/108 executable successes and 72/72 correct infeasible-command rejections in a controlled tabletop Hiwonder xArm 1S study; overall correct handling is 172/180 (0.956; 95% Wilson CI [0.915, 0.977]). The simplified Robot Operating System (ROS)/Gazebo comparison records no collisions or infeasible false executions for QER–HFV. Targeted boundary experiments additionally show 0.9942 mean cosine preservation for 4-bit embeddings, extend candidate-fleet scaling to 80 robots per task, improve correct handling of 300 ambiguous/vague commands from 0.6267 to 0.8600 (paired difference +0.233; 95% bootstrap CI [0.167, 0.300]) with an escalation policy, and complete a 72-hour Raspberry Pi 5 replay with 259,200 decisions, two recoverable events, and no crashes or restarts. The results support QER–HFV as a reusable pre-command admissibility interface rather than a formal safety certificate or global scheduling optimizer.

title: Optimizing AI-Derived CAC Volume Thresholds on Non-Gated Chest CT for Detection of Actionable Coronary Artery Calcium
container-title: Journal of Thoracic Imaging
3c9ed0cddc3373928643ecb34d2f2050b4181c7f.abstract: Purpose: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) visually estimated on non-electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated chest CTs is reported inconsistently, limiting identification of high-risk individuals. Although automated AI-derived CAC scoring offers the potential to standardize reporting and improve reliability, this method warrants rigorous validation. Materials and Methods: Three hundred thirty-two patients (59% female, median age 62) who underwent a non-gated chest CT within 1-year of a dedicated cardiac CT with Agatston’s CAC score (CACscore) were identified between 2016 and 2022. AI-Rad Companion (Siemens) was used to compute CAC volume (AI-CACvol). AI-CACvol performance was compared with radiologists’ qualitative CAC reports (H-CACqual) using optimized thresholds for identifying actionable CAC. Model performance was further validated in a postimplementation population. Results: Median AI-CACvol was 20.3 mm³ (IQR 0-188.65), strongly correlated with CACscore (Spearman ρ=0.91, 95% CI: 0.88-0.94); median 31.55 Agatston Units (AU), IQR: 0 to 250). Agreement with CACscore was higher for AI-CACvol versus H-CACqual (weighted kappa 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84, 0.91; vs. 0.85, 95% CI: 0.82, 0.88; P =0.022). At a cutoff of 70 mm³, AI-CACvol demonstrated superior sensitivity compared with H-CACqual for detecting CAC≥100 AU, with greater sensitivity (95% vs. 75%) and comparable specificity (92% vs. 94%). In a validation cohort of 39 patients (64% female, median age 67 y), median CACscore was 43 AU (IQR 0-215) and median AI-CACvol 29.7 mm³ (IQR: 0 to 219.4). The same 70 mm³ cutoff achieved 100% sensitivity and 88% specificity for CAC≥100 AU (n=13). Conclusion: AI-derived CAC volume from non-gated chest CTs correlates strongly with reference CAC scores, showing high sensitivity at actionable thresholds. This supports potential opportunistic screening, though impact on outcomes requires study.

title: Emotional Differences Between Human- and AI-Generated Texts
e4113200a35dbe821d2c547448efdaf50b4b4a80.abstract: Abstract AI is often conceptualized primarily as a cognitive tool, with its outputs assumed to convey information rather than emotional expression. This study challenges that assumption by systematically comparing the emotional characteristics of human- and AI-generated text across 25 languages using five emotional measures: sentiment polarity, sentiment categories, Valence-Arousal-Dominance (VAD), basic emotion classification, and fine-grained emotion classification. The results reveal a systematic difference in the emotional profiles of AI- and human-generated text across languages. Compared with human writing, AI-generated text generally exhibits higher valence, arousal, and dominance, while expressing fewer negative emotions. These findings extend our understanding of the affective characteristics of generative AI and highlight important implications for applications in customer service, marketing, personalized communication, and AI-generated content detection.

title: AI Anxiety, Digital Overload, and Technostress in a Polycrisis Context: A Moderated Mediation Study of Emotional Exhaustion and Psychological Well-Being Across Four Industry Sectors
287811c3d509c854883b0a89f89875e174e3e465.abstract: Abstract Background : The concurrent occurrence of AI-induced disruption, rapid post-pandemic digitalization, and macroeconomic instability has fundamentally reshaped the psychological demands of modern work, creating a polycrisis. Staff members in digital work environments experience rising AI anxiety, digital overload, and technostress, but how such polycrisis-related demands impact PWB through these mechanisms and the extent to which personal resources may act as a shield against such an effect has not been comprehensively understood yet. Based on the assumptions of the Job Demands-Resources model, the present study examines a model of moderated mediation, wherein emotional exhaustion mediates the demand-PWB association, and psychological capital (PsyCap) moderates and strengthens PWB. Methods: Cross-sectional surveys using six psychometric scales were conducted among 340 full-time workers from sectors such as IT, Health care, Education, and Banking/Finance. Hypotheses regarding the structure were validated using CB-SEM with 5,000 bias corrected bootstraps whereas sector-specific MGA and fsQCA identified configurations related to lower PWB. Results: All three job demands were able to predict emotional exhaustion: AI anxiety (β = 0.396, p < 0.001), digital overload (β = 0.333, p < 0.001), and technostress (β = 0.318, p < 0.001), explaining 32.1% of the variance. Emotional exhaustion fully mediated the influence of all three variables on PWB (β = -0.434, p < 0.001) through bootstrapped indirect effects. PsyCap had a significant direct effect on PWB (β = 0.460, p < 0.001) for all four sectors. Through MGA, sector-specific differences emerged with regard to AI anxiety, which was more important in the IT sector, digital overload in Healthcare and Banking/Finance, and technostress in the Education sector. In fsQCA, digital overload was found as a necessary condition for low PWB (consistency = 0.909), where there were three configurations, each required low PsyCap as a boundary condition (solution consistency = 0.841, coverage = 0.573). Conclusions: Demands resulting from polycrisis are linked to low PWB mainly because of emotional exhaustion, and demand salience differs significantly across sectors. Low PsyCap functions as a universal boundary condition for low levels of well-being. Organisations should prioritise PsyCap development as an industry-invariant approach in addition to demand management, which takes into account the characteristics of the job.

title:
How Much Should Artificial Intelligence Do Without a Physician?
An Autonomy Scale for AI Agents in Solid Organ Transplantation.
70f263f55880c20a80acd3b4a4d6e6cdd9d0b4c1.abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence in surgery and transplantation is moving from tools that give a single output toward software agents that retrieve data, plan several steps, use other tools, and take actions. Existing autonomy classifications and device frameworks address physical autonomy and fixed-function outputs well, but they do not specify oversight for systems whose behavior depends on intermediate decisions and tool use. Methods: We developed a governance framework by combining Yang and colleagues’ six-level autonomy scale with an agentic overlay covering tool use, data access, action scope, and persistence. We mapped the framework against current U.S. guidance for AI-enabled devices and the American Medical Association’s 2026 framework for agentic AI. We illustrated its application with four worked examples from solid organ transplantation: donor procurement, machine perfusion, and post-transplant monitoring with cell-free DNA and donor-specific antibodies, assigning each plausible agent function a level and governance tier and identifying the controls that apply. Results: The framework assigns each agent function to one of four governance tiers based on autonomy level, reversibility, and consequence. Tier A (levels 0 to 1) requires accuracy testing and query logging. Tier B (level 2) requires bounded limits, full action logs, and drift monitoring. Tier C (level 3) requires clinician approval of each consequential action, prospective evaluation, and named accountability. Tier D (levels 4 to 5) is not recommended for high-consequence decisions in the current evidence period. In the transplant example, the organ-acceptance decision is assigned to Tier C with clinician decision authority, allocation pairing is excluded from agent action, and a protocol-defined perfusion-time limit is enforced deterministically outside the model. Across the four examples, clinicians approve each consequential action, no viability marker drives acceptance alone, and automatic immunosuppression changes are excluded. Conclusions: Oversight of agents in transplant care should scale with autonomy, reversibility, and consequence rather than with product category. Binding rules should be enforced in deterministic code rather than left to model reasoning. Prospective evaluation is required before any agent in a high-consequence transplant decision advances beyond Tier C.

title: Please Forward this Postdigital Feminist Chain-Letter on Living with AI in Higher Education
container-title: Postdigital Science and Education
97107e75549a7b1d23b73a701cdc9f4ca9237854.abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) enters higher education within established hierarchies of knowledge and expertise, becoming entangled with judgments about who sounds authoritative and which forms of writing carry weight. Those judgments were gendered, long before GenAI arrived. Drawing on feminist postdigital inquiry and collaborative, experimental approaches to knowledge production, this article reports a chain-letter experiment. Thirteen academics who identify as women or gender-diverse, from nine countries, write in relation to the letters preceding their own. The chain letter produces knowledge through response, so that each letter is partial and the argument accumulates between them. Read together, the letters describe a persistent need to defend expertise within a field shaped by masculine norms of authority, and the frustration and exhaustion this produces. Authors variously report work intensifying rather than easing, critique of GenAI tools being reframed as failures of individual users, and a sense that AI-assisted writing diminishes what makes teaching and research pleasurable. Their positions differ, with some refusing these tools while others work closely with them. At the same time, the exchange brings solidarity, hope and relief, and the discovery that these difficulties are structural as well as personal. The letters suggest that GenAI makes long-standing, gendered questions about expertise and working conditions more pressing, and that these remain shared and unfinished. The article closes with an open invitation to join a feminist and postdigital conversation about GenAI in research and education.

title: A Teacher's Concerns about AI in Primary School: Critical Thinking, Personal Data and the Fear of Cognitive Dependence
container-title: Advances in Mobile Learning Educational Research
48daf9f5949effd20204e7775dffc33ae168a630.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is already part of pupils' everyday lives and of school life. Written from the perspective of a primary school teacher and principal, this perspective paper examines three interrelated concerns of the author herself. These concerns arose from a wish to protect her pupils and led her to study the topic for her own professional development and to help her colleagues make teaching safer and better. They concern developing critical thinking towards AI-generated answers, protecting the personal data of minors, and the fear that excessive assistance from AI will weaken pupils' thinking. Drawing on a narrative, non-systematic review of recent research on cognitive offloading, the European and Greek regulatory framework, and illustrative examples from the author's own teaching practice and lesson scenarios for primary school, it argues that the fear of cognitive dependence is a plausible concern rather than an established finding for primary school pupils. The available evidence, which comes mainly from adolescents and adults, suggests that the form of AI support (whether it replaces the learner's effort or scaffolds it) may be an important factor. AI is regarded throughout as a valuable tool; the risk lies mainly in the way it is used. The classroom examples come from ordinary lessons whose only purpose was to teach pupils to question AI answers and to protect themselves when using AI. They were not planned as research, no research data were collected, and they are offered as the author's practitioner reflections, not as findings. The author's classroom experience illustrates that such activities can be implemented in ordinary primary school lessons, but their effects on pupils' critical thinking have not yet been evaluated. The paper relates the three concerns to long-standing educational principles, in particular Socratic questioning, Dewey's reflective thought and Vygotskian scaffolding. On this basis, it proposes a simple, as yet untested three-step classroom protocol (``think -- ask -- check''), age-appropriate data protection rules, and a role for school leadership, and outlines questions for future research.

title: Slip Detection for Robotic Grasping with LSTM and TCN: Edge AI Evaluation on Embedded Platforms
container-title: Journal of Intelligent & Robotic Systems
6055ae5b60252dbfa2a2679fdf1a98b6863dffdc.abstract: Abstract Reliable object grasping is essential for robotic manipulation in real-world environments, such as manufacturing and assembly. Undetected slips can lead to task failure, while effective slip detection enables robots to adapt their grip in real time, improving robustness and safety. In earlier work, we showed that Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks can be deployed on edge devices for real-time slip detection, but that study used a manually labelled dataset and reported only accuracy and F 1 scores, which limited comparisons of model–hardware combinations. In this work, we collect a large slip detection dataset using a Fin Ray-inspired soft gripper with tactile Force Sensing Linear Potentiometers (FSLPs), a Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensor, and an encoder, to generate slip and no-slip labels from automatically estimated ArUco marker poses. We design and evaluate lightweight LSTM and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) architectures trained on sensor sequences and compare their performance on a held-out test set. We then deploy the selected models on several embedded platforms, including Nvidia Jetson AGX Orin, Google Coral Dev Board Micro, ESP32, and Arduino Nicla Sense ME, and benchmark accuracy, F 1 score, average inference time, and estimated average energy per inference. The results show that accurate slip detection is feasible even on constrained microcontroller- class hardware, and provide a more comprehensive comparison of model and hardware choices than previous work.

title: Sustained improvement, persistent limits
container-title: Australian and International Journal of Rural Education
f528ccc99309e143a4c9f152db785b153da375c8.abstract: Despite a growing body of literature on instructional leadership in South African schools, there is limited research examining how such leadership is sustained over extended periods or interrogating the structural limits of what even committed principals can achieve in chronically under-resourced rural contexts. This qualitative single case study examines the instructional leadership practices of a principal who has led a rural secondary school in South Africa's North West Province for 25 years, transforming its Grade 12 pass rate from 48% to consistently above 70%. Data were generated through an in-depth semi-structured interview to explore practices which enabled sustained improvement, which contextual conditions constrained those practices and what broader lessons the case offers for understanding instructional leadership under conditions of persistent disadvantage. The findings reveal that sustained improvement was enabled by a concrete performance orientation, deliberate cultivation of learner aspirations, direct involvement in teaching and learning and a distinctively interpersonal approach to school climate and staff motivation. However, the study also surfaces the significant structural limits within which this leadership was enacted, including chronic teacher absenteeism, learner attrition, over-age learner dilemmas, departmental dysfunction and resource scarcity. The study argues that instructional leadership in such contexts is contextually bounded rather than universally transformative and that sustained school performance cannot be fully understood without accounting for what the system failed to provide.

title: Interpretable Alzheimer's disease diagnosis based on distance-aware rotary attention with multi-scale cross-complementarity
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
db79042e3aed8fced742b0732a1fc5c78ce3e1b2.abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by a progressive decline in memory and cognitive function. Existing methods fail to comprehensively capture the multi-level structural variations across different brain regions, making it difficult to provide reliable diagnostic evidence and pathological insights for clinical use. Methods The interpretable algorithm with distance-aware rotary attention and multi-scale cross-complementary (IDRA-MCC) is first proposed to address the limitations in AD diagnosis and improve the interpretability of model discrimination. The study included 604 subjects from the ADNI dataset (207 AD, 195 cognitively normal (CN), 74 progressive mild cognitive impairment (pMCI), and 128 stable mild cognitive impairment (sMCI) and 196 subjects from the OASIS dataset (105 AD and 91 CN). First, standardized preprocessing is applied to reduce inter-subject variability. Then, a dual-scale patch feature modeling was adopted to construct a distance-aware rotary attention (DRA) module that can explicitly encode relative positional dependencies and sequence-level locality, enhancing the perception of key brain regions. Meanwhile, a multi-scale cross-complementary (MCC) module is designed to achieve cross-scale feature interaction and fusion, capturing multi-level pathological patterns. Finally, an adaptive token aggregation (ATA) mechanism is designed to highlight discriminative responses, and anatomical backtracking is achieved through token-weight visualization, thereby improving model interpretability. Results Interpretability analysis shows that the identified high-response regions are highly consistent with brain regions previously associated with AD and MCI progression, including the precuneus in the pMCI vs. sMCI task. Conclusions IDRA-MCC achieves both high performance and interpretability across different tasks on the ADNI and OASIS datasets, showing potential for AD-related progression assessment and future clinical applications.

title: Prophylactic oxytocin infusion rate and adequate uterine tone in repeat cesarean delivery: a randomized dose-response trial
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
b31e043f2239bb5798dac8983381fd2e75bb43de.abstract: Background The dose-response relationship of an infusion-only prophylactic oxytocin regimen in women undergoing repeat cesarean delivery remains uncertain. We evaluated adequate uterine tone at six dose levels (saline placebo at 0 IU/h and five active infusion rates of 4–20 IU/h) and estimated the originally targeted ED90. Methods In this single-center, randomized, double-blind dose-finding trial, 120 women aged 21–34 years undergoing elective repeat cesarean delivery before labor were assigned to saline placebo (0 IU/h) or oxytocin infusion at 4, 8, 12, 16, or 20 IU/h immediately after fetal delivery, without an initial bolus. The primary outcome was adequate uterine tone (score ≥ 7 on a 0–10 scale) at 3 min, assessed before rescue uterotonics. Logistic regression was the primary dose-response model; probit regression, an asymmetric complementary log-log model, isotonic regression, and assumptions for the two missing primary outcomes were examined in additional analyses. Results Primary outcome data were available for 118 women. The observed adequate-tone rate increased from 5.3% (1/19) in the placebo (0 IU/h) group to 90.0% (18/20) at 20 IU/h. In the primary logistic analysis, the estimated ED50 was 9.92 IU/h (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.72–12.09 IU/h), and the post hoc ED80 was 16.62 IU/h (95% CI, 13.93–20.80 IU/h). The logistic model-estimated ED90 was 20.54 IU/h (95% CI, 17.00–26.50 IU/h), with a point estimate above the highest tested rate of 20 IU/h. The requirement for rescue oxytocin decreased with increasing infusion rate ( P &lt; 0.001). Estimated blood loss and recorded potential oxytocin-related adverse events did not differ significantly among groups; this trial was not powered for hemorrhage or uncommon adverse events. Conclusion In this selected population, adequate uterine tone increased across the tested dose levels of 0–20 IU/h. The model-estimated ED90 point estimate lay outside the tested range and depended on extrapolation. An infusion rate around 20 IU/h should be viewed as a candidate for further evaluation, not a definitive recommended dose. Findings should not be extrapolated to bolus-plus-infusion regimens or laboring and emergency cesarean deliveries. Clinical Trial Registration https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=39583 , Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR1900023469, registered on May 30, 2019.

title: AI in communication education: a sociotechnical perspective on algorithmic automation and human mediation in Ecuador
container-title: Frontiers in Political Science
e87192d8e8ba84d92a7130d3881f914a8186cbc2.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence is transforming higher education and professional communication, creating a tension between technological automation and human critical thinking. In teaching communication, this tension highlights the need to rethink the skills students should develop as AI becomes increasingly integrated into academic and professional practice, especially the ability to use AI strategically without losing human judgment, ethical reasoning, and decision-making in their context. Methodology The study uses an exploratory-descriptive, cross-sectional, mixed-methods design combining quantitative and qualitative evidence to explore how students and program directors in Ecuador perceive AI integration in communication education. It surveyed 230 students across seven institutions and conducted 12 semi-structured interviews with directors. Survey analysis identified AI usage patterns, while thematic analysis of interviews focused on benefits, barriers, ethics, and priorities. Initially, Pearson's chi-square test examined associations with sociodemographics, but it was unreliable due to low expected cell counts. Findings are presented as descriptive patterns, not inferential or population-level conclusions. Results Students report using AI mainly for communication (28.70%), trend prediction and audience analysis (13.04%), and segmentation (9.57%). Four AI applications were identified: operational efficiency, strategic analysis, audience management, and digital optimization. The gender-based chi-square test was inconclusive ( χ 2 = 12.728; df = 14; p = 0.548), with over 50% of cells having fewer than 5 responses. Among directors and coordinators, common uses included content generation, assisted writing, research, data analysis, and audience engagement. The thematic analysis revealed four patterns: operational efficiency, decision-making, automation vs. human judgment, and training needs. Discussion and conclusions Communication students in Ecuador mainly use AI to improve efficiency and effectiveness, with key applications in trend prediction, audience analysis, and segmentation. Program leaders see AI as useful in content creation, research, and audience engagement. The study identifies four AI use areas: operational efficiency, strategic analysis, audience management, and digital optimization. The study highlights tension between automation and human judgment, stressing the continued importance of critical thinking, creativity, ethics, and context. It proposes a framework balancing AI automation with human input to support strategic communication decisions.

title: From emotional comfort to relational investment in generative AI companionship: evidence from SEM and fsQCA
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
6c8384f16783c106639bef8d6d4125fd000ef3d8.abstract: With the rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI), chatbots are evolving from instrumental assistants into emotionally responsive companions. This study develops a low-friction relational process model to examine the relationships linking generative AI companionship with emotional relief and positive social investment. AI emotional responsiveness, non-judgemental interaction, and memory-based continuity were conceptualized as interaction conditions, while perceived being understood, deep self-disclosure, and synthetic attachment were specified as psychological mechanisms. Structural equation modeling (SEM), bootstrap mediation analysis, moderation analysis, and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) were employed to analyse 765 valid responses from generative AI chatbot users. The SEM results show that non-judgemental interaction exhibits the most consistent pattern of associations with perceived being understood, deep self-disclosure, synthetic attachment, emotional relief, and positive social investment. Perceived being understood and synthetic attachment show relatively stable mediating patterns, whereas deep self-disclosure is significantly associated with emotional relief but shows a less consistent association with positive social investment. Perceived AI safety and self-disclosure habit play differentiated moderating roles. The fsQCA findings reveal three configurations for high emotional relief and four configurations for high positive social investment, complementing the SEM results. This study provides a systematic account of generative AI companionship and offers implications for safer and relationship-oriented AI design.

title: Audience appraisal of AI generated visual media across viewers and scenes
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
bfe9ed4d52f73ab8b93caff7355f18ed32b05f34.abstract: How do audiences relate the authenticity, emotional meaning, trustworthiness, and acceptability of AI-generated visual media? For cultural exhibitions and other uses of reconstructed pasts, emotional appeal and perceived credibility need not coincide, and audience responses may differ across scenes. We examine these questions through an appraisal-oriented account of AI-generated reconstructions of urban everyday life. Study 1 ( N = 513) used Mode-A composite PLS-SEM with 24 items representing eight constructs to estimate viewer-level evaluation associations. Ten of eleven hypothesized paths were supported. Nostalgic response was associated with acceptance intention, but its hypothesized positive association with trust was not supported after perceived authenticity and AI traces were considered. Study 2 independently compared baseline and treated versions of 12 scenes using a nonrandomized design (primary N = 780). The overall perceived-authenticity difference was not significant (0.010, 95% CI [−0.033, 0.052], p = 0.656). Perceived AI traces were higher in the treated group in the fixed-scene analysis (0.060, 95% CI [0.025, 0.096], BH-adjusted p = 0.007), but the interval crossed zero in a post hoc scene-level condition random-slope model (0.060, 95% CI [−0.098, 0.219]). Condition-by-scene interactions were significant for all eight constructs. Together, the studies show why the appraisal of AI-generated pasts should distinguish emotional reception from trust and examine particular proposed scenes rather than rely on a single average authenticity rating.

title: Generative AI feedback use and deep cognitive engagement in university EFL writing: a mixed-methods study of autonomy, self-regulated learning, and AI literacy
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
afb75769dc989373555c79649418b5d149ca608a.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to obtain feedback in English as a foreign language (EFL) writing, but its educational significance depends on how learners interpret and regulate that feedback. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory and self-regulated learning theory, this explanatory sequential mixed-methods study examined an AI-supported motivated self-regulated learning framework using a cross-sectional survey of 486 university EFL students and follow-up interviews with 20 students. Structural equation modeling identified a positive direct association between reported AI feedback use and deep cognitive engagement, together with a positive indirect statistical association through learning autonomy and self-regulated learning. The AI feedback use–autonomy association was stronger at higher modeled levels of AI literacy. Interview accounts described feedback-related control, critical evaluation, and awareness of AI limitations, alongside contrasting experiences of rapid polishing and careful evaluation despite limited familiarity with AI. Integration of the two strands highlighted variation in how learners evaluated and incorporated feedback. These self-report findings do not establish temporal ordering or causal effects. They identify learner agency, strategic regulation, and critical evaluation as relevant considerations for future investigations of AI-supported writing.

title: Information overload, cognitive fatigue, and postgraduates’ intention to use generative artificial intelligence for English academic writing: the role of lower-order cognitive offloading
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
44519a3982b4f3a7618933a7c685ba32b093e792.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence (AI) returns large amounts of information that postgraduates must judge and integrate when they write in English. The stressor-strain-outcome framework suggests that such overload strains cognitive resources and weakens plans for further use. This study tested whether cognitive fatigue links perceived information overload with later behavioral intention to use AI for English academic writing. It also tested whether lower-order cognitive offloading, such as having AI summarize papers, conditions the overload-fatigue association. Methods In total, 475 Chinese master’s and doctoral students who used AI for English academic writing completed three surveys at two-week intervals. Overload and offloading were measured at Time 1, fatigue at Time 2, and intention at Time 3. A moderated mediation model adjusted for baseline fatigue, baseline intention, and AI-use frequency. Results Higher perceived information overload accompanied higher cognitive fatigue 2 weeks later and weaker behavioral intention 4 weeks later, net of baseline levels. Cognitive fatigue was associated with weaker later intention and carried part of the overload-intention association. The overload-fatigue association was weaker at higher levels of lower-order cognitive offloading. Among the most frequent offloaders it was not statistically significant, which does not indicate its absence. The indirect association through fatigue was likewise weaker at higher offloading. These patterns held with additional covariates, a competing interaction with AI-use frequency, and shortened scales. Conclusion In this sample, cognitive fatigue accompanied the prospective association between overload and weaker plans to use AI. This pathway was weaker among postgraduates who delegated foundational tasks more often. Writing programs can teach students which foundational tasks to delegate, and tool developers can limit output overload.

title: Language-related task-fMRI patterns and restorative online brain–computer interfaces in post-stroke aphasia: a protocol for a systematic review with voxel-based meta-analysis and narrative synthesis
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
e822ca4134a5d8c8d7727c1f6f03ee68aa979a93.abstract: Background Post-stroke aphasia (PSA) can restrict everyday communication, social participation and access to rehabilitation. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) during language tasks (task-fMRI) identifies group-level regional activation patterns across distributed language networks, whereas restorative online brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) adjust feedback or training progression contingent on real-time neural signals. Here, restorative denotes a prespecified rehabilitation purpose rather than demonstrated therapeutic benefit. We will examine both evidence streams within language production and comprehension. Methods This protocol describes a systematic review incorporating voxel-based meta-analysis and a focused narrative BCI synthesis. Searches will cover PubMed, Embase via Embase.com, Web of Science Core Collection and APA PsycINFO via Ovid, adding IEEE Xplore for the BCI component. The primary task-fMRI outcome is spatial convergence of positive blood-oxygen-level-dependent responses for task &gt; baseline during production in adults with PSA; comprehension serves as a secondary model. Spatial pooling requires at least 10 independent inputs per domain, accepting compatible whole-brain maps, complete signed coordinate sets, or confirmed whole-brain reports of no suprathreshold peaks in either direction. Domains below this minimum will be described without spatial pooling or vote counting. Eligible BCI studies must have a prespecified restorative aim and evaluate adults with PSA over at least two training sessions featuring online neural control, reporting a longitudinal neural outcome, an independent pre–post language or functional-communication outcome measured without online BCI assistance, or both. BCI implementation and outcomes will still be synthesized narratively when regional classification is not possible. Conclusion The review addresses three predefined objectives: identifying consistent task-fMRI convergence in PSA, describing trained neural features and reported clinical associations in restorative BCIs, and relating reported cortical BCI targets to peaks from the corrected task-fMRI meta-analysis for the corresponding language domain. Trail registration: CRD420261457995.

title: Trustworthy AI for multimodal load-response modelling in team sports: a scoping review and full-text validation audit
container-title: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
92eda9136a55028de3d61b3243328292f5ffe5c2.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI), machine-learning and conventional statistical prediction methods are increasingly used in team-sport athlete monitoring, but it remains unclear whether current studies are validated and reported in ways that support trustworthy prospective use. This scoping review mapped predictive-modelling studies in team-sport athlete monitoring and multimodal load-response modelling and audited their validation and reporting practices. Methods Searches were conducted in OpenAlex, PubMed, Scopus and SPORTDiscus for records published from 2010 to 2026. After deduplication, screening and updated OpenAlex rerun screening, 258 studies were included and audited from full text. Systematic duplicate screening was not performed; full-text eligibility assessment and original audit coding were completed by a single reviewer. Data were extracted on publication characteristics, sport context, data modalities, modelled outcomes, model families and validation practices. A 10-domain trustworthy-AI audit assessed prediction context, temporal validity, repeated-observation independence, external validation, leakage control, calibration, class-imbalance handling, interpretability, uncertainty reporting and deployment/actionability. Bibliometric and NLP analyses provided complementary field mapping. A second reviewer independently assessed 45 studies from the original 223-study audit subset across all ten audit domains. Results The literature expanded rapidly after 2021, with performance modelling and injury-risk prediction as the dominant applications. Studies frequently used GPS/GNSS, session-RPE/internal load, wellness/sleep, HR/HRV, neuromuscular testing, IMU/accelerometry and video-derived features. Random forests, logistic/linear models and gradient boosting were the most common model families. Deployment-relevant validation remained limited. After targeted reassessment and updated-search incorporation, temporal validity was strongly documented in 28 studies (10.9%), while independent external validation was strongly documented in one study (0.4%) and partially documented in one additional study (0.4%). Leakage control, calibration, repeated-observation independence and model-level uncertainty reporting were also uncommon. Pre-correction exact agreement in the independent audit subset was 65.3% overall and varied substantially across domains. Discussion Predictive modelling in team-sport athlete monitoring is expanding, but model development has advanced faster than trustworthy validation practice. Future studies should define the intended decision context, preserve temporal and player-level data structure, prevent leakage, report calibration and uncertainty, validate models under realistic deployment conditions and translate outputs into practitioner-facing decision support.

title: A study on the synergistic effects of teacher–student interaction patterns and an AI-based emotional feedback system in secondary school chemistry laboratory classes: an intervention experiment grounded in inquiry-based instruction
container-title: Frontiers in Education
96b6b86b3b878503d2576ece5930fa96e5fb585b.abstract: While prior research has examined how teacher-student interaction influences student learning in conventional chemistry laboratory instruction, few studies have systematically disentangled the synergistic mechanisms that connect dynamic patterns of teacher-student interaction with AI-driven emotional feedback systems-and, critically, how these interactions jointly shape educational outcomes in AI-integrated chemistry laboratory classrooms. This gap constrains the evidence-informed design of emotion-responsive, intelligent chemistry pedagogy. This study employed a mixed-methods design integrating a quasi-experimental intervention with qualitative thematic analysis. A semester-long intervention was implemented with two cohorts of ninth-grade students: an experimental group ( n = 40) receiving inquiry-based chemistry laboratory instruction augmented by an AI-powered emotional feedback system, and a control group ( n = 38) receiving equivalent inquiry-based instruction supported solely by conventional teacher-student interaction. The study comparatively analyzed students' emotional experiences across the two instructional conditions. Distinct emotional trajectories emerged between the groups. The AI-supported experimental group exhibited a statistically significant increase in chemistry laboratory anxiety over the semester, with no meaningful improvement in subjective achievement. In contrast, the control group maintained stable anxiety levels and demonstrated consistent growth in perceived achievement. Moreover, the control group outperformed the experimental group in procedural compliance and the rigor of hands-on laboratory operations. No statistically significant intergroup differences were observed for other affective indicators-including sense of accomplishment and willingness to collaborate. These findings advance the theoretical understanding of human-machine collaborative pedagogy within intelligent learning environments. Empirically grounded, they yield actionable insights for the design of chemistry laboratory instruction in AI-integrated settings-particularly in developing learner-centered, emotion-aware frameworks for human-AI co-teaching.

title: AI-enabled medchain framework for secure healthcare data management
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
0cdcb98b9f23f572b51db909c53cf6fc8d567487.abstract: The rapid evolution of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies and wearable health monitoring devices has changed modern healthcare by enabling continuous remote patient monitoring and collecting real-time personal health records (PHRs). However, privacy, data breaches, authentication failures, and feature dimensionality in large-scale healthcare systems make secure and effective management of sensitive patient health information (PHI) more challenging. This study introduces an AI-powered MedChain system that uses blockchain, advanced cryptography, and smart IoT devices to protect sensitive healthcare data in transit, during classification, and at rest. The proposed system leverages secure consensus-based authentication to tailor protection strategies based on the sensitivity of patient data. This study presents an AI-enabled MedChain framework for the secure management of healthcare data, considering the aspects of sensitive-data classification, feature selection, Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based data augmentation, secure encryption, key management, authentication, and blockchain-based record management. The framework begins with C-score Min–Max normalization to preprocess and standardize healthcare records. A novel Fuzzy Intensive Support Scalar Vector Machine (FI-SSVM) computes the Absolute Confidential Feature Scaling Behavior Rate (AC-FSBR) to classify sensitive and non-sensitive data. To mitigate overfitting and high-dimensionality issues, the Spectral Sensitive Fit-Whale Optimization Algorithm (SSF-WOA) is employed for mutual feature selection. Furthermore, a Long Short-Term Memory Generative Adversarial Network (LSTM-GAN) is used to identify sensitive margins and accurately classify personalized health records. For secure storage and transmission, the system integrates with a dedicated blockchain network termed MedChain. Initially, it employs an Integrated Data Hash Indexing Policy (IDHIP) to manage sensitive records, followed by Multi-Parity Starvation Foldable Advanced Encryption Standard (MP-SFAES) for robust block-level encryption. Key management and consensus are governed by the Medi-Consensus Chain Link Policy Key Management (MC-CLPKM). The Metaverse-Master Proofing Registry Authentication Policy uses Secure Handover Mutual Peer-to-Peer (SHM-P2P) to verify identity and govern access. In managing and sharing sensitive healthcare records, AI-driven data classification, blockchain-based immutability, high-level cryptographic encryption, and decentralized design improve visibility, traceability, and efficiency. The proposed MedChain framework thus provides a comprehensive, scalable, and secure infrastructure for next-generation healthcare ecosystems.

title: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition network based on moment channel attention
container-title: Frontiers in Psychiatry
c72c11c36c7f9de5d76a34d7745e168510ab8cb0.abstract: While most cross-subject EEG emotion recognition studies focus on average accuracy, the high inter-subject variability of EEG signals causes severe performance inconsistency across individuals. This inconsistency poses a critical barrier to real-world deployment but has received insufficient attention. To address this issue, this study proposes a hybrid emotion recognition model integrating moment channel attention and Transformer, termed the Moment Attention Convolution–Emotion Transformer Network (MAC-ETN). The proposed hybrid network consists of three components: a local temporal feature extractor, a Moment Channel Attention Network (MCA), and a global temporal feature extractor. Specifically, depthwise and separable convolutions are employed to extract local temporal features. The moment channel attention mechanism incorporates the first-order moment (mean), second-order moment (variance), and third-order moment (skewness) for channel importance calibration; and global dependency modeling is achieved through a Transformer encoder. Performance evaluation is conducted on two public datasets, DEAP and MAHNOB-HCI, using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV). The experimental results show that the main advantage of MAC-ETN lies in markedly reduced cross-subject performance variability rather than higher mean accuracy. On the DEAP dataset, the mean accuracy of MAC-ETN (61.26% for arousal and 60.47% for valence is lower than that of the strongest baselines reported under the same LOSO protocol, while its accuracy standard deviation (7.88% and 5.31%) is the lowest among all compared methods. On the MAHNOB-HCI dataset, the F1 standard deviation of MAC-ETN is 1.48% for arousal and 0.30% for valence, far below the values reported for the baselines in the literature, although the latter were obtained under a subject-dependent protocol and with a different F1 definition, so this comparison is indicative only. These results indicate that MAC-ETN reduces cross-subject performance variability at a moderate level of accuracy, which is relevant for practical EEG-based emotion recognition applications.

title: Sensory Atypicalities in Individuals with Co-occurring Autism Spectrum Disorder and Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Scoping Review Protocol
container-title: F1000Research
8950afc0f516da7ecef9fb15e6dc98dc249cdf1d.abstract: Abstract* Sensory atypicalities are recognized as a core feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and are associated with a wide range of functional outcomes. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) frequently co-occurs with ASD and may influence sensory experiences and sensory information processing through attentional and inhibitory mechanisms. Although an increasing number of studies have examined sensory atypicalities in co-occurring ASD and ADHD (ASD + ADHD), the evidence remains fragmented because of variability in the sensory modalities, constructs, and assessment methods employed. A scoping review is needed to map the extent and nature of the evidence on atypical sensory experiences and sensory information processing in individuals with ASD + ADHD. The review aims to clarify the contribution of ADHD comorbidity to sensory heterogeneity within ASD and identify priorities for future research. Specifically, it will examine the sensory modalities and constructs assessed, the assessment methods used, characteristics of sensory functioning, as well as associations with a wide range of outcomes. The review will include peer-reviewed primary studies published in English from 2013 onward that include individuals with ASD + ADHD and compare them with individuals with ASD. To clarify the contribution of ADHD comorbidity, studies that compare individuals with ASD and those with ADHD will also be reviewed. Eligible studies must examine sensory experiences or sensory information processing in at least one sensory modality. MEDLINE, Web of Science, and PsycINFO will be searched. Reference lists of included studies and relevant review articles will also be screened. Two reviewers will independently screen titles, abstracts, and full texts. Any disagreements will be resolved through discussion, and if consensus cannot be reached, a third reviewer will be consulted. Data will be charted using a standardized Excel-based form and summarized descriptively using tables, figures, and narrative synthesis.

title: Effects of structured generative AI feedback on data science students' critical thinking: a propensity score matching approach
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
78ca80acca2067ba6d3f281f7059b4acc4060b96.abstract: Background AI feedback holds promise for supporting student learning, but unstructured use can lead students to passively accept AI-generated answers, weakening their independent reasoning. This study examined whether structured AI feedback affects undergraduate students' critical thinking, learning performance, and engagement in a data science analytics course. Methods An exploratory two-class quasi-experimental study was conducted in a three-month undergraduate data science course ( N = 167). One class received four-phase structured AI feedback, while the comparison class received conventional instructor feedback. Propensity score matching was used to improve comparability on observed baseline characteristics. Critical thinking was assessed using an adapted 40-item assessment covering five dimensions. Results Students receiving structured AI feedback demonstrated higher post-test critical thinking scores than matched controls, with a baseline-adjusted difference of 5.64 points (95% CI [3.62, 7.65], p &lt; 0.001). A significant between-group difference in pre-to-post changes was also observed. Dimension-level analyses revealed significant differences in Evaluation of Arguments, Interpretation, Recognition of Assumptions, and Inference, while Deduction showed no significant difference. Higher learning performance, cognitive engagement, and behavioral engagement were also observed in the structured AI feedback group, whereas emotional engagement did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion The findings provide exploratory evidence of differences in critical thinking and learning outcomes between the structured AI feedback and conventional instructor feedback classes. They highlight the potential relevance of feedback designs that encourage students to actively evaluate, question, and revise AI-supported analytical work, while underscoring the need for further studies that can isolate intervention-specific effects.
